items.author: Life And Style Desk
items.content:
Indian actor Janhvi Kapoor has condemned an AI-generated deepfake that manipulated footage from her Devara: Part 1 song Chuttamalle, calling the non-consensual use of her image a “deeply violating” act and warning that the issue reflects a broader reality faced by women.
The altered video, which circulated widely online, digitally manipulated footage featuring Kapoor from the 2024 film and presented her in a sexually explicit manner that was not part of the original production. The incident has triggered strong reactions across the Indian film industry, while renewing concerns about the misuse of artificial intelligence to target women.
Breaking her silence on the controversy on Instagram, Kapoor said the issue extends well beyond the particular video involving her. She argued that the misuse of technology reflects a broader problem surrounding the way women’s bodies, choices and boundaries are treated.
"The criminal misuse of technology to objectify women and circulating fictionalised content without consent is deeply violating, bordering on sexual assault. Almost every woman in my industry has faced some version of this. And women everywhere are increasingly being subjected to it," she wrote.
According to Kapoor, consent should not be viewed as complicated or open to interpretation. A woman’s decisions about her body, appearance and personal boundaries remain hers alone, regardless of what she wears or what choices she may have made previously.
She further argued that the growing threat posed by AI-generated abuse comes on top of the physical and social pressures women already face. In her view, technology has created another avenue through which women can be subjected to harassment and violations of their privacy.
"It is about the larger reality of being a woman. The gaze, the judgement, the constant negotiation for safety and the feelings that our boundaries somehow remain open to interpretation. That threat has now expanded into the digital sphere," she said.
Screengrab: janhvikapoor/Instagram
Kapoor also called for a wider change in social attitudes, saying responsibility should not rest solely on women or their families to protect themselves from harassment. Instead, she said society must challenge the attitudes that lead people to believe they are entitled to cross another person’s boundaries.
The actor thanked her Devara co-star Jr NTR for speaking out against the manipulated video. NTR had earlier condemned the clip and said he would pursue legal action against those responsible for creating and circulating it.
The controversy has once again highlighted the growing challenges posed by AI deepfakes, particularly when the technology is used to fabricate intimate or degrading material involving people without their knowledge or consent.
Kapoor ended by emphasising the importance of recognising women’s right to control their own images, bodies and boundaries.
"I hope everything unfolding around us right now forces those who participate in any form of harassment to introspect. Is it really too much for a woman to ask to simply be treated and seen as a human being? Her body, her image, her boundaries, her choice".
Her message ultimately centred on a basic principle: women should be treated as people with the right to control their own images, bodies and boundaries.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
The leader of Yemen's Saudi-backed government announced the beginning of a major military operation against the Iran-backed Houthis on Sunday, aimed at seizing the ‌territory under their control.
Regional and western officials had told Reuters earlier this week that Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies were planning to launch an assault on the Houthis, with the Saudis leading aerial combat and Yemeni forces fighting on the ground.
"Today, I announce the start of military operations to retake the remaining territory of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory," Yemeni ​President Rashad al-Alimi said in a televised address.
The Houthis, meanwhile, said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area ​of Saudi Arabia, claiming the attacks caused major fires, in response to what they said were 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes on ⁠Yemen in the past 12 hours.
There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia.
'Opportunities for de-escalation exhausted'
Al-Alimi said the decision to launch the counteroffensive came after all opportunities for de-escalation had been ​exhausted, accusing the Houthis of responding to efforts to calm the conflict with further mobilisation and escalation.
"Our position today is to assume the national responsibility of confronting the Houthi militia, after ​all opportunities for de-escalation have been exhausted," he said.
Al-Alimi said he had ordered the armed forces, security forces and all military formations to begin carrying out their assigned tasks under approved plans.
Saudi Arabia entered neighbouring Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition in support of the internationally recognised government, which the Houthis had driven out of the capital Sanaa.
Al-Alimi thanked Saudi Arabia for its support, saying the ​kingdom had "stood alongside Yemen in the darkest circumstances," and called on Yemen's regional allies and international partners to support the country, its armed forces and state institutions.
The US is already ​providing intelligence to support Riyadh's operations in Yemen, while some regional and European nations are providing mainly defensive military aid to the kingdom, six people with knowledge of the Saudi preparations told Reuters.
A truce agreed ‌between the ⁠warring parties in 2022 largely held until this year, when the Houthis launched missile and drone attacks on Saudi shipping and oil infrastructure in a spillover from the Iran war.
Houthis' lightning offensive
The Houthis have so far maintained the initiative on the ground, weeks after seizing the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait in a lightning offensive down the coast that saw government forces collapse.
Bab el-Mandeb is the southern exit passage of the Red Sea, a key shipping route between the Mediterranean and Asia that has assumed even more importance this year as an alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, ​which has been effectively closed by the ​Iran conflict.
Read More: Araghchi says Tehran serious about diplomatic path, rules out ‘military solution’ to end war
The Houthis already controlled the northwest ⁠of the country, where most of the population live.
In the last 48 hours, the Houthis have also made gains against government and local forces on strategic hilltops near Yemen's Taiz, military sources said, advancing on the last road between the city and Aden on the southern coast, ​where the Saudi-backed Yemeni government is based.
Houthi control over the Taiz-Aden road would lead to an effective siege of the city, Yemen's ​third-largest, inhabited by hundreds of ⁠thousands of civilians and where thousands of government forces are also stationed.
It would also consolidate control of that flat coastal Bab el-Mandeb area by seizing the rugged mountains overlooking them in the western Taiz countryside, according to Mohammed Al-Qadhi, a veteran Yemeni journalist from Taiz now working as a political analyst.
"This will help them protect their back in case of any operation against the coastline, and ⁠make recapturing ​those areas much more difficult," he said.
The city is important not just for its strategic location; Yemeni President Rashad ​al-Alimi is from the region, and a siege of Taiz would amplify an already-dire humanitarian situation in the country.
Three-in-four families in parts of Yemen are going hungry from the impact of the surge in fighting, which has displaced ​tens of thousands of people and disrupted supplies to millions, the World Food Programme said last week.

Tak lama setelah Xiaomi meresmikan REDMI 17 setelah resmi di Indonesia beberapa pekan lalu, Xiaomi Global memutuskan untuk rilis saudara kembar dengan penamaan yang berbeda. Dinamakan POCO C95 Pro, smartphone terbaru POCO satu ini membawa tampilan yang cukup identik, begitu pula spesifikasinya. items.content:
Tak lama setelah Xiaomi meresmikan REDMI 17 setelah resmi di Indonesia beberapa pekan lalu, Xiaomi Global memutuskan untuk rilis saudara kembar dengan penamaan yang berbeda. Dinamakan POCO C95 Pro, smartphone terbaru POCO satu ini membawa tampilan yang cukup identik, begitu pula spesifikasinya. Meski ada satu fitur ekstra yang absen alias tidak ikut diturunkan dari REDMI.
Ya, ini merupakan situasi yang lumrah dilakukan oleh Xiaomi maupun POCO. Umumnya, opsi yang ditawarkan lewat merek POCO bisa ditawarkan dengan harga sedikit lebih terjangkau. Bagaimana bisa? Lain halnya dengan smartphone Xiaomi yang lebih mudah didapatkan secara langsung, terutama ketika kini toko resmi luring Xiaomi sudah semakin banyak tersedia di berbagai wilayah di Indonesia. Lantas apakah spesifikasi POCO C95 Pro benar-benar identik?

Spesifikasi POCO C95 Pro, Tak Dilengkapi Lampu RGB
Dari tampilan desain POCO C95 Pro, memang terlihat sangat mirip dengan REDMI 17 4G, mulai dari opsi warnanya hingga bentuk modul kamera belakangnya. Dimensinya pun sama persis, tergolong cukup bongsor mengingat ukuran layarnya tergolong sangat luas. Memiliki ketebalan hingga 8,8mm, dengan bobot sedikit melampaui 232 gram.
Bodi POCO C95 Pro juga membawa sertifikasi IP64, sehingga tahan dari debu dan cipratan air. Namun bila dilihat secara seksama pada bagian bodi belakang, terlihat sedikit perbedaan dibandingkan desain REDMI 17. Yakni ada pada modul kamera utamanya—sama-sama mengusung dua lingkaran hitam dengan lampu kilat.
Namun begitu, spesifikasi POCO C95 Pro tak dilengkapi dengan lampu RGB khusus—sebuah fitur yang diperkenalkan lewat REDMI 17 4G, tidak hanya untuk fitur personalisasi tambahan, namun juga fungsi pemberitahuan seperti notifikasi ketika smartphone diletakkan dengan layar menghadap ke bawah. Selain fitur satu ini, semua spesifikasi kedua smartphone terbilang identik.
Mulai dari layar 6,9 inci HD+ 120Hz, chipset Helio G91-Ultra 12nm dari MediaTek, hingga kapasitas baterai besar 7500 mAh. Sudah tersedia untuk pasar global, harga POCO C95 Pro dibanderol mulai USD169 (Rp3 jutaan) untuk varian memori 6+128GB. Dan bila nantinya tersedia resmi di Indonesia, besar kemungkinan bakal dijual sedikit lebih terjangkau dibandingkan harga REDMI 17 4G.
Tetap Andalkan Daya Tahan Baterai Andalan
Melihat halaman produk resminya, POCO C95 Pro membawa kapasitas baterai besar 7500 mAh yang diklaim bisa digunakan hingga dua hari penuh, atau memutar musik hingga 91 jam maupun memutar video hingga 28 jam nonstop. Proses pengisian dayanya pun bisa berjalan cepat lewat dukungan fast charging 45W, membutuhkan waktu kurang dari 100 menit untuk isi daya dari nol sampai penuh.
Pengguna juga bisa memanfaatkan baterai POCO C95 Pro sebagai powerbank, yang bisa alirkan daya hingga 22,5W. Layar POCO C95 Pro juga sudah terproteksi Gorilla Glass 7i, membawa sertifikasi TUV agar lebih nyaman dipandang mata, serta diperkuat setup speaker stereo dengan mode volume maksimal sampai 300%. Dan untuk setup kamera POCO C95 Pro sendiri, diperkuat sensor utama 50MP f/1.8, dan dipasangkan bersama sensor sekunder, serta 8MP f/2.1 di sisi depan.
POCO sematkan dukungan perekaman video dari kedua sisi kamera sekaligus alias dual video. Smartphone ini jalankan Android 16, dengan tampilan antarmuka HyperOS 3, dengan fitur-fitur ekstra di dalamnya termasuk Xiaomi HyperIsland untuk tampilan notifikasi lebih intuitif.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
In the northern Finnish town of Muhos, 36-year-old farmer Joni Pitkanen is preparing for life with a new neighbour -- just kilometers away, tech giant Google is planning to build new data centres.
The planned data centres are part of an announced 13-billion-euro ($15-billion) investment in Finland over the next two years -- the US tech giant's single biggest investment in Europe.
A few kilometers down the gravel road that passes by Pitkanen's farm, the forest has already been cut down on land acquired by Google, with excavators now clearing the ground and rumbling trucks shuttling back and forth to the construction area located next to major power lines.
"The project is so massive that it's basically hard to really grasp, even though we're right here on the sidelines," Pitkanen said, as a few cows dozed in a meadow in front of the barn.
Google's expansion plans include the Finnish municipalities of Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala as well as Hamina, where it already operates a data centre. 
The massive investment prompted US President Donald Trump to urge Google to rethink its plans in a message on his Truth Social network.
Pitkanen said he was so far "fairly positive" about the project, as it will bring "large-scale business activity" and "life" to the rural municipality with a population of only around 8,800 people.
"But of course we are concerned about... how we can prepare for the energy consumption," he added.
In his office in the small village centre, Muhos mayor Kimmo Hinno told AFP that Google's "massive investment" kept him busy these days as "no industry of this type" existed here at present.
"This will completely change the situation for the entire municipality and the Oulu region," he said, adding that he expected "thousands of workers" of different nationalities during the construction period -- who will need both housing and other services.
Read More: OpenAI safety employee quits, says ‘time for trial and error is over’
Outside a grocery store, 60-year-old nurse Aila Heilima said she hoped the investment would "motivate young people to stay" in Muhos for work, instead of moving to bigger towns in search of job opportunities.
But Google's plans have already sparked controversy.
The Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) is currently investigating whether company Tuike Finland, which represents Google, had cleared more than 300 hectares of forest in Muhos without a mandatory environmental impact assessment.
"In our view, operations at this construction site should be suspended until it is clarified whether the project is in compliance with the law," Hanna Halmeenpaa, chair of the board of the Finnish Association for Nature Conservation, who filed the request with the agency, told AFP at the edge of the deforested area. 
"From the satellite images, we've seen that nature sites which should be preserved have also been logged," she added, explaining that the size of the clear-cut area was comparable to 420 football fields.
Google, meanwhile, told AFP in an email that "tree felling activities have been taking place in compliance with Forestry Act requirements" and they "were awaiting further guidance from LVV on this matter."
"We have conducted extensive nature surveys covering the entire area as part of the zoning and Environmental Impact Assessment processes, to ensure high-value nature zones within the sites have been protected during forestry works," said Sondre Ronander, communications manager for Google in Finland.
Finland has seen a spike in data centre investments, with its cool climate and relatively stable and cheap electricity that is mostly produced without fossil fuels thanks to nuclear plants as well as extensive wind and hydro power.
Prime Minister Petteri Orpo's right-wing government has prioritised attracting data centre investments to the Nordic country, which is grappling with record-high unemployment and sluggish economic growth.
But, as dozens of the energy guzzling centres are now under construction and many more planned by companies including Microsoft and TikTok, uncertainty around energy prices, grid capacity and environmental effects have sparked a public debate in Finland. 
A citizen's initiative demanding stricter regulation regarding data centre energy use and consequences for the environment gathered more than 50,000 signatures in just three days after it opened, meaning it will have to be reviewed.

items.summary:
Although called Tiangong, or "Heavenly Palace," China's space station is becoming less distant and more like home, as astronauts bring the comforting tastes into orbit.
The Chinese space kitchen now serves nearly 200 food items. Alongside dumplings and mooncakes, home-style dishes such as Kung Pao chicken, mapo tofu and fried rice have made it onto the station's menu.

items.author: xinhua.
items.content:
Although called Tiangong, or "Heavenly Palace," China's space station is becoming less distant and more like home, as astronauts bring the comforting tastes into orbit.
The Chinese space kitchen now serves nearly 200 food items. Alongside dumplings and mooncakes, home-style dishes such as Kung Pao chicken, mapo tofu and fried rice have made it onto the station's menu.
Videos showing astronauts savoring freshly cooked meat and cakes in orbit have gone viral. Their smiling faces and bright eyes make the aroma almost leap off the screen.
Yang Liwei, the country's first astronaut, joked at a recent press conference that he was envious. He said astronauts can now use air-frying equipment in space and enjoy baked chicken wings in orbit. During his Shenzhou-5 mission in 2003, which lasted less than one day, his diet was limited to packaged instant food that could not be heated.
Microgravity, cosmic radiation and the enclosed cabin environment impose strict requirements on space diets. Floating particles and droplets may drift into instruments and trigger malfunctions. Since Yuri Gagarin, the first human to travel into space, paste-like food and compressed energy bars had long served as the standard meals for astronauts.
In June 2013, Wang Yaping, together with two fellow male crewmates, carried out the 15-day Shenzhou-10 space mission. People remembered this female astronaut with a ponytail for her space lecture. At the same time, the image of her floating a "zongzi," a leaf-wrapped rice dumpling, by hand also left a deep impression on the public.
Zongzi is traditionally enjoyed during the Dragon Boat Festival, which happened to coincide with the Shenzhou-10 mission that year. To help the astronauts celebrate, this special snack was added to the spaceship pantry.
Eight years later, Wang spent Spring Festival aboard the Tiangong space station during the Shenzhou-13 mission. It is also China's first six-month-long space stay. Scientists customized the cuisine: for instance, they prepared dumplings with seafood fillings because Wang grew up by the sea, and plenty of spicy food for crew member Ye Guangfu, who was born in chili-obsessed Sichuan Province.
At that time, the core module Tianhe had several sections, including those for working, sleeping, dining and exercising. The videos of Shenzhou-13 crew practicing calligraphy and playing Taichi became social media hits.
China completed the construction of its space station in 2022, with one core module and two lab modules forming a 110-square-meter orbital structure. Oxygen can be fully regenerated, and water recovery exceeds 95 percent.
Since then, long-duration spaceflights have become routine, and the Chinese "space home" can host up to six astronauts in orbit at a time.
Space residency is also set to last even longer. One member of the Shenzhou-23 crew, currently aboard the Tiangong, will conduct a one-year in-orbit stay. Moreover, as China pushes further into deep-space exploration, these extended stays will become the norm, which means astronauts' diets will be more important than ever.
Read More: Chinese rocket firm, disease research lab to test space pharmaceutical payloads
Because weightlessness causes bone calcium loss and muscle atrophy, space food must be high in calcium and protein, low in sodium and balanced in dietary fiber. According to the Astronaut Center of China, researchers have developed space food that counteracts oxidative damage, supports immunity, reduces fatigue and regulates the gut microbiome.
But taste is another problem. In microgravity, blood shifts upward, causing nasal congestion and cutting smell sensitivity by at least 30 percent. Since taste is closely tied to smell, astronauts often find food bland. The center's researchers have responded with adding more strong-flavored dishes, with liquid soy sauce and concentrated chili sauce.
New technology has also played a big role in keeping astronauts well-fed.
The astronaut center, in collaboration with private companies, has upgraded the "space kitchen" with a suite of intelligent appliances for drinking water, food reheating and baking. This allows astronauts in orbit to enjoy hot meals within 20 minutes, rather than waiting longer or eating cold food. Liu Weibo, an expert with the center, gave an example of the hot-air baking oven, which is a pioneering Chinese design for space use that can efficiently remove cooking fumes and allow astronauts to enjoy barbecue in orbit.
During a space lecture for Hong Kong and Macao students last month, Shenzhou-23 crew member Li Jiaying, or Lai Ka-ying in Cantonese, showed freshly baked cakes and said they reminded her of egg waffles, a popular snack from her hometown. She is a Hong Kong local.
Space food supplies have also become more diverse and nutritious, including more fruits and vegetables, as well as frozen steak and chicken wings. The next-generation cargo craft Qingzhou, designed for future in-orbit supply delivery, will have greater cold-chain transport capacity.
However, long-term space residency requires reducing dependence on Earth's supplies, said center expert Bian Qiang. "The controlled ecological life-support tests we are conducting are intended to build an ecosystem in space that regenerates water, air and food on site, to reduce extraterrestrial survival's dependence on Earth resupply and ultimately achieve self-sufficiency."
Since the Shenzhou-16 mission in 2023, China has been growing plants in orbit. It has tested more than 20 varieties from 14 plant species, including lettuce, carrots, potatoes and wheat.
The Shenzhou-18 crew in 2024 was tasked with raising fish in an "aquarium" to study how space affects their growth. Scientists said the work may one day allow astronauts to enjoy fish from their own in-orbit harvests.
China is targeting a crewed lunar landing by 2030. Living on the moon will make resupply much more challenging because of the increased distance from Earth.
"We plan to build a Chinese 'lunar vegetable garden' on the moon," Bian said.
From heating, baking to farming, feeding astronauts well in space is not a luxury. It is part of the mission, bringing a taste of home to the universe.

Google Pixel 10a Gets $100 Price Increase in the US
The Pixel 10a was previously available in the US for $499. Its starting price has now increased to $599. The higher price applies to the base model, while other storage options can cost more.
The price change comes at a time when smartphone manufacturers are facing higher component costs. Other major smartphone brands have also started increasing prices for some of their devices.
Google has not provided an official explanation for the Pixel 10a price increase. However, rising costs across the smartphone supply chain could be one factor behind the decision.
Pixel 11 Series Pricing Unchanged for Now
Google has not increased the prices of the Pixel 11 series so far. However, further price changes cannot be ruled out if component and production costs continue to rise.
The Pixel 10a price increase could therefore be an early sign of broader pricing changes across Google’s smartphone lineup.
For consumers, the higher price makes the Pixel 10a less affordable than before. Buyers who were considering the phone may now have to compare it more closely with other smartphones in the same price range.
For now, the $599 price is confirmed on Google’s US online store, while Google has yet to publicly comment on the change or indicate whether similar increases will affect other markets.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is reportedly preparing a major change to the way users access Channels. WhatsApp is working on moving Channels directly into the Chats tab on both Android and iOS.
Currently, users need to open the separate Updates tab to find and follow Channels. Under the planned change, Channels could appear alongside regular conversations in the Chats section, making them easier to access without switching between tabs.
The change could also lead to the removal of the Updates tab. WhatsApp may use the space to introduce a new Contacts tab, where users could see contacts who are currently active.
WhatsApp May Move Channels to Chats Tab, Replace Updates With Contacts
The app is testing different ways to integrate Channels into the Chats tab. On Android, users who already follow Channels may eventually see a prompt asking how they want those Channels to appear.
One option would place followed Channels directly in the chat list. Another option would automatically archive them for users who do not want Channels mixed with their personal conversations.
WhatsApp is currently testing three different layouts for Channels in the Chats tab. The company is expected to choose the final design based on feedback and testing results before making it available more widely.
The same change is also being developed for iPhone users. However, the iOS version is still under development and is not yet available for beta testing.
Updates Tab Could Be Replaced
Moving Channels out of the Updates tab could make the existing section unnecessary. WhatsApp could therefore replace it with a Contacts tab.
The new section is expected to provide a dedicated place for users to see which contacts are active. This would represent another change to WhatsApp’s navigation system as the company continues to reorganize its main features.
However, the final design has not been confirmed yet. WhatsApp is still testing the new layout, so the interface could change before the feature reaches regular users.
Channel Status Feature Also Expanding
Alongside the navigation changes, WhatsApp is expanding Channel Status to more users on Android and iOS.
The feature allows Channel administrators to post temporary photo and video updates that disappear after 24 hours. Followers can view these updates through the channel interface, the Updates section, and the channel information screen.
WhatsApp decides which Channels receive access to the feature, and administrators cannot manually request activation.
See Also: WhatsApp Starts Rolling Out Restricted Chats on Android Beta – What Does it Mean
Availability
The Channels-in-Chats feature is still being tested and may not be available to all beta users. The iOS version is currently under development, while Android users may see the feature as WhatsApp expands its testing.
WhatsApp has not announced when the redesigned navigation will be released to everyone. The company could also make further changes based on testing before the final version rolls out.
For now, users will need to continue accessing Channels through the existing interface until WhatsApp officially introduces the new design.

items.title: Alcaraz through to Japan Open semis
items.summary:

His Canadian opponent was forced to withdraw after suffering an injury to his upper right thigh in the first game of the second set.
Defending champion Alcaraz will play fellow Spaniard Jaume Munar for a place in the final after the world number 64 ended the impressive run of 86th-ranked Kyrian Jacquet of France.
The match was hard-fought until Shapovalov's retirement, with Alcaraz troubled by the variety of his game as the world number 46 mixed deep shots with drop shots, and power with spin.
Alcaraz, who saved four set points against Matteo Arnaldi on Saturday, salvaged another here at 5-4 down and went on to seal the tie-break with a passing shot before Shapovalov's injury.
The Australian Open champion is playing only his third event since returning from a months-long wrist injury, having reached the quarter-finals

Alcaraz, who saved four set points against Matteo Arnaldi on Saturday, salvaged another here at 5-4 down and went on to seal the tie-break with a passing shot before Shapovalov's injury.
The Australian Open champion is playing only his third event since returning from a months-long wrist injury, having reached the quarter-finals of the US Open last month.
Later on Sunday, Valentin Vacherot upset France's Arthur Fils 7-5, 4-6, 6-4 to set up a semi-final against Jiri Lehecka.
Fils seemed to be making short work of the big-serving world number 18 when he earned two set points at 5-3.
But he then caved in, losing the next four games to hand Vacherot the opener on a superb down-the-line return.
Fils forced a deciding set after an intense battle, pumping his fist and rallying the crowd, but eventually succumbed in a tight two-hour, 20-minute match.
Lehecka, the Czech world number 23, breezed into the semi-finals with a 6-1, 6-1 demolition of Paraguay's Adolfo Daniel Vallejo, wrapping up the win in under an hour.

items.title: When New York turns the movies into a summer ritual
items.summary:
From Bryant Park to Pier 17 and Manhattan rooftops, New Yorkers are turning movie and television screenings into shared summer rituals, where the setting, the crowd and the stories become part of the experience.
There is something different about watching a movie in New York when the cinema has no walls.
Instead of rows of seats in a dark theatre, there is grass beneath you, people arriving with blankets and snacks, friends trying to find a good spot, couples settling in beside strangers and a city skyline providing a backdrop that no movie theatre could reproduce.
Then the lights go down and, for the next two hours, hundreds of people are watching the same story together.
That simple idea has become one of New York's most enjoyable summer rituals. Across the city, parks, waterfronts and rooftops are transformed into temporary cinemas.
Some screenings are devoted to beloved classics, while others are built around the latest television obsession.
Photo: Author

items.author: Nawal Ahmad
items.content:
From Bryant Park to Pier 17 and Manhattan rooftops, New Yorkers are turning movie and television screenings into shared summer rituals, where the setting, the crowd and the stories become part of the experience.
There is something different about watching a movie in New York when the cinema has no walls.
Instead of rows of seats in a dark theatre, there is grass beneath you, people arriving with blankets and snacks, friends trying to find a good spot, couples settling in beside strangers and a city skyline providing a backdrop that no movie theatre could reproduce.
Then the lights go down and, for the next two hours, hundreds of people are watching the same story together.
That simple idea has become one of New York's most enjoyable summer rituals. Across the city, parks, waterfronts and rooftops are transformed into temporary cinemas.
Some screenings are devoted to beloved classics, while others are built around the latest television obsession.
Photo: Author
Many of the outdoor events are free and operate on a first-come, first-served basis, while special screenings may require registration or reservations. But what they have in common is the feeling of watching something together.
After experiencing several of these events myself, I have started to think that the movie is sometimes only half of the attraction.
Bryant Park is one of the clearest examples of how this works. Its Movie Nights have become a New York summer tradition, with people arriving well before the film begins to claim a place on the lawn.
The atmosphere starts building long before the opening credits, as people bring blankets, meet friends, bring food and settle in for an evening rather than simply arriving for a two-hour screening.
This year, the summer movie-night special ended with The Truman Show being screened for the second time, as watchers came in the afternoon and waited until after sunset for the film to begin.
Sitting on the lawn in the middle of Manhattan and watching a film that so many people already know by heart made the experience feel strangely new.
Photo: Author
The movie itself was familiar, but the setting and the audience changed it. Someone laughs at a line you have heard ten times before, someone reacts to a scene you had forgotten was coming, and people around you quietly comment on moments as they happen. You become part of an audience again.
Perhaps that is one reason these screenings feel particularly appealing now, when so much entertainment is consumed privately and on demand.
Streaming has made it possible to watch almost anything at any time, but it has also made entertainment increasingly solitary. Outdoor cinema brings back the simple pleasure of reacting to a story alongside other people.
Television becomes a communal event
The phenomenon is not limited to old movies. Last summer, I experienced the other side of this culture with The Summer I Turned Pretty.
I went to Bryant Park for a special screening of the first two episodes of the show's third and final season. Fans gathered on the lawn with blankets, snacks and friends, and the atmosphere was closer to a concert or fan gathering than an ordinary television screening.
Photo: Author
What made the evening particularly memorable was the appearance of the cast. The actors came onto the stage to greet the fans, turning what had already been a large communal viewing experience into a live fan event.
For people who had followed the characters and storylines through the previous seasons, suddenly seeing the cast in front of them added another layer to the experience.
The audience already had theories, favourite characters and strong opinions about what was going to happen next. So when something happened on screen, the reaction travelled across the lawn: laughter, screams, cheers and collective gasps. It was essentially a giant group chat, except everyone was sitting together in the same physical space.
That is where watching television becomes something more than watching television. The audience is no longer simply consuming an episode; it is participating in a shared cultural moment.
City skylines become part of the film
The same idea takes on a completely different atmosphere at Pier 17. Brooklyn Bridge Park's Movies With A View brings free outdoor films to the waterfront, where audiences can watch with New York Harbor and the Manhattan skyline behind the screen. The screenings are first-come, first-served, making arriving early part of the ritual.
I first watched Forrest Gump at Pier 17, where the waterfront setting changes the entire feeling of a familiar film. The light changes as the evening progresses, the water moves, buildings begin to glow and the skyline becomes part of the visual experience. Somewhere between the real city and the movie on the screen, the two begin to overlap.
You are not just watching Forrest Gump anymore. You are watching Forrest Gump in New York on a summer night. That distinction sounds small, but it is exactly what makes these events memorable. The location becomes part of the story you remember later, just as much as the film itself.
Photo: Author
Branding for entertainment
The Summer I Turned Pretty experience also showed another side of this new entertainment culture.
For the show's finale, I attended a special screening event at the rooftop at 230 Fifth, where the atmosphere was much closer to a nightlife event than a traditional television screening. There was a bar-style rooftop setting, fans gathered around the screening and the feeling that the finale was an occasion rather than simply another episode.
There were even Sephora gift bags with Summer Fridays lip balms as part of the special collab.
That detail might sound incidental, but it says a lot about where entertainment culture is going. The show was not only being watched; it was being experienced, photographed, branded and remembered. The screening itself became content, the rooftop became part of the story, and the gift bag became something to photograph and take home.
The people attending were not just viewers anymore. They were part of a community of fans who could say they were there.
Photo: Author
This is where the relationship between entertainment and brands becomes particularly interesting. Streaming platforms and advertisers have realised that audiences do not necessarily want another advertisement telling them to watch something. Increasingly, they want to be invited into the world of the show.
The Summer I Turned Pretty Bryant Park event is a good example. Prime Video partnered with T-Mobile to transform the park into an experience inspired by the show's Cousins Beach setting, with themed installations and fan activities. The event brought the fictional world of the series into a real New York park and gave fans an opportunity to interact with the show beyond simply watching it on a screen.
The brand is no longer simply interrupting the entertainment; it is helping construct an experience around it. A beauty company can appear through gift bags, a telecommunications company can create a fan experience and a streaming platform can transform a television premiere into a physical gathering. The marketing becomes experiential.
And that can be remarkably effective because people are more likely to remember an experience than an advertisement. You may forget seeing a sponsored post online, but you are less likely to forget sitting on a lawn with hundreds of fans, watching a new episode and then seeing the cast walk onto the stage in front of you.
There is a larger cultural reason these evenings work. New York is one of the most densely populated cities in the world, yet it can also be surprisingly isolating. We pass thousands of people every day without knowing anything about them. Outdoor cinema temporarily changes that dynamic because everyone is looking at the same screen, waiting for the same scene and reacting to the same ending.
For a few hours, strangers become a temporary community.
That may be the most interesting thing about the city's outdoor cinema culture. It is not really about replacing the movie theatre; it is about adding something that the theatre, and certainly streaming at home, cannot provide: a sense of occasion, a sense of place and a sense that other people are experiencing the same thing at exactly the same moment.
Perhaps that is why New Yorkers keep coming back, bringing blankets, snacks and friends and waiting for the sun to go down. In a city where everyone is constantly moving, these screenings offer a rare opportunity to stop, sit beside strangers and share a story from beginning to end.
Because sometimes we do not just want to watch the story. We want to have someone beside us when it happens.

items.title: Apple Watch Series 12 Review: Familiar Looks, Tracks Like a Beast
items.summary: Apple Watch Series 12 is one of those upgrades that becomes more convincing the longer you use it. The design has barely changed, but Apple has made meaningful improvements where they matter more. The new Health Sensing System detects heart rate quicker and takes readings more frequently, while the Readiness score finally brings sleep, activity, recovery and other health metrics into one easy-to-understand number. Battery life was another pleasant surprise during my review, regularly lasting beyond a full day and draining noticeably slower during runs than on the Series 10 and Series 11.

items.content:
Dalal Street emerged as a founder’s paradise in 2025, with 18 Indian startups listing on the bourses and collectively mopping up a record ₹41,248 Cr from the public markets.
The surge was driven by a combination of macroeconomic tailwinds and regulatory support. While robust GDP growth projections helped revive investor appetite, SEBI’s reforms played a key role. Measures such as simplified DRHP filings reduced red tape, while more flexible ESOP rules allowed founders to retain meaningful ownership.
Retail investors also fuelled the frenzy as demat accounts crossed the 20 Cr mark. The OFS component dominated public issues last year, providing liquidity to the early backers of the new-age tech companies. Post-listing performance also followed the usual curve, with investors rewarding companies that prioritised profits, sustainable growth and governance over hype.
“⁠Besides the readiness that startups showed in their unit economics, there is also an increase in the founders committing to their businesses for next couple of decades and grow their businesses by adding adjacent profit pools – something that the public markets reward handsomely,” said Ashish Kumar, cofounder and general partner at Fundamentum Partnership.
Building on the momentum, fourteen new-age tech companies have already made their D-Street debut so far this year. Of these, ESDS Software Solution, Klassroom, RentoMojo, SEDEMAC, Kissht, LEAP India and Shiprocket made a bumper debut on the bourses.
Nevertheless, the IPO pipeline remains strong. Twenty six startups have already filed their DRHPs with SEBI, while over 25 are in various stages of finalising their IPO plans. Unicorns like OYO, Razorpay and Zetwerk alone could raise over ₹34,000 Cr in 2026, making it one of the biggest years for startup IPOs.
However, recalibration is likely to define 2026 as investors are expected to prioritise strong fundamentals, profitability and low cash burn when backing new-age tech companies.
“IPO-bound startups in 2026 will be increasingly defined by their ability to demonstrate predictable cash flows, sustainable unit economics, and operational discipline rather than headline growth alone. Public market investors will place greater emphasis on governance, capital efficiency and long-term value creation, favouring companies that balance scale with financial prudence,” Orios Venture Partners’ managing partner Rehan Yar Khan told Inc42.
There are other challenges as well. Average retail subscription levels are moderating, while foreign institutional investors (FIIs) are pulling back in droves, reflecting caution amid geopolitical tensions and muted secondary market performance. The ongoing conflict in West Asia has further complicated the situation.
Yet, the overall outlook remains bullish for new-age tech IPOs. Maturing business models, deeper domestic capital pools and an evolving regulatory framework favouring transparency position India as a leading startup IPO hub.

Investment advisory startup StockGro has pre-filed its DRHP with SEBI, eyeing an IPO in the range of ₹2,000 Cr to ₹2,500 Cr
