The
items.author: Debarghya Sil
items.content:
The past fortnight has brought several developments around Apple in India. The iPhone 18 Pro and Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo began shipping, putting the company’s latest hardware in focus. But another development has drawn attention: Apple Pay, a service the company has been talking about bringing to India for more than a decade, is finally here.
Apple launched the service in India on September 30, 2026, allowing users to pay at physical stores, within apps and on websites using an iPhone, iPad or Apple Watch.
In 2016, then CEO Tim Cook during his visit to India said that Apple was looking at bringing Apple Pay to India, and had even met the then ICICI Bank CEO Chanda Kochhar to understand the bank’s views on mobile payments. Ten years later, Apple Pay is finally here, but the payments landscape has changed considerably.
The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) processed 24.51 Bn transactions worth ₹29.82 Lakh Cr in August 2026, as per the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).
The question is whether Apple can find room in a market where consumers already have several ways to pay.
Narrower Than The US Version
Apple Pay allows users to add eligible cards to Apple Wallet and authenticate payments through Face ID, Touch ID or their device passcode. At physical stores, they can tap their devices against compatible contactless terminals. Online, they can pay without repeatedly entering card details.
The India offering is narrower than the service available in the US, where customers can use cards from a wider range of participating banks and issuers. US users can also access Apple Cash for person-to-person money transfers, subject to eligibility. Apple has not announced a comparable service for India.
At launch, Apple Pay supports eligible Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards. RuPay cards and cards from other banks are not supported under the initial rollout. This limits the number of consumers who can use the service, even among iPhone owners.
Tarun Pathak of Counterpoint Research said Apple’s entry is late from both a global launch and competition standpoint, but pointed to regulatory requirements and the relatively small size of India’s installed iPhone base as possible reasons for the delay.
“Clearance of regulatory and technical roadblocks allowed Apple to hold its standard global architecture when it comes to Apple Pay experience built around NFC card tokenisation, plus the native Apple ecosystem leveraging the security of Face ID, Touch ID, and Apple Watch integration for fast NFC tap-to-pay at POS terminals,” Pathak said.
Apple’s approach keeps the payment experience tied to its own devices and security architecture. However, the restricted bank rollout means the company will need to expand its partnerships before the service can reach a wider customer base.
UPI Poses A Challenge For Apple Pay
UPI’s dominance presents a different challenge for Apple Pay. Unlike markets where card-based payment plays a larger role, India has built a digital payment ecosystem around direct bank-to-bank transfers, with consumers using apps such as PhonePe and Google Pay for everyday transactions.
According to the Reserve Bank of India’s Payment System Report, December 2025, UPI accounted for 85.5% of digital transaction volume. This figure underlines how firmly UPI is embedded in India’s payment ecosystem, leaving Apple Pay to build adoption in a market where consumers already have an established way to pay.
Apple Pay’s launch in India does not support UPI integration. Its initial use case is therefore centred on consumers who own compatible Apple devices and hold eligible credit cards. With Apple Pay, the company is offering contactless payments, but Apple will need to give users a reason to choose card-based payment through its devices when UPI is already widely available.
The availability of tap-to-pay alone may not be enough to change consumer habits. Samsung Wallet already offers NFC-based payments on compatible Galaxy devices, alongside other wallet features. Despite Samsung supporting UPI payments, it has hardly made a dent.
An industry insider who has worked in fintech told Inc42 that the service is unlikely to make a major difference to the sector in its current form.
“Apple Pay launch is only restricted to Axis Bank, with no UPI integration. Even today Android users are around 90% of the mobile phone users. Apple Pay is just allowing you to save the card and pay via NFC,” the insider said.
The insider also pointed to existing options for Android users, saying popular apps such as Phonepe have integrated card-based payment features for Visa and Mastercard users. The source expects some Apple users to adopt the service for high ticket purchases but does not see it as a threat to the fintech industry.
The insider also questioned whether Apple would enter UPI, citing NPCI’s transaction data storage requirements and Apple’s policies of not storing transaction details.
Can Apple Pay Drive Card Payments?
Apple Pay’s entry could give a push to credit card transactions, particularly among iPhone users who prefer using cards for higher value purchases. Amrish Rau, MD and CEO of Pine Labs, had anticipated the service’s India entry before its launch, arguing that it could shift some transactions towards cards as credit card payments and UPI continue to grow.
“We do believe Apple Pay will enter the market before the end of this year. What that is going to do is flip and create a spread in terms of how payment transactions will happen. More and more payment transactions will go back to credit cards, as credit cards plus UPI continue to grow in the market,” Rau said during the company’s Q1FY27 earnings discussion.
Data from the Reserve Bank of India’s Payment System Report, December 2025 points to the growth in credit card spending. Credit card spending rose to ₹23.2 Lakh Cr in calendar year 2025, up from ₹8.9 Lakh Cr in 2021. Private banks also strengthened their position in the segment, accounting for 71.1% of outstanding credit cards.
Debit card usage, meanwhile, has moved in the opposite direction. Transaction volumes fell 67% between CY2021 and CY2025, as consumers increasingly shifted to UPI for everyday payments.
The divergence matters for Apple Pay. While UPI has become a common choice for routine transfers and purchases, credit cards continue to serve consumers looking for credit, rewards and payment flexibility. Apple pay could make card payments more convenient by allowing users to tap their devices at compatible terminals instead of carrying a physical card.
However, growth in credit card spending does not automatically translate into demand for Apple Pay. Besides, its reach will also depend on how many consumers are willing to change their existing payment habits.
For Apple, the immediate opportunity may be to increase the frequency with which existing users pay by card through its devices. Whether that translates into a meaningful shift in India’s payment mix will depend on wider bank support, merchant acceptance and consumer adoption.
Edited By Nikhil Subramaniam

items.summary: Sambhav Jain, a 28-year-old software engineer, died by suicide after jumping from a 41st-floor balcony. Police are investigating personal difficulties and financial issues stemming from a recent divorce and medical expenses. Jain's father had suggested he return home to resolve a monetary dispute. The authorities are examining evidence, including CCTV footage and WhatsApp messages.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu
Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has sworn in the newly elected 21 local government chairmen and their deputies, charging them to prioritise service delivery, accountability and responsible use of public resources.
The governor urged the officials to take their oath of office seriously, review it regularly and consider displaying it in visible locations as a constant reminder of their responsibilities.
“As you begin your journey, know that it is a call to serve,” Soludo told the chairmen, urging them to be their brothers’ and sisters’ keepers, which he said was in line with the agenda of the ruling All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA).
He said the officials should put aside their expectations and immediately focus on the responsibilities of office.
“I know that when you were applying for the job, you had all manner of aspirations, promises and expectations. Welcome to the world of reality and the clock starts ticking today. The work has already begun,” he said.
Soludo also emphasised the need for the officials to account for their time in office, noting that even the minutes spent at the swearing-in ceremony had already become part of their official responsibilities.
The governor noted what he described as APGA’s dominance in Anambra State over the past 20 years, saying the party’s candidates had, in the latest council election, faced little opposition in many areas.
He reminded the chairmen that previous administrations had helped build the structures on which they were assuming office, urging them to leave the local government system stronger for their successors.
Soludo also urged the new council leaders to embrace innovation while ensuring that their actions remained within the law.
He specifically called for measures to make the local government system more sustainable, noting that the new local government laws permitted councils to pool resources for the effective management of common financial obligations.
The governor advised the chairmen to study the handover notes from their predecessors and carefully assess the assets and liabilities they had inherited, given the challenges confronting the councils.
The swearing-in followed the declaration of the results of the local government election conducted on August 30, 2026.

items.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has deployed the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations, DIG Shehu Umar Nadada, to Imo State to coordinate the rescue of prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and other passengers abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway on Thursday, October 1, 2026.
The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Etuk, disclosed this in a statement issued on Saturday in Abuja.
According to the statement, Nadada arrived in Imo with two Commissioners of Police and conducted an on-the-spot assessment of the situation and the ongoing search-and-rescue operation.
The statement said the DIG also reviewed the operational strategies, deployment of personnel and operational assets, and issued further directives to strengthen the coordinated response.
The assessment was conducted alongside the Imo State Commissioner of Police, CP Audu Bosso; the Commissioner of Police in charge of Federal Operations, CP Akpan Anifiok; the Commissioner of Police in charge of the Police Mobile Force; other service commanders and members of the management team of the Imo State Police Command.
The police said the search-and-rescue operation had been intensified, with additional tactical teams and operational assets deployed to identified areas, supported by intelligence-led tracking of the abductors.
The statement said the police were also working closely with other security agencies to secure the safe rescue of the abducted persons and apprehend those responsible.
The statement quoted Nadada as assuring the public that the Nigeria Police Force remained committed to rescuing the 20 abducted persons and would sustain the operation until its conclusion.
He urged members of the public and the media to remain calm and vigilant, while calling on anyone with credible information that could assist the operation to contact the police or the nearest security formation.
The statement assured that all information received would be treated with strict confidentiality and that further updates would be provided as the operation progresses.

items.author: Oboh
items.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
The Benue State government has suspended the Buruku crossing point branch of the Nigeria Union of Maritime Workers, NUMW, following Saturday’s boat mishap, with several passengers still unaccounted for.
The state Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Denis Iyaghigba, ordered the immediate suspension of the union after conducting an on-the-spot assessment of the scene of the accident.
The Commissioner also ordered the suspension of the line operator and directed the arrest and detention of the boat skipper involved in the mishap.
The measures, according to the government, were part of immediate steps to prevent a recurrence of the incident and ensure compliance with safety regulations at the state’s waterways.
The government, in a statement issued by the Head, Media and Public Orientation, Office of the Commissioner for Marine and Blue Economy, Lubem Gena, said the Ministry had activated its search and rescue operations following the accident.
It said the search operation was being conducted in collaboration with local divers to intensify efforts to locate passengers who remained unaccounted for.
According to the statement, “the Benue state government has suspended the Buruku crossing point branch of the Nigeria Union of Maritime Workers, NUMW, following Saturday’s boat mishap in which several passengers remain unaccounted for despite the rescue of others.”
The Commissioner, who visited the scene of the incident, also directed that the line operator be suspended while the boat skipper be arrested and detained pending further investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident.
The statement quoted Iyaghigba as saying that the government was determined to establish what led to the mishap and take measures to prevent similar incidents on the state’s waterways.
“The Ministry has since activated its search and rescue processes and is working with local divers to intensify the search and rescue,” the Commissioner said.
He disclosed that an inter-ministerial committee had also been constituted to investigate the incident and establish its immediate, remote and underlying causes.
Iyaghigba said the committee would interrogate the circumstances surrounding the mishap and make recommendations aimed at strengthening safety standards at river crossing points across the state.
He further ordered strict compliance with the mandatory use of life jackets at all river crossing points in the state.
According to him, the directive was part of measures to strengthen safety and protect passengers using waterways across Benue.
The Commissioner also raised concern over an abandoned barge at the crossing point which was believed to have contributed to the accident. He consequently gave the owner of the abandoned barge a seven-day ultimatum to evacuate it from the crossing point or risk having it confiscated by the state government.
The statement said the Commissioner would work closely with relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies, MDAs, during the week to further interrogate the circumstances surrounding the accident and strengthen safety measures across the state’s waterways.
“The government said further details would be made available, but at the moment, investigations and rescue efforts continue,” the statement added.
The latest development followed the boat mishap at the Buruku crossing point on Saturday morning where a wooden boat conveying passengers capsized while crossing the River Katsina-Ala.
Several passengers were rescued following the accident, while others were reported missing, prompting the activation of search and rescue operations by the state government.
The post Benue Boat Mishap: Govt arrests boat driver, suspends maritime workers’ union appeared first on Vanguard News.

Nigerian comedian and actor Julius Agwu has opened up about a personal complication which followed the brain surgery he had in the United States.
Agwu underwent brain surgery in 2015 after doctors reportedly discovered three tumours in his brain. One of the tumours was said to be about the size of a golf ball.
Agwu disclosed that he experienced a loss of sexual function after the procedure, revealing the previously little-discussed impact during a recent episode of the Beer Parlour Talk Show uploaded on Saturday.
The comedian was discussing the effects of his health battle on his body, career and personal life when the host asked if the brain condition or surgery had affected other aspects of his health, including his sexual function.
Agwu responded, “After I do am, prick no dey work again now. He no dey work.”
Other participants on the programme, including Mr Patrick, subsequently discussed the nerve involved in the surgery and its connection to the brain as they sought to explain the effect Agwu described.
Agwu also reflected on his influence on Nigeria’s comedy industry, particularly his role in popularising the combination of music and comedy.
“Music comedy na me form am o, that is to tell you how my brain dey work,” he said.
The conversation later became emotional as Agwu broke down in tears while reflecting on his career, relationships and the people he felt abandoned him during his difficult period.
“God wey I dey serve, anybody wey get hand for wetin happen to me. I go dey look. My friends deserted me. They stopped talking to me, many of them. It is well,” he said.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
Vice President Kashim Shettima has defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the nation was “teetering on the verge of collapse” before the withdrawal of fuel subsidy and unification of exchange rates.
The Vice President urged Nigerians to be “generous” to a leader he credits with saving the economy.
Speaking after a meeting with Tinubu at the President’s Lagos residence, Shettima said the administration had been in “regular contact” with the President throughout his sojourn abroad and was “updating him on developments in the nation.”
“We are quite thrilled that he is back on the beat, and we have been in regular contact throughout his sojourn abroad,” Shettima said.
“Advances in science and technology have made it possible to really have impactful leadership wherever one might find himself. So we have been in regular contact. We speak almost every other day, and we are updating him.
“He saved the economy… saved the nation from falling to pieces”
While defending Tinubu’s policies, the Vice President insisted that the decisions to remove the petrol subsidy and realign multiple exchange rates were “far-reaching” and necessary to avert economic disaster.
“As usual, impactful decision-making that will touch the lives of the Nigerian people. It’s absolutely essential that Nigerians need to be generous to this poor man,” Shettima said.
“When we assumed the mantle of leadership, our foreign reserves was a staggeringly low 3.9 billion dollars — that was not enough to import oil for one month. He had the courage and the conviction to take far-reaching decisions.
“The withdrawal of the fuel subsidy, the realignment of the multiple exchange rates, were far-reaching decisions.”
“He literally… the economy was actually teetering on the verge of collapse. He saved the economy. I want Nigerians to understand this fundamental truism.
“We are on the road to Caracas. He saved our economy. He saved the nation from falling to pieces,” Shettima added.
Acknowledging the hardship many Nigerians face, Shettima struck a defiant tone, insisting that relief programmes are already in the pipeline.
“We appreciate the pains Nigerians are going through, but tough times do not last forever. Tough people do,” he said.
He announced a series of interventions targeted at the Northeast, including e-logistics deployment, electric tricycles, and electric taxis and buses, aimed at “assuaging the pains of our people.”
“In the next couple of weeks, we are going to launch e-logistics in the North East, we are going to run 10,600 electric tricycles to ease the pains of the people in the North East, and 300 buses and taxis, e-taxis. All these were meant to ameliorate the sufferings of our people,” Shettima said.
He also highlighted the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) as a “masterstroke” to assist students of limited means.
“The president has empathy, a lot of empathy for the common man. The NELFUND is a masterstroke aimed at assisting students of limited means to have access to drink from the Western Spring. So be rest assured that we’ll come up with programmes and projects to ease the pains of the people,” he said.
With elections looming, Shettima acknowledged the political temperature but insisted that governance would not be sacrificed on the altar of campaigning.
“Politics is in the air, but we will combine politics and governance,” he said.

items.content:
Lamine Yamal continued his superb goalscoring form as Spain secured a 3-1 win over the Czech Republic on Saturday in the Nations League.
The world champions moved three points clear of England at the top of Group A3, after Thomas Tuchel’s side demolished Croatia 7-0 earlier on in Rijeka.
Spain cruised into a two-goal lead with Yamal and Rodri Hernandez on target but Jiri Slama gave the Czechs a chance by pulling one back with 20 minutes to go.
However Mikel Merino wrapped up Spain’s win late on after Ladislav Krejci was sent off for the Czechs as Spain racked up a 41st consecutive unbeaten game, including the World Cup final win over Argentina in July.
Spain coach Luis de la Fuente made several changes in Oviedo from Tuesday’s win over Croatia, including handing debuts to full-back Ivan Fresneda and striker Roberto Fernandez.
It was one of Spain’s star names, though, who lit up the game early on, something he is beginning to make a habit of.
Yamal, who scored in the second minute of Spain’s first two games against England and Croatia, waited as long as the sixth before breaking the deadlock.
The 19-year-old winger, a major candidate for the Ballon d’Or, produced an exquisite finish from the right of the box, curled into the top corner after taking a touch to earn himself room to shoot.
Spain coach De la Fuente put his hands to his head in apparent shock at the quality of Yamal’s superb strike. It was the youngster’s 11th goal in his last eight games for club and country.
The winger’s Barcelona team-mate Rodri doubled Spain’s lead after 35 minutes, arriving in the box to drill into the top corner after the ball fell nicely for him.
De la Fuente took off Yamal at half-time to give the young Barcelona star a break before Tuesday’s visit to face Croatia.
With the teenager no longer gracing the Carlos Tartiere pitch the pace of the game slowed in the second half.
The Czechs pulled one back through Slama, who produced an excellent low finish across David Raya after Adam Hlozek played him in.
Arsenal stopper Raya was fortunate a few minutes later when he conceded possession with a misplaced pass while out of his goal, but the visitors could not capitalise.
Raya also spilled the ball badly and Ryan Naderi turned home but the goal was disallowed for a foul on Robin Le Normand.
Czech Republic’s determined efforts to battle back were derailed by Krejci’s red card, with the defender shown a second yellow for pulling back Fernandez.
Liverpool winger Victor Munoz prodded wide before Merino rounded off the win in the final stages with a finish from close range.

He said: “I had already contacted the Imo State CP. We have been talking since the day of the incident, and he assured me that the victims would be rescued unhurt.”

items.author: Ayesha Saghir
items.content:
Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) senior leader Khawaja Saad Rafique has blamed those who had "trampled" Pakistan for the country's present state, saying repeated amendments to the Constitution had failed to alter the fundamental reality that the country could not function without constitutional rule.
Speaking at a dialogue on "Good Governance and Rebuilding of a Collapsed System" organised by Leeds University at a local hotel in Lahore on Saturday, Rafique said those responsible included martial law rulers and their political facilitators.
He also held accountable sections of the judiciary for handing down judgments under doctrine of necessity.
He deplored that a "factory of traitors" had been established in the country, questioning how late Sindhi nationalist and politician G M Syed could have been called a traitor without being allowed to speak and instead being subjected to repression.
He said conditions in Balochistan had worsened and questioned how the state could conceal internal repression. He also asked who had prepared the militias in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, saying the whole nation was now paying the price in blood.
Speaking at the conference, former caretaker prime minister Anwaar-ul-Haq Kakar said he did not believe the country's system had completely collapsed, but acknowledged that its delivery mechanism was very weak.
He said governments based on accountability were recognised by the world and that democracy was the system capable of running them.
Kakar said democracy was a form of governance, but political parties had turned themselves into family systems.
Senior lawyer Hamid Khan said no democratic government had been allowed to complete its course in Pakistan and argued that this eventually resulted in the country being split into two.
Former federal minister and senior political leader Muhammad Ali Durrani said Pakistan had never truly experienced governance.
He said maintaining the status quo was no longer an option and urged people to act rather than expect everything to happen without effort.
Durrani warned that the younger generation was slipping away and that if its mindset was not understood, young people would no longer accept the status quo.
He said the public remained excluded from power and resources to such an extent that even a chief minister needed an aircraft.
"Bridging the distance between power and the people is now an urgent need."
He said politicians claimed they had been placed in power by force, through "Form 47 with a rope around their necks", and asked who should be considered responsible.
In his view, the person who forcibly installed someone in power was not the only culprit; the person who accepted the arrangement was also responsible.
Durrani said those operating under a hybrid system should decide for themselves whether that made them liable under Article 6.
He warned that Pakistan would not function unless public problems and authority were handed back to the people.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Israel said on Saturday that it attempted to kill Hamas’s top leader in the Gaza Strip in an airstrike on an apartment that local officials said killed five people, four of them women.
The pre-dawn strike came on the anniversary according to the Jewish calendar of the October 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest-ever day for Israel which retaliated with a devastating offensive in Gaza.
The Israeli military said it aimed to kill Ali al-Amoudi, describing him as the “right-hand man” of slain Hamas chief Yahya Sinwar and saying he was involved in planning the October 7 attack.
Israel said it was reviewing whether it killed or injured him.
It said it targeted him after learning that he was inside an apartment building, saying it showed that Hamas was using civilians as human shields.
“Today, al-Amoudi is the most senior Hamas figure in the Gaza Strip and is directly involved in Hamas’s terror activities and in rebuilding the organisation for war. The terrorist was struck in order to remove the threat,” a military statement said.
“Steps were taken to mitigate harm to civilians, including the use of precise munitions,” the military said, adding it “regrets any harm caused to uninvolved individuals”.
Israel killed Sinwar in Gaza in October 2024, in what many Israelis saw as a major symbolic victory, although Israel has vowed to keep destroying Hamas even since a US-brokered ceasefire was declared a year ago.
Amoudi is considered Hamas’s top person in the Gaza Strip. The movement’s leader Khalil al-Hayaa lives in Qatar and has tried to manoeuvre diplomatically to Hamas’s advantage.
Hayaa agreed in July to a US plan for Hamas to give up its weapons, in what President Donald Trump hailed as a breakthrough but Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu dismissed as insincere.
– Christians among dead –
An official at Gaza City’s Al-Shifa hospital told AFP it received at dawn the bodies of five people and a number of injured following an airstrike in the Rimal neighbourhood.
It said the dead were two women and their daughters, as well as a man.
Mahmoud Bassal, the spokesman for the civil defence agency which operates as a rescue force under Hamas authority, said two missiles directly hit the apartment, causing a fire and damaging the building.
Two of the five victims were Christians, the hospital director said.
Mourners gathered later on Saturday at the small Greek Orthodox church of Saint Porphyrius in Gaza City for the funeral of the two women, identified as 56-year-old Maysaa Abu Daoud and her 36-year-old daughter Mary Al-Najjar.
Ihab Ayad, a relative of the women, said that they had been “minding their own business” at home when Israel carried out the strike.
“We didn’t hurl stones or fire rockets. If any child among us carries a stone, they call him a terrorist, a murderer. But they possess the most powerful arsenal and destroy everything,” he said.
Around 1,000 Christians, most of them Orthodox, live in the Palestinian territory. A larger Palestinian Christian community lives in the West Bank, although emigration has increased since the start of the war.
The Hamas-led October 7 attack killed 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.
The massive Israeli offensive in response has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which is under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Israeli forces have killed more than 1,440 people since the announcement of the ceasefire a year ago, according to Gaza’s health ministry.
The Israeli military has identified five deaths in its ranks over the same period, as well as the death of one civilian contractor.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
The Allied Peoples Movement (APM) senatorial candidate for Oyo Central Senatorial District, Ambassador Olufemi Ajadi Oguntoyinbo, has called on President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to resign over what he described as worsening insecurity in the country.
Ajadi also urged Tinubu to abandon his reported bid for re-election in 2027 if his administration could not adequately address the security challenges confronting Nigerians.
He made the call while reacting to the reported abduction of 19 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to their orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states.
The prospective corps members were reportedly abducted after gunmen attacked two buses along the Owerri-Onitsha Road in Umunoha, Imo State, on Thursday.
Ajadi described the incident as unacceptable, particularly because the victims were young Nigerians travelling to participate in the national service programme.
“It is ridiculous and unreasonable that corps members who are travelling to serve their motherland should be kidnapped.
“These are young Nigerians who have completed their education and are being deployed to contribute to the development of their country,” he said.
The APM candidate urged Tinubu to direct security agencies to intensify efforts to locate and rescue the abducted prospective corps members, saying their safe return should be treated as a national priority.
“Mr President must make the immediate rescue of these corps members a priority. It is the responsibility of the government to protect Nigerians, particularly young people who are travelling across the country in the service of their nation,” he said.
Ajadi also expressed concern over the reported demand for N50 million ransom for each of the 19 victims, which would amount to N950 million if the reported figure is accurate.
He said the government should take measures to strengthen security on major highways used by prospective corps members and other Nigerians travelling between states.
Ajadi said the reported abductions and other security incidents required stronger measures by the Federal Government to protect lives and property.
He said the President should consider resigning if the abducted corps members could not be rescued.
“If these corps members are unable to be rescued, then Mr President should resign. It is barbaric for the father of the nation to continue his duty as President while some of his children are in the den of kidnappers,” he said.
He further urged Tinubu not to seek re-election in 2027 if his administration was unable to find effective solutions to the country’s security challenges.
“Tinubu should resign because he has not been able to meet the responsibility of solving the insecurity in the nation. He should not bother to contest in the 2027 general election. He should rather resign now,” Ajadi said.
He urged security agencies to sustain search-and-rescue operations until all the abducted prospective corps members were safely reunited with their families.
Ajadi also appealed to Nigerians to provide useful information to security agencies that could assist in the rescue operation and help prevent further attacks on travellers.

items.content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri
The North-East Governors Forum (NEGF) on Saturday unveiled an 11-point communique at the end of its 13th regular meeting which took place in Maiduguri, the Borno state capital. Floating the North-East Air shuttle was part of the resolutions reached..
The governors unanimously recommitted to speaking with one voice and acting with one purpose on matters of common subregional concerns as they relate to security, social, economic integration and development.
The meeting was Chaired by Professor Babagana Umara Zulum who is also the Chairman of the NEGF and Chief Host.
Present at the meeting were governors Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri (Adamawa state), Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya (Gombe), Mohammed Auwal Jatau (Deputy Governor of Bauchi state), representing the governor, and Idi Barde Gubana, Deputy Governor of Yobe state, representing the governor of Yobe state.
Their counterpart from Taraba was absent – and including his deputy.
Also in attendance was the Deputy Governor of Borno state, Umar Usman Kadafur.
Reading out the Communique at the end of their deliberations, Adamawa State Governor, Fintiri, said the Forum continues to appreciate the level of cooperation and collaboration among member-states since its inaugural meeting in Gombe in March 2020.
He said the forum’s role remains a work in progress.
The following communiqué was presented at the end of the meeting:
“Forum notes the tremendous achievements it has made in the last six years, noting that the most significant achievement was the unity of forum members, resulting in the Forum delivering tangible result in the infrastructural development of the subregion.
“Forum appreciates Mr. President for the renewed attention on the Port Harcourt–Jos–Bauchi–Gombe-Maiduguri rail corridor and frontier oil exploration at Kolmani and the Akwanga–Jos–Bauchi–Gombe–Biu–Maiduguri highway.
“Forum however, calls on Federal Government to revisit the exploration activities earlier commenced but subsequently stalled in Magumeri and Gubio Local Government Areas of Borno State.
“Forum acknowledges the concerted effort made by member states in providing power and energizing the subregion. It has moved the energy agenda from isolated state concerns to a regional energy agenda. The Dadinkowa hydropower plant now feeds the national grid. It encourages all member states to take advantage of the new electricity law and abundant sunshine to strengthen the electricity needs of the subregion and expanding solar and mini-grid solutions for development.
“Forum reiterates its long-standing concern over the seeming neglect of the Mambila Hydro power plant and call on the Federal Government to take advantage of the recent clearance of the legal encumbrance with the the arbitration ruling on the matter, to expedite action on the completion and take-off of the plant.
“Forum acknowledges the intervention role of the North East Development Commisssion (NEDC), in the Subregion. It calls for more investment in the Education sector, especially the release of the long-awaited scholarship awards to indigent students of the subregion and deploying more resource into the campaign for reducing the burden of out of school children and a coordinated support for the Tsangaya education.
To ease the cost of transportation, strengthen logistics and open the region to more economic activities, Forum agreed to partner with Green Ville Energy to build and provide more CNG and LNG stations within the region.
“Forum equally acknowledges and appreciates the support of the Federal Government through the NEDC in providing 10,000 Electric Tricycles, 10 Electric Buses and 300 Electric Taxes with a view to lessening the burden of transportation, to be launched in October.
“Forum acknowledges the appreciable success recorded in the onslaught against the insurgency in the north- East; the courage and sacrifice of the Armed Forces and other security agencies, the resilience of the people and the commitment of Governments at all levels, but regrets that the subregion is still confronted by daunting humanitarian and infrastructural challenges. Forum thus, reaffirm its commitment to supporting the Armed Forces and other security agencies while strengthening inter-State cooperation, intelligence sharing, community engagement and coordinated responses to emerging threats and at the same time, addressing the underlying socio-economic conditions that can expose the young people to exploitation by criminal and extremist elements.
“Forum acknowledges that the North-East has one of the youngest populations in the country, and this represents both an enormous opportunity and a responsibility.
“Forum Therefore, recommit to equipping the young people with quality education, vocational and entrepreneurial skills, technology and meaningful employment opportunities for a secure and prosperous region where the youth see a future for themselves and have legitimate opportunities to build dignified livelihoods.
“Forum decries the quantum of harm done to the environment through deforestation and agrees to partner with the Institute of Forest Research to train forest experts in the region.
“The next meeting is to hold on 18th – 19th December, 2026 at Gombe, Gombe state”. Fintiri explained on behalf of the NEGF Chairman, Professor Zulum.”
Vanguard News

items.title: Wike accuses Amaechi of using mother’s death for political purposes
items.summary:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has accused former Transportation Minister Rotimi Amaechi of “descending so low” by bringing his late mother into political arguments.
Wike spoke on Saturday during a visit to the Uzugbani Ekpeye National Executive Council at Ekpeye House in Ahoada East Local Government Area of Rivers State.
He was reacting to Amaechi’s claim during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday: the policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration contributed to his mother’s death by making it difficult for his family to afford her medication.
Wike criticised Amaechi for bringing his mother into political arguments, saying the deceased should be “resting peacefully.”

items.content:
Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has accused former Transportation Minister Rotimi Amaechi of “descending so low” by bringing his late mother into political arguments.
Wike spoke on Saturday during a visit to the Uzugbani Ekpeye National Executive Council at Ekpeye House in Ahoada East Local Government Area of Rivers State.
He was reacting to Amaechi’s claim during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Friday: the policies of President Bola Tinubu’s administration contributed to his mother’s death by making it difficult for his family to afford her medication.
Wike criticised Amaechi for bringing his mother into political arguments, saying the deceased should be “resting peacefully.”
“Anybody who watched television last night would cry when somebody is bringing his own mother to play politics. Your mother that we thought should be resting peacefully,” Wike said.
“In one of the videos, he said if ADC wins election, his mother would be very happy,” Wike said.
“So, the only condition is that your mother will not be happy if ADC does not win. Too bad! She will not be happy. But ADC will not win. How can you bring a loved one who just died to bring in politics?”
Wike also questioned Amaechi’s claim that he could not afford his mother’s medication, citing his former positions as Speaker of the Rivers State House of Assembly, governor and minister.
“This was a speaker for eight years, from 1999 to 2007. This was a governor for eight years, from 2007 to 2015,” he said.
“This was a minister for eight years, from 2015 to 2023, and your mother was sick, and you are telling the whole world, and because of the policy of Tinubu, you couldn’t buy drugs for your mother, and so your mother died.”
The FCT minister further questioned why Amaechi did not seek financial assistance from friends and associates if he could not afford the medication.
“You have told the world that your wife is an industrialist, yet an industrialist couldn’t give you money to buy drugs for your mother,” Wike said.
“Look at who-is-who who came with all private jets to bury a woman whom you could not buy drugs for because you were taking care of other people. You didn’t tell them, ‘My mother was sick, can you help me? Give me money; let me buy drugs.’”
Wike described Amaechi’s comments as an attempt to use his mother’s death for political purposes.
“People can descend so low to use their mother to play politics,” he said.
He also questioned Amaechi’s claim that he could not afford his mother’s drugs, referring to properties he said the former governor owns in Old GRA, Port Harcourt, and Abuja.
“Look at the house you are living in in Old GRA, look at the house you are living in in Abuja, and then you say you are unable to buy drugs, and that was why your mother died. Enough is enough of this kind of embarrassment,” Wike said.

In his opening remarks, the Chairman of the Local Organising Committee, Prof. Emmanuel Akinfala, said 18 sports will feature in the 10-day competition.
Prof. Akinfala, who is the Deputy Vice-Chancellor, Administration, OAU, disclosed that about 50 universities from Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal and Sierra Leone have already arrived, with more expected before full commencement on Monday.
“We are going to have eighteen games, and everything will be done within ten days. The games include football, volleyball, handball, badminton, chess, table tennis, lawn tennis, hockey, cricket, swimming, eSports, and squash,” he said.
The Pro-Chancellor of Obafemi Awolowo University, Ambassador Adejare Bello, said the university is proud to host the 15th edition of the competition.
Bello assured that OAU will deliver a memorable Games, adding that the organising committee has put a lot in place to make the participating universities enjoy the competition.
“This is the 15th edition, and in the last 10 years, OAU has hosted it for the second time. The last time was in 2023 and now again in 2026,” Bello said.
He stressed the importance of sports to academic life, noting that, “It is not good to walk day and night without exercising your body. It is medically recommended that if you sit in a place for one or two hours, you have to move around and stretch your legs.
“It is even recommended that you take at least 10,000 steps in a day. The university encourages that, notwithstanding that we are here to learn and do research, we must be involved in exercise,” he added.

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
Pakistan has given an ambitious deadline of December next year to sell its nine power distribution companies that are annually bleeding Rs700 billion, but the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has questioned the model that does not completely stop haemorrhaging even after privatisation.
The government has assured the IMF that it would sell these distribution companies by December 2027, except Quetta Electricity Supply Company, which alone caused Rs154 billion losses in fiscal year 2025.
The government plans to retain most of the past liabilities before the sale and would also continue with the highly uneconomical but politically correct policy of maintaining the same electricity price across the country for both privatised and state-owned entities, according to the sources.
The Privatisation Commission this week briefed the IMF about its plan to sell power distribution companies and its engagement with the prospective buyers. According to the Central Monitoring Unit of the finance ministry, the 10 power distribution companies caused Rs299 billion in losses and another Rs551 billion was given in subsidies during fiscal year 2025. This brings total annual bleeding to Rs850 billion.
The IMF was informed that the government would sell nine power distribution companies by the end of next December, with the first batch of three efficient companies to be sold by March next year. The government was earlier planning to sell these three companies by December this year, but its plan is facing at least a three-month delay.
The privatisation of Faisalabad, Gujranwala and Islamabad power distribution companies was at the due diligence stage, which the government now expects to complete in three months.
The IMF was told that Fesco will be sold in January, Gepco in February and Iesco in March next year. When contacted, the spokesman for the Privatisation Commission confirmed that the IMF has been given the first quarter timeframe to privatise the first batch of three power distribution companies.
The government has planned to sell nine of these entities in four different batches by taking advantage of a healthy momentum created by the sale of Pakistan International Airlines.
According to the spokesman, the second batch, comprising Hyderabad and Sukkur power distribution companies, would be privatised between April and June next year. Another four companies, Peshawar, Hazara, Lahore and Multan power distribution companies, are targeted to be sold by December next year, according to the Privatisation Commission.
However, Quetta, which caused Rs112 billion losses and consumed another Rs54 billion in subsidy in the last fiscal year, is not part of the privatisation plan.
According to the approved privatisation structure, the government will separate land as an asset and the liabilities of pensioners from the balance sheets of Faisalabad, Gujranwala and Islamabad power distribution companies. As of June 2025, the total liabilities of the retired employees of just three companies were equal to Rs312 billion, which may further jump due to the splitting of balance sheets based on March 2026 results.
In June last year, the total assets of these companies were Rs1.2 trillion compared to liabilities of Rs1.05 trillion, showing a total net positive equity of Rs145 billion. The assets and liabilities are planned to be parked in a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV).
The sources said that detailed discussions were also held with the IMF about the government's approved transaction structure, which would not end inefficiencies and the pressure on the budget would also remain even after privatisation.
The IMF also questioned the government about any lessons that it learnt from the controversial privatisation of K-Electric – the country's only privatised entity. Despite privatisation, the government has kept Rs163 billion worth of subsidies in this fiscal year's budget for K-E.
In case the final multi-year tariff of Rs32.37 per unit is implemented, the annual subsidy requirement would come down to around Rs120 billion.
The Privatisation Commission informed the IMF that it would continue the policy of uniform tariff post-privatisation of these entities. However, this negates the purpose of privatisation as the consumers of efficient power distribution companies would still be paying the cost of inefficiency in Quetta, Peshawar and Sukkur.
The spokesman for the Privatisation Commission said that the privatisation transactions are "being structured based on a uniform tariff continuing post-privatisation and the investors (have also been) informed about it".
The IMF also inquired about the implications of carving out the liabilities from the balance sheets of the companies that would be sold. The lender was of the view that this model would not help stop the bleeding. But the Privatisation Commission officials took a stance that, on the same model, PIA had been privatised.
The government had parked Rs673 billion in losses in PIA Holding Company, which jumped to Rs817 billion as of June this year.
The spokesman said that it was "not correct" that the IMF has issues with the proposed privatisation structure that may reduce the bleeding for the government, but it doesn't completely stop the building up of losses.

The Faisalabad Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry (FWCCI) has approved the establishment of a board of management to strengthen institutional oversight and accelerate its ongoing and planned initiatives for women's empowerment, business development and export promotion.
FPCCI Vice President Qurrat-ul-Ain, speaking as chief guest at the FWCCI Annual General Meeting, said the proposed board would provide an institutional mechanism for expediting the chamber's projects and future initiatives.
She highlighted FWCCI's progress since its establishment in 2017, particularly the launch of Pakistan's first Women Business Incubation Centre in 2021, which was upgraded into a Women Resource Centre in 2023. In 2024, the chamber established the Pakistan Women Export Facilitation Centre (PWEFC) to help women entrepreneurs access international markets and develop export-oriented businesses.
Qurrat-ul-Ain said efforts were also underway to acquire 100 acres of land at the Faisalabad Industrial Estate Development and Management Company (FIEDMC) for a proposed Women Entrepreneurs Enclave. Separately, efforts were being made to secure two acres at FIEDMC for a dedicated building for PWEFC and FWCCI.
She paid tribute to founding president Rubina Amjad for her contribution to establishing and developing the chamber and urged members to support newly elected President Kanwal Saeed and her team. Outgoing President Shahida Aftab presented an overview of the chamber's achievements during her tenure and thanked the executive committee and members for their cooperation.
Taking charge for the 2026-28 term, Kanwal Saeed said her leadership would focus on addressing internal and external challenges, improving communication with members, strengthening trust and participation, and enhancing financial discipline.
She said the FWCCI should demonstrate clear value to its members by highlighting the opportunities, services and benefits that could stem from active participation rather than relying solely on membership contributions. Newly elected Senior Vice President Samia Tahir and Vice President Dr Sania Arshad also addressed the AGM, while Punjab Provincial Ombudsperson Dr Najma Afzal attended as special guest.
Founding president Rubina Amjad congratulated the newly elected office-bearers and executive committee, while outgoing Vice President Maimoona Imran conducted the AGM proceedings, which were attended by a large number of FWCCI members.

Investors head into a part of the calendar that tends to be upbeat for US stocks, but that seasonal strength is under threat from a number of challenges, including a surge in bond yields and the market's apparent dependence on massive AI spending.
As the fourth quarter kicks off, the stock market is already on pace for a solid year. The benchmark S&P 500 as of Friday had gained nearly 13% in 2026 and sat about 1% below its mid-August record high. Markets face a busy end of 2026, with the start of corporate earnings season and a pivotal Federal Reserve meeting in coming weeks, along with the looming November 3 mid-term elections that will decide control of the US Congress.
"It does tend to be a seasonally strong period, however I think this year investors are facing some headwinds as we go into the fourth quarter," said Tracie McMillion, Head of Global Asset Allocation Strategy at the Wells Fargo Investment Institute.
Since 1945, the S&P 500 averaged an increase of 4.2% in the fourth quarter, with the index posting gains 85% of the time, according to research firm CFRA. That average percentage rise is more than twice that of the other three quarters.
Fourth quarters of mid-term years have generally been even stronger, with an average gain of 6.4%, as stocks "benefit from the lifting of election uncertainty," Sam Stovall, Chief Investment Strategist at CFRA, said in a note. While fourth quarters tend to shine, mid-term years overall historically have been subpar, a trend stocks have defied so far in 2026. The S&P 500 has averaged a 15% dip in mid-term years historically, while the deepest drop so far this year has only been 9%, according to McMillion of the Wells Fargo institute.
The firm is on "high alert" for a pullback between now and election day, she said, for example, if it looks like the Democrats can wrest full control of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republican party. "If we were to see a change in the leadership in the House and the Senate combined, then we think that could have some policy ramifications that could impact the markets," she said, while adding that a pullback could be a buying opportunity.
The most immediate issue for stock investors is the jump in bond yields. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield on Thursday hit 5.34%, its highest level in 24 years. Yields, which rise when bond prices fall, have soared amid expectations for strong economic growth, surging energy costs that are driving up inflation, and increased competition for capital as companies issue debt to fund AI expansions. Higher yields likely already are impeding the market's advance, investors said. They can create more investment competition for equities and pressure stock valuations, while translating into more expensive borrowing costs throughout the economy.
"The interest rate story is the biggest headwind," said Chuck Carlson, Chief Executive Officer at Horizon Investment Services. "You're going to need some relief on that front. I don't necessarily think the market will tank per se, but to get a meaningful rally in the face of that, I think is going to be a struggle for the market."

By Dayo Johnson, Akure
Ondo State Governor, Lucky Aiyedatiwa, has assured corps members deployed to the state of a safe, peaceful and conducive environment throughout their one-year national service.
Aiyedatiwa gave the assurance during the swearing-in ceremony for the 2026 Batch ‘C’ Stream I corps members deployed to Ondo State, held at Ikare-Akoko.
Represented by the Commissioner for Youth and Sports Development, Segun Henry Omoyofunmi, the governor said the security and welfare of corps members remained priorities of his administration.
“Let me assure you that the security and welfare of corps members remain important priorities of this administration.
“The state government will continue to work closely with the NYSC and relevant security agencies to ensure that corps members serving in Ondo State enjoy a safe, peaceful and conducive environment throughout their service year,” he said.
The governor urged the corps members to take full advantage of the Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development (SAED) programme, saying the skills acquired could help them become self-reliant after their service year.
“The skills you acquire through this programme can become valuable tools for self-reliance, entrepreneurship and sustainable livelihoods beyond the service year.
“The Ondo State Government remains committed to creating an enabling environment for young people to develop their talents, establish businesses and contribute meaningfully to the economic growth of our state,” he said.
Aiyedatiwa also advised the corps members to serve with integrity and discipline while respecting the people and institutions in their host communities.
He urged them to embrace diversity, build relationships across cultural and geographical boundaries, and remain committed to national unity and peaceful coexistence.
“I therefore charge you to uphold the rules and regulations of the NYSC scheme and to conduct yourselves in a manner worthy of responsible Nigerian youths.
“Be ambassadors of unity, agents of positive change and champions of peace wherever you find yourselves,” he added.
In her address, the NYSC State Coordinator, Kuburat Omowumi Bakare, also urged the corps members to take the SAED programme seriously.
She said the initiative offered practical and entrepreneurial skills that could enhance their economic independence and contribute to job creation.
“This initiative offers you practical and entrepreneurial skills that can enhance your economic independence and contribute to job creation.
“I urge you to take full advantage of the training opportunities available and to develop competencies that will remain relevant beyond your service year,” she said.
Bakare advised the corps members to be good ambassadors of the NYSC, their families and their institutions, urging them to serve with humility, integrity and dedication.
She also appreciated Governor Aiyedatiwa for his continued support for the NYSC scheme and the welfare of corps members in the state.
The Chairman of the NYSC Governing Board, represented by the Permanent Secretary, Lanre Abiodun, urged the corps members to approach their service year with an open mind, a positive spirit and a determination to make meaningful contributions.
He also appealed for continued cooperation among government institutions, host communities, employers, traditional institutions, security agencies and other partners to enable corps members contribute effectively wherever they are deployed.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Joseph Erunke
Former Minister of Information and Culture, Alhaji Lai Mohammed, has urged African governments to reposition the Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions (MICE) industry as a major economic tool, saying the continent currently accounts for only about four per cent of a global market estimated at $1.3 trillion.
Mohammed said African countries could no longer afford to treat MICE mainly as a tourism activity, arguing that business events should be deliberately used to attract investment, expand trade, build partnerships and create jobs.
The former minister made the call while speaking as a panellist at the ninth Africa MICE Summit in Mombasa, Kenya, themed, “Building Africa’s MICE Economies.”
He said conferences and exhibitions should serve as platforms for bringing investors, buyers, policymakers, experts and businesses directly into African economies.
“ MICE should not be seen simply as people coming to Africa, staying in hotels, eating in restaurants and flying home.
“MICE is an economic instrument. It can bring investors, buyers, policymakers, experts and businesses into our economies. In other words, MICE can become Africa’s deal-making engine,” he said.
Mohammed urged African countries to develop MICE strategies around their respective economic and cultural strengths rather than competing indiscriminately for the same events.
He cited Nigeria’s entertainment industry, Kenya’s athletics and tourism sectors, South Africa’s conference industry and Rwanda’s emergence as a regional business gateway as examples of comparative advantages that could be converted into stronger MICE economies.
The former minister also advocated collective African bids for major international events, with hosting responsibilities shared among countries.
He cited the joint hosting of the 2026 FIFA World Cup by Canada, Mexico and the United States as an example of how countries could collaborate to stage major international events.
Turn events into economic ecosystems
Mohammed identified Lagos as a potential case study in transforming events into wider economic opportunities, recalling a study commissioned during his tenure as minister which indicated that about 20,000 events were held in the city every month.
He also cited the growth of “Detty December” as evidence of how major events could stimulate activity across sectors including aviation, hospitality, transportation, entertainment, media, fashion, technology and retail.
“The opportunity is to turn events into ecosystems,” he said.
However, Mohammed, who chairs the Board of Trustees and Governing Council of the Eko Tourism Foundation, said Africa’s MICE ambitions would remain constrained without significant improvements in infrastructure and ease of movement across the continent.
He listed convention centres, hotels, airports, transportation networks, digital infrastructure and reliable utilities among the facilities needed to attract major international events.
He also called for improved intra-African air connectivity, wider adoption of e-visas and visa-on-arrival arrangements where appropriate, as well as expedited visa processing for accredited conference delegates.
Beyond physical infrastructure, Mohammed said African countries must strengthen their broader investment environments, warning that political uncertainty, policy reversals, weak institutions and corruption could undermine investor confidence.
“Africa does not only have to sell its opportunities. It has to sell credibility,” he said.
Shift from delegate numbers to investment
Mohammed said African governments should also change how they measure the success of business events.
Rather than focusing mainly on delegate numbers and hotel occupancy, he urged governments to track investments attracted, business meetings held, trade generated and jobs created through MICE activities.
He further advocated the establishment of empowered National Convention Bureaux in African countries to bid for major international events, coordinate government and private-sector efforts, facilitate business visitors, generate MICE intelligence and measure the economic impact of events.
According to him, smaller African countries could also become significant MICE destinations by positioning themselves as platforms connecting businesses and markets rather than merely as destinations for consumption.
He cited Rwanda’s positioning as a regional business gateway as an example of how a smaller country could leverage strategic positioning to attract business events.
Mohammed said the ultimate test of any MICE event should go beyond attendance figures.
“Did an investment come? Did a trade relationship begin? Did a business partnership emerge? Did jobs get created?
“That is when MICE stops being merely an event, and becomes an engine of economic transformation,” he said.
Delegates from 19 countries participated in the two-day summit, which was formally opened by the County Executive Council Member for Tourism, Culture and Trade, County of Mombasa, Mohamed Osman Ali.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
US President Donald Trump has called on Congress to introduce mandatory prison sentences for people convicted of defrauding Medicare, Medicaid and Social Security, while proposing personal financial liability for state and local politicians who knowingly fail to stop fraud.
Trump made the call in a video posted on Truth Social on Saturday, saying the proposed legislation would eliminate probation as an option for people convicted of stealing from federal benefit programmes.
“Today, I’m calling on Congress to pass legislation to address fraud in Medicare, Medicaid, and Social Security programs,” Trump said.
“First, Congress must impose mandatory minimum sentences on fraudsters who steal from critical benefit programs designed to take care of the sick, feed the hungry, care for our children, and protect our senior citizens, retirees.”
He said people convicted of stealing from the programmes should face lengthy prison terms, with tougher penalties based on the amount stolen.
“Under our proposal, probation is no longer an option for the fraudsters. If you steal from the American people, you will go to prison, and for a long period of time,” he said.
“And the more you steal, the longer you’ll stay in that prison. Not only that, but if you’re a convicted fraudster who gets caught stealing from the American people a second time, your sentence will be doubled.”
Trump also proposed doubling the sentence of convicted fraudsters who are caught committing the offence for a second time.
“If you’re a convicted fraudster who gets caught stealing from the American people a second time, your sentence will be doubled,” he said.
The president further proposed making state and local politicians personally liable for losses caused by fraud if they knew about it, had the power to stop it but failed to act.
“Under our proposal, if a state or local politician knows about fraud and has the ability to stop it, but does nothing about it, they can be personally liable for the full loss of the American taxpayers’ money that they should have stopped and they should have saved,” Trump said.
Trump did not provide specific sentencing ranges or explain in the video what legal standard would determine whether an elected official knew about fraud or had the ability to prevent it.
The proposal comes amid stepped-up federal efforts by the Trump administration to combat fraud involving government benefit programmes.
“This legislative proposal will make fraudsters think long and hard before they keep stealing from the American people and will make crooked and corrupt politicians think also long and hard before they ignore fraud that they can stop and that they should stop,” Trump said.
He ended the video with a warning: “So from now on, fraudsters, we’re watching you.”

By Ikechukwu Nnochiri

…as FG okays quarterly policy dialogue
By Ikechukwu Nnochiri
ABUJA — Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) on Friday identified vote-buying as a major problem that the Federal Government must find ways to tackle ahead of the 2027 general elections.
In separate presentations at the 2026 National CSOs Summit held in Abuja, representatives of various organisations working to promote credible, transparent and inclusive elections in the country decried the repeated failure to prosecute individuals previously arrested for vote-buying.
They said the country’s electoral process would continue to be undermined unless stringent measures were adopted to ensure the prosecution and conviction of offenders, thereby serving as a deterrent to others.
In his remarks, the Executive Director of the Value Rebirth and Empowerment Initiative (VREI), Pastor Edewor Egedegbe, argued that a credible and peaceful election requires informed citizens.
He maintained that reports of inadequate funding for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) “raise serious concerns about preparations for the election, which is just months away.”
He added that late funding not only disrupts the planning process but also increases the risk of avoidable failures.
Insisting that the electoral body had not done much in terms of voter enlightenment, Egedegbe said INEC must also open its books by publishing what it has received so far.
“It should start procurement of needed items and embark on the training of essential manpower.
“Democracy succeeds where citizens participate in the process without fear or intimidation,” he added.
For his part, the Executive Director of the Peering Advocacy and Advancement Center in Africa (PAACA), Chief Ezenwa Nwagwu, highlighted the importance of encouraging citizens to register and obtain the Permanent Voters Card (PVC), which he said carries more value than a bank Automated Teller Machine (ATM) card.
“This is what we should be emphasising. The cost of electricity is embedded in the PVC, so also is the cost of education and everything about life in the country.
“It is not about asking people to take money from candidates and vote their conscience. When you sell your PVC, it diminishes your citizenship.
“The fact that you think the law does not work in the country does not mean that you cannot be used as an example to show how the law works,” Nwagwu stated.
He blamed the recurring cases of vote-buying during elections on what he described as “the pauperisation of citizens.”
“Until we realise the powers we have as citizens, we will continue to shortchange ourselves.
“We should always ask ourselves this question: if votes don’t count, why then do politicians place value on your votes?
“As we move towards the 2027 general elections, we as citizens have to re-examine ourselves and take over the power of polling units from the politicians. The citizens must drive the process,” he insisted.
Meanwhile, the federal government said it had approved the establishment of a quarterly civil society policy dialogue forum to institutionalise citizens’ participation in policy formulation, implementation and evaluation.
The Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, who represented President Bola Tinubu at the summit, said the forum would provide a structured platform for evidence-based advocacy and ensure that community-level concerns were reflected in government decisions.
He also pledged the FG’s commitment to expand civic space for social accountability, including greater collaboration with accredited CSOs on public finance transparency, budget tracking and monitoring of humanitarian and grassroots interventions.
“This administration firmly believes that no nation can achieve inclusive, equitable and sustainable development without a vibrant, credible and responsible civil society operating within an open and enabling civic space,” he added.
The National Convener of the CSOs Summit, Ambassador Kunle Yusuff, who is the Director-General of the Civil Society Organisations on Community Advancement and Humanitarian Empowerment Initiative (CSCHEI), said the aim was to galvanise the various organisations to brainstorm on the way forward as the nation braces for another round of elections.
Yusuff said the summit was proposing a sustainable partnership compact through which the government, civil society and the private sector could work jointly on national priorities rather than operating from positions of suspicion.
According to him, the proposed framework will provide a mechanism for monitoring government policies, budgets and electoral promises, while ensuring that information generated from communities reaches relevant authorities.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday invited to Israel as a guest of honour the Indian captain of a Tel Aviv-bound flydubai flight who offered a dramatic account of how he saved the plane after being attacked.
Netanyahu said he wanted Captain Smit Machchhar and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, one of Israel’s key international partners, to light a flame at a national ceremony for Israel’s Independence Day next May, saying the role was usually reserved for Israeli citizens.
“You are a true hero of the brave peoples of India and Israel and you are a hero of the entire world,” Netanyahu said in a video his office released of his telephone conversation with the hospitalised captain.
UAE investigators have said that the co-pilot planned the “terrorist act” by attacking Machchhar with an axe.
Asked how the attack unfolded, Machchhar said the co-pilot had asked to take time to pray, as devout Muslims do five times a day.
“A lot of locals, they do pray, which is not out of the ordinary. While he was praying, out of respect, I was just looking at the front and not at the back,” Machchhar said.
“Suddenly after I think I would say about four to five minutes, there was a big blow to the back of my head. My first thought was that there was catastrophic damage to the aircraft and something is not right.
“But then after that the blows kept coming one after the other. That’s when I realised that it’s not the aircraft, it’s the other guy who was in the cockpit with me.”
While saying his memory was not entirely clear due to his injury, Machchhar said he managed to pull open the cockpit door “but I think he shut it back closed.”
“I had that one last fight left in me,” Machchhar explained, saying he knew he faced certain death if not.
“That’s when I pushed against everything. I gave everything that I had and just went for the door and opened the door and thankfully people were waiting.”
AFP

By Kingsley Omonobi
The Inspector-General of Police (IGP), Olatunji Disu, has deployed the Deputy Inspector-General of Police in charge of Operations, DIG Shehu Nadada, to Imo State to coordinate the rescue of the prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and other passengers abducted along the Owerri-Onitsha Expressway on Thursday, 1 October 2026.
Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete *niedu made this known in a statement on Saturday in Abuja
The statement said the DIG arrived in Imo State with two Commissioners of Police and conducted an on-the-spot assessment of the situation and the ongoing search-and-rescue efforts.
It added that the DIG also reviewed the operational strategies, deployment of personnel as well as operational assets, and provided further directives to strengthen the coordinated response.
The statement further explained that the assessment was conducted alongside the Imo State Commissioner of Police, Audu Bosso; the Commissioner of Police, Federal Operations, Akpan Anifiok; the Commissioner of Police in charge of the Police Mobile Force; as well as other Service Commanders and members of the Management Team of the Imo State Police Command.
It pointed out that the search-and-rescue operation had been further intensified, with additional deployments of tactical teams and operational assets across identified areas, backed by intelligence-led tracking of the suspects.
The statement added that “the Police are working in close coordination with sister security agencies to ensure the safe rescue of the abducted persons and the apprehension of the perpetrators.
“The DIG Operations, DIG Shehu Umar Nadada, assured members of the public that the Nigeria Police Force is committed to securing the safe rescue of the 20 abducted persons and will sustain the operation until the mission is successfully concluded.
“He urged members of the public and the media to remain calm and vigilant and encouraged anyone with credible information that could assist the operation to promptly contact the Police or the nearest security formation.”
The statement assured that “all information received will be treated with strict confidentiality and further updates will be issued as the operation progresses.”

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
The co-pilot of flydubai flight FZ1073, which was bound for Israel, attempted to carry out a "terrorist attack" with an axe during the flight, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general said on Saturday.
The co-pilot was identified as Hammam al-Hammami, an Omani national, a source with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters.
A second source briefed on the investigation confirmed the co-pilot's name. UAE authorities did not immediately respond to a request for confirmation of his identity.
Disaster was averted on Wednesday after passengers and crew subdued the co-pilot, who had attacked the captain in what Israeli officials said was an apparent attempt to crash the plane carrying more than 170 passengers and crew.
While Emirati authorities and the airline have not publicly identified the co-pilot, Israeli officials have previously said he is an Omani national. Oman has not commented on the incident.
"Investigations into the incident involving flydubai flight FZ1073 found that the co-pilot had attempted to carry out a terrorist attack," Prosecutor General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi said in a statement carried by the UAE's state news agency.
The co-pilot attacked the pilot inside the cockpit with a crash axe and attempted to take control of the aircraft, the prosecutor general said. A crash axe is typically kept in the cockpit for use during emergencies such as crashes.
The investigation into flight FZ1073, including the suspect's motives, is ongoing, and the findings will be released once the "necessary procedures" have been completed, the prosecutor general said. The UAE is leading the investigation.
The airline is owned by Dubai's government.
The prosecutor general's comments were the first by Emirati investigators to describe the incident as an attempted terrorist attack.
Following the release of the prosecutor general's statement, Anwar Gargash, a senior adviser to the UAE president, said on X that the Gulf country had zero tolerance for terrorism and would show no leniency toward extremist rhetoric.
Flydubai said the circumstances surrounding the incident were still under investigation and that it was not in a position to comment further, a spokesperson said on Saturday.
Reuters could not immediately verify professional and social media pages reportedly belonging to the co-pilot, which suggested he had worked for other airlines.
Royal Air Maroc told Reuters, in response to a question about his potential employment there in the past, that he had undergone a three-month training with the airline in 2025 but his application to work there afterwards was rejected. RAM did not elaborate.
