items.author: Ronggo
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – AGON mengumumkan kehadiran monitor AGP257FT (2/10) untuk kebutuhan gaming mutakhir. Monitor revolusioner tersebut menghadirkan kecepatan refresh rate 1050Hz resolusi 1920×1080. Refresh rate itu jadi yang tertinggi saat ini dikombinasikan dengan waktu respons 0,1ms dan teknologi Oxide panel proprietary, menciptakan pengalaman gaming yang terasa nyaris sempurna untuk para pemain kompetitif yang mengejar setiap frame.
AGON AGP257FT tidak hanya mengejar angka tinggi pada spesifikasi semata tapi juga menghilangkan jeda antara input pemain dan feedback visual di layar. Dalam esports di mana pertandingan bisa diputuskan dalam millisecond, monitor seperti ini menjadi peralatan yang sama pentingnya dengan mouse dan keyboard berkualitas tinggi.
Menggunakan panel berbasis teknologi Oxide yang terintegrasi dengan desain sirkuit GIA, AGP257FT mampu mendorong kristal cair dengan kecepatan yang jauh lebih cepat dari panel LCD konvensional. Artinya, transisi warna dan gerakan di layar tidak hanya terlihat lebih halus secara matematika, tapi juga terasa lebih responsif. Setiap pergerakan mouse, setiap peluncuran proyektil dalam permainan, setiap reaksi menghindar musuh akan terlihat dengan ketajaman yang luar biasa.
Selain kecepatan, AGON juga memperhatikan kesehatan mata pemain yang bermain berjam-jam. Hardware-based Low Blue Light solution mengurangi cahaya biru berbahaya langsung dari sumber backlight, bukan hanya melalui software filter yang sering membuat warna tampak kuning. Teknologi Circular Polarization yang tersertifikasi TÜV Rheinland menghasilkan cahaya yang lebih menyerupai sinar alami, mengurangi silau dan kelelahan mata tanpa mengorbankan performa responsif.
Baca juga: Aksesori vivo Selfie Monitor Bikin Vlogging Pakai vivo X500 Jauh Lebih Mudah
Spesifikasi AGON AGP257FT dan Prakiraan Harganya
Spesifikasi lengkap monitor ini mencakup panel Fast IPS dengan dukungan NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible untuk sinkronisasi refresh rate tanpa tearing. Motion Blur Reduction Plus (MBR+) meminimalkan blur saat gerakan cepat, membuat objek yang bergerak tampak lebih tajam dan terdefinisi. VESA DisplayHDR 400 memberikan brightness dan dampak visual yang lebih besar tanpa mengorbankan responsiveness, sementara resolusi 1920×1080 dipilih karena itu adalah sweet spot antara performa grafis dan kecepatan rendering pada refresh rate setinggi ini.
Dari segi harga, AGON belum mengumumkan nominal pasti untuk AGP257FT. Mengingat ini adalah monitor gaming flagship dengan teknologi proprietary tercanggih, kemungkinan harga akan berada di kisaran premium, kemungkinan antara tiga hingga lima juta rupiah ketika diluncurkan. Untuk perbandingan, monitor esports flagship lain di pasar saat ini berada pada rentang harga Rp2,5 hingga 4 juta, tapi AGP257FT menawarkan refresh rate yang berbeda.
Sementara untuk kehadirannya di Indonesia masih belum dikonfirmasi oleh AGON secara resmi. Monitor flagship seperti ini biasanya diluncurkan lebih dulu di pasar Asia Timur seperti Taiwan, Hong Kong, dan Jepang sebelum ekspansi ke pasar regional lainnya termasuk Indonesia. Jika mengikuti pola peluncuran AGON sebelumnya, AGP257FT kemungkinan akan tersedia di Indonesia sekitar tiga hingga enam bulan setelah peluncuran global, melalui distributor resmi dan partner retail besar seperti toko komputer di mall-mall.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have not yet reached an agreement on the draft Auto Policy 2026-31, with the Fund asking for more data before the proposed policy moves forward.
According to sources, the issue was discussed during the latest economic review talks between Pakistan and the IMF. The government has prepared the final draft of the Automotive and Auto Parts Manufacturing Policy 2026-31, but it will now require IMF approval before being presented to the federal cabinet.
During the discussions, Pakistani officials briefed the IMF on proposed tax measures for electric and hybrid vehicles. Under the draft, electric vehicles (EVs) would face a 1% sales tax, while the sales tax on other hybrid vehicles could rise to 18%.
IMF Seeks More Data on Pakistan’s Draft Auto Policy 2026-31
The government also discussed plans to increase vehicle exports. It has set a long-term goal of taking exports from the auto sector above $3 billion by linking local manufacturers and auto parts producers with international supply chains.
The proposed policy also aims to provide greater protection to vehicle buyers. Under the draft, manufacturers would be responsible if the price of a vehicle increases after a customer has booked it. Companies would also have to provide an expected delivery date when accepting a booking.
The Ministry of Industries and Production prepared the policy with several objectives, including reducing vehicle prices, improving manufacturing quality, increasing exports, and encouraging the production and adoption of electric vehicles.
One of the key proposals is to connect Pakistan’s auto parts industry with global supply chains. The policy would also introduce performance targets for manufacturers, along with penalties for companies that fail to meet them and incentives for those that achieve their targets.
The draft places particular focus on electric vehicles. The government plans to promote EVs and increase competition in the sector to encourage innovation, new technologies and improved vehicle features.
Customs duties on conventional vehicles are proposed to fall by up to 80% over the next five years. The draft also calls for similar treatment of plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) and range-extended electric vehicles (REEVs).
Several tax incentives have also been proposed for electric vehicles, including exemptions from federal excise duty, capital value tax and withholding tax. Equipment used for EV charging stations could face a customs duty of just 1%.
See Also: IMF Agrees to Withdraw Proposed Tax Hike on Solar Panels and Stationery Ahead of Budget 2026-27
The government has also proposed increasing the financing limit for electric vehicles to Rs10 million. The repayment period could be extended from three years to five years to make EV financing more accessible to buyers.
The policy includes specific export targets for the automobile industry. Car manufacturers would be required to export 4% of production during 2026-27, with the target rising to 20% by 2030-31. For auto parts manufacturers, the export target would increase from 5% to 15%.
The draft also proposes the adoption of international vehicle standards. Pakistan plans to adopt 62 global standards and introduce another 45 standards by 2029.
According to the policy document, the proposed measures could help Pakistan save around $17 billion in foreign exchange between 2026 and 2031.
However, the IMF has yet to approve the draft and has requested additional information before further discussions. The policy will therefore remain under review until Pakistan and the Fund reach an understanding on its proposed measures.

The Galaxy S27 Ultra remains the biggest question mark. Samsung’s System LSI div
items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Samsung has reportedly started mass production of its next-generation Exynos 2700 chipset, giving the company more time to prepare the processor for its upcoming Galaxy S27 series. However, it is still unclear whether the chip will power the top-end Galaxy S27 Ultra.
According to a report from Korean publication The Elec, Samsung has set a production target for the Exynos 2700 that is more than 10% higher than the target for the Exynos 2600. The increase is reportedly linked to the expected addition of the Galaxy S27 Pro to the company’s flagship lineup.
The Galaxy S27, Galaxy S27+, and Galaxy S27 Pro will use the Exynos 2700 in markets such as South Korea and Europe. In the US and China, these phones are reportedly expected to use Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 instead.
Samsung Begins Mass Production of Exynos 2700 Ahead of Galaxy S27 Launch
The Galaxy S27 Ultra remains the biggest question mark. Samsung’s System LSI division, which develops the Exynos chipset, is reportedly pushing for the Exynos 2700 to be used in the company’s most expensive S-series model. Using its own chipset in the Ultra could benefit Samsung’s semiconductor business while also demonstrating the performance of the new processor.
However, Samsung MX, the division responsible for its smartphones, will make the final decision. Several factors are reportedly being considered, including benchmark performance, thermal efficiency, Qualcomm’s chipset pricing and Samsung’s ability to produce enough Exynos 2700 units.
Earlier reports claimed that internal testing showed promising results for the Exynos 2700. The chip was reportedly around 9.5% faster than the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 in multi-core Geekbench testing. Qualcomm’s processor was still ahead in single-core performance. These results have not been independently verified, so they should be treated as early information rather than confirmed retail performance.
See Also: Tecno Maintains Strong Local Presence as Samsung Production Falls and Xiaomi Misses Top 10
The Exynos 2700 is expected to be manufactured using Samsung’s second-generation SF2P 2nm Gate-All-Around process. Compared with the first-generation SF2 process used for the Exynos 2600, the newer manufacturing technology is claimed to deliver up to 12% better performance, 25% lower power consumption and an 8% smaller chip size.
Samsung is also expected to make architectural improvements to the processor. The Exynos 2700 could use Arm’s newer C2 CPU cores, replacing the C1 cores found in the Exynos 2600.
The start of mass production also fits the expected launch schedule for Samsung’s next flagship phones. Chipsets generally require several months of production and preparation before they are ready for commercial devices. If the current timeline remains unchanged, the Galaxy S27 series could arrive around February or March 2027.
For now, Samsung appears to be preparing the Exynos 2700 for several Galaxy S27 models, but the final decision on the Galaxy S27 Ultra has yet to be made.

items.author: APP
items.content:
A delegation of the All Parties Hurriyat Conference (APHC), led by Convener Ghulam Muhammad Safi, on Saturday called on President Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Dr Muhammad Najib Khan and discussed the latest situation in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir (IIOJK).
The meeting discussed Indian actions in IIOJK, alleged human rights violations, the situation of Hurriyat leaders and activists, and efforts to highlight the Kashmir issue at the international level.
The AJK president said the Jammu and Kashmir dispute was an internationally recognised issue and its final settlement should be in accordance with the aspirations of the Kashmiri people and relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions, a press release issued here said.
He said the Kashmiri people should be given their right to self-determination to decide their future, and appreciated Pakistan’s political, diplomatic and moral support for the Kashmir cause.
Dr Najib Khan said the unilateral actions of August 5, 2019 could not change the disputed status of Jammu and Kashmir or affect the Kashmiri people’s right to self-determination.
He called upon the international community to take notice of the situation in IIOJK and urged the UN human rights bodies and international observers to be given access to the territory for an impartial assessment of the situation.
The president also called for highlighting alleged human rights violations, arrests of political activists and Hurriyat leaders and restrictions on freedom of expression in IIOJK.
He said the United Nations should fulfill its commitments to the Kashmiri people and urged the international community to press India for implementation of relevant UN resolutions.

Ghulam Muhammad Safi and other Hurriyat leaders congratulated Dr Muhammad Najib Khan on his election as President of AJK and conveyed their best wishes to him.
The APHC convener briefed the AJK president on the latest situation in IIOJK and the challenges faced by Hurriyat leaders and activists.
He said the Hurriyat Conference would continue its political and diplomatic efforts to highlight the Kashmir issue at the global level and advocate the right to self-determination of the Kashmiri people.
The delegation included Muhammad Farooq Rehmani, Mehmood Ahmed Saghar, General Secretary Advocate Pervaiz Ahmed Shah, Syed Faiz Naqshbandi, Sheikh Abdul Mateen, Sheikh Muhammad Yaqoob, Chaudhry Shaheen Iqbal and Information Secretary Imtiaz Wani.
The participants resolved that the political leadership of Pakistan and AJK, the Hurriyat Conference and other stakeholders would continue joint efforts to highlight the Kashmir issue internationally and convey the voice of the Kashmiri people to the world.
Speaker of the AJK Legislative Assembly Chaudhry Tariq Farooq was also present during the meeting.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Elon Musk's xAI on Friday persuaded a US federal appeals court to halt Minnesota's first-in-the-nation ban ​on AI-generated fake nude images as the technology and social media company ‌pursues a lawsuit alleging that the law is unconstitutional.
The St. Louis-based 8th US Circuit Court of Appeals in its order put the law on hold for now, granting a request for an ​injunction by xAI. A lower court judge last month had rejected Musk's bid ​for an order stopping the law.
The state's anti-"nudification" law, which took ⁠effect on August 1, prohibits website operators, software developers and others from allowing users ​to create realistic images depicting an intimate body part that is not shown in ​an original photo of an identifiable individual.
xAI alleges the measure restricts free speech protected by the US Constitution.
Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison's office said in a statement on Friday it is disappointed by ​the appeals court ruling and will defend the new state law as xAI's ​appeal moves forward.
Read More: New Mexico wants Meta to pay up to $40 billion in penalties after data privacy trial
"Minnesota's nudification ban outlaws AI technology products from generating sexual images that harm and harass ‌people ⁠in the vilest way possible," Ellison spokesperson John Stiles said.
xAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
US District Judge Donovan Frank ruled last month that xAI had not shown it would suffer irreparable harm while challenging the law and said the ​company had waited too ​long to seek ⁠emergency relief.
In its appeal, xAI disputed the judge's finding that it delayed bringing suit. The company also said its Grok Imagine tool ​includes "rigorous protections" against creating nudified or sexualized images of real ​people.
xAI has ⁠begun suing users whom it alleges are evading Grok’s technological blockers to create sexual images of people without their consent.
Minnesota had urged the appeals court not to block the law. The ⁠state ​has said it adopted the measure this year to ​combat the spread of what it called a "staggering amount (of) child sexual abuse material that AI products like ​Grok Imagine generate."

Jakarta, Gizmologi – Telkomsel secara resmi meluncurkan Paket Bundling Canva Pro Lite pada tanggal 28 September 2026 di Jakarta untuk mendukung pembuatan konten visual secara lebih cepat dan mudah. Paket berlangganan ini dirancang khusus guna memfasilitasi pengguna dalam berkreasi dari mana saja dengan penawaran harga terjangkau mulai dari Rp8.000 per hari. Integrasi layanan ini memberikan akses penuh Canva Pro Lite bagi satu pengguna yang digabungkan secara praktis dengan kuota internet harian dari Telkomsel.
Melalui berlangganan Canva Pro Lite, pelanggan dapat meningkatkan kualitas desain visual berkat akses terhadap lebih dari 3,6 juta template serta lebih dari 141 juta koleksi foto, video, grafis, fon, hingga aset audio premium. Layanan ini menyediakan ragam fitur profesional unggulan seperti alat pengeditan gambar, fitur pengelolaan merek, penyesuaian ukuran kanvas, serta perencanaan unggahan media sosial. Solusi ini diharapkan dapat mempermudah pelaku UMKM dalam mendesain materi promosi, membantu pelajar menyusun presentasi, serta mendukung profesional menjaga konsistensi identitas merek.
“Kami melihat kreativitas digital kini menjadi bagian dari keseharian banyak orang, baik untuk belajar, bekerja, membangun usaha, maupun mengekspresikan diri. Melalui Paket Bundling Canva Pro Lite, Telkomsel ingin membantu pelanggan mengubah ide menjadi karya dengan cara yang lebih praktis dan terjangkau. Pilihan masa aktif yang fleksibel, akses fitur premium, dan kuota internet dalam satu paket menjadi wujud komitmen kami untuk terus Melayani Sepenuh Hati, dengan menghadirkan solusi digital yang benar-benar terasa manfaatnya,” ungkap Kemas M. Fadhli VP Digital Lifestyle Telkomsel.
Baca juga: Riset Canva: 98% Profesional Indonesia Gunakan AI untuk Presentasi
Pilihan Paket Bundling Telkomsel Canva
Pembelian paket berlangganan ini dapat diakses secara langsung lewat aplikasi MyTelkomsel maupun berbagai kanal distribusi penjualan Telkomsel lainnya. Setelah pembayaran berhasil diverifikasi, pelanggan akan mendapatkan SMS berisi tautan aktivasi yang disarankan untuk dibuka dan diaktifkan paling lambat tiga hari setelah diterima. Apabila masa aktif paket berakhir, akun pelanggan akan dikembalikan secara otomatis menjadi akun Canva Free, namun seluruh hasil desain yang telah dibuat akan tetap tersimpan dan bisa diakses kembali kapan pun.
Paket Bundling Canva Pro Lite ini secara eksklusif dapat dinikmati oleh seluruh pelanggan prabayar SIMPATI dan pascabayar Halo dengan tiga varian pilihan yang harganya sudah mencakup pajak:
Paket 1 Hari: Tersedia dengan harga Rp8.000, mencakup akses fitur Canva Pro Lite beserta kuota internet 0,5 GB.
Paket 7 Hari: Tersedia dengan harga Rp20.000, mencakup akses fitur Canva Pro Lite beserta kuota internet 1 GB.
Paket 30 Hari: Tersedia dengan harga Rp38.000, mencakup akses fitur Canva Pro Lite beserta kuota internet 2 GB.
“Di Canva, misi kami adalah memberdayakan setiap orang untuk dapat mendesain dan menyampaikan ide mereka dengan penuh percaya diri, terlepas dari latar belakang maupun pengalaman desain yang dimiliki. Canva Pro Lite menjadi salah satu cara kami mewujudkan misi tersebut di Indonesia, dengan memberikan lebih banyak pilihan dan fleksibilitas agar setiap orang dapat menemukan pengalaman Canva yang paling sesuai dengan kebutuhan kreatif mereka,” ucap Stefanie Herlie, Country Manager Canva Indonesia.
Stefanie juga menambahkan bahwa kolaborasi bersama Telkomsel ini menjadi langkah strategis Canva dalam memberdayakan masyarakat agar lebih percaya diri saat merancang visual desain demi mendorong pertumbuhan ekosistem ekonomi kreatif digital.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The National CERT has issued a warning to organisations against the growing cybersecurity and data-governance risks arising from uncontrolled use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools, urging them to immediately block the leakage of sensitive information to public and unapproved AI platforms.
In its latest advisory, “Safe and Secure Use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) Tools and Platforms”, National CERT said rapid adoption of public AI chatbots, coding assistants, browser extensions, AI-enabled applications and third-party AI services was creating new security risks for organisations.
It cautioned that unauthorised use of GenAI, commonly referred to as “Shadow AI”, could expose sensitive information, intellectual property, credentials, source code and other organisational data.
National CERT Issues Warning Over Cybersecurity Risks of Unauthorised AI Use
The advisory also flagged risks from prompt injection, insecure AI-generated code, malicious integrations, inaccurate AI outputs and compromised third-party AI models.
National CERT has advised organisations to establish and enforce a mandatory Generative AI Acceptable Use Policy, clearly defining approved, restricted and prohibited uses of AI tools and setting requirements for data handling, access, accountability and oversight.
It stressed that classified, confidential, sensitive, personal, proprietary, credential-related and other restricted organisational information must not be submitted to public or unapproved AI platforms.
Organisations have also been directed to maintain a centrally vetted and regularly reviewed registry of approved AI tools, models, browser extensions, plugins, application programming interfaces (APIs) and platforms, while restricting access to unauthorised AI services.
The advisory further called for mandatory human review of AI-generated code and other critical outputs before deployment, publication, operational use or incorporation into organisational decision-making.
National CERT recommended extending data loss prevention (DLP), access monitoring and endpoint security controls to AI interfaces to detect sensitive-data submissions, unauthorised AI usage, suspicious API activity and Shadow AI.
It also urged organisations to align their AI governance and security practices with recognised international frameworks, particularly the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) and OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model (LLM) Applications.
See Also: HEC, National CERT Join Hands to Strengthen Cybersecurity in Higher Education
The CERT further called for regular staff training on safe prompting, sensitive-data handling, AI-generated code, AI hallucinations, prompt injection, deepfakes, third-party AI risks and organisational GenAI policies.
Organisations were also advised to maintain appropriate audit trails of authorised AI tool access and usage for security monitoring, compliance verification, incident investigation and accountability, subject to applicable privacy requirements.
National CERT said organisations should continuously monitor for sensitive-data exposure, Shadow AI, unauthorised AI plugins and APIs, prompt injection, unreviewed AI-generated code, suspicious AI access and policy violations.
In case of an AI-related security incident, organisations should immediately contain unauthorised access, preserve relevant evidence and logs, revoke compromised credentials or API keys, investigate possible exposure and implement corrective measures, it added.
The advisory said incidents involving sensitive-data exposure through AI tools, prompt-injection exploitation, AI supply-chain compromise or violations of GenAI usage policies must be reported to National CERT Pakistan.
The post National CERT Issues Warning Over Cybersecurity Risks of Unauthorised AI Use appeared first on PhoneWorld.

items.content:
Apple said on Friday that it plans to change its Mac operating system to make it more obvious when AI agents ask ​to access all of the data on Macs.
Some users have criticized Meta's ‌Muse, an AI agent capable of carrying out complex tasks like canceling unused subscriptions or haggling for better prices. These people claimed the agent accessed what users believed to be private messages.
On ​Apple's iPhones and iPads, no single app can access data inside another ​app by default, a technique called sandboxing. But Apple's Macs are ⁠more flexible, with a "Full Disk Access" option that allows apps such as cloud ​backup services to access all the data on a machine, with a user's permission.
Apple ​on Friday said some developers were using the Full Disk Access feature in ways that could put users at risk.
"Going forward, we will introduce additional controls to ensure that users who genuinely ​wish to grant an app this extraordinary level of access can only do so ​with very explicit user action," Apple wrote in a post.
Read More: OpenAI dismisses 3 researchers over alleged mishandling of sensitive information
"As AI agents become increasingly capable and autonomous, ‌the ⁠risks associated with this level of access will grow substantially. We are committed to ensuring users clearly understand these risks before granting such access, so they can make informed decisions about their own data and privacy."
Apple's move comes after Inc magazine technology ​columnist Jason Aten accused ​Meta's Muse, opens new tab of ⁠reading private messages on his Mac. He said he had not enabled Full Disk Access.
Meta spokesperson Andy Stone pushed back against ​those claims last week, saying Muse's access to Apple's Messages app ​is strictly ⁠opt-in.
"You have to enable both Full Disk Access and the Messages connector for Muse to be able to read your Messages content," Stone wrote on social media platform X. "It ⁠can't read ​your Messages unless you do this. And it ​can be revoked at any time."
Apple declined to comment beyond its post. Meta did not immediately respond to ​a request for comment.

Qaiser said the PTI side stipulated that a meeting with Imran must take place first and only then would it proceed further.
"We hold a very clear stance on the issue of terrorism; we want peace in our province."
Leader of the Opposition in the Senate Raja Nasir Abbas told the media there was a deadlock on "small issues". He said the issue of the meeting with Imran could not be resolved.

However, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said: "Look, we don't have a consensus on foundational issues," adding that he could not say that he foresaw both sides moving forward on a mutually acceptable plan of action. 
PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar said the long march would go ahead and was "intact". He said the party's demands should be addressed and said governor rule or an emergency were not the answers to the long march.
PPP Senator Sherry Rehman said they had performed their constitutional and democratic role. 
"We constantly talked with them on every point, whatever their concerns were were heard and debated and shared with our leadership. The agreement draft was changed four times."
She said it was the PPP's stance that, given the terrorism situation, there could be no compromise, and that it was "not a small matter". 
Rehman added that agreement was achieved on many points but disagreements remained on some. 
"They have refused to do an agreement," she said.
Prime Minister's aide Rana Sanaullah said the basic issue related to K-P's security situation, with the federal government demanding that the provincial government fulfil its responsibilities in this regard and play its role.
He said there was no reassurance from the other side about this. "They made changes in the drafts two to three times, but despite that, the K-P government is not ready to cooperate to play its role in the war against terrorism and this is absolutely unacceptable. Sanaullah said the government had provided various reassurances to the PTI regarding its demands about Imran. He added that the long march would not be allowed to enter Islamabad.

Achakzai refuses to back down on Oct 4 long march
Meanwhile, TTAP chief Mehmood Khan Achakzai refused to withdraw his demand, saying the long march would not be called off until a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan took place.
Speaking to a private television channel, he demanded that Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi be allowed to meet the PTI founder, while also giving an assurance that the chief minister would not speak to the media after the meeting.
He said a decision to call off the long march, scheduled for Oct 4, could be taken after consultation with the PTI founder, adding that whatever joint decision was reached after the meeting would be accepted.
Earlier in the evening, amid reports of successful government-opposition negotiations, PTI leader Shaukat Yousafzai welcomed the development as a positive step for the country.
Yousafzai said the success of the talks should not be viewed as a victory or defeat for any particular side, but rather as a victory for Pakistan. He noted that he had previously made the same position clear through a letter, emphasising that negotiations were the best way to resolve political differences.
Addressing the issue of terrorism, Yousafzai called on the federal government to support the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government in efforts to eliminate terrorism and improve security in the province.
He also said that the imposition of Governor’s Rule would have caused significant damage and expressed hope that the government would provide PTI with adequate political space.
Yousafzai further expressed the expectation that court decisions concerning PTI founder Imran Khan would be implemented in accordance with the law.
A day earlier, the first round of talks between the government and opposition concluded with the two sides deciding to meet again on Saturday (today) in the NA speaker’s chamber. The negotiations come amid continued tensions after PTI announced a long march towards Islamabad on September 27 that was rescheduled to October 4. Currently, the standoff between the federal and provincial governments remains unresolved.
The speaker, in a statement, said the previous day’s session was held in a “very cordial atmosphere” and expressed hope that all sides would continue the dialogue in the same spirit.
Sadiq also thanked members of the government, PPP and opposition for participating in the talks.

As per the statement, Federal Ministers Engineer Ameer Muqam, Mohsin Naqvi and Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, Minister of State Talal Chaudhry and Prime Minister’s Adviser Rana Sanaullah are representing the government during the meeting. Furthermore, the PPP delegation comprises Senator Sherry Rehman, Naveed Qamar and Ijaz Hussain Jakhrani.
On the other hand, PTI is represented by Barrister Gohar Khan, Raja Nasir Abbas, Aamer Dogar, Asad Qaiser and Haleem Adil Sheikh, along with Salman Akram Raja, according to the NA’s statement.
The talks are being held as part of efforts by the government, PPP, and the opposition to engage in dialogue on matters of political importance.
Read: Govt, opposition conclude first round of talks ahead of PTI’s Oct 4 march
On Friday, the NA spokesperson revealed that detailed discussions were conducted on the country’s political situation, with the government, PPP, and opposition apprising each other of their respective positions. However, the first round of talks ended without a conclusive decision from either quarter. The parties also refrained from mudslinging in accordance with an agreement reached during the talks.
Defence Minister alleges PTI, KP govt supporting unrest
Earlier in the day, Defence Minister Khawaja Asif questioned whether the PTI and the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government hired terrorists to spread sedition, riots and chaos under the guise of protests on October 4.
He made these remarks in connection with a video he shared on X alleging that PTI’s social media accounts shared footage showing non-custom-paid vehicles from Waziristan.
In a statement shared on social media, he further alleged that “unemployed young men” were paid and sent around the camps of police and security forces to spread unrest, adding that some of them might not even have identity cards.
“Now, if these ignorant fools attack any government institution tomorrow, just like it happened in the past, and the police or forces disperse them in self-defence, then will the narrative against the state be built from the ready social media accounts sitting there, just like before?” The defence minister posed a question.
He also asked why the cops were not checking the convoy to determine whether the people travelling in the vehicles were terrorists with covered faces or ordinary citizens, and whether the non-custom-paid vehicles were carrying weapons or explosive materials.

items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
Rogo, a US-based financial-services AI startup, raised $30 Mn this month. What made this unique was that some of the world’s largest banks, including Barclays, BNP Paribas, Citi, MUFG and Société Générale, invested in this company, even though it has VC backing too.
Nine global banks are now on Rogo’s cap table, representing nearly $20 Tn in combined assets.
Rogo isn’t an isolated case. Large banks and their venture investment arms are increasingly taking big bets on AI companies.
Such investments have grown at a compounded annual rate of 21% since 2023, per an Evident AI analysis of the 50 biggest global banks, with Wells Fargo, Citi and Goldman Sachs the most active US bank investors.
Recent deals around the world and in India back this trend. Citigroup and Spain’s Santander have both taken stakes in Tokyo-based Sakana AI, which builds foundational models and custom AI for financial services.
In India, examples include HDFC Bank and Canara Bank’s investments in CoRover as well as IDFC Bank’s partnership with Sarvam to build an R&D lab with the aim of developing the world’s first self-improving bank.
Three forces seem to be pushing banks past the old vendor relationship. Deep integration into regulated, high-stakes workflows requires more trust and customisation than an arm’s-length license can provide.
Owning a stake or co-building the R&D gives banks influence over a roadmap they’re increasingly dependent on. And for BFSI institutions sitting on enormous proprietary data and distribution, contributing that data to jointly built AI systems can be more valuable than a services contract.
“License provides a means to access technology, while investment or co-development may result in a more profound collaboration between a bank and a startup. Cocreation gives the bank an ability to affect product architecture and work flows instead of simply fitting the bank’s processes into a ready-made solution,” said Mukesh Pandey, founder of consultancy firm Rupyaa Paisa.
Whether this becomes the default model for bank-AI relationships, or stays concentrated among the largest, most AI-forward institutions, is still an open question.
So is what this means for smaller AI startups negotiating with a bank that is simultaneously their client, their investor and increasingly their co-developer. The ones that end up without any bank partnerships or strategic investments may struggle to get the same access to data, distribution and trust.
Banking On AI
HDFC Bank’s move on CoRover, the Bengaluru-based conversational AI firm behind BharatGPT, was described as the first investment by a leading private bank in a model maker.
That isn’t CoRover’s only investor with a bank. Canbank Venture Capital Fund, the wholly owned VC arm of Canara Bank, had already invested in CoRover.
CoRover’s founder and CEO Ankush Sabhrawal said that the association between the company and the banking ecosystem has moved from being a typical startup-investor partnership to a strong technological and domain collaboration.
Further, Sarvam’s partnership with IDFC FIRST Bank is a particularly interesting example. The companies said they would work towards building what they describe as a “self-improving bank.”
Their collaborative R&D lab will focus on frontier AI research, post-training and AI safety, with systems designed to learn from customer interactions, human corrections, exceptions and eventual outcomes. The partnership is intended to bring AI research closer to the bank’s own operating environment, allowing models and systems to be tested against the institution’s specific problems and improved using production outcomes.
Sarvam has also built a growing footprint across financial services through more deployment-oriented partnerships. With Mahindra Finance, the startup’s voice AI has been used across customer-facing workflows, and Sarvam’s current enterprise portfolio lists Mahindra Finance alongside IDFC FIRST Bank, Tata Capital and SBI Life among its financial-services customers.
While not a bank, Bajaj Finance recently picked up a 5% stake in Delhi NCR-based TrueFan AI, a generative-video startup whose avatars Bajaj was already using at scale for customer engagement and dealer communication. The deal sits under the NBFC’s new Finserv Intelligence programme, which plans to invest ₹1,500–2,000 Cr into early stage AI, cybersecurity and fintech startups.
For banks and indeed NBFCs, AI is increasingly becoming more than another technology procurement category. Besides just being mere customers, banks and NBFCs are becoming financial stakeholders in the company building the technology.
India’s banking and financial-services sector is beginning to show early signs of the same shift.
Are Indian Banks Moving Fast?
Beyond financial resources, bank-led investments bring with them insights into the operational nature of financial services, including areas where AI technologies could be applied effectively in the area of customer support, employee assistance, knowledge management, multilingual engagement, etc.
“The feedback provided by banks becomes useful for determining specific areas where AI needs more accuracy, context, security, and compliance. It is crucial for BharatGPT, as the majority of banking transactions involve multilingual clients and difficult financial terms. The company views the controlled customization as a use of the client’s approved knowledge reference points, algorithms, and mechanisms instead of utilising proprietary information in a standard solution,” CoRover’s Sabharwal added.
That kind of close, iterative feedback loop is easier to justify when the sector on the other end of it is already AI’s biggest spender.
BFSI holds the largest share of India’s AI market, largely on the back of early adoption for fraud detection, risk management, customer service, and personalised financial solutions. The sector’s focus on digital transformation and data-driven decision-making has made it a key driver of AI demand — reaching a market size of over $1 Bn in 2025, and projected by research firm IMARC Group to grow to $9.4 Bn by 2034 at a CAGR of 26.5%.
A more significant change may actually be happening outside the cap table. Indian banks and financial institutions are increasingly working directly with AI startups to adapt technology to specific banking workflows, rather than simply purchasing a general-purpose AI product.
The logic behind these tie-ups was laid out plainly by Axis Bank’s Prasad Lad, the head of the bank’s business intelligence unit.
He said Axis is working with startups across voice AI, document reading and rapid UI/UX prototyping, adding that this isn’t an area where the bank can build everything in-house. “Startups such as Sarvam bring capabilities, particularly across Indian languages, that would be difficult for a bank to develop internally,” he added.
Kotak Mahindra Bank, on the other hand, has started leveraging AI across software development, employee productivity, customer service and experience, credit decisioning, and marketing. While most of the AI work is done by in-house team, the bank leans on startup partners for niche requirements, said Vijay Narayanan, Head of Innovation and AI, without specifying the startups Kotak Mahindra Bank is currently working with.
Humans In The Banking Loop
That same efficiency the AI partnerships are built to deliver is already showing up in headcount. Axis Bank reported a decline of over 3,100 employees in FY26, which it attributed to sustained investments in technology and productivity enhancements. HDFC Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and ICICI Bank have seen similar headcount reductions, directly or indirectly tied to AI-led automation.
In some cases, roles are being revised. “We expect 50-60% of our employees to be repurposed into sales and relationship roles over the next two years, with no layoffs as part of this transition but we continue to hire, especially for specialised technology talent,” Salee S Nair, MD and CEO, Tamil Nadu Small Mercantile Bank.
As with other layoffs in recent times, many have wondered whether these strategic investments are resulting in less humans in the banking loop.
Axis Bank CEO Amitabh Chaudhry told Bloomberg that investments in AI and technology would let the bank expand its business without a proportional rise in staff, signalling slower hiring even as operations scale up.
This is not a new experience for Indian banks by any means.
Every step taken by Indian banks in the past two decades has come with such cutbanks — whether it is internet banking, mobile banking and digital payments or indeed the AI banking future that banks are rushing to embrace.
But with every new technology jump, there have been teething pains, bugs and major tech gaps, which is why the buck always stops at the humans leading the banks. With AI, this human responsibility will grow by magnitudes because fewer humans will be running the banks.
So even if banks are ready for an AI future as they are demonstrating today with their investments, the next major discussion has to cover what the role of humans will be in this future.

items.author: xinhua.
items.content:
A jade pendant bearing a small golden Sanxingdui mask rested against dancer Wu Yufei's chest as he stepped onto the stage of the "America's Got Talent" finale. Commissioned by his wife, this piece of home was by his side as he wowed the audience.
At the finale, 27-year-old Wu, from Sichuan Province in southwestern China, shared the stage with humanoid robots made by Unitree, performing in a fusion of robotics, ink-wash aesthetics, and contemporary stage performance.
"Robots are not merely technological achievements, but can also become creative partners on stage and a new medium for artistic expression," said Fang Zhenghua, the Chengdu choreographer who directed the team's performances.
Wu said their experience in the United States has been genuinely heartwarming. He, along with Fang, showcased not only the advances in humanoid robot technology, but also young people's vision of the future relationship between technology and humanity, adding that audiences are incredibly enthusiastic.
At their audition, Wu performed alongside machines that danced and flipped in time with the music. The act received a unanimous yes from all four judges.
By the September 8 quarterfinals, Wu and the robots were performing martial arts alongside human dancers, kicking and flipping across the stage.
Judge Howie Mandel imagined a martial arts version of the film "I, Robot" and predicted it would be "the most viral moment we're going to have this season." Actress Sofia Vergara pressed her Golden Buzzer, sending the team directly to the Sept. 22 final.
For Wu, however, some of the most memorable exchanges happened away from the machines.
This marked his fourth trip to the United States. He had met a number of American dancers on past trips from the East Coast to the West Coast of the country. They made dance videos together on American streets, capturing times when they moved and played music together.
"Dance is a universal language," he said.
When he made it to the finale, some of those friends reached out on social media to wish him luck. He also received encouraging messages from local viewers he had never met.
Read More: Chinese rocket firm, disease research lab to test space pharmaceutical payloads
"Even though we come from different countries and speak different languages, at that moment they were sincerely wishing me well in the competition," Wu said. "That stayed with me. It felt quite warm."
Wu grew up visiting the Sanxingdui Ruins, a site associated with the ancient Shu Kingdom dating back some 3,000 to 4,500 years. He said visiting the site was "like going to a park." During the contest, he brought one of those familiar faces across the Pacific, jokingly calling it a "mysterious force from the East."
For Fang, inspiration also comes from familiar stories and everyday life. Over the years, his team has incorporated elements like Sichuan opera face-changing, the traditional Chinese composition "A Hundred Birds Paying Homage to the Phoenix," and Three Kingdoms stories into the performances.
For the finale, choreographer Fang wanted to share a Chinese aesthetic that overseas audiences might know less well than kung fu. Water sleeves offered one way to do that, with robots becoming partners in expressing an old art form.
Wu's appearance came in a year when American audiences encountered Chinese creativity in several different settings. In July, Chinese artists joined the Hollywood Film Music Orchestra for a "Black Myth: Wukong" concert in Los Angeles, while Lincoln Center expanded its previous Shanghai Day celebration into Chinese Arts Week. September brought Chinese dance dramas, including "Dream of the Red Chamber," to New York.
On the final stage, flowing sleeves and humanoid robots brought something of China to American viewers, and the friendship had also become part of the story that Wu and his performers would take back home.

items.content:
Maisa, a 17-year-old in a poor Paris suburb who aspires to be an English teacher, joined tens of thousands of other students and their supporters this week in protests that spread across France over ​dilapidated schools, classroom overcrowding and teacher shortages.
At Lycee Le Corbusier school in Aubervilliers, a suburb north of Paris in the Seine-Saint-Denis department, protesters said schools in poor ‌neighbourhoods like theirs faced the worst conditions.
“Last year I took the high school French exam without a French teacher, and teachers have a huge impact,” Maisa said.
"These are not conditions to study in."
As protests raged at more than 1,200 French high schools this week, police responded with tear gas and rubber bullets in some cases. More than 5,000 people were arrested, and some protesters were seriously hurt with eye injuries, broken teeth and blows to ​the head. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez called it a "climate of unacceptable violence" and called for order.
French students have blocked schools across the country, demanding more teachers, smaller classes and better-equipped schools.
Some protests escalated into clashes with police, while teachers, firefighters and other public workers also demonstrated over funding and resources. pic.twitter.com/eOpPqHF87P
— Al Jazeera English (@AJEnglish) September 29, 2026
Amelia, 15, joined Maisa in the crowd outside the school gates and held a ​sign reading, "Our address should not decide our future". She said she was demonstrating to demand the same rights as students elsewhere in the country.
"The education ⁠authority is not investing enough in the suburbs. It's classist and racist," she said.
Read: French high school blockades continue as protests spread to universities
Ulysse Rabate, a political scientist at Paris 8 University, said the protests show the way that France's marginalised ​urban neighbourhoods are increasingly influencing national politics.
"When there is a collapse of the public service, of public education, those who feel it the most, and the most violently, are those at the bottom," he ​said.
Political flashpoint
The nationwide demonstrations and blockades, which began last week, have become a political flashpoint at a sensitive moment for the government, which announced a series of deeply unpopular spending cuts in its 2027 budget on Thursday.
The education budget is set to increase by a below-inflation 1.7% to €65.53 billion, excluding teacher pensions.
The education ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Education Minister Edouard Geffray said that education remained a priority and the ​below-inflation budget increase was due to population decline.
The protests started in the Parisian suburbs, where poverty levels are high, then spread to Paris itself and other French towns, including Marseille, Strasbourg, Tours ​and Lille.
French authorities detained 625 people as high school protests over teacher shortages, class sizes, long schedules and poor conditions escalated into clashes with police.
The protests, which began around Paris and spread nationwide, affected 356 schools. At least 83 police and…
— Clash Report (@clashreport) October 1, 2026
At Lycee Le Corbusier, classes including maths, humanities, English and sport have been cancelled since the start of the academic year due to a teacher shortage, according to Karima Kara Ali, an elected parent representative.
In ‌Seine-Saint-Denis, two-thirds ⁠of high schools took part in protests on Thursday, the CGT labour union said. Youth, teachers and parents in four towns complained of unsanitary school conditions and chronic staff shortages, including nurses and social workers.
🇫🇷 ⚠️ French high school students lit fires outside schools and faced off with police on Friday as a protest movement that has forced the closure or disrupted education at more than 560 establishments showed no sign of abating ➡️ https://t.co/iIQtqmkIJE pic.twitter.com/hlggNkhldT
— AFP News Agency (@AFP) October 2, 2026
Louise Paternoster, a representative for the Seine-Saint-Denis branch of the CGT's education union, said the area does not get adequate resources for its student population and their educational needs.
Two-thirds of schools in the department have unfilled teacher positions, according to a union survey.
Not enough teachers
"Our students are losing out on study time. Some schools don't have drinking water. We are not equal to other ​departments," she said, blaming shortages on government cuts ​of 3,256 teacher positions nationwide in 2026.
In ⁠Pantin, a town on the northeastern edge of Paris, teacher Dilan Roche joined her students as they protested outside their school this week to support their demands and protect them from the police.
"What they wrote on banners, we wrote in a letter to the local education authority: overcrowded classes, ​no nurses, no social workers — which is problematic for students with learning difficulties, many living in precarity," she said.
While France ranks in the ​middle of OECD countries for ⁠spending on education, the average expenditure per secondary school student has remained little changed over the last decade, standing at €11,660 in 2024 and €11,910 in 2010, according to education ministry data.
The last nationwide high school protest movement on this scale demanding more funding came in the 1990s. That followed the government sharply expanding access to the baccalauréat, the school-leaving exam that typically paves the way to university, without providing schools ⁠with sufficient additional ​resources, said Professor Clemence Cardon-Quint at Paul Valery University, who researches education funding.
The movement won an increase in funding, but ​spending per student later stagnated despite growing demands on schools.
Cardon-Quint said students and teachers have taken on additional responsibilities over the years, including navigating Parcoursup, the university admissions system introduced in 2018 and criticised by some students and teachers as ​opaque and discriminatory.
"In a period of budgetary restraint, it is more difficult to reduce inequalities," said Cardon-Quint.

Nexus Sees Mixed Returns Across Funds
AceVector’s IPO also provided partial exit to Nexus Venture Partners, although returns varied
items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Snapdeal parent AceVector’s initial public offering (IPO) provided an exit opportunity to several of its early investors and promoters, with SoftBank-backed Starfish I Pte Ltd emerging the biggest beneficiary of the offer-for-sale (OFS) component.
At the issue price of ₹32 per share, Starfish I, a SoftBank entity and the company’s largest shareholder, raked in about ₹88.3 Cr by selling 2.76 Cr shares, representing about two-thirds of the total OFS proceeds. The transaction represented an 0.08X return multiple on the shares being sold, according to AceVector’s RHP.
Starfish will continue to hold 11.3 Cr shares, valued at about ₹361.8 Cr at ₹32 apiece, after the IPO.
AceVector’s ₹420 Cr IPO comprised a fresh issue of ₹287 Cr and an OFS of up to 4.16 Cr shares worth about ₹133 Cr at the upper end of the price band of ₹30-₹32, valuing the company at ₹1,741 Cr.
Nexus Sees Mixed Returns Across Funds
AceVector’s IPO also provided partial exit to Nexus Venture Partners, although returns varied significantly across its investment vehicles.
Nexus India Direct Investments II sold 73.9 Lakh shares for ₹23.6 Cr, representing a 1.03X return multiple. The fund retains 3 Cr shares worth about ₹96.7 Cr at the IPO price.
Meanwhile, Nexus Opportunity Fund Ltd sold 8.4 Lakh shares for ₹2.6 Cr, representing a 0.14X return multiple, while Nexus Ventures III sold 4.6 Lakh shares for ₹1.4 Cr at a 0.07X multiple.
Together, the three Nexus entities sold 86.9 Lakh shares.
Other selling shareholders included FIH Business Global, Rupen Investment and Industries and Centaurus Trading and Investments. FIH sold 17.4 Lakh shares for ₹5.6 Cr, while Rupen Investment and Centaurus sold 2.7 Lakh shares each for about ₹86 Lakh.
Individual Investors See MultiBagger Returns
The sharpest returns were booked by individual shareholders. Kenneth Stuart Glass sold 13.2 Lakh shares for ₹4.2 Cr at ₹32 apiece. The transaction represented a 5.42X return multiple, making it the highest return among selling investors.
Glass still holds 30.7 Lakh shares, worth about ₹9.8 Cr at the IPO price.
Meanwhile, Laurent Bernard Amouyal booked a substantial return on investment after selling 2.2 Lakh shares for ₹72 Lakh, representing a 4.38X return multiple. He retains 5.2 Lakh shares worth around ₹1.7 Cr.
On the other hand, former Snapdeal chief strategy and investment officer Jason Ashok Kothari sold 11.1 Lakh shares for ₹3.5 Cr, with a 0.78X return multiple, while retaining another 11.1 Lakh shares valued at ₹3.5 Cr.
AceVector had earlier proposed a substantially larger OFS but trimmed the component by 34.9% to 4.16 Cr shares. Starfish alone reduced its proposed sale from 4.23 Cr shares to 2.76 Cr.
The company raised ₹13 Cr through a pre-IPO placement, which brought down the fresh issue to ₹287 Cr. The fresh capital is earmarked largely for Snapdeal, including ₹132 Cr for marketing and business promotion and ₹50 Cr for technology infrastructure, while the remaining proceeds are intended for acquisitions and general corporate purposes.
Founded in 2010 by Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal, AceVector started off as ecommerce platform, Snapdeal. Following the collapse of its proposed merger with Flipkart in 2017, it pivoted to a value-focused ecommerce model.
Besides Snapdeal, AceVector’s offerings include listed ecommerce SaaS company Unicommerce and consumer brands business Stellaro Brands. The group adopted the AceVector identity in 2022.
Ahead of opening the public issue for subscription, AceVector raised ₹189 Cr from anchor investors. Helios Mutual Fund and Taurus Ethical Fund were the only domestic mutual funds to participate, together picking up 93.75 Lakh shares, or 15.87% of the anchor allocation.
AceVector’s IPO closed on Tuesday (September 29), receiving 4.93X subscription. Investors placed bids for 36.61 Cr shares against 7.42 Cr shares on offer.
On the financial front, AceVector’s restated net loss narrowed nearly 64% to ₹45.5 Cr in FY26 from ₹126.3 Cr in FY25. Operating revenue rose 29.2% to ₹510.3 Cr from ₹395 Cr.

items.author: Ronggo
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – MagPro meluncurkan AeroLev 1850 sebagai platform pendingin (chiller) berkapasitas 1,85 MW di Jakarta (1/10) lalu. Perusahaan patungan (joint venture) antara CIGU Technology Corp. Ltd. dan EPG Data Technology (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., merancang platform ini untuk memenuhi kebutuhan pusat data kecerdasan buatan (AI) generasi berikutnya dengan mengintegrasikan teknologi pendinginan udara dan bantalan magnetik (magnetic bearing). Mesin pendingin ini mampu beroperasi secara optimal pada suhu lingkungan mencapai 45°C, sehingga menjadi solusi tepat bagi pusat data di wilayah dengan keterbatasan air dan iklim bersuhu tinggi seperti Indonesia.
Seiring lonjakan kebutuhan daya komputasi AI yang berdampak pada peningkatan panas perangkat, operator pusat data dituntut memiliki infrastruktur pendinginan yang terukur tanpa harus menambah konsumsi air. AeroLev 1850 menjawab tantangan tersebut dengan memadukan desain bangunan tanpa menara pendingin, teknologi levitasi magnetik bebas oli, dan sistem kontrol cerdas. Dengan meniadakan kebutuhan air untuk sistem pendinginan evaporatif, platform ini mengatasi kendala operasional yang krusial bagi pusat data yang berlokasi di wilayah kering.
“Seiring keterbatasan air menjadi salah satu pertimbangan utama dalam pengembangan pusat data, AeroLev 1850 menghadirkan pendekatan yang lebih Tangguh untuk mendukung kebutuhan pendinginan pusat data AI,” ujar William Wu, General Manager Nanjing CIPU Technology Co., Ltd.
Keandalan AeroLev 1850 didukung oleh kompresor levitasi magnetik berpendingin udara khusus yang menawarkan tingkat efisiensi isentropik hingga 87%. Perangkat ini dilengkapi dengan kondensor yang telah dipatenkan untuk menghasilkan tingkat pendinginan lanjutan (subcooling) lebih dari 3°C, serta kipas EC standar yang mengoptimalkan efisiensi energi.
Secara keseluruhan, teknologi ini memberikan efisiensi energi hingga 40% lebih tinggi, tingkat kegagalan 8% lebih rendah, dan menekan biaya pemeliharaan hingga 10% lebih murah dibandingkan dengan kompresor konvensional yang menggunakan pelumas berbasis oli. Sistem ini juga mengadopsi teknologi free cooling yang memanfaatkan suhu udara sekitar saat sedang rendah untuk mengurangi waktu kerja kompresor, konsumsi listrik, dan biaya operasional.
Baca juga: Akun X Microsoft Diretas, Sempat Promosikan Token Kripto
AeroLev 1850 Mendukung Teknologi Masa Depan
Dari sisi fleksibilitas infrastruktur, AeroLev 1850 telah disiapkan untuk mendukung tren teknologi masa depan seperti pendinginan langsung ke cip (direct-to-chip) dan pendinginan cair dengan metode imersi (immersion liquid cooling). Platform ini mampu menyuplai air dingin bersuhu hingga 45°C guna mendukung teknologi pendinginan bersuhu tinggi tanpa menuntut investasi besar untuk perombakan infrastruktur. Selain itu, desain modularnya yang terstandarisasi memungkinkan pemasangan yang cepat serta ekspansi kapasitas yang fleksibel sejalan dengan bertumbuhnya beban komputasi AI.
Menurut William Wu, bahwa teknologi ini memfasilitasi pertumbuhan komputasi AI secara efisien di lingkungan yang menantang sekaligus memastikan investasi infrastruktur tetap relevan dalam jangka panjang. Sebagai produsen, MagPro saat ini mengoperasikan fasilitas manufaktur seluas lebih dari 6.000 meter persegi serta dua laboratorium berpendingin udara yang mampu menguji unit dengan kapasitas hingga 2.000 kW.
Entitas induknya, CIGU, merupakan perusahaan publik di STAR Market Tiongkok yang telah mendistribusikan lebih dari 10.000 unit teknologi maglev ke seluruh dunia. EPG melengkapi kemitraan strategis ini dengan rekam jejak lebih dari 20 tahun sebagai penyedia infrastruktur pusat data modular prefabrikasi yang didukung fasilitas manufaktur di Shanghai dan Malaysia.
“MagPro menandai langkah penting dalam strategi teknologi pendinginan global kami. Dengan menggabungkan keahlian EPG dalam bidang teknik dan implementasi dengan teknologi inti levitasi magnetik milik CIGU, kami membangun infrastruktur digital yang lebih tangguh dan hemat sumber daya, serta tidak terlalu bergantung pada ketersediaan air. AeroLev 1850 mencerminkan komitmen kami untuk memajukan infrastruktur pusat data yang ramah lingkungan dan membangun ekosistem digital yang lebih berkelanjutan di seluruh dunia.” ujar Alick Wan, Pendiri dan Chairman EPG Data Technology (Shanghai) Co., Ltd.

items.author: Muhammad Saleem Jhandeer
items.content:
Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah on Saturday sought a detailed report from Inspector General of Police Javed Alam Odho over the killing of five people in Ratodero of District Larkana in Sindh.
Earlier in the day, police said five people, including a passerby, were killed when armed men riding a motorcycle opened fire at a shop on the Jacobabad Road in Sindh’s Ratodero. Police further said the incident was linked to an old dispute within the Ghangro tribe.
The chief minister directed the IGP to ensure that those involved in the killings were brought to justice and ordered immediate measures to uphold peace in the area.
CM Shah said the loss of human lives in tribal disputes was “highly regrettable” and prayed for the eternal peace of the deceased. He also conveyed condolences to the bereaved families.
Read: Drug addicts target local infrastructure in Karachi
Following the order of the chief minister, IGP Odho asked Larkana DIG Sheeraz Nazeer to report back on the mass murders.
According to a statement issued by his office, IGP Odho directed that the suspects be arrested without delay and that all available resources be utilised to apprehend them.
He also directed that law and order in the area be maintained at all costs and that effective measures be taken to ensure the protection of citizens’ lives and property.
Meanwhile, Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar also took serious notice of the Ratodero firing incident and sought an immediate and detailed report from the DIG Larkana regarding the incident.
The incident
On Saturday morning, gunmen on a motorcycle killed five people in Madeji Kacha area of Ratodero and fled the scene undeterred. Following the incident, a heavy contingent of police reached the area and shifted the bodies to a hospital.
According to police, the deceased were identified as Rajab, Bilawal, Riaz, Qurban Ghanghro and a passerby, Abdullah Brohi.
Police also cordoned off the area and launched a search operation to arrest those involved in the mass murder, claiming that the suspects had been identified.
According to an official statement issued by Larkana Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Azhar Khan Mughal, the incident occurred due to an old feud within the Ghangro tribe.
“The enmity between two groups of Ghangro tribe is long-standing, spanning over 5-7 years. During this period, more than 16 persons from both sides have lost their lives in different incidents of murder and counter-murders,” it stated, adding that the feud was ongoing and both sides were harbouring criminals.
According to SSP Mughal, five persons were nominated as accused in the latest firing incident. The four suspects were identified as Ehsan Ghangro, Bachu Korai, Yaseen Dahani, and Safiullah Dahani, while another unidentified person was also nominated as a suspect.
He further said the suspects were taking shelter in hideouts located in the Kacha area, suspecting that they were shielded by the dens of Long Jatoi and Hafeez Kalhoro.
Highlighting police action taken in the case, SSP Mughal said, Larkana police was put on high alert to “prevent any spillover or retaliatory action in Keti of Larkana”.
He further revealed that the district police, alongside Shikarpur police, have kicked off an operation in Madeji Kacha to apprehend the nominated suspects in the mass murder case.

items.title: Nintendo Menutup Mario Kart Tour Selamanya, 7 Tahun Perjalanan Berakhir Tanpa Versi Offline
items.summary:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Nintendo resmi menutup layanan Mario Kart Tour pada 29 September 2026 lalu. Mungkin banyak gamer yang melewatkan informasi ini, karena meskipun terhitung banyak yang memainkannya, namun sebenarnya versi lite dari Mario Kart ini tidak pernah benar-benar memenuhi ekspektasi. Perjalanan selama tujuh tahun pun berakhir tanpa pengumuman berarti, bahkan tidak ada peluang hadir dalam versi offline.
Dalam tujuh tahun beroperasi, Mario Kart Tour berhasil mengumpulkan lebih dari 200 juta download serta meraup sekitar 270 juta dolar dalam pendapatan sebelum akhirnya menutup. Angka itu mengesankan di permukaan, tapi jika dibandingkan dengan franchise lain, Mario Kart Tour tidak pernah menjadi hit besar yang diharapkan Nintendo. Pada saat pengumuman penutupan diumumkan, game hanya menghasilkan sekitar 650 ribu dolar per bulan, angka yang terus menurun sejak Nintendo menghapus mekanik gacha di akhir 2022 karena adanya kritik dari komunitas gamer.

items.author: Ronggo
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Nintendo resmi menutup layanan Mario Kart Tour pada 29 September 2026 lalu. Mungkin banyak gamer yang melewatkan informasi ini, karena meskipun terhitung banyak yang memainkannya, namun sebenarnya versi lite dari Mario Kart ini tidak pernah benar-benar memenuhi ekspektasi. Perjalanan selama tujuh tahun pun berakhir tanpa pengumuman berarti, bahkan tidak ada peluang hadir dalam versi offline.
Dalam tujuh tahun beroperasi, Mario Kart Tour berhasil mengumpulkan lebih dari 200 juta download serta meraup sekitar 270 juta dolar dalam pendapatan sebelum akhirnya menutup. Angka itu mengesankan di permukaan, tapi jika dibandingkan dengan franchise lain, Mario Kart Tour tidak pernah menjadi hit besar yang diharapkan Nintendo. Pada saat pengumuman penutupan diumumkan, game hanya menghasilkan sekitar 650 ribu dolar per bulan, angka yang terus menurun sejak Nintendo menghapus mekanik gacha di akhir 2022 karena adanya kritik dari komunitas gamer.
Penutupan Mario Kart Tour mungkin realitas yang harus dihadapi Nintendo bahwa tidak semua platform dapat mereka kuasai. Dimulai dengan Super Mario Run pada 2016, Nintendo mencoba memecahkan pasar mobile dengan IP terkenal mereka, namun hasilnya selalu underwhelming dibandingkan dengan game mobile dari publisher lain.
Sebenarnya, timeline penutupan sendiri sudah dimulai sejak 7 Juli 2026 ketika Nintendo menghentikan pembelian Ruby currency dan membuat semua Gold Pass subscription gratis hingga akhir. Jadi pemain hanya punya waktu sekitar tiga bulan untuk menikmati game sebelum semuanya hilang. Ini adalah praktik baku Nintendo dalam menangani live-service shutdown, memberikan notis yang jelas tapi tetap membuat transisi yang agak kasar bagi pemain setia yang menghabiskan waktu dan uang.
Baca juga: Sony Patenkan Controller PlayStation dengan NFC untuk Pembayaran
Bisakah Mario Kart Tour Kembali?
Pertanyaan yang muncul kemudian adalah apakah Nintendo akan mengembalikan Mario Kart Tour dalam bentuk lain? Jawabannya hampir pasti tidak. Nintendo tidak pernah membuat offline version untuk live-service game apapun yang mereka tutup, termasuk Fire Emblem Heroes, Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp, dan sejumlah game mobile lainnya. Keputusan bisnis ini sangat berbeda dengan bagaimana studio lain menangani shutdown, banyak yang setidaknya menawarkan offline build agar pemain bisa tetap memainkan game yang sudah mereka investasikan waktu dan uang.
Di sisi lain, konten Mario Kart Tour tidak benar-benar hilang semua. Ada part track dan item dari game mobile ini sudah di-repurposing menjadi DLC untuk Mario Kart 8 Deluxe di Switch, sebagai bagian dari Booster Course Pass. Artinya esensi dari Mario Kart Tour tetap hidup, hanya saja dengan format sesuai platformnya.
Tapi siapa tahu, mungkin di suatu hari nanti Nintendo akan membuat Mario Kart Tour: Remastered atau versi Switch 2 yang mengambil konsep original namun dalam format yang baru. Ya, kan?
Penutupan Mario Kart Tour sebenarnya jadi tamparan pahit tentang sifat live-service gaming: tidak ada jaminan sebuah game akan tetap ada selamanya. Untuk komunitas mobile gaming pun, hal semacam ini memperlihatkan risiko investasi waktu dan uang untuk bisa eksis di sana. Berbeda dengan game yang dibeli dan bisa dimainkan secara offline. Bagaimana menurutmu, Gizmo Friends?

Key Startup Funding Highlights Of The Week
Cleantech topped the funding charts this week, powered by the sole $180 Mn Series C round of electric vehicle (EV) maker Simple Energy.
Proptech was the second-most funded sector this week as home interior startup Gravity bagged $15 Mn. Agritech and fintech followed at $10.4 Mn each, while edtech saw Arivihan raise $10.2 Mn.
Ecommerce yet again led in deal activity, with four startups collectively raising $3.8 Mn.
Early stage funding activity remained lukewarm this week as seed-stage and pre-seed startups raised $3.3 Mn across four deals.
Alteria Capital emerged as the most active investor this week, backing three startups.
Startup Fund Updates Of The Week
Seed-stage VC firm WEH Ventures marked the first close of its third fund at an undisclosed amount. The fund is targeting a corpus of ₹250 Cr and is expected to close by mid-2027.
VC firm Peak XV Partners launched the twelfth cohort of its Surge accelerator programme, which will incubate 18 startups across AI, robotics, space, consumer, healthcare and fintech. Seven Indian startups also made the cut.
Startup M&A Updates Of The Week
ITC completed the acquisition of Yoga Bar’s parent Sproutlife Foods. The FMCG giant has picked up the remaining 52.5% stake for around ₹645 Cr, taking its total shareholding in the D2C healthy food brand to 100%.
Startup IPO Updates Of The Week
Fintech unicorn Moneyview made a stellar stock market debut this week, with its shares listing at ₹55.6 on the BSE, a premium of 64% over the issue price of ₹34. On the NSE, the stock listed at ₹55, a premium of nearly 62% over its issue price.
Led by NIIs, AceVector’s ₹420 Cr IPO was oversubscribed 4.93X on the final day of bidding, receiving bids for 36.61 Cr shares against 7.42 Cr shares on offer. It’s set to make its market debut on October 5.
Defence tech startup Tonbo Imaging received SEBI’s nod for its proposed IPO, which consists solely of an OFS of up to 1.81 Cr equity shares.
Used-car marketplace Cars24 expects to complete its reverse flip from Singapore to India by April 2027, after which it plans to file its DRHP for an IPO.
StockGro’s parent AssetGro Fintech pre-filed its DRHP with SEBI via the confidential route for a proposed IPO. The potential ₹2,500 Cr public issue will include a fresh issue worth ₹800 Cr and an OFS component.
Other Developments Of The Week
MobiKwik cofounder and CFO Upasana Taku bought an additional 1.07 Lakh shares of the listed fintech company for ₹2.1 Cr, increasing her stake to 10.24% from 10.11% earlier.
Ola Electric’s board approved a rights issue of up to ₹1,000 Cr. It will now decide on particulars like the price of the rights issue, rights entitlement ratio, record date and timing of the issue soon.
SBI Mutual Fund purchased 1.18 Cr Swiggy shares, taking its total shareholding in the foodtech giant to around 5.1%. The open-market transaction was pegged at over ₹300.6 Cr.
Jio Financial Services and Allianz infused ₹640 Cr into their general insurance joint venture (JV), Jio Allianz General Insurance, through a rights issue.

items.author: Ronggo
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Plaud, perusahaan pengembang perangkat AI wearable, secara resmi hadir di Indonesia dengan meluncurkan dua produk andalannya, yakni Plaud Note Pro dan NotePin S. Kedua perangkat keras ini dirancang khusus untuk merekam percakapan secara langsung, kemudian mengubahnya menjadi rangkuman terstruktur serta memberikan informasi yang dapat ditindaklanjuti oleh para profesional. Solusi ini didukung oleh kemampuan transkripsi kecerdasan buatan yang mencakup lebih dari 112 bahasa, termasuk dukungan penuh untuk Bahasa Indonesia, bahasa Jawa, dan bahasa Sunda.
Kehadiran teknologi ini berupaya menjawab tantangan tingginya beban kerja dan keterbatasan waktu yang dialami pekerja modern di Indonesia. Berdasarkan data dari survei Global Workforce Hopes and Fears 2025 oleh PwC, sebanyak 69% responden dari Indonesia tercatat telah memanfaatkan teknologi AI dalam rutinitas kerja mereka.
Di sisi lain, riset Work Trend Index 2025 dari Microsoft mengindikasikan bahwa 88% pekerja di Indonesia merasa kekurangan waktu atau energi untuk menuntaskan pekerjaan mereka. Dengan kemampuan menangkap konteks serta beradaptasi terhadap pergantian bahasa dan beragam dialek secara akurat, ekosistem perangkat Plaud diharapkan mampu menghemat waktu profesional secara signifikan tanpa menghilangkan elemen kolaborasi antarmanusia.
“Di Indonesia, kemajuan akan tercipta lebih baik ketika tetap menjunjung kebersamaan dan hubungan antarmanusia, yang menjadi semangat utama gotong royong. Seiring dengan kehadiran Plaud di Indonesia, kami ingin membantu para profesional mendapatkan kembali sumber daya mereka yang paling berharga, yaitu waktu. Dengan mengurangi beban mencatat, membuat transkripsi, dan melakukan tindak lanjut secara manual, AI seharusnya tidak menggantikan penilaian manusia, tetapi memberikan lebih banyak ruang untuk kolaborasi yang bermakna, pengambilan keputusan yang tepat, dan hal-hal yang benar-benar penting,” kata Megumi Yoshinaga, Head of APAC Marketing, Plaud.
Baca juga: OpenAI Dots Hadir di ChatGPT Pro, Ini 3 Profesi yang Disasar
Ketersediaan dan Harga Produk Plaud
Untuk menyesuaikan dengan kebutuhan mobilitas pekerja, Plaud mendesain produknya dalam dua form factor: Pertama, Plaud Note Pro yang punya dimensi seukuran kartu kredit. Perangkat ini dapat ditempelkan secara magnetis di bagian belakang ponsel yang kompatibel dengan fitur MagSafe. Fungsi intinya adalah untuk merekam panggilan telepon serta percakapan tatap muka secara langsung.
Sementara itu, Plaud NotePin S merupakan perangkat berdesain ringkas dan ringan yang fleksibel dikenakan pengguna sebagai kalung, klip, gelang, atau sekadar disematkan layaknya pin di kerah baju. Gawai ini dirancang khusus untuk mendukung pekerjaan bermobilitas tinggi, seperti rapat, sesi wawancara, konsultasi, maupun kerja lapangan.
Kedua gawai tersebut terintegrasi dengan ekosistem Plaud Intelligence yang memungkinkan hasil transkripsi, ringkasan, dan poin utama untuk dicari dan dilihat kembali. Pengguna juga disediakan fitur custom vocabulary guna menambahkan istilah-istilah spesifik yang relevan dengan bidang industri mereka. Pada bulan depan, Plaud berencana memperkenalkan kapabilitas AI agentic terbaru di pasar Indonesia, yang memampukan sistem untuk secara otomatis mengubah wawasan percakapan lampau menjadi draf email tindak lanjut, dokumen, dan hasil pekerjaan lainnya. Draf otomatis tersebut nantinya bisa didistribusikan secara langsung ke berbagai aplikasi produktivitas yang terhubung, seperti Notion, Slack, dan Linear.
Indonesia diproyeksikan akan menjadi pasar terbesar Plaud di wilayah Asia Tenggara pada tahun 2030 mendatang dengan perkiraan basis pengguna melampaui 1 juta orang. Tren pertumbuhan positif ini telah terlihat dari metrik penggunaan aktif mingguan produk Plaud di Indonesia yang melonjak hingga dua kali lipat pada semester pertama tahun 2026. Secara global, teknologi perusahaan yang berbasis di San Francisco ini telah diadopsi oleh lebih dari 2,5 juta profesional yang tersebar di lebih dari 170 negara.
Untuk ketersediaan di pasar domestik, Plaud Note Pro ditawarkan secara resmi dengan harga Rp3.499.000, sedangkan varian NotePin S dibanderol seharga Rp3.449.000. Perangkat yang telah memenuhi standar keamanan data global ISO 27001 dan GDPR ini dapat dibeli secara luring di hampir 70 jaringan toko ritel fisik seperti Urban Republic, Gramedia, dan iBox. Konsumen juga dapat mengakses produk ini secara daring melalui situs web resmi Plaud wilayah Asia Tenggara serta berbagai platform e-commerce utama.

LCD panels, which once dominated the market, have been phased out in most segments in favour of more advanced display technologies. Today, buyers can choose from AMOLED, OLED, pOLED, and other types. Meanwhile, high-end smartphones are also increasingly advertised with another term — LTPO. It is often mentioned alongside 120Hz refresh rates and always-on displays. However, LTPO is not simply another type of screen panel, but a backplane technology that helps a display dynamically adjust its refresh rate depending on what is being shown.
