items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Sazgar Engineering Works Ltd (SEWL) wants to add a premium Chinese electric brand to its line-up, but it has not yet decided how, or at what price, the cars would reach Pakistani buyers. The Sazgar ARCFOX EV launch is on the company’s plan, and the answer to both questions is waiting on the government’s new auto policy.
The company told the stock exchange on Friday that it intends to introduce ARCFOX new energy vehicles (NEVs) in Pakistan. NEV is the term local assemblers use for electric and plug-in hybrid cars. Management gave more detail at a corporate briefing on Saturday.
What Sazgar has said about ARCFOX
ARCFOX is a high-end intelligent electric vehicle brand from BAIC Group. According to Sazgar’s filing, the brand combines premium design with advanced technology and involves engineering and technology collaboration with Magna and Huawei.
Management said ARCFOX is positioned high in the semi-premium segment. It also ranks among the higher-positioned brands among China’s 109 automotive brands, the company said.
That puts it above the mass-market NEVs that most local assemblers have focused on so far. Whether Pakistan has enough buyers at that price level is a question the company has not addressed publicly.
CKD or CBU: the policy decides
The company has not said whether ARCFOX would be assembled locally from kits (CKD) or imported as fully built units (CBU). Management said that choice depends on the new auto policy.
The difference affects price, taxes, and jobs. Local assembly generally attracts lower duties than complete imports and builds a supply chain at home, but it needs volume to justify the investment. Imports let a company test demand at lower cost and with less commitment.
Management also said the government is likely to support plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs) going forward. Future launches, it said, will follow that view.
Absorbing the tax increase
Sania Irfan of Topline Securities said Sazgar is currently absorbing the increase in general sales tax (GST). The company expects a favourable auto policy soon, possibly with lower taxes, and does not want to hurt customers buying vehicles today at the higher rate.
She said management is waiting for the new policy before making major pricing decisions. Current prices rest on the taxes as notified, and the company is not raising them despite 18% GST for now.
For buyers, that means today’s price list may not last. If the policy lowers taxes, waiting could pay off. If it does not, the company may have to pass the cost on. Nothing in the briefing gives a date for the policy.
Products and expansion
Sazgar said the launch of Canon Alpha is expected in the coming months and will be priced competitively. Last week it displayed a broad upcoming NEV line-up at the Pakistan Auto Show (PAPS), alongside the Tank 300 and Jolion Max.
The company has also announced a Rs22bn expansion, including a new paint shop, which management expects to finish within 9 to 10 months. Around Rs17bn of that will be financed by debt and the rest through equity.
The bet behind the timing
The pattern here is unusual. Sazgar is committing to a large capital programme, taking on debt for most of it, and holding prices steady, all while the policy that would shape demand is still unpublished. Rs17bn of Rs22bn means debt covers roughly 77 percent of the plan.
That reads as confidence that the policy will favour NEVs and that tax relief is coming. If the policy arrives later than expected or with fewer incentives than assumed, the company would carry both financing costs and thinner margins from absorbing GST.
The PHEV signal is the most practical clue. Plug-in hybrids suit a market with limited public charging, since they can run on petrol when a charger is not available. A policy that supports them would fit the infrastructure that exists today better than one built around fully electric cars alone.
What it means for Pakistani buyers
For most car buyers, an ARCFOX will be out of reach at semi-premium pricing. The more relevant effect is on the wider market. Each new NEV entrant adds competition, and competition tends to push assemblers toward better pricing and more local content.
Buyers weighing a purchase now face an awkward wait. Prices reflect existing taxes, the policy may change them, and the launch dates for new models are still loose.

items.title: Sony Patenkan Controller PlayStation dengan NFC untuk Pembayaran
items.summary:
Sony kembali mengeksplorasi kemungkinan baru untuk controller PlayStation. Perusahaan tersebut mengajukan paten untuk controller yang dapat membaca informasi pembayaran dari kartu kredit, ponsel, maupun gift card di dekatnya, sehingga pengguna berpotensi membeli game tanpa harus memasukkan detail kartu secara manual melalui konsol.
Paten berjudul “Video Game Controller-Driven Information Transfer” tersebut diajukan pada Maret 2025 dan baru dipublikasikan pada 17 September 2026. Dalam konsepnya, controller berfungsi sebagai penghubung antara metode pembayaran dan konsol. Ketika sistem meminta informasi pembayaran, pengguna cukup mendekatkan kartu atau perangkat ke controller untuk memindahkan informasi yang diperlukan.
Proses tersebut disebut dapat memanfaatkan NFC, Bluetooth, atau kontak langsung, tergantung perangkat yang digunakan. Controller kemudian memberikan konfirmasi melalui cahaya, suara, atau getaran setelah informasi berhasil dibaca sebelum meneruskannya ke konsol. Salah sat
items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Sony kembali mengeksplorasi kemungkinan baru untuk controller PlayStation. Perusahaan tersebut mengajukan paten untuk controller yang dapat membaca informasi pembayaran dari kartu kredit, ponsel, maupun gift card di dekatnya, sehingga pengguna berpotensi membeli game tanpa harus memasukkan detail kartu secara manual melalui konsol.
Paten berjudul “Video Game Controller-Driven Information Transfer” tersebut diajukan pada Maret 2025 dan baru dipublikasikan pada 17 September 2026. Dalam konsepnya, controller berfungsi sebagai penghubung antara metode pembayaran dan konsol. Ketika sistem meminta informasi pembayaran, pengguna cukup mendekatkan kartu atau perangkat ke controller untuk memindahkan informasi yang diperlukan.
Proses tersebut disebut dapat memanfaatkan NFC, Bluetooth, atau kontak langsung, tergantung perangkat yang digunakan. Controller kemudian memberikan konfirmasi melalui cahaya, suara, atau getaran setelah informasi berhasil dibaca sebelum meneruskannya ke konsol. Salah satu ilustrasi bahkan menunjukkan gift card yang digunakan untuk menambahkan saldo tanpa perlu memasukkan kode secara manual.
Baca Juga: Cath Bowie Raih Rekor Guinness, Jadi Streamer Fortnite Perempuan Tertua di Usia 78 Tahun
Bisa untuk Selain Pembayaran
Sistem PlayStation Tap-to-Pay (Sumber: Eureka by Patsnap)
Konsep transfer informasi dalam paten tersebut sebenarnya tidak terbatas pada transaksi. Sony juga membayangkan teknologi serupa untuk memindahkan ID pemain, memungkinkan pengguna lain bergabung ke sesi multiplayer, atau mengirim screenshot dan klip permainan ke ponsel.
Ada pula skenario penggunaan di toko atau pameran. Misalnya, seseorang mencoba demo sebuah game dan kemudian cukup mendekatkan ponsel ke controller untuk menambahkan versi penuh game tersebut ke library agar dapat dimainkan nanti. Namun, seluruh skenario tersebut masih sebatas konsep yang dijelaskan dalam dokumen paten.
Belum Tentu Hadir di PlayStation
Hal penting yang perlu diperhatikan, Sony belum mengonfirmasi bahwa teknologi ini akan hadir sebagai fitur pada PS5 ataupun konsol generasi berikutnya. Ilustrasi dalam paten juga menggunakan desain yang menyerupai DualSense biasa, tanpa menunjukkan perangkat baru yang secara khusus dibuat untuk sistem pembayaran tersebut.
Sony sendiri sebelumnya telah mengajukan sejumlah paten controller dengan konsep yang cukup eksperimental. Beberapa di antaranya mencakup AI yang membantu mengisi input controller serta desain controller dengan layar sentuh tanpa tombol fisik. Karena perusahaan rutin mengeksplorasi berbagai teknologi melalui paten, keberadaan dokumen ini belum menjadi indikasi bahwa fitur tersebut pasti akan diproduksi atau digunakan pada perangkat PlayStation mendatang.

items.title: Dari e-KYC hingga AI, Telkom Solution Bawa Solusi Digital untuk Industri Keuangan
items.summary:
Transformasi layanan keuangan digital tidak berhenti pada aplikasi pembayaran atau kanal transaksi. Di belakangnya terdapat kebutuhan terhadap konektivitas, pusat data, keamanan siber, pengelolaan data, hingga teknologi kecerdasan buatan (AI).
Kebutuhan tersebut menjadi salah satu fokus kehadiran Telkom Solution dalam Festival Ekonomi Keuangan Digital Indonesia (FEKDI) & Indonesia Fintech Summit & Expo (IFSE) 2026 yang berlangsung di Jakarta International Convention Center (JICC), Jakarta, 24–26 September 2026.
Sebagai umbrella brand layanan B2B ICT Telkom, Telkom Solution membawa portofolio teknologi yang mencakup konektivitas, cloud dan data center, aplikasi digital, cybersecurity, serta solusi berbasis AI untuk kebutuhan sektor keuangan.
Kehadiran tersebut menjadi bagian dari kolaborasi Telkom dan Danantara Indonesia dalam mendorong penguatan ekosistem ekonomi dan keuangan digital Indonesia.

items.author: Bambang Dwi Atmoko
items.content:
Transformasi layanan keuangan digital tidak berhenti pada aplikasi pembayaran atau kanal transaksi. Di belakangnya terdapat kebutuhan terhadap konektivitas, pusat data, keamanan siber, pengelolaan data, hingga teknologi kecerdasan buatan (AI).
Kebutuhan tersebut menjadi salah satu fokus kehadiran Telkom Solution dalam Festival Ekonomi Keuangan Digital Indonesia (FEKDI) & Indonesia Fintech Summit & Expo (IFSE) 2026 yang berlangsung di Jakarta International Convention Center (JICC), Jakarta, 24–26 September 2026.
Sebagai umbrella brand layanan B2B ICT Telkom, Telkom Solution membawa portofolio teknologi yang mencakup konektivitas, cloud dan data center, aplikasi digital, cybersecurity, serta solusi berbasis AI untuk kebutuhan sektor keuangan.
Kehadiran tersebut menjadi bagian dari kolaborasi Telkom dan Danantara Indonesia dalam mendorong penguatan ekosistem ekonomi dan keuangan digital Indonesia.
Baca juga: Telkom Solution Bidik Segmen Pasar Enterprise dengan Tiga Solusi Digital Unggulan
Infrastruktur Digital Menjadi Fondasi
Bagi industri keuangan, integrasi berbagai lapisan teknologi menjadi semakin penting karena layanan digital melibatkan banyak pihak, mulai dari institusi perbankan, perusahaan pembiayaan, koperasi, regulator, hingga penyelenggara layanan keuangan.
Direktur IT Digital Telkom, Faizal Rochmad Djoemadi, mengatakan pemerataan sistem keuangan digital membutuhkan dukungan infrastruktur dan teknologi yang dapat menghubungkan berbagai elemen dalam ekosistem tersebut. “Pemerataan sistem keuangan digital membutuhkan fondasi teknologi yang kuat dan terintegrasi secara end-to-end,” ujar Faizal saat menghadiri FEKDI & IFSE 2026.
Menurut dia, kapabilitas Telkom mencakup infrastruktur digital, platform dan aplikasi, pengelolaan data, cybersecurity, hingga solusi berbasis AI. Kapabilitas tersebut diarahkan untuk mendukung pengembangan layanan keuangan yang lebih terintegrasi dan menjangkau masyarakat di berbagai wilayah.
Pendekatan ini menunjukkan bahwa kebutuhan transformasi digital di sektor keuangan berada di lebih banyak lapisan dibanding sekadar menyediakan kanal transaksi digital.
Dari e-KYC hingga QRIS
Di ajang FEKDI x IFSE 2026, Telkom Solution menempatkan solusi digital sebagai bagian dari ekosistem yang melibatkan institusi keuangan sekaligus penggunanya. Untuk industri perbankan, perusahaan menyebut integrasi solusi digital dapat digunakan untuk mendukung produktivitas layanan dan efisiensi operasional, sekaligus meningkatkan pengalaman nasabah. Sementara dari sisi pengguna, teknologi tersebut mencakup berbagai proses seperti pembukaan rekening menggunakan electronic Know Your Customer (e-KYC), pembayaran digital, hingga pembuatan QRIS.
Aspek keamanan juga menjadi bagian dari solusi tersebut, terutama karena semakin banyak proses layanan keuangan berlangsung secara digital. Telkom Solution juga menyasar institusi keuangan di luar perbankan, termasuk Bank Perkreditan Rakyat (BPR), koperasi, dan perusahaan multifinance.
Untuk kelompok tersebut, infrastruktur cloud dan data center yang didukung jaringan TelkomGroup disebut dapat digunakan untuk menyesuaikan kapasitas teknologi dengan kebutuhan bisnis.
Dengan pendekatan seperti ini, cloud dan data center tidak hanya ditempatkan sebagai infrastruktur pendukung, tetapi sebagai bagian dari fondasi untuk menjalankan layanan keuangan digital.
Cybersecurity dan Fraud Jadi Bagian Ekosistem
Semakin terintegrasinya layanan keuangan digital juga membawa kebutuhan terhadap keamanan dan pengawasan. Telkom Solution menyebut integrasi sistem dan data dapat membantu regulator melakukan monitoring dan pengawasan. Integrasi tersebut juga dapat mendukung penyelenggara layanan keuangan dalam memenuhi kebutuhan kepatuhan.
Di sisi lain, kemampuan mitigasi fraud turut menjadi bagian dari portofolio yang ditawarkan untuk mendukung keamanan ekosistem. Hal ini relevan karena digitalisasi layanan keuangan membuat semakin banyak proses, data, dan interaksi nasabah berpindah ke sistem digital. Karena itu, konektivitas dan kemudahan akses perlu berjalan bersamaan dengan pengamanan sistem serta data.
Bagi mitra penyelenggara layanan keuangan, Telkom juga menyebut integrasi ekosistem dapat mendukung pengembangan kanal pembayaran, konektivitas dengan institusi perbankan, serta efisiensi dan kolektibilitas.
AI Masuk ke Portofolio B2B ICT
Salah satu teknologi yang turut masuk dalam portofolio Telkom Solution adalah artificial intelligence (AI). Namun, dalam konteks industri keuangan, AI ditempatkan sebagai salah satu bagian dari rangkaian kapabilitas digital yang lebih luas. Teknologi tersebut berjalan bersama konektivitas, cloud, data center, aplikasi, pengelolaan data, dan cybersecurity.
Pendekatan ini penting karena implementasi AI di sektor keuangan membutuhkan fondasi data dan infrastruktur yang mendukungnya. AI tidak berdiri sendiri sebagai aplikasi, melainkan bergantung pada ketersediaan data, sistem komputasi, konektivitas, serta aspek keamanan.
Telkom sendiri menyatakan penguatan kapabilitas digital tersebut merupakan bagian dari sinerginya bersama Danantara untuk mendorong kedaulatan digital dan finansial Indonesia.
Fokus Berikutnya: Kebutuhan Industri
Kehadiran di FEKDI x IFSE 2026 juga menjadi bagian dari upaya Telkom Solution untuk mengembangkan portofolio B2B ICT yang menyesuaikan kebutuhan sektor keuangan. Telkom menyatakan pengembangan kapabilitas ke depan akan diarahkan untuk mendukung kebutuhan industri sekaligus membangun ekosistem ekonomi dan keuangan digital yang lebih terintegrasi.
Bagi industri, arah tersebut memperlihatkan bahwa transformasi keuangan digital semakin membutuhkan integrasi antara berbagai komponen teknologi. Mulai dari jaringan yang menghubungkan layanan, infrastruktur cloud dan data center untuk menjalankan sistem, aplikasi untuk kebutuhan operasional dan nasabah, hingga cybersecurity dan AI.
Faizal mengatakan integrasi berbagai kapabilitas TelkomGroup diharapkan tidak hanya menjawab kebutuhan teknologi, tetapi juga memberikan manfaat bagi ekosistem ekonomi dan keuangan digital secara lebih luas.
Dengan demikian, partisipasi Telkom Solution di FEKDI x IFSE 2026 bukan sekadar menampilkan portofolio teknologi. Forum tersebut menjadi ruang bagi Telkom untuk menunjukkan bagaimana kapabilitas B2B ICT-nya diarahkan ke kebutuhan sektor keuangan yang semakin bergantung pada infrastruktur digital, keamanan, integrasi data, dan layanan berbasis teknologi.

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Timnas Pokemon Unite Indonesia berhasil menorehkan sejarah baru di Asian Games 2026 Aichi-Nagoya, Jepang, di mana kontingen Merah Putih berhasil mempersembahkan medali perak setelah kalah dari tuan rumah Jepang.
Perjalanan timnas Indonesia yang diperkuat Marcello Hillers (Cell), Muhammad Haikal (Zoe), Novrizal Diananta Said (Illuna), Denny Ardianyanto (AXQ), dan Judha Pangabean terlihat meyakinkan sejak fase grup.
Baca Juga: Cath Bowie Raih Rekor Guinness, Jadi Streamer Fortnite Perempuan Tertua di Usia 78 Tahun
Keluar sebagai pemuncak Grup B dan mengamankan tiket ke babak gugur, skuad Merah Putih tampil dominan saat melawan Malaysia dan menutup pertandingan dengan kemenangan 2-0 untuk mengamankan tempat di babak berikutnya.
Performa solid juga terus ditampilkan atlet esports asal Indonesia ini. Saat berhadapan dengan Filipina, Marcello dkk berhasil mencatat kemenangan meyakinkan dengan skor 2-0 dan memastikan diri melangkah ke partai perebutan medali emas di Asian Games 2026 Aichi-Nagoya, Jepang.
Timnas Pokemon Unite Indonesia Sempat Unggul di Final
Di partai final, timnas Tanah Air berhadapan dengan tim Pokemon Unite dari Tuan Rumah. Pertandingan berlangsung dalam format best of five (Bo5).
Indonesia mengawali laga dengan baik dan berhasil merebut kemenangan pada game pertama. Hasil tersebut sempat membuka peluang bagi skuad Merah Putih untuk membawa pulang medali emas.
Asian Games 2026: Timnas Pokemon Unite Indonesia Raih Perak
Namun Jepang mampu bangkit pada game berikutnya. Tuan rumah mengambil alih momentum pertandingan dan memenangkan tiga game secara beruntun.
Indonesia akhirnya harus mengakui keunggulan Jepang dengan skor akhir 1-3. Meski gagal meraih emas, hasil tersebut tetap memastikan medali perak untuk cabang Pokemon Unite di Asian Games 2026.
Pencapaian ini menjadi salah satu hasil terbaik Indonesia di nomor esports Asian Games 2026, sekaligus menunjukkan daya saing skuad Pokemon Unite Indonesia di level internasional.
Timnas Esports Indonesia Resmi Finalisasi 34 Atlet untuk Asian Games 2026
Timnas Indonesia MLBB memulai perjuangan di Asian Games 2026 pada 29 September dengan menghadapi Malaysia dan Arab Saudi di fase grup.
Pengurus Besar Esports Indonesia (PB ESI) bersama Kementerian Pemuda dan Olahraga (Kemenpora) resmi merampungkan fase Entry By Name untuk kontingen esports Indonesia yang akan berlaga di Asian Games 2026 di Aichi-Nagoya, Jepang. Sebanyak 34 atlet telah ditetapkan untuk mewakili Indonesia pada delapan nomor pertandingan yang lolos ke tahap final.
Fase Entry By Name menjadi tahapan akhir dalam proses administrasi dan verifikasi atlet sebelum keberangkatan menuju Asian Games 2026. Pada tahap ini, seluruh nomor pertandingan serta susunan atlet yang diajukan PB ESI menjalani evaluasi akhir oleh Tim Peningkatan Prestasi Olahraga Nasional (PPON) Kemenpora.
Sebelumnya, Indonesia mengajukan sembilan nomor pertandingan esports untuk Asian Games 2026. Namun setelah proses evaluasi dan verifikasi selesai dilakukan, hanya delapan nomor yang masuk ke dalam finalisasi kontingen Indonesia. Satu nomor yang tidak lolos pada tahap ini adalah Competitive Martial Arts (CMA).
Delapan Nomor Pertandingan Resmi Berangkat ke Jepang
Timnas Esports Indonesia sebelumnya berhasil mengamankan tiket Main Event Asian Games 2026 melalui sejumlah nomor yang mengikuti fase kualifikasi regional Asia. Beberapa nomor yang sukses lolos antara lain Honor of Kings, Identity V, Naraka: Bladepoint, Mobile Legends: Bang Bang, dan PUBG Mobile.
Selain itu, Indonesia juga diproyeksikan tampil pada nomor eFootball, Gran Turismo, dan Pokémon Unite. Dengan demikian, total terdapat delapan nomor pertandingan yang akan menjadi wakil Indonesia pada cabang olahraga esports di Asian Games 2026.
Manajer Timnas Esports Indonesia, Glorya Famiela Ralahallo, mengatakan pihaknya menghormati seluruh proses evaluasi yang dilakukan bersama Kemenpora. Menurutnya, fokus saat ini adalah memastikan seluruh atlet dapat menjalani persiapan secara optimal menjelang turnamen.
Ada Perubahan Roster di Tim Mobile Legends
Syauki “Nino” Sumarno saat wawancara tentang persiapan timnas MLBB menuju Asian Games 2026. (Gizmologi/ Yuslianson
Selain menetapkan jumlah atlet dan nomor pertandingan, PB ESI juga mengumumkan adanya perubahan roster pada tim Mobile Legends: Bang Bang. Albert Neilsen “Alberttt” Iskandar resmi masuk ke dalam susunan pemain Timnas Indonesia untuk Asian Games 2026.
Masuknya Alberttt membuat komposisi roster MLBB mengalami penyesuaian. Berdasarkan dokumen final Entry By Name, Alberttt menggantikan Muhammad Halim Adicondro sebagai bagian dari proses evaluasi kebutuhan teknis yang dilakukan tim pelatih dan Badan Tim Nasional selama masa persiapan hingga kualifikasi regional.
Dengan komposisi 34 atlet yang telah ditetapkan, PB ESI kini memasuki tahap pematangan persiapan menjelang Asian Games 2026. Targetnya tentu tidak hanya sekadar tampil kompetitif, tetapi juga menjaga tren positif perkembangan Esports Indonesia yang dalam beberapa tahun terakhir terus menunjukkan peningkatan di level internasional.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Allegations Hit Bharat Taxi
The arrival of Bharat Taxi promised zero commissions and empowered drivers. But its rollout has triggered allegations of vigilantism, passenger intimidation, forced app deletions and thefts across Gujarat. So, why is the state-backed ride-hailing service in the middle of a full-blown storm?
Alleged Coercion & Intimidation: Drivers describe groups threatening violence and stealing money after stopping cabs mid-ride. Passengers, meanwhile, report being forced to cancel app bookings and delete Uber and Rapido apps. Fear of retaliation keeps many from approaching police, while passengers worry about safety and ride availability during trips.
The Economic Reality: Launched earlier this year, Bharat Taxi’s zero-commission model promised driver ownership and profit-sharing. But drivers allege that bookings are too sparse to sustain incomes. Many report being pressured to quit Uber and Rapido despite insufficient Bharat Taxi demand, risking EMI defaults and livelihood loss. Without adequate ride volume, the platform’s economic viability remains unproven.
Conflicting Police Signals: Social media videos show individuals in police uniforms both promoting Bharat Taxi and warning against coercion, deepening public confusion. The key concern for drivers remains that harassment could persist in the absence of clear enforcement on the streets. For now, questions remain over passenger safety and platform choice.
The Looming Questions: The allegations underscore the tension between the cooperative model and private platforms in India’s urban mobility landscape. While Bharat Taxi’s zero-commission structure may appeal to many, coercive tactics could undermine its legitimacy and passenger trust. Resolution requires clear police action, transparent communication and protection of driver and passenger choice.
Without these, the alleged incidents could risk confidence in app-based ride-hailing across Gujarat and push users and drivers toward unregulated alternatives. So, what has really gone wrong with Bharat Taxi? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
Weekly Funding Rebounds
Indian startups cumulatively managed to raise $203.4 Mn last week, up 3.4X compared to $58.9 Mn in the preceding week. Deal count also zoomed 50% week-on-week to 21. Ultraviolette and Ema emerged as the most funded startups last week.
AI emerged as the most funded sector last week, with five AI startups bagging a combined $89.3 Mn. Ecommerce led in deal activity, with six startups collectively raising $3.8 Mn.
Early stage funding activity also remained strong as seed-stage startups raised $20.3 Mn across five deals last week. Peercheque and Sauce.VC were the most active investors of the week, backing two startups each.
InMobi Gets A New Backer
Private equity firm True North has acquired a minority stake in the IPO-bound adtech startup. The secondary deal saw the PE firm lapping up 2-3% stake in InMobi for $50 Mn to $60 Mn. There was also a small equity component to the transaction.
Founded in 2007, InMobi provides marketing and monetisation solutions to brands, advertisers and publishers. It also operates social commerce platform Roposo, and Glance, an AI-based Android lockscreen platform. It has raised $774 Mn to date.
The fundraise comes as InMobi is redomiciling back to India from Singapore, ahead of its potential $1 Bn IPO. Earlier this year, the startup also appointed bankers to helm its public issue, which will target a valuation of $6 Bn to $10 Bn.
Bearish Week For Startup Stocks
Of the 65 new-age tech stocks under Inc42’s coverage, 37 ended last week in the red and fell between 0.01% and 35%. The remaining 28 gained between 0.3% and 24.6%.
Capillary Technologies and Zelio were the biggest gainers last week, while PB Fintech and Turtlemint were the biggest losers. The combined market capitalisation of the 65 listed startups declined to $166.6 Bn from $170.2 Bn the previous week.
This week, investors will track developments involving the US and Iran, Brent crude prices, US bond yields, and the Rupee, alongside other domestic economic cues for market direction.
Aequs Eyes ₹650 Cr
The contract manufacturing company has received board nod to raise up to ₹650 Cr via a preferential issue of warrants to the promoter group, Mellwood Trustee Services. Aequs will issue 2.8 Cr warrants at ₹231.55 apiece.
While ₹325 Cr will be payable upfront upon allotment, the balance will have to be paid after the exercise of the warrants. Upon full conversion of the warrants, the aggregate holding of the promoter group will increase to 60.73% from 59.09% currently.
The fresh capital will be used to expand its manufacturing capacity, invest in subsidiaries and for other general corporate purposes. Founded in 2006, Aequs offers manufacturing services to enterprises. Its clients include Airbus, Boeing and others.
IIT Madras Bets On Deeptechs
IIT Madras and Unicorn India Ventures have marked the first close of their deeptech-focused IITM Unicorn Frontier Fund I at ₹450 Cr. The fund claims to have already deployed nearly ₹55 Cr across four startups.
Launched in February this year, the fund has a base corpus of ₹600 Cr and an additional greenshoe option of ₹400 Cr. The ₹1,000 Cr fund is targeting the final close by December 2026. Its backers include IIT Madras alumni and family offices.
Managed by Unicorn India Ventures, the fund aims to build a portfolio of 25 startups across defence tech, spacetech, semiconductors, robotics and AI. The fund will dish out cheques in the range of ₹15 Cr to ₹25 Cr.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Can Neuromod Commoditise Sewage Treatment Plants?
Designing wastewater plants in India can be expensive, slow to install and difficult to maintain. Neuromod Aqua is addressing this bottleneck by turning wastewater treatment into a standardised, modular infrastructure product.
The Modular Approach: Founded in 2026, Neuromod Aqua builds modular treatment systems for sewage and industrial effluents. Its portfolio includes sewage treatment plants, effluent treatment plants, reverse-osmosis systems, zero-liquid-discharge units and demineralisation plants.
The Factory Model: Neuromod’s systems use technologies such as MBBR, MBR and SBR, with modules manufactured in a controlled environment and deployed according to site requirements. This approach reduces project timelines and simplifies maintenance. The startup also expects recurring revenue from monitoring and maintenance contracts, giving it a business model that extends beyond one-time sales.
The Road Ahead: Neuromod is targeting real-estate developers, hospitality firms and infrastructure projects, where water recycling and wastewater compliance are increasingly becoming operational necessities. Going forward, it plans to validate its sewage treatment plant, complete initial commercial deployments and expand service capabilities.
With India’s wastewater treatment market projected to become a $19.4 Bn opportunity by 2034, can Neuromod make bespoke water treatment plants for factories?

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Moshood Oshunfurewa
The machinery of Nigeria’s democracy is grinding towards 2027, yet the omens are anything but auspicious. What we are witnessing is not the meticulous preparation for a credible election, but the slow, deliberate construction of a political powder keg. The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), an institution whose credibility was already left in tatters after the 2023 general elections, is now at the centre of a confluence of dangers: predatory governors, a fundamentally opaque budget, and damning technological revelations that suggest the last election was a dress rehearsal for a more sophisticated heist. The question is no longer whether the 2027 election will be free and fair, but whether the nation can survive its outcome.
The revelations from the election data platform Mundx Analytics regarding the 2023 presidential election should have triggered a national emergency. Its analysis of 103,399 result sheets with readable device metadata found that a staggering 48.8 per cent, approximately 50,432 result sheets, were uploaded to INEC’s IReV portal from non-BVAS devices, including personal phones. INEC had repeatedly promised that results would be uploaded directly from the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) machines, a pledge that was the cornerstone of the Electoral Act 2022’s transparency provisions. The presence of over 50,000 result sheets from private devices, with brands like Infinix, Tecno, and Samsung identified, raises profound questions about the chain of custody. Who uploaded these results, under whose authority, and what happened to the data in the intervening period? While Mundx Analytics is careful to note that its findings do not establish that votes were altered, they expose a catastrophic breach in the digital accountability of the electoral process. This was not a minor logistical hiccup; it was a systemic failure that opened the door to manipulation on an industrial scale. It was a clear signal that the technology designed to protect the people’s mandate could be effortlessly bypassed.
This technological vulnerability is exacerbated by the increasingly brazen interference of state governors. The 2027 election cycle is already being defined by the audacious attempts of governors to predetermine outcomes and deliver entire geopolitical zones to favoured candidates. The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) rightly condemned the declaration by the Chairman of the South-East Governors’ Forum that the zone’s governors had collectively resolved to work for the re-election of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, describing it as an affront to constitutional democracy. This is not an isolated incident. The International Society for Civil Liberties and the Rule of Law (InterSociety) has accused six governors—Soludo, Alia, Okpebholo, Nwifuru, Mbah, and Uzodimma—of promoting political intolerance and suppressing opposition activities, with allegations ranging from attacks on opposition supporters to the abuse of state power. When governors, who are the chief executives of their states, begin to speak as though they own the votes of millions of citizens, they undermine the very foundation of democratic sovereignty. Their actions create a climate of fear and intimidation that makes a mockery of the notion of a free and fair contest.
But if governors are the foot soldiers of electoral subversion, the opaque and frankly outrageous budget of INEC provides the ammunition. The commission’s proposed N873.78 billion budget for the 2027 elections, combined with a separate N171 billion request for 2026, has sparked national outrage for good reason. This is a staggering sum in a country where 62.9 per cent of citizens are multidimensionally poor, and it is being requested by an institution that cannot account for over N126.46 billion in electoral funds from the previous cycle. The Auditor-General’s report identified over N112.15 billion allegedly paid for ballot boxes and other materials without competitive bidding or a Certificate of No Objection from the Bureau of Public Procurement. This is not merely a question of fiscal prudence; it is a matter of national security. A budget of this magnitude, shrouded in secrecy and lacking in accountability, is a treasure chest for corruption. It fuels the suspicion that elections are no longer a civic exercise but a colossal business venture for political elites and their cronies, further eroding public trust in the entire democratic project.
Nyesom Wike, the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory and the erstwhile leader of the G5 governors’ bloc, has openly detailed a strategy that amounted to the coordinated manipulation of electoral outcomes across multiple states during the 2023 presidential election. In a televised interview, Wike revealed that the G5 deliberately “allowed” Peter Obi to win in Edo and Cross River States, while intentionally “stopping” him from winning Rivers State because it would “send the wrong message”. This is not a denial of rigging; it is a confession of it, dressed up in the language of political strategy. The Resource Centre for Human Rights and Civic Education (CHRICED) rightly raised the alarm, noting that such claims suggest “possible abuse of state power during the electoral process” and “subversion of democratic norms by individuals entrusted with public authority”. The credibility of Wike’s claim is further bolstered by independent evidence: a BBC investigation found that the collation officer for Oyigbo Local Government Area in Rivers State, who presented himself as a lecturer, submitted falsified figures that multiplied Tinubu’s votes by six and halved Obi’s. If a serving minister can openly boast about determining who “wins” and “loses” in sovereign states, then the sovereignty of the people is not merely threatened—it has already been surrendered to a cabal of self-appointed kingmakers.
The logical endpoint of this malfeasance is a crisis of legitimacy, one that will almost certainly be resolved not at the ballot box but in the courts. The 2023 elections have already established a dangerous precedent in which the judiciary, rightly or wrongly, became the final arbiter of who holds power. As Cardinal John Onaiyekan lamented, Nigeria’s recent experience has shifted the determination of election outcomes from polling stations to courtrooms. This trend is set to worsen in 2027. With INEC’s chairman already acknowledging a litany of pending court cases over party primaries, and with the Supreme Court issuing judgments that reshape the electoral landscape just months before the election, the stage is set for a legal quagmire. The risk is not just that the courts will determine the next president, but that, in doing so, they will destroy the last vestiges of their own credibility. 
When a winner is declared by a judge rather than by the people, the state loses its moral authority, and the seeds of prolonged unrest are sown.
It is within this combustible context that we must heed the warnings that the ghost of the 2020 #EndSARS protests continues to haunt the nation. The violent suppression of that movement, which led to widespread anarchy and an estimated $305 million in damage in Lagos alone, demonstrated how quickly legitimate grievances can spiral into chaos. The current disillusionment among young Nigerians, facing unemployment, insecurity, and a political class that seems entirely disconnected from their suffering, is arguably more profound than it was in 2020. The opposition, as I have argued before, is fragmented and self-sabotaging, offering no credible alternative. In the absence of a trusted political outlet, and with INEC’s credibility shattered and the judiciary’s neutrality questioned, the potential for a revolt that surpasses the scale and intensity of #EndSARS is a genuine and frightening possibility. Another stolen election, another court-sanctioned presidency, could very well be the spark that ignites a conflagration of civil unrest and anarchy that no institution can contain.
The path to 2027 is fraught with peril. Nigeria stands at a crossroads. The confluence of an untrustworthy electoral commission, the overbearing ambition of governors, a secretive and bloated budget, the technological loopholes that render the ballot insecure, and the growing reliance on judicial pronouncements instead of popular will is creating a perfect storm. The killing of #EndSARS protesters was a scar on the nation’s conscience, a warning of the state’s capacity for violence and the people’s capacity for rage. If the 2027 election is perceived as another grand deception, the resulting upheaval will not be a protest; it will be a reckoning. The time for genuine electoral reform and the restoration of institutional integrity is now, before the final embers of hope are extinguished and the nation is consumed by the anarchy that looms on the horizon.

items.content:
By Clifford Ndujihe & Luminous Jannamike
The Supreme Court’s restoration of key provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 has opened a fresh legal front over the nominations of some Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, and other opposition parties’ candidates ahead of the 2027 elections.
With the apex court’s verdict other parties affected include the Social Democratic Party, SDP; Allied Peoples Movement, APM; People’s Redemption Party, PRP; and a candidate of the All Progressives Congress, APC.
The judgment does not automatically disqualify the affected candidates. Rather, it restores statutory requirements that could expose individual nominations to legal challenges where evidence shows that membership, registration or nomination procedures did not comply with the law.
In its unanimous judgment of September 24, 2026, the apex court restored Sections 77(5), 77(6), 77(7) and 84(2) of the Electoral Act, holding that the provisions were not inconsistent with the 1999 Constitution and setting aside the earlier Court of Appeal decision that had voided them.
The restored provisions require parties to rely on the membership register submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, at least 21 days before a primary. A party cannot use a different register, while nominations are to be conducted through direct primaries or consensus.
That means candidates could face challenges where evidence shows that they were not on the relevant register, joined a party after the register was submitted, participated in another party’s primary or emerged through a process that did not comply with the applicable requirements.
PDP candidates in the eye of the storm
Although, the Supreme Court made no candidate-specific findings against PDP candidates, those in the eye of the storm include Senator Saliu Mustapha, Kolo Jiya, Professor Iyabo Obasanjo and Senator Olubiyi Fadeyi.
Pantami’s case already before court
In Gombe State, the case involving former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Professor Isa Ali Pantami, predates the Supreme Court judgment.
A Federal High Court had nullified the PDP governorship primary that produced Pantami and ordered the party to conduct a fresh exercise in accordance with its constitution, guidelines and applicable electoral laws. The court also barred Pantami from continuing to present himself as the party’s candidate.
The PDP has fixed Tuesday (tomorrow) September 29 for the fresh governorship primary, with Pantami, Khamisu Ahmed.
Mailantarki and Usman Aliyu Garry cleared to participate.
Pantami’s case is, therefore, not a consequence of the Supreme Court judgment alone. It is already governed by a separate Federal High Court order.
His movement into the PDP after failing to secure the APC governorship ticket had featured in the dispute over the earlier primary, including questions around the process through which he emerged as the party’s candidate.
The fresh exercise now provides another opportunity for the party to establish compliance with the applicable membership and nomination requirements.
Mustapha, Jiya face register questions
Questions have also been raised over the PDP senatorial candidacies of Senator Saliu Mustapha in Kwara Central and Kolo Jiya in Kwara North.
Both politicians were previously associated with the APC before moving into the PDP camp, backed by the Saraki-led G15 alliance, which is working with the FCT Minister Nyesom Wike-led Rainbow Coalition.
The central questions concerned whether their names appeared on the PDP membership register submitted to INEC within the prescribed period and whether waivers granted them were sufficient to qualify them for participation in the party’s nomination process.
The Kwara PDP has rejected suggestions that the Supreme Court judgment automatically invalidated their candidacies.
The party said Mustapha did not participate in the earlier PDP senatorial primary and became the candidate after the withdrawal of the initial nominee. 
It also maintained that the affected new members obtained the required waivers before taking part in party activities.
The PDP maintains that the waivers regularised their membership and made them eligible for the relevant processes.
Any challenge, however, would turn on the documentary record; the PDP register submitted to INEC, its date of submission, the terms of the waivers and the process through which each candidate emerged.
Iyabo Obasanjo’s return under scrutiny
The candidacy of Dr Iyabo Obasanjo in Ogun Central has also come under scrutiny, following the judgment.
Obasanjo resigned from the APC on May 31, 2026, after losing the party’s governorship ticket, returned to the PDP on June 15 and was presented as its Ogun Central senatorial candidate two days later.
The timing has prompted questions over whether her name was contained in the PDP register submitted to INEC at least 21 days before the relevant nomination exercise.
There is, however, no Supreme Court ruling directly disqualifying Obasanjo.
Her media aide, Dr Odun Agbalajobi, rejected suggestions that the judgment had invalidated her candidacy.
“Senator Iyabo Obasanjo was not a party to that case,” her media aide said, adding that the judgment did not issue any order disqualifying her from contesting the Ogun Central senatorial election.
A PDP chieftain in Ogun, Adeoye Adewale Adeniran, also accused the APC of twisting the judgment in relation to Obasanjo’s candidacy.
“The APC is twisting the Supreme Court judgment to stop Iyabo Obasanjo,” Adeniran said, accusing the opposition of using misinformation and political propaganda over her eligibility.
Those are political claims and do not constitute a judicial finding on Obasanjo’s eligibility.
Fadeyi rejects disqualification claim
In Osun, Senator Olubiyi Fadeyi has rejected reports that the Supreme Court judgment had ended his bid to return to the Senate.
Fadeyi said no court had issued an order disqualifying him and described reports to that effect as speculative.
“For clarity sake, there is no clear evidence on Fadeyi’s disqualification from any court sitting, hence, the report of his alleged disqualification remains speculative and unfounded,” Fadeyi said.
He also defended the process through which he obtained the PDP ticket.
“The processes to bestow the PDP ticket on Senator Olubiyi Fadeyi for second term in office is clear, legal and approved by all relevant party executives,” he said.
Fadeyi further maintained that the PDP complied with the electoral law and its own rules.
“The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP followed the provisions of electoral law and everything was done in accordance with the law and party’s laid down rules,” he said.
The Supreme Court made no specific finding concerning Fadeyi’s membership status or nomination.
The emerging disputes will, therefore, turn on the records behind individual nominations rather than on the Supreme Court judgment as an automatic disqualification order.
The critical documents are the membership registers submitted to INEC, their dates of submission, any waivers granted to new members and the records showing how candidates emerged through the relevant primary or consensus process.
Where those records establish non-compliance, they could provide grounds for candidate-specific litigation. Until such a defect is established, political strategists believe the Supreme Court ruling itself does not invalidate the PDP nominations.
Other opposition parties’ candidates that appear disqualified include formee IGP Adamu Idris, SDP; Nasarawa; Abdulrahman Haske, APM, Adamawa; Sen. Shehu Buba, PRP, Bauchi; Lawal Daura, APM, Seyi Makinde’s running mate; and Farouk Mustapha, APC, Bauchi deputy governorship candidate.

items.content:
International footballer Faiq Bolkiah, widely regarded as the world’s richest footballer, has become a free agent after his contract with Thai League 1 side Ratchaburi FC expired.
The 28-year-old Bruneian winger remains committed to pursuing a professional football career despite coming from a royal family with an estimated fortune of more than $20 billion.
Bolkiah’s wealth dwarfs that of even the sport’s biggest stars. Forbes currently estimates Cristiano Ronaldo’s net worth at around $1.2 billion and Lionel Messi’s at $1.1 billion, making Bolkiah’s reported family fortune many times larger than the personal wealth of either superstar.
Bolkiah is the son of Prince Jefri Bolkiah and nephew of Brunei’s Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah. Despite his privileged background, he has spent much of his life pursuing football professionally.
Born in Los Angeles and raised in England, Bolkiah came through the youth systems of Southampton, Chelsea, and Leicester City before moving into senior football with Portuguese club Maritimo.
He later moved to Southeast Asia, spending two seasons at Chonburi FC before joining Ratchaburi in 2023. He made 23 appearances for the club and scored two goals.
Bolkiah has also represented Brunei at international level and captains his country. With his Ratchaburi contract now expired, he is assessing opportunities with clubs in other leagues as he looks to continue his football career.

items.content: Washington DC: United States President Donald Trump expressed confidence that the conflict with Iran will be won "very soon," while acknowledging that fresh military strikes ahead of the US midterm elections are "possible."Speaking to Fox News on the sidelines of the PGA Tour Presidents Cup on Sunday (local time), Trump said that an end to the confrontation would cause global oil prices to fall sharply, reiterating that denying Tehran a nuclear weapon is the primary American objective.Also Read: Iran ready for ‘doomsday war’ with US, foreign minister says after Trump rejects ceasefire"I think what's going to happen is we're going to win this war very soon, and as soon as we win it, the oil will go down, way down to what it was before the war," Trump told Fox News.When asked specifically whether military strikes could resume before the upcoming midterm elections, Trump declined to take the option off the table."I don't want to say that. I don't want to say that. I mean, it's possible, but I just don't want to say that," Trump said.Emphasising the core focus of US policy, he added, "And the key is, Iran will not have a nuclear weapon," noting that nuclear deterrence was "key to the whole thing."When asked about 'Operation Economic Outcast' and whether the US is succeeding through military pressure or economic sanctions, Trump asserted that the US is making progress on both fronts."I think both. I think we'll win it both ways. We've already won it really from a military standpoint," Trump said, adding, "But that doesn't mean we've stopped that."Speaking on the impact of economic pressure, Trump claimed that Iran's economy has been completely dismantled."We're certainly winning it very big. If you look at their economy, it's gone. They have no economy," Trump said.Describing the collapse of Iran's currency and soaring domestic costs, he stated, "The value of their money is, as they say, valueless. We have inflation. They have inflation now of close to 300%. I heard 318% as of this morning. 300, meaning their money is shot, their economy is shot, their military is shot. They're in trouble."Also Read: Trump rejects Iran’s 7-day ceasefire proposal, expects bombing to resume after US midterms: ReportMeanwhile, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi, in an interview with NBC News' "Meet the Press" earlier today, said his country is ready for a "doomsday war" with the US after President Donald Trump publicly rejected Tehran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.In the interview with NBC News, Araghchi said, "We are fully prepared for the war to be resumed. We stand firm in the face of any new aggression, even if it comes to a doomsday war. We don't care about U.S. midterm elections. We care about our national interests. At the same time, we stand ready for diplomacy. It is up to President Trump to choose."Reacting to Trump's public rejection, Araghchi pointed out that the rejection had not been formally communicated to Tehran through designated diplomatic channels.He reiterated that Iran remains willing to reopen the maritime corridor as part of a negotiated settlement to end the hostilities. "We want our monies, our assets, which are illegally frozen, to be released. We want to be able to sell our oil," Araghchi said, noting that these terms mirrored a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) signed in June for a temporary ceasefire, which collapsed shortly thereafter following reciprocal strikes."If you ask us, there is no reason why we should go back to diplomacy," Araghchi remarked. "But I am still trying diplomacy because I think we shouldn't miss any chance for peace."

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Apple resmi merilis macOS 27 Golden Gate pada 14 September 2026 sebagai sistem operasi terbaru untuk perangkat Mac. Dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya, update ini tidak hanya membawa penyegaran tampilan lewat Liquid Glass, tetapi juga memperluas integrasi Apple Intelligence ke berbagai bagian sistem.
Salah satu perubahan terbesar hadir melalui Siri generasi baru yang kini mendapatkan kemampuan AI lebih luas. Apple juga menghadirkan Visual Intelligence, peningkatan Shortcuts, serta berbagai fitur berbasis AI di Safari, Photos, Mail, Messages, dan sejumlah aplikasi lainnya. Di sisi lain, macOS 27 juga menjadi penanda penting dalam transisi Apple karena sistem operasi ini hanya mendukung Mac dengan Apple Silicon.
Baca Juga: iPadOS 27 Bikin iPad Jadul Lebih Kencang, Kompatibel Untuk Tablet Rilisan 2020
Liquid Glass Mendapat Penyempurnaan
Liquid Glass kini semakin rapih dan sempurna (Louis/Gizmologi)
Secara visual, macOS 27 Golden Gate masih mempertahankan bahasa desain Liquid Glass yang pertama kali diperkenalkan pada generasi sebelumnya. Namun, Apple melakukan sejumlah penyempurnaan untuk meningkatkan keterbacaan dan konsistensi antarmuka. Pengguna kini dapat mengatur tampilan Liquid Glass, mulai dari material yang lebih transparan hingga tampilan yang lebih tinted.
Apple juga memperbarui toolbar, sidebar, ikon aplikasi, serta sejumlah elemen antarmuka lainnya. Perubahan tersebut membuat tampilan macOS tetap mempertahankan karakter transparan dan dinamis, tetapi dengan kontras yang lebih baik sehingga informasi di layar lebih mudah dibaca.
Di luar tampilan, Apple turut melakukan optimasi pada performa sistem. Beberapa peningkatan menyasar AirDrop, network file browsing, Safari, Spotlight, penggunaan memori, hingga responsivitas sistem. Pengguna yang menggunakan monitor ultrawide juga mendapatkan dukungan resolusi dan refresh rate yang lebih tinggi pada konfigurasi tertentu.
Siri AI Jadi Salah Satu Perubahan Terbesar
Pembaruan terkait Siri AI yang menjadi lebih cerdas (Louis/Gizmologi)
Perhatian utama pada macOS 27 Golden Gate datang dari Siri AI. Apple menghadirkan Siri dengan kemampuan percakapan yang lebih luas, pemahaman konteks personal, serta kemampuan membantu pengguna melakukan berbagai tindakan lintas aplikasi. Siri juga mendapatkan aplikasi khusus dengan riwayat percakapan yang dapat disinkronkan melalui ekosistem Apple.
Salah satu kemampuan yang cukup menarik adalah Personal Context. Dengan fitur ini, Siri dapat menggunakan informasi yang tersedia di perangkat, termasuk dari aplikasi seperti Mail, Messages, dan Photos, untuk memahami permintaan yang membutuhkan konteks lebih luas. Siri juga dapat membantu menulis, memberikan masukan terhadap teks, hingga menyesuaikan gaya penulisan melalui fitur Write with Siri.
Apple turut mengintegrasikan AI dengan Spotlight. Pengguna dapat memanggil Siri langsung melalui Spotlight untuk mengajukan pertanyaan atau meminta bantuan tanpa harus membuka aplikasi secara terpisah. Namun, kemampuan Siri AI tersebut masih berstatus beta dan ketersediaannya bergantung pada bahasa, wilayah, serta perangkat yang digunakan.
Visual Intelligence & AI Mulai Masuk ke Berbagai Aplikasi
Visual Intelligence dengan Siri AI (Louis/Gizmologi)
Selain Siri, macOS 27 Golden Gate membawa Visual Intelligence ke Mac. Fitur ini memungkinkan pengguna memilih konten yang tampil di layar dan meminta sistem untuk menganalisisnya. Pengguna dapat memanfaatkan kemampuan tersebut untuk memahami gambar, teks, atau informasi tertentu yang sedang ditampilkan.
Apple juga memperluas penggunaan AI ke aplikasi lain. Photos mendapatkan kemampuan seperti Spatial Reframing dan Extend untuk membantu mengubah komposisi maupun memperluas area foto. Clean Up juga mendapatkan peningkatan untuk menghapus objek yang mengganggu dari gambar.
Di Safari, Apple menghadirkan fitur seperti pengelompokan tab otomatis berdasarkan topik serta Notify Me untuk memantau perubahan tertentu pada sebuah halaman. Sementara itu, Passwords dapat membantu pengguna menangani beberapa masalah keamanan akun, termasuk perubahan password tertentu.
Shortcuts juga mendapatkan perhatian melalui kemampuan membuat workflow menggunakan bahasa natural. Pengguna cukup menjelaskan tindakan yang ingin dilakukan dan sistem dapat membantu menyusun Shortcut tersebut. Perubahan ini menunjukkan bagaimana Apple mulai menggabungkan AI dengan otomatisasi, bukan hanya menjadikannya sebagai chatbot.
Mail, Messages, Calendar dan Produktivitas Ikut Diperbarui
Pembaruan UI Calendar (Louis/Gizmologi)
Apple juga memperluas integrasi AI ke aplikasi produktivitas. Calendar mendapatkan kemampuan untuk membantu membuat atau mengedit agenda berdasarkan deskripsi natural. Mail mendapatkan pencarian yang lebih relevan dengan sistem ranking yang membantu menempatkan pesan paling sesuai di posisi teratas.
Messages juga mendapatkan contextual suggestions yang dapat memberikan opsi tindakan berdasarkan isi percakapan. Dengan pendekatan tersebut, pengguna tidak selalu perlu berpindah aplikasi ketika ingin melakukan tindakan yang berkaitan dengan informasi dalam sebuah pesan.
Dari sisi aksesibilitas, Apple meningkatkan VoiceOver dan kemampuan sistem dalam memberikan deskripsi terhadap konten visual. macOS 27 Golden Gate juga membawa sejumlah kontrol baru untuk keamanan anak, termasuk Ask to Browse dan pengaturan komunikasi serta waktu penggunaan perangkat.
macOS 27 Akhiri Era Intel dan Mulai Tinggalkan Rosetta
(Louis/Gizmologi)
Di balik seluruh fitur tersebut, macOS 27 juga menjadi tonggak penting bagi transisi Apple menuju Apple Silicon. Sistem operasi ini hanya kompatibel dengan Mac yang menggunakan chip Apple Silicon, sehingga Mac berbasis Intel berhenti mendapatkan versi macOS terbaru setelah macOS Tahoe 26.
Apple juga mulai mengakhiri ketergantungannya terhadap Rosetta. macOS 27 menjadi versi terakhir yang mendukung Rosetta untuk menjalankan aplikasi Intel pada Apple Silicon secara umum. Meski demikian, Apple masih mempertahankan dukungan tertentu untuk game lama yang bergantung pada framework berbasis Intel.
Dengan demikian, macOS 27 bukan sekadar pembaruan tahunan untuk Mac. Apple mulai menempatkan Apple Intelligence lebih dalam ke sistem operasi, sementara transisi dari Intel ke Apple Silicon memasuki tahap akhir. Saat ini Apple bahkan sudah menguji macOS 27.2 melalui developer beta, meskipun belum ada indikasi bahwa versi tersebut membawa perubahan besar yang sudah diumumkan untuk pengguna umum.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Enewaridideke Ekanpou
A tide is a tide anywhere, but a tide assumes connotative colours when it becomes triangular in build and action. Like a cumulonimbus cloud endowed with both positive and negative potentials, there must be something hidden behind a triangular tide. There must be something equally iconographic about a triangular tide too when viewed imagistically. The iconography of a triangular tide tells a deeper story best understood by students of mysticism, particularly when it is symbolically carved around the Governor of Delta State, Sheriff Oborevwori.
Governor Oborevwori is a product of two oppositional political forces that deployed ‘capacitation’ and ‘incapacitation’ as political weapons of goal realisation in 2023. Neither of these two oppositional political forces was disposed to being divorced from its ideological convictions, which daily bred a large following—sometimes within the same political formation that shelters all. Like barnacles stuck to mangrove roots, these two oppositional political forces firmly held and pursued their ideological persuasions without distractions in 2023. It had the echoes of a furious flood devotedly at work within its geographically marked time and space.
The political forces of capacitation democratically sought to enthrone Oborevwori as governor of Delta State because they believed he had the needed administrative magic wand to end the political plagues of Deltans. Contrarily, while the visionary forces of capacitation were strategically at work, the forces of incapacitation also sought to terminate this widely applauded governorship dream with an imaginative creation that Oborevwori had educational deficiencies which demanded disqualification from the governorship race. Upon these imagined deficiencies, the struggle to stop him resulted in 38 lawsuits. These 38 lawsuits were vigorously pursued to crumble his political ambition. Oborevwori emerged from this deliberately muddied fight stronger and healthier than even the legendary phoenix and the honey badger (ratel). From the politically muddied waters created to disable him politically, Governor Oborevwori emerged a stainless creature who had a great dream for Deltans like Lee Kuan Yew of Singapore.
From the tussle between the two oppositional political forces in the rhetorically embellished, turgid scramble for political space in 2023, Oborevwori became the emergent political third force. However, unlike Wole Soyinka’s ‘third force’, memorably captured in The Man Died, which was intellectually built in the days of the Nigerian Civil War of 1967–70 to centre on the utilisation of “the ensuing military stalemate to repudiate and end both the secession of Biafra and the genocide-consolidated dictatorship of the Army” (19), Governor Oborevwori’s third force was ideologically envisioned to end political persecution, political marginalisation and developmental blackout in Delta State. The beloved preoccupation of Governor Oborevwori was that no Deltan must be serpentined by political persecution and developmental blackout.
Stainless and stronger from the vindictively muddied waters created by the forces of incapacitation, a tide now flows around Governor Oborevwori. The tide has a triangular formation that terminates in the unity of three forces. These three forces carry theological echoes of the biblical Trinity of God the Father, God the Son and God the Holy Spirit. Pulled irresistibly like a furious flood in its geographically and geometrically marked season, the triangular tidal flow is today driven unstoppably by the infrastructural, educational and ideological radiance of Governor Oborevwori in his undistracted pursuit of his vision of the rapid development of Delta State in all spheres of human engagement.
Captivated by Oborevwori’s visible developmental radiance, which is devoid of discrimination in its spread, Delta Central, Delta North and Delta South Senatorial Districts have ideologically forged a trinity of support from their own foundry. This forged trinity of support is patterned theologically upon the Trinity of God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. This is a stirring allegorical appropriation of a biblical discourse comfortably applied to politics!
Activated by the formation of a trinity of support from their tripartite foundry, a certain triangular tide has begun a journey of victory from the three senatorial districts of Delta State. The triangular tide journeys from the north, south and central to Osubi. From Osubi, it journeys to Asaba. Asaba is seen as the termination point of the triangular tide. Unmistakably outlined in the tidal flow is the fact that there are no longer political forces of incapacitation in Delta State politics in 2027. This is comprehensively communicated by the trinity of the three senatorial districts in Delta State. For Governor Oborevwori in 2027, it would be a mere effortless enactment of the democratic ritual of casting the votes for him without any waiting oppositional tide lurking around any of the senatorial districts. The triangular tide in Delta State has journeyed to all the brooks, canals, rivers and tributaries.
A people piloted by discernment in any political engagement know that any APC dugout canoe journeying to Asaba for Oborevwori or for any other candidate would not encounter the threat of navigational disaster because all the creeks, brooks, canals, rivers and tributaries have been sufficiently alerted and aligned by the triangular tide, which had long carried out reconnaissance and feasibility operations. Governor Oborevwori’s radiant performance record of commitment to bursary awards and scholarships to Delta State students alone through the Delta State Bursary and Scholarship Board from 2023 to 2026 can enfeeble, disable and dismantle any waiting navigational challenge in the river of politics in Delta State in 2027. What about the recent provision of 50 fishing boats, 15-horsepower Yamaha outboard engines and fishing nets to fishermen in Warri South, Warri North and Warri South-West Local Government Areas of Delta State by Governor Oborevwori as quintessential components of his broader vision of empowerment for Deltans?
Regulated by the triangular tide, which is geographically and geometrically marked in Delta South, Central and North Senatorial Districts, the electoral victory of Governor Oborevwori in 2027—as respectively echoed by Dr Julius Takeme, the Executive Chairman of Burutu Council, and other political heavyweights during the gathering of the Delta South Senatorial District at Brown Hill Event Centre in Warri on September 10, 2026—is a concluded matter. To align correspondingly with this tidal allegory, traditional rulers of Urhobo extraction have publicly pronounced Governor Oborevwori as the 2027 sole governorship candidate in the Delta Central Senatorial District. This is inexorably the course steadily taken by the triangular tide in all three senatorial districts in Delta State.
Incontrovertibly, a matter that allegorically enjoys the imprimatur and blessings of the Trinity of God the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, imagistically suggested and emblazoned by a triangular tide, is beyond the puny incursions of mortals who are habitually excited by spoiler tasks lethally reinforced with sustained psychological warfare on the political front.
•Dr Ekanpou writes from Akparemogbene, Delta State

items.title: Policybazaar, Turtlemint Feel The Squeeze
items.summary:

items.author: Bismah Malik
items.content:
Riya, 27, wants to buy her first family-floater health cover on Policybazaar. But before she sees a single price, the app asks for her name, phone number and city.
Within minutes, her phone starts ringing. She settles on a plan with an annual premium of ₹20,000.
Riya never sees the other half of the transaction. In this case, the insurer, the one that Riya selected, pays Policybazaar a small commission from the ₹20,000 premium.
And of course, there could be other commissions involved such as renewal or lack of claims, but this is primarily the economic model behind digital insurance distribution.
All that could change if the insurance regulator has its way. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI) released a consultation paper on September 23, looking to reintroduce commission caps on premia paid by first-time policy buyers and customers renewing policies.
While the likes of Policybazaar, Paytm, PhonePe and other insurance distributors have charged commissions from insurers as a percentage of the gross premia thus far, the IRDAI’s proposals could bring in commission caps across health, term (life) and motor insurance products.
For life insurers, total expenses of management policies would be capped at 12.5% of premium within five years, general insurers’ at 20%, as against 30% earlier.
In addition, IRDAI has also taken note of the practice of distributors seeking personal details of prospective customers before revealing the relevant policies, their terms and pricing. IRDAI called this a dark pattern on insurance apps along with other practices which it labelled mis-selling.
The regulator’s rationale is that there has been a whopping jump of payouts to distributors between FY23 and FY25 to the tune of 125%, whereas new business premiums only rose by 28% in the same period. The value of commissions more than doubled from ₹48,000 Cr in FY21 to ₹1.08 Lakh Cr in FY25.
Thus, the regulator is of the opinion that commissions and payouts to distributors have outpaced premium growth, which has created a high-cost, commission-led insurance model that is not sustainable.
Policybazaar’s Tough Week
When it comes to individual companies, PolicyBazaar’s net profit nearly doubled YoY to ₹162.9 Cr in the June quarter (Q1 FY27) from ₹84.7 Cr in the same quarter last year.
Operating revenue also jumped 40% YoY to ₹1,888.3 Cr in the quarter under review from ₹1,348 Cr in Q1 FY26
In Q1 FY27, Policybazaar parent PB Fintech said the blended take-rate (average commission in a given period) on the core online insurance was 18.5%.
If implemented, the IRDAI commission caps would dent the revenue severely. Brokerage Jefferies estimates that PolicyBazaar’s commissions on new health cover could likely see a 33%-50% drop.
Analysts have framed these changes as a long-term benefit to the insurance industry, because insurers can pass on the savings from commission to customers and this could bring premiums down across the industry. This should ideally bring more individuals into the insurance net.
On the other hand, Policybazaar, Turtlemint and the likes are wary of any changes to the existing model. On an analyst call on Thursday, Policybazaar said it earns less than an insurance agent on the same policy. The management was responding to shareholders after the PB Fintech stock plummeted by 34-36% and hit its 52-week lows,
PB Fintech said the immediate impact from the proposed IRDAI guidelines ”is quite extreme” but it also said that the stock erosion is overblown. PB Fintech’s life and non-life insurance business is split equally (50:50) in terms of revenue, and it expects more impact on the non-life insurance business from the proposed changes.
The IRDAI is particularly going after commissions on renewals. PB Fintech’s renewal revenue hit ₹1,003 Cr in Q1 FY27, up 55% YoY and this is its highest-margin revenue stream. Notably, health insurance was its fastest-growing product, with new premium collections up 59% YoY in Q1 FY27.
The draft guidelines essentially hit the growth engine of Policybazaar. The management, however, said it is not yet clear whether the caps would apply to existing policies or only new ones.
The capping of commissions would most likely hit the company’s bottomline immediately.
According to the management commentary, the company sees its life insurance products business to be more resilient whereas its non-life business could be down by 25% to 33%.
On the brighter side, PB Fintech’s management expects volumes to rise 15–20% if general insurance commissions fall 60%, which would soften the hit. But that depends on insurers passing the savings on to customers, which management wants IRDAI to ensure with further regulation.
What The Street Is Saying
PB Fintech closed Thursday down 35.98% at ₹1,210 on the BSE, at its lower price band, with its market cap down to ₹55,993 Cr. This was its steepest single-day fall since listing. Turtlemint closed at its 20% lower circuit at ₹109.04.
The two new-age stocks and other legacy insurance players bled heaviest on Thursday with investors continuing to exit their positions even on Friday, two days after IRDAI’s announcement.
How the tables have turned. Only a month ago, Bernstein was among PB Fintech’s biggest bulls. In its August note, Bernstein gave an outperform rating to PB with a ₹2,310 target price.
Now, it’s calling the proposed commission cuts far more severe than expected, saying PB Fintech will be the most impacted. Bernstein has concerns for PB’s health and motor insurance unit economics, and estimates that current call centre costs cannot hold up at these take-rates.
Jefferies estimated that a 10% cut in new business commission rates means a 10–12% fall in earnings for PB Fintech, Turtlemint and other insurance distributors. Similarly, Citi said that distribution economics could compress 70–90% in several high-margin categories. Macquarie, HSBC and Emkay all flagged PB Fintech as among the most exposed.
PB Fintech claimed there will be no impact in the ongoing financial year, but expects FY28 to be a volatile fiscal year. It aims to get earnings back on track by FY29, shifting from “passionate growth” to “rational growth”.
While brokerages focused on PB Fintech, Turtlemint might be even worse off.
The major challenge surrounding Turtlemint is its revenue concentration with general insurance contributing to nearly 90% of its revenues in Q1 FY27
With the draft guidelines suggesting no commissions for distribution on new-vehicle third party insurance and proposing a capping at 5% on own-damage policies, the core revenue base of Turtlemint will experience a major hit.
Additionally, unlike Policybazaar, Turtlemint doesn’t sell to customers directly.
Its partners sell through the Turtlemint app, with commissions being shared between Turtlemint and these partners. The acquisition and payment to these partners alone constituted 77.45% of total expenses before the IPO, and Turtlemint’s disclosures after listing are not clear on this expense.
But with the commission pool potentially shrinking, Turtlemint’s very model is under threat.
The Cushion For Go Digit And Acko
While stocks of insurance distributors fell, Go Digit stood to gain. The company’s stock gained 6.21% in the week even as PB Fintech and Turtlemint fell by over 30% each.
Unlike Policybazaar and Turtlemint, Go Digit and Acko are not distributors but insurers and can actually sell policies directly to individuals, or through aggregators like PB Fintech, Paytm, PhonePe and other apps.
For Go Digit, motor insurance constitutes a significant portion of its Gross Written Premium. Motor insurance reported a 5.3% YoY increase in net premium earned (NPE) to ₹1,510.1 Cr in Q1 FY27, up from ₹1,430 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year.
If the new guidelines are implemented, it is expected that like many insurers, Go Digit’s commission expenses will reduce substantially which would add to its profits, but it could lose out on some topline with the price of premiums potentially dropping.
What could pose a big problem is their dependence on digital distributors channels which can impact the company in the long term, if distributors turn commission hungry and push policies from other insurers which have higher premiums in comparison to Go Digit or Acko, both of which compete on cost thanks to their tech-first approach.
Acko is aiming to list next year at a H1 2027 at a $2 Bn-$2.5 Bn valuation, and its insurance arm turned profitable in FY26. Although its pitch has always been direct selling, much of its growth has come through embedded partnerships on consumer apps, and brand-value payments that now count as commission. Acko also risks some impact on its business due to dependence on digital channels for policy distribution.
While the final comments on the suggested IRDAI regulations will come by October 25, 2026, most of the industry expects a pushback by the insurance distributors and insurers alike.
PB Fintech has stated that it will seriously consider becoming an insurer itself, and is exploring its own insurance and reinsurance products on the back of proposed changes in the distribution business.
That echoes PB Fintech chairman Yashish Dahiya’s earlier warning that hard caps is a potential existential threat to distributors. And soon this threat could be a reality.
MARKETS WATCH: NEW ISSUES, POST-IPO JOURNEY & MORE
Moneyview IPO Subscribed 6X By Day 2: Digital lender Moneyview’s ₹1,092 Cr IPO was subscribed 6.01X at the end of the second day, with non-institutional investors bidding 15.41X and retail 5.18X. QIBs have so far bid for just 0.25X of their quota. The issue closes on September 28, with listing tentatively set for October 1.
Snapdeal Parent AceVector Opens IPO After ₹189 Cr Anchor Round: AceVector raised ₹189 Cr from anchor investors at ₹32 a share ahead of its ₹420 Cr IPO, with only two domestic mutual funds taking part. The issue was subscribed 23% on day one and closes on September 29.
Aequs To Raise ₹650 Cr Via Preferential Issue: The contract manufacturer will issue warrants to its promoter to fund capacity expansion across its aerospace and consumer businesses, including its Hosur facility. Shareholders will vote on the proposal at an EGM on October 22.
Spinny Files Confidential DRHP: The used-car marketplace has confidentially filed its draft IPO papers with SEBI and is looking to raise ₹2,500 Cr to ₹3,000 Cr through a mix of fresh issue and offer for sale.
[Edited By Nikhil Subramaniam]

items.title: 2026 WTD: TCI introduces two tourism destinations in Badagry
items.summary:
By Onyeka Ezike
Tourists Club International (TCI) has announced the establishment of two new tourism destinations in Badagry, Lagos State—the Tourists Club International Art Gallery and the Tourists Club International Forest Reserve.
The announcement was made on Sunday to commemorate the 2026 World Tourism Day, whose theme is “Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism.”
The theme highlights the growing influence of digital platforms and artificial intelligence on how travellers discover destinations, plan journeys and experience tourism. The official global celebration is being hosted by El Salvador.
