items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Spacetech startup GalaxEye has secured ₹63.84 Cr in financial support under the Centre’s Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund to develop its next-generation multisensor satellite technology.
The Technology Development Board (TDB), under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), has signed an agreement with the Bengaluru-based startup to provide the support through optionally convertible debentures.
The project has a total approved cost of ₹247.69 Cr, the Centre said in a statement. It aims to develop an indigenous satellite capable of OptoSAR imaging at a resolution finer than 0.5 metres. The project will take the technology from Technology Readiness Level (TRL) 6 to TRL 9, progressing from a demonstrated prototype towards a system proven in operation.
GalaxEye’s technology combines synthetic aperture radar (SAR) and electro-optical (EO) imaging. While optical imaging can be affected by cloud cover and lighting conditions, SAR can capture images through clouds and without daylight. By combining the two, the startup aims to provide high-resolution Earth observation across different weather and lighting conditions.
The proposed satellite’s applications include wide-area and long-range surveillance, detection of people and vehicles, and target classification, the government said.
“The agreement with GalaxEye reflects TDB’s focus on enabling indigenous capabilities in emerging space technologies and supporting their journey towards commercialisation,” TDB secretary Rajesh Kumar Pathak said.
GalaxEye Builds Its Satellite Capabilities
Founded in 2021 by Suyash Singh, Denil Chawda, Kishan Thakkar, Pranit Mehta, and Rakshit Bhatt, GalaxEye builds multi-sensor earth observation satellites designed to provide high-resolution imaging and geospatial intelligence catering to sectors such as defence, agriculture, infrastructure and disaster management.
The startup raised ₹44.2 Cr as part of an ongoing Series A round earlier this year, with investors including Speciale Invest, Rainmatter, MV Core and Mounttech Growth Fund. The IIT Madras-incubated startup has raised nearly $27 Mn in funding to date from investors like Speciale Invest, Mela Ventures, and Anicut Capital.
The startup claims to be building the world’s first multi-sensor earth observation satellite and aims to deploy a constellation of indigenous micro-satellites with data fusion capabilities.
Earlier this month, GalaxEye received a US patent for satellite imaging technology, the first of its kind for an Indian spacetech startup. The patent covers the core architecture behind the startup’s proprietary OptoSAR technology.
This came after the startup launched its maiden OptoSAR satellite under ‘Mission Drishti’ in May, which was touted as India’s largest privately built earth observation satellite and the world’s first imaging satellite using OptoSAR. However, it lost communication with the satellite in July due to an anomaly linked to a geomagnetic solar storm.
The startup is now targeting the launch of two new OptoSAR satellites in the next two years while expanding its in-house capabilities to further strengthen quality, reliability, and execution.
Spacetech Funding Enters New Phase
The agreement adds to support for spacetech startups under the Centre’s ₹1 Lakh Cr RDI Fund, approved in July 2025 to increase private-sector participation in research, development, and innovation.
The fund is designed to finance technology development and commercialisation through long-term capital. It operates through a two-tier structure, with the Anusandhan National Research Foundation acting as the first-level custodian and institutions such as TDB and the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council serving as second-level fund managers.
According to the government statement, TDB has approved 22 projects with a combined project cost of ₹4,744 Cr, involving ₹2,192 Cr in RDI support.
GalaxEye joins other spacetech startups backed under the programme. In May, Dhruva Space secured ₹105 Cr for Project Garud, which aims to develop a standardised satellite platform for large-scale deployments across telecom, earth observation, and national security applications.
The public funding comes alongside larger private investments in the sector. Indian spacetech startups have raised nearly $250 Mn in 2026 so far. These include Skyroot Aerospace’s $60 Mn round, which made it India’s first spacetech unicorn, and Pixxel’s $100 Mn Series C to expand satellite manufacturing and imaging capabilities.

items.title: Pintu Hadirkan Tokenized Stocks, Akses Saham Global Apple, Google, Tesla hingga Chevron
items.summary:
Akses terhadap saham perusahaan global kini tidak hanya menjadi urusan investor yang sudah terbiasa dengan pasar modal internasional. Pintu menghadirkan fitur tokenized stocks yang memungkinkan pengguna mendapatkan akses terhadap aset saham global melalui aplikasi Pintu.
Kehadiran fitur ini menarik karena membuka cara baru bagi investor Indonesia untuk mengikuti pergerakan perusahaan-perusahaan global. Dengan fitur ini, pengguna bisa mengakses saham Chevron, Apple, Google, Tesla, Meta berbagai perusahaan global terkemuka lainnya yang melantai di bursa saham.
Namun, tokenized stocks bukan sekadar mengganti bentuk saham menjadi token. Ada sejumlah aspek yang perlu dipahami, mulai dari aset yang menjadi dasar token, hak investor, likuiditas, biaya, hingga risiko produknya. Dengan kata lain, kemudahan akses tidak serta-merta berarti mekanismenya sama dengan membeli saham secara langsung di bursa.

Apa Itu Tokenized Stocks?
items.author: Bambang Dwi Atmoko
items.content:
Akses terhadap saham perusahaan global kini tidak hanya menjadi urusan investor yang sudah terbiasa dengan pasar modal internasional. Pintu menghadirkan fitur tokenized stocks yang memungkinkan pengguna mendapatkan akses terhadap aset saham global melalui aplikasi Pintu.
Kehadiran fitur ini menarik karena membuka cara baru bagi investor Indonesia untuk mengikuti pergerakan perusahaan-perusahaan global. Dengan fitur ini, pengguna bisa mengakses saham Chevron, Apple, Google, Tesla, Meta berbagai perusahaan global terkemuka lainnya yang melantai di bursa saham.
Namun, tokenized stocks bukan sekadar mengganti bentuk saham menjadi token. Ada sejumlah aspek yang perlu dipahami, mulai dari aset yang menjadi dasar token, hak investor, likuiditas, biaya, hingga risiko produknya. Dengan kata lain, kemudahan akses tidak serta-merta berarti mekanismenya sama dengan membeli saham secara langsung di bursa.
Baca juga: 5 Cara Trading Futures Pakai PINTU Secara Aman dan Mudah
Apa Itu Tokenized Stocks?
Tokenized stocks adalah representasi digital dari saham perusahaan publik yang diterbitkan dalam bentuk token di atas jaringan blockchain. Konsep ini memungkinkan investor di berbagai negara, termasuk Indonesia, memiliki eksposur terhadap saham perusahaan besar Amerika Serikat seperti Nvidia, Amazon, Meta, Chevron dan lainnya tanpa harus membuka rekening broker luar negeri.
Sederhananya, saham tertokenisasi merupakan token digital yang nilainya mengacu pada harga saham asli di bursa tradisional. Setiap token biasanya didukung oleh saham fisik yang disimpan oleh kustodian atau lembaga keuangan teregulasi, sehingga pergerakan harga token mengikuti pergerakan harga saham acuannya. 
Melalui fitur ini, pengguna Pintu dapat mengakses saham perusahaan global melalui aplikasi tanpa harus menggunakan mekanisme pembelian saham secara langsung seperti pada pasar saham konvensional. Konsep tersebut menjadi menarik karena pasar saham global memiliki banyak perusahaan yang selama ini sulit dijangkau investor ritel Indonesia. Dengan tokenisasi, akses terhadap aset tersebut dapat diintegrasikan ke dalam ekosistem aset digital yang sudah digunakan pengguna.
Namun, investor tetap perlu memahami struktur produknya. Hal yang perlu diperhatikan antara lain underlying asset, hak yang melekat pada token, likuiditas, biaya, serta risiko yang mungkin berbeda dibandingkan kepemilikan saham secara langsung.
Karena itu, istilah tokenized stocks tidak sebaiknya langsung dipahami sebagai “saham biasa dalam bentuk digital”. Struktur dan hak investor perlu dilihat berdasarkan mekanisme produk yang ditawarkan.
Cara Kerja Tokenized Stocks
Ilustrasi trading (Foto: Sergeitokmakov/Pixabay)
Proses penerbitan tokenized stocks umumnya dimulai dari lembaga penerbit yang membeli saham asli di bursa AS, lalu menguncinya di kustodian sebagai jaminan. Setelah itu, token digital senilai saham tersebut diterbitkan di blockchain seperti Solana atau Ethereum, sehingga bisa diperjualbelikan oleh pengguna di seluruh dunia selama platform mendukung.
Karena berjalan di atas blockchain, transaksi token saham ini dapat diselesaikan hampir seketika tanpa proses kliring berhari-hari seperti di bursa konvensional. Sebagian platform bahkan menyediakan sesi perdagangan di luar jam bursa AS, termasuk saat akhir pekan, meski dengan likuiditas yang cenderung lebih tipis dibanding jam bursa aktif.
Dua nama yang paling sering muncul dalam ekosistem saham tertokenisasi adalah xStocks dan Ondo Finance. xStocks dikembangkan oleh Backed Finance asal Swiss dan telah mencatat volume transaksi on-chain lebih dari delapan miliar dolar AS. Token xStocks tersedia di beberapa jaringan blockchain seperti Solana, Ethereum, dan TON, dengan skema backing 1:1 dari kustodian teregulasi sehingga pengguna dapat menarik token ke dompet pribadi maupun menggunakannya di ekosistem DeFi.
Sementara itu, Ondo Global Markets tercatat sebagai penerbit terbesar di kategori ini berdasarkan total value locked, menembus satu miliar dolar AS dalam waktu kurang dari delapan bulan sejak diluncurkan pada September 2025. Ondo menawarkan lebih dari 260 saham dan ETF asal AS yang tersedia di berbagai jaringan blockchain, lengkap dengan mekanisme pelacakan total return termasuk dividen.
Saham Chevron yang Jadi Perhatian Investor
Salah satu contoh saham global yang patut dicermati adalah Chevron yang baru-baru ini menarik perhatian para investor. Chevron adalah perusahaan energi asal Amerika Serikat yang sahamnya diperdagangkan di New York Stock Exchange dengan ticker CVX.
Pada 15 September 2026, saham Chevron sempat mencapai US$217,78 dalam perdagangan intraday dan ditutup di US$217,77, yang menjadi level tertinggi 52 minggu terbaru. Namun, beberapa hari kemudian saham tersebut terkoreksi dan ditutup pada US$203,67 pada 21 September. Pergerakan tersebut memperlihatkan satu hal penting: akses yang lebih mudah terhadap saham global tidak menghilangkan risiko pasar.
Dalam kasus Chevron, pergerakan saham tidak terlepas dari dinamika industri energi global. Konflik geopolitik dan perubahan ekspektasi terhadap pasokan minyak dapat memengaruhi harga crude oil, yang kemudian menjadi salah satu faktor yang diperhatikan investor ketika menilai perusahaan energi.
Chevron juga memiliki sejumlah perkembangan bisnis yang menjadi perhatian pasar. Pada 2025, perusahaan mencatat produksi global sekitar 3,7 juta barel setara minyak per hari, naik 12% dibandingkan tahun sebelumnya. Peningkatan tersebut antara lain didorong oleh akuisisi Hess dan sejumlah proyek produksi di Kazakhstan, Permian Basin, serta Gulf of America.
Pada September 2026, Chevron juga mengumumkan kesepakatan baru dengan pemerintah Venezuela. Perusahaan berencana menginvestasikan lebih dari US$7 miliar selama lima tahun untuk memperluas operasi di negara tersebut dan meningkatkan produksi menjadi sekitar 600.000 barel per hari.
Bagi investor, perkembangan tersebut menunjukkan bahwa ketika mengakses saham global, yang dihadapi bukan hanya pergerakan harga di layar aplikasi. Kinerja perusahaan tetap dipengaruhi berbagai faktor, mulai dari kondisi industri, komoditas, strategi bisnis hingga geopolitik.
Apa yang Perlu Dipahami Investor?
Kemudahan mengakses saham global melalui tokenized stocks membuat pemahaman terhadap produk menjadi semakin penting.
Pertama, investor perlu mengetahui aset apa yang menjadi underlying dari token tersebut dan bagaimana hubungan antara token dengan aset yang mendasarinya.
Kedua, pahami hak yang diperoleh investor. Kepemilikan token tidak otomatis berarti seluruh hak yang melekat pada kepemilikan saham secara langsung juga berlaku dengan cara yang sama.
Ketiga, perhatikan likuiditas dan biaya. Harga aset global dapat bergerak cepat, sementara mekanisme transaksi tokenized stocks dapat memiliki karakteristik tersendiri.
Keempat, tetap perhitungkan risiko pasar dan nilai tukar. Perubahan harga saham global dapat menghasilkan keuntungan maupun kerugian, sementara aset yang menggunakan denominasi mata uang asing juga menghadirkan faktor kurs.
Hal ini penting karena contoh seperti Chevron menunjukkan bagaimana cepatnya kondisi pasar dapat berubah. Rekor harga yang tercapai pada satu titik tidak menjamin harga akan bertahan di level tersebut.
Bagaimanapun juga, tokenized stocks membawa pendekatan baru terhadap akses investasi global. Bagi investor Indonesia, nilai utamanya terletak pada kemudahan mendapatkan eksposur terhadap aset global melalui platform digital.
Namun, kemudahan tersebut tetap perlu diikuti pemahaman mengenai bagaimana produk bekerja. Sebelum bertransaksi, investor perlu membaca ketentuan produk, memahami underlying asset, hak yang diperoleh, biaya, likuiditas, serta risiko yang menyertainya.
Dengan begitu, tokenized stocks tidak hanya dilihat sebagai cara yang lebih praktis untuk mengakses saham global, tetapi juga sebagai instrumen yang perlu dipahami karakteristiknya sebelum digunakan.

items.author: Inc42 BrandLabs
items.content:
After the proliferation of AI adoption, enterprise India has started to ask whether its infrastructure is robust enough to survive the shift. With the country’s enterprise AI market expected to cross $71 Bn by 2030, boardroom mandates around AI are accelerating, cloud costs are spiralling, data pipelines are buckling under the weight of unstructured inputs, and CTOs are discovering that pilots that worked in isolation can collapse the moment they are pushed into production at scale.
Therefore, enterprises across sectors are moving beyond productivity tools into core product development and delivery processes, including coding copilots, automated testing, and AI-driven IT service management.
As a result, the conversation and its implementation are now shifting from experimentation to predictability, governance and cost control.
To unpack this shift, India’s leading tech voices joined Inc42 and Oracle for CTO Dialogues, featuring a roundtable on ‘Building The Infrastructure Backbone For AI At Scale’, followed by a fireside chat and a session exploring where enterprise AI strategies often fall short.
The roundtable was moderated by Sameer Dhanrajani, CEO of 3AI and AIQRATE, and featured the following speakers:
Ankit Mehra, cofounder and CEO, GyanDhan
Mashiyat Hussain, engineering lead, Backend, HYPD
Nitish Gupta, SVP – technology, NimbusPost
Sanjeev Singh, VP engineering, DeHaat
Shubhanshu Chouhan, CTO, Pidge
Vivek Gupta, senior director and head of technology cloud sales at Oracle India
Building A Robust Infra Backbone For AI
The roundtable, moderated by Dhanrajani, addressed the harder question of how enterprises actually operationalise AI at scale, with six leaders spanning cloud, fintech, D2C, agritech, logistics and last-mile delivery.
Oracle India’s Vivek Gupta opened the conversation by arguing that enterprises chasing AI at scale are often solving for the wrong constraint.
“AI at scale is not a GPU problem… It’s an engineering problem that needs to be solved,” said Gupta.
According to Gupta, the bottleneck for many companies when implementing AI is not compute availability, but the ability to define a clear business outcome before they begin building. That focus on the problem itself resonated with GyanDhan’s Ankit Mehra, who pushed back against the instinct to reach for AI as a default fix.
Having run workloads at his own company for testing purposes, Mehra said he had seen more problems traced to poorly framed questions than to actual scale limitations.
“Really solve for the problem that you’re trying to solve rather than just running with the hype part of it,” Mehra added.
But even when the problem is clearly defined, the data feeding these systems can present a different set of challenges.
HYPD’s Hussain brought the conversation to data itself, describing the unpredictability of user-generated content on a creator platform, with comments arriving from varied regions and formats and no consistent pattern to model against.
“Data variety is a major problem for us. We cannot always predict what kind of data we will receive. For example, on our platform, creators receive comments from people across different regions and backgrounds, making it difficult to predict the nature and variety of the data,” said Hussain.
That unpredictability becomes even more complex when AI is layered on top of existing data challenges, and the VP of engineering at DeHaat, Singh, reiterated the same. According to Singh, the nature of the problem has shifted over the past decade, from a pure data-management challenge to a compounded one.
“Earlier it was only a data problem, shuffling of data, creating or churning our money. Now it’s a data-plus-AI problem. So, we have faced both,” said Singh.
For businesses operating at scale, however, identifying the problem and managing the data is only part of the equation. The infrastructure itself has to be tailored to the use case.
The SVP of technology at NimbusPost, Gupta, grounded the discussion in logistics, where infrastructure decisions vary sharply by use case and margin. Getting the right setup, he said, comes only through costly trial and error.
“The right choice would come out of experimentation, and that experimentation would need a good amount of money… infrastructure is something wherein different industries would have different use cases,” he said.
And that experimentation becomes even harder when AI is deployed in live operational environments, where a wrong decision can directly affect costs and performance.
Chouhan, CTO of Pidge, concluded on a note of caution around automation in last-mile operations. Rider and delivery allocation, he said, still cannot be handed fully to opaque models.
“We cannot rely on an ambiguous, black-box algorithm like AI to always make the right decision. If we put AI in that place, our costs will go up, and we cannot guarantee performance,” said Chouhan.
Hidden Costs And Risks Of Scaling AI
The conversation then moved from the roundtable to a fireside chat, where the focus shifted from the broader challenges of building AI infrastructure to the risks enterprises face as they scale these deployments from pilots.
Dhanrajani, also moderating the fireside, opened the AI infrastructure conversation by pressing his two panellists, Ankit Gupta, CTO of Policybazaar for Business, and Nitin Kaushik, director of technology, Cloud Engineering, at Oracle, on where enterprise AI strategies tend to break down first.
Building AI capability, Gupta argued, is not only an infrastructure and use-case problem. According to him, it is also a trust challenge that many organisations underestimate. He noted that, without the right controls, prompts and AI-agent interactions can create pathways to expose sensitive enterprise information.
“Earlier we used to say, it is garbage in, garbage out, but today, the risk is that poorly governed inputs can lead to sensitive information getting out. That is why security, data governance, identity, and access controls must be designed into AI systems from the start,” Gupta said.
Oracle’s Kaushik picked up the thread when the conversation turned to cost, an issue Dhanrajani termed as the “elephant in the room” for most enterprises deep into their AI rollouts.
Token consumption, Kaushik said, is rising in ways many organisations are not prepared for. “I have met customers that are consuming trillions of tokens a day. We hear cases where organisations say their AI bills are beginning to approach – or even exceed – the value they associate with the business impact they are receiving.”
Infra Gap Behind AI Deployment
Kaushik followed the fireside chat with a deeper look at why AI deployments break down after the pilot stage. According to Oracle’s director of cloud engineering, companies face three recurring challenges behind AI implementation.
Cloud costs are often unpredictable, and data silos can create multiple versions of the same dataset – undermining the consistency and reliability of AI outputs. At the same time, cloud infrastructure has traditionally been built to prioritise availability over performance.
According to him, Oracle rebuilt from the infrastructure layer up with dedicated compute and memory, off-box virtualisation to reduce network load on the CPU, and RDMA-based networking designed to deliver low-latency communication across GPU clusters.
Taken together, the roundtable and fireside chat pointed to a common thread: enterprise AI’s biggest constraints are not just computational, but organisational. Enterprises are grappling with engineering discipline, data governance, cost visibility and trust, rather than mere GPU access.
Tech leaders across the sessions converged on the same view that these factors, alongside access to compute, will ultimately determine whether an AI deployment survives the move from pilot to production.

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Indonesia lagi-lagi dipercaya untuk menjadi tuan rumah perhelatan turnamen World Esports Championship 2026 (WEC26). Kabar ini diumumkan secara langsung oleh International Esports Federation (IESF) lewat akun Instagram mereka.
“Dunia bersatu di Indonesia. Indonesia akan menjadi tuan rumah IESF World Esports Championship! 2016, 2022, 2026. Tiga edisi. Satu bangsa. Sebuah babak baru. WEC26 | 15-20 Desember 2026. Dunia akan hadir. Apakah Anda siap?,” tulis IESF di akun Instagram mereka, Jumat (25/9/2026).
Menurut organisasi esports tersebut, WEC26 akan menghadirkan lebih dari 500 atlet dari lebih dari 110 federasi esports nasional yang sudah menjadi anggota organisasi.
Baca Juga: Apple Akui Bug Face ID iPhone 18 Pro, Siap Hadirkan Perbaikan Segera Lewat Pembaruan Software
“Bersama-sama kita telah mencetak sejarah dengan menyelenggarakan ajang esports terbesar di tepi pantai, di Bali pada tahun 2022,” ujar Presiden IESF, Vlad Marinescu. 
“Kini kami yakin, bersama-sama kita akan menghadirkan pengalaman dan kondisi terbaik bagi seluruh atlet yang telah lolos kualifikasi untuk ajang ini,” kata
Selain jadwal pelaksanaan, IESF juga mengumumkan lima nomor pertandingan yang akan dipertandingkan pada edisi tahun depan. Kelima game tersebut adalah Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, Mobile Legends: Bang Bang, PUBG Mobile, dan eFootball.
Indonesia Kembali Jadi Tuan Rumah WEC26
Penunjukan ini menjadikan Indonesia kembali menjadi tuan rumah World Esports Championship setelah sebelumnya pernah menggelar turnamen serupa pada 2016 dan 2022.
Meski IESF belum mengungkap kota maupun venue penyelenggaraan, keputusan tersebut memperlihatkan bahwa Indonesia masih dipandang sebagai salah satu pasar esports terbesar sekaligus salah satu negara dengan pengalaman penyelenggaraan turnamen internasional yang cukup matang.
Dalam beberapa tahun terakhir, Indonesia rutin menjadi lokasi berbagai kompetisi esports regional maupun dunia, mulai dari Mobile Legends hingga PUBG Mobile.
Detail Turnamen WEC26 Masih Menunggu Pengumuman
Sayangnya, IESF belum secara detail mengungkap lokasi penyelenggaraan, format kompetisi, pembagian grup, jadwal pertandingan, maupun informasi terkait tiket untuk penonton.
Informasi tersebut diperkirakan akan diumumkan secara bertahap menjelang pelaksanaan turnamen pada Desember 2026.
Dengan status Indonesia sebagai tuan rumah, WEC26 berpotensi menjadi salah satu agenda esports internasional terbesar yang digelar di Tanah Air tahun depan.
Pelatnas Timnas Esports Indonesia Disiapkan hingga 2027
Pelatnas Timnas Esports Indonesia disiapkan hingga Mei 2027. Simak agenda menuju Asian Games 2026, Global Esports Games, dan kompetisi berikutnya. (Gizmologi/ Yuslianson)
Di sisi lain, Pengurus Besar Esports Indonesia atau PB ESI baru saja mengungkap lebih detail tentang program Pemusatan Latihan Nasional (Pelatnas) Timnas Esports Indonesia tidak berhenti setelah Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 berakhir.
Dalam sesi bersama media di Jakarta, Selasa (15/9/2026), PB ESI menyiapkan rangkaian Pelatnas hingga Mei 2027 untuk menghadapi sejumlah kompetisi internasional berikutnya.
Asian Games menjadi target terdekat pelatnas timnas esports Indonesia, disusul Global Esports Games (GEG) Los Angeles pada akhir tahun. Setelah itu, program berlanjut sebagai bagian dari persiapan menghadapi kompetisi antarnegara pada 2027. Detail turnamen yang menjadi sasaran setelah GEG sejauh ini belum diumumkan.
Para atlet juga tidak hanya berfokus pada kemampuan teknis dan strategi permainan. PB ESI juga menggunakan konsep sports science mencakup kondisi fisik dan mental, nutrisi, pengelolaan beban latihan, hingga analisis performa.
Lantas, seperti apa agenda Timnas Esports Indonesia dalam beberapa bulan ke depan?
Target Terdekat Pelatnas Timnas Esports Indonesia
Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 berlangsung pada 19 September hingga 4 Oktober. Khusus esports, pertandingan dijadwalkan berlangsung pada 23 September–2 Oktober di Aichi Sky Expo.
Indonesia akan turun di delapan nomor, yakni Mobile Legends: Bang Bang, Honor of Kings, Identity V, Naraka: Bladepoint, Pokémon Unite, eFootball, Gran Turismo 7, dan PUBG Mobile.
PB ESI memasang target satu medali emas, tiga perak, dan empat perunggu. “E-football disebut menjadi salah satu nomor yang diharapkan bisa menyumbangkan emas untuk Indonesia,” kata Manajer Tim Nasional Esport Indonesia, Glorya Famiela Ralahalo, dalam sesi di Jakarta.
Ia menambahkan, “pelatnas timnas esports Indonesia menuju Asian Games sendiri sudah berlangsung sekitar dua bulan. Menjelang keberangkatan, beberapa atlet juga menjalani international training camp dan uji tanding di luar negeri, termasuk untuk nomor Naraka: Bladepoint dan Identity V.”

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Microsoft reportedly canceled three Halo projects that were in development before major layoffs hit the studio formerly known as 343 Industries. Details about the canceled games have now emerged, giving fans a look at what the future of the popular franchise could have looked like.
According to reports from insider RebsGaming and The Verge, the studio had been working on three separate Halo projects at the same time. These included a new mainline game, a smaller title based on the Halo novel First Strike, and updated versions of classic Halo games.
Microsoft Reportedly Canceled Three Halo Projects During Studio Overhaul
The First Strike project was reportedly the most advanced of the three. The game was planned as a smaller experience set between the events of the first and second Halo games.
The project was expected to feature five story missions along with a Firefight mode. It was also reportedly designed to connect planned remakes of Halo 2 and Halo 3. If development had continued, the game could have arrived as early as next year.
Another team was working on an early concept for a full-fledged Halo 7. The project was still far from entering full production, but developers had reportedly prepared a new vision for the game.
The new concept included a fresh story campaign, player-versus-player multiplayer and cooperative player-versus-environment gameplay. Developers were also reportedly planning an expanded version of Halo’s Forge creation tool.
The team presented this updated vision to Xbox leadership, including Matt Booty, before the layoffs. However, Halo 7 remained in the early stages of development, meaning the game was still several years away from release.
The third project reportedly involved updated versions of older Halo games. Details about the remastered titles remain limited, but the project was part of the studio’s broader plans for the franchise.
See Also: Microsoft and Google Take Down $66 Million Cybercrime Marketplace
The development of all three projects was disrupted by major layoffs at the studio. Following the cuts, only around 30 employees reportedly remained. The remaining staff included key engineers, artists, and support workers.
The studio has since moved away from its previous role as the primary developer of Halo games. It was renamed Halo Studios and shifted toward a support-focused role within Microsoft’s wider gaming operations.
The cancellation of these projects could mark a major change in Microsoft’s approach to the Halo franchise. While the series remains an important Xbox property, the reported shift suggests that Microsoft is taking a different approach to future Halo development.
For now, there is limited information about when fans can expect the next major Halo game. The canceled projects show that several different ideas were being explored behind the scenes before the studio’s restructuring changed the direction of the franchise.

OpenAI may soon introduce a new artificial intelligence model designed specifically for cybersecurity. OpenAI is reportedly preparing to preview GPT-6 Cyber within the next few days as it works to strengthen its position in the rapidly developing AI security market.
According to a report by Fortune, OpenAI could unveil GPT-6 Cyber during its Dev Day event on September 29. The company may also preview the model earlier than that date. The full launch is reportedly expected within the next few months.
Alongside the new model, OpenAI is also said to be working on a product that will help customers deploy GPT-6 Cyber more securely. The company has not yet revealed the name or full details of this product.
OpenAI May Preview GPT-6 Cyber Security Model Within Days
GPT-6 Cyber is already being tested through OpenAI’s Daybreak preview program. The program provides selected and verified partners with access to advanced AI models so they can test their cybersecurity capabilities and identify potential vulnerabilities.
The planned launch comes at a time when AI-powered cyber threats are receiving increased attention. Several frontier AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, have recently faced incidents involving AI systems being used in cyberattacks or security testing environments.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei have also called for greater caution around the rapid development of advanced AI systems. The concerns have grown as researchers continue to examine how autonomous AI agents could be used by attackers.
OpenAI has already announced a major cybersecurity initiative through its Daybreak program. The company plans to spend $1 billion to subsidize access to its advanced AI models for cybersecurity defenders around the world. The initiative is intended to help security researchers and organizations use AI to identify and respond to cyber threats.
However, the growing use of AI in cybersecurity presents a difficult challenge. The same technology that can help defenders detect vulnerabilities can also give attackers more powerful tools.
Security professionals are increasingly turning to AI for protection. An EY survey published in March 2026 found that 96% of corporate cybersecurity leaders considered AI a core cybersecurity solution. 95% said they had already deployed AI in some form. However, the use of autonomous AI agents was still largely in an exploratory stage.
The survey also highlighted concerns about the risks posed by AI-powered attacks. Around 90% of respondents said employees who are not prepared for AI-driven cyberattacks could become their biggest security weakness.
See Also: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna with Better Performance and Lower Costs
Another survey by the Institute for Security and Technology found that 72% of national security professionals considered adversarial use of AI one of their top three security concerns. At the same time, 78% viewed cybersecurity as one of the three most promising areas for AI.
This highlights the growing race between AI-powered attacks and AI-based security tools. As companies develop more capable models, cybersecurity is becoming an increasingly important part of the AI industry.
OpenAI recently introduced its Sol and Luna models, which focus on improving AI performance while reducing costs. The possible arrival of GPT-6 Cyber would add another major focus to the company’s expanding AI lineup.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Hospitality-focused AI startup Dextr AI has raised $6.7 Mn (about ₹64.2 Cr) in a seed funding round led by Elevation Capital, with participation from Foundation Capital.
The startup plans to deploy the fresh capital towards product development, team expansion, and scaling its AI deployments across global hospitality markets, including India.
Founded in 2025 by Sajid Shariff and Scott Arnold, Dextr AI builds specialised AI agents for hospitality businesses. Its platform automates tasks across reservations, guest management, back-office operations, staffing, sales, and marketing.
Dextr said it serves hundreds of properties across the US, Canada, the UK, and other European markets, including franchised properties operating under brands such as Hilton, Wyndham, Best Western, and IHG.
The startup claims to process more than 1 Mn interactions every month. It also said its platform collects payments through voice-based reservations, processing tens of millions of dollars monthly on behalf of customers.
As part of its India expansion plans, Dextr is targeting operational gaps such as missed calls, unanswered enquiries, staffing shortages, and unattended guest requests.
Dextr follows what it calls a “forward-deployed” model, under which its AI strategists and engineers work directly with hospitality businesses to identify tasks for automation and integrate its agents into their operations.
Its Daisy agent handles voice-based reservations, booking changes, and upselling in more than 90 languages. Alfred manages guest requests, complaints, and contactless check-ins, while Manny handles staff rostering, task allocation, productivity tracking, and potential overtime.
Another agent, Cosmo, supports direct bookings through AI-powered search, targeted marketing campaigns, and efforts to bring back past guests.
Dextr currently has a team of nearly 20 employees, spread across India and the US, including AI product builders, strategists and engineers.
For Elevation, Dextr is another investment in startups automating customer interactions and business workflows. In October last year, the investor led GreyLabs AI’s ₹85 Cr Series A round, which also saw participation from Z47 and angel investors. GreyLabs focuses on financial institutions, offering voice agents and speech analytics to automate contact centre operations.
Elevation also led a $6 Mn funding round in Adopt AI, which helps users automate software workflows through text commands. These investments span both industry-specific applications, such as hospitality and financial services, and tools designed to automate workflows across businesses.

Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited (PTCL) is expanding its consumer device portfolio with the launch of the Apple iPhone 18 Pro series across its Service Centers, in partnership with Mercantile, Apple’s Authorized Distributor in Pakistan.
Beginning with the official launch, customers will be able to purchase the iPhone 18 Pro series at five PTCL Service Centers in Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi. The offer reflects PTCL’s vision of delivering a richer digital experience by making premium technology more accessible and bringing the latest devices together with high-speed connectivity.
PTCL & Mercantile to offer iPhone 18 Pro series with two-year warranty, protection and connectivity benefits
Customers purchasing an iPhone 18 Pro series through PTCL will receive a two-year warranty, comprising one year from Apple and an additional year from Mercantile, along with a 12-month protection plan. Device purchases will also include complimentary PTCL connectivity benefits. Multiple payment options will be available at purchase.
The offer furthers PTCL’s broader strategy to develop its consumer device and electronics business alongside its core connectivity portfolio. With 194 Service Centers and Joint Shops across 96 cities, PTCL is leveraging its existing retail footprint to offer customers access to premium devices alongside fixed broadband and Flash Fiber services.
Commenting on the launch, Amad Khan, Chief Marketing Officer, PTCL, said, “Our ambition is to make the PTCL Service Centre experience more relevant to the way customers live and connect today. The availability of the iPhone 18 Pro series through our partnership with Mercantile brings together a premium device, trusted after-sales support and PTCL connectivity in one proposition. It is another step in evolving our retail network beyond connectivity and into a broader destination for technology and digital services.”

Nauman Durrani, CEO, Mercantile Pakistan, said, “We are pleased to partner with PTCL in bringing the iPhone 18 Pro series to customers through its established retail network. items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Dating startup Rivet has raised $10.5 Mn (about ₹100.6 Cr) in seed funding from Peak XV Partners, Shine Capital, and Blume Ventures to build and scale its community-driven matchmaking platform.
The startup plans to use the fresh capital to develop its product, expand distribution, and scale across the US. It announced its nationwide US launch yesterday.
Besides US, Rivet has an office in Delhi NCR, with its engineering and machine learning teams largely based in India.
Founded in 2025 by former Tinder and Match Group executive Taru Kapoor and Rajat Sahni, who previously served as CEO of CarDekho’s used-car business, Rivet offers a dating platform built around community recommendations.
The startup calls its model “social matching”. Users can join as “matchers” to assess potential pairs and recommend introductions they think would work.
These recommendations contribute to a social matching score for each potential pair. Pairs with high scores are introduced to each other, after which both individuals independently decide whether to connect and begin a conversation.
People who are not looking to date can also join solely as matchers. The startup describes its model as a “give-to-get” approach, allowing users to help others find connections while receiving recommendations for themselves.
The startup also counts former Tinder and OkCupid CEO Elie Seidman among its early investors. Seidman advised and mentored Kapoor during Rivet’s development.
The startup competes with dating and matchmaking platforms such as Tinder, Hinge, Bumble, The League, and Wingman. Its community-driven approach makes participation by people willing to recommend matches an important part of its expansion, alongside attracting singles seeking connections.
Rivet’s pitch centres on addressing the frustration of browsing profiles without finding a connection. Kapoor argued that while dating apps expanded the pool of potential partners, they also made the experience feel transactional and isolating.
The startup is betting that recommendations from other people can help surface potential matches that users might otherwise dismiss on swipe-based apps.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Mega Motor Company (MMC), the official partner of BYD in Pakistan, announced that BYD has reached a major milestone of 10,000 vehicles on Pakistani roads, marking the fastest ramp-up by a new-entrant New Energy Vehicle (NEV) brand in the country’s automotive history. The achievement reflects strong consumer demand, growing confidence in new energy mobility and the momentum BYD-MMC has built in the Pakistani market ahead of the commencement of local assembly.
BYD entered Pakistan with the BYD Atto 3 and BYD Seal and has since expanded its portfolio to five models. The lineup now also includes the Atto 2, Pakistan’s top-selling EV, the Sealion 7, and the Shark 6, the country’s first plug-in hybrid (PHEV) pickup, extending new energy mobility across a wider range of consumer needs and lifestyles.
“The significance of 10,000 vehicles goes well beyond the number itself. It reflects the progress MMC has made in building the foundations for new energy mobility in Pakistan,” said Aly Khan, CEO of Mega Motor Company. “From the outset, our focus has been on building for the long term, establishing the capabilities, infrastructure and market presence needed to support this transition at scale. We are pleased to have BYD as our partner and to have worked closely together at every step to bring this vision to life. As we move towards the next step in our journey, MMC is preparing to launch Pakistan’s first and largest NEV assembly facility, marking a new chapter in our commitment to the future of mobility in Pakistan.”
The pace of adoption also points to a broader shift in consumer confidence. Reaching 10,000 vehicles demonstrates the strength of demand BYD-MMC has established across multiple segments, even as Pakistan’s NEV market remains at an early stage of development.
“Pakistan has quickly become an important market in BYD’s global journey, and the trust consumers have shown in our brand is particularly significant to us,” said Liu Xueliang, Vice President of BYD Co. Ltd. General Manager of BYD Asia Pacific Auto Sales Division. “Every BYD owner who has chosen to embrace new energy technology reinforces our commitment to this market. We are working closely with MMC to ensure the right mix of products is available to Pakistani consumers at the right time, supporting a seamless customer experience throughout their new energy journey. We will continue bringing BYD’s world-class technology and innovation to Pakistan and expanding our presence in the market as consumer needs evolve.”
The next milestone in Pakistan’s NEV journey is already taking shape, with the upcoming BYD-MMC facility set to become the country’s largest state-of-the-art plant dedicated exclusively to the production of NEVs. The facility will mark a significant step forward in the development of Pakistan’s NEV ecosystem, taking the country from the adoption of imported NEVs to their production locally.

items.author: Michael Carroll
items.content:
LIVE FROM UNWRAPPED DIGITAL INDUSTRIES: The co-founder and CTO of Sateliot told Mobile World Live standards, choice and spectrum access are as important to a successful IoT play as the connectivity technology.
In a keynote, Marco Guadalupi (pictured) said Sateliot is keen to show potential customers how its approach of providing full interoperability between terrestrial networks and its low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellation can meet the growing needs of the IoT sector.
Guadalupi said mobile operators are a key element in expanding coverage, while spectrum rights are essential in an industry which spans multiple territories and jurisdictions.
The company believes 3GPP and other standards are important to covering the “massive market” and uses spanning agriculture, logistics and environmental monitoring industries.
Standardisation helps keep the cost of sensors down and promotes a market where customers are free to select connectivity providers, elements Guadalupi explained instil the confidence for companies to invest in the sector.
Of course, satellites remain a fundamental element in Sateliot’s business. It has six in orbit (four currently in operation) and is on the brink of launching five more, adding “more capacity to the constellation” and broadening the footprint.
Guadalupi explained there is little room to manoeuvre on the price of connectivity itself because it is largely market driven, so Sateliot is exploring opportunities to differentiate itself on the services provided and its ability to provide connections in areas where terrestrial coverage is lacking.
During the keynote, Guadalupi explained why collaboration, not competition with mobile operators is essential and offered predictions on the evolution of the satellite IoT market, including the likely impact of reduced capability devices.
You can find the keynote and more in the full Unwrapped: Digital Industries event page, here.

Oracle sent a force majeure notice to a Blue Owl Capital unit developing Project Jupiter, a New Mexico data centre tied to the Stargate AI programme, Bloomberg reported.

Bloomberg reported Oracle could defer rent for three years after payments begin if the companies agree a power-related force majeure event has occurred. Oracle would still pay other interim costs and rent over the full term of the lease.
The scale of the power challenge is considerable. The 2.45GW campus would consume roughly as much electricity as 1.8 million homes. It forms part of the Stargate venture Oracle, OpenAI and SoftBank unveiled with US President Donald Trump in January 2025. The programme was initially valued at $100 billion and has since grown beyond $400 billion.
New Mexico officials twice rejected a permit for a natural gas pipeline, and approval for the Bloom Energy fuel-cell system is still pending. The state Supreme Court has twice paused a scheduled hearing, but Oracle continues to say the campus is on track.
SemiAnalysis expects power to reach the campus in 2029, two years later than its earlier estimate, because the air-quality permit remains unresolved and the gas pipeline has not been approved.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian startup Thally has launched to provide the product knowledge layer for software teams, keeping documentation, websites, support platforms, and other connected places where users learn about a product aligned as that product changes.
Launched this month by founder Ekene Eze, Thally allows a team to creates a documentation site on Thally, connect its product repositories, and connect the customer-facing content repositories it wants Thally to maintain.
When a product change comes through, Thally works out what it means for users and traces the impact across those connected surfaces. It then opens pull requests containing completed updates and the evidence behind them. The team can verify where the information came from, edit the changes, and approve what gets published.
“For example, changing an authentication flow could affect an API reference, a quickstart, a support article, and a code example in a blog post. Updating just the API reference would leave people following outdated instructions elsewhere. Thally finds and updates the affected connected content,” Eze told Disrupt Africa.
“It also provides a documentation platform with search, custom domains, versioned deployments, rollbacks, and AI assistants. The same documentation can be read by people in a browser or accessed by AI tools through Markdown, JSON, and MCP.”
Eze said he had had the idea for Thally for a long time, but only officially started working on it in March.
“The idea grew out of my work in developer experience at Flutterwave, Netlify, and LI.FI. Across those companies, keeping documentation aligned with the product required a lot of investigation before any writing could begin,” he said.
“I would collect one-pagers from product managers, read Linear tickets, inspect changelogs and code changes, then figure out every public place that needed updating. Even when we updated the documentation, a website page, an old support article, or an integration example could get missed.”
That recurring experience became the starting point for Thally, which has launched to fill the gap between a product change and accurate information everywhere customers learn about it.
“As teams use AI coding assistants to ship faster, there is more change to keep up with and less time to investigate each release manually,” said Eze.
“The outdated information remains online, where both customers and AI tools can still find it. That creates a feedback loop. An AI assistant can read a forgotten guide and generate a new integration using a method that has already been deprecated. A missed content update can become a broken integration, extra support work, or lost customer trust.”
Fully bootstrapped, Thally released a beta in August and launched publicly this month.
“Teams including Hackmamba.io, Procta.org, and LI.FI participated in the beta as design partners, helping us test the product,” Eze said.
“We now have more than 100 active workspaces on Thally. At least 100 workspaces are currently going through the 14-day free trial. That is an encouraging early signal. We hope to convert those trials into paid subscriptions as teams see the value of using Thally.”
Thally is a global product, and already has users in the US, Europe, India, the Middle East, and Africa. Its business model combines an open-source documentation engine with paid cloud subscriptions.

items.content:
Enterprise tech startup CodeKarma is in talks to raise $5 Mn to $6 Mn in a fresh funding round, sources told Inc42.
The round will be led by existing investors Prosus and Accel, the sources added. The discussions are ongoing, and the contours of the transaction could change.
Queries sent to CodeKarma and Accel did not elicit a response until the time of publishing this story. A Prosus spokesperson declined to comment on market speculation.
The development comes a little over a year after CodeKarma raised $2.5 Mn in its pre-seed round, co-led by Prosus, Accel, and Xeed Ventures. SenseAI Ventures and Stargazer Ventures also participated in the round.
Founded in 2024 by Anantharam Vanchi Prakash and Priyanka Nahata, CodeKarma operates a production intelligence platform that maps the behaviour of software in production directly to its underlying code.
Prakash, a former Amazon and Flipkart executive, is the startup’s cofounder and CEO, while Nahata serves as its cofounder and CTO.
The Bengaluru-based startup’s platform helps developers and AI agents identify active and dormant code, detect performance issues, understand dependencies between different parts of a software system, and assess the risks associated with changing code.
CodeKarma currently offers four products. KarmaLens provides production insights within developers’ integrated development environments, while KarmaDomain maps dependencies across microservices and APIs. KarmaPulse gives engineering leaders an overview of operational issues, and KarmaIQ supplies production context to AI coding agents.
During its previous fundraise, CodeKarma said it planned to deploy the capital to strengthen its AI capabilities, enter new enterprise verticals, expand its presence in the US, hire employees, and invest in product development.
Prakash had also said that the startup was working towards building autonomous software agents that could go beyond identifying problems in code and act on fixing them.
The funding talks come amid growing investor interest in startups building software-development tools and infrastructure for the AI era.
In July, AI software engineering startup Vorflux raised $15 Mn in a seed funding round led by Y Combinator. The same month, AI software creation startup Emergent raised $130 Mn at a valuation of $1.5 Bn.
Meanwhile, Inc42 exclusively reported in June that vibe-coding startup Rocket was in talks to raise fresh funding in a SIG-led Series A round. Accel, which is expected to participate in CodeKarma’s proposed round, is also an existing investor in Rocket.
Investor interest extends to the wider AI ecosystem. Indian AI startups raised $676 Mn across 57 deals in the first half of 2026, more than four times the $162 Mn raised across 30 deals during the corresponding period last year.

items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
items.content:
Kini semakin banyak perangkat dalam keseharian masyarakat yang selalu tersambung ke internet, dengan smartphone yang utamanya menjadi “perangkat pusat” alias perangkat utama. Mulai dari berkomunikasi, akses konten hiburan hingga main game, semua bisa dilakukan dari smartphone, mulai kelas flagship hingga kelas entri. Dan survei terbaru dari Opera mengungkap fakta penting terkait akses internet dari smartphone.
Sebelumnya, menurut laporan dari We Are Social (2025) mengatakan bila orang Indonesia rata-rata menghabiskan waktu sekitar 4,5 jam dalam satu hari, hanya untuk akses internet melalui smartphone. Sementara dari seluruh traffic web yang ada di Indonesia, 71,93% di antaranya diakses dari smartphone. Menunjukkan bila smartphone juga benar-benar menjadi perangkat utama di kalangan masyarakat Tanah Air.
Dengan adanya kenaikan harga komponen yang berimbas pada kenaikan harga smartphone, tidak heran kalau beberapa di antara Gizmo friends memilih untuk tetap menggunakan smartphone lama. Sehingga performa aplikasi menjadi penting, terutama ketika digunakan untuk akses internet. Dan Opera mencoba untuk mempelajari kebiasaan masyarakat terkini.
Baca juga: Counterpoint: Pengiriman Chip Smartphone Global Turun 15% di Semester I 2026
Smartphone Kelas Entri Tetap Mendominasi Untuk Berselancar di Dunia Maya
Untuk itu, Opera baru saja melakukan survei di Indonesia yang melibatkan lebih dari 2000 responden, demi memahami lebih jauh aktivitas pengguna mereka, sekaligus bagaimana pengguna memanfaatkan berbagai fitur di dalam peramban atau browser Opera. 
Dari hasil survei tersebut, alasan nomor satu pengguna memilih peramban Opera, adalah aspek kecepatan. Hasil ini menunjukkan bila pengguna memang mencari pengalaman berselancar di internet yang terasa cepat dan ringan pada smartphone—terutama ketika diakses melalui perangkat dengan kemampuan yang lebih terbatas seperti smartphone kelas entri.
Fakta berikutnya, survei Opera menunjukkan bila sekitar 63% responden mengakses internet lewat smartphone kelas entri hingga menengah, dengan harga di bawah USD185 atau tidak melebihi Rp3 jutaan. Angka atau tren tersebut sejalan dengan riset Counterpoint Q2 2025 lalu, yang menunjukkan bila segmen harga smartphone kurang dari USD150 meningkat 3% secara tahunan.
Dengan begitu, diketahui bila smartphone terjangkau masih menjadi bagian penting dari pasar smartphone secara global, termasuk dari kebanyakan pengguna Opera di Indonesia. Menjadi justifikasi Opera untuk terus menghadirkan fitur-fitur yang relevan demi meningkatkan pengalaman menjelajah web, tentunya dengan cepat dan aman.
Opera Hadirkan Fitur yang Lebih Relevan Bagi Pengguna
Walau dirancang agar pengguna bisa akses internet dengan cepat, Opera tetap hadirkan fitur ekstra yang dinilai esensial, diharapkan agar pengguna tak perlu mengunduh aplikasi terpisah yang kemudian bisa memberatkan smartphone atau mempersempit ruang penyimpanan. Salah satu andalannya adalah ad-blocker terintegrasi, memungkinkan pengguna Opera mampu jelajah internet tanpa iklan dan elemen mengganggu lainnya.
Dari survei Opera, sekitar 60% pengguna menggunakan perambah untuk akses video pendek, sehingga fitur seperti ad-blocker menjadi relevan. Dan untuk menghemat kuota data, fitur data saver juga bisa dimanfaatkan, agar bisa menghemat biaya akses internet. Turut hadir pula fitur VPN gratis dan terintegrasi di dalam peramban Opera—sekitar 58% pengguna telah mengetahui fitur ini.
Menariknya lagi, Opera juga menawarkan fungsi akal imitasi alias AI. Di mana pengguna bisa memanfaatkan peramban Opera untuk mencari informasi, merangkum, sampai menyelesaikan sejumlah tugas. Dari semua fitur ekstra yang disebutkan, mana yang paling bermanfaat bagi Gizmo friends dalam aktivitas berselancar di dunia maya sehari-hari?

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
A Jazz customer has lodged a complaint with the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority, alleging that a paid family package remained unusable despite appearing active in the Jazz World app and showing a substantial remaining balance.
The complainant said he subscribed to the Jazz We Fantastic package on September 23, 2026, paying approximately Rs 6,000. According to the complaint, the package continued to appear active in the app with around Rs 4,782 in balance, but services were not working on the primary number or on five linked users.
The customer said he contacted the Jazz helpline multiple times and also visited a franchise, but the issue remained unresolved. He said he has retained call recordings, screenshots, and payment evidence to support his complaint.
The complaint further claims that other customers at the franchise were experiencing similar problems, though this has not been independently verified.
Customer Raises Questions Over Validity Loss and Possible Double Payment
A key concern raised in the complaint is that package validity continues to run even when paid services are unavailable.
The customer argued that if a package remains unusable for two or three days, users may lose part of the paid validity period and may be forced to buy another package to restore connectivity.
He did not accuse Jazz of deliberately causing the problem but asked PTA to determine whether the issue was a technical fault and whether affected users should receive compensation, refunds, or extensions to package validity.
The complainant has asked PTA to investigate whether other Jazz subscribers are facing the same problem, whether Jazz’s billing and customer-service practices comply with applicable rules, and whether customers are effectively being pushed into purchasing new packages while existing paid bundles remain unusable.
He has also requested restoration of the service, an extension for the affected period, and compensation or a refund where applicable.
At the time of writing, the complaint represents the customer’s allegations. A response from Jazz or a formal finding from PTA would be needed to establish the cause of the service failure or whether any regulatory violation occurred.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
Update| September 25, 20:00 IST
Shares of PB Fintech ended 3.6% lower at ₹1,165.50 apiece on the BSE. Turtlemint remained locked at its 20% lower circuit at ₹87.30 throughout the trading session.
Original| Sepetmber 25, 13:00 IST
The sell-off in insurtech stocks continued for the second straight session today as the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India’s (IRDAI) proposed overhaul of insurance distribution commissions rattled investors.
Shares of Policybazaar parent PB Fintech fell as much as 7.8% to touch a fresh 52-week low of ₹1,115.10 on the BSE. Meanwhile, Turtlemint shares opened at their 20% lower circuit of ₹87.30, which was also the stock’s fresh all-time low.
The stocks later pared some of their losses. At 12:21 IST, PB Fintech was trading 5.12% lower at ₹1,148.10, with a market capitalisation of ₹53,128.6 Cr (about $5.5 Bn).
Turtlemint was trading 18.84% lower at ₹88.55, giving the insurtech company a market capitalisation of ₹2,607.6 Cr (about $272 Mn).
At the prevailing prices, PB Fintech shares have fallen about 39% across the two sessions, while Turtlemint has declined about 35% from its level before the sell-off began.
The rout began yesterday after IRDAI released a consultation paper proposing product- and channel-specific commission ceilings for insurance distributors. The proposed framework would reintroduce product-level commission caps more than three years after the regulator removed such limits in April 2023 and shifted to an expenses of management (EoM) framework.
Under the proposed framework, commissions for insurance distributors would vary based on the product, distribution channel and effort involved in selling and servicing a policy. Open-architecture insurance distribution entities such as Policybazaar and Turtlemint’s insurance broking arm would generally face lower caps than individual agents and other distributors.
For digital insurance distributors, the proposed changes could put pressure on revenue from health, motor and life insurance, while forcing platforms to rethink customer acquisition costs and sales incentives.
PB Fintech cofounder and group chairman Yashish Dahiya said during an investor call yesterday that the proposals have “almost forced” the company to consider entering insurance manufacturing, which would allow it to design, underwrite, and sell policies itself, though it would wait for greater regulatory clarity.
The proposals are not final, with IRDAI inviting stakeholder comments until October 25.
‘Much Worse Than Imagined’
As PB Fintech and Turtlemint extended their sell-off, brokerages began quantifying the potential impact of IRDAI’s proposed overhaul.
Bernstein described the proposed commission cuts as “much worse than imagined”, warning that they could unravel PB Fintech’s unit economics, particularly in health and motor insurance.
Jefferies retained its ‘Buy’ rating on PB Fintech but cut its price target to ₹1,540 from ₹2,050. It estimated that a 10% reduction in new business commission rates could translate into a 10%-12% decline in earnings. The brokerage also flagged the proposals as a risk for Turtlemint.
Bank of America retained its ‘Neutral’ rating on PB Fintech but cut its price target to ₹1,410 from ₹1,970. It described the proposals as directionally negative for online insurance brokers, though it expects the impact on Policybazaar’s life and term insurance businesses to remain manageable.
Morgan Stanley said that the net present value of PB Fintech’s health insurance business could fall 60%-70% under the proposed framework, while the impact on its life insurance business could be relatively limited.
HSBC downgraded PB Fintech to ‘Hold’ and cut its price target to ₹1,150 from ₹2,100. It also slashed its FY28 and FY29 earnings per share estimates by 56% and 17%, respectively.
Motilal Oswal Securities said that the proposals could reduce PB Fintech’s FY28 core online insurance revenue by 30%. Without cost reductions or additional revenue streams, this could translate into a 46% cut to its earnings estimate.
Citi said distribution economics could compress by 70%-90% across several high-margin insurance categories if the proposals are implemented in their current form.

According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is developing the feature as part of a larger change to its iOS interface. The company is testing a dedicated Contacts tab that could replace the current Updates tab in the bottom navigation bar.
With this change, Status updates and Channels are expected to move to the Chats section. The new Contacts tab will focus more on information related to people saved in a user’s phone.
The birthday reminder will rely on the birthday details stored in the iPhone Contacts app. Users who have already added birthdays to their contacts will not need to enter the information again in WhatsApp.
Those who have not saved a birthday can simply add it to the relevant contact in the iPhone Contacts app.
Birthday reminders will remain visible
The feature was spotted in WhatsApp beta for iOS version 26.38.10.18, which is available through TestFlight.
When a contact has a birthday, WhatsApp can display a cake emoji along with a “Birthday today” label below the person’s name. The reminder is designed to remain visible throughout the day.
This could help users avoid missing a birthday simply because they did not open the Contacts tab at the right time.
See Also: WhatsApp Plus Users Can Now Customize Their Emoji Reactions on Android
More information coming to the Contacts tab
The new Contacts tab is expected to offer more than a simple list of saved phone numbers. WhatsApp is also working on displaying information such as contacts’ statuses, recent activity, and birthdays.
The changes are part of WhatsApp’s broader effort to make its iOS navigation more focused on contacts and personal connections.
The birthday reminder feature is still under development. It is currently being tested with beta users, so WhatsApp may make additional changes before releasing it to the public.
For now, iPhone users who want to prepare for the feature can make sure birthdays are correctly saved in their iPhone Contacts app.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Federal Minister for Economic Affairs Senator Ahad Khan Cheema chaired a meeting to review the implementation of the PM Fuel Relief Scheme. Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar, Federal Minister for Petroleum Ali Pervaiz Malik, Federal Minister for IT Shaza Fatima Khawaja, the Minister of State for Finance, and representatives of relevant institutions and provincial governments attended the meeting.
The Ministry of IT and the Pakistan Digital Authority (PDA) briefed the meeting on the scheme’s implementation. It was informed that more than five million people have registered under the scheme and fuel tokens are being generated successfully. Registration-related and other issues at most petrol pumps have also been resolved.
PM Fuel Relief Scheme: Over 5 Million People Registered So Far
“On the Prime Minister’s directions, the Fuel Relief Scheme is progressing successfully across the country,” Minister Cheema said.
The meeting reviewed registration difficulties faced by some rickshaw and loader owners, particularly where vehicles are not registered with provincial Excise Departments. Provincial representatives informed the meeting that registration of rickshaws had begun. Eligible owners will be able to benefit from the scheme once their vehicles are registered. The meeting was also informed that owners of registered motorcycles are receiving relief under the scheme.
Minister Cheema called for the registration-related issues faced by rickshaws and loaders to be addressed promptly. He said eligible owners should not be left out of the relief effort and asked the Pakistan Digital Authority to include vehicle-registration and token-payment complaints in a dedicated complaint portal, to be made operational at the earliest.
See Also: PTA Starts Inspecting Telecom Towers Backup Power to Prevent Mobile Service Disruptions
The PDA informed the meeting that it would work to launch the portal as soon as possible so that users could register complaints and seek resolution of their issues.
The Minister welcomed visits by Members of Parliament to petrol pumps in their constituencies, in line with the Prime Minister’s directions. He said that real-time updates and feedback from these visits were helping improve the system.
The meeting was informed that most payments to petrol pumps had been made. State Bank representatives said that pending payment issues were expected to be resolved within a day or two. Minister Cheema emphasized that payment delays should not disrupt the scheme’s implementation.
Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting Attaullah Tarar said that public awareness efforts were underway through media and on-ground outreach, and that all possible steps were being taken to inform citizens about the scheme.
Minister Cheema expressed satisfaction with the performance of provincial governments and district administrations in implementing the scheme.

items.title: Young Japanese find new outlets for peace activism amid rising tensions in the Pacific
items.summary:
Young activists are reshaping protest into something accessible, individual, and nonhierarchical
Originally published on Global Voices
Tattsu’s “Hibiya Kōen Lunch Protest.“ Every Monday and Friday, he spreads out placards about government policies, from health care to peace issues, on a blue tarp in Hibiya Park during lunch hours, inviting people to sit and discuss with him over lunch. items.author: Jo Carter
items.content:
Young activists are reshaping protest into something accessible, individual, and nonhierarchical
Originally published on Global Voices
Tattsu’s “Hibiya Kōen Lunch Protest.“ Every Monday and Friday, he spreads out placards about government policies, from health care to peace issues, on a blue tarp in Hibiya Park during lunch hours, inviting people to sit and discuss with him over lunch. Photo taken by Jo Carter. Used with permission.
This post is part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” With this Spotlight, we seek to explore the many forms of protest, the tactics states use to delegitimize and suppress them, and the complex relationship between protest and democracy. You can support this coverage by donating here.
August 15, 2026, marks the 81st anniversary of the end of World War II — a date when Allied nations celebrated victory over the Axis powers, including Japan. The date triggers a complex collective emotion in Japan: For some Japanese, it is a moment for deep reflection over the country’s history of wartime violence. For others, the anniversary dredges up feelings of remorse, pain, or humiliation, as the war and the atomic bomb that ended it, took hundreds of thousands of their countrymen’s lives.
This year, the anniversary landed amid Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s push, as part of her broader right-leaning agenda, to amend the country’s pacifist postwar constitution, stepping away from a strictly pacifist framework.
Meanwhile, Japanese peace activists commemorated the date with a variety of events and rallies. Attending several of these gatherings, Global Voices observed Japanese peace activism shifting from a more ideological, often confrontational and hierarchical approach among the older generation to a more individualized, accessible, pop-culture-centered approach among young people.
The academic left
The first event was a leftist symposium, “The 81st Year of the Post-War Era: A Dialogue to Halt the Collapse of Democracy,” organized by Civic Cultural Forum on August 15 at the Japan Education Center, a few miles away from Yasukuni Shrine — a controversial site which has been criticized by China, Korea, and even Japan’s own left-wingers for including more than 1,000 convicted WWII war criminals’ names in its “Book of Souls,” an honored list of people who have devoted their lives to Japanese society.
Three professors from The University of Tokyo opened the discussion with their critical perspectives on the current civil society crisis in Japan.
Among them, Professor Tetsuya Takahashi, who is a known critic of Japanese nationalism, pointed out that the Japan-U.S. security treaty signed in 1951, which grants the U.S. military forces access to its land, air, and sea for mutual defence purposes, had led to the “colonization” of Okinawa, as much of the island was handed over to the U.S. military, while Indigenous people there were stripped of their lands and rights.
Takahashi criticized the mainland liberal left for failing Okinawans, as they did not challenge the structural discrimination against minority citizens.
The 81st Year of the Post-War Era: A Dialogue to Halt the Collapse of Democracy. Photo taken by Jo Carter. Used with permission.
The 156-seat venue was packed, with some standing through the whole three and a half hour gathering. The vast majority of attendees were well-educated retirees in their 60s and older, comfortable with academic discussions on complex issues such as geopolitics and post-war political theory.
Some participants expressed concern about the very few young faces in the room. Sociologist Yuki Honda explained this by noting that the younger generation was overwhelmed by despair of an unjust society:
今の若い人たちは将来への不安から権威主義的になっています。自分が生き残ることに必死なあまり、強者におもねり、弱者を叩くようになってしまっています。
Despair is driving young people to authoritarianism. These days, they are desperate to survive and often end up trying to suck up to the powerful and punch down on the vulnerable.
Stressed street protests
On the same day, numerous protests took place near Yasukuni Shrine, including one from conservative groups advocating for “reverence for the heroic spirits of the war dead,” and another by anti-war left-wing groups calling for “the pledge of non-war and peace.”
An Okinawan activist, Takamatsu Gushiken, known as the “bone hunter,” because he has spent nearly 40 years searching caves in southern Okinawa for the remains of soldiers from the Battle of Okinawa, held a symbolic hunger strike to protest the government’s plan to relocate U.S. Marine Corps Air Station Futenma to a new location in Henoko, which would require mass land reclamation using sand from southern Okinawa. Many remains have yet to be excavated from Southern Okinawa, and Gushiken argues that the project is disrespectful to the dead on both sides of the battle.
During the Battle of Okinawa (April 1–June 22, 1945), at least 149,425 Okinawan people were killed or forced into suicide upon defeat, with their remains yet to be recovered. Gushiken launched his first hunger strike in 2021, when the relocation plan was made public.
Takamatsu Gushiken. Photo taken by Jo Carter. Used with permission.
On the eve of the anniversary of the end of WWII on August 14, Gushiken expressed worries at the event “A Talk by Takamatsu Gushiken: No More Battle of Okinawa, No More War” about the Prime Minister’s remarks on Taiwan and its implications for Okinawa:
私たちは戦争が起きたら死ねと言われているんです。[…]台湾有事が起きたら沖縄本島は屋内避難せよと言われています。人口が多いから避難させられないということです
We are basically told to die if war breaks out. […] If a Taiwan contingency happens, the large population on Okinawa’s main island makes it impossible for us to evacuate outside the prefecture.
Highlighting U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth’s statement in March 2025, that “Japan would be on the front lines of any contingency we might face in the western Pacific,” he appealed to the young generation to see the war in terms of human lives rather than geopolitical interests.
On August 15, as Gushiken approached the Yasukuni Shrine, a right-winger blocked his way and shoved him and his team down to the small corner of the slope.
In the afternoon, another confrontation took place as 50 activists from Hantenren (the Anti-Emperor Association) held their annual protest near the Shrine; a group of right-wing protesters attacked them while shouting discriminatory slurs such as “Korean, go back to your country!” and “you old hag.” Eventually, police officers had to move in to separate the two groups.
Japanese police officers stepped in as right-wing protesters approached anti-war activists. Photo taken by Jo Carter. Used with permission.
Young people forging thier own path to peace
Many young Japanese find academic talks and street conflicts unappealing and far removed from conventional activism. However, that doesn’t mean they don’t care about politics and peace issues.
Young activist Tattsu (@kizuki11674), for example, created his own strategy to make political action more accessible. Every Monday and Friday, he spreads out placards about government policies, from health care to peace issues, on a blue tarp in Hibiya Park during lunch hours, inviting people to sit and discuss with him over lunch. The park is highly symbolic and considered Japan’s first people’s park, as it hosted the first large-scale social protest in 1905 to challenge the imperial state. Tattsu brands his activism “Hibiya Kōen Lunch Protest” — a way to transform intense political debate into a calm, friendly conversation.
On August 13, Tattu explained the rationale behind his action to GV:
街頭演説やスタンディングは、常に嫌がらせや理不尽な質問に晒されます。特に政権に反対するとき、反対派は「じゃあ代替案を出せ」と要求してきます。これが、人々がデモに参加するハードルを上げています。
Street speeches or standing on the sidewalk always expose us to harassment and absurd questions. In particular when one challenges the government, opponents often look for debate: ‘So, what's your alternative?’ This raises the hurdle for people to join protests.
He believed that ordinary people should be involved in political deliberation regardless of their knowledge. Rather than directly criticizing the government, Tattsu’s placards adopt manga-style or pop aesthetics, and their messages appeal to individual choices and their effects, such as:
私が戦争で傷ついて欲しく無いと願う人々の中にはあなたの事も含まれています
I wish the people I care about wouldn’t be hurt in war, and that wish includes you.
黙っていればそのまま。声を上げれば社会は動く。
Staying silent changes nothing. Raise your voice and society moves.
This shift toward individual autonomy over party-driven dogma was emphasized by a Park Lunch Protest participant Yuichi Nakata, who became a peace activist in 2015 when the Abe administration passed the peace and security legislation:
ネットの普及によりデモ活動は政治家の手を離れましたが、ネットでの連帯だけでなく、人と人との対面での対話が必要です。
With the spread of the internet, demonstrations moved beyond the politicians’ control. Beyond online solidarity, face-to-face dialogue among citizens is now necessary.
August 15 anti-war rally at downtown Shinjuku South Gate. Photo taken by Jo Carter Used with permission.
Tattu is not alone; young activists are reshaping protests into something accessible, individual, and nonhierarchical. This trend of people valuing participation of their own free will was also evident at the August 15 anti-war rally at downtown Shinjuku South Gate. The event drew participants of all ages and genders, with participants sporting idol penlights and brightly colored, pop-style placards borrowed from popular fandom culture.
Photo taken by Jo Carter. Used with permission.
One participant wore a protest sign that read, “General Citizen: I have no affiliation with any political party.” Indeed, unlike conventional political gatherings, about 100 people stood in a circle, passing a microphone in an open, free-speech format. The messages, mostly from younger speakers, leaned on gut-level appeals: “I just want to keep enjoying violent action movies in peace — so, no war.” “I have two high schoolers. I’m not sending them to the battlefield. Don’t kill children! Don’t kill adults! Don’t kill anybody!”
The atmosphere was relaxed and encouraging; many spoke up against politicians’ view that nukes are a crucial deterrent in navigating current global tensions.
Watching this open-mic circle, a veteran participant who had attended the afternoon’s academic symposium marvelled with tears in her eyes,
かつてのデモは、労働組合が作ったプラカードをかかげて、指示されたスローガンを復唱するだけでした。でも今は、ここにたくさんの若い人がいて、みんなが自分の言葉で話している。本当に素晴らしいことです。
In the past, protests were just about holding union-made placards and chanting union-made slogans. But now, there are so many young people here…seeing everyone speak in their own words here is wonderful.
Written by Jo Carter
