items.author: Taiwo George
items.content:
The ADC Presidential Campaign has entered a new phase of organisation, coordination and nationwide mobilisation with Senator Augustine Okwudiri Akobundu assuming responsibility as Director-General of the Presidential Campaign Council.
With the council already unveiled, the focus now shifts from composition to execution — from assembling the campaign structure to activating it across the country.
At the centre of that task is Senator Akobundu, a retired Colonel of the Nigerian Army, former Minister of State for Defence, experienced party administrator and serving Senator representing Abia Central Senatorial District.
His mandate is clear: coordinate the political, organisational and operational machinery of the campaign, align its structures across the federation and ensure that every arm of the Presidential Campaign Council works with discipline, coherence and purpose.
It is a responsibility for which his career has prepared him extensively.
From the discipline and strategic demands of the military to national party administration, executive public service and legislative representation, Senator Akobundu brings to the assignment decades of experience in leadership, organisation and public service.
A graduate of the Nigerian Defence Academy, Akobundu served the Nigerian Army in several command and staff appointments before retiring as a Colonel in 2000. His military career exposed him to the demands of strategic planning, coordination and disciplined execution.
Following his retirement from the military, he built a career spanning business, politics and public administration.
He served as Chairman of the Board of Management of the University College Hospital, Ibadan, and later as Minister of State for Defence under President Goodluck Jonathan in 2015.
His political experience is equally extensive.
Over the years, Senator Akobundu has occupied several senior positions in party administration, including National Vice Chairman and South-East Zonal Chairman, as well as National Organising Secretary.
That background in political organisation and national party management is central to the task before him: harmonising campaign structures, coordinating stakeholders, strengthening field operations and ensuring that the various components of the Presidential Campaign Council function as one national organisation.
Today, Senator Akobundu represents Abia Central Senatorial District in the National Assembly, where his legislative and constituency work has focused on education, infrastructure, healthcare, youth empowerment and human-capital development.
His interventions have included scholarships, vocational and digital-skills programmes, medical outreaches and infrastructure initiatives across his constituency.
He has also used the floor of the Senate to raise issues of critical infrastructure, including the Umuahia–Ikot Ekpene Federal Road.
Senator Akobundu formally joined the African Democratic Congress in March 2026 and has since become part of the party’s national political structure.
His appointment as Director-General therefore brings together the experience of a soldier, administrator, politician and legislator at the operational centre of the presidential campaign.
The campaign structure has been unveiled.
The leadership is in place.
The task before the Director-General is now to convert that structure into a coordinated national campaign operation.

items.content:
Sindh Agriculture University (SAU), Tandojam, has announced admissions for 2027 for a wide range of undergraduate degree programs at its main campus, Khairpur College of Agriculture and Management Sciences, and SAU Campus Umerkot.
According to the official admission advertisement, the last date to apply is October 30, 2026. The university will hold the pre-admission entry test on November 8, 2026, with test centres in Hyderabad, Sukkur and Umerkot.
The university has invited fresh applications for programs in agriculture, veterinary sciences, engineering, food sciences, information technology, computer science, software engineering, English, and other fields. Applicants can submit their forms through the SAU admission portal.

Degree Programs at Main Campus
SAU is offering undergraduate programs through several faculties and departments at its main campus in Tandojam.
The Faculty of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Sciences offers Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) along with BS programs in Dairy Technology, Poultry Science, and Fisheries & Aquaculture.
Under the Faculty of Crop Production, students can apply for B.Sc. (Agri.) Hons. The Faculty of Crop Protection also offers B.Sc. (Agri.) Hons.
The Faculty of Agricultural Social Sciences offers B.Sc. (Agri.) Hons. and BS English (Language & Literature).
Agricultural Engineering and Technology Programs
The Faculty of Agricultural Engineering & Technology offers B.E. (Agri.) along with BS programs in Environmental Science and Agro-Industrial Engineering Technology.
These programs are designed for students who want to pursue undergraduate studies in agricultural engineering, environmental sciences, and related technical fields.
Food Science and Technology Programs
The Institute of Food Sciences and Technology is offering B.Sc. Food Science & Technology and BS Human Nutrition & Dietetics.
Students interested in food technology and nutrition can apply for these programs under the university’s undergraduate admission schedule.
Computer and IT Programs
The Information Technology Center offers BS programs in Information Technology, Computer Science and Software Engineering.
The university also lists BS computing programs under its eligibility criteria for students who have completed Intermediate, A-Level or an equivalent qualification.
Khairpur College and Umerkot Campus Programs
The Khairpur College of Agriculture and Management Sciences offers B.E. (Agri.), B.Sc. (Agri.) Hons., B.Sc. (Hons.) Food Science & Technology, BS Software Engineering, and BS English (Language & Literature).
At the SAU Campus Umerkot, students can apply for B.Sc. (Agri.) Hons., BS Information Technology, BS English (Language & Literature), and BS Software Engineering.
Eligibility Criteria
Candidates with Intermediate, A-Level or an equivalent qualification can apply for the listed undergraduate programs, subject to the requirements of the selected degree.
The advertisement states that candidates from Pre-Medical, Pre-Engineering, Pre-Computer/General Science, Commerce, Arts and F.A/F.Sc. backgrounds can apply where applicable. Candidates generally need at least 50% marks in the annual examination.
For B.E. (Agri.), the advertisement requires a minimum of 60% marks in Intermediate.
Candidates applying for BS programs in Fisheries & Aquaculture, Dairy Technology, Environmental Science and Agro-Industrial Engineering Technology need at least 50% marks in the relevant examination.
SAU Pre-Admission Entry Test 2027
The university has scheduled its pre-admission entry test for November 8, 2026.
Candidates will take the test at designated centres in Hyderabad, Sukkur, and Umerkot. Applicants should complete their registration and fee payment before the deadline so they can take part in the admission process.
Scholarships and University Facilities
SAU has highlighted several facilities for students in its admission advertisement. These include scholarships and financial support, accredited degree programs, smart classrooms, high-tech laboratories and modern libraries.
The university also lists a Wi-Fi-enabled smart campus, incubation and job placement centre, national and international linkages, strong industry and alumni networks, sports and recreation facilities, a 24/7 ambulance service and a CCTV-monitored campus.
The advertisement also states that the university has 85% or more PhD faculty and provides opportunities for national and international conferences.
How to Apply for SAU Admissions 2027
Applicants can register online through the SAU admission portal and complete the application form with their personal and academic details.
A valid CNIC, email address, mobile number, and WhatsApp number are required for registration. The university has also listed a Rs. 3,000 non-refundable processing fee per seat, category or quota, which candidates can pay through HBL or 1Bill.
Applicants must upload the required documents, payment receipt or challan, and two passport-size photographs with a white or blue background.
Candidates from outside Sindh may apply against reserved or merit seats through the relevant nominating agency. The university states that self-finance applications may also be considered.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Great Wall Motor (GWM) showcased its latest pickup trucks, the Poer P300 and Poer P500, at the Pakistan Auto Parts Show. The two plug-in hybrid electric vehicle (PHEV) pickups combine off-road capability, premium interiors, and modern technology as GWM prepares for their potential launch in Pakistan.
GWM Poer P300 PHEV: A Rugged Hybrid Pickup
The GWM Poer P300 is designed as a heavy-duty lifestyle pickup focused on utility, off-road driving, and everyday practicality. It features a bold exterior with a high bonnet, black front grille, painted bumpers, crystal LED headlights, integrated daytime running lights, and LED fog lamps.
The pickup comes with large wheel arch cladding for additional protection during off-road use. It rides on 18-inch wheels with all-terrain tyres and uses a front double-wishbone suspension setup.
The cargo bed features a scratch-resistant and waterproof liner, along with a damper-assisted tailgate and an additional bed cover with dedicated dampers.
Built on a ladder-frame chassis, the Poer P300 uses rear leaf-spring suspension and offers a towing capacity of up to 3,500 kg.
Interior and Technology
Inside, the Poer P300 features a dark-themed cabin with soft-touch materials on key areas.
The pickup comes with a 12-inch digital instrument cluster and a 14-inch touchscreen infotainment system with Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, and a 360-degree camera system.
The cabin also includes an aviation-style gear selector, physical controls for four-wheel-drive modes, a rear differential lock, drive modes, and an electronic parking brake.
Other features include dual-zone climate control, ventilated front seats, powered driver seat adjustment, paddle shifters, and a sunroof.
 
GWM Poer P500 PHEV: A Luxury Pickup Truck
The GWM Poer P500 takes a more premium approach, borrowing design inspiration from the GWM Tank 500 SUV.
Compared with the P300, the P500 features a more refined exterior with body-coloured panels, a chrome-accented grille, satin silver window surrounds, and Tank 500-inspired LED headlights.
It also comes with 18-inch wheels, red brake calipers, and a 540-degree surround-view camera system.
Unlike the P300’s leaf springs, the P500 uses a rear coilover suspension setup designed to provide a more SUV-like ride.
The pickup also features a split tailgate that can open conventionally or horizontally from the centre.
Premium Interior Inspired by Tank 500
The P500 cabin features an executive-style layout with wood-inspired trim, soft-touch leather surfaces, and ambient lighting.
It comes with perforated leather seats, while the second row offers heated and ventilated seats, a Boss Seat adjustment function, and dedicated rear air-conditioning vents.
The pickup also includes a premium Infinity sound system and a panoramic sunroof.

GWM displayed the Poer P300 and Poer P500 at the Pakistan Auto Parts Show to showcase its upcoming product lineup and evaluate consumer response.

Merit and Selection
The admission notice sets out a merit-based selection process for eligible candidates. Candidates with FSc Pre-Medical qualifications will have their merit calculated under the prescribed formula, while Matric Science candidates will also be considered according to the stated admission criteria.
The notice also provides additional marks for Hafiz-e-Quran candidates under the applicable rules.

Khyber Medical University (KMU) has announced the schedule for its Centralized Admission Test (CAT) 2026 for admissions to relevant undergraduate programs for the 2026-27 academic session.
According to the university’s latest admission notice, the second CAT will be held on October 3 and 4, 2026, while candidates can register until September 28. KMU has also scheduled the third CAT for November 7 and 8, with the registration deadline set for November 2, 2026.

items.title: How Golden Fertilizer Became Farmers Choice Brand In Nigeria
items.summary:
Nigeria’s agricultural productivity conversation is shifting. For years, much of the attention around agricultural inputs has understandably focused on access: whether farmers can obtain fertilizer, improved seeds and other essential inputs at an affordable cost in rural communities.
But getting inputs into farmers’ hands is only one part of the productivity equation. How effectively are those inputs translating into greater value for farmers?
For a farmer investing scarce resources in another planting season, the true value of an agricultural input is measured in the field; in the health of the crop, the quality of the produce, the yield at harvest, and the income generated from every hectare cultivated. This thinking is increasingly reflected in Nigeria’s wider agricultural policy direction. items.content:
Nigeria’s agricultural productivity conversation is shifting. For years, much of the attention around agricultural inputs has understandably focused on access: whether farmers can obtain fertilizer, improved seeds and other essential inputs at an affordable cost in rural communities.
But getting inputs into farmers’ hands is only one part of the productivity equation. How effectively are those inputs translating into greater value for farmers?
For a farmer investing scarce resources in another planting season, the true value of an agricultural input is measured in the field; in the health of the crop, the quality of the produce, the yield at harvest, and the income generated from every hectare cultivated. This thinking is increasingly reflected in Nigeria’s wider agricultural policy direction. Under the Nigerian Farmers Soil Health Scheme, the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, and the International Institute of Tropical Agriculture (IITA) are advancing vital input knowledge needs. Such needs as; crop- and location-specific fertilizer recommendations, improved fertilizer efficiency, and the principles of applying the right nutrient source at the right rate, time, and place. The direction recognizes a fundamental point, agricultural productivity depends not only on access to inputs, but on farmers having the right inputs and using them effectively.
Against this backdrop, the responsibility of agricultural brands has evolved. For Golden Fertilizer, a business entity of FMN Agro Ltd, this responsibility forms the bedrock of their Yield Transformation Agenda.
Long known to smallholders and commercial growers as “The Farmers’ Friend,” Golden Fertilizer has moved beyond a transactional relationship with growers. Its Yield Transformation approach connects high-quality inputs with agronomic education, improved farming practices, and practical field demonstrations designed to support farmers in achieving better productivity and returns. The philosophy is straightforward, the value of a bag of fertilizer is realized when the right product, applied appropriately and supported by the right farming practices, contributes to healthier crops, stronger yields, and more sustainable farmer livelihoods.
The proof of this approach is evident in the testimonies of the farmers themselves. For James Zubairu, the difference was visible in the condition of his farm:
“Sincerely speaking, we have seen the blessing in it and we have also seen how beautiful the farm came out. Golden Fertilizer is the original fertilizer we know. We thank God they brought the fertilizer back again. The farm is good and beautiful,” Zubairu noted.
Sadatu Abubakar similarly pointed to the appearance of her beans and maize, describing crops that attracted the attention of people around her.
“The truth is, this fertilizer that was given to us from the company is very good. Anyone who sees our beans produce admires it. Just like when they see our maize plants, people ask us where we get it from,” Abubakar said.
For Usman Musa, his experience translated into a willingness to recommend Golden Fertilizer to other growers.
“I would like to advise fellow farmers that any farmer who wants to farm and really see results should use Golden Fertilizer.It will give you more quality and also boost your farm. Your farm will be good, and you will get good and plenty of farm produce”, Musa remarked.
These individual experiences are supported by a broader approach to farmer engagement. Golden Fertilizer’s 2026 Green Field Days, its annual farmer training and empowerment programme, provide one example of how the Yield Transformation Agenda is being taken directly into farming communities. Held across Kano, Bauchi, Gombe, Adamawa, Kaduna, and Niger States, the program reached more than 7,500 farmers cultivating approximately 3,000 hectares across 25 Local Government Areas, with a focus on maize and soybean production.
Rather than just listening to lectures, farmers participated in practical sessions around seed selection, fertilizer application, and improved crop management.
The field demonstrations combined improved maize and soybean varieties with tailored nutrition solutions, including Golden Fertilizer NPK 20-10-10 and the Golden Soybean Blend. This illustrates an integrated approach in which the quality of the input works alongside appropriate application, seed selection, and agronomic knowledge. To date, Golden Fertilizer’s broader initiatives have reached over 230,000 farmers across Nigeria, combining access to agricultural inputs with training, technical knowledge, and practical engagement intended to improve productivity and farm profitability. The scale of this engagement also gains context within the broader agricultural footprint of Flour Mills of Nigeria (FMN). Operating through FMN Agro Ltd, Golden Fertilizer leverages FMN’s integrated farm-to-table model spanning local sourcing, processing, and the manufacture and nationwide distribution of agro-inputs, including seeds and fertilizer.
This wider value-chain presence matters because Nigeria’s agricultural productivity challenge cannot be solved through any one intervention in isolation. For fertilizer brands, this raises the bar. Product quality remains fundamental, but the relationship with farmers increasingly extends beyond the point of purchase. Value is also reflected in how effectively farmers are supported to understand their inputs, improve their practices, and maximize the potential of each planting season.
This is where Quality, Yield Transformation, and “The Farmer’s Friend” Promise converge for Golden Fertilizer. Superior Quality provides the foundation. Yield Transformation defines the approach to turning those inputs into stronger agricultural outcomes. And the “Farmer’s Friend” promise solidifies the lasting relationship Golden Fertilizer has with the people responsible for converting those inputs into food, livelihoods, and economic value.
Nigeria’s next agricultural gains will depend on many factors, but one principle is increasingly clear: inputs must deliver on the farm, and Golden Fertilizer’s strongest validation remains the farmers who continue to choose, use, and recommend the brand based on the abundance of their harvests.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Snapdeal parent AceVector has raised ₹189 Cr from anchor investors ahead of the opening of its initial public offering (IPO) tomorrow (September 25).
The company allotted 5.91 Cr shares to anchor investors at ₹32 apiece, the upper end of its IPO price band.
Only two domestic mutual funds — Helios Mutual Fund and Taurus Ethical Fund — participated in the anchor round, together picking up 93.75 Lakh shares, or 15.87% of the allocation. Helios acquired 62.48 Lakh shares through two schemes, while Taurus bought 31.25 Lakh shares worth ₹10 Cr.
Negen Undiscovered Value Fund, a Category III AIF operated by Negen Investment Trust, was the largest anchor investor, picking up 1.25 Cr shares, or 21.16% of the round, for ₹39.99 Cr. Singularity Growth Opportunities Fund II invested ₹26.99 Cr, while TIMF Holdings acquired 15.63 Lakh shares.
With the anchor round completed, AceVector’s ₹420 Cr IPO will open for public subscription on September 25 and close on September 29. The company is expected to list on the stock exchanges on October 5.
The IPO values the Snapdeal and Unicommerce parent at ₹1,741.4 Cr and comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹287 Cr and an offer for sale (OFS) of 4.16 Cr shares.
The public issue marks AceVector’s second attempt to list after its earlier plans were shelved in 2022.
SoftBank-backed Starfish I Pte Ltd, AceVector’s largest shareholder with a 30.68% stake, has cut its proposed OFS by 34.8% to 2.76 Cr shares from 4.23 Cr shares in the company’s draft prospectus. Starfish I is part of AceVector’s promoter group.
Three Nexus-affiliated entities — Nexus India Direct Investments II, Nexus Opportunity Fund Ltd and Nexus Ventures III Ltd — will collectively sell 86.96 Lakh shares, down from 1.33 Cr shares proposed earlier. Foxconn-backed FIH Business Global will sell 17.41 Lakh shares.
Meanwhile, individual investor Priyanka Shreevar Kheruka, who had proposed to sell 19.37 Lakh shares in the draft prospectus, will not participate in the OFS. Other selling shareholders include Jason Ashok Kothari, Rupen Investment and Industries and Centaurus Trading and Investments.
AceVector plans to deploy a significant portion of the fresh capital towards Snapdeal, its value-focused ecommerce marketplace.
The company has earmarked ₹132 Cr for marketing and business promotion over till FY29. This includes ₹40 Cr in FY27, ₹55 Cr in FY28 and ₹37 Cr in FY29.
The spending will cover digital and social media campaigns, influencer-led promotions, product discovery and performance marketing, with a focus on building Snapdeal’s presence among value-conscious consumers in Tier 2 and smaller cities.
AceVector will also invest ₹50 Cr in Snapdeal’s technology infrastructure. The funds will be used for cloud computing, storage, networking, software and related technology requirements. According to the company, these investments will support customer engagement and retention through personalised recommendations, improvements to the shopping experience and A/B testing.
AceVector expects these requirements to increase as Snapdeal’s user engagement grows and the company expands its use of AI-based capabilities.
The remaining more than ₹100 Cr of the IPO proceeds has been earmarked for acquisitions. However, AceVector has not identified any specific acquisition targets, meaning the deployment will depend on opportunities that emerge after the listing.

items.summary:
Dozens of delegates streamed out as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday mounted a forceful defence of Israel's actions in the region at the United Nations, seeking to counter growing international isolation ahead of elections he could lose.
As Netanyahu took to the rostrum, officials walked out of the General Assembly meeting of world leaders in protest, prompting him to describe them as "moral cowards".
Dozens of delegates walked out of the assembly hall as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began his UN General Assembly address on Thursday. Netanyahu’s speech came as Israel faced growing criticism from world leaders at this year’s assembly over its genocidal war in Gaza. pic.twitter.com/QA5nUnI8cM

The
items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Dozens of delegates streamed out as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday mounted a forceful defence of Israel's actions in the region at the United Nations, seeking to counter growing international isolation ahead of elections he could lose.
As Netanyahu took to the rostrum, officials walked out of the General Assembly meeting of world leaders in protest, prompting him to describe them as "moral cowards".
Dozens of delegates walked out of the assembly hall as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu began his UN General Assembly address on Thursday. Netanyahu’s speech came as Israel faced growing criticism from world leaders at this year’s assembly over its genocidal war in Gaza. pic.twitter.com/QA5nUnI8cM
— Al Jazeera Breaking News (@AJENews) September 24, 2026
Before Netanyahu's speech, large crowds demonstrated near UN headquarters and elsewhere in New York, against his appearance and accusing him of committing "genocide" in Gaza.
The protests included anti-Zionist Orthodox Jews carrying signs describing Netanyahu as a "war criminal", as well as American and Israeli Jewish opposition groups and Western and Palestinian organisations opposing the genocidal war.
Delegates walk out as Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addresses the 81st United Nations General Assembly at UN headquarters in New York City, US, September 24, 2026. REUTERS
The Yedioth Ahronoth Israeli newspaper said that "large crowds" left the hall immediately after Netanyahu took the podium, before he began speaking.
Israel's Channel 12 also published an image showing most of the hall's seats empty.
Read More: Netanyahu's fleeting visit to New York mirrors strained US ties
Netanyahu has been wanted by the ICC since 2024.
He used his UN address to berate New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani for calling him a war criminal, Western European leaders for what he called succumbing to the "antisemitic mobs", and Qatar and Turkiye for allegedly spreading lies about his country.
"You tried to stop me from coming here. You tried. You tried to silence me. Well, you can't silence me. You can't silence the truth," Netanyahu said of Mamdani.
Mamdani campaigned for office on a promise to have Netanyahu arrested for alleged war crimes should he visit the largest US city, but later said he had determined he lacked the legal authority to do so.
This week, Mamdani described Netanyahu as "the architect of a horrific genocide against Palestinians".
Addressing the mayor directly after a feud in the run-up to his arrival in New York, Netanyahu falsely accused Mamdani of supporting Hamas.
"To all those spreading these lies about my country and about our brave soldiers, whether they sit in this hall or in the office of the antisemitic mayor of New York, I say this: Shame on you!"
Netanyahu, who rejected the war crimes allegations, was making his first visit to New York since Mamdani took office in January.
In a statement, Mamdani said: "As he has done time and again, Prime Minister Netanyahu used his speech to repeat baseless lies ​meant to sanitise his genocide of Palestinians. Yet no lie can change the fact that he remains the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant alleging war crimes and crimes against humanity.”
Demonstrators protest ahead of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's address to the United Nations 81st General Assembly in New York City, US, September 24, 2026. REUTERS
With general elections less than five weeks away, Netanyahu spoke for about 40 minutes in what amounted to a campaign-style speech, broadcast live in evening prime time on all four of Israel's main television channels.
Ahead of his speech, Netanyahu's government paid to place 500 pro-Israel and anti-Iran billboards and dozens of trucks carrying messages in support of Israel across Manhattan, his office said in a statement.
Netanyahu, who is seen losing power in opinion polls, showcased what he said was Israel's fight on seven fronts.
Israel's longest-serving prime minister has in the past made a visual spectacle of his UN appearances, using charts, diagrams and props to warn of Iran's nuclear programme, which Tehran says is for civilian purposes.
Read More: How would Jewish supremacists act?
On Thursday, he held up a pager in reference to an attack that crippled Iran-backed Hezbollah members in Lebanon and showed a Starlink satellite internet receiver, which he said he would leave for the Iranian delegation.
"So when they inevitably defect, they too will be able to freely tell their story on social media," he said, adding that it was only a matter of time before the Iranian authorities would be toppled by the people.
Street protests in New York
Anti-Israel protesters took to New York City streets. Several hundred protesters gathered near the United Nations, with dozens blocking traffic and chanting, "Stop arming Israel, let Gaza live" and "Stop arming Israel, let Iran live."
Police detained them.
The election campaign in Israel is unfolding amid mounting criticism of the country's Gaza war.
Netanyahu was making a short visit to the United States for his UN address and, unusually, without a planned meeting with US President Donald Trump, whom he praised during his speech.
"We will continue to defend our state. We will continue to win because we have no other choice. In this battle against the barbarians, we've had no greater partner than President Trump. I thank him. I thank him for his bold leadership," he said.
Deepening isolation
Israel has faced deepening diplomatic isolation since launching its war in Gaza ​in response to the Hamas-led ⁠attacks on Israel nearly three years ago.
Netanyahu is unable to travel to many countries because of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant, issued against him and his then-defence minister as well as the then-military commander of Hamas in 2024.
Earlier this month, once-steadfast allies Britain, France and Canada announced sanctions targeting Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, which drew a muted response from Washington.
"The leaders of these countries have chosen to succumb to the antisemitic ⁠mobs. They've chosen ​weakness. They've chosen appeasement," Netanyahu said.
He played down worsening violence in the occupied West Bank by Israeli settlers, describing it as "a ​handful of young juvenile delinquents, about 150 in number, who throw stones, who chop down olive trees".
"Occasionally ... they lit some fires. I can't stand that. I won't stand for vigilantism. We're a country of law."

Galaxy S27 dan Galaxy S27+ disebut akan hadir dengan RAM 12GB serta pilihan storage 256GB dan 512GB. Jika informasi tersebut akurat, maka Samsung berpotensi menjadikan 256GB sebagai kapasitas dasar baru untuk lini Galaxy S reguler.
Langkah ini sejalan dengan tren di segmen flagship premium mulai menawarkan ruang penyimpanan lebih besar sebagai standar, terutama untuk mengakomodasi ukuran aplikasi, foto, video, serta fitur berbasis AI yang semakin banyak memanfaatkan penyimpanan lokal.
Meski demikian, raksasa teknologi asal Korea Selatan itu belum memberikan konfirmasi resmi terkait konfigurasi memori di varian standar dari Galaxy S27 series tersebut.
Model Pro dan Ultra Pakai Memori Generasi Baru
Bocoran yang sama juga menyebut Galaxy S27 Pro akan tersedia dalam konfigurasi RAM 12GB dengan pilihan storage hingga 1TB. Sementara itu, Galaxy S27 Ultra dikabarkan akan tetap menjadi model dengan spesifikasi tertinggi. 
Varian tersebut hadir dengan opsi RAM hingga 16GB yang dipasangkan dengan storage 1TB.
Selain kapasitas lebih besar, Samsung juga dikabarkan sedang mempertimbangkan penggunaan standar memori LPDDR6 dan penyimpanan UFS 5.1 untuk model tertentu dalam keluarga Galaxy S27.
Jika terealisasi, kombinasi tersebut berpotensi menghadirkan peningkatan bandwidth memori dan kecepatan transfer data dibanding generasi sebelumnya. Namun hingga saat ini belum jelas apakah teknologi tersebut akan tersedia di seluruh model atau hanya varian kelas atas.
Fokus Samsung Bukan Lagi Menambah RAM
Menariknya, bocoran terbaru tidak menunjukkan peningkatan kapasitas RAM yang agresif pada sebagian besar model Galaxy S27. RAM 12GB disebut masih menjadi konfigurasi utama untuk model reguler, Plus, dan Pro. Sementara peningkatan ke 16GB tampaknya tetap eksklusif untuk konfigurasi tertinggi Galaxy S27 Ultra.
Hal ini menandakan perusahaan mungkin bakal lebih fokus pada peningkatan efisiensi, kecepatan memori, dan kapasitas penyimpanan dibanding sekadar menambah jumlah RAM.
Tentu saja, seluruh informasi tersebut masih berada dalam tahap rumor dan dapat berubah sebelum pengumuman resmi dilakukan. Samsung sendiri diperkirakan baru akan memperkenalkan Galaxy S27 Series pada awal tahun depan.
Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra Dikabarkan Bawa Baterai 5.700 mAh
Samsung Galaxy S27 Pro dan Galaxy S27 Ultra kembali menjadi sorotan setelah kedua smartphone tersebut disebut telah mendapatkan sertifikasi 3C di China. Sertifikasi tersebut mengungkap dukungan pengisian daya kabel hingga 60W untuk keduanya. Angka ini sama seperti yang ditawarkan Galaxy S26 Ultra, sehingga Samsung tampaknya belum melakukan peningkatan pada sektor kecepatan charging.
Perubahan yang lebih menarik justru terlihat pada kapasitas baterai. Berdasarkan informasi dari sertifikasi 3C, Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra disebut memiliki baterai dengan kapasitas terukur 5.534 mAh. Angka tersebut kemungkinan akan dipasarkan sebagai kapasitas tipikal 5.700 mAh, atau meningkat sekitar 700 mAh dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya.
Kemudian, Samsung Galaxy S27 Pro juga disebut membawa peningkatan kapasitas baterai dengan rating 5.087 mAh, yang kemungkinan dipasarkan sebagai 5.200 mAh. Jika informasi tersebut benar, kapasitas baterainya bahkan akan lebih besar dibandingkan Galaxy S26 Ultra, meski S27 Pro memiliki bodi yang lebih kecil.
Kapasitas Baterai Naik, Charging Masih Sama
Peningkatan baterai menjadi perubahan yang cukup menarik karena Samsung selama beberapa generasi terakhir relatif konservatif dalam meningkatkan kapasitas baterai flagship. Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra yang disebut membawa kapasitas tipikal 5.700 mAh akan memberikan tambahan sekitar 700 mAh dibandingkan pendahulunya.
Namun, peningkatan tersebut belum diikuti perubahan pada teknologi pengisian daya. Sertifikasi 3C menunjukkan Galaxy S27 Pro dan S27 Ultra sama-sama mendukung charging kabel 60W. Artinya, Samsung masih mempertahankan angka yang sama seperti Galaxy S26 Ultra.
Artikel berjudul Bocoran Galaxy S27 Series Muncul, Apa yang Berubah pada RAM dan Storage? yang ditulis oleh Yus Lianson pertama kali tampil di Gizmologi.id

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
For insurance distributors, the commission earned on every policy is central to their business model. It determines how much they can spend to acquire customers, the products they prioritise, and the economics of their partnerships with insurers.
This equation may now change.
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has proposed a sweeping overhaul of the insurance distribution ecosystem in its consultation paper ‘Recalibrating Economics Of Insurance Distribution’.
The proposals come more than three years after IRDAI removed product-wise commission caps in April 2023 and shifted to an expenses of management (EoM) framework, giving insurers greater flexibility in determining distributor payouts.
However, the regulator now believes that commissions and other distributor payments have risen disproportionately and is proposing to bring back product-level ceilings, tighten insurers’ overall expense limits, and scrutinise indirect incentives.
The scale of the potential disruption was reflected in the stock market today. Shares of Policybazaar parent PB Fintech ended the session 35.98% lower at ₹1,210 apiece on the BSE.
Turtlemint shares remained locked at the 20% lower circuit, ending at ₹109.10 apiece. The stock also touched its lowest level since the insurtech company’s listing in June. HDFC Life Insurance Company’s shares plunged 6.13%, while those of ICICI Prudential Life Insurance fell 4.23%.
Brokerages said the proposed limits could sharply compress the economics of insurance distribution, particularly in categories where prevailing payouts are far above the suggested caps.
For insurtechs and other insurance distributors, the changes could affect revenue from health, motor, and life insurance policies. They may also force platforms to rethink customer acquisition expenditure, insurer partnerships, sales incentives, and product prioritisation.
However, the impact would vary widely across products and distribution channels.
The Commission Reset: From Flexible Payouts To Product-Wise Caps
The biggest proposed change is the return of product-level commission limits. IRDAI has suggested separate ceilings based on the insurance segment, distribution channel, product complexity, and effort involved in selling and servicing a policy.
Under the proposed framework, open-architecture insurance distribution entities (IDEs) would include insurance brokers such as Policybazaar and Turtlemint’s insurance broking arm, as well as banks and NBFCs registered as corporate agents. Since these entities can distribute products from multiple insurers, they would generally face lower commission ceilings than individual agents and other associates operating under closed architecture.
For general insurance, the proposed caps include:
New-vehicle third-party motor insurance: Nil for IDEs and 2.5% for agents and associates.
New-vehicle own-damage, personal accident, and legal liability insurance: 5% for IDEs and 10% for agents and associates.
Old-vehicle third-party insurance: 2.5% for IDEs, 5% for agents and associates, and 2.5% for garages.
Old-vehicle own-damage, personal accident, and legal liability insurance: 10% for IDEs, 15% for agents and associates, and 10% for garages.
Individual health insurance: 15% for IDEs and 20% for agents on new policies. The proposed limits fall to 5% and 10%, respectively, for renewals and ported policies.
Group health insurance: 2.5% for IDEs and 5% for agents, subject to monetary ceilings of ₹100 Lakh. Hospitals would face a 1% cap, subject to a ₹25 Lakh ceiling.
Marine cargo insurance: 10% for IDEs and 15% for agents.
Marine hull insurance: 10% for both IDEs and agents.
Miscellaneous retail insurance: 15% for IDEs and 17.5% for agents.
Miscellaneous corporate and group insurance: 10% for IDEs and 15% for agents.
For risks below ₹500 Cr, IDEs could earn commissions of up to 7.5%, while agents could earn up to 10%. These limits would fall to 6.25% and 7%, respectively, for risks between ₹500 Cr and ₹2,500 Cr, and to 5% and 5.5% for risks above ₹2,500 Cr.
The framework is based on the effort required to sell and service a product. Mandatory or near-mandatory products would attract nil or low commissions, while products requiring greater selling and servicing efforts would have higher ceilings.
Why Motor Insurance Faces A Bigger Reset
Motor insurance is among the segments likely to be most affected. IRDAI’s analysis found that motor insurance currently carries an average commission rate of 24%, with payouts ranging from 13% to 50%.
Motor insurance commissions increased 259% between FY23 and FY25, compared with a 34% rise in premiums during the period.
The proposed ceilings, particularly the nil commission for IDEs selling third-party insurance for new vehicles, could therefore weigh on distributors with significant exposure to motor insurance.
It may also reduce the ability of distributors to subsidise customer acquisition or offer incentives using the high commissions generated from own-damage and bundled motor policies.
What Changes For Health Insurance
The difference between prevailing payouts and the proposed ceilings is also significant in health insurance, which is among the most important categories for digital insurance distributors.
IRDAI has proposed limiting commissions for IDEs to 15% of the premium on new individual health insurance policies and 5% on renewals and portability. Agents would be permitted commissions of up to 20% on new policies and 10% on renewals and portability.
Jefferies said new-business health insurance commissions could decline to 15%-20% from more than 30%, while renewal commissions could fall to 5%-10%.
The sharper ceiling on renewals could particularly affect distributors that have spent heavily to acquire policyholders on the expectation of earning recurring commissions over multiple years.
Platforms may consequently have to lower acquisition costs, charge separately for some services, or generate more revenue from claims assistance, technology, lending, and other financial products.
What Changes For Life Insurance
For individual non-linked and linked life insurance policies, the proposed first-year commission limits would range from 5% to 20% for IDEs and 6.25% to 25% for agents, depending on the premium payment term.
For policies with a premium payment term of at least 10 years, the proposed caps would be 20% for IDEs and 25% for agents. Renewal commissions would generally be lower, with a maximum ceiling of 7% for these policies.
Other proposed life insurance commission limits include:
Individual pure-term, single-premium policies: 7.5% for IDEs and 10% for agents.
Individual pure-term, multi-year policies: 25% for IDEs and 30% for agents in the first year, followed by renewal caps of 7.5% and 10%, respectively.
Group pure-term, single-premium policies: 1.5% for IDEs and 2% for agents, subject to monetary ceilings.
Single-premium pension, deferred annuity, and immediate annuity policies: 0.5% for IDEs and 0.75% for agents.
Annuities purchased using NPS proceeds: Nil commission.
Loan-linked individual pure-term policies: 2% for single-premium policies and 2.5% in the first year for multi-year policies, with a 1% renewal cap.
The low ceilings proposed for loan-linked insurance are significant for banks, NBFCs, and embedded-insurance distributors, which frequently sell such policies when issuing loans.
Citi identified credit-linked insurance as one of the most vulnerable categories. According to the brokerage, payouts for group credit life insurance have risen to nearly 45%, while commissions in NBFC-led channels average around 42%.
Bringing these payouts down to the proposed levels would therefore involve a far steeper reduction than the headline commission caps suggest.
It Is Not Just About Commissions
IRDAI has also proposed lowering insurers’ overall EoM limits, which cap the share of premiums that insurers can spend on commissions and other operating expenses.
For life insurers, EoM would have to fall to 15% of gross direct premium income within two years and 12.5% within five years. For general insurers, the proposed ceiling would decline to 25% within two years and 20% within five years.
The regulator said the existing framework has failed to deliver sufficient cost discipline.
The proposals would also increase regulatory scrutiny of insurers and distributors.
All insurers would have to undergo cost audits covering expenses and payments to intermediaries. IDEs with annual insurance-related revenue exceeding ₹100 Cr would also require cost audits, while those with revenue above ₹50 Cr would have to disclose financial information, including revenue, expenses, related-party payments, and PAT.
IRDAI also wants to simplify the distribution structure into three categories: insurance distribution entities (IDEs), insurance distribution persons (IDPs) and market infrastructure institutions (MIIs).
IDEs would have a proposed minimum capital requirement of ₹10 Lakh and could operate under an open architecture, allowing them to distribute products from multiple insurers. Distributors would also get greater flexibility to undertake other permitted financial and non-financial activities.
For digital insurance, MIIs such as Bima Sugam could serve as neutral digital marketplaces where customers compare and purchase policies. The proposed Public Insurance Registry (PIR) would support policy discovery, verification, portability, transparency, and grievance redressal.
This could change how insurtechs acquire customers. If more customers discover and buy insurance through common digital platforms, distributors may have to compete more on technology, service and product discovery rather than customer access alone.
Tighter Rules To Curb Mis-Selling
The consultation paper also targets practices that may encourage forced or unsuitable insurance sales. Banks and NBFCs registered as IDEs would not be allowed to compulsorily bundle insurance with loans or other financial products.
If a lender offers a lower interest rate to customers buying insurance, it would have to disclose the interest rates available with and without the policy. Customers would also have to be allowed to choose another insurer.
IRDAI has also proposed restrictions on incentives for bank and NBFC employees selling insurance, including foreign trips, luxury gifts, milestone bonuses, and contest rewards.
Each policy would have to be linked to the salesperson or agent responsible for the sale. The regulator has also proposed making mis-selling information available through the PIR and allowing insurers to claw back commissions in such cases.
The immediate risk for insurance distribution platforms is lower revenue per policy in segments where commissions are currently well above the proposed ceilings.
The sell-off in PB Fintech and Turtlemint reflects the market’s initial assessment of this commission gap. However, the final impact will depend on whether IRDAI retains the proposed ceilings following industry consultations or softens them in response to the pushback anticipated by brokerages.
The proposals are not final. IRDAI has invited comments from stakeholders until October 25, following which the final framework will determine their impact on insurance distributors and their business models.
Edited by Vinaykumar Rai

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
IPO-bound fintech startup Navi saw its net loss for the fiscal year FY26 widen by 268.7% to ₹465.99 from ₹126.4 Cr in the prior fiscal year.
The bottom line swelled despite a 16.2% uptick in Navi’s top line, with its operating revenue for the fiscal increasing to ₹2,981.7 Cr from ₹2,565 Cr in the year-ago fiscal. Including other income of ₹108.9 Cr, Navi’s total income for the year stood at ₹3,090.6 Cr.
While the company’s total expense for the fiscal crossed the ₹3,500 Cr mark, its tax expenses halved YoY to ₹42.2 Cr.
In terms of operational metrics, Navi claims its FY26 lending book grew 57.2% YoY to ₹13,138 Cr. Meanwhile, its monthly transacting users more than doubled to 2.9 Cr.
Loan disbursements in the fiscal also grew 73% YoY to ₹23,332 Cr while its assets under management amounted to ₹19,740 Cr. Furthermore, its gross and net NPA ratios also declined to 1.25% and 0.16% respectively.
Important to note that Navi is India’s fourth largest UPI player, commanding 3.5% market share and processing about 80 Cr transactions monthly.
As per a report by CareEdge Ratings, Navi turned profitable on PBT basis in Q1 FY27, registering a profit of ₹104 Cr . As per a report by CareEdge Ratings, Navi’s total income for the quarter stood ₹1,165 Cr.
Based on the company’s improving QoQ profitability status, CareEdge Ratings upgraded Navi’s credit rating to CARE A+. Important to note that the ratings agency cited unaudited financials from Navi for the quarter.
“Ratings continue to derive strength from Navi’s experienced promoter, Sachin Bansal, its scalable technology-led business model and integrated financial services ecosystem, supported by adequate capitalisation and a diversified resource profile,” the ratings agency said.
However, it flagged asset quality risks due to high concentration of personal loans, comprising 92% of Navi’s AUM.
Founded by Sachin Bansal and Ankit Agarwal in 2018, Navi offers financial products across lending, insurance, mutual funds and UPI payments. Its lending business provides home loans, personal loans and loans against property through its NBFC and partner institutions.
Bansal stepped down as the startup’s CEO in February 2025 and transitioned into the role of executive chairman while Rajiv Naresh took over as CEO. Abhishek Dwivedi was named CEO of its NBFC arm Navi Finserv.
Notably, the fintech startup raised its maiden institutional funding round for the first time last month when it announced that it was raising $100 Mn from global tech investor Prosus, subject to regulatory approval.
According to reports, it is also gearing up to file its IPO papers by December as it seeks to raise ₹3,000 Cr through a fresh issue of shares. Notably, the startup earlier filed for an IPO in 2022, but eventually deferred its plans to list on the bourses.
Where Did Navi Spend In FY26?
In FY26, Navi’s total expenses grew faster than its top line, surging 28.8% YoY to ₹3,514.4 Cr from ₹2,729.1 Cr in FY25.
Finance Costs: Finance costs increased 32.7% to ₹1,123.2 Cr from ₹846.6 Cr.
Other Expenses: Navi’s other expenses grew 79.5% to ₹1,111.6 Cr from ₹619.3 Cr.
Employee Benefits Expense: Navi’s staff-related expenditure grew 13.4% to ₹619.2 Cr from ₹546 Cr.
Impairment On Financial Instruments: Impairment costs decreased 29.4% to ₹407.9 Cr from ₹577.6 Cr.
Policyholders’ Expense In Insurance Operations: Spending under this line item more than doubled to ₹199.7 Cr from ₹79.3 Cr.
Depreciation And Amortisation: Depreciation expenses slipped 12.7% to ₹52.8 Cr from ₹60.3 Cr.

items.title: Samsung Wallet Adds Fingerprint Authentication for UPI Payments Up to Rs 10,000 in India
items.summary: Samsung has introduced fingerprint-based authentication for UPI payments through Samsung Wallet in India. Galaxy users can authorise eligible transactions worth up to Rs. 10,000 without entering their UPI PIN. The company says the on-device authentication can help users avoid exposing their PIN while making payments in public and may reduce failures caused by incorrect PIN entries. Samsung Wallet also supports contactless card payments, bill payments and digital storage, while its Trips feature brings travel bookings and tickets together in a single timeline.

The actor is currently filming The Batman: Part II, which reunites him with director Matt Reeves following the 2022 original. Pattinson previously said he was excited to see how the new film develops.
The sequel will introduce several new cast members alongside returning performers. Scarlett Johansson and Sebastian Stan have joined the franchise, while Colin Farrell, Jeffrey Wright, Andy Serkis, Jayme Lawson, Gil Perez-Abraham, Sebastian Koch and Brian Tyree Henry are also set to appear.
Pattinson has had a busy 2026, with appearances in The Drama and The Odyssey already released. His portrayal of To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen in Primetime is scheduled to arrive on Friday, while Dune: Part Three is set for release on December 18.
Despite his demanding schedule, Pattinson said during the Venice Film Festival that he would have been “devastated to have dropped any of” his projects this year.
The Batman: Part II is scheduled to be released on October 1, 2027. Reeves returns as director, with Pattinson reprising his role as Bruce Wayne.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
easypaisa digital bank, Pakistan’s leading digital bank, has entered into a strategic partnership with Transsion, one of the world’s largest smartphone manufacturers, to make digital financial services more accessible for millions of Pakistanis.
As part of the initiative, the easypaisa app will come pre-installed on more than five million new smartphones across Transsion’s leading brands in Pakistan, including Infinix, TECNO, and itel, enabling users to access digital banking and financial services from the moment they activate their devices.
As smartphone adoption continues to rise across the country, with 3G/4G Device uptake reaching 71.6% , both organizations aim to leverage technology to bridge gaps in financial accessibility and drive greater participation in formal financial services. The partnership is particularly relevant for underserved and unbanked populations, many of whom are accessing smartphones and mobile internet for the first time.
The agreement was formally signed by Farhan Hassan, Chief Digital Officer, easypaisa digital bank, and Michael Wang, Vice President Global Partnerships, Transsion, in the presence of senior representatives from both organizations, in Islamabad.
Speaking on the occasion, Farhan Hassan, Chief Digital Officer, easypaisa digital bank, said, “At easypaisa, our mission has always been to simplify access to financial services and create opportunities for every Pakistani. This partnership with Transsion represents a significant step forward in making digital banking available at the point where consumers begin their digital journey. By embedding access to financial services directly onto smartphones, we are removing barriers, expanding reach, and bringing millions more people into the formal financial ecosystem. Together, we are helping accelerate Pakistan’s journey towards a more inclusive and digitally empowered economy.”
Muhammad Abdul Qadeer, Country Manager, Transsion Pakistan, said, “This partnership reflects the power of combining technology, scale and local market understanding to create meaningful digital experiences for consumers. With millions of smartphones entering the hands of Pakistani consumers through our brands, integrating access to trusted digital financial services such as easypaisa creates an opportunity to make financial inclusion a natural part of the smartphone journey. We are proud to collaborate with easypaisa on an initiative that can deliver meaningful impact at scale across Pakistan.”
The collaboration reflects a shared commitment to leveraging ecosystem partnerships to address barriers to financial inclusion and accelerate digital adoption. By combining Transsion’s extensive smartphone footprint with easypaisa’s comprehensive suite of digital banking products and services, the initiative is expected to strengthen customer acquisition, increase app penetration and drive greater user engagement with formal financial services.
As Pakistan’s first digital bank, easypaisa continues to expand its ecosystem through strategic partnerships that make financial services simpler, safer and more accessible. The pre-installation initiative represents another milestone in easypaisa’s efforts to reach underserved communities, empower consumers through technology and contribute to the development of a more connected and inclusive digital economy.
With over 60 million registered users and as the country’s first digital bank to commence commercial operations, easypaisa remains aligned with the State Bank of Pakistan’s vision of driving inclusive economic growth and continues to expand its range of financial products and services, catering not only to its existing users but also to millions who remain unbanked or underbanked.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Federal Minister for IT and Telecommunication Ms. Shaza Fatima Khawaja today inaugurated Huawei’s national-level Spare Parts Repair Center in Islamabad, aimed at building local repair capacity, reducing reliance on overseas services, and strengthening Pakistan’s telecom infrastructure. Huawei Pakistan CEO Mr. Ethan Sun was also present.
Speaking on the occasion, Federal Minister for IT and Telecommunication Ms. Shaza Fatima Khawaja said that Digital Nation Pakistan is built on the vision of developing a skilled, future-ready workforce that can compete and create value in global markets. She emphasized that Pakistan is moving decisively from being a consumer of technology to becoming a creator, builder and exporter of digital solutions, powered by the skills and innovation of its people. The Minister said that the establishment of the Repair Center represents an important step in strengthening Pakistan’s digital and telecom ecosystem, while creating greater local capacity and expertise. She appreciated Huawei’s investment in Pakistan and its commitment to knowledge transfer and capacity building, noting that such partnerships strengthen the resilience of the country’s telecom infrastructure and contribute to a more capable, connected and digitally empowered Pakistan.
Ethan Sun, CEO of Huawei Pakistan, said: “Huawei is proud to partner with Pakistan in building sustainable technical expertise. This center reflects our vision of translating global technology into local capability, ensuring faster service and stronger networks for the country.”
The Repair Center provides comprehensive repair, testing, troubleshooting, and maintenance for Huawei telecom equipment deployed nationwide. Local diagnosis and repair translate into faster turnaround times, greater network resilience, and significant cost savings — ultimately enhancing service for customers. Spanning 16 specialized repair desks, the facility supports over 180 equipment item codes across wireless, microwave, digital power, and access-network technologies, backed by Huawei’s proprietary diagnostic platforms for fault detection and load testing.
Staffed by more than 10 local hardware specialists with over twelve years of Huawei maintenance experience and expert-level training from Huawei’s China headquarters, the Center embodies Huawei’s knowledge-transfer model in action. It can process over 10,000 modules annually, returning more than 6,000 repaired components to service each year at an average success rate of approximately 60 percent — reducing both replacement needs and dependency on overseas repair. The facility’s local capability also allows Huawei to respond swiftly during national disasters or emergencies, when network continuity is critical.
In a nutshell, the Repair Center advances Pakistan’s telecom infrastructure by enabling faster local maintenance, reducing overseas repair dependency, and supporting network continuity during both emergencies and routine operations.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday said Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian had hailed Pakistan’s efforts for peace in the region and conveyed that the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) remained fully acceptable to Iran.
The prime minister was speaking to media representatives alongside his Lebanese counterpart Nawaf Salam after he met with the Iranian president on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Asked about the Islamabad MoU, under which Pakistan had mediated between Iran and the United States, the prime minister said Pakistan’s entire leadership was united in its resolve to further accelerate efforts for peace under the memorandum.
Read More: US and Iran discuss phased deal to reopen Hormuz and end US blockade, sources say
The premier also expressed particular concern over the situation in the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, saying brotherly and friendly countries were making efforts to reduce the tensions there.
He said he had also discussed the issue with the Iranian president during their meeting and told him that establishing peace in the region was an urgent need of the hour and that Pakistan would, as before, play its role in this regard.
PM Shehbaz Sharif talks to media
https://t.co/olJQsOpRCs
— Pakistan TV (@PakTVGlobal) September 24, 2026
PM Shehbaz said President Pezeshkian had appreciated Pakistan’s efforts and said the Islamabad MoU was still fully acceptable to Iran and that Tehran was ready to take it forward.
Shehbaz condemned the continued atrocities against Lebanon, calling them unacceptable. “Pakistan and Lebanon would work together to promote peace in the region jointly,” he said.
PM Shehbaz reaffirms readiness to play ‘constructive role’ for regional peace
Earlier, PM Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakistan’s readiness to continue playing a “sincere and constructive role” in support of regional peace during a meeting with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
The meeting took place a day before the premier is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly on Friday.
According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office, the two leaders reaffirmed the close and longstanding ties between Pakistan and Iran and underscored the need to further strengthen bilateral cooperation across all areas of mutual interest.
Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif met with the President of Islamic Republic of Iran, H.E. Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian today, on the sidelines of the 81st Session of United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York.
Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq… pic.twitter.com/BHkCwC2QNI
— Prime Minister's Office (@PakPMO) September 24, 2026
“Both leaders also exchanged views on the evolving regional situation,” the statement said.
The prime minister expressed deep concern over the prolonged conflict and emphasised the need for restraint, de-escalation and sustained diplomatic engagement to achieve lasting peace and stability in the region.
PM Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakistan’s readiness to continue playing a sincere and constructive role in support of regional peace and stability, while underscoring the importance of building on and implementing the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding.
“President Pezeshkian appreciated Pakistan’s principled diplomacy and concerted efforts for regional peace and security,” the statement said.
The Iranian president also underscored the enduring strength of Pakistan-Iran relations, rooted in shared history, culture and faith, and reaffirmed Tehran’s strong desire to further deepen multifaceted cooperation.
The two sides agreed to work for regional peace, security and prosperity, while underlining the importance of maintaining regular consultations and close coordination to address prevailing challenges and seize opportunities, the statement added.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Defence Minister Khawaja Muhammad Asif, SAPM Tariq Fatemi and senior officials from both sides were also present.
The prime minister later, in a post on X, said he had an "important exchange" on the evolving regional situation.
"I reiterated Pakistan’s deep concern over the prolonged conflict and stressed the urgent need for restraint, de-escalation and sustained diplomacy. We remain committed to building on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding and will continue to play a sincere and constructive role in the pursuit of lasting peace and stability in the region."
It was a pleasure to meet my dear brother, President Dr. Masoud Pezeshkian, in New York today on the sidelines of UNGA.
We reaffirmed the deep and longstanding bonds between Pakistan and Iran and our shared desire to further strengthen bilateral cooperation across all areas of… pic.twitter.com/MB0DkERKVj
— Shehbaz Sharif (@CMShehbaz) September 24, 2026
Pakistan has already made several mediation attempts during the seven-month-old conflict. Islamabad hosted indirect contacts between the United States and Iran and has continued to argue that the dispute cannot be resolved through military means.
Those efforts have gained urgency as the conflict has begun affecting both major maritime energy routes in the region. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely reduced, while the security situation around Bab el-Mandeb has also deteriorated.
The strait has become the central bargaining chip in efforts to end the nearly seven-month US-Iran conflict, with Iran seeking relief from the US blockade that is choking its economy and Washington seeking free passage for ships on the global oil supply route now ‌blocked by Tehran.
The latest escalation has also pushed up global energy prices and increased pressure on Gulf states to find a diplomatic way out.
Meanwhile, Washington and Tehran remain far from resolving their differences. US President Donald Trump has said he hopes the war with Iran is nearing an end, but negotiations remain stalled.
The talks face a big obstacle as neither side wants to be the first to surrender its leverage, according to comments to Reuters by two Iranian sources, two regional officials and two Western diplomatic sources, but behind Iran's stance is a recognition of the economic cost of prolonged confrontation.
A deal before the midterms could benefit Trump, as reopening Hormuz could ease tensions in the Gulf, contain oil prices and help bring down politically sensitive US gasoline prices.
Iran's chances of gaining much-needed economic relief may be greater while Trump still has a greater political incentive to strike a bargain.
However, former US negotiator Dennis Ross said he saw only ​a 30% chance of an agreement being reached before the vote, but that both sides may have stronger reasons to make a deal before than after the midterms.
After the midterms, Ross said, Trump may face fewer constraints and be more willing to intensify pressure or consider military options.

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
OpenAI kembali menjadi sorotan. Kali ini, sebuah agen AI milik perusahaan kecerdasan tersebut dilaporkan sukses mengakses file non-publik di portal statistik Medicare Australia.
Disebutkan, agen AI milik OpenAI tersebut berhasil menembus sistem keamanan portal tersebut ketika sedang dipakai untuk menjalankan tugas riset internal.
Insiden peretasan oleh AI tersebut diungkap langsung oleh Perdana Menteri Australia, Anthony Albanese. Menurut pemerintah Australia, kejadian tersebut berlangsung pada 18 Juni ketika model AI milik OpenAI sedang melakukan penelitian tentang pengeluaran obat-obatan publik di Australia.
Baca Juga: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Resmi, Qualcomm Kini Punya Dua Chip Flagship
Dilansir The Hacker News, Kamis (24/9/2026), agen AI yang mencoba memperoleh data dari Medicare Statistics Reporting Service Portal tersebut beberapa kali ditolak oleh sistem.
Alih-alih berhenti, model tersebut menemukan cara lain untuk mendapatkan informasi yang dicari dan akhirnya memperoleh akses tidak sah ke sebagian area portal.
“Agen AI menemukan jalan untuk melewati pembatasan tersebut,” kata Albanese dalam konferensi pers di New York. Pemerintah Australia menyebut model tersebut mengakses file publik maupun non-publik yang berada di dalam portal statistik tersebut.
Portal yang Diretas Agen AI Tidak Berisi Data Pasien
Meski terdengar mengkhawatirkan, pemerintah Australia menegaskan bahwa portal yang diakses bukan sistem yang menyimpan data pribadi pasien atau memproses klaim Medicare.
Sam Altman beri clue kehadiran Orion lewat ketikan di X.
Portal tersebut digunakan untuk menyediakan statistik agregat terkait layanan kesehatan dan pengeluaran pemerintah. Hingga saat ini, pemerintah maupun OpenAI menyatakan belum menemukan bukti bahwa data pribadi warga Australia ikut diakses.
OpenAI mengatakan informasi yang diperoleh model mencakup statistik kesehatan agregat dan nama file internal. Perusahaan juga menyebut tidak menemukan indikasi bahwa rekam medis pasien berhasil diakses.
OpenAI Dikritik karena Terlambat Memberi Tahu
Salah satu aspek yang mendapat sorotan adalah lamanya waktu notifikasi. Menurut pemerintah Australia, insiden terjadi pada Juni. OpenAI mengaku baru mengetahui aktivitas tersebut pada Agustus saat melakukan peninjauan terhadap perilaku model selama proses evaluasi internal.
Namun pemerintah Australia baru menerima pemberitahuan pada 10 September. Albanese mengatakan dirinya telah berbicara langsung dengan CEO OpenAI Sam Altman dan menyampaikan kekhawatiran pemerintah Australia terkait insiden tersebut. 
Ia juga mengkritik cara perusahaan menyampaikan laporan, yang disebut hanya dikirim melalui alamat email publik milik Services Australia. 
Pemerintah Australia kini membentuk tim investigasi yang melibatkan Australian Signals Directorate dan AI Safety Institute untuk menelusuri detail insiden tersebut.
Kenapa Kasus Peretasan Agen AI Ini Penting?
Kasus ini menarik karena berbeda dari insiden keamanan siber konvensional. Berdasarkan penjelasan pemerintah Australia, OpenAI tidak secara sengaja meminta model untuk membobol sistem pemerintah. Agen AI tersebut awalnya hanya ditugaskan mencari informasi terkait pengeluaran obat-obatan publik.
Namun ketika menemui hambatan, model tersebut mencari cara alternatif untuk mencapai tujuannya. OpenAI sendiri mengakui bahwa model melakukan tindakan yang tidak mereka maksudkan selama proses evaluasi internal.
Insiden ini muncul di tengah meningkatnya perhatian industri terhadap perilaku AI Agen yang semakin otonom. Dalam beberapa pekan terakhir, OpenAI juga mulai mempublikasikan laporan mengenai kasus-kasus “misaligned behavior” atau perilaku model yang tidak sepenuhnya mengikuti batasan yang diharapkan pengembang.
Meski dampak langsung insiden Medicare disebut relatif terbatas, kasus ini menjadi pengingat bahwa tantangan AI modern tidak lagi hanya soal akurasi jawaban. Semakin banyak sistem AI yang mampu menjalankan tugas secara mandiri, semakin penting pula memastikan model memahami batasan yang tidak boleh dilewati saat mengejar tujuan yang diberikan.
OpenAI Dorong AS Pimpin Standar AI Global
Sam Altman, CEO OpenAI
Di sisi lain, OpenAI menyerukan agar Amerika Serikat (AS) untuk memimpin upaya internasional dalam menyusun standar AI global, termasuk skenario recursive self-improvement (RSI).
RSI sendiri adalah kondisi saat model AI mampu mengembangkan dirinya sendiri secara otomatis. Usulan standar AI global ini disampaikan lewat blog post resmi perusahaan pada Senin, 21 September 2026, tepat menjelang sesi tingkat tinggi Sidang Majelis Umum PBB di New York.
Rencananya, CEO OpenAI Sam Altman akan memberi pengarahan kepada 15 negara anggota Dewa Keamanan PBB minggu ini, sebagaimana dikutip dari Reuters, Selasa (22/9/2026).
Perusahaan menilai, standar bersama diperlukan untuk mengukur kemampuan model, menilai risiko, dan menetapkan protokol pelaporan insiden AI secara konsisten lintas negara.
Namun OpenAI menegaskan, standar tersebut tidak dimaksudkan sebagai mekanisme lisensi atau persetujuan wajib sebelum model AI dirilis ke publik.
Standar AI Global Bukan Sekadar Soal Teknologi
Perdebatan mengenai standar AI global sebenarnya tidak hanya berkaitan dengan aspek teknis. Di baliknya terdapat pertanyaan lebih besar: siapa yang akan menentukan aturan dasar bagi teknologi semakin memengaruhi ekonomi, pendidikan, industri, hingga keamanan nasional.
Selama beberapa tahun terakhir, Amerika Serikat dan China sama-sama berupaya memperluas pengaruh mereka dalam pengembangan dan tata kelola AI. Karena itu, usulan OpenAI agar AS memimpin pengembangan standar AI dunia global berpotensi menjadi bagian dari kompetisi lebih luas di bidang teknologi.
Jika standar tertentu diadopsi secara luas oleh banyak negara, maka perusahaan dan pengembang AI di berbagai wilayah kemungkinan perlu menyesuaikan produk mereka dengan kerangka tersebut.

items.content:
Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry on Thursday said the government’s priority was to resolve the issue with Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) through dialogue and hoped that better sense would prevail before the party’s planned march on Sep 27.
The PTI last month announced a September 27 march in Islamabad to demand the release of Imran Khan, with caravans from across the country expected to converge on the federal capital. The party also planned protests, shutdowns and demonstrations along major highways in cities, including Lahore, Karachi, Hyderabad and Quetta.
Talking to a private television programme, Capital Talk, while recalling the previous PTI protest, the minister admitted that it had not been managed properly last time but said things would be different this time.
Read: PTI Sept 27 protest: IHC rules no political party, public office holder can block roads in Islamabad
“The government believes in minimum use of power, but one thing is very clear this time ... Islamabad is very far away in this manner,” Talal said.
He said the protesters would be treated respectfully, escorted and sent back in the same manner, but warned that if they wanted to come to turn Islamabad into “Somnath”, they would neither be allowed to come nor be able to take anything back.
“The route that can be opened through talks cannot be opened through a march,” he said.
Responding to a question, Talal said there was a difference between the PTI and PML-N long marches, saying the PTI believed that the state would be forced to move on the back foot and did not want to move through political dialogue or the political process.
“If they wanted to move forward, they would never have resigned from the assemblies; neither would May 9 or any such incident have happened. Even now, how are they talking about Somnath?” he said.
He argued that this was the reason why the government was taking all these preventive measures.
The minister said the government’s priority was to resolve the issue without any long march, as this would serve neither the country, their party nor even their leadership.
Also Read: Shafi Jan rejects Naqvi's PTI protest warnings
Asked whether the issue could be resolved through negotiations and dialogue, the minister replied in the affirmative and said that ask the PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar what constitutional right was being denied to the party, describing him as “a very fair man”.
“Ask the K-P chief minister why you are coming and what you want,” he said, adding that the PTI’s demands had nothing to do with the issues of ordinary people but concerned an issue involving a leader.
He warned that no one could dictate terms to the state.
“One thing has to be ended in this country, whether it is TLP or PTI: you cannot dictate terms to the state,” he said, adding that this would not happen and that they would not meet the PTI founder through such means.
Talal also alleged that the PTI was influenced by the Joint Action Committee in Azad Jammu and Kashmir and believed in creating the same environment and adopting the same strategy.
He said the closure of roads would eventually affect ordinary people in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.
“All stakeholders of the state are very clear that no nonsense, whether it is from TLP or anyone else, can be allowed. It cannot happen that someone brings 25,000 to 50,000 people to the state, to Islamabad, and says that because I want this, I will get it done before I leave. This will not happen,” he said.
The minister categorically denied that roads had been closed, saying the containers had only been brought to the capital to prevent any situation that could endanger people’s lives and property.
“There is no doubt that hundreds of containers are currently present in Islamabad, but no road has so far been closed,” he said.
He said some routes were currently closed, including the motorway, GT Road and some roads on the northern side, and expressed hope that the issue would be resolved without any confrontation.
Read More: Rangers deployed in Islamabad, Punjab districts to maintain law and order
“If even a single member of the security forces or a protester is killed, it is Pakistanis who will suffer. We do not want a situation where we are face to face, tear gas is being used,” Talal said, adding that “the other side is always very heavily armed” and referring to them as “non-political people”.
Asked when the containers would be removed, the minister said he was hopeful that they would not have to be used.
“We should remain positive. We hope that before the 27th, within the first 24 to 48 hours, common sense will prevail,” he concluded.

items.author: Z Ali
items.content:
The Supreme Court has stayed the trial of Dr Shahnawaz Kumbhar’s alleged custodial killing and desecration of his body, days before proceedings were due to begin at the Mirpurkhas district and sessions court, throwing into question the Sindh High Court’s order shifting the case from the Anti-Terrorism Court.
The apex court issued the stay on a petition by Dr Ibrahim Kumbhar, complainant in the FIRs concerning Dr Shahnawaz’s alleged custodial killing and desecration. The petitioner has sought restoration of the ATC’s jurisdiction, challenging the SHC’s April 7 order directing the transfer of the case to the sessions court.
The sessions court was scheduled to commence the trial on September 29. Advocate Sajjad Ahmed Chandio, representing the complainant, argued before the Supreme Court that the case should continue before the ATC and objected to the circumstances in which it was transferred.
In a further twist, Chandio told the apex court that Sindh’s deputy prosecutor general, who was expected to prosecute the case against the accused police officers, had instead filed an application on behalf of a DIG and two SSPs accused in the FIR, seeking transfer of the case from the ATC.
The counsel argued that since one of the FIRs under trial had been registered with the FIA, the Sindh deputy prosecutor general had no jurisdiction to represent the accused in seeking transfer of the case. According to him, the matter was supposed to be handled by the federal law officer. The Supreme Court has issued notices to the Prosecutor General Sindh, Advocate General Sindh and Attorney General for Pakistan for October 13, fixing the matter before a three-member bench.
Dr Shahnawaz Kumbhar was shot dead in what the complainant describes as a staged police encounter on September 19, 2024, after he surrendered to Mirpurkhas police in Karachi in connection with a blasphemy FIR. After his death, his body was allegedly set on fire by a mob while it was being transported to a graveyard in Umerkot district for burial.
The first FIR was registered at Sindhri Police Station, Mirpurkhas, on September 27, 2024, under sections 201, 364, 302, 34, 147, 148, 149 and 120-B of the Pakistan Penal Code, Sections 6 and 7 of the Anti-Terrorism Act 1997, and Sections 8 and 9 of the Torture and Custodial Death Prevention and Punishment Act 2022.
A second FIR was registered at the FIA’s Composite Circle Mirpurkhas on October 29, 2024, in connection with the allegation of custodial killing.
Former DIG Mirpurkhas Javed Sonharo Jiskani, former SSP Mirpurkhas Muhammad Asad Chaudhry and former SSP Umerkot Asif Raza Baloch are among 23 accused in the case. The three police officers had approached the ATC Mirpurkhas seeking transfer of the case to the district court, arguing in effect that the terrorism provisions incorporated into the FIR should not apply. The ATC rejected their plea on October 23, 2025. They subsequently approached the SHC, but their two separate criminal revision applications were dismissed on December 12, 2025.
However, a division bench of the SHC comprising Justice Miran Muhammad Shah and Justice Muhammad Hassan subsequently ordered the ATC on April 7, 2026, to transfer the case to the district and sessions court along with the complete record.
The complainant has now challenged that transfer before the Supreme Court, seeking permission for the ATC to proceed with the trial. The apex court’s stay means the sessions court proceedings scheduled for September 29 can not proceed pending further orders in the matter.

He particularly cited the recent sponsorship of a surgical operation to separate conjoined twins from Kano as evidence of Saudi Arabia’s continued humanitarian support for the people of the state.
Yusuf congratulated the government and people of Saudi Arabia on the National Day, describing the occasion as a celebration of unity, cohesion and development.

The event was attended by representatives of the governors of Jigawa, Katsina and Sokoto states, members of the diplomatic corps, academics, senior officers of the Nigerian Army, police and other security agencies, Islamic scholars and members of the business community.
