items.author: Tim Gizmo
items.content:
Sejak Apple memperkenalkan MacBook Neo, segmen laptop dengan harga lebih terjangkau mendapat perhatian baru. Sesuai namanya, MacBook Neo ditempatkan sebagai versi yang lebih murah dari lini MacBook, sehingga membuka peluang bagi konsumen yang ingin masuk ke ekosistem Apple dengan bujet lebih terbatas.
Namun, bagi sebagian konsumen, harga MacBook Neo mungkin masih berada di atas bujet yang tersedia. Di titik inilah laptop Windows di kisaran Rp8 jutaan menjadi menarik untuk dilihat.
Salah satunya Infinix XBOOK 14 Neo. Dari penamaannya saja, ada kesan bahwa laptop ini hadir di tengah tren baru laptop terjangkau yang menggunakan embel-embel “Neo”. Dengan harga mulai Rp7.999.000, XBOOK 14 Neo menawarkan laptop 14 inci dengan desain tipis dan ringan.
Di kelas harga yang berdekatan, konsumen sebenarnya punya pilihan dari merek yang sudah lebih lama bermain di pasar laptop. Salah satunya adalah Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14IRU8.
Keduanya memang tidak sepenuhnya ditujukan untuk pasar yang sama. XBOOK 14 Neo hadir ketika perhatian terhadap laptop murah kembali meningkat, sementara IdeaPad Slim 3 merupakan bagian dari lini laptop mainstream Lenovo.
Namun, ketika harganya berdekatan, spesifikasi keduanya menarik untuk dibandingkan. Apalagi pada konfigurasi tertentu, kedua laptop sama-sama menggunakan Intel Core i3-1315U. Lantas, apa saja perbedaannya?
Layar 14 Inci, beda karakter
Perbedaan paling mudah terlihat ada pada layar. Infinix XBOOK 14 Neo menggunakan panel IPS 14 inci dengan resolusi 1920 x 1200 piksel dan rasio 16:10. Sementara Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14IRU8 menggunakan panel TN 14 inci beresolusi 1920 x 1080 piksel dengan rasio 16:9. Keduanya memiliki refresh rate 60Hz.
Rasio 16:10 pada XBOOK 14 Neo memberikan area vertikal yang lebih panjang dibandingkan layar 16:9. Untuk aktivitas seperti mengerjakan dokumen, browsing atau membuka halaman web, tambahan area vertikal ini dapat mengurangi kebutuhan scrolling.
Jenis panel juga berbeda. XBOOK menggunakan IPS, sedangkan IdeaPad Slim 3 menggunakan TN. Keduanya tercatat memiliki cakupan warna 45% NTSC pada lembar perbandingan yang digunakan. Dengan demikian, XBOOK 14 Neo menawarkan kombinasi IPS + 16:10, sementara Lenovo memilih TN + 16:9.
Desain
Sebagai Macbook Neo wannabe, Infinix XBOOK 14 Neo menawarkan pilihan warna yang lebih beragam. Anak muda yang menjadi target marketnya bisa memilih warna mencolok yang sesuai karakternya seperti Twilight Purple, Shadow Blue, Sonic Yellow, dan Volcano Grey. Sementara Lenovo hanya menawarkan 1 warna saja yaitu Arctic Grey.
Jika laptop akan sering dibawa bepergian, bobot menjadi salah satu spesifikasi yang lebih mudah diterjemahkan ke penggunaan sehari-hari. XBOOK 14 Neo memiliki bobot 1,2 kg, sementara IdeaPad Slim 3 tercatat 1,37 kg. Ada selisih sekitar 170 gram.
Angka tersebut memang tidak besar jika dilihat di atas kertas. Tetapi ketika laptop, charger, mouse, dan aksesori lain masuk ke dalam tas, bobot total bisa bertambah. Karena itu, laptop yang lebih ringan memiliki keuntungan tersendiri bagi pengguna yang sering berpindah tempat.
Dimensi keduanya juga tidak identik. XBOOK tercatat berukuran 314,2 x 219,7 x 17,4 mm, sedangkan IdeaPad Slim 3 berukuran 324,3 x 213,8 x 17,9 mm. Keduanya masih berada dalam kategori laptop 14 inci yang relatif mudah dibawa, tetapi XBOOK sedikit lebih ringan.
Prosesor sama, Konfigurasi berbeda
Pada aspek prosesor, keduanya lebih dekat daripada yang mungkin terlihat. Infinix XBOOK 14 Neo tersedia dengan pilihan Intel Core i3-1315U dan Core i5-1335U, sedangkan Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 14IRU8 dalam lembar spesifikasi ini menggunakan Core i3-1315U.
Artinya, jika yang dibandingkan adalah varian Core i3, keduanya menggunakan prosesor yang sama. Perbedaan pengalaman penggunaan kemudian lebih banyak ditentukan oleh aspek lain seperti RAM, layar, storage, baterai, bobot, serta konektivitas.
XBOOK memiliki keuntungan dari sisi pilihan konfigurasi karena konsumen tidak terpaku pada Core i3. Tersedia pula varian Core i5-1335U untuk pengguna yang membutuhkan kemampuan pemrosesan lebih tinggi. Namun, tentu saja pilihan prosesor yang lebih tinggi juga membawa konsekuensi harga.
Memori DDR4 vs LPDDR5
Bagian yang menarik berikutnya adalah memori. XBOOK 14 Neo menggunakan DDR4 8GB atau 16GB, sedangkan IdeaPad Slim 3 menggunakan LPDDR5 8GB. Secara generasi teknologi memori, LPDDR5 lebih baru dibandingkan DDR4. LPDDR5 dirancang untuk menawarkan bandwidth lebih tinggi dengan karakteristik konsumsi daya yang lebih rendah, sehingga cukup umum digunakan pada perangkat tipis dan ringan.
Tetapi angka generasi memori tidak otomatis berarti laptop akan terasa jauh lebih cepat dalam semua aktivitas. Untuk penggunaan sehari-hari seperti Microsoft Office, browsing dengan sejumlah tab, meeting online, atau streaming, kapasitas RAM juga menjadi faktor penting. Dalam konteks ini, pilihan XBOOK hingga 16GB memberikan ruang lebih besar bagi pengguna yang menjalankan banyak aplikasi sekaligus.
Sebaliknya, LPDDR5 pada Lenovo menawarkan teknologi memori yang lebih baru, tetapi konfigurasi yang tercantum pada lembar perbandingan adalah 8GB. Jadi, perbedaannya bukan sekadar DDR4 versus DDR5, melainkan juga kapasitas memori yang tersedia pada masing-masing konfigurasi.
Konektivitas
Untuk konektivitas nirkabel, keduanya relatif berimbang. Baik XBOOK 14 Neo maupun IdeaPad Slim 3 mendukung Wi-Fi 6. Bluetooth-nya masing-masing berada di versi 5.2 dan 5.1. Perbedaan justru terlihat pada port fisik.
Keduanya memiliki satu USB-C dengan fungsi penuh, HDMI 1.4, serta jack audio combo. Namun, XBOOK menyediakan tiga USB-A 3.2, sementara Lenovo memiliki dua USB-A 3.2. Selisih satu port mungkin terlihat sederhana, tetapi bisa berguna bagi pengguna yang masih mengandalkan banyak perangkat USB-A, seperti mouse, keyboard, flash drive, dongle, atau hard disk eksternal.
Dalam hal ini, XBOOK menawarkan sedikit lebih banyak fleksibilitas tanpa harus bergantung pada hub USB tambahan.
Baterai dan Charger
Perbedaan lainnya terdapat pada kapasitas baterai. XBOOK 14 Neo menggunakan baterai 55Wh, sedangkan IdeaPad Slim 3 memiliki kapasitas 47Wh. Secara kapasitas, XBOOK memiliki tambahan 8Wh atau sekitar 17 persen dibandingkan Lenovo.
Namun, kapasitas baterai tidak bisa langsung diterjemahkan menjadi daya tahan baterai yang 17 persen lebih panjang. Durasi pemakaian juga dipengaruhi prosesor, layar, tingkat kecerahan, aplikasi yang digunakan, pengaturan daya, dan berbagai faktor lain.
Selain itu, salah satu perbedaan yang cukup relevan untuk gaya hidup mobile adalah cara mengisi daya. XBOOK 14 Neo menggunakan pengisian daya 65W melalui USB-C, sedangkan IdeaPad Slim 3 menggunakan adaptor AC 65W.
Besaran dayanya sama-sama 65W, tetapi pendekatannya berbeda. USB-C memberikan fleksibilitas lebih besar karena konektor yang sama sudah banyak digunakan pada berbagai perangkat modern. Jika charger USB-C yang digunakan memenuhi kebutuhan daya dan standar kompatibilitas laptop, satu charger berdaya sesuai dapat berpotensi digunakan untuk lebih dari satu perangkat, misalnya laptop, tablet, atau smartphone.
Tetapi perlu digarisbawahi: tidak semua charger USB-C 65W otomatis kompatibel dengan setiap laptop. Pengguna tetap perlu memastikan dukungan pengisian daya, profil daya, serta spesifikasi charger dan kabelnya.
Lenovo dengan adaptor AC 65W menawarkan pendekatan yang lebih konvensional. Charger tersebut ditujukan untuk laptop dan tidak memberikan fleksibilitas lintas perangkat seperti ekosistem charger USB-C. Bagi pengguna yang sering bekerja mobile, perbedaan ini bisa lebih berarti daripada sekadar melihat angka “65W” di spesifikasi.

Kehadiran MacBook Neo membuat laptop di kelas harga terjangkau menjadi semakin menarik untuk dibandingkan. Bukan berarti setiap laptop Windows di sekitar Rp8 juta otomatis menjadi pesaing langsung MacBook Neo. Namun, konsumen yang sebelumnya hanya mencari laptop Windows dengan spesifikasi tertentu kini bisa saja menjadikan harga MacBook Neo sebagai salah satu referensi ketika menentukan bujet.
Dari sisi harga, XBOOK 14 Neo memang masuk lebih rendah. Berdasarkan lembar perbandingan, XBOOK 14 Neo dibanderol mulai Rp7.999.000 untuk konfigurasi Core i3, sedangkan Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 memiliki SRP Rp8.999.000 untuk konfigurasi 8GB/256GB.
Infinix XBOOK 14 Neo juga tersedia dalam beberapa konfigurasi lain, termasuk Core i3 dengan SSD 512GB serta Core i5 dengan SSD 512GB.
Di titik tersebut, Infinix XBOOK 14 Neo menawarkan pendekatan yang cukup berbeda. Laptop ini membawa layar IPS 16:10, bobot 1,2 kg, baterai 55Wh, tiga USB-A, serta charging 65W melalui USB-C. Pilihan konfigurasi hingga Core i5 dan RAM 16GB juga memberi ruang lebih bagi konsumen yang membutuhkan spesifikasi lebih tinggi.
Sementara itu, Lenovo IdeaPad Slim 3 berada di kelas yang sama dengan pendekatan yang lebih konvensional. Laptop ini tetap menawarkan prosesor Core i3-1315U, LPDDR5, Wi-Fi 6, SSD hingga 512GB, dan bobot yang masih tergolong ringan di 1,37 kg.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Mumbai-based fintech Easy Platform Services, which owns and operates digital lending startup Zype, turned profitable in FY26, posting a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of ₹5.3 Cr against a loss of ₹12.9 Cr in FY25.
The startup’s consolidated total income jumped 66.6% to ₹176.6 Cr during the year from ₹106 Cr in FY25, according to ratings agency ICRA.
Easy Platform continued to remain profitable in the first quarter of the ongoing fiscal year. It provisionally posted a PAT of ₹6.1 Cr on a total income of ₹66 Cr in Q1 FY27.
The financial figures were disclosed in ICRA’s rationale for assigning a provisional A-(SO) rating to pass-through certificates (PTCs) worth ₹8.07 Cr issued by Nebula Trust 2026, a special-purpose trust set up for the securitisation transaction. The instruments are backed by a pool of personal loan receivables originated by Easy Platform’s NBFC subsidiary, Respo Financial Capital.
Easy Platform’s total managed assets increased 63.5% to ₹621.2 Cr in FY26 from ₹379.9 Cr in the previous fiscal year. They rose another 28.5% to a provisional ₹798.4 Cr in Q1 FY27.
Easy Platform also witnessed an improvement in asset quality. Its gross stage 3 ratio declined to 2.2% in FY26 from 3% in FY25 and fell further to 1.7% in Q1 FY27. Stage 3 assets largely comprise credit-impaired loans that are overdue for more than 90 days.
Meanwhile, capital-to-risk weighted assets ratio (CRAR) increased to 33.3% in FY26 from 24.7% in FY25. The ratio moderated to 23.6% in Q1 FY27 but remained above the regulatory requirement of 15%.
Founded in 2019 by Yogi Sadana and the late Ajay Relan, Easy Platform operates digital lending platform Zype, which offers unsecured personal loans to salaried individuals across Tier I, II, and III cities.
Easy Platform is also the parent company of Respo, in which it owns a 100% stake. The RBI-registered NBFC primarily offers unsecured personal loans through Zype, which supports customer acquisition, underwriting, loan servicing, and collections.
Respo received its NBFC licence from the RBI in June 2023. It also operates as an IRDAI-registered corporate agent and earns commission income from the distribution of insurance products.
Zype raised ₹90 Cr (about $10.3 Mn) in its Series B funding in August 2025 in a round led by Japanese VC firm UNLEASH Capital Partners, with existing investor Xponentia Capital also participating. The fundraise took Zype’s total equity capital raised since inception to about $28 Mn.
As of June 30, 2026, Xponentia Opportunities Fund I and Xponentia Opportunities Fund II cumulatively held an 85.5% stake in Easy Platform. UNLEASH Capital held a 4.7% stake, while Sadana owned 3.7%.
Zype competes with consumer lending platforms such as Fibe, KreditBee, and Navi.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is rolling out a new customization feature for its premium subscribers on Android. The feature lets WhatsApp Plus users customize their own emoji reactions instead of using the default emojis shown in the message reaction tray.
The new option is currently rolling out to some beta testers through WhatsApp beta for Android version 2.26.38.4. According to WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is releasing the feature gradually, so it may take some time before it appears for all eligible users.
WhatsApp Plus Users Can Now Customize Their Emoji Reactions on Android
WhatsApp normally shows six default emojis when users want to react to a message. With the new feature, WhatsApp Plus subscribers can replace any or all of these emojis.
Users can select any emoji from the full emoji keyboard and assign it to one of the six reaction slots. This gives subscribers more control over which reactions appear when they respond to messages.
Once users save their choices, the updated emojis appear in the reaction tray immediately.
How to Customize WhatsApp Reaction Emojis
WhatsApp provides an option to change the reaction emojis through the app’s settings. Users can open Settings, go to Chats, and look for the Default reactions section.
The six existing reaction emojis appear there. Users can tap any of them and select a replacement from the emoji keyboard. They can change one emoji or customize all six slots.
WhatsApp also offers a quicker way to make these changes. When users open the emoji keyboard while reacting to a message, they can find the default reactions at the top. Tapping Edit allows them to modify the reaction tray without leaving the conversation.
Feature Is Limited to WhatsApp Plus Subscribers
Although non-subscribers may see the default reactions section in their settings, they cannot customize the emojis without a WhatsApp Plus subscription.
The feature is part of the second set of benefits being introduced for premium subscribers. WhatsApp has already added other personalization options for Plus users, including custom themes, app icons, premium stickers, and the ability to pin up to 20 chats.
Custom emoji reactions add another personalization option for users who want to change the way they interact with messages.
See Also: WhatsApp Lets Users Access Instagram and Facebook Media Directly
Gradual Android Rollout
WhatsApp is currently making the feature available to a limited number of beta testers. Users with the compatible Android beta version may see the new option, but the feature is not yet available to everyone.
The company is expected to expand the rollout to more users over the coming weeks. WhatsApp has not confirmed when custom emoji reactions will reach all WhatsApp Plus subscribers.
For now, Android users who do not see the option may need to wait for a future update or a wider server-side rollout.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The cybercrime group ShinyHunters has claimed that it hacked the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and stole sensitive information linked to current and former FBI employees as well as people who applied for jobs at the agency.
The group made the claim on its dark web site on September 22. It said the stolen information could include data related to almost all FBI agents and other agency employees. However, the FBI has not confirmed that the attackers accessed such a large amount of information.
ShinyHunters Claims It Hacked the FBI and Stole Employee Data
ShinyHunters claimed that several FBI services were affected, including Criminal Justice, human resources, and Medlink systems. The group also said it carried out the attack in response to an FBI public service announcement issued in May 2026.
That FBI announcement warned about ShinyHunters’ activities involving Canvas, an online learning management platform. The agency had also advised potential victims not to pay ransom demands. ShinyHunters later accused the FBI of spreading false information about its activities and said the public warning had not stopped its operations.
The group also rejected reports linking it to The Com, a decentralized cybercrime collective. ShinyHunters described those reports as misinformation and denied being part of the wider group.
ShinyHunters Claims PeopleSoft Zero-Day Attack
A ShinyHunters spokesperson told The Register that the attackers gained access by exploiting what they described as a new zero-day vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft. The group claimed the flaw allowed remote code execution and was used to compromise the FBI’s jobs website.
The FBI’s jobs website was also reportedly defaced with a message claiming that the site had been seized by ShinyHunters. The website is currently showing a scheduled maintenance message.
There is currently no public confirmation of a new pre-authenticated remote code execution zero-day in Oracle PeopleSoft matching the group’s claim. ShinyHunters has previously exploited a different PeopleSoft vulnerability, CVE-2026-35273, to gain access to enterprise networks and extort victims.
This means the latest claim still needs to be verified through technical evidence and an official investigation.
FBI Investigating the Claims
The FBI has acknowledged that it is aware of claims involving unauthorized activity against FBIjobs.gov. In a statement shared with Reuters, the agency said it is investigating the incident.
The statement does not confirm that ShinyHunters accessed FBI employee records or other sensitive databases.
The distinction is important because cybercriminal groups sometimes make claims before investigators can establish the full scope of an intrusion. At this stage, the alleged theft of information involving FBI agents and job applicants remains unverified.
The incident follows another high-profile move by ShinyHunters, which recently hijacked the dark web leak site associated with the Clop ransomware operation. The group used the site to issue a ransom demand and challenge its target.
Attack Shows Growing Focus on Trusted Access
Cybersecurity experts say the incident, if confirmed, would be notable because of the target involved. Cato Networks Vice President of Threat Intelligence Etay Maor said a public claim of compromising a law-enforcement agency is different from attacks against ordinary businesses.
Maor also noted that ShinyHunters has continued operating despite arrests, infrastructure seizures, and other disruption efforts. He described the group as an evolving criminal brand rather than a fixed group of people using the same infrastructure.
According to Maor, recent ShinyHunters campaigns have increasingly focused on trusted access routes. These include help-desk social engineering, malicious OAuth applications, and stolen tokens used to connect SaaS services.
The FBI investigation will determine whether ShinyHunters’ claims about the alleged breach are accurate and how much data, if any, the attackers obtained. Until investigators release more technical details, the full impact of the reported incident remains unclear.

items.title: Nigerian fintech startup Grey launches new payout routes to Senegal, Ivory Coast, Cameroon, Rwanda
items.summary:
Nigerian startup Grey, the Y Combinator-backed cross-border payment platform, is now enabling direct payout to Senegal, Ivory Coast, Cameroon and Rwanda.
Grey enables individuals and businesses to easily own and manage multi-currency accounts in USD, GBP, and EUR, supporting transfers to more than 170 destinations. It also offers access to virtual cards.
With this new payout, migrants, diaspora communities, as well as individuals and businesses, can now send payments directly to recipients in these countries. Users can now send funds in the recipient’s local currency, including Rwandan francs (RWF), Central African CFA francs (XAF), and West African CFA francs (XOF).
Together, these four markets account for more than US$7 billion in remittance flows. Grey’s expansion is supporting these existing financial connections while making cross-border payments more accessible for the people and businesses that depend on them.
“Senegal, Ivory Coast, Cameroon and Rwanda have growing diaspor
items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
Nigerian startup Grey, the Y Combinator-backed cross-border payment platform, is now enabling direct payout to Senegal, Ivory Coast, Cameroon and Rwanda.
Grey enables individuals and businesses to easily own and manage multi-currency accounts in USD, GBP, and EUR, supporting transfers to more than 170 destinations. It also offers access to virtual cards.
With this new payout, migrants, diaspora communities, as well as individuals and businesses, can now send payments directly to recipients in these countries. Users can now send funds in the recipient’s local currency, including Rwandan francs (RWF), Central African CFA francs (XAF), and West African CFA francs (XOF).
Together, these four markets account for more than US$7 billion in remittance flows. Grey’s expansion is supporting these existing financial connections while making cross-border payments more accessible for the people and businesses that depend on them.
“Senegal, Ivory Coast, Cameroon and Rwanda have growing diasporas that send money home to support families, education, healthcare, and fund businesses. At the same time, people are travelling to Rwanda for vacations, to visit friends and relatives, for business and conferences. Yet cross-border payment has not always matched the strength of these relationships. With these new payouts, we’re making it easier for individuals and businesses to send money to these countries in their local currencies.” said Idorenyin Obong, CEO and co-founder of Grey.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Update | September 23, 13:10 IST
Electric two-wheeler startup Ultraviolette Automotive has raised $85 Mn (about ₹813 Cr) in a Series E round co-led by Yali Capital and TDK Ventures. Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan and other investors also participated in the round.
Cofounder and CEO Narayan Subramaniam told Inc42 that the startup would use the capital to expand its manufacturing capacity and product portfolio, as well as strengthen its distribution network in India and overseas.
“We are looking to enter new markets, including the US, Latin America, and Southeast Asia. The idea behind the fundraise is to cover all these different areas. To begin with, it is going into facility expansion, where Tesseract will now see a rapid ramp-up as well,” he said.
Subramaniam said Ultraviolette expects to begin production of its Tesseract electric scooter and Shockwave electric motorcycle over the next few months.
Both products have missed their original delivery schedule. When Ultraviolette unveiled them in March 2025, it said deliveries would begin in Q1 FY26. Neither has entered customer deliveries yet.
Ultraviolette’s website now says the Tesseract’s final variants and configurations will be unveiled in Q1 2027, with deliveries commencing shortly thereafter. The startup has not disclosed a revised delivery timeline for the Shockwave.
While India’s E2W market is dominated by relatively affordable scooters, Ultraviolette is positioning the Tesseract as a performance-focused offering.
The startup claims that the Tesseract is India’s first scooter built on a 100-volt architecture, compared with the 48-volt systems commonly used in the segment. According to the startup, the architecture offers greater power and efficiency, as well as faster charging.
Meanwhile, cofounder and CTO Niraj Rajmohan said Ultraviolette’s revenue grew around fourfold to about ₹130 Cr in FY26 from approximately ₹30 Cr in FY25.
The startup is yet to file its audited FY26 financial statements. In FY25, its operating revenue jumped 114% YoY to ₹32.3 Cr, while its net loss widened 89% to ₹116.3 Cr.
Original | September 11, 14:16 IST
Electric two-wheeler (E2W) maker Ultraviolette Automotive is set to raise an additional ₹373.04 Cr as part of its ongoing Series E funding round from investors Yali Capital, TDK Ventures, among others.
As per an MCA filings accessed by Inc42, Ultraviolette’s shareholders consented to allot on preferential basis through private placement 8.15 Lakh Series E3 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) worth ₹2,435 each, aggregating to ₹197.5 Cr. The startup also allotted 7.24 Lakh Series E4 CCPS, netting ₹175.5 Cr.
“The investments are part of a currently ongoing fundraise; we have nothing further to add at the moment,” the startup said in response to Inc42’s questions pertaining to the round.
Of this, Ultraviolette has raised ₹249.2 Cr from Yali Capital’s Yali Deeptech Fund I as well as TDK Ventures. TDK Ventures first backed the startup in August 2025 when it led its $21 Mn funding round while Yali Capital will be new to Ultraviolette’s cap table.
There are a host of angel investors participating in this round including, Adi Hirji Jehangir, Anshumi Desai, Janak Desai, Mahak Khabia, Zafar Ahmadullah, among others.
The investment comes almost a year after the startup raised $45 Mn as part of the Series E round from Zoho and Lingotto. Overall, the startup has raised more than $135 Mn till date from other investors like TVS Motors, Qualcomm Ventures, Breathe Capital and Mudhal Partners.
The new investment comes as the E2W manufacturer is building its manufacturing facility, the BIGGA factory.
Ultraviolette To Invest ₹1,000 Cr In Manufacturing
The E2W maker is investing more than ₹1,000 Cr over the next five years to expand its manufacturing footprint, with its upcoming BIGGA Factory set to take its annual production capacity to as much as 2.5 Lakh vehicles in the initial phase.
The startup intends to invest approximately ₹800 Cr in the new facility, while another ₹200 Cr is being deployed to expand its existing Bengaluru plant. The new facility will initially have an annual capacity of 2.5 Lakh vehicles, which can eventually be scaled to 5 Lakh vehicles, cofounders Narayan Subramaniam and Niraj Rajmohan told Inc42.
The capacity expansion comes as Ultraviolette looks to move beyond its initial premium, performance-led positioning and target larger segments of the E2W market with new products such as the Shockwave and Tesseract.
However, the startup said the strategy itself has not changed.
“Ultraviolette was conceived from the outset as an electric-vehicle platform company,” the founders said, highlighting that the F77 was the first expression of this approach, followed by the X-47 crossover. The upcoming products, they said, will allow the company to address “significantly larger customer segments” while retaining its focus on technology, safety, performance and range.
The cofounders claim that demand across its existing portfolio already exceeds 10,000 units a month, while it has received tens of thousands of bookings for upcoming products. It plans to commission capacity progressively in line with demand.
Ultraviolette currently has an installed capacity of around 30,000 vehicles annually at its Bengaluru facility, which is being expanded to 50,000-60,000 units. The plant will continue to serve as a manufacturing, engineering and technology hub after the BIGGA Factory comes online.
It is also targeting international markets, with exports expected to account for around 25% of revenue over the next five years.
“BIGGA Factory converts that technology foundation into industrial scale,” the founders said, positioning the facility as a key step towards building a global electric-mobility business.
To note, the startup launched its F77 motorcycles in the United Kingdom, in November last year, and claimed to be present in 12 countries across Europe, as of its last fundraise.
For the month of August, overall E2W registrations fell by 16.2% to 1.72 Lakh units from 2.05 Lakh units in July, based on Vahan data. Ultraviolette sold 583 E2Ws, down 17% from 702 vehicles in July. It holds 0.3% market share in the domestic market.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Honor has confirmed that its upcoming Magic 9 series flagship smartphones will use Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chipset. The company says the new processor will bring major improvements in performance, graphics, artificial intelligence and imaging.
Honor shared the confirmation on Weibo on September 23. The announcement comes shortly after Qualcomm introduced the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 family of mobile processors.
Honor Confirms Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Chipset for Magic 9 Series
The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 is built using a 2nm manufacturing process and uses Qualcomm’s latest Oryon CPU architecture. It also features a new Adreno GPU and Hexagon NPU for graphics and AI workloads.
Qualcomm has introduced two versions of the processor: the standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and the more powerful Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. Both chips are designed for high-end smartphones, but the Extreme version offers additional graphics and AI performance.
The standard Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 uses the Adreno 845 GPU. Qualcomm claims it can deliver a 10% improvement in CPU performance and up to a 35% boost in graphics performance compared with its predecessor. The Extreme model uses the Adreno 850 GPU and reportedly delivers up to a 44% improvement in GPU performance.
See Also: Honor Confirms New X9e Pro With Huge 11,000mAh Battery
The new chipset also features an 18MB GPU with dedicated high-speed video memory. Qualcomm has added Agentic AI capabilities to the platform, allowing smartphones to run personal AI models directly on the device. This could support local AI assistants that can process voice and data without relying entirely on cloud services.
Honor has not yet confirmed which Magic 9 models will use each version of the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6. However, current reports suggest that the standard Magic 9 or Magic 9 Super Edition could use the regular chipset, while the Magic 9 Pro Max could receive the more powerful Extreme version.
The Magic 9 Pro Max has already appeared on Geekbench with a processor listed as the “8 Elite Gen 6 Pro.” This has led to speculation that the phone could feature the Extreme variant.
Honor has also highlighted improvements in imaging and overall performance with the new chipset. However, the company has not yet revealed the complete specifications of the Magic 9 lineup.
More details could emerge on September 28, when Honor is expected to provide further information about the Magic 9 series and its Snapdragon-powered models.

items.title: NCCIA Targets Dating-App Fraud Network as 206 Suspects Booked in Islamabad Call Centre Raids
items.summary:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has registered two separate cases against 206 suspects, including 12 foreign nationals, following raids on call centers in Islamabad allegedly linked to organized online fraud.
According to case details, the suspected network used online dating applications as an entry point to approach potential victims, build regular communication, and gradually gain their trust before steering them towards online tasks and purported investment opportunities.
Investigators allege that victims were encouraged to deposit money through online platforms after being promised financial returns.
The cases indicate that the alleged operation was not limited to one form of fraud. The call centers were also suspected of conducting deceptive activities in the name of loan recovery, online trading, and investment while operating under the appearance of legitimate information technology businesses.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) has registered two separate cases against 206 suspects, including 12 foreign nationals, following raids on call centers in Islamabad allegedly linked to organized online fraud.
According to case details, the suspected network used online dating applications as an entry point to approach potential victims, build regular communication, and gradually gain their trust before steering them towards online tasks and purported investment opportunities.
Investigators allege that victims were encouraged to deposit money through online platforms after being promised financial returns.
The cases indicate that the alleged operation was not limited to one form of fraud. The call centers were also suspected of conducting deceptive activities in the name of loan recovery, online trading, and investment while operating under the appearance of legitimate information technology businesses.
Dating Apps Used as Gateway to Broader Online Fraud
One of the raided call centers was operating in Sector G-10, Islamabad, according to the case record.
Authorities allege that the facility was being used for unlawful cyber activities while presenting itself as an IT business. A large number of women were also found among those allegedly working at the premises.
The alleged fraud model relied on prolonged communication rather than one-off messages. Suspects would first establish contact with victims, maintain conversations, and build confidence before introducing financial tasks or investment offers.
Investigators believe this approach was designed to make the schemes appear credible and increase the likelihood that victims would transfer funds.
During the raids, NCCIA officials seized computers, electronic equipment, and other digital material allegedly connected with the operations.
The suspects have been booked under Section 14 of the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016, along with Sections 419, 420, 34, and 109 of the Pakistan Penal Code.
The investigation is continuing, with authorities expected to examine the seized digital material to establish the scale of the operation, financial flows, and the roles of individual suspects.
The latest cases highlight the growing use of social and dating platforms as a starting point for more elaborate financial scams, where personal interaction is allegedly used to build trust before victims are directed towards fraudulent investment or money-transfer schemes.

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Selain Find X10 dan Find X10 E, OPPO juga resmi memperkenalkan Find X10 Pro Max, model paling premium di keluarga Find X10 yang baru akan meluncur di pasar China.
Tampil sebagai seri paling tinggi, OPPO Find X10 Pro Max langsung mencuri perhatian dengan konfigurasi tiga kamera belakang 200MP yang diklaim menjadi pertama di industri smartphone.
Dari sisi fotografi, spesifikasi Find X10 Pro Max sudah dilengkapi dengan kamera utama 200MP sensor berukuran 1/1,3 inci dan aperture f/1.5, kamera ultrawide 200MP dengan sudut pandang 124 derajat, serta kamera telefoto 200MP dengan focal length setara 70mm.
Kemampuan fotografi ponsel ini juga semakin lengkap dengan optical image stabilization (OIS) pada kamera utama dan telefoto, sementara kamera depan menggunakan sensor 50MP dengan autofocus.
Selain kamera, Find X10 Pro Max jadi salah satu HP Android pertama yang menggunakan chipset Dimensity 9600 Pro dari MediaTek. Disebutkan, chip ini membawa peningkatan performa dan efisiensi daya dibanding generasi sebelumnya.
Layar Oppo Find X10 Pro Max
Oppo Find X10 Pro Max
Untuk bagian layar Oppo Find X10 Pro Max, perusahaan membekali perangkat ini dengan panel AMOLED 6,78 inci beresolusi 1272 x 2772 piksel, sudah mendukung refresh rate hingga 144Hz untuk sejumlah aplikasi dan game tertentu, dan refresh rate adaptif hingga 120Hz. Tingkat kecerahan puncaknya diklaim mencapai 2.000 nit.
Sebagai pendukung performa sehari-hari, perusahaan menyematkan baterai silikon-karbon berkapasitas 8.000mAh di Oppo Find X10 Pro Max. Smartphone ini juga sudah mendukung pengisian cepat SuperVOOC 80W melalui kabel dan wireless charging 50W.
Raksasa teknologi itu mengklaim, baterainya masih mampu mempertahankan setidaknya 80 persen kapasitas setelah lima tahun penggunaan.
Terkait dengan OS (sistem operasi), Oppo Find X10 Pro Max sudah menjalankan ColorOS 17 berbasis Android 17 dan telah mengantongi sertifikasi IP66, IP68, serta IP69 untuk ketahanan terhadap debu dan air. Smartphone ini tersedia dalam pilihan warna Moon White, Warm Orange, dan Light Titanium.
Di China, harga OPPO Find X10 Pro Max dijual mulai dari 6.799 yuan atau sekitar Rp 18 jutaan untuk varian 12GB/256GB. Varian 12GB/512GB dibanderol 7.499 yuan (Rp 20 juta), sedangkan model 16GB/512GB dijual 7.999 yuan atau sekitar Rp 21 juta.
Untuk konfigurasi tertinggi Oppo Find X10 Pro Max dengan RAM 16GB dan penyimpanan 1TB, harganya mencapai 8.999 yuan atau di Rp 24 jutaan.
Meski baru diumumkan untuk pasar China, OPPO telah mengonfirmasi Find X10 Pro Max akan dipasarkan secara global dalam waktu mendatang. Hingga saat ini belum ada informasi resmi mengenai ketersediaannya di Indonesia.
OPPO Find X10 dan Find X10 E Resmi Meluncur
OPPO Find X10 dan Find X10 E resim dikenalkan di Tiongkok, bersamaan dengan Find X10 Pro Max. Keduanya ditempatkan sebagai pilihan yang lebih terjangkau dibanding model Pro Max, tetapi tetap membawa sejumlah fitur yang cukup tinggi, termasuk layar AMOLED dengan refresh rate tinggi dan baterai berkapasitas besar.
Find X10 menjadi model yang lebih tinggi di antara keduanya. Smartphone ini menggunakan layar AMOLED 6,59 inci dengan resolusi 1272 x 2768 piksel, refresh rate hingga 144Hz, touch sampling 288Hz, serta tingkat kecerahan puncak 2.000 nit. Performanya mengandalkan Dimensity 9600M, yang disebut merupakan versi rebrand dari Dimensity 9500 dengan fabrikasi 3nm.
Sementara itu, OPPO Find X10 E hadir dengan spesifikasi yang lebih rendah, tetapi tetap mempertahankan layar AMOLED 6,59 inci. Resolusinya 1256 x 2760 piksel dengan refresh rate 120Hz, touch sampling 240Hz, dan kecerahan hingga 1.800 nit. Chipset yang digunakan adalah Dimensity 9500s, yang juga diproduksi dengan proses 3nm.
OPPO Find X10 membawa konfigurasi kamera yang cukup tinggi di kelasnya. Kamera utama 200MP menggunakan sensor 1/1,4 inci dengan aperture f/1.6 dan OIS dua sumbu. Kamera ultrawide 50MP memiliki autofocus dan sudut pandang 120 derajat, sedangkan kamera periskop 200MP menawarkan optical zoom 2,8x dan OIS dua sumbu. Kamera depannya memiliki resolusi 50MP dengan autofocus.
Kemudian, OPPO Find X10 E menggunakan konfigurasi yang lebih sederhana. Kamera utamanya beresolusi 50MP dengan sensor 1/1,4 inci, sedangkan ultrawide dan telefoto masing-masing 50MP. Kamera telefoto menawarkan optical zoom 3x, sementara kamera selfie beresolusi 32MP. Perbedaan ini menunjukkan posisi Find X10 E yang lebih menekan harga dibanding mengejar spesifikasi kamera setinggi Find X10.
Baterai Besar Jadi Salah Satu Daya Tarik
Find X10 dibekali baterai 8.000 mAh dengan pengisian 80W kabel dan 50W nirkabel. Find X10 E bahkan membawa kapasitas 7.025 mAh dengan dukungan pengisian yang sama. Keduanya juga memiliki sertifikasi IP66, IP68, dan IP69 serta menjalankan ColorOS 17 berbasis Android 17.
Di China, Find X10 dijual mulai CNY 5.499 atau sekitar Rp12 jutaan untuk konfigurasi 12GB/256GB, sementara Find X10 E mulai CNY 4.999 atau sekitar Rp11 jutaan dengan konfigurasi yang sama. items.title: Gupshup’s AI Rebuild: Can It Stay Ahead Of The Platforms It Runs On?

items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
For a company that started out sending SMSes, Gupshup has spent nearly two decades learning one thing: how businesses talk to their customers.
That experience is now becoming the foundation for its next bet: conversational AI.
Gupshup is no longer positioning itself simply as a messaging infrastructure company. Its product stack is expanding from SMS and WhatsApp to voice AI, AI agents, campaign orchestration and tools that allow enterprises to connect multiple AI models with customer-engagement channels.
The shift is already showing up in the business. At the global level, CEO and cofounder Beerud Sheth said for FY26, Gupshup is roughly $350 Mn business and profitable.
But that is not the real story here given that global revenue in FY23 was around $300 Mn. More importantly, Sheth said 25% of the revenue today now comes from AI-related offerings. And this transition also resulted in some workforce reduction over FY26, but the CEO believes Gupshup is different from a conventional startup launching an AI product because it has seen how communication and messaging has evolved.
Today, Gupshup is effectively trying to AI-ify an existing enterprise customer base, using the infrastructure, relationships and transaction volumes accumulated over years as its competitive moat.
From Messaging APIs To AI-Powered Conversations
Gupshup’s evolution has broadly tracked the evolution of customer engagement.
The company started with SMS and basic messaging in 2004. WhatsApp brought richer, two-way conversations, while RCS and other channels expanded the ways businesses could interact with customers. Gupshup now sees AI-powered conversations across text and voice as the next stage, having entered the segment in February 2025.
“We’ve been doing this business for 15–20 years,” Sheth said in an interaction with Inc42. The company’s focus, he said, has been helping businesses engage customers through mobile messaging and voice, with newer interfaces potentially emerging over time.
The important distinction is that Gupshup does not see voice AI as a standalone channel.
Its recently launched voice AI offering is a self-serve platform for deploying AI agents that handle customer calls. The company says these agents can resolve inbound support calls, qualify leads and automate operational calls such as scheduling, verification and payment reminders.
The platform starts at $0.035 (₹3.50) per minute, compared with industry pricing that can range from $0.05 to $1 per minute. Sheth expects the cost of voice AI to fall further as the underlying technology becomes more efficient. Gupshup is also experimenting with smaller, specialised models that can deliver faster and cheaper inference for specific use cases.
The platform is model-agnostic, with integrations including Deepgram, ElevenLabs and Cartesia. The company is also evaluating open-weight and Indian models.
Gupshup’s existing voice infrastructure is another part of the equation. The company acquired voice technology business Knowlarity in 2022 for $100 Mn, giving it an established voice stack. According to Sheth, Knowlarity’s infrastructure handles around 500 Mn calls a month.
Gupshup is now adding an AI layer to that infrastructure and integrating it with the broader platform.
Voice AI is only one part of that strategy. In April, the company introduced Super Agent, an orchestration layer designed to bring multiple customer-engagement functions into a single interface.
Businesses today have to manage messaging channels, campaigns, customer journeys, AI agents, CRM systems, payments, catalogues, human escalation and analytics, often across different platforms. Super Agent is designed to bring these workflows together through natural-language instructions.
Rather than building another foundation model, Gupshup is positioning itself as the layer connecting different models to its APIs, workflows and enterprise integrations. A customer could use Meta’s Business Agent, OpenAI, Anthropic or an open-weight model while relying on Gupshup for the surrounding infrastructure.
The company has also launched Superclaw, a self-hosted, on-device version of Super Agent built on the open-source OpenClaw platform.
These AI products and other advanced orchestration capabilities now account for roughly a quarter of Gupshup’s revenue, according to Sheth. He added that the newer offerings are growing faster than the company’s traditional messaging business.
This is not Gupshup’s first shift in response to a changing technology landscape.
The company began as SMS Gupshup, allowing users to create interest-based groups and receive SMS updates, similar to early social-media platforms. After around four years of rapid growth, rising SMS costs began to weigh on the business. Gupshup subsequently moved away from the consumer-facing model and focused on enterprises in 2011.
The company is now attempting another transition as business messaging changes again.
“Every business has to support more than just messaging. It needs to support voice and, eventually, other channels that may emerge, such as video, smart glasses and other surfaces. Businesses will need to manage interactions across all these channels,” Sheth said.
Can Incumbency Become An AI Advantage?
This is where Gupshup’s strategy becomes particularly interesting. Sheth describes its advantage as a combination of “incumbency and innovation.”
India’s voice AI market is expanding rapidly, with projections estimating the sector to grow from roughly $130–$150 Mn to nearly $1 Bn by 2030, while the broader conversational AI market is forecast to reach $3.7 Bn by 2033.
But the opportunity comes with a crowded competitive landscape. AI-native startups are building specialised agents, voice interfaces and vertical applications from scratch. Their advantage is speed and product focus.
Gupshup starts from the opposite end. It already has the customers, messaging infrastructure and enterprise relationships. The company serves more than 50,000 businesses across 130 countries and processes over 120 Bn messages annually across WhatsApp, voice, web and mobile. That gives it a potentially powerful distribution advantage.
Sheth said customers that started with SMS years ago subsequently added WhatsApp, RCS, AI, chatbots, campaign management and other tools. As customers adopt more products, their spending with Gupshup rises.
That is also translating into higher revenue per customer. “For the same customer, deal sizes are increasing because they are using more products. Many customers started with SMS, then added WhatsApp, followed by RCS, and are now using AI, chatbots, campaign platforms and other products,” said Sheth. Some of its largest customers can spend as much as ₹10 Cr a month, he added.
But the financial picture is less straightforward.
Gupshup’s India entity saw revenue decline from ₹2,051 Cr to ₹1,943 Cr in FY25, while net profit fell from ₹54 Cr to ₹26 Cr. Sheth argues that the India entity does not represent the company’s entire global business, but the numbers nonetheless show the challenge of translating the AI transition into financial growth.
The company has also faced pressure on its valuation.
In January, a fund run by Fidelity Investments marked down its valuation of Gupshup to $278 Mn, more than 80% below the $1.4 Bn valuation at which Fidelity first invested in 2021 through a secondary transaction. The fund had previously marked down its holding to $697 Mn as of July 2023.
The markdown came amid a broader reset in software valuations as investors reassessed the durability of traditional SaaS businesses in the age of AI. Gupshup also laid off more than 100 employees last year as part of a cost-cutting exercise.
Sheth did not comment on these parts of the past year for the company.
The AI pivot is more than a product expansion; it is also a test of whether an established messaging business can create a new growth engine before its legacy business becomes structurally less attractive.
The Meta Problem
While incumbency may give Gupshup a head start, it does not insulate the company from intensifying competition.
Meta-owned WhatsApp is a case in point. Gupshup is a Meta Business Solution Provider (BSP), giving businesses access to the WhatsApp Business API. But WhatsApp itself launched Meta Business Agent this year, bringing AI-powered capabilities that can automate customer interactions, recommend products, book appointments, qualify leads and provide 24/7 support.
That puts WhatsApp closer to the application layer Gupshup is increasingly targeting with its own AI offerings. Sheth argues that Gupshup’s model-agnostic approach will remain relevant even as individual platforms build their own AI capabilities.
“Meta has launched Meta Business Agent, which comes with its own LLM and agent capabilities. But regardless of which model is being used, Gupshup’s role remains the same: helping enterprises put the different components together and orchestrate them,” said Sheth.
Enterprises, he added, do not want to be locked into a single model as the AI landscape changes rapidly. They want the flexibility to use different models for different applications, which Gupshup believes gives its orchestration layer a role to play.
The same dynamic is emerging in business messaging. Reliance Jio has introduced new pricing for RCS messaging for businesses following its partnership with Apple to extend RCS support to iOS users in India. This brings Apple into India’s business messaging market alongside Google, potentially challenging WhatsApp’s dominance in rich, two-way messaging.
For Gupshup, RCS is a double-edged sword. Apple and Jio could expand the market for rich business messaging, but they also bring more competition to the infrastructure layer where Gupshup has historically made money.
That makes the company’s shift towards AI orchestration more important. If messaging infrastructure becomes increasingly commoditised, Gupshup needs to capture value higher up the stack.
The Road To The Public Market
This mix of opportunity, competition and financial pressure makes Gupshup’s next move worth watching.
Just last year, the company raised another $60 Mn from Globespan Capital Partners and EvolutionX Debt Capital to support product innovation and expansion across markets including India, the Middle East, Latin America and Africa.
The company is also exploring listing venues and evaluating the legal, tax and structural implications of potentially redomiciling to India from the US. Sheth has indicated a potential 12–24 month window for a listing, although there is no firm IPO date yet.
An IPO would put Gupshup’s AI narrative under a much tougher lens. But IPO talk is not new in Gupshup’s context, nor is the reverse flipping, which Sheth first talked about in February 2025.
The company brought in Ravi Dugar, who took Awfis through its IPO, as CFO in March 2026, and this is a concrete signal that Gupshup is looking to overcome the reverse flipping hurdle and list in India.
Investors will not simply want to know how many AI agents the company has launched. They will want to know whether AI is producing higher revenue per customer, improving margins, increasing retention and creating a durable competitive moat.
That is ultimately the bigger bet behind Gupshup’s AI push. The company is betting that its incumbency is not a legacy burden but an asset, and that years of customer relationships, messaging infrastructure, voice capabilities and enterprise integrations can make it easier to move customers into an AI-first world.
The question is whether that installed base can become a genuine AI moat before the companies controlling the underlying channels, models and AI interfaces capture more of the value.
[Edited by Nikhil Subramaniam]
The post Gupshup’s AI Rebuild: Can It Stay Ahead Of The Platforms It Runs On? appeared first on Inc42 Media.

The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) has won three awards at the PASHA ICT Awards 2026 for its work in digital identity, biometric verification, and public service delivery.
According to NADRA, the Pak ID mobile app received an award in the Government and Citizen Services category. The app has recorded more than 22 million downloads and provides citizens in Pakistan and abroad with access to identity-related and other digital services.
NADRA Wins Three Awards at PASHA ICT Awards 2026
NADRA’s Multi-Biometric Verification System (MBVS) also received an award in the Community and Remote Services category. The system provides an alternative method for biometric verification and helps improve access to identity verification services.
The authority’s Proof of Life Certificate service won an award in the Digital Government category. The service allows pensioners to complete their proof-of-life verification through the Pak ID app and other supporting channels.
NADRA said the three awards recognize its efforts to make digital identity and government services easier, more accessible and more efficient for citizens.

The recognition also highlights the growing role of digital platforms in delivering public services. Through services such as Pak ID, MBVS and the Proof of Life Certificate, NADRA is expanding access to identity and verification services for citizens inside Pakistan and overseas.
The PASHA ICT Awards recognize technology initiatives and digital solutions across different sectors. NADRA’s three awards at the 2026 event highlight the authority’s ongoing focus on digital transformation and citizen-focused services.

Opus 5.5 diklaim menawarkan performa setara Claude Fable 5.1 untuk sebagian besar tugas, namun dengan biaya 40 persen lebih murah dibandingkan Opus 5, sebagaimana dikutip dari keterangan perusahaan, Rabu (23/9/2026).

items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Anthropic resmi merilis Claude Opus 5.5 pada Selasa, 22 September 2026. Model kecerdasan buatan (AI) baru ini menjadi generasi pertama dari keluarga Claude 5.5 yang tersedia untuk seluruh pengguna, mulai dari aplikasi mobile, desktop, hingga API.
Opus 5.5 diklaim menawarkan performa setara Claude Fable 5.1 untuk sebagian besar tugas, namun dengan biaya 40 persen lebih murah dibandingkan Opus 5, sebagaimana dikutip dari keterangan perusahaan, Rabu (23/9/2026).
Walau biaya operasional model baru ini lebih terjangkau, perusahaan malah semakin memperketat keamanan AI mereka untuk menghindari skenario berisiko tinggi.
Peluncuran ini datang pada saat industri AI tengah memberi perhatian lebih besar terhadap keamanan model frontier atau model AI paling canggih yang saat ini dikembangkan perusahaan teknologi besar.
Soroti Penurunan Perilaku Berisiko di Claude Opus 5.5
Claude Opus 5.5. (Gizmologi/ Yuslianson)
Salah satu klaim utama dalam peluncuran Claude Opus 5.5 adalah penurunan perilaku yang mencoba melewati batas pengamanan sistem.
Anthropic mengatakan pengujian internal menunjukkan model baru ini 85% lebih jarang melakukan tindakan yang mengarah pada pelanggaran batas keamanan dibanding Claude Opus 5 dan Mythos 5.1. Perusahaan menyebut sebagian besar kejadian yang terdeteksi pada model sebelumnya tergolong berisiko rendah dan dilaporkan sendiri oleh model selama proses evaluasi.
Untuk mendukung klaim tersebut, perusahaan melibatkan organisasi eksternal seperti Frontier Design dan METR dalam proses evaluasi sebelum model dirilis ke publik.
Keamanan AI Jadi Sorotan
Anthropic mengungkap sejumlah kasus penyalahgunaan Claude untuk operasi siber, pengawasan, penipuan, hingga aktivitas berisiko lainnya dalam Threat Intelligence Report September 2026.
Peluncuran Claude Opus 5.5 ini langsung menjadi sorotan. Dalam beberapa bulan terakhir, keamanan AI menjadi topik utama di industri teknologi. Berbagai perusahaan AI menghadapi pertanyaan mengenai bagaimana model yang semakin otonom harus diuji dan dibatasi.
Anthropic sendiri sebelumnya mengungkap telah menghentikan sementara sebagian evaluasi keamanan dan pelatihan tertentu setelah menemukan perilaku yang tidak sesuai harapan pada agen AI dalam lingkungan pengujian. Perusahaan kemudian memperketat pengawasan dan menambah mekanisme kontrol sebelum melanjutkan program tersebut.
Di saat yang sama, industri AI juga diramaikan oleh sejumlah laporan mengenai model yang berhasil mengakses sistem di luar lingkungan simulasi ketika menjalani pengujian keamanan. Peristiwa tersebut mendorong perusahaan AI untuk meningkatkan investasi pada sistem evaluasi dan pengamanan model.
Anthropic Tetap Kejar Performa
Meski fokus utama peluncuran berada pada keamanan, Anthropic menegaskan Claude Opus 5.5 tetap dirancang untuk bersaing dalam tugas pengembangan perangkat lunak dan pekerjaan teknis lainnya.
Menurut perusahaan, model baru ini menawarkan performa setara dengan Fable 5.1 untuk sejumlah tugas teknis, namun dengan biaya yang lebih rendah. Anthropic juga menyebut Claude Opus 5.5 mampu mengungguli beberapa model pesaing pada benchmark pengembangan perangkat lunak tertentu.
Selain Opus 5.5, Anthropic mengatakan keluarga Claude 5.5 akan diperluas melalui peluncuran Claude Sonnet 5.5 dan Claude Haiku 5.5 di masa mendatang.
Anthropic Bongkar Penyalahgunaan Claude
Di sisi lain, Anthropic baru saja membongkar sejumlah kasus penyalahgunaan Claude, di mana chatbot tersebut dipakai pelaku kejahatan untuk operasi siber, pengawasan negara, penipuan online, hingga riset biologis berbahaya.
Informasi ini diungkap langsung oleh perusahaan lewat laporan Threat Intelligence Report yang terbit 10 September 2026. Laporan ini merangkum temuan tim keamanan Anthropic sepanjang Desember 2025 hingga Agustus 2026.
Kasus-kasus di dalam laporan ini bukan potret penyalahgunaan Claude secara umum, melainkan beberapa pilihan insiden paling serius yang berhasil dideteksi tim keamanan perusahaan, sebagaimana dikutip dari keterangan Anthropic, Sabtu (12/9/2026).
Pelakunya pun beragam, mulai dari kelompok yang diduga mendapat dukungan negara, kriminal bermotif finansial, vendor spyware komersial, lembaga propaganda, hingga individu dengan kepentingan politik.
Claude Jadi “Operator” Serangan Siber
young lady hacking a computer network, or using computer
Di ranah kejahatan siber, peran Claude bergeser dari sekadar alat bantu menulis kode menjadi bagian dari operasi itu sendiri. Anthropic mendapati penggunaan AI untuk membangun malware, phishing kit, sampai perangkat surveillance,
Dalam beberapa kasus lainnya, AI juga dipakai untuk menjalankan perintah langsung ke jaringan korban dan mengekstrak data. Salah satu operasi multi-agent yang ditemukan bisa menjalankan reconnaissance dan pencurian data ke banyak target sekaligus.
Mengerikannya, satu serangan rampung dalam dua sampai tiga jam dan satu operator bisa menangani puluhan korban dalam waktu bersamaan.
Meski begitu, Anthropic mengingatkan keputusan penting masih berada di tangan manusia. Pemilihan target, monetisasi hasil serangan, dan evaluasi hasil umumnya tetap dilakukan operator.
Dengan kata lain, AI lebih berperan sebagai pengganda kecepatan, skala, dan efisiensi sebuah operasi.

Perbedaan tersebut terlihat dari fitur yang dibawa masing-masing perangkat. REDMI Watch 6 Active menonjolkan layar AMOLED, Bluetooth Call, dan desain ramping, sementara REDMI Watch 6 Lite membawa GPS independen dual-band untuk aktivitas luar ruangan. Ketiga perangkat tersebut tersedia melalui official store Xiaomi Indonesia di Tokopedia. Harganya mulai Rp449.000 untuk Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Active, sedangkan REDMI Watch 6 Active dan REDMI Watch 6 Lite masing-masing dibanderol Rp649.000 dan Rp999.000 sebagai harga SRP.

items.author: Bambang Dwi Atmoko
items.content:
Xiaomi memperkenalkan tiga wearable baru untuk pasar Indonesia, yakni REDMI Watch 6 Active, REDMI Watch 6 Lite, dan Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Active. Ketiganya menawarkan pendekatan berbeda, mulai dari smartwatch untuk kebutuhan harian hingga perangkat yang lebih ditujukan untuk aktivitas olahraga.
Perbedaan tersebut terlihat dari fitur yang dibawa masing-masing perangkat. REDMI Watch 6 Active menonjolkan layar AMOLED, Bluetooth Call, dan desain ramping, sementara REDMI Watch 6 Lite membawa GPS independen dual-band untuk aktivitas luar ruangan. Adapun Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Active hadir dalam bentuk yang lebih ringkas dengan daya tahan baterai hingga 21 hari.
Ketiga perangkat tersebut tersedia melalui official store Xiaomi Indonesia di Tokopedia. Harganya mulai Rp449.000 untuk Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Active, sedangkan REDMI Watch 6 Active dan REDMI Watch 6 Lite masing-masing dibanderol Rp649.000 dan Rp999.000 sebagai harga SRP.
REDMI Watch 6 Active punya layar AMOLED 1,85 inci dan Bluetooth Call
REDMI Watch 6 Active menjadi pilihan yang lebih berorientasi pada penggunaan sehari-hari. Perangkat ini menggunakan layar AMOLED HD berukuran 1,85 inci, sehingga area tampilannya cukup besar untuk melihat informasi seperti notifikasi maupun informasi aktivitas.
Untuk kebutuhan komunikasi, smartwatch ini mendukung Bluetooth Call. Pengguna dapat melakukan panggilan melalui jam tangan tanpa harus selalu mengambil smartphone. Xiaomi juga menempatkan desain sebagai salah satu aspek REDMI Watch 6 Active. Bodinya memiliki ketebalan 9,9 mm dan menggunakan mekanisme quick-release strap, sehingga tali dapat dilepas dan diganti.
Daya tahan baterainya diklaim mencapai 18 hari dalam sekali pengisian daya. Perangkat ini juga memiliki fitur Always-on Display (AOD) untuk menampilkan informasi tertentu pada layar tanpa harus selalu mengaktifkan layar secara penuh.
Dengan kombinasi tersebut, REDMI Watch 6 Active lebih ditujukan untuk pengguna yang mencari smartwatch dengan fungsi dasar sehari-hari, tetapi tetap ingin mendapatkan layar AMOLED dan fitur komunikasi dari pergelangan tangan.
REDMI Watch 6 Lite membawa GPS dual-band untuk olahraga outdoor
Berbeda dari Watch 6 Active, REDMI Watch 6 Lite lebih menitikberatkan kemampuan pelacakan aktivitas olahraga, terutama untuk kegiatan di luar ruangan. Perangkat ini menggunakan layar AMOLED 1,96 inci dengan bezel tipis. Fitur yang menjadi pembeda utamanya adalah Dual-band GPS Tracking independen, sehingga pelacakan lokasi dapat dilakukan langsung dari smartwatch tanpa bergantung sepenuhnya pada smartphone.
Xiaomi juga menyebut REDMI Watch 6 Lite mendukung lebih dari 150 mode olahraga. Untuk aktivitas yang berhubungan dengan air, perangkat ini memiliki ketahanan air 5 ATM dan dapat digunakan untuk aktivitas seperti berenang.
Daya tahan baterainya juga mencapai hingga 18 hari. Artinya, perbedaan utama Watch 6 Lite dibandingkan Watch 6 Active bukan semata ukuran layar, melainkan keberadaan GPS independen dan jumlah mode olahraga yang jauh lebih banyak.
Bagi pengguna yang rutin melakukan aktivitas seperti berjalan, berlari, atau berolahraga di luar ruangan, keberadaan GPS di perangkat menjadi salah satu faktor yang patut diperhatikan karena rute aktivitas dapat dilacak tanpa harus selalu membawa smartphone.
Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Active lebih ringkas dengan baterai hingga 21 hari
Di posisi paling terjangkau, Xiaomi memperkenalkan Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Active. Bentuknya lebih ringkas dibandingkan dua smartwatch REDMI Watch tersebut, dengan layar berukuran 1,47 inci. Perangkat ini menggunakan metallic-look frame yang memberikan tampilan berbeda dari gelang kebugaran konvensional.
Xiaomi Smart Band 11 Active juga memiliki ketahanan air 5 ATM, pemantauan kesehatan sepanjang hari, serta dukungan lebih dari 50 mode olahraga. Salah satu angka yang paling menonjol adalah daya tahan baterainya. Xiaomi mengklaim Smart Band 11 Active dapat digunakan hingga 21 hari dalam sekali pengisian daya.
Dengan harga Rp449.000, perangkat ini menempatkan diri sebagai opsi paling sederhana dan terjangkau dalam trio wearable baru Xiaomi. Fitur yang dibawa lebih berfokus pada pemantauan aktivitas dan kesehatan dibandingkan fungsi smartwatch seperti panggilan Bluetooth.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s Universal Service Fund has a fresh budget to work with, and this time the numbers come with a specific target: 3.66 million people across 21 districts who are still waiting for reliable mobile broadband.
The USF Policy Committee approved a Rs32.90 billion outlay for fiscal year 2026-27 at a meeting chaired by Federal Minister for IT and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja. The session also cleared 15 new 4G projects spanning 1,893 mauzas, according to details reported by The Express Tribune.
How the Budget Breaks Down
The approved allocation splits into two main streams. Rs24.89 billion goes toward disbursements on projects already under construction, while Rs6.56 billion is earmarked for new initiatives launching in the coming year.
USF Chief Executive Officer Mudassar Naveed, along with senior management, walked the committee through the fund’s proposed project portfolio and spending priorities for FY27 before the budget was signed off.
To keep implementation moving without delay, the committee separately approved releasing Rs5.57 billion as the first-quarter tranche. That upfront release matters practically: USF projects often stall in their early months waiting for funds to clear, so front-loading the first quarter’s allocation is meant to avoid that bottleneck.
What’s Already Running, and What’s New
USF currently has 28 projects under implementation. Of these, 17 fall under the Next Generation Broadband Service Delivery (NG-BSD) category, covering mobile broadband rollout, while 11 are Next Generation Optical Fibre Network Services (NG-OFNS) projects, which extend fibre backbone infrastructure to underserved regions.
The new funding adds nine more NG-BSD projects and four additional NG-OFNS projects to that pipeline. The committee also approved block allocations for smaller lots under both programmes, a mechanism USF typically uses to fund connectivity in scattered, low-population settlements that don’t justify a standalone large-scale project.
The Scale Behind the Numbers
The 15 new 4G projects specifically target 3.66 million people spread across 1,893 mauzas in 21 districts. That figure gives the budget approval a concrete human scale rather than leaving it as an abstract fiscal allocation, and it signals where USF’s near-term priority sits: mobile broadband expansion over other connectivity types.
For context, a mauza in Pakistan’s administrative structure is a revenue village or land unit, often smaller than a full union council, meaning these projects are aimed at genuinely localised, hard-to-reach populations rather than district headquarters or towns that likely already have some coverage.
Why This Round of Funding Stands Out
USF budgets are an annual fixture, but the scale and split of this one point to a continued shift toward mobile broadband over fixed infrastructure. Nine new NG-BSD projects against four new NG-OFNS projects suggest the fund is prioritising last-mile mobile access over fibre backbone expansion this cycle, likely because mobile broadband reaches end users faster and at a lower per-connection cost in sparsely populated terrain.
That said, approved budgets and disbursed funds are not the same thing. USF has previously faced delays between policy approval and on-ground project completion, so the real test of this Rs32.90 billion allocation will be how much of it translates into working towers and live connections within the fiscal year, not how quickly it clears committee.
The Bigger Picture for Digital Inclusion
Pakistan’s digital divide remains sharply regional, with connectivity concentrated in urban centres while large parts of Balochistan, interior Sindh, and northern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa continue to lag. The Ministry of IT and USF have framed this budget as part of a sustained push to close that gap, expand telecom access, and support digital inclusion in remote areas.
Whether this translates into meaningfully improved coverage will depend less on the approval itself and more on execution speed, an area where USF’s track record has been mixed. The 3.66 million target gives this year’s plan a measurable benchmark that wasn’t as explicit in previous budget cycles, which at least makes it easier to check progress against, come the next fiscal year.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority has a new officer overseeing how strictly telecom operators are held to their obligations. Brigadier (Retd) Amir Shehzad has been named Director General Enforcement, taking over the division with immediate effect after a reassignment ordered by the PTA Chairman.
From Licensing to Enforcement
Shehzad’s move is a lateral shift rather than a fresh induction. He previously held the post of DG Licensing at the authority, a role centred on issuing and managing telecom licences rather than policing compliance after they’re granted.
The switch to enforcement puts him on the operational side of PTA’s regulatory work, the division responsible for monitoring whether telecom companies are meeting the service standards, spectrum conditions, and consumer-protection rules attached to their licences. It’s a shift from paperwork-heavy oversight to a role with more direct, ground-level accountability.
What the Enforcement Role Covers
PTA’s enforcement wing handles a broad mandate: checking network quality against licensing benchmarks, acting on consumer complaints that escalate beyond operator-level resolution, and taking action against unauthorised telecom activity, including grey traffic and illegal device operations.
Shehzad has been assigned two specific priorities in his new post: improving the overall quality of telecom services and strengthening the enforcement mechanism itself. Both point to an authority under pressure to show it can back its regulations with follow-through, not just policy on paper.
Shehzad’s Own Framing of the Role
Speaking after taking charge, Shehzad described the DG Enforcement post as an important and challenging assignment. He said his approach would centre on meeting the expectations of three stakeholders at once: the federal government, the PTA itself, and telecom consumers.
He added that consumer expectations specifically would remain a key consideration as he carries out the role, a statement that reads more as a stated priority than a commitment to specific reforms.
Why This Matters for Pakistani Telecom Users
For ordinary subscribers, enforcement leadership changes rarely make headlines, but they shape outcomes that do reach consumers eventually: how fast complaints about call drops or billing disputes get escalated, how seriously operators take service-quality audits, and how aggressively PTA pursues unregistered SIMs or unauthorised network equipment.
Pakistan’s telecom sector has faced recurring criticism over service quality, particularly in areas where network congestion and inconsistent coverage persist despite operators technically meeting minimum licence conditions.
The Broader Pattern
This appointment fits a wider trend at PTA of moving officers between licensing, compliance, and enforcement functions rather than hiring externally for these posts. That internal rotation model has advantages in institutional continuity, but it also means enforcement priorities can shift each time leadership changes hands, since incoming officers bring their own read of what needs tightening first.
Whether Shehzad’s tenure produces measurable improvement in service-quality metrics or enforcement action against non-compliant operators will be the real test of this appointment. Statements about meeting stakeholder expectations are, for now, just that, statements. The authority’s own complaint and enforcement data over the coming months will show whether the change in leadership brings a change in outcomes.

items.summary:
Indian Startup IPOs In Full Swing
Indian startup IPO spring is in full bloom. Snapdeal parent AceVector is all set to list on the bourses next month, Spinny has filed its draft IPO papers, and Furlenco is pushing the needle on its D-Street debut.
Snapdeal’s IPO Deck: In its second attempt at a listing, the Snapdeal parent’s ₹420 Cr issue blends a ₹287 Cr fresh raise and a trimmed OFS of 4.16 Cr shares. It has also set the IPO price band at ₹30-₹32, valuing the company at ₹1,741 Cr at the upper end of the spectrum. The IPO will open next week.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Indian Startup IPOs In Full Swing
Indian startup IPO spring is in full bloom. Snapdeal parent AceVector is all set to list on the bourses next month, Spinny has filed its draft IPO papers, and Furlenco is pushing the needle on its D-Street debut.
Snapdeal’s IPO Deck: In its second attempt at a listing, the Snapdeal parent’s ₹420 Cr issue blends a ₹287 Cr fresh raise and a trimmed OFS of 4.16 Cr shares. It has also set the IPO price band at ₹30-₹32, valuing the company at ₹1,741 Cr at the upper end of the spectrum. The IPO will open next week.
What works in AceVector’s favour is its healthy top line, improving unit economics, non-metro focus, value ecommerce play and a stake in Unicommerce.
Spinny Files DRHP: The used car marketplace has confidentially filed its DRHP for a ₹2,500-₹3,000 Cr IPO, targeting a 2027 listing. With revenue nearing ₹6,000 Cr in FY26 and losses narrowing, Spinny is betting on its full-stack retail, financing and ancillary services to sustain growth and woo investors.
Furlenco Gears Up For IPO, Too: Following rival RentoMojo’s suit, Furlenco has also kicked off its IPO proceedings. The startup plans to soon appoint ICICI Securities as an advisor for its up to ₹1,200 Cr public issue, which will target a valuation of around ₹7,000 Cr. Furlenco is looking to launch the IPO in FY28.
The Broader IPO Wave: New-age tech companies continue to make a beeline for the public markets. As per Inc42 data, 24 startups have already filed their DRHPs, while over 25 are in various stages of finalising their IPO plans. Unicorns like OYO, Razorpay and Zetwerk alone could raise over ₹34,000 Cr in 2026, making it one of the biggest years for startup IPOs.
Startups now see IPOs as a credible exit and growth capital source. Recent strong debuts, policy support and investor appetite for niche businesses are further encouraging founders. With much on the anvil, here is all about who is debuting on the bourses next…
From The Editor’s Desk
Zetwerk-Ayr Settle Dispute
The two companies have reached a settlement by agreeing to dismiss all claims asserted in lawsuits, pending before a US business court and a Bengaluru court. The financial and other terms of the settlement have not been disclosed.
Zetwerk had alleged that Ayr founder Anirudh Reddy downloaded hundreds of files and used the data to pursue Zetwerk’s clients. Ayr denied the allegations and filed counter claims accusing Zetwerk of trade-secret theft and trademark infringement.
The resolution removes a major legal overhang as Zetwerk prepares for its IPO. The B2B manufacturing startup last month filed its DRHP with SEBI for a public issue, which comprises a fresh issue of shares worth ₹2,600 Cr and an OFS of up to 9.6 Cr shares.
Sol Foundry Bags $4 Mn
Emerging out of stealth mode, the AI startup has raised ₹38 Cr in a funding round from General Catalyst, Nexus Venture Partners and others to fuel R&D, AI model development and hiring.
Founded in 2025, Sol Foundry’s AI assistant can research a topic, assemble a document, find calendar slots and draft replies using context drawn from scattered email conversations. The model-agnostic platform initially plans to target professionals.
The startup is pre-revenue and has not yet finalised pricing. It plans to explore usage- or outcome-based billing plus a fixed component. It is also pursuing a prosumer-first model, allowing individuals to sign up before expanding into enterprise sales.
Captain Fresh’s FY26 Show
The B2B seafood brand claims to have retained profitability in FY26. This came on the back of consolidated net revenue zooming 52% YoY to ₹5,169 Cr in the fiscal under review and adjusted EBITDA nearly tripling YoY to ₹371 Cr.
Meanwhile, Captain Fresh was saddled with a debt of ₹2,300 Cr at the end of FY26, which the startup attributed to higher working capital requirements during the fiscal. The company now claims to be on track to achieve ₹10,000 Cr in revenue in FY27.
Founded in 2020, Captain Fresh operates a global packaged seafood business. It sources seafood from more than 30 countries and serves nearly 2,500 customers. The IPO-bound startup has raised nearly $250 Mn to date.
PhonePe Sets Eyes On The UAE
The Walmart-backed fintech giant has received in-principle nod from the Central Bank of the UAE for two payment licences. The approvals will enable the startup to offer retail payment services and issue stored-value products such as digital wallets.
This takes PhonePe another step closer to launching its payments operation outside India. However, the fintech major will still have to fulfil the remaining regulatory requirements to begin commercial operations in the Middle Eastern nation.
The development comes days after PhonePe’s monetisation prospects in India received a boost from the reintroduction of MDR on certain UPI transactions. On the back of this, the startup has revived its IPO plans and is now targeting a public listing by March 2027.
ED Chargesheets EMT Cofounder
The Enforcement Directorate has filed a chargesheet against EaseMyTrip cofounder and chairman Nishant Pitti in the Mahadev online betting app money laundering case. Pitti said he was not aware of any chargesheet and would contest any such charges.
The agency also provisionally attached demat shares belonging to Pitti worth ₹59.6 Cr under the PMLA. The ED has also sought a special PMLA court’s permission to confiscate the shares, alleging that they constitute proceeds of crime.
The agency has accused him of facilitating the entry of alleged illegal betting proceeds into the Indian stock market through FPIs. Even last year, ED had alleged that Pitti was connected to a network that used betting proceeds to manipulate several stocks.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Can Agriculture Fund Vaimanika’s Defence Ambitions?
India’s drone industry is growing. But farmers still lack access to affordable drone spraying, while defence forces need mission-ready UAVs for high-risk operations. Vaimanika Aerospace is addressing both needs through drone services and a vertically-integrated stack.
A Full-Stack Operator: Founded in 2022, Vaimanika operates an agriculture-focused drone-as-a-service network. Farmers and institutional customers can access precision spraying on a pay-per-acre basis. The startup also earns through drone sales, pilot training, maintenance and franchise-led services. Its agriculture network includes around 210 drones and has generated nearly ₹35 Cr in spraying revenue.
The Defence Portfolio: Vaimanika’s second growth engine is defence. Its portfolio spans heavy-payload UAVs, ISR platforms, FPVs and counter-UAS systems. Its systems have undergone field validation with Indian Army formations, including high-altitude trials and a 105 kg payload test.
Integrating Vertically: The startup is developing its own airframes, avionics, ground-control stations, communications hardware, battery systems and autonomous-flight software. Greater control over these mission-critical components could help Vaimanika customise systems for difficult terrain and reduce reliance on external suppliers.
Eye On The Prize: Vaimanika claims to have clocked ₹52.6 Cr in revenue in FY26 against a profit after tax of ₹9.47 Cr. The startup is now converting the cash and engineering base from its agri-focused drone business to fund its defence UAV pitch. So, can Vaimanika disrupt the status quo and build a scalable drone tech business?
Infographic Of The Day
As many as 13 startups have already listed on the bourses so far this year, 24 have filed their DRHPs, while 25+ are in various stages of planning their IPOs. Here is all about who is going public in the Indian startup realm in 2026….
