items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
The International Chamber of Commerce last week rescued Nigeria from yet another set of predators determined to suck the last drop of blood still running in the country’s economic veins. It rejected the criminal claim for damages for a breach of contract to the tune of USD 2.35 billion by Sunrise Power Transition Company, an organisation owned by Nigerian-born Leno Adesanya. The ICC also rejected the settlement claim of USD 400 million by Sunrise and ordered it to pay Nigeria’s legal expenses of USD 11.82 million. While USD 11 million may not look like a huge amount of money for a country to forfeit, USD 2.35 billion is, by all standards, a lot to lose, especially to faceless groups of international fraudsters.
All the way from Paris, France, the ICC saved Nigeria from the embarrassment of being dragged before another international body and being brazenly robbed with the apparent imprimatur of international law. We appear before such bodies ill-prepared and without the heart to fight for what is rightfully ours, betrayed already by children, actually bastards, spawned from the loins of prostitutes. Those who exploit us in this manner know us for who we are: a people lacking any strand of patriotic fibre to fight for the good of their country. We are the first to say the worst things about Nigeria, and since foreigners know this about us, it takes them little or no effort to persuade us to join in the brutal rape of our land. Yet those who have the responsibility to save us from such gross violations either look away or go into the fight half-heartedly and unprepared to do what it takes to restore the country’s honour.
We saw this in the way the Bakassi Peninsula was given away and eventually lost to Cameroon. Even when it comes to the issue of defending the country’s interests or citizens against foreigners or foreign interests, Nigeria takes a laid-back attitude. It was what played out in the Nigeria versus Process and Industrial Development (P&ID) case that the Supreme Court in the United Kingdom ruled on less than a year ago. For the best part of nearly 15 years, Nigeria looked on as criminal businesspeople dragged her across foreign courts and arbitration bodies. It was not until 2022 or thereabouts, when assets such as aircraft and others were being seized and the country was being embarrassed around the world, that the Muhammadu Buhari government decided to take the fight to the criminal aggressors. Anyone looking at the manner in which Nigeria was being disgraced could not have hesitated to conclude that the country was as guilty as charged. But the moment we decided to take more than a passing interest in the case, the tide changed.
P&ID was a shell company. It dubiously won a 20-year Gas Supply and Processing Agreement (GSPA) contract in 2010 to help harness and refine Nigeria’s large deposit of “wet” gas that was being flared. Since this agreement was never meant to be executed, neither party to the agreement acted on it. This was the case until P&ID decided to initiate a legal process against Nigeria for the breach of a contract that was not only fraudulently won but was also never intended to be executed. The London tribunal to which Nigeria was dragged ordered the country to pay P&ID USD 6.6 billion, which soon grew to USD 11 billion in damages. It was after this that Nigeria, through the EFCC, chose the path of legal challenge and ultimately won a reprieve through the wise Justice Robin Knowles of the English High Court. The judge set aside the tribunal ruling and was able to show that the original contract awarded to P&ID was fraudulently obtained through the corrupt enrichment of Nigerian officials. On October 22, 2025, the British Supreme Court finally dismissed P&ID’s appeal and ordered it to pay Nigeria’s legal costs of GBP 44 million.
In the Sunrise–Mambila Hydropower Project, the Federal Executive Council expressly rejected Sunrise’s bid to construct a 3,050-megawatt hydroelectric power station. It was to be located in Kakara Village, on the Donga River, around Gembu, on the Mambila Plateau in Taraba State. Despite the FEC’s rejection, the then Minister of Power, Olu Agunloye, allegedly gave Sunrise, a near-bankrupt shell company with no expertise in hydropower, the go-ahead for the project.
The names of Atiku Abubakar, former vice-president, and Abubakar Malami, attorney-general and minister of justice under the Buhari administration, appeared in the Mambila Hydroelectric Power Project case at the ICC.
Malami has already forfeited assets worth billions of naira to the Federal Government of Nigeria in diverse cases. He basically sold Nigeria to Sunrise in his advocacy that $400 million, rather than $200 million, be paid as damages to Sunrise. It did not matter to Malami that Nigeria was bleeding financially or that the reputation of President Muhammadu Buhari, his principal, as a man of integrity, was at stake. Both President Muhammadu Buhari and President Olusegun Obasanjo were present at the ICC’s hearing and testified on behalf of Nigeria in 2023.
Rather than address the integrity issue raised by the Paris court, Atiku Abubakar continues to shadow-box and has dismissed it as political. In his press conference last week, he spoke on everything except the issue.
Atiku is still dancing around the issue of his role in the Mambila–Sunrise business. What is political about this? Throughout his political and civil service career, the former VP has had to contend with issues of probity. The ICC case has only brought home the point more forcefully, and he must respond to it if he knows he is clean.
The post A Daniel has again come to judgement in the Mambila Hydroelectric Power Project, by Rotimi Fasan appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Akinbayo Wahab
items.content:
By Peter Duru, Makurdi
The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, in Benue State, Chief Michael Aondoakaa, SAN, has promised to establish specialised geriatric units in hospitals across the state to provide free basic healthcare and minor surgical procedures for elderly citizens if elected governor in 2027.
Aondoakaa, a former Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, said the initiative would form part of his administration’s broader agenda on healthcare, security, pensioners’ welfare, infrastructure development and prudent management of public resources.
Speaking in Makurdi, the PDP candidate said government had both a moral and constitutional responsibility to cater for citizens who had spent their productive years contributing to the development of the state.
According to him, the proposed geriatric units would be specially equipped to provide elderly people with quality and specialised medical care in a conducive environment.
He said basic healthcare services and minor surgical procedures would be provided free of charge to senior citizens under the proposed programme.
“We have a duty to care for our elderly people who are in their late 60s, 70s, 80s and older.
“Beyond government responsibility, it is part of our African culture to honour and support those who have worked hard and sacrificed for society. They deserve access to quality healthcare and dignity in old age,” Aondoakaa said.
He said his administration, if elected, would place healthcare and security among its foremost priorities, stressing that the two sectors were fundamental to the wellbeing and development of the state.
“Our healthcare system must be responsive to the needs of ordinary people, especially the vulnerable and the elderly.
“At the same time, government must take seriously its responsibility to protect lives and property because security is the foundation of development,” he stated.
On the recurring debate over livestock management and ranching in the state, Aondoakaa maintained that ranching should primarily remain a private business venture, with government creating the necessary environment for private investors and livestock owners to operate.
“Ranching is a private enterprise. Government’s role is to create an enabling environment, not to take over the business itself,” he said.
The PDP candidate also expressed concern over the hardship faced by retired civil servants in the state, particularly those affected by outstanding pensions and gratuities.
Aondoakaa argued that workers who dedicated several decades to the service of the state should not face hardship and uncertainty after retirement.
“Those who spent their productive years serving the state should not be abandoned in retirement.
“Pensioners are entitled to their benefits and should be treated with dignity and respect,” he said.
He further argued that the payment of salaries, pensions and gratuities should not be portrayed as extraordinary achievements by any government, describing them as fundamental obligations arising from the relationship between the state and its workforce.
“Salaries and pensions are not favours. They are obligations arising from the relationship between government and its workers.
“Fulfilling those obligations should be routine and not something that is celebrated as an extraordinary achievement,” Aondoakaa added.
On infrastructure, the PDP governorship candidate promised to adopt a more consultative, professionally driven approach to conceiving and executing major government projects.
He said his administration would subject major projects to rigorous scrutiny while involving relevant ministries, technical experts and other stakeholders to ensure that public funds were properly utilised.
“There will be proper consultation before major projects are undertaken. Our focus will be on infrastructure that improves the lives of the people and delivers measurable value for public funds,” he stated.
Aondoakaa also pledged to make greater use of the expertise and institutional knowledge available within the state’s civil service.
He described career civil servants as a reservoir of technical competence and institutional memory, saying their knowledge should be better utilised in government planning and project implementation.
“Our civil servants possess invaluable knowledge and experience. They understand how government works and should be actively involved in planning and implementing development projects. We must make better use of that expertise,” he said.
The former Attorney General said his administration would also prioritise policies capable of translating public resources into tangible improvements in the lives of residents.

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
Following the exit of the Super Falconets at the quarter final stage of the FIFA Under-20 women’s World Cup in Poland on Sunday, fresh information has revealed how two key members of the squad missed the tournament.
Nigeria went to Poland without captain Joy Igbokwe, and creative midfielder Faridat AbdulWahab, due to visa-related issues.
Captain Igbokwe was a colossal loss due to her leadership and energetic ball-winning attributes, while AbdulWahab, Igbokwe’s teammate at Nasarawa Amazons in the NWFL, is a creative spark whose passing range could have cut through a stubborn Colombia.
Despite their absence, the Falconets recorded the 2026 highest tournament win with a 10-1 victory over New Caledonia, and the Moses Aduku-led ladies sent England’s young Lionesses packing in a shocking but well-deserved 3-0 win.
The team was seconds from forcing extra-time against Colombia despite a second half red card, but conceded in the 92nd minute to crash out at the last-eight stage.
However, their absence was ultimately felt, and Colin Udoh, a former media officer of the Super Eagles, has claimed that both players lied during their visa interview at the Polish embassy.
According to his post on social media platform X, Udoh revealed that multiple officials in the Nigeria football federation confirmed both Igbokwe and AbdulWahab failed to provide a honest response multiple times to a question asked during the visa interview.
“They were asked the same question three times, and each time, they were not honest with their answers, even when that answer was on the computer in front of the visa officer.”
Udoh, who is married to Super Falcons legend, Mercy Akide, however, refrained from revealing the question, but added that the intervention of NFF officials and subsequent appeals did not yield a positive response due to the lack of sincerity from the players.
Igbokwe was named Nasarawa Amazons’ player of the season, and made the NWFL team of the season, while AbdulWahab starred for Nigeria’s women under-17 Flamingos at the 2024 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in the Dominican Republic before he was promoted to the Under-20 team.

items.author: Ado Abubakar Musa, Jos
items.content:
Gunmen reportedly ambushed security operatives attached to Operation Rainbow, a state security outfit in Plateau State, in Bariki Ladi Local Government Area of the state, on Tuesday, killing a policeman.
Three civilians were also reportedly killed in a separate incident at Rakok, also in Barkin Ladi LGA.
The security operatives were reportedly attacked along the Gagshi Road in the local government area.
The two incidents, according to separate sources, brought the reported death toll to four, amid renewed attacks in parts of Barkin Ladi, where the government imposed dusk to dawn curfew, on Monday.
ADC: It’s a national disgrace for Tinubu to be in France while Macron is at UNGA
SBM report: Nigerians must reject Tinubu same way they’ve rejected subsidy removal – Atiku
A security operative, who spoke on condition of anonymity, also confirmed the attack, saying, “We just experienced an ambush in which a security personnel attached to Operation Rainbow was killed.”
He added that the sad incident occurred around 4pm.
President of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, BYM, Barr. Dalyop Solomon Mwantiri, who confirmed the reported ambush, said he narrowly escaped being caught up in the incident.
He described the latest development as an indication that the security situation in the state was taking a “bigger dimension.”
Mwantiri said the attacks were no longer confined to the night, adding that incidents are now occurring in broad daylight.
He said, “I would have also been involved in that incident if not that God, out of His mercy, saved me.”
He said, “This security challenge has entered another level. This thing is taking a bigger dimension.This will not be night attack again. This will not be even during daytime.”
He urged security personnel and other relevant authorities not to relent in their efforts to protect lives and property and restore peace to affected communities.”
Meanwhile, a community leader, Mr Lawrence Gyang, said three persons were killed at Rakok, also known as Kafi Abu, in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area on Tuesday.
Gyang alleged that one person and two unidentified women were killed in broad daylight, while attending the funeral of two persons, who were also allegedly killed the previous day, while travelling to Gashish District.
According to him, the victims were among mourners who had gathered for the funeral when the incident occurred.
Our correspondent reports that despite the curfew, tensions continue to increase in Barkin Ladi and adjoining communities, following a series of attacks in parts of the LGA areas in recent days.
The Police Public Relations Officer in the state, SP Alabo Alfred, had not responded to inquiries from our correspondent as of the time of this report.

items.author: Bassey Willie
items.content:
Rivers State Chief Judge, Justice Simeon Chibuzor-Amadi, has ordered the release of 14 inmates from the Port Harcourt Maximum Security Custodial Centre.
This is part of activities marking the 2026/2027 Legal Year Opening and the 2026 Gaol Delivery Exercise.
Justice Chibuzor-Amadi, who released the inmates during the visit to the correctional centre, on Tuesday, said the exercise was conducted pursuant to the Criminal Justice “Release from Custody Special Provisions Act” and it’s aimed at decongesting the custodial facility.
He explained that those released included inmates who had spent periods exceeding the maximum sentence prescribed for their alleged offences, as well as others whose cases had been delayed through no fault of their own.
He urged officials of the correctional facility to protect confidential information, particularly details of inmates scheduled for release, to avoid unnecessary tension.

Uba Sani Approves N3.659 bn For Retirees, Pays N21.455bn In Three Years
Addressing the released inmates, the Chief Judge urged them to return to society as ambassadors of peace and good conduct, warning that those who re-offend may not receive a similar opportunity.
Justice Chibuzor-Amadi also cautioned the youths in the state against being used by politicians to cause violence during the political season, noting that young people are often victims of political violence.
He encouraged those who maintained their innocence to use the opportunity to engage in lawful and meaningful activities, acquire productive skills, improve their livelihoods, and make positive contributions to their families and communities.
He added that the exercise reinforces the commitment of the Rivers State Judiciary and Ministry of Justice to decongest correctional facilities, uphold the fundamental right to fair hearing, and ensure that justice is administered fairly, promptly and in accordance with the law.
The Rivers State Controller of Corrections, Richard Moses-Williams, commended the judiciary for the exercise, describing gaol delivery as an important measure in addressing congestion in custodial facilities.

items.title: Noma: The neglected disease devastating children in northern Nigeria
items.summary: Noma is a rapidly progressing and often fatal infection of the face and mouth. It mostly affects 2- to 6-year-old children, especially in poor communities.

items.content:
Mediavest, the media agency of Brainchild Communications Pakistan, has been named the No. 1 Agency at the Dragons of Pakistan 2026, marking a significant achievement for the agency and its teams.
The recognition comes in a year that saw increased participation from agencies and clients, making the competition at the Dragons of Pakistan more extensive than in previous editions. Securing the top position against a stronger and broader field underscores the significance of Mediavest’s achievement.
The recognition reflects Mediavest’s continued focus on strategic thinking, effective media solutions and impactful work for its clients, further strengthening its position within Pakistan’s advertising and communications landscape.
Commenting on the achievement, Farhan Khan, CEO, Brainchild Communications Pakistan, said: “Winning awards is a significant achievement on its own. To win it three years in a row is not just a milestone-it’s a testament to our unwavering commitment to excellence and our refusal to settle for “good enough”. In our industry, consistency is the hardest thing to maintain. Trends shift, technology evolves, and consumer behaviors change rapidly. However, our team has proven that when you combine bold creativity with rigorous strategy, you create a standard of work that stands the test of time. These wins belong to every single member of our team who pours their passion into every project, and to our clients who trust us to push the boundaries.”
Three Consecutive Years of Leadership
Mediavest’s 2026 achievement extends Brainchild Communications Pakistan’s three year leadership at the Dragons of Pakistan, with a group agency securing the No. 1 position each year. Mediavest ranked No. 1 in 2024, Publicis Media Pakistan in 2025, and Mediavest again in 2026.
This three year run highlights the strength and consistency of the Brainchild Communications Pakistan group, with Mediavest, Publicis Media Pakistan and Starcom Worldwide Pakistan each contributing to the group’s continued presence among the country’s leading agencies.
The group’s regional track record is equally strong, with Brainchild Communications named Agency Network of the Year at the Dragons of Asia in both 2023 and 2024.
Mohibullah Seenharo, Associate Director, Brainchild Communications Pakistan, said: “Reaching the top spot at the Dragons of Pakistan is a defining moment for Brainchild Communications Pakistan. It is a reflection of our people, our clients’ trust and our commitment to creating work that makes an impact. This recognition inspires us to push boundaries and set an even higher benchmark for the industry.”

items.content:
The United States and Iran held a three-hour meeting on Tuesday as Tehran signalled a willingness to revive diplomacy and potentially reopen the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz, even as US President Donald Trump warned that he could "annihilate" the Islamic Republic if no agreement was reached.
Trump told reporters at the United Nations that US officials had held a "very good" three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation. He gave few details, saying the talks had ended about an hour before he spoke to reporters. "It was a meeting that lasted for three hours. It was a very good meeting," Trump said.
"I can't imagine why they wouldn't want to do it; it's greatness or obliteration," he remarked hours after his address to the UN General Assembly. Trump used the speech to issue a stark warning to Tehran, saying he faced a choice between reaching a deal and destroying Iran's ability to attacking against other countries.
"I have a big decision to make," the US president told the General Assembly, asking whether a deal could allow Iran to rebuild or whether he should "annihilate the Islamic Republic" and drive it "into hell with no chance of survival". The Iranian delegation did not attend the session when Trump spoke.
However, talking to the media persons after a meeting with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham in New York on the sidelines of UNGA session, Trump adopted a conciliatory tone, saying Washington and Tehran had been talking even on Tuesday.
He expressing his confidence that a settlement with Iran could eventually be reached. "They want to talk to us. They have been talking to us, even today they've been talking to us, and the relationship is developing," Trump said.
He reiterated that US would not allow Iran to obtain a nuclear weapon, saying the issue remained central to any possible agreement. He called for the economic isolation of Iran until it stopped attacks on commercial shipping, abandoned its nuclear ambitions and ended support for what he described as terrorism.
Earlier, Trump told the General Assembly that he believed a deal with Iran could be reached after the US midterm elections in November, saying Tehran was waiting to see how he performed in the vote before making a decision.
The Iranian side, meanwhile, signalled that diplomacy remained possible but insisted that Washington would need to change its approach. A senior Iranian official said that Tehran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if US military pressure was eased and the blockade on Iranian ports lifted.
The official described the UN General Assembly as a "golden opportunity" for Washington to return to diplomacy, saying the United States should formally declare that it wanted to resolve the dispute diplomatically and then agree on a timetable.
Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who led Iran's negotiating team in previous talks, struck a harder line, saying Tehran would never surrender and that Trump could not impose his power on the Iranian people and armed forces.
The contrasting positions came against the backdrop of an almost seven-month-old conflict that has disrupted regional security, commercial shipping and energy markets. The Strait of Hormuz, through which a major share of global oil and gas shipments normally passes, remains at the centre of the confrontation.
At the UN, Trump was also due to meet leaders of Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, all of which have a direct interest in restoring secure navigation through Hormuz while balancing their relations with Washington and Tehran.
The developing diplomatic activity came as Trump used much of his UN address to defend his administration's record and its handling of several international conflicts. He said the United States had restored its strength and portrayed his administration as an active force for ending wars.
In his address, Trump also singled out Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, calling him a "terrific man" while repeating his claim that his administration's diplomatic efforts helped end the May 2025 Pakistan-India conflict. He said world leaders had sent him letters thanking him for his mediation efforts.
"The Prime Minister of Pakistan, terrific man, said that Donald Trump was responsible for saving thirty million lives and probably many more than that," the president noted, as he credited his administration's diplomatic efforts to end multiple global conflicts and received letters of thanks from world leaders.
For now, the three-hour meeting between the US and Iranian officials has produced no announced agreement, but it marked the latest direct indication that diplomatic channels remain active despite the increasingly severe rhetoric surrounding the conflict.

The Nigerian Supreme Council for Islamic Affairs (NSCIA) has mobilised traditional rulers and political leaders for a special national prayer for Nigeria.
The event is scheduled to hold in Abuja on September 30.
Among those expected to participate in the gathering are Muslim governors, members of the National Assembly, ministers and other public officials.
Others are Emirs and representatives of Islamic organisations and State Councils for Islamic Affairs.
The prayer will take place at the Abuja National Mosque Complex from 4:30pm to 6:30pm under the leadership of the NSCIA President-General and Sultan of Sokoto, Alhaji Muhammad Sa’ad Abubakar.
The council said the gathering would be an opportunity for Muslims to collectively seek divine intervention for the country.
It listed peace, security, unity, good governance and national progress listed among the major areas of supplication.
The NSCIA Public Affairs Officer, Abbas Jimoh, announced the programme in a statement on Tuesday.
He urged invited participants and Muslims across the country to make arrangements to attend.
The national prayer will precede the council’s General Assembly, which is also scheduled to take place at the Abuja National Mosque Complex on October 1.
The October 1 meeting is expected to bring together a wider cross-section of Muslim leadership, including the Sultan; the Deputy President-General (North) and Shehu of Borno, Alhaji Abubakar ibn Umar Garbai El-Kanemi; Deputy President-General (South), Alhaji Rasaki Oladejo; Secretary-General, Prof Is-haq Oloyede; and Deputy Secretary-General, Prof Salisu Shehu.
The gathering will also include representatives of the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, as well as Muslim governors, lawmakers, ministers, heads of government agencies and Islamic organisations.
According to the council, the General Assembly will provide a platform for consultation and deliberation on matters affecting the NSCIA, the Muslim Ummah and the country.
The council has urged participants to attend both engagements.
It called on Muslims nationwide to use the occasion to pray for the country.

items.content:
‎President Bola Tinubu has tasked local government councils across Nigeria to prioritise food security, healthcare, education, infrastructure, job creation and support for local enterprises as part of efforts to make his administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda felt at the grassroots.
‎
‎Tinubu gave the charge in a speech delivered by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, George Akume, at the National Conference for Chairmen of the 774 Local Government Councils and Chairmen of Traditional Rulers’ Councils in Nigeria in Abuja on Tuesday.
‎
‎The conference, which began on Tuesday, will run until Thursday, with the theme, “Cascading President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda to the Grassroots.”
‎
‎The President said the success of government policies should be measured by their impact on communities rather than by announcements made in Abuja.
‎
‎“The true test of policy is not what is announced in Abuja, but what changes in our worlds, villages, towns and communities,” Tinubu said.
‎
‎He urged local government chairmen to ensure that Nigerians experienced improvements in primary healthcare, basic education, rural roads, access to safe water, food production, support for small businesses and opportunities for women and young people.
‎
‎“Local government autonomy is not an end in itself; rather, it is an instrument for service and development,” he said.
‎
‎Tinubu said the financial autonomy granted local governments by the Supreme Court had placed a greater responsibility on elected council officials to deliver effective and measurable governance.
‎
‎“The autonomy pronounced in the judgment of the Supreme Court of Nigeria places a huge responsibility on all chairmen, elected councillors and their management teams to deliver impactful governance at the grassroots level,” he said.
‎
‎According to him, council chairmen have the advantage of knowing the specific needs of their communities, including areas where clinics lack medicines, farmers require support and young people need opportunities.
‎
‎“Your knowledge of where a clinic lacks medicine, where farmers need support, where young people need opportunities and where tension is beginning to rise will help to deliver these dividends,” the President said.
‎
‎Tinubu urged councils to adopt evidence-based decision-making, technology and reliable statistics in planning and implementing development projects.
‎
‎He said local governments must become “centres of planning, delivery, early warning and measurable results” rather than remain passive recipients of Federal Government initiatives.
‎
‎The President said the Renewed Hope Agenda must become visible in communities through food security, healthcare, education, infrastructure, jobs and local enterprise.
‎
‎“The Renewed Hope Agenda must become visible at the grassroots, especially in food security, healthcare, education, infrastructure, jobs and local enterprise,” he said.
‎
‎He urged councils to actively participate in Federal Government initiatives as development partners and strengthen their capacity for coordination and innovation.
‎
‎“Local government authorities cannot afford to remain passive recipients of Federal Government initiatives without active participation as development partners,” Tinubu said.
‎
‎FG plans electronic tracking of council projects
‎
‎The Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs, Dr Onwosoro Maduka Ihemelandu, said the ministry was developing stronger mechanisms to monitor development projects and interventions at the local government level.
‎
‎Ihemelandu said the ministry had identified gaps in the availability of project information, geographical identification of projects, implementation monitoring, verification, coordination and access to reliable information for management decisions.
‎
‎“The Federal Ministry of Special Duties and Inter-Governmental Affairs intends to fill these gaps through collaboration with local governments,” he said.
‎
‎He said the ministry planned to strengthen its electronic tracking system to improve project visibility, monitoring and accountability across the 704 local government areas covered by its proposed framework.
‎
‎“The proposed E-Tracking methodology will be an extension of our current GIS-EMIS. We have software which we use to track projects and programmes across the federation. We want to improve it and add this E-Tracking component to enable us to monitor projects across the 704 local government areas collaboratively with local government chairmen and other stakeholders,” Ihemelandu said.
‎
‎According to him, the framework would capture project locations, distribution and sectors, implementing authorities and contractors, project values, implementation timelines, fiscal progress, field evidence, risks, challenges and required actions.
‎
‎He said the system would “improve the visibility of projects and interventions across the 704 local government areas,” strengthen evidence-based monitoring and verification, and provide timely information for management decisions.
‎
‎Ihemelandu also linked the conference to the Federal Government’s food security drive, saying a technical session would examine the application of modern technology to agriculture and food exports.
‎
‎“This is in line with the administration’s agenda of ensuring food security and self-sufficiency in food production,” he said.
‎
‎He said the programme was also connected to an action plan to cultivate 1.5 million hectares of land in communities nationwide.
‎
‎The Permanent Secretary added that participants would receive information on investment opportunities in rural communities, including a presentation on Canadian direct foreign investment.
‎
‎The Minister of Special Duties and Intergovernmental Affairs, Zaphaniah Bitrus Jisalo, said local governments and traditional rulers had critical roles to play in translating the Renewed Hope Agenda into tangible development at the grassroots.
‎
‎Jisalo said the conference was approved by President Tinubu and was designed to strengthen collaboration among the Federal, state and local governments, with traditional rulers serving as important partners.
‎
‎“The Council of Traditional Rulers is a significant platform for creating collaboration among the Federal, State and Local Governments,” he said.
‎
‎The minister said the local government, as the tier of government closest to the people, had a critical role in translating national policies and programmes into strategic goals.
‎
‎He said the gathering would provide an opportunity to develop practical strategies for improving service delivery, strengthening intergovernmental relations, enhancing accountability and ensuring that Federal Government interventions reached intended beneficiaries.
‎
‎“This gathering provides an opportunity to deliberate on practical strategies for improving service delivery under the Renewed Hope Agenda, strengthening intergovernmental relations, enhancing accountability and ensuring that Federal Government interventions effectively reach their intended beneficiaries,” Jisalo said.
‎
‎He described traditional rulers as critical stakeholders because of their influence and close connection with their communities.
‎
‎

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The National Assembly Secretariat has begun implementing austerity measures in the wake of a surge in petroleum prices, introducing a new duty system under which half of its officers and staff will work from offices while the other 50% will work from home on a rotational basis.
According to the NA Secretariat, the new arrangements are being implemented under the austerity notification issued on September 18. Employees working from home will remain available by telephone, email and WhatsApp and may be called to the office at one hour's notice whenever required.
Under the notification, 50% of employees working from home will not be entitled to a diet allowance or overtime. Employees will also be prohibited from leaving their station without prior permission.
As part of the austerity measures, fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50%, with the reduction to remain in effect for three months. A complete ban has also been imposed on the purchase of all types of new vehicles.
The NA Secretariat has also decided to reduce its non-ERE budget by 5% on a monthly basis during the 2026-27 financial year.
Meetings will preferably be held through video conferencing, although intra-city meetings will remain exempt from the restriction. Standing committee meetings have also been encouraged to be held virtually.
Under the austerity policy, the number of meetings is to be kept at the minimum possible level until the situation returns to normal.
To implement the September 18 notification, the National Assembly Secretariat has also assigned duties to a number of officers, including additional secretaries, joint secretaries and director generals.
Under the instructions, officers will be permitted to call one subordinate officer and one staff member from their respective wing. Additional staff may also be called in when required, subject to approval from the relevant authorities.
Requests to call more than 50% of the staff will be subject to valid reasons and recommendations from the concerned authorities.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The federal information minister on Tuesday ruled out the possibility of imposing governor's rule in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) province, whose ruling party, the PTI, plans to march on Islamabad on September 27 to seek the release of incarcerated party founder Imran Khan.
Addressing a press conference in K-P's provincial capital, Federal Information Minister Atta Tarar clarified that the federal government had no plans to remove the PTI government. "The province needs people's rule not the governor's rule," he said.
A day earlier, Federal Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, while responding to a question during a press conference in Lahore, stated that the government had already made it clear to the PTI that the prime minister, in consultation with our law ministry, would utilise whatever legal options were available.
The minister said the PTI talked about dialogue, but it was unclear with which responsible person in the party the federal government should engage. "The government has repeatedly offered talks. Political tensions can only be resolved through dialogue and constitutional and legal means," he added.
Tarar reiterated that the PTI would not be allowed to disrupt law and order in Islamabad, rejecting what he described as politics of violence and confrontation.
"We reject the politics of violence and confrontation," he said, adding that nobody would be allowed to block roads or affect citizens' rights in violation of Islamabad High Court (IHC) orders.
The minister said If the provincial government believed that people had voted for it to secure the release of an imprisoned individual, such an approach could take the province decades backward.
Tarar said the release of the person—former prime minister Imran Khan—for whom "illegal means" were allegedly being adopted could only take place in accordance with the law.
Criticising the K-P government, the federal minister said the same party had been in power in the province for a long time, but he did not see significant development work there. He said questions should also be raised about issues relating to deforestation and mining.
He said the people were paying taxes but were not receiving the facilities that fell within the provincial government's responsibilities. "The chief minister's job is to serve the province, improve governance and provide facilities to the people, not to incite them for protest activities," Tarar said.
He also questioned the absence of provincial government leaders from the funerals of security personnel and civilians martyred in terrorist incidents. "Public resources should not be spent on rallies, processions and protest activities by the PTI. Public resources should be spent on the public," he said.
Tarar said the K-P government had been provided a substantial amount under the National Finance Commission for the National Action Plan and should give a complete account of its utilisation.
Referring to the Kohat incident, Tarar said counterterrorism operations would continue and nobody would be allowed to disturb peace and order. He claimed that evidence had emerged that Afghan territory was being used in some terrorist incidents and said Pakistan had responded to it.

items.author: Rana Yasif
items.content:
The Lahore High Court (LHC) on Tuesday sought further arguments on the maintainability of a plea challenging the detention of PTI founder Imran Khan's sister Aleema Khan and her driver under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.
LHC Justice Abher Gul Khan heard the petition filed by Shahraiz Khan, Aleema's son, challenging her detention orders. The counsel for the petitioner informed the court that Aleema Khan was arrested first and her detention order was issued afterwards.
During the proceedings, the court asked the petitioner's counsel whether he had first approached the relevant authority against the detention order. The counsel replied that the case was quite different from others.
"It appears that the arrest was made first and the DIC meeting was held afterwards," he told the court. He submitted that the District Intelligence Committee (DIC) meeting and issuance of the detention notification took place on the same day.
Justice Khan observed that the court would examine the issue, adding that it was going to reserve its decision on the maintainability of the petition. On the counsel's request, however, the judge adjourned the hearing until Sept 25 for further arguments.
Aleema Khan was detained by the authorities on Sunday after the Lahore deputy commissioner's (DC) office ordered her detention for 30 days. Her two sisters, Dr Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, were also detained under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance.
The detention of the Khan sisters came amid a crackdown on Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) ahead of the party's planned march on Islamabad on September 27. Shahraiz Khan, Aleema's son, had filed the petition through advocate Rana Mudassar Umar, challenging the detention of his mother and aunts.

items.author: Kamran Yousaf
items.content:
France has expressed appreciation for Pakistan's diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions in the Gulf and is looking to deepen bilateral ties with Islamabad despite its longstanding strategic relationship with India, diplomatic sources said on Tuesday.
The assessment came as Pakistan and France held the eighth round of their Joint Security Commission in Islamabad, with the talks focusing on defence and security cooperation as well as regional developments.
French Secretary General for Defence and National Security (SGDSN) Nicolas Roche led the French delegation, while Pakistan's Defence Secretary Lt Gen (retd) Muhammad Ali headed the Pakistani side.
Diplomatic sources said France viewed Pakistan's efforts to promote diplomacy and dialogue in the Gulf positively, particularly at a time of heightened regional tensions.
They said Paris was also interested in developing closer relations with Islamabad, although France's strategic partnership with India remained an important element of its South Asia policy.
The sources pointed out that high-level exchanges between Pakistan and France had been relatively limited in recent years.
Roche's visit is particularly significant because the last French secretary general for defence and national security to visit Pakistan was in 2019.
The sixth round of the Joint Security Commission was held in Rawalpindi in July 2019. The mechanism has been meeting since 2011 to maintain high-level exchanges on security cooperation and counterterrorism.
A senior Pakistani foreign office official described Roche's visit as important, saying it reflected "steady progress" in bilateral ties.
"France is an important European and international player and has a permanent seat on the UN Security Council. We want to continue making strides in our relationship," the official told The Express Tribune on condition of anonymity.
The official, however, cautioned against expecting any major breakthrough from the current engagement.
"Nothing dramatic is expected, but the effort is to keep the relationship moving forward," the official said.
The two sides agreed to continue bilateral dialogue and engagement under the Pakistan-France Roadmap for Bilateral Cooperation adopted in 2023. They also agreed that the next round of the Joint Security Commission would be held in France on mutually agreed dates.
The discussions covered security and defence cooperation, regional security developments, counterterrorism, drug trafficking, piracy and other forms of transnational organised crime.
The official also highlighted the longstanding defence relationship between Pakistan and France, particularly in the naval domain.
France has historically played an important role in the development of Pakistan's submarine capability. Pakistan acquired Daphné-class submarines from France in the 1960s and later obtained Agosta submarines. In 1994, Islamabad signed a contract with the French company DCN for three Agosta 90B submarines, with technology transfer allowing two of the vessels to be built at Karachi Shipyard.
The French-origin Agosta 90B programme also involved technology transfer and training for Pakistani engineers, creating an industrial link between the two countries that continued beyond the original acquisition.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Tuesday urged the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) to press the Afghan Taliban to take concrete and verifiable steps to prevent their soil from being used for terrorist attacks against neighbouring countries.
Dar appealed while addressing a meeting of the OIC Contact Group on Afghanistan on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
Recalling the withdrawal of US troops from Afghanistan in August 2021, Dar described it as a “watershed moment” for the country.
Read More: Pakistan warns Afghanistan after Kohat attack, says it can eliminate terror threats ‘wherever they are’
“Pakistan was the first country to open its doors to our Afghan brethren at the time,” he said, adding that Islamabad had also hosted the 17th Extraordinary Session of the OIC-CFM on Dec 19, 2021, to garner the solidarity of Islamic countries and mobilise international support to address the humanitarian situation in Afghanistan.
“It was hoped that the Taliban would honour Afghanistan's international obligations and their own commitments by eliminating terrorism, promoting inclusivity and protecting the human rights of its citizens,” the foreign minister said.
However, he said, the expectations of OIC members and the wider international community had remained unfulfilled.
Dar said the Taliban had consequently “failed to seize the opportunity to integrate Afghanistan with the wider world and to improve the lives of the Afghan people” because of what he described as their “misplaced priorities and flawed ideologies”.
“As fellow OIC members, regional partners and neighbours, we can help Afghanistan integrate with the international community. But the Taliban must first take the steps necessary to create a conducive environment,” he said.
Dar said the foremost requirement was “concrete and verifiable actions” to prevent Afghan soil from being used for terrorism against neighbouring countries.
Read: Pakistan carries out 'calibrated' air strikes against terrorist hideouts near Afghan border after K-P attacks
He particularly referred to attacks against Pakistan that, he said, were planned and orchestrated from Afghanistan with external backing to destabilise the region.
“Pakistan is seriously concerned over the presence of more than two dozen terrorist groups inside Afghanistan, particularly the TTP, BLA and Majeed Brigade, ISIL-K (Daesh), Al-Qaida and ETIM that threaten regional and international peace and security,” he said.
He said Pakistan’s law enforcement agencies were making “enormous sacrifices” to counter terrorism as Pakistanis continued to be targeted and martyred by terrorist groups operating with impunity from Afghan soil.
Dar recalled the suicide bombing at a mosque in Kohat in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa the previous week, saying it had “martyred at least 24 Pakistanis”.
He also thanked Qatar, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia for their mediation and “sincere efforts” to counsel the Taliban and find amicable solutions.
Dar said the OIC, as “a collective voice of the Muslim world”, had a vital role in addressing the situation in Afghanistan and urged the group to call on the Taliban to take several steps, foremost among them eliminating terrorism and ending the patronage of terrorist groups.
“They must not allow Afghan soil to be used for orchestrating terrorist attacks against neighbouring countries,” he said.
He also called on the Taliban to honour their international obligations and commitments and curb trafficking through illegal smuggling networks, including narcotics, weapons and human trafficking.
Dar further urged the Taliban to lift restrictions on women and girls that were contrary to Islamic principles and norms of Muslim society and to reconsider policies that denied fundamental freedoms to ordinary Afghans.
He said Afghans had “already suffered enough from civil war and conflict”.
Dar referred to the ninth OIC Ministerial Conference on Women, held in Islamabad on July 12-13, 2026, which had expressed “deep concern” over continued restrictions on girls’ education and women’s employment in Afghanistan.
He also called for governance through a politically inclusive process involving all ethnicities and minorities.
Also Read: No change in Pakistan's Afghan policy
The foreign minister urged the Taliban to facilitate the resettlement and integration of Afghan returnees in their homeland, while saying the international community also had a responsibility to share the burden.
Dar said international donors must provide adequate funding to meet Afghanistan’s humanitarian aid requirements and support its socio-economic development.
In this regard, he commended the work being done by the OIC Office in Kabul, as well as humanitarian support provided through the Afghanistan Humanitarian Trust Fund and the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre.
“No country desires normalcy and stability in Afghanistan more than Pakistan, and no country has suffered from the consequences of instability and insecurity in Afghanistan more than Pakistan,” he said.
Dar reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to supporting efforts aimed at achieving a stable and prosperous Afghanistan at peace with itself and its neighbours, but stressed that this would require “mutual respect, sincerity and demonstration of necessary political will by the Taliban.”
Tensions between the two countries have escalated over the last year amid mutual accusations over cross-border militancy. Islamabad has long maintained that terrorists linked to the TTP operate from Afghan territory, while Kabul has denied the allegations and accused Pakistan of violating its sovereignty through alleged strikes.
Pakistan has maintained that meaningful engagement with the Taliban government cannot resume unless Kabul takes concrete and verifiable action against banned terrorist groups, particularly the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which Islamabad says operates from Afghan territory to plan and carry out attacks inside Pakistan.
The issue of terrorist sanctuaries remains the central source of friction between the two countries. Islamabad has repeatedly conveyed to Kabul that assurances alone are insufficient and that Pakistan wants to see demonstrable action against groups it considers responsible for attacks on its territory.
The Pakistani position also extends to other terrorist organisations operating from Afghan territory, including the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA).
The deterioration in bilateral ties, particularly over the TTP issue, has significantly narrowed the space for diplomatic initiatives.
Pakistan appears to be keeping diplomatic channels and limited institutional contacts open while refusing to resume substantive engagement with Kabul until it sees concrete and verifiable action against militant groups operating from Afghan soil.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The European Union ambassador has said that there is significant scope for expanding economic and commercial relations between Pakistan and the European Union through higher exports, greater investment, technology transfer and stronger business-to-business (B2B) cooperation.
EU Ambassador Raimundas Karoblis was talking to an All Pakistan Business Forum (APBF) delegation, where the two sides discussed bilateral trade and investment, joint ventures, GSP+ market access, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), technical and vocational education and training (TVET), and emerging regulatory requirements in the European market.
The meeting was attended by APBF President Syed Maaz Mahmood, Secretary-General Amir Munir Malik, Mian Faheem Qamar, Patron-in-Chief of Sundar Trade and Industry Association, Haroon Ali Khan, Chairman Pakistan Chemical Manufacturing Association, Shahzad Azam, Chairman PIEDMC, Brigadier (Retd) M Sajid Khokhar, Chairperson Tevta Punjab, Nasir Ali Zia, Director Masood Textile, Aziz Ullah Goheer, Secretary-General Pakistan Textile Exporters Association and other business leaders.
The ambassador said Pakistan had benefited considerably from the GSP+ scheme and stressed that the country could further benefit by fully implementing ILO conventions, diversifying its export base, increasing value addition and developing a skilled workforce.
According to the latest European Commission assessment, Pakistan's exports to the EU reached about €8.3 billion, with the EU accounting for around 28% of Pakistan's total exports. The EU remained Pakistan's largest export market, while textiles and clothing constituted roughly 75% of Pakistan's exports to the bloc. In 2025, bilateral trade in goods between the EU and Pakistan stood at €12.2 billion.
Karoblis emphasised closer interaction between Pakistani and European businesses to identify new areas of commercial cooperation. He also highlighted the importance of skills development and workforce preparation.
APBF appreciated EU support for technical and vocational education and training, saying a better-skilled workforce could serve both Pakistan's domestic economy and overseas labour markets. EU-supported TVET programmes have focused on demand-driven skills and employment opportunities, while an evaluation of the TVET-III programme recorded 118,946 competency-based training graduates and 19,530 workplace-based trainees.
Pakistan's overseas workforce is also an important source of foreign exchange. Workers' remittances reached a record $41.6 billion in FY2025-26, with remittances from EU countries contributing about $5.23 billion during the year.
APBF President Syed Maaz Mahmood said Pakistan's business community wanted stronger and more practical economic engagement with the EU, particularly through B2B contacts, investment and joint ventures.
He also called for greater support for SMEs to meet European certification, documentation and compliance requirements and make fuller use of GSP+ market access.
Maaz Mahmood said SMEs constituted a major part of Pakistan's economic base, but many smaller businesses faced difficulties in meeting the cost of international certifications and increasingly stringent European standards. Technical assistance and easier access to information, he said, could help Pakistani SMEs enter European supply chains and expand exports.
The APBF president also briefed the EU envoy on the forum's initiatives to develop business linkages between Pakistani enterprises and international markets, saying the organisation was ready to facilitate direct interaction between Pakistani and European businesses through B2B meetings, sector-specific linkages and joint ventures.
APBF Secretary-General Amir Munir Malik welcomed Ambassador Karoblis and his team while APBF members shared sector-specific views and highlighted the challenges faced by SMEs in meeting international standards, obtaining certifications and completing documentation for foreign markets.
During the interaction, the participants of the meeting said stronger technical cooperation with European institutions could help Pakistani companies improve production standards, meet environmental and social requirements and become more competitive in international supply chains.

items.title: AI a powerful engine for financial inclusion
items.summary:
Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority Chairman Bilal Bin Saqib has said that artificial intelligence and tokenisation can become the developing world's most powerful engines for financial inclusion, provided they are built for people left outside of the financial system.
He delivered a keynote address on financial inclusion, AI and tokenisation at a forum marking 50 years of microcredit at the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly.
Speaking at the Social Business, Youth and Technology Forum, Saqib, who is also the minister of state, spoke about the choice now facing emerging economies as the rules of global finance were rewritten.
The address placed Pakistan's own journey within a wider story. Worldwide, an estimated 1.3 billion adults remain without an account at any financial institution, while close to 900 million of them already own a mobile phone. The gap, he argued, was no longer one of technology but of rails and rules, and of the willingness to build them.

items.content:
The Universal Service Fund (USF) policy committee approved a Rs32.90 billion budget for fiscal year 2026-27 on Tuesday and advanced 15 4G projects that target 3.66 million people across 1,893 mauzas in 21 districts.
Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja chaired the meeting. USF Chief Executive Officer Mudassar Naveed and senior management presented the programme portfolio and budget priorities.
The committee allocated Rs24.89 billion for payments on ongoing work and set aside Rs6.56 billion for new initiatives. It also released Rs5.57 billion for the first quarter so teams could execute the approved programme without delay.
USF currently runs 28 projects – 17 Next Generation Broadband Service Delivery schemes and 11 Next Generation Optical Fibre Network Services schemes. The new allocation covers nine additional NG-BSD projects, four NG-OFNS projects and block funds for small lots that reach remote settlements.
Official project data shows that 15 contracted 4G schemes carry a combined subsidy of Rs14.008 billion and cover a target population of 3.66 million. The Kurram project leads progress with 75% completion. It covers 40 mauzas and 251,980 people with a Rs92.25 million subsidy.
Five projects stand at 50%, which include Pishin, Chiniot, Abbottabad, Badin and Kohat. Pishin spans Pishin, Killa Abdullah and Quetta, covers 306 mauzas and targets 574,545 people with a Rs1.32 billion subsidy – the largest population among the 15 schemes.
Chiniot covers 117 mauzas and 333,267 people. Abbottabad covers 61 mauzas and 157,473 people. Badin covers 144 mauzas and 432,666 people. Kohat, including the former Frontier Region Kohat, covers 24 mauzas and 41,404 people. Umar Kot and Khuzdar stand at 25%. Umar Kot covers 142 mauzas and 243,695 people with a Rs914.61 million subsidy. Khuzdar covers 144 mauzas and 75,637 people and holds the largest subsidy of about Rs2.945 billion.
Work continues on Small Lot P-15, Gujranwala, Muzaffargarh, Mansehra, Haripur, Rajanpur and Sujawal. Small Lot P-15 covers nine mauzas in Bahawalnagar, Faisalabad, Sheikhupura and Hafizabad and targets 15,700 people.
Gujranwala and Mandi Bahauddin cover 160 mauzas and 234,573 people. Muzaffargarh targets 498,927 people across 138 mauzas. Rajanpur covers 215 mauzas and 301,512 people. Sujawal covers 144 mauzas and 246,759 people.
These projects extend 4G coverage, open online services and create connectivity-enabled opportunities in underserved communities. The Ministry of IT and Telecom and USF pursue digital inclusion and close the digital divide through sustained, targeted investment. WITH ADDITIONAL INPUT FROM APP

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
A day after Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal sought a role for the Planning Commission in the International Monetary Fund (IMF) talks and described it as "fiscal numbers" focused, the Ministry of Finance on Tuesday turned down the assertion.
The "IMF programme is demonstrably not confined to numbers or fiscal targets", said the ministry in a detailed response. The finance ministry also sought to make a distinction between its role "for overall programme coordination" and agreement on benchmarks that were the responsibility of other divisions and provincial governments. The ministry's reaction came the day the IMF mission landed in Karachi for the fourth review of the $7 billion loan programme, which is expected to continue till October 7.
"Concerned ministries and institutions participate and lead technical discussions, including benchmark setting relating to their respective mandate," said the finance ministry. A day earlier, Ahsan Iqbal had said that he recommended to the prime minister that a representative of the Planning Commission should also be included in the team that would negotiate with the IMF. The planning minister said that the IMF programme was not just about numbers, but it would have implications for economic growth, development and people.
The statement added that the Finance Division "fully recognises that macroeconomic stabilisation is a means towards sustainable and inclusive economic growth". The finance ministry further said that certain assertions and interpretations regarding the Ministry of Finance, Pakistan's engagement with the IMF, and the government's economic stabilisation programme did not accurately reflect the facts or institutional process.
It said that this could create an incorrect impression among the public and market participants. "The IMF programme is a whole-of-government programme, not a Finance Division programme," it added. The characterisation that the Ministry of Finance has maintained tight control over programme design and negotiations did not accurately reflect the institutional arrangements underlying Pakistan's IMF programme, said the ministry.
It added that a clear distinction needed to be maintained between the Finance Division's responsibility for overall programme coordination, and the agreement on benchmarks with the IMF leading to policymaking, legislative and implementation responsibilities of respective federal ministries and provincial governments.
However, the finance ministry did not comment whether it was ready to accept a representative of the Planning Commission as part of the IMF parleys. But the ministry said that the appropriate policy debate was therefore not stabilisation versus growth but how to transition from stabilisation towards sustainable growth without any fiscal and external imbalances that necessitated reverting to the IMF stabilisation programmes, as witnessed in the past.
It added that the IMF's Extended Fund Facility and the Resilience and Sustainability Facility encompassed reforms and commitments falling within the mandates of multiple federal and provincial institutions, including the Finance Division, Planning Commission, Ministry of Planning, Ministry of Energy, provincial governments, FBR, SBP and other relevant stakeholders.
The ministry stressed that the published IMF programme explicitly encompassed growth-enhancing structural reforms, social protection, governance, energy-sector efficiency, climate resilience and reduction of distortions in the economy. The latest IMF staff report specifically states that policy discussions focused on accelerating reforms to support stronger growth, while protecting vulnerable households. While reacting to the talk of petroleum levy being the central point of the IMF programme, the finance ministry said that the levy was not the central point of the loan programme.
The assertion that the Finance Division has made PDL the "central point" of the IMF programme is misleading. The programme's fiscal strategy was substantially broader and revolved around FBR revenue mobilisation, expansion of the tax base, provincial taxation and expenditure rationalisation, it added. The finance ministry said that for the current fiscal year, the IMF programme specifically emphasised the need for additional revenue mobilisation and strengthening FBR performance rather than relying solely on petroleum taxation.
The petroleum levy is one of the revenue instruments, and describing it as the centrepiece of the programme materially overstates its role, according to the ministry. The finance ministry admitted that while the programme did not prescribe a single permanent headline PDL rate in the manner suggested, the published programme documents contained explicit details concerning petroleum pricing and levies. These include the alignment of domestic fuel prices with international prices through regular adjustments.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Pine Labs’ early backer Mastercard has exited the company by selling its entire 4.31% stake through a bulk deal on Tuesday. The investor offloaded 4.97 Cr shares at ₹187.75 apiece, fetching ₹933.6 Cr.
The deal was executed at a 5% discount to Pine Labs’ closing price today. Mutual funds and foreign institutional investors emerged as key buyers, with ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company picking up the largest chunk of 93.1 Lakh shares, according to BSE data.
Societe Generale bought 87.7 Lakh shares, while Citi Group acquired 66.7 Lakh shares. BNP Paribas, Goldman Sachs, Franklin Templeton, Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, Morgan Stanley and Susquehanna Pacific were among the other buyers.
This is Mastercard’s second major stake sale in Pine Labs since the company’s IPO in November 2025. The investor sold 59.2 Lakh shares in the IPO for ₹130.9 Cr, generating 1.7X returns on its initial investment. Mastercard first backed Pine Labs in 2020.
Several of Pine Labs’ early institutional backers have pared their holdings since its listing. Actis, Invesco and Madison India have also offloaded shares in the company.
The latest exit comes despite Pine Labs’ recent recovery on the bourses. The stock remains down more than 15% year-to-date but has gained over 25% in the past month, partly following the reintroduction of merchant discount rates (MDR) on UPI. Pine Labs shares closed Tuesday 2.07% higher at ₹197.55.
The recent rally has also been supported by positive brokerage commentary.
Motilal Oswal initiated coverage on Pine Labs on September 21 with a ‘Buy’ rating and a target price of ₹250, citing projected growth across its payments businesses.
The brokerage expects Pine Labs’ digital infrastructure and transaction platform to grow revenue at a 24.5% CAGR through FY28, while its issuing and acquiring platform is projected to grow revenue at 23% CAGR.
It expects overall revenue, adjusted EBITDA and PAT to grow at 24%, 46% and 129% CAGR, respectively, between FY26 and FY28, with adjusted EBITDA margins rising to 28.7% by FY28 from 9% in FY24.
In the first quarter of FY27, Pine Labs net profit skyrocketed 4X YoY to ₹4.8 Cr while its operating revenue zoomed 20% YoY to ₹736.9.

items.author: Ankush Das
items.content:
So far, AI in the inbox has so far meant assistance in drafting.
Microsoft has pushed Copilot deeper into Outlook, Google has embedded Gemini across Workspace, to provide AI assistants designed to organise inbox, draft replies in your specific tone, and capture meeting notes directly. Almost all of them still wait for the final go-ahead.
Sol, a proactive AI assistant, wants to flip that order. Founded in 2025 by three former Cred executives, Anish Karan, Prateek Srivastava and Ranjith Nair, the startup emerged from stealth today with $4 Mn (over ₹38 Cr) from General Catalyst, Nexus Venture Partners, DeVC, Peercheque and Kunal Shah.
The offering: if a user has already written “I’ll send the deck” or “I’ll set up time”, an AI automatically begins working without waiting for a prompt.
The product scans a user’s Gmail (Google Mail) for commitments and then produces the work those promises imply, from research and documents to slide decks, calendar coordination and reply drafts assembled from several threads. The user retains final approval.
Sol runs in its own computer environment, can browse the web and draws on a library of more than 100 specialist skills, running on OpenAI’s model under-the-hood. Some of the use cases include:
Creating or reviewing a document in Word or Notion, or building and reviewing slides
Finding and shortlisting time slots across internal and external calendars
Running research ahead of a reply or a decision
Drafting replies that pull context from scattered email threads
The idea surfaced during the cofounders stint at Cred. While Karan worked in the product of the fintech major, Nair was in the design and product team, and Srivastava was the engineering lead.
After identifying the problem, Karan spoke to around 55 enterprise teams from the US, South Korea and Australia to check whether the problem was local for companies in India. It was not.
“People whose work runs through email often have to repeat themselves: first in email, then again when they ask an AI tool to act,” Karan told Inc42. “We shouldn’t have to become experts in AI to benefit from it.”
Commercially, Sol is pre-revenue with no pricing tiers fixed yet. Karan says the pricing model will be usage or outcome-based with a fixed component to start, since the work varies in volume and complexity per user. Pricing will be in US dollars with no India currency pricing plan yet.
He declined to commit to a gross margin target, arguing that model costs are falling and adoption matters more, for now.
The go-to-market motion is “prosumer” first: anyone can sign up (waitlist at the moment), and an enterprise sales motion follows once enough people in one organisation use it.
Integrations begin with Google Workspace, covering Gmail, Docs and Slides, while Outlook is open to a small group of testers. The stack is model-agnostic, using OpenAI models today with routers that switch between them, and runs on AWS in the US.
Karan argues Sol has no direct competitor, only the workflow it replaces, and that reliability plus a simple interface are the moats a challenger must cross. That claim faces incumbents bundling agents into the inbox for free, and the trust problem every email agent inherits: an unapproved draft is harmless, but an approved one carries the user’s name.
Karan explains that the fresh capital is earmarked mainly for R&D, including talent, model costs and customer time. Sol plans to widen access beyond the waitlist soon.
Whether proactive assistants become the default layer of work email, or get absorbed into Gmail and Outlook as features, only time will tell.

items.content:
Anthropic on Tuesday launched Claude Opus 5.5, a new AI model that it ​says delivers performance comparable to its top-tier Fable 5.1 while ‌costing 40% less to run than its predecessor.
The release lands amid growing debate over AI risks. CEO Dario Amodei earlier this month called on ​the global AI community to slow down the pace ​of releasing new capabilities to address safety concerns.
Anthropic ⁠said Opus 5.5 underwent external testing by independent ​AI safety research groups Frontier Design and METR before launch ​and includes safeguards previously reserved for its most capable systems.
According to Anthropic, Opus 5.5 outscored rival OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol on a software ​development benchmark while costing roughly one-third as much ​to run.
Read More: Trump says US will henceforth call AI 'super intelligence'
Opus 5.5 is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million ‌output ⁠tokens, 20% below Opus 5, Anthropic said. The model is available on platforms including Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.
The model also scored better than previous systems in internal safety tests ​and was about ​85% less ⁠likely than Opus 5 or Mythos 5.1 to attempt to bypass containment boundaries in ​a dedicated evaluation, the company said.
Claude Sonnet ​5.5 ⁠and Claude Haiku 5.5 will be released in the coming weeks, the company said, bringing many of the same performance, ⁠speed and ​safety improvements.
Anthropic is also expanding ​programs that give vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences researchers broader access to the ​model.
