items.content:
Myanmar's Wai Khin Hnin on Sunday became the first Asian Games gold medallist in teqball, an acrobatic football-table tennis hybrid making its debut at this year's event in Japan.
Watched by Barcelona and Spain football legend Carles Puyol, Wai Khin Hnin beat Indonesia's Sumaya, who goes by one name, 2-1 in the final to capture the inaugural women's singles title.
Teqball was invented 14 years ago in a garage in Hungary and features players kicking a ball over a curved table, incorporating elements of the southeast Asian sport sepak takraw.
The sport has grown quickly and featured at the 2023 European Games.
Wai Khin Hnin lost the first set of the final but came back to win 10-12, 12-8, 12-9 and claim gold.
"I'm delighted, I'm thankful to my head coach for believing in me and selecting me to play in the women's singles. I believed that I could do it," she said.
"My next goal is to win the gold medal for Myanmar at the 2027 SEA Games."
The competition has seen a diverse range of players vying to become the Asian Games' first teqball medallists.
The Philippines men's team featured three 14-year-olds including Prince Agustin, who lost in the singles bronze-medal match.
Japan were represented by Takahiro Nodomi, who also works as a comedian.
"I played football until high school, gave up, started teqball in my late 30s, and made it to this big stage at 40," he said.
"If the message that 'even old guys can work hard' reached everyone, then I feel I was able to release some 'old guy power'."
Indonesia's Husni Uba represented his country in sepak takraw at four previous Asian Games.
"After I was done with the sepak takraw competition at the 2018 Asian Games I didn't expect to be back again, especially for teqball," said the 44-year-old.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The government has decided to accelerate efforts to improve the quality of IT education in Pakistan, identify unapproved educational institutions, and align the practical skills of IT graduates with international standards.
A high-level meeting on the IT Skills Assessment Test and the accreditation framework for computing education was held under the chairmanship of Federal Minister for Economic Affairs and Establishment, Senator Ahsan Iqbal. The meeting reviewed educational standards, accreditation procedures, and the skills of IT graduates in relation to industry requirements.
During the meeting, the federal minister directed the Ministry of IT to develop an effective system to identify unapproved institutions and academic programmes. The system aims to protect students from enrolling in unrecognized programmes.
Govt Moves to Improve IT Education Quality, Tighten Accreditation System
The meeting also stressed the need to provide students with reliable information about the accreditation status of universities, affiliated colleges and individual academic programmes. This would help students make informed decisions before enrolling in computing and IT programmes.
Officials informed the meeting that more than 33,000 students from 188 institutions participated in the IT Skills Assessment Test. Senator Ahsan Iqbal directed officials to align the assessment framework with international standards and the changing requirements of the technology industry.
The authorities were also asked to prepare a detailed report on the performance of participating institutions and the test results of their students. The report will help identify institutions where academic programmes require improvements.
The meeting also examined cases in which students complete all requirements for a degree but fail practical skills assessments. Officials were also asked to review cases where students pass the skills assessment without completing their degrees.
The government believes such cases require a detailed review of educational standards, examination systems and the relevance of academic curricula to industry requirements.
The federal minister also called for stronger cooperation between educational institutions and the IT industry. He directed officials to consult the Pakistan Software Houses Association and other industry stakeholders to bring skills assessments, professional certifications and academic programmes closer to market requirements.
See Also: Govt Will Unveil New Auto Policy Soon, Haroon Akhtar Khan Says
The meeting also considered a proposal to introduce mandatory skills assessment tests at different stages of academic programmes. However, officials were directed to assess the potential impact of such tests on students and educational institutions before taking a final decision.
The government also stressed the need for stronger coordination between the Higher Education Commission (HEC), National Computing Education Accreditation Council (NCEAC), Ministry of IT and other relevant federal and provincial institutions.
According to the government, the measures aim to improve the quality of IT education, protect students from unrecognized programmes, develop skills according to industry needs, and create better employment opportunities for Pakistani IT graduates.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
The Indian spacetech ecosystem is entering its most critical phase yet. After years of experimentation and ambition, spacetech startups must now prove they are on a path to commercial viability.
Investors are already betting on this transition. According to Inc42’s data, homegrown spacetech startups have already raised $252.9 Mn so far this year, nearly double what the sector raised in 2025.
Leading the momentum is Skyroot Aerospace. The startup became India’s first spacetech unicorn in May after it raised a $60 Mn round. Subsequently, it was successful in becoming the first Indian private company to place a rocket into orbit with its Vikram-1 mission. It is now lining up a bigger $200 Mn round.
Earlier this month, Temasek-backed hyperspectral imaging startup Pixxel’s $100 Mn Series C round made headlines as the single-largest funding round raised by a spacetech startup in India.
So, why are spacetech startups suddenly the flavour of the season? A key reason is the deepening policy push. The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) earlier this year began deploying capital from its ₹1,600 Cr Antariksh Venture Capital Fund. Similarly, the state-backed ₹1 Lakh Cr Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) fund also recently allocated nearly ₹834 Cr to spacetech startups in its inaugural cohort.
The buzz around the sector hasn’t just been about money coming in, but real achievements too.
GalaxEye recently became the first Indian startup to secure a US patent for its OptoSAR satellite imaging technology. Agnikul Cosmos also completed a test firing of its Agnite engine, which boasts India’s first semi-cryogenic engine and the largest 3D-printed single-piece rocket engine in the world.
Despite this, finding commercial viability is a looming concern for many spacetech startups. In addition, there are concerns around the frothy spacetech valuations. Under the current scheme of things, can Indian spacetech startups convert milestones into scalable and sustainable business models?
What Are VCs Betting On?
Earlier this year, Union minister of state (MoS) Jitendra Singh pegged the size of India’s space economy at around $9 Bn and projected that it would grow to nearly $45 Bn over the next decade. Behind this projected market size is an entire value chain:
First comes the infrastructure layer that enables launches, including ground stations, launch vehicles, and the components that act as inputs for the rockets
Then come payloads – the satellites and sensors that hitch a ride on the rocket and generate data from orbit
From there comes the ‘downstream’ data intelligence and applications layer, comprising analytics and services that process the raw data from the previous step.
It is this ‘downstream’ layer that Viju George, a partner at Mela Ventures, believes has the most promise. “Revenue models in satellites tend to be very lumpy and capex-driven, whereas data streams tend to be high-margin recurring revenue,” he observed.
The upstream input layer is relatively more commoditised, as per George. But that doesn’t mean it’s not investable.
“If you’re able to take the shovels approach, where you provide the components to satellites like avionics, communication infrastructure, and others, that is a kind of a multipurpose play. With that positioning, you’re not really dependent on a single satellite brand winning or losing,” he added.
Ashish Taneja of GrowX Ventures, an early investor in Pixxel, also believes that the nascent earth observation segment is a huge market opportunity. He added that the infrastructure layer is a “big thing too” as it continues to be a supply-constrained market.
But have the potential and the promise of spacetech taken investors too far?
The Gap Between Hype & Market Demand
The rapid influx of capital into the spacetech sector is creating concerns around valuations, market size and whether the demand required to justify these bets has materialised yet.
“I worry about the valuations because now somehow we are in the FOMO zone,” George said, adding that he is unsure whether the market is large enough to support current valuations. The risk, he said, is “whether you are paying a little bit more for market demand that is not yet evident.”
The valuation question is especially pronounced for capex-heavy businesses, where large cheques are being signed based on potential future launch cadence and scale, even as India’s launch capacity is still developing.
Space hardware also carries risks around technology, manufacturing, launch and satellite longevity. Satellites are expected to operate for around five to six years, but India does not yet have enough historical data to establish how reliably newer constellations will perform over that period.
Because of limited launch experience and deployments, investors are finding it tough to benchmark execution capability or predictable revenues. The growing number of startups is also raising the investment bar, with multiple ventures now attacking similar problems.
To achieve scale, spacetech startups will need to expand their base beyond government buying, which has, thus far, acted as an anchor customer. These emerging players will also need to tap into foreign sovereign buyers and commercial enterprises as well.
But demonstrating competitive cost, reliability, performance and consistency will be key to competing in international markets.
As such, GrowX’s Taneja remarks that “not many people will make the cut” in attracting sustained capital, predicting consolidation as startups expand beyond their initial products and become vertically integrated space infrastructure companies. Simply put, he believes that stronger players could eventually acquire or absorb smaller companies.
What Will It Take To Win Capital?
The first phase of Indian spacetech hinged on visions and ideas. But growing market maturity and an influx of new ventures have turned investor focus to identifying which businesses can turn technical breakthroughs into large, durable markets.
A startup may solve an extremely difficult engineering or deeptech problem, but that alone does not guarantee a scalable business.
“Early stage investors like to see milestones because we think they are the precursor to valuations and revenues. But once growth investors come in, they like to see tangible metrics,” said Mela Ventures’ George.
In 2018-19, investors were largely evaluating founder quality, technical capabilities, and whether building satellites and propulsion systems out of India was even possible. This is no longer the case.
“I want a precise use case. I want clarity on the use case. I want a differentiated solution which is defensible in the long run,” said Taneja.
Investors also want clarity on who will buy the product, how it will be used and what makes the offering difficult to replicate. Hence, established spacetech startups have more of an advantage now in attracting growth funding as they have a track record to show.
Signs of market maturity are also evident with global investors now participating in larger rounds, while domestic growth-stage funds are also beginning to enter Series B and beyond. But the funding pool remains smaller, particularly for capital-intensive spacetech businesses that require significant funding before reaching scale.
This could make the public markets increasingly relevant to the sector’s long-term funding cycle. Once companies have spent years building technology, establishing revenues and reaching sufficient scale, public listings could provide another route to capital and liquidity.
For early investors, meanwhile, the long development cycle itself can create multiple opportunities for valuation repricing as spacetech startups move from technical milestones to commercial deployment.
Taneja cited a 17X outcome over around five years, following the sale of a small portion of GrowX’s stake during Pixxel’s recent $100 Mn fundraise.
Regardless, the investment thesis has evolved substantially from when the first spacetech startups created the market a decade ago. The real challenge now is not reaching the stars, but turning that journey into a stellar business.

items.author: Life And Style Desk
items.content:
Maitreyi Ramakrishnan has spoken about the changing landscape of South Asian representation in Hollywood, saying that while the industry still has work to do, the growing presence of varied and authentic stories has helped move the conversation forward.
Speaking to Gulf News about her new Netflix film Best of the Best, Ramakrishnan reflected on how representation has evolved in recent years. “In recent years, representation has gotten strides farther than where we were before. It's personality first, and then the non-changeable factors of their cultural backgrounds is additional information,” she said.
For Ramakrishnan, progress does not necessarily mean dismissing the work that came before. “But I have to give the dues where it's deserved. We did have past representations that might not have necessarily been what we fully resonated with or saw ourselves in, but sometimes even just existence, though might not be reflective of your experience, still moves the needle,” she said.
She added that projects such as Best of the Best are part of a much longer journey, built on the efforts of performers and creators who pushed for South Asian characters and stories to have a place in Western entertainment.
“A project like ours stands on the backs of all those past projects that you know paid their dues and fought the good fight to get that side role, because it all builds together. That's the only way we're going to continue,” Ramakrishnan said.
That idea of moving beyond surface-level representation is also reflected in the film's dance sequences. Best of the Best centres on a university Bollywood-fusion dance team, allowing the filmmakers to incorporate multiple South Asian dance traditions rather than treating them as a single style.
Ramakrishnan was particularly emphatic about the care taken with the choreography. “All these dance styles come from very rich cultures and histories and our choreographers kept it real. We're not settling for just waving our hands in the air anymore. That's not happening,” she said.
Director Lena Khan has similarly spoken about the multicultural nature of the project.
In a previous interview with Variety, Khan noted that the world around the characters reflects the reality of a country where people from different cultural backgrounds live alongside one another. “At some point this country and the world is just full of people in different cultures,” she said.
According to Variety, the production's choreography drew from styles including Kuthu, Bharatanatyam and Pakistani-influenced dance, reflecting the different cultural backgrounds represented by the fictional university team.
The film, which began streaming globally on Netflix on September 18, follows childhood friends Maya, played by Ramakrishnan, and Anjali, portrayed by Priyanka Kedia, as they arrive at UCLA and join its competitive Bollywood-fusion dance team.
What initially appears to be an exciting new chapter quickly becomes a tougher journey as the pair set their sights on the US championship.
The ensemble includes Lilly Singh, Janina Gavankar, Ankur Rathee, Chaneil Kular, Nico Greetham, Nihar Duvvuri, Shreya Navile, Amryn Khurana, Tanishq Joshi, Saara Chaudry and Sasha Bhasin.
For Ramakrishnan, the project also represents another stage in a career that began with one of Netflix's most visible South Asian-led coming-of-age series.
Her breakout came with Never Have I Ever, which premiered during the Covid-19 pandemic and quickly became a global streaming success. Reflecting on the unusual circumstances surrounding her sudden rise to fame, Ramakrishnan told Gulf News that the timing initially made the experience feel somewhat unreal.
“Never Have I Ever season one came out in COVID and because everything was online, it kind of felt a little fake at first. It was right after Tiger King, Love is Blind, and Too Hot to Handle. So, everyone's bars were really low, and we slid right in there with a nice little comedy that's actually a story about grief,” she said.
Ramakrishnan was only 18 when Never Have I Ever arrived, thrusting her into an industry she was still learning to navigate. She credits creator Mindy Kaling with helping her adjust to the sudden attention and the demands that came with it.
“I got the biggest gift in having the best first boss in the world with my icon and one of the first true faces and pioneers of South Asian representation in the West, Mindy Kaling,” she added.
She recalled Kaling as someone who did not simply make the transition into fame easier, but remained direct with her while looking out for her as a young newcomer.
“She always kept it real and never went easy on me. She would always lead with her heart and truly saw me as a young kid who she realised she plucked out of nowhere and doesn't know this world. She really took such good care of me,” Ramakrishnan said.
With a characteristic touch of humour, she added: “So, I didn't crash out, I'm not shaving my head yet. We're still here. So, I guess we're all right.”
Now, with Best of the Best, Ramakrishnan is stepping into another story rooted in South Asian culture while playing a character navigating friendship, ambition, identity and the pressures of competition.
For an actor whose career began amid a major shift in how South Asian teenagers were portrayed on screen, the film offers another opportunity to expand what that representation can look like — this time through friendship, collegiate life and the energetic world of competitive dance.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Artists in Gaza ‌have painted a mural of Macklemore wrapped in a Palestinian flag on a huge slab of concrete in the ruins of Gaza City, after the US rapper was kicked off Ed Sheeran's upcoming tour for calling for a "Free Palestine".
The mural, on a slab that leans against ruined buildings surrounded by rubble, depicts the "Thrift Shop" rapper raising a ​fist in the air. "Thank you for using your voice for Palestine," it reads.
"We wanted to send a message to thank rapper Macklemore ​in this simple way," said Anne Redwan, 26, who designed and painted the mural with fellow artist Qusai ⁠al-Helo.
"As an artist living under siege here in Gaza, we are waiting for support from anyone who can see (the) persecution we live under," she ​told Reuters. "We can paint murals bigger than this to express our feelings."
Macklemore, who has long supported Palestinian causes, was cut from British pop star Sheeran's ​musical lineup over remarks on stage criticizing Israel's military assault in Gaza, which was launched after Hamas-led fighters attacked Israel in October 2023.
Sheeran said he was unable to keep Macklemore on the tour after stadium owners refused to let him appear. US billionaire Robert Kraft, owner of Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts where his New England Patriots ​football team plays, said he had barred Macklemore from appearing there for antisemitism, which the rapper denies.
Nearly a year after a ceasefire ended major ​fighting in Gaza, reconstruction has yet to begin. Most buildings have been destroyed and more than two million residents are confined to around a third of the ‌enclave's territory, ⁠mostly in tents or crowded rooms in damaged buildings among the ruins.
A US-brokered plan to end the war has stalled, with negotiators failing to agree conditions for Hamas to disarm and Israel to withdraw its troops.
The furore over Sheeran's tour has led to a series of pledges from those involved to send money. Macklemore said on Wednesday he would donate his $1 million in net earnings from the tour to six aid groups supporting Gaza.
Kraft, in turn, ​said Sheeran had told him he ​would donate $2 million for aid ⁠in the region, and had asked him to match the pledge. Sheeran has not commented on any donations. Macklemore's donation drew a matching $1 million pledge from Ms Rachel, a popular children's TV personality.
Aid agency officials said the ​boost in celebrity attention could help bring more support to Gaza, where nearly all residents rely on ​aid for food, water, ⁠medical care and shelter.
"But what's really most important is that people who have been so generous keep funding over a sustained time," said Toby Fricker, a local official with UNICEF. "That's why we really call for sustained support, not one-off peaks, but sustained."
Hussein Murtaja, who runs a Gaza humanitarian group that provides mental ⁠health support ​to children, said Macklemore's solidarity matters more than the money he donated.
"When artists of this ​stature, with this many followers or fans, all come to know more about the cause, and support reaching a political solution, support achieving peace for the people of Gaza... That ​means a great deal to us."

items.title: Mengintip Desain vivo X500, Tampilan Berubah Total Mirip iPhone?

Tampilan Desain vivo X500 Dibuat Lebih Kekinian
View this post on Instagram
Tim Gizmologi berkesempatan untuk melihat langsung desain vivo X500 sesaat jelang peluncuran resminya besok (21/9). Dari segi tampilan, memang jauh berbeda dibandingkan generasi sebelumnya. Terlihat dari dimensi yang memang sedikit membesar, serta perombakan pada tampilan bodi belakangnya. Meski tetap membawa sebuah lingkaran besar sebagai rumah dari ketiga sensor kameranya.
Alih-alih hadir dengan sebuah modul lingkaran besar yang diletakkan di tengah atas bodi belakangnya, tampilan desain vivo X500 diubah, di mana lingkaran tersebut disematkan ke dalam sebuah “rumah” modul kamera baru berbentuk persegi panjang, yang mendominasi bagian atas perangkat. Tidak dapat dipungkiri, desain seperti ini membuatnya terlihat seperti iPhone 18 Pro, di mana Apple menyebutnya “camera plateau”.
Dan mirip seperti iPhone terbaru, setup lampu kilatnya juga diletakkan berjauhan dari rumah ketiga sensor kamera vivo X500. Yang masih bisa dibilang menjadi pembeda, selain bentuk lingkaran yang sudah disebutkan tadi, adalah adanya dua logo ZEISS; satu tercetak dengan warna biru ikonik, dan satu lagi dalam bentuk cetak teks bertuliskan “vivo | ZEISS co-engineered”. Seolah menambah kesan bila smartphone ini memang ingin hadirkan kemampuan kamera lebih serius.
Selebihnya, bodi belakang hanya didominasi oleh logo vivo di sisi bawah, sementara permukaan bodinya bertekstur matte. Sehingga meski tampil dalam warna hitam, tidak begitu mudah menempel bekas sidik jari, dan tidak terasa licin dalam genggaman.
Membesar, Namun Tetap Lebih Kompak Dibandingkan Flagship Kebanyakan
Menariknya, tak seperti generasi sebelumnya yang sempat mengecil, vivo kembali menghadirkan desain vivo X500 dalam dimensi lebih besar. Namun begitu, tak sepenuhnya “kembali” ke ukuran vivo X200. Diperkirakan membawa dimensi layar kisaran 6,5 – 6 inci, alias masih sedikit lebih kompak dibandingkan flagship kebanyakan yang berukuran layar 6,8 – 6,9 inci.
Selain dari segi desain vivo X500, masih belum banyak yang dibocorkan terkait spesifikasi. Namun dipastikan bila smartphone vivo kelas flagship terbaru satu ini siap membawa sejumlah inovasi hingga peningkatan pada kemampuan kameranya. Tidak lain juga berkat penggunaan cip MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Series terbaru.

items.author: Gargi Sarkar
items.content:
A customer scans a QR code at a neighbourhood shop, enters a passcode and the payment is done. Similarly, a wholesaler pays a supplier, friends split a dinner bill, and consumers buy groceries, all without handling cash.
Over the past decade, the QR code has quietly become one of the most visible symbols of Digital India. But India’s digital payments revolution is now entering a new phase.
From October 15, select high-value UPI payments will no longer be entirely free for merchants. Under the new framework, a 0.4% merchant discount rate (MDR) will apply to specified person-to-merchant UPI transactions above ₹2,000. The charge has been capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 and above. The new framework has been introduced at a time when UPI has reached enormous scale. For context: UPI processed 24.51 Bn transactions worth ₹29.82 Lakh Cr in August alone.
This has created some uneasiness in the market, even as the government says around 96% of P2M UPI transactions will remain unaffected. According to the merchants Inc42 spoke with on the condition of ano nymity, the 0.4% MDR charge may not sound like much, but repeated across hundreds of transactions, it can take a visible bite out of margins.
And that’s where UPI’s next chapter gets complicated.
After years of encouraging businesses and consumers to embrace digital payments, the ecosystem is now being asked to pay up for the infrastructure. Consequently, FMCG distributors and retailers have raised concerns about the impact on their margins, while petrol pump dealers in several states have threatened to stop accepting UPI payments above ₹2,000 unless they are exempted.
Fuel stations in Mumbai have sought a waiver, while dealers in Maharashtra are deliberating whether to accept UPI at pumps. Similarly, traders in Ghaziabad have already put up notices saying “UPI Payment Will Not Be Accepted” for transactions affected by the new MDR framework.
The merchant backlash is only one side of the UPI story, where scale, rather than monetisation, has been the protagonist for a decade. Now, with visible pushback from merchants, could UPI’s monetisation push once again change how Indians choose to pay?
Payments Were Never Truly Free
Debit cards already carry an MDR for merchants, with RBI’s framework allowing charges of up to 0.9% for certain merchants with annual turnover above ₹20 lakh, while the ceiling for QR-code-based card acceptance is 0.8%. Credit cards typically carry higher merchant charges, given the interchange and other fees involved in the card ecosystem. Even cash comes with a cost. Once customers exhaust their free ATM withdrawal limit, banks charge around ₹23 per transaction.
But UPI made that cost almost invisible.
For consumers, scanning a QR code has felt like the closest thing to a free payment system. There is no fee staring back at you at the point of purchase, no cash to count and no need to think about the machinery sitting behind the transaction.
That simplicity has been central to UPI’s rapid adoption. The network has operated under a zero-MDR regime for a long time, with banks and other ecosystem participants supported through incentives and other mechanisms. And now it is time to monetise the endeavour, with some believing 0.4% MDR is just the beginning.
“This is not going to end at just 40 basis points,” said a Mumbai-based fintech founder, arguing that other participants in the payments ecosystem could eventually seek a larger share.
According to him, the costs around processing, fraud prevention, technology and compliance are likely to grow as UPI moves into higher-value commerce and increasingly complex financial use cases. “This could solidify the case for more participants seeking revenue from the network.”
Who Wins In The MDR Tug-Of-War?
The return of MDR creates a direct, transaction-linked revenue pool around UPI, but the question is: who gets paid?
The biggest beneficiaries may not be the payment apps consumers see on their phones, but the banks and infrastructure providers that sit underneath each transaction.
Citi estimates that the new framework could create an annual revenue pool of around ₹16,000-₹17,000 Cr. Of this, roughly 60% could accrue to banks and UPI handles, 25% to UPI app providers, and the remaining 15% to non-bank payment aggregators.
Goldman Sachs has a somewhat different estimate. It expects 50% of the pool to go to issuing banks and PSPs, 20% to third-party application providers and 30% to acquiring banks. Across brokerages, the overall opportunity is estimated at ₹15,000-₹20,600 Cr annually.
Within banking, the gains could be particularly meaningful for lenders that process a large share of UPI transactions or have merchants doing higher-value business. Citi estimates that Yes Bank could see a 6-12% increase in gross profit from the new MDR, while Bank of Baroda, Punjab National Bank and IndusInd Bank could see around a 2% PBT benefit each. Axis Bank, SBI and Federal Bank could see a 1-2% benefit.
Then the second layer of beneficiaries is the payment apps.
Even a minority share of the MDR pool could create a significant new revenue stream at their existing scale, particularly if they capture a larger share of higher-value merchant transactions.
Payment aggregators and other fintech infrastructure providers form another layer of beneficiaries. They could capture part of the MDR pool for providing merchant acceptance, payment processing and related infrastructure. But their share is expected to be smaller than banks and UPI application providers.
Citi’s estimate puts non-bank payment aggregators at around 15% of the overall pool.
Back To Cards Or Cash?
There is another side to the equation. The new MDR regime could make the economics of card networks, such as Visa and Mastercard, relatively more attractive, particularly for higher-value transactions where merchants may reconsider their payment options.
That makes enforcement of the no-pass-through rule even more important, as any increase in the effective cost of accepting UPI could prompt merchants to explore alternative payment rails.
“It’s very difficult to keep saying, ‘Make sure that they do not pass on the charge.’ But how do you enforce that? How can you stop an ecommerce platform from passing on the charge? To check that at a granular level may be a nightmare and could end up being more expensive for the industry just to comply,” said Sharat Chandra, founder of EmpowerEdge Venture.
He also pointed to the difficulty regulators have faced in monitoring practices such as dark patterns on commerce and consumer platforms. In his view, tracking whether MDR is being passed on could present a similar challenge.
But the bigger risk to UPI will be when merchants decide to use another payment method.
“More merchants will get creative and try to see how they can circumvent these channels. Cash will bounce back into the equation,” Chandra said.
He took an example of monthly groceries and daily essentials that can easily cross the ₹4,000-₹5,000 mark. “Until now, UPI had them covered. But now, it is going to pinch price-sensitive people.”
Meanwhile, a LocalCircles survey found that 53% of surveyed UPI users said they would move away from UPI for payments above ₹3,000 if merchants passed the MDR on to them. Among these respondents, 27% said they would shift to credit cards, 14% to debit cards and 12% to cash or bank transfers.
There could also be workarounds. Take a ₹5,000 purchase. In theory, it could be split into multiple smaller UPI transactions to stay below the threshold. Whether this becomes common will depend on how banks, payment aggregators and NPCI monitor transactions and enforce the new framework.
Cash does not carry an MDR at the point of acceptance. It does have handling, reconciliation, security and cash management costs. These leave UPI with a tricky balancing act, and the last thing UPI needs is to make people reach for their wallets again.
[Edited by Shishir Parsher]

Beberapa karya terpilih kemudian mendapat apresiasi langsung dari BABYMONSTER lewat aktivitas membuat OPPO Bubble Charm.

Reno16 Series juga dibekali kamera selfie 50MP Ultra-Wide yang dirancang untuk membantu pengguna mengambil foto bersama dengan bidang pandang lebih luas.
Pengalaman Planet Reno juga sudah dimulai sebelum sesi fan meet up. Di area venue, pengunjung dapat menemukan Planet Wonder, Fans Wall, Reno Café, dan BABYMONSTER Corner untuk mencoba perangkat, membuat kreasi, hingga meninggalkan pesan bagi BABYMONSTER.

OPPO Reno16 Pro 5G dengan RAM 12GB dan penyimpanan 256GB dibanderol Rp 14.999.000. Sementara OPPO Reno16 5G tersedia dalam dua konfigurasi, yakni 12GB/256GB seharga Rp 12.999.000 dan 8GB/256GB seharga Rp 11.999.000.
Adapun OPPO Reno16 F 5G dijual seharga Rp 8.699.000 untuk varian 8GB/256GB dan Rp 7.999.000 untuk 8GB/128GB.

OPPO akhirnya mengumumkan jadwal peluncuran Find X10 Series di China. Lini smartphone flagship terbaru ini akan diperkenalkan pada 22 September 2026, dengan tiga model yang terdiri dari Find X10, Find X10 Pro Max, dan Find X10 E. Peluncurannya berlangsung hanya sehari setelah vivo memperkenalkan X500 Series di pasar yang sama.
Selain tanggal peluncuran, OPPO mulai membuka informasi mengenai desain, pilihan warna, serta konfigurasi RAM dan penyimpanan ketiga perangkat melalui toko online resminya di China. Perusahaan sebelumnya juga sudah mengungkap sejumlah fitur utama yang akan dibawa lini Find X10.
Dari ketiga model tersebut, Find X10 Pro Max menjadi varian dengan desain kamera paling mencolok. Smartphone ini membawa modul kamera berbentuk persegi yang menampung tiga sensor 200MP. Sementara LED flash dan sensor lainnya ditempatkan pada modul berbentuk pil yang berada di sisi kanan kamera utama.

items.title: iPhone 18 Pro Max dan iPhone Duo Lolos Postel Komdigi, Ini Bocoran Harganya

Dari data yang tim Gizmologi dapat, Minggu (20/9/2026), sertifikat untuk ketiga perangkat itu terbit pada 17 September. Ketiganya terdaftar atas nama PT Apple Indonesia.
Baca Juga: GIGABYTE Resmi Bawa Empat Lini Laptop Gaming 2026 ke Indonesia
Ada tiga model yang tercatat, mulai dari A3717 untuk iPhone 18 Pro, A3714 merupakan iPhone 18 Pro Max, dan A3720 untuk iPhone Duo. Sesuai dengan sertifikat TKDN Kemenperin, ketiga iPhone baru tersebut didaftarkan oleh PT Apple Indonesia dengan nilai TKDN 40 persen.
Dengan demikian, Apple telah melewati dua tahap penting untuk mempersiapkan iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, dan iPhone Duo untuk masuk pasar Indonesia. Meski begitu, Apple belum mengungkap secara resmi tanggal penjualan maupun harga ketiga ponsel tersebut di Indonesia.
Bocoran Jadwal Penjualan iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone 18 Pro Max
items.author: Yus Lianson

Trio iPhone baru Apple, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max dan iPhone Duo diketahui sudah mengantongi sertifikat Postel dari Kementerian dan Digital (Komdigi).

Ada tiga model yang tercatat, mulai dari A3717 untuk iPhone 18 Pro, A3714 merupakan iPhone 18 Pro Max, dan A3720 untuk iPhone Duo. Sesuai dengan sertifikat TKDN Kemenperin, ketiga iPhone baru tersebut didaftarkan oleh PT Apple Indonesia dengan nilai TKDN 40 persen.
Dengan demikian, Apple telah melewati dua tahap penting untuk mempersiapkan iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, dan iPhone Duo untuk masuk pasar Indonesia. Meski begitu, Apple belum mengungkap secara resmi tanggal penjualan maupun harga ketiga ponsel tersebut di Indonesia.
Bocoran Jadwal Penjualan iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone 18 Pro Max di Indonesia
Sebelumnya, Apple enthusiast Bagus Hernawan mengungkap perkiraan waktu penjualan iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone 18 Pro Max di Indonesia pada 16 Oktober 2026.
iPhone 18 Pro Max
Kedua model tersebut disebut akan hadir bersama sejumlah perangkat Apple lain, yakni Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4, dan AirPods 5. Informasi tersebut masih berupa bocoran dan belum dikonfirmasi Apple.
Sementara itu, jadwal iPhone Duo disebut belum pasti. Bocoran yang beredar mengarah pada 30 Oktober atau 2 November 2026 sebagai perkiraan waktu penjualan di Indonesia.
Bocoran Harga iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone Duo
Bagus Hernawan juga membagikan perkiraan harga awal ketiga perangkat Apple tersebut di Indonesia. Nominal yang beredar adalah:
iPhone 18 Pro: mulai Rp27.999.000
iPhone 18 Pro Max: mulai Rp29.999.000
iPhone Duo: mulai Rp44.999.000
Perlu dicatat, angka tersebut belum merupakan harga resmi Apple Indonesia. Harga final, konfigurasi penyimpanan, serta ketersediaan setiap model masih menunggu pengumuman resmi Apple.
Dengan terbitnya sertifikat Postel, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, dan iPhone Duo kini semakin siap untuk masuk pasar Indonesia. Namun, kepastian tanggal penjualan dan harga resmi masih berada di tangan Apple.
Spesifikasi Utama iPhone 18 Pro Series
iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone 18 Pro Max sama-sama menggunakan chip A20 Pro. Keduanya juga membawa kamera utama Fusion 48MP dengan aperture variabel, Dynamic Island berukuran lebih kecil, serta modem C2 rancangan Apple.
Apple menawarkan kedua model dalam warna hitam, perak, Glacier Blue, dan Burgundy. Kapasitas penyimpanan dimulai dari 256GB dan tersedia hingga 2TB.
Melalui situs resminya, Apple sudah memastikan iPhone 18 Pro dan iPhone 18 Pro Max akan segera hadir di Indonesia. Hanya saja, perusahaan masih belum mengungkap jadwal pemesanan awal, tanggal penjualan perdana, maupun daftar harga lokal.
Dengan sertifikat TKDN yang kini sudah terbit, perhatian berikutnya tertuju pada sertifikasi perangkat telekomunikasi serta pengumuman dari Apple dan mitra distributor resmi. Ketika dua tahap tersebut terpenuhi, jadwal peluncuran trio iPhone terbaru di Indonesia seharusnya semakin jelas.
iPhone Duo Bakal Jadi Lini Sendiri dari Apple
John Ternus, CEO Apple dengan iPhone Duo (Sumber: BBC)
Apple ternyata punya alasan tersendiri memilih nama iPhone Duo untuk perangkat foldable pertamanya. Sebelumnya, smartphone ini lebih sering disebut sebagai iPhone Ultra dalam berbagai rumor. Namun, menurut laporan Bloomberg, nama Duo dipilih bukan sekadar untuk membedakan perangkat tersebut dari lini iPhone lain, melainkan karena Apple disebut punya rencana memperluas keluarga foldable di masa depan.
Nama Duo dinilai lebih mudah dikembangkan menjadi beberapa varian. Laporan yang disampaikan Mark Gurman menyebut Apple sedang mempertimbangkan model seperti iPhone Duo Max dengan ukuran lebih besar, iPhone Duo mini yang lebih kecil, hingga iPhone Duo SE sebagai model yang lebih terjangkau. Strategi ini membuat nama Duo lebih fleksibel dibandingkan Ultra.
Selain itu, kata “Duo” juga cukup jelas menggambarkan karakter utama perangkat, yakni dua layar dalam satu bodi. Penamaan tersebut juga membuatnya konsisten dengan nama seperti Air dan Pro yang sama-sama singkat. Meski demikian, belum diketahui apakah Apple mempertimbangkan fakta bahwa Microsoft sebelumnya sudah menggunakan nama Surface Duo untuk perangkat dual-screen miliknya.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
When Vineet Chirania was scaling his train-ticket booking startup, Trainman, a decade ago, he encountered a problem that would eventually inspire his next venture. His team relied on Datadog, an application monitoring tool, to track the performance of its software systems. Then one day, the startup received an unexpectedly high bill after one of its developers started feeding additional custom metrics into Datadog.
Over at BharatPe, senior engineering executive Vijay Aggarwal was facing a similar challenge with another observability giant, New Relic.
Both Aggarwal and Chirania quickly realised the problem. As apps grow and generate more telemetry data, monitoring costs become increasingly difficult to forecast. Add concerns around data residency and dashboard latency, and the pain points become hard to ignore.
These experiences eventually led the duo to build CubeAPM, an observability platform that claims to reduce enterprise monitoring costs by as much as 60-80%, while keeping customer data within their own cloud environments.
Today, the bootstrapped startup serves around 50 enterprise customers, including Delhivery, RedBus, PolicyBazaar, Shadowfax and the Ola Group. Simultaneously, CubeAPM claims to be churning an annual recurring revenue (ARR) of nearly $1.5 Mn, up roughly 3-4X over the past year, all while remaining profitable since inception.
But CubeAPM’s ambitions extend beyond being an affordable alternative to incumbents. The startup is betting that its architecture, designed around self-hosting, data residency and AI-assisted troubleshooting, can help it carve a place in the global observability market, which is estimated to become a $20 Bn opportunity by 2031.
From Trainman To CubeAPM
The origins of CubeAPM are deeply rooted in the founders’ operational experiences. Chirania spent much of his career building Trainman, which eventually scaled to more than 30 Mn app downloads before being acquired by the Adani Group.
Aggarwal, meanwhile, built his reputation leading engineering teams at high-scale internet startups. Before founding CubeAPM, he served as the CTO of BharatPe and earlier headed engineering at Grofers (now Blinkit).
Both hail from IIT Roorkee. After Chirania exited Trainman, the two reconnected and discovered that they had experienced the same frustrations with observability software.
“The common thread was application performance monitoring. We had used different tools, but the problems were remarkably similar: unpredictable pricing, poor visibility into future costs, and challenges around data residency,” said Chirania.
Initially, the founders believed modest cost savings would be sufficient to convince enterprises to switch platforms. But most observability purchases are displacement sales. Customers already have a monitoring platform in place, and migrating critical infrastructure monitoring systems requires massive engineering effort. Saving 15% or 20% wasn’t compelling enough.
“We realised customers were willing to migrate only if the economics were dramatically better, sending us back to the drawing board,” Chirania said.
Reinventing The Observability Architecture
At its core, observability software helps engineering teams understand what is happening inside their apps. When a website slows down or a payment service crashes, observability platforms collect telemetry data, such as logs and metrics, to help teams identify the root cause and resolve issues quickly.
However, scaling observability is a key challenge as enterprises generate massive volumes of telemetry data, making real-time storage, indexing and analysis increasingly expensive and resource-intensive. Moreover, traditional observability vendors such as Datadog and New Relic typically operate SaaS-based models, where customer data is sent to the vendor’s cloud for processing and storage.
CubeAPM takes a different route to reduce costs. Rather than moving customer data outside their environments, the startup installs its platform inside the customer’s own cloud infrastructure. The approach allows data to remain within the customer’s cloud environment and satisfies compliance requirements more easily than foreign SaaS platforms.
According to the founders, this architecture addresses three key enterprise concerns simultaneously: cost, data residency and latency.
The architecture also reduces data transfer costs that enterprises often incur when moving large volumes of information to external vendors. More importantly, the startup claims it can deliver significantly faster dashboard performance because the data remains geographically closer to customer workloads.
This model, however, created a new challenge: how to manage and support a system running inside a customer’s environment.
To solve this, CubeAPM developed a framework that sends only minimal operational metadata to its own systems, allowing its engineers to monitor deployments remotely and provide support without accessing sensitive customer data.
Tech Behind Cost Advantage
Cost reduction is the centrepiece of CubeAPM’s value proposition. The startup argues that traditional observability platforms often charge customers across multiple dimensions, including hosts, users, indexed data, custom metrics and support plans.
As infrastructure scales, those variables compound and make bills difficult to predict.
To solve this, CubeAPM prices its products primarily on data ingestion volume, bundling unlimited users, hosts, retention and support into a single pricing model. While this simplicity resonates with enterprises that struggle to forecast monitoring expenses, the real differentiator comes from its underlying infrastructure efficiency.
According to Chirania, the startup has developed proprietary compression and storage technologies that dramatically reduce the amount of infrastructure required to store telemetry data. He claims CubeAPM can compress 100 GB of incoming data into roughly 4 GB of stored data, reducing storage, compute and memory requirements.
This efficiency becomes important because customers host the platform within their cloud environments.
The startup also emphasises compatibility with existing observability ecosystems. Rather than forcing customers to replace their existing stacks, CubeAPM works with popular telemetry agents and standards, including OpenTelemetry, Datadog, New Relic and Elastic.
This interoperability allows migrations to happen relatively quickly, reducing one of the biggest barriers to adoption. “We wanted switching to feel like hours rather than weeks,” Chirania said.
Building A Full-Stack AI Observability Platform
What began as an application performance monitoring tool has gradually expanded into a broader observability suite. CubeAPM now offers six major modules:
Application Performance Monitoring (APM)
Log Management
Infrastructure Monitoring
Real User Monitoring (RUM)
Synthetic Monitoring
Error Tracking
The startup’s typical users are engineering, DevOps and site reliability engineering (SRE) teams. Most begin usage with APM before expanding into additional modules.
This “land-and-expand” motion has become a major growth driver for CubeAPM. According to Chirania, roughly half the company’s customers currently use multiple products within the CubeAPM suite.
Now, as AI reshapes software development, CubeAPM sees observability becoming even more critical as AI-generated code may eventually create systems that developers understand less intuitively than the software they write themselves.
As a result, identifying root causes could become more difficult, increasing reliance on observability platforms. To prepare for that shift, CubeAPM has begun integrating AI capabilities directly into its workflow.
One of its recent launches is an MCP server that allows AI coding assistants, including Cursor, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex and Gemini, to access telemetry data directly from CubeAPM. This allows engineers to skip dashboards altogether, query logs through AI agents and troubleshoot issues through conversational root-cause analysis.
The startup is also using AI internally. Over the next 12-24 months, AI-powered troubleshooting is expected to become one of CubeAPM’s primary product priorities.
Chasing The Enterprise Stack
Unlike many enterprise software startups chasing growth through venture capital, CubeAPM has remained entirely bootstrapped. The startup says that its GTM strategy has largely relied on founder networks, particularly within India’s tech ecosystem, where both founders have spent years building relationships. This approach has helped the startup, which operates with a team of 25 employees, acquire customers without large marketing budgets.
Moreover, CubeAPM claims to report renewal rates above 95%, which management attributes to its support model. Rather than relying exclusively on ticketing systems, it creates direct communication channels with clients through Slack, WhatsApp, Microsoft Teams or Google Chat, allowing engineers to respond quickly during incidents.
For now, the company remains focused on enterprise and mid-market customers. Ironically, despite being founded by startup veterans, CubeAPM has intentionally avoided targeting startups due to purely economic reasons.
Migration efforts make the most sense for organisations already spending substantial amounts on observability software. For smaller startups, the savings generated by switching platforms may not justify the integration effort.
This could change in the future, with CubeAPM now exploring a dedicated startup offering.
CubeAPM says its platform now powers more than 1 Bn requests a month across its customer base of 50 clients. It currently claims an ARR of nearly $1.5 Mn while remaining profitable.
The Road Ahead
CubeAPM’s biggest challenge may not be technology but market penetration. The observability category is dominated by well-capitalised global incumbents that have spent decades building products, ecosystems and distribution channels. Convincing enterprises to replace mission-critical infrastructure monitoring tools may not be easy.
The startup’s answer is to focus relentlessly on the areas where it believes incumbents remain vulnerable: predictable pricing, data residency, support quality and infrastructure efficiency.
International expansion is also emerging as a priority. While most customers are currently based in India, CubeAPM sees significant opportunities in the US, Europe, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, particularly among enterprises with stringent compliance requirements.
Despite investor interest in infrastructure software and AI, the founders say they are in no rush to raise capital.
Their goal remains straightforward: build a globally trusted observability platform that helps enterprises monitor complex software systems at a fraction of the cost of traditional vendors.

items.title: Ini Rahasia Apple Tingkatkan Performa iPhone 18 Pro, Mulai Cip A20 Pro Hingga Sistem Pendingin yang Didesain Ulang
items.summary:
Apple secara resmi memulai penjualan iPhone 18 Pro Series, flagship terbaru yang beberapa waktu lalu diluncurkan bersamaan dengan smartphone lipat perdananya, iPhone Duo. Walaupun iPhone Duo memiliki daya tarik tersendiri lewat desain baru, varian Pro tetap memikat dengan keunggulan yang dibawa. Termasuk aspek performa iPhone 18 Pro yang meningkat signifikan, lebih pas untuk kreator maupun penggunaan lebih intensif.
Ya, secara tampilan, iPhone 18 Pro Series memang masih terlihat identik seperti generasi sebelumnya—wajar saja, mengingat Apple baru saja merombak ulang desain iPhone 17 Pro, di mana kini sepenuhnya menggunakan material aluminium unibodi. Sebagai pembeda, hadir empat opsi warna baru yang juga dibedakan dengan permukaan kaca belakangnya, kini dibuat tidak begitu kontras dengan material aluminium pada bodi.
Selain kamera yang ditingkatkan mulai dari kemampuan pengambilan video sampai variable aperture, peningkatan performa iPhone 18 Pro juga menjadi salah satu sorotan utama.
items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
items.content:
Apple secara resmi memulai penjualan iPhone 18 Pro Series, flagship terbaru yang beberapa waktu lalu diluncurkan bersamaan dengan smartphone lipat perdananya, iPhone Duo. Walaupun iPhone Duo memiliki daya tarik tersendiri lewat desain baru, varian Pro tetap memikat dengan keunggulan yang dibawa. Termasuk aspek performa iPhone 18 Pro yang meningkat signifikan, lebih pas untuk kreator maupun penggunaan lebih intensif.
Ya, secara tampilan, iPhone 18 Pro Series memang masih terlihat identik seperti generasi sebelumnya—wajar saja, mengingat Apple baru saja merombak ulang desain iPhone 17 Pro, di mana kini sepenuhnya menggunakan material aluminium unibodi. Sebagai pembeda, hadir empat opsi warna baru yang juga dibedakan dengan permukaan kaca belakangnya, kini dibuat tidak begitu kontras dengan material aluminium pada bodi.
Selain kamera yang ditingkatkan mulai dari kemampuan pengambilan video sampai variable aperture, peningkatan performa iPhone 18 Pro juga menjadi salah satu sorotan utama. Tidak hanya membuatnya mampu jalankan game terberat, namun juga berpengaruh terhadap kemampuan AI, sampai memberikan efisiensi daya yang juga lebih maksimal.
Baca juga: iPadOS 27 Bikin iPad Jadul Lebih Kencang, Kompatibel Untuk Tablet Rilisan 2020
Cip A20 Pro Bawa Neural Engine Jauh Lebih Superior
Menjadi inti dari performa iPhone 18 Pro, adalah cip 2 nanometer terbaru dan pertama dari Apple untuk lini smartphonenya, yakni A20 Pro. Dibandingkan seri A19 Pro, cip satu ini membawa bandwidth memori 50% lebih tinggi, membawa arsitektur CPU, GPU, hingga Neural Engine yang baru. Plus, sistem pendingin yang juga berperan besar dalam memberikan performa terbaik.
Apple sebutkan bila cip A20 Pro mampu mengantarkan performa iPhone 18 Pro signifikan lebih tinggi, yakni hingga 20% pada CPU dan hingga 40% pada GPU. Kini setiap inti pada keenam inti CPU didukung oleh neural accelerator terintegrasi, yang juga diklaim lebih cepat dibandingkan cip lainnya. Dan bagian penting lainnya yang ikut ditingkatkan, adalah Neural Engine yang kini digandakan, memberikan total hingga 32 inti.
Neural Engine yang memiliki performa dua kali lebih kencang ini dinilai penting, karena mampu mempercepat pemrosesan AI dan machine learning secara langsung di perangkat, alias berjalan secara lokal atau on-device. Apple sebutkan bila ini merupakan salah satu keandalan performa iPhone 18 Pro, di mana tak semua pemrosesan AI memerlukan server Private Cloud Compute, alias dapat diproses secara langsung di dalam perangkat.
Disebutkan juga bila Apple memiliki alasan tersendiri untuk mengusung dua Neural Engine 16 inti, alih-alih memperbesar satu Neural Engine. Di mana selain lebih efisien daya, juga lebih sesuai dengan keperluan pemrosesan AI saat ini, termasuk algoritma kamera baru yang juga memungkinkan hadirnya sejumlah fitur baru saat menangkap gambar maupun merekam video.
Sistem Pendingin Baru Juga Kontribusi Besar Performa iPhone 18 Pro
Selain dari sisi chipset, pelengkap lainnya seperti sistem termal juga penting dalam memberikan performa iPhone 18 Pro lebih maksimal. Kali ini, Apple merancang sistem pendingin berbasis ruang uap alias vapor chamber berukuran hingga tiga kali lebih luas dibandingkan pada iPhone 17 Pro. Hal tersebut juga dimungkinkan berkat integrasi vapor chamber secara langsung ke bagian sasis tengah perangkat, sehingga lebih efektif mendinginkan kinerja chipset.
Selain itu, terinspirasi dari bagaimana mereka merancang cip khusus lini laptopnya, Apple juga menempatkan blok silikon di sebelah memori, menjauhkan memori dari jalur termal cip yang kemudian memungkinkan cip menempel langsung ke vapor chamber. Dipadukan dengan material baru, performa iPhone 18 Pro bisa tetap maksimal 40% lebih lama dibandingkan generasi iPhone sebelumnya.
Artinya, Gizmo friends bisa melakukan tugas berat lebih lancar tanpa ada risiko throttling terlalu cepat, seperti main game dengan visual kompleks lebih lama, atau skenario lain seperti penggunaan kamera di luar ruangan yang terkadang membuat smartphone cepat panas dan layar mudah meredup. Dan berkat efisiensi cip baru, Apple juga bisa menghadirkan daya tahan baterai paling lama dalam sejarah iPhone, hingga 43 jam pemutaran video pada iPhone 18 Pro Max.
Artikel berjudul Ini Rahasia Apple Tingkatkan Performa iPhone 18 Pro, Mulai Cip A20 Pro Hingga Sistem Pendingin yang Didesain Ulang yang ditulis oleh Prasetyo Herfianto pertama kali tampil di Gizmologi.id

items.summary: Temporary files can build up on a Windows 11 PC and gradually take up valuable storage space. You can clear them using Windows' Settings app, the Disk Cleanup tool or the Temp folder. This guide explains where to find temporary files, how to remove them safely and when it makes sense to clear them.

items.title: GIGABYTE Resmi Bawa Empat Lini Laptop Gaming 2026 ke Indonesia, Harga Mulai Rp23 Jutaan
items.summary:
GIGABYTE resmi membawa jajaran laptop gaming terbarunya ke pasar Indonesia melalui peluncuran yang digelar di Jakarta pada 18 September 2026. Ada empat lini yang diperkenalkan, yakni AORUS MASTER 16 Gen 2 sebagai model flagship, GIGABYTE AERO X16 untuk pengguna yang membutuhkan perangkat tipis, GIGABYTE GAMING A16 sebagai laptop gaming serbaguna, serta GIGABYTE EAGLE di kelas entry-level.
Seluruh lini tersebut menggunakan kombinasi prosesor AMD Ryzen dan GPU NVIDIA GeForce RTX. GIGABYTE juga membekali perangkatnya dengan GiMATE, asisten AI yang diproses langsung di laptop. Pendekatan on-device ini ditujukan untuk mengurangi ketergantungan terhadap layanan berbasis cloud, meski manfaatnya tetap bergantung pada kemampuan AI dan fitur yang tersedia pada masing-masing perangkat.
Dari sisi harga, pilihan yang tersedia cukup lebar. AORUS MASTER 16 Gen 2 dengan Ryzen 9 9955HX3D dan RTX 5080 dibanderol Rp72,89 juta, sedangkan GIGABYTE EAGLE dengan Ryzen 5 7533HS dan RTX 4050 berada di Rp23,38
items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
GIGABYTE resmi membawa jajaran laptop gaming terbarunya ke pasar Indonesia melalui peluncuran yang digelar di Jakarta pada 18 September 2026. Ada empat lini yang diperkenalkan, yakni AORUS MASTER 16 Gen 2 sebagai model flagship, GIGABYTE AERO X16 untuk pengguna yang membutuhkan perangkat tipis, GIGABYTE GAMING A16 sebagai laptop gaming serbaguna, serta GIGABYTE EAGLE di kelas entry-level.
Seluruh lini tersebut menggunakan kombinasi prosesor AMD Ryzen dan GPU NVIDIA GeForce RTX. GIGABYTE juga membekali perangkatnya dengan GiMATE, asisten AI yang diproses langsung di laptop. Pendekatan on-device ini ditujukan untuk mengurangi ketergantungan terhadap layanan berbasis cloud, meski manfaatnya tetap bergantung pada kemampuan AI dan fitur yang tersedia pada masing-masing perangkat.
Dari sisi harga, pilihan yang tersedia cukup lebar. AORUS MASTER 16 Gen 2 dengan Ryzen 9 9955HX3D dan RTX 5080 dibanderol Rp72,89 juta, sedangkan GIGABYTE EAGLE dengan Ryzen 5 7533HS dan RTX 4050 berada di Rp23,38 juta. Di antara keduanya terdapat AERO X16 dan GAMING A16 dengan beberapa konfigurasi berbeda.
Baca Juga: COMPUTEX 2026: GIGABYTE Perkenalkan AORUS INFINITY, Keyboard & Mouse Gaming dengan Layar OLED
Empat Kelas Laptop untuk Kebutuhan Berbeda
AORUS MASTER 16 Gen 2 menjadi model dengan spesifikasi tertinggi, menggunakan Ryzen 9 9955HX3D dan RTX 5080 Laptop GPU. Laptop ini memiliki layar OLED 16 inci beresolusi 2.5K dengan refresh rate 240Hz, sementara sistem pendinginnya dirancang untuk mendukung system power hingga 230W. Di sisi lain, AERO X16 membawa pendekatan berbeda dengan bodi setebal 16,75 mm dan bobot 1,9 kg, menggunakan Ryzen AI 7 350 dan pilihan RTX 5070 atau RTX 5060.
GAMING A16 menempati kelas menengah dengan Ryzen 7 260 dan pilihan hingga RTX 5060, sementara EAGLE menjadi model paling terjangkau dengan Ryzen 5 7533HS dan RTX 4050. Keduanya menggunakan layar 16 inci 16:10 dengan refresh rate hingga 165Hz. Dengan rentang spesifikasi tersebut, perbedaan utama antarproduk bukan hanya terletak pada GPU, tetapi juga mobilitas, kapasitas performa, dan kebutuhan pengguna yang dituju.
GiMATE Jadi Fitur AI Utama
GiMATE menjadi salah satu fitur yang coba dibawa GIGABYTE ke seluruh lini barunya. Sistem ini menggabungkan kontrol hardware dan software, pemantauan sistem secara real-time, serta perintah suara melalui mekanisme Press and Speak. Beberapa fungsi yang ditawarkan mencakup pengaturan performa, pendinginan, daya, hingga audio.
GIGABYTE juga menyediakan GiMATE Creator untuk kebutuhan generasi gambar AI dan GiMATE Coder untuk membantu menghasilkan, memperbaiki, serta mengoptimalkan kode menggunakan bahasa alami. Selain itu, seluruh laptop yang diluncurkan mendapatkan garansi pabrik dua tahun, termasuk Accidental Damage Protection dan global warranty service dengan ketentuan tertentu.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Polytron merayakan 51 tahun perjalanannya di Indonesia melalui Polytron Fest 51st Anniversary yang digelar di Parkir Selatan Gelora Bung Karno (GBK), Jakarta, pada 19–20 September 2026. Perayaan tersebut sekaligus menjadi ajang peluncuran kampanye “Bangga Terus Melangkah”, kolaborasi bersama MALIQ & D’Essentials, serta pengenalan produk pendingin udara terbaru.
Memasuki usia lebih dari lima dekade, kini memiliki portofolio yang mencakup berbagai kategori elektronik, mulai dari televisi, perangkat audio, peralatan rumah tangga, hingga kendaraan listrik dan laptop. Perusahaan yang berdiri di Kudus pada 1975 ini juga menyebut perayaan tersebut sebagai bentuk apresiasi terhadap masyarakat yang telah menjadi bagian dari perjalanan bisnisnya di Indonesia.
Di sisi lain, mereka tidak hanya membawa agenda perayaan. Kampanye “Bangga Terus Melangkah” turut dilengkapi program sosial bersama Kitabisa.com melalui gerakan “5.100 Langkah Baik”. Program ini mengajak masyarakat membagikan cerita mengenai langkah baik mereka melalui media sosial, yang kemudian dikonversikan menjadi donasi untuk kebutuhan pendidikan dan bantuan alat usaha bagi pelaku UMKM.
Baca Juga: Ini Strategi Polytron Memperkuat Posisi di Industri Elektronik Nasional
Gandeng MALIQ & D’Essentials hingga Program Sosial
Dalam kampanye tersebut, mereka juga menggandeng MALIQ & D’Essentials melalui sebuah proyek video musik yang akan dirilis kemudian. Kolaborasi ini dibangun berdasarkan kesamaan perjalanan kedua pihak yang telah bertahan dan berkembang selama bertahun-tahun.
Program “5.100 Langkah Baik” menjadi bagian lain dari kampanye dengan pendekatan yang lebih langsung kepada masyarakat. Setiap satu share dari konten kampanye Polytron dikonversikan menjadi donasi Rp51.000. Dana tersebut disebut akan disalurkan untuk beasiswa pendidikan serta bantuan alat usaha bagi UMKM yang membutuhkan.
Hadirkan AC dengan Perintah Suara Tanpa Internet
Bersamaan dengan perayaan tersebut, Polytron memperkenalkan AC Neuva Pro dengan fitur Voice Sense. Fitur ini memungkinkan pengguna memberikan sejumlah perintah suara langsung ke unit AC tanpa membutuhkan koneksi internet.
Polytron menyebut teknologi tersebut memproses perintah secara offline sehingga respons tidak bergantung pada jaringan. Pengguna dapat memberikan instruksi seperti “Hai Polytron”, “Nyalakan AC”, atau “Suhu Nyaman”. Meski demikian, efektivitas fitur dalam penggunaan sehari-hari tetap akan bergantung pada kemampuan sistem mengenali suara dan kondisi lingkungan. Polytron sendiri menempatkan Voice Sense sebagai salah satu upaya menghadirkan kontrol perangkat yang lebih praktis.

items.title: ELECTIONS: Nigeria is still pursuing shadows, by Tonnie Iredia
items.summary:
In less than 4 months from now, Nigeria will hold its 2027 general elections; yet, not many would believe the assurances by the electoral body that the process will be free and fair.  No one can blame the doubting Thomases because the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC is notorious for not keeping its word. Just before the last general elections in 2023, INEC told the nation that it would premise its operations on modern technology: indicating specifically that there would be both manual and electronic collation of votes etc.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Raphinha scored a superb hat-trick to earn Barcelona a 3-1 win at Sevilla on Saturday in La Liga and preserve their 100 percent record.
Hansi Flick’s side moved six points clear of Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, who visit Atletico Madrid in a derby clash on Sunday.
The Spanish champions were given the biggest test of their season to date but overcame Sevilla at the Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan thanks to Raphinha’s treble.
The Brazil international has started the season in sensational form, playing out of position as a central striker.
La Liga’s top goalscorer, Raphinha reached 12 goals in seven league appearances with a second consecutive hat-trick.
Barcelona sporting director Deco said the former Leeds winger had agreed to extend his stay at the club until 2030 ahead of the game, and Raphinha celebrated in style.
Flick handed Croatian goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic his debut in goal with Joan Garcia out injured.
Hosts Sevilla, fifth, started strongly, making Barca uncomfortable, and took the lead through Youssouf Fofana in the 19th minute.
Felix Correia escaped Eric Garcia and crossed for Fofana to nod home at the near post.
Teenage star Lamine Yamal almost pulled Barca level but Sevilla goalkeeper Odysseas Vlachodimos managed to push his curling effort against the post and out.
It was no surprise when the Catalans did equalise that it was Raphinha who was the man to score.
He cleverly shifted his body weight to escape a defender and slipped the ball home with a low finish.
Yamal sent another shot over and after Sevilla fans whistled him, goaded them to keep doing so.
Although the 19-year-old did not score himself, he did create Raphinha’s next two goals.
Early in the second half Yamal crossed and Raphinha headed home to put Barca in front.
Arguably his best finish was yet to come, with Yamal sending Raphinha through, for the Brazilian to dink the ball over the goalkeeper.
Barca missed several chances to extend their lead, with Anthony Gordon getting his feet wrong and a Dani Olmo free-kick beaten away.
Nevertheless Barca claimed an eighth win from eight games across all competitions this season, as they continue setting the pace in the Spanish top flight.
Elsewhere Celta Vigo thrashed Racing Santander 5-0, Athletic Bilbao and Alaves drew 0-0 and Osasuna were held 1-1 by Rayo Vallecano.
AFP

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
A resurfaced video of Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote’s three daughters has triggered reactions online after Halima Dangote revealed that she and her sisters did not grow up “spoilt” despite their privileged background.
The video, which resurfaced on X on Saturday, was taken from Bloomberg’s Next Africa special featuring Halima, Mariya and Fatima Dangote.
The interview, filmed at the Dangote family’s Lagos residence, was published by Bloomberg in August 2026.
Halima, Fatima and Mariya occupy senior positions within the Dangote Group as the conglomerate continues to develop its succession structure.
Speaking about how she and her sisters handled their privileged upbringing, Halima said they had intentionally maintained a low profile and preferred to have their professional achievements define them.
“We are not spoilt,” she said.
Elaborating, Halima said the sisters avoided drawing attention to their family background when interacting with people from similar circles.
“Any time we meet with our co-peers — like the kids of our dad’s friends, or people that we’re supposed to — we don’t… I mean, everyone has his own job. We are more… we’re quiet in the sense that we don’t say who we are.
“It’s, I don’t know if it’s fortunate or unfortunate, now people recognise us. But it was easier when we were not recognised; you know, our results speak for themselves.”
She said the three sisters also differed from people who were comfortable displaying their lifestyles and possessions on social media.
“I mean, some people are really comfortable with social media, with being known, with being expressive. I don’t think we are — all three of us are not expressive of what we have or what we own or what we’re doing,” she said.
Halima said she and her sisters preferred their performance at work to serve as the measure of their success.
“I think, like Fatima and Mariya said, the results are just the ones speaking for themselves: the sale of this business, the profit of this, the EBITDA, our growth, growing to $100 billion. We are all in those key positions and, I mean, numbers don’t lie,” she added.
Dangote has previously said having a male heir was not a priority for him, arguing that his three daughters were capable of taking over the family business.
“Sometimes when God doesn’t give you something, don’t push. I don’t think a son would have done something better than these three daughters that I have. That one, I think, you know, it’s not my priority,” he said.

Obasanjo made the remarks during an interview with media personality Bae U, published on Saturday, while recalling his initial impression of Charlie Boy and how it changed after he witnessed the entertainer’s dedication to caring for his parents.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has spoken about his changing perception of entertainer Charles Oputa, popularly known as Charlie Boy, saying he once wished the entertainer had taken after his late father, Justice Chukwudifu Oputa.
Obasanjo made the remarks during an interview with media personality Bae U, published on Saturday, while recalling his initial impression of Charlie Boy and how it changed after he witnessed the entertainer’s dedication to caring for his parents.
Asked why he often referred to Charlie Boy as “Jaga Jaga”, Obasanjo initially described the entertainer as someone he knew little about.
“Well, Charlie Boy is so jaga jaga that I don’t know anything about him,” Obasanjo said.
The former President then contrasted his view of Charlie Boy with his high regard for his late father, Justice Oputa, whom he described as one of the Nigerians he respected during his lifetime.
“He has a good father, Justice Oputa. Oh, what a great man. I wish Charlie Boy had resembled him,” he said.
Obasanjo, however, said his perception began to change after he visited Justice Oputa and discovered that Charlie Boy was responsible for his care.
“When I first came to know Charlie Boy, I had no iota of regard or respect for him.
“But when I went to visit Justice and it was in Charlie Boy’s house. I didn’t know it was in Charlie Boy’s house.
“So the first thing that put me off in that house, I saw a motorcycle in front of the house. The way the motorcycle was dressed and all that, I said, ‘What is this?’
“And then I went inside the house. I saw how Justice was being taken care of and by who? Charlie Boy.
“Ah, so I started changing my mind about Charlie Boy and until Justice Oputa died, Charlie Boy took perfect care of him, looked after him and he really behaved like a good child would give to his father.”
The former President said Charlie Boy’s care for his mother further changed his opinion of the entertainer.
“He didn’t stop there. He did the same to his mother. And I used to frequently visit the mother, who was a great humorous woman.
“Charlie Boy took care of her. Then I started changing my mind. I changed my mind about him,” he said.
Obasanjo also recalled asking Charlie Boy about his unconventional appearance and public persona, saying the entertainer explained that it was part of how he made a living.
According to the former President, the explanation contributed further to his changing perception of Charlie Boy, whom he described as intelligent.
“Then one day I asked him, I said, ‘Look, Charlie Boy, what is all this?’
“You said that Jaga Jaga, all those Jaga Jaga things that I see, is to make chop-chop and he’s an intelligent boy, that Charlie Boy, all Jaga Jaga, because you cannot do Jaga Jaga to earn a living without being intelligent,” he said.
Obasanjo said he eventually developed some fondness for the entertainer, although he admitted that it was limited.
“So now I like him a bit, not too much,” he said.

items.content:
By Henry Umoru, ABUJA
STRONG indications have emerged that crisis looms in the family of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, as the national leadership of the party has disowned the 59-member Presidential Campaign Council comprising zonal and state coordinators put in place by the OK Movement.
The OK Movement, a political platform established to mobilise support for the joint ticket of the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Dr Rabiu Kwankwaso.
In a statement on Saturday, the National Chairman of NDC, Senator Cleopas Moses said that the PCC announced by the movement did not emanate from the party and should be disregarded by the public and the media.
The statement is titled “Re: Purported OK Movement PCC Announcement”.
According to the National Chairman, all candidates of the party must appreciate that they are not running as independent candidates against the backdrop that they are products of the party and remain subject to the authority and discipline of the party, just as he warned that only the party’s leadership can constitute and announce a Presidential Campaign Council PCC.
He said that no member, candidate, or support group should, under any guise, undermine the party or demarket the party, stressing that henceforth, no individual or group is authorized to announce, constitute, or publish any campaign council, structure, or organ in the name of the party without prior approval from the National Working Committee (NWC).
The statement by the NDC National Chairman disowning the action of the group read, “The leadership of our party ,the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has noted with concern a publication credited to one John Ugulu announcing a Presidential Campaign Council under the guise of “OK Movement.”
“For the avoidance of doubt, the party wishes to state categorically as follows:
“The party hereby dissociates itself in totality from the said OK Movement PCC announcement. It did not emanate from the party and should be disregarded by the public and the media.
“All candidates of the party must appreciate that they are not running as independent candidates. They are products of the party and remain subject to the authority and discipline of the party. Therefore. only the party’s leadership can constitute and announce a Presidential Campaign Council PCC.
“No member, candidate, or support group should, under any guise, undermine the party or demarket the party.
“Henceforth, no individual or group is authorized to announce, constitute, or publish any campaign council, structure, or organ in the name of the party without prior approval from the National Working Committee (NWC).
The party recognizes and deeply appreciates the contributions of all support groups and encourages their continued support. We welcome even more support groups who identify with our mission to rescue Nigeria.
“While the party will continue to work collaboratively with all support groups, such groups should not see themselves as alternative party structures or parallel organs of the party.
“We expect a stop to unnecessary attacks against the party on whose platform our candidates are running. If there are any differences or grievances, support groups and members are advised to refer such matters to the party through appropriate internal channels for resolution rather than resorting to public attacks.
“For this act of affront and his excesses during the primary election in Lagos State, and for his repeated disregard for party authority, the party is constrained to enforce disciplinary measures against Mr. Ugulu. He is hereby referred to the appropriate disciplinary organ of the party for necessary action in line with the provisions of the party’s constitution.
“The party remains focused on its issue-based campaign and is committed to delivering a New Nigeria that is Possible.”
OK Movement
Recall that the OK Movement, a political platform established to mobilise support for the joint ticket of the Nigeria Democratic Congress presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Dr Rabiu Kwankwaso on Thursday put in place 59-member Presidential Campaign Council comprising zonal and state coordinators.
The group had also unveiled directors for mobilisation, women affairs, strategy, security, legal affairs and other key areas ahead of the 2027 general elections.
The OK Movement publicly presents itself as a nationwide platform associated with the Obi–Kwankwaso political project ahead of the 2027 presidential election, stressing that its campaign structure will continue to focus on mobilisation and engagement across the 36 states and the FCT.
In a statement in Abuja by the movement’s National Secretary, Saadatu Sani, the Presidential Campaign Council is expected to take the movement’s message and programme to Nigerians across the states, local government areas, wards and communities.
The statement said the campaign council is headed by John Ughulu as Director-General, while Saadatu Sani serves as National Secretary.
It added that the structure includes six zonal coordinators: Suleiman Abubakar for North Central, Hashimu Dungurawa for North West, Amadu Gwambe for North East, Dr Adebayo Adefolaseye for South West, Christopher Ighodaro for South South and El-Shaddai Ikeh for South East.
Other appointments include Ibrahim Jabir as FCT Coordinator, while Maiyaki Samson, Tokji Mandim, Yusuf Abdullahi, Aliyu Tershaku, Awal Goma and Kazeem Olawuyi were named coordinators for Kogi, Plateau, Nasarawa, Benue, Niger and Kwara respectively.
The statement noted that coordinators were also appointed for Kaduna, Sokoto, Kano, Zamfara, Jigawa, Kebbi and Katsina in the North West, while Adamawa, Gombe, Taraba, Bauchi, Yobe and Borno have coordinators in the North East.
