Lautaro Martinez rode to Inter Milan’s rescue on Saturday as the Serie A champions fought back from two goals down to force a 2-2 draw at Roma.
With both sides holding perfect records heading into the top-two clash in the capital, it was an early season glimpse of what may well be the Scudetto race this term.
Gian Piero Gasperini’s Roma have arguably been the most impressive team in Italy so far this season, with Donyell Malen’s free-scoring form and a miserly defence giving them four wins from four.
Manu Kone’s double had given Roma a 2-0 lead at half-time but for the second time in a week Cristian Chivu’s side, inspired by Martinez’s brace, showed mettle as the champions fought back from such a deficit.
“There is a lot of positivity in this side, both teams could’ve won it,” Gasperini told DAZN.
“I think we played on level terms… This match must give us confidence going forward.”
Following the announcement earlier in the day of the death of Sandro Mazzola at the age of 83, both sides paid hommage to the former Inter Milan and Italy playmaker prior to kick-off, with the Nerazzurri also sporting black armbands.
Roma raced out of the blocks as Kone sent them ahead with less than six minutes on the clock when he readjusted his body well to rifle home Nahuel Molina’s knockdown.
It was the France midfielder’s first goal of the season as Inter again made a sluggish start that will worry coach Chivu.
The champions had also bounced back from being 2-0 down inside the opening 16 minutes at home to Udinese to emerge 5-3 winners on Monday.
But Inter were not at the races for most of the opening period at the Stadio Olimpico as Paulo Dybala twice threatened to double the hosts’ advantage.
A clever Curtis Jones pass then presented Alessandro Bastoni with a chance at goal seven minutes later, but the Inter defender thrashed the ball against the post from a tight angle.
However, just as Inter slowly seemed to be waking up, Kone had the ball in the net again when he tucked in from close range at the back post on 37 minutes.
His celebrations were initially cut short by the assistant’s flag before VAR intervened and, after a lengthy review, referee Davide Massa pointed to the centre circle as the 25-year-old skipped off in delight after notching the sixth Serie A goal of his career.
– Inter awaken –
Former Inter defender Chivu delivered some choice words to his charges at half-time, which will “remain between me and the players”, the Romanian said.
“I will focus on the second half, which in terms of attitude, grit and character was remarkable,” Chivu added. “We were up against a great opponent, we know what Roma represent, and it was an entertaining match.”
Inter captain Martinez halved the deficit less than a minute after the interval with a scuffed finish from Marcus Thuram’s pull-back that just crept perfectly into the side netting of Mile Svilar’s far post.
Dutch forward Malen came within a forehead’s breadth of adding to his tally of six goals in the 68th minute with a slick touch and turn in a crowded box, only for his venomous strike to cannon to safety off Inter stopper Josep Martinez’s brow.
Just as the match appeared to be petering out going into the final 10 minutes, a sudden goalmouth scramble saw Svilar make a sharp save before Martinez headed onto the bar under pressure.
Inter, however, managed to recycle the ball and it came back to the Argentine international inside the box and this time he made no mistake as he controlled with his thigh and arrowed a finish past the Serb to ensure the spoils were shared.
Elsewhere, third-placed Cagliari climbed to 12 points courtesy of a 1-0 win at Udinese, while Bologna and Torino played out a 1-1 draw in Emilia-Romagna.
Venezia host Roma’s city rivals Lazio in Saturday’s final match.

items.content:
The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) says fuel pump prices are determined by market forces and not fixed by the regulator under the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021.
The NMDPRA management made this known in a statement on Saturday, in response to concerns over the recent increase in pump prices of petrol.
It acknowledged the financial difficulties faced by Nigerians following the rise in fuel prices, noting that the situation is putting pressure on households, transport workers and businesses.
NMDPRA said Section 205(1) of the PIA provided that wholesale and retail prices of petroleum products should be based on unrestricted free-market pricing conditions.
It said the provision meant that NMDPRA did not fix pump prices or issue administrative price templates.
“Pursuant to the PIA 2021, Section 205(1) provides that wholesale and retail prices of petroleum products shall be based on unrestricted free market pricing conditions.
“Section 205(2)–(4) restricts government intervention in pricing strictly to exceptional circumstances where there is formal evidence of declared market failure. No such market failure has been declared.
“Section 216 empowers the authority to prevent anti-competitive practices, price-fixing, and the abuse of market dominance,” it said.
NMDPRA said it was also conducting joint security operations with the Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant security agencies to intensify surveillance along border corridors.
It said the measure was aimed at curbing illegal cross-border diversion of petroleum products and ensuring supply stability.
The authority said deregulation did not exempt petroleum operators from regulatory compliance or fair-trade standards.
It said that, under its Memorandum of Understanding with the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC), both agencies maintained joint surveillance to monitor price-gouging, collusion, under-dispensing and compromised product quality.
NMDPRA said it was also opening dedicated feedback and reporting channels for members of the public and industry stakeholders to report irregular pricing and exploitative trade practices.
It said the reports would be subjected to regulatory investigation and enforcement where necessary.
“NMDPRA remains steadfast in fulfilling its statutory mandate to ensure energy security, foster fair competition and protect consumers within the PIA’s legal framework,” it said. (NAN)

items.content:
Former Nigerian Navy officer and security commentator, Commodore Kunle Olawunmi (retd.), has called for accountable governance, democratic consent and peaceful constitutional change, saying no political office should be regarded as greater than the people.
Olawunmi made the call in a public statement titled “Democratic Consent: No Presidency Is Greater Than the People,” issued on Saturday, September 19, 2026.
He said citizens should be able to support or criticise a government without being accused of disloyalty, stressing that a country and its government were not the same.
According to him, political responsibility should rest with those who exercise public power and should not be attributed collectively to an ethnic or geographical community because an officeholder shares its origins.
“A country is not the same as its government. Nor is an ethnic community the same as the politicians who come from it,” he said.
Olawunmi cited Section 14 of the 1999 Constitution, which provides that sovereignty belongs to the people and that the security and welfare of citizens should be the primary purpose of government.
He said patriotism should not prevent citizens from questioning government policies or demanding solutions to problems affecting their daily lives.
“Love of country cannot require indifference to the suffering of its people,” he said, adding that concerns about insecurity, hardship, education and access to justice should not automatically be interpreted as disloyalty.
On government reforms, Olawunmi drew a distinction between the Oronsaye Report and the 2014 National Conference, saying the two exercises addressed different aspects of governance.
He noted that the Oronsaye Report focused on the rationalisation of federal agencies and the cost of government, while the 2014 National Conference considered broader issues including devolution of power, political restructuring and national security.
He said assessing the success of reforms required examining documented actions, including agencies merged, laws amended, savings achieved and proposals that remained outstanding.
“Approval is not completion,” he said, stressing that political endorsements alone could not establish whether reforms had been fully implemented.
Olawunmi also said constitutional change could not be achieved solely through presidential endorsement, noting that Section 9 of the Constitution provides a process involving the National Assembly and state legislatures.
Addressing debates over Nigeria’s constitutional future, including proposals for stronger federalism, regional autonomy and changes in political status, he said such proposals must be considered within the framework of existing law and with the consent of the people.
He cited provisions of the Constitution and the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights relating to sovereignty, self-determination, equality, participation in government and territorial integrity.
According to him, any referendum or other process aimed at determining a change in constitutional status would require a lawful basis, a clearly defined question, agreed rules and safeguards for those who disagree.
“A crowd cannot speak for everyone, and a leader’s claim to represent a community is not evidence that every member shares the same preference,” he said.
Olawunmi further cautioned against collective blame and intimidation in political disputes, saying warnings about possible disorder should not be used to justify attacks on peaceful residents or people holding opposing views.
He said political change, whether through elections or constitutional reform, should remain centred on the protection of human life and citizens’ ability to participate freely in decisions affecting their future.
“No presidency is greater than the people. No political ambition is more sacred than human life,” he said.
He added that replacing an administration would not, by itself, guarantee accountable government, saying the central issue remained how power was exercised and whether citizens could challenge its misuse without fear.
“The enduring concern is whether people can live safely, speak freely and make political choices without coercion,” Olawunmi said.

items.author: Henry Oduah
items.content:
Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has denied authoring a purported letter addressed to the Obi of Onitsha, Igwe Nnaemeka Alfred Ugochukwu Achebe, amid the ongoing dispute over political and financial issues in Anambra State.
The letter, dated September 19, 2026, and titled “The Future of Ndigbo is Bleak”, criticised Governor Chukwuma Soludo’s claims concerning liabilities allegedly incurred by Anambra during Obi’s tenure as governor.
The purported document called for the state’s financial records to be made available for scrutiny.
“Let the records be opened. Let the books be examined. Let every legitimate question be answered with evidence,” the said letter read.
Obi has recently challenged claims by the Anambra State Government that his administration left unpaid loans, maintaining that he did not leave outstanding salaries, pensions or obligations to contractors for completed projects.
He had also said he would stop campaigning if evidence was produced to contradict his position.
The Anambra State Government, however, said on Wednesday that eight external loan facilities contracted during Obi’s administration remained outstanding when he left office on March 17, 2014.
The state government said the outstanding balance on the loans stood at N127.4 billion as of June 30, 2026, based on the official exchange rate and figures it attributed to the Debt Management Office.
Amid the dispute, the purported letter circulated on social media, prompted a response from Obi on Saturday.
Obi said the document was fabricated and urged members of the public and the media to disregard it.
“My attention has been drawn to a fake letter circulating on social media, purportedly written by me to His Majesty, Igwe Nnaemeka Alfred Ugochukwu Achebe, the Obi of Onitsha, concerning political and financial matters in Anambra State,” Obi wrote.
“This document is entirely false, malicious, and a fabrication by mischievous elements aimed at misleading the public. Furthermore, the signature appended to the letter is completely forged.
“I urge the public and media to disregard this spurious publication. My focus remains steadfastly on issues of national development, accountability, and building a better future for our people – never on cheap fabrications.”

items.content:
By Elizabeth Osayande
Academic activities may remain suspended in all Lagos State-owned universities following the ongoing indefinite strike declared by their academic staff unions.
This comes four days after the Lagos State University arm of the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU-LASU, declared an indefinite strike over the state government’s failure to implement the 2025 ASUU/FGN Agreement, with the institution’s chairman vowing that the industrial action will continue.
Recall that all three Lagos State-owned universities — Lagos State University (LASU), Ojo; Lagos State University of Education (LASUED), Oto/Ijanikin; and Lagos State University of Science and Technology (LASUSTECH), Ikorodu — unanimously agreed to embark on strike on Tuesday.
In a communiqué signed by the Secretary of the ASUU-LASU Steering Committee, Comrade Thanny Nooem, and the Coordinator, Comrade Oluwaseun Babalola, the union said the decision followed months of what it described as “patient and constructive engagement” with the government without a resolution of the issues in dispute.
“This unfortunate and avoidable action has become necessary due to the continued failure of the government to address the union’s longstanding agitation over the implementation of the 2025 ASUU/FGN Agreement,” the statement said.
ASUU-LASU said it was demanding the “full domestication and implementation of the 2025 ASUU/FGN Agreement” as a condition for calling off the strike.
“The strike shall be total and comprehensive until there is a satisfactory resolution of the issues in dispute,” the union added.
The union expressed regret over the development, noting that previous efforts to resolve the matter through dialogue had not yielded the desired outcome.
The industrial action is expected to disrupt teaching and other academic activities across LASU campuses pending further developments.
The union ended its statement with the slogan “Aluta continua, victoria ascerta.”
Meanwhile, speaking with Vanguard on Saturday, the Chairman of ASUU-LASU, Comrade Oluwaseun Babalola, insisted that the strike continue.
“Yes, the strike continues. We have written to the state government and the management, yet they have not initiated any dialogue to resolve the issue,” he said.

“We heard that the bandits demanded only N300,000 each and two 25-litre jerrycans of petrol as ransom for the two men abducted on their way from the farm. For the driver, the bandits collected N2 million ransom from his family.
“The driver was released today (Saturday) and has since reunited with his family in Kwatsama village. We also heard that preparations are being made for the payment of the N30 million ransom to free the abducted imams.
“According to reliable information, a serving senator from Zamfara State has pledged to pay the ransom to free the Imams. We hope this won’t take long.”
Ibrahim appealed to the authorities to intensify efforts to free the Imams, lamenting that the clerics might have been tortured and, due to their age, could be seriously traumatised.
“The Imams are aged and their stay in the bandits’ den alone could make their health conditions deteriorate. The government should therefore hasten efforts to free them,” he said.
A son of one of the kidnapped Imams, who preferred anonymity, said the families were delighted with the latest development.
“This new development has raised our hope regarding the return of our fathers and the other religious leaders,” he said.

“We are hoping that the money can be raised before the expiration of the deadline given by the bandits,” he said.
Daily Trust reports that the kidnapped clerics are: Malam Muhammadu Shehu, Chief Imam of Dakko Juma’at Mosque; Malam Murtala Dakko, Deputy Imam, Dakko Juma’at Mosque; Malam Muhammad Yahuza, Chief Imam of Dogon Madacci 1st Juma’at Mosque; Malam Magawata Abdullahi, Chief Imam of Dogon Madacci 2nd Juma’at Mosque; Malam Bala Hogun, Chief Imam of Hogun Juma’at Mosque and Malam Muhammad Tasi’u, Chief Imam of Kwatsama Juma’at Mosque.
The clerics were abducted last week Saturday by suspected bandits at Gidan Bature village in Damri Ward, Bakura LGA.
According to multiple sources, the bandits ambushed the clerics, kidnapped and took them into the forest.
One of the sources said the clerics were on their way to Talata Mafara to attend a meeting at the residence of Senator Abdulaziz Yari.
“You know that in an effort to escape bandits, travellers have deserted major roads. We now resort to feeder roads for safety. Unfortunately for the clerics, the bandits staged an ambush along the Dakko-Damri feeder road and abducted them.
“We suspect the abductors had prior knowledge of the route the clerics followed. Bakura shares borders with Bukkuyum and Anka. So the clerics travelled through feeder roads from Lambar Bakura to Dambi, and then to Sabon Garin Dambi before heading to Talata Mafara,” the source said.
Malam Hassan Mai-Fanta, Chief Imam of Izala 2nd Mosque in Shinkafi town, who also attended the meeting with the abducted scholars, told Daily Trust that he left Talata Mafara earlier than the victims.
“I also attended the meeting at Senator Abdulaziz Yari’s residence, but those of us from Shinkafi Local Government left Talata Mafara town earlier than the abducted scholars. I only heard about their abduction yesterday.
“This is unfortunate. The bandits spare nobody. If they could have the audacity to kidnap Islamic scholars, then who will be spared? I urge the government to ensure the rescue and safe return of the abducted clerics,” he concluded.

items.content:
By Henry Umoru
Senators from the 19 Northern states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), under the aegis of the Northern Senators Forum, NSF, have called for an independent, thorough and transparent investigation into the deaths of 37 suspected illegal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, in Niger State to ascertain the remote and immediate causes of the tragic incident.
According to the Senators, Nigerians must know who ordered the arrests, where the detainees were taken, who authorised their detention in the facility, whether the room was fit for human habitation, when the distress calls were made, who heard them, what action was taken, and the precise circumstances in which each victim died.
The Northern Senators said the investigation should involve the National Human Rights Commission, the Nigerian Bar Association, credible civil society organisations and independent forensic experts.
A statement signed on Saturday by the Chairman of the Northern Senators Forum, Senator Abdulaziz Musa Yar’adua, APC, Katsina Central, read, £The Northern Senators Forum joins the nation in mourning the reported deaths of 37 young Nigerians in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna, Niger State. The circumstances surrounding their deaths, in which they were reportedly confined in a small room and cried for help before they choked to death, are deeply disturbing and unacceptable.
“No Nigerian, regardless of the allegation against him, should lose his life in the custody of an agency established to protect lives and property. The sanctity of human life and the dignity of every person in custody must be upheld at all times.
“The Northern Senators Forum therefore demands an immediate, transparent and independent investigation into the entire chain of events. Nigerians must know who ordered the arrests, where the detainees were taken, who authorized their detention in the facility, whether the room was fit for human habitation, when the distress calls were made, who heard them, what action was taken, and the precise circumstances in which each victim died. The investigation should involve the National Human Rights Commission, the Nigerian Bar Association, credible civil society organizations and independent forensic experts.
“We equally demand independent autopsies for all 37 victims, with representatives of the families and independent pathologists allowed to participate. If criminal negligence, unlawful detention, reckless conduct or any deliberate act contributed to these deaths, those responsible must be prosecuted, irrespective of their rank or position.
“This tragedy must also trigger a nationwide review of detention facilities operated by all security agencies to ensure that no Nigerian is ever again placed in a situation where a cry for help becomes a cry that nobody answers.
“The Northern Senators Forum commends the Federal Government for ordering a full and independent enquiry into this matter and the Niger State Government for the proactive steps taken so far, including support for the families and cooperation with investigators.
“The Northern Senators Forum extends its deepest condolences to the families of the deceased and to the people of Niger State. May Almighty Allah (SWT) forgive the shortcomings of the departed, grant them Al-Jannatul Firdaus, and give their families the fortitude to bear this immeasurable loss.”

items.content:
By Efe Onodjae
Importation of arms and ammunition into Nigeria rose by 104.31 per cent in the first half of 2026, reaching N55.06 billion, according to data from the National Bureau of Statistics, NBS.
Read Also: 2027: Fear grips Nigerians as political thugs begin actions that truncated 1st Republic, hurt 2nd Republic
The figure, contained in the NBS Foreign Trade Statistics for the second quarter of 2026, represents an increase of N28.11 billion from the N26.95 billion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.
The development has heightened concerns over the movement of arms into the country, particularly against the backdrop of recent interceptions of consignments of pump-action rifles by the Nigeria Customs Service, NCS.
The increase also comes less than a year before the 2027 general elections, with security experts and stakeholders raising concerns over the possible factors driving the movement of arms into the country.
Speaking on the development, a professor at Lagos State University, LASU, Prof. Dapo Thomas, said insecurity, political activities and the growing demand for weapons could contribute to the increase in gun-running.
Thomas said gun-running had become a business for some individuals, adding that security challenges could encourage an increase in the supply of illegal arms
The don, however, cautioned against attributing the increase solely to the forthcoming elections, saying insecurity and other factors could also be responsible for the development.
Thomas said although election periods had historically been associated with increased demand for weapons, government and security agencies must remain vigilant and strengthen measures to check the inflow of arms.
He urged the government, Customs, Police and other agencies responsible for border control and the movement of goods to intensify surveillance and monitoring of consignments entering the country.
According to him, continued security lapses could create an environment conducive to criminal activities and illegal arms trafficking.
Agents react
Also speaking, the National President of the National Council of Managing Directors of Licensed Customs Agents, NCMDLCA, Lucky Amiwero, commended the NCS over its recent interception of consignments of pump-action rifles imported from Turkey.
Amiwero said the interceptions underscored the need for stronger cargo inspection and intelligence-sharing mechanisms to prevent prohibited items from entering the country.
He said detecting concealed prohibited items in containers was not an easy task, stressing the importance of proper inspection of cargo.
Amiwero said: “We have to commend the Customs for what they are doing. Intercepting those things is not an easy thing to intercept.
“You bring up containers, they can arrange it in different ways you will not understand. If the containers are not properly inspected, you will not know that they are in there.”
He called for greater cooperation among countries in cargo screening and information sharing, noting that pre-arrival information could assist Nigerian authorities in identifying suspicious consignments before they reach the country’s ports.
Importers speak
Meanwhile, the Secretary-General of the Importers Association of Nigeria, Ahmed Yar’Adua, said the association would meet with the NCS over the recent interceptions and concerns surrounding the movement of arms through the ports.
Yar’Adua, who disclosed this in an interview with Vanguard, said the association had commenced discussions on the development and would engage Customs on the issue.
The engagement is expected to bring stakeholders in the importation and clearance chain together to examine the circumstances surrounding the movement of prohibited consignments through the nation’s ports and consider measures to prevent a recurrence.
The NBS figures showed that arms and ammunition imports increased from N26.95 billion in the first half of 2025 to N55.06 billion in the first half of 2026, representing a 104.31 per cent increase.
The development has therefore placed renewed attention on the channels through which arms and ammunition enter the country and the capacity of relevant agencies to detect and prevent illicit consignments.
Vanguard News

items.author: Ahsan Gardezi
items.content:
Saudi Arabia is facing a security crisis that could eventually change its regional strategy. The latest Houthi operations have reached Saudi cities, and Riyadh is quickly losing its oil-export routes. To top it all off, Pakistan and Turkey are busy at home so the 2026 Defense Pact looks off the table.
This has put Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in a tight spot. ‘How do I get myself out of this mess without bringing Israel closer?’ he must be thinking.
On September 19, Saudi authorities issued the first aerial threat alert for Riyadh since the latest Ansar Allah strikes began. Explosions were reported near the capital’s airport. Earlier, Houthi attacks had hit or threatened areas including Jeddah, Taif, Abha, Khamis Mushait and Jazan.
“The bigger problem is not the missiles and drones. The Saudi regime wants its new defense partners to strike parts of Yemen for face-saving. With the Makkah Defense Pact dysfunctional, Israel could be offered an olive branch,” a veteran historian told ProPakistani in an informal conversation.
The Houthis have also advanced along the Red Sea and captured the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Hormuz is blocked at the other end. This creates a strategic problem for Riyadh.
Reuters reported earlier that Saudi Arabia is also seeking additional military assistance from Pakistan, Egypt, France and Britain. None of them has committed to a direct intervention so far.
That brings Israel into the equation.
Israel Fits Here
Israel has extensive help from the United States, particularly with artillery, missile defense, intelligence and drone warfare. Reports this week say Israeli officials are attempting to use the Houthi excuse to push their case for expanding influence near Riyadh.
Saudi Arabia still continues to publicly condition normalization with Israel on meaningful progress toward Palestinian statehood. The Houthi pressure is changing that position.
If Houthi attacks continue to threaten Saudi cities, airports, oil infrastructure and Red Sea shipping, Riyadh may eventually face a choice between maintaining political distance from Israel and accepting deeper Israeli security cooperation.
That could also test Pakistan’s new defense relationship with Saudi Arabia. I will not mention some statements issued by top intelligence agencies in the region but here’s the deal: The defense pact is entering its first and arguably final strategic test.
For Saudi Arabia, the issue is no longer simply Yemen. It is whether the kingdom can secure itself. And if the Houthi presence continues to grow, Israel may increasingly become part of that calculation.
The views expressed here belong to the author.

items.content:
The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) has deployed Abdulhamid Kabara as the new commandant of its Niger State Command following the deaths of 37 suspected illegal miners in custody.
Kabara replaces Suberu Aniviye, who was suspended as Niger NSCDC commandant after the 37 suspects died in Minna, the state capital, on Thursday.
Abubakar Muti, NSCDC spokesperson in Niger State, announced in a statement on Saturday that Kabara formally assumed office and took over the command on Friday, September 18.
The Federal Government had ordered Aniviye’s immediate suspension following the deaths.
“The assumption of office comes at a particularly sensitive period for the Command, following the unfortunate deaths of some persons arrested in connection with suspected illegal mining activities in the State,” the statement reads.
Muti said Kabara expressed “deep sadness over the loss of lives and extended his heartfelt sympathy to the families of the deceased and everyone affected by the unfortunate incident”.
The new commandant said the corps remained committed to its statutory responsibilities, including arrests, investigations, enforcement and the fight against illegal mining, but stressed that the protection of human life must remain a priority.
“At a moment like this, beyond arrests, investigations, enforcement and the fight against illegal mining, we must remember one fundamental truth: every human life matters,” he said.
“The loss of any human life is painful, and our thoughts and prayers are with the families who are mourning at this difficult time.”
Kabara also emphasised that law enforcement responsibilities must be balanced with the need to protect people in custody.
He said the responsibility of safeguarding society and enforcing the law must go hand in hand with upholding the dignity, safety and welfare of persons in custody.
The deployment comes as authorities face scrutiny over the circumstances surrounding the deaths of the 37 suspected illegal miners in NSCDC custody.

items.author: Ayobami
items.content:
Mikel Arteta said Arsenal’s 3-0 defeat by Brighton was a reminder of “how tough every game” in the Premier League is as the defending champions were beaten for the first time this season.
Brighton dominated from the off at the Amex Stadium and punched holes in Arsenal’s normally resolute defence thanks to long-range strikes from Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas before half-time.
Chema Andres rose highest to head in a third from a corner early in the second period as Arsenal lost by more than two goals for the first time in over three years.
“Extremely disappointed. First of all I think we have to congratulate Brighton for the victory, I think they deserve it,” said Arteta.
“I think they were the better team. From our side there were certain basics that you need to accomplish in football, especially in the Premier League, that we were very far from.”
The Gunners have been tipped to cruise to the title after ending their 22-year wait to be crowned champions of England last season.
Arsenal started the campaign in ominous fashion, winning all seven games before Saturday in all competitions.
But Arteta said defeat served a timely reminder ahead of a three-week international break of how tough the season will be.
“It’s a big lesson for us. Is that a reminder to some of the players how tough every game is,” added the Spaniard.
“That’s not going to take away what the team has done and the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup.
“With 18 players coming back, what we’ve done and the way we’ve competed and the amount of games we’ve won has been remarkable.
“But this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level.”

Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, has described Saturday’s bye-elections in Gombe, Kano, Bauchi and Delta states as dress rehearsals for the 2027 General Election, insisting that no electoral contest should be dismissed as trivial or routine.

“These four bye-elections provide indispensable operational lessons for the Commission as we systematically chart our roadmap toward the 2027 General Election.
“We must resist the temptation to view any exercise as merely an ordinary by-election. Every election is a critical component of our broader preparations for the 2027 General Election, allowing us to continuously audit our logistics framework, stress-test our technological deployment, and evaluate administrative field readiness,” Amupitan said.
The INEC Chairman, who was accompanied by National Commissioners and senior management officials, monitored the bye-elections as operational reports arrived from the field.
Amupitan reassured Nigerians of the Commission’s resolve to uphold electoral integrity, noting that operational bottlenecks encountered before polling were swiftly identified and resolved.
“Our primary mandate in the Situation Room is monitoring and proactive crisis resolution. Whatever administrative or field challenges arose before the day of the elections, the Commission was able to nip them in the bud effectively. We remain committed to refining our processes so that every subsequent exercise reflects higher standards of efficiency and public confidence,” the chairman added.
He thanked everyone present in the situation room, especially the technical team, for ensuring the Commission was able to monitor the multi-state exercise seamlessly and assess field performance without any hitch.

items.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru
Four distinguished Nigerians have been conferred with honorary designations as Ambassadors of Humanitarian Affairs and Goodwill Ambassadors during a high-level side event on the margins of the ongoing 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York.
The investiture ceremony took place on 18 September 2026 at the United Nations Headquarters, Conference Room 11, as part of the UNGA High-Level Global Executive Roundtable Side Event 2026.
The Global Organization for Sustainable Development Goals (GOFSDGs), an organisation in Special Consultative Status with the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), partnered with the Civil Society Organizations on Community Advancement and Humanitarian Empowerment Initiative (CSCHEI) and collaborated with the United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR) to confer the honorary titles.
According to a statement by Dr. Sophie Romma Murashkovsky, on behalf of the Organizing Committee, UNGA High-Level Global Executive Roundtable Side Event 2026, the five honourees and their designations are: Hon. Mr. Kunle Yusuff, MON, Director-General, CSCHEI – Ambassador of Goodwill, Mr. David Luftglass, Chief Executive Officer, Renaissance Assets Holdings Corporation, USA – Ambassador of Goodwill, Dr. Judith Ogbara, Chief Executive Officer, Rosem Energy Ltd and Chairperson, AAE Foundation, Nigeria – Ambassador for Humanitarian Affairs, Mr. Dahiru Biu – Ambassador of Goodwill and
Duke Kelvin Iyke Asogwa – Ambassador for Humanitarian Affairs.
The ceremony was officiated by the Secretary-General of the International Human Rights Commission, the Founder of Open Diplomacy International, and representatives of UNITAR.
The Organising Committee explained that the conferment followed “a rigorous due diligence and assessment of track record, integrity, and measurable contributions to humanitarian advancement, in full alignment with the United Nations Charter and the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.”
It stated that the honourees were selected based on demonstrated leadership in advancing humanitarian principles, community-driven development, and inclusive social protection systems, consistent commitment to accelerating the implementation of SDGs 1 (No Poverty), 3 (Good Health and Well-being), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), 13 (Climate Action), 16 (Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions) and 17 (Partnerships for the Goals) at national and sub-national levels
Other criteria included Proven capacity to leverage and mobilise multi-stakeholder partnerships, catalyse resources, and foster goodwill for vulnerable and hard-to-reach populations and exemplary service that enhances Nigeria’s positive engagement in the multilateral system and reinforces inclusive multilateralism and South-South cooperation.
The organising committee stated that the honorary status “confers not only recognition but also responsibility — to uphold the core humanitarian principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality, and independence; to champion accountability to affected populations (AAP), sustainability, and the principle of Leaving No One Behind (LNOB); and to serve as credible bridges between Nigeria, the global humanitarian community, and the international investment and donor ecosystem.”
The statement noted that at the conclusion of the High-Level Global Executive Roundtable, participants adopted three key resolutions: “To operationalize the Global Partnership Network Support System (GPNSS) as a catalytic platform to facilitate private sector access to sustainable, blended, and concessional financing for humanitarian and development initiatives.
“To institute a structured follow-up, capacity-building and impact-tracking mechanism anchored by UNITAR and other relevant UN entities, Donor Agencies and International Non-Governmental Organizations (INGOs).
“To mandate the newly decorated Ambassadors to serve as focal champions and goodwill envoys for resource mobilization, high-level advocacy, and localization of humanitarian interventions in alignment with UN standards and humanitarian principles.”
The organising committee congratulated the newly decorated Ambassadors and “strongly encourages them to continue to align their future engagements, programmatic interventions, and strategic partnerships with the mandates of the United Nations, bilateral and multilateral Donor Agencies, Development Partners, Development Finance Institutions, and INGOs.”
“We call upon all stakeholders to provide the necessary technical and financial support to enable them to effectively deliver on this noble mandate,” it added.

Raphinha, 29, joined Barcelona from Leeds in 2022 and became a key player when coach Hansi Flick arrived in 2024.

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
An executive director of London-based Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA) has said that Pakistan can address the issue of large budget discrepancies by improving the governance framework, effective regulations and bringing information transparency.
In an interview with The Express Tribune, Lucia Real Martin said that the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) are "gold standards" but local adjustments can be made, provided there is no deviation that undermines confidence. ACCA Executive Director Relations Lucia Real Martin spoke about a host of issues related to the association's possible support for improving public finance management in Pakistan, the future of the accounting profession, statistical discrepancies and implementation of the IFRS.
She spoke at length on a question about a Rs853 billion statistical discrepancy reported by the federal and four provincial governments in the accounts of fiscal year 2025-26. "There are a number of things to ensure that those discrepancies are not there. We need to contribute to those institutions in becoming credible and they can become credible, if they understand the importance of reporting transparent information and to do that they need to actually understand what they need to report on," said Martin.
She said that improvement in governance framework, training and knowledge can help address the statistical discrepancy in the budget. The governance framework definitely has to be one of the elements in addition to effective regulations to address large statistical discrepancies, she added.
The executive director said that four elements are to have credible institutions, which have governance frameworks that help bring transparency in information. Having all of that is professional capacity, and this is where the ACCA comes in to provide capacity not only at the technical level but at the ethical level, said Martin.
IFRS implementation
The Cabinet Committee on SOEs last week relaxed the international reporting standards to avoid booking losses in accounts of energy-sector companies and commercial banks due to the chronic circular debt.
"From ACCA's perspective, global standards are the gold standards, but even the global standards need a journey," said the executive director. She noted that over 140 countries are now applying the IFRS, although many have adapted to these standards according to their local context. Adopting the IFRS according to the pace of the country is not wrong and continuing to strive to embrace the global standards would give confidence to investors and the narrative to the government and institutions and promise to the youth that Pakistan is a country that can be global, she added.
She further explained that if the adjustment in these standards is to deviate from the global standards and to create a separate local environment, then it is a breach and once the dent is created, then the separation between the local environment and the global investment environment becomes challenging. Ongoing commitment to the global standards will continue to build confidence in the international arena, with the IMF and with investors, said Martin.
The Central Monitoring Unit (CMU) of the finance ministry had also warned against relaxing these standards but the Cabinet Committee on SOEs did not comply with the advice. According to Rule 9 of the IFRS, aging receivables previously treated as guaranteed recoverable now generate direct impairment charges, exposing systemic fiscal interconnectedness, warned the CMU. During her visit, the executive director also met with Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb. She said that the ACCA has been discussing with Pakistan the possibility of cooperation in the service economy.
Ticket to overseas
Responding to a question about the ACCA affiliates and members settling in Dubai and London, Martin said there are always people who want to get either international experience or move abroad for a different life and this happens everywhere but obviously in Pakistan it is disproportionate.
She said that the answer to this is to build a service economy where organisations are part of global organisations or serve global clients and therefore young people in Pakistan can be able to work with the UK, the US and other Asian countries right from Pakistan.
Unlike a decline in interest in the accounting profession, Martin said that the trend is encouraging in Pakistan. But she added that there are only 22,000 active professional accountants in Pakistan and for the ambitions that the government has for export of services, this number is not enough. "Pakistan's young population is a goldmine, and these people are willing to become professional accountants." Accounting profession has a bright future, and it hinges on the young talent of Pakistan. ACCA members do not have authority to sign statutory audits of companies. But these members work for large corporate firms and perform all other tasks.
ACCA charges the fee in pound sterling. To a question, she said that in future fee structures can be considered in local currencies but she did not give a timeframe. There is a rate card for Pakistan, which is lower than in the UK, but it is still paid in pounds. The economic hardship cases are also acknowledged.

Islamabad has all the capabilities to become far more than Pakistan's administrative capital and it can emerge as a regional centre of investment, innovation, technology and international commerce, remarked Islamabad Chamber of Commerce and Industry (ICCI) President Sardar Tahir Mehmood, while calling for a bold economic vision to transform the federal capital's strategic advantages into tangible business and investment opportunities.

Yet, he noted, those advantages had not been brought together under a unified economic strategy capable of attracting international businesses, investment, technology and high-value services.
"Islamabad has the location, the talent, the institutions and the international connectivity; what it needs now is an economic vision that brings these strengths together and turns them into opportunity, investment and growth," Mehmood said.
He proposed the formulation of a long-term Islamabad Economic Master Plan to establish a clear economic identity for the capital, with priority sectors including technology and IT-enabled services, digital trade, investment, business tourism, international conferences, education, healthcare, financial services and other knowledge-intensive industries. "Such a strategy could position Islamabad as a competitive regional business destination while creating new opportunities for entrepreneurship, employment and exports."

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Anthropic is considering rolling out a new AI model to counter OpenAI's momentum since its launch of GPT-6 Astra, according to sources, ahead of an expected IPO and after its CEO called for an industry-wide slowdown.
The timing of a potential launch aimed at addressing competitive pressure from a direct rival follows Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call on the global AI community to slow down the pace of releasing new capabilities to address safety concerns, the sources said. "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models," Amodei wrote in a 3,800-word essay on September 12.
The essay, which painted a bleak picture of swarms of AI agents taking over the internet and outpacing human control, drew support from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.
OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, released this month, has gained traction among businesses, prompting concerns among some investors who told Reuters they are re-evaluating Anthropic's position as the leading provider of enterprise AI tools.
Anthropic is evaluating the safety of its next model as part of its deliberations over a release, one of the people familiar with the matter said. Some of the discussions involve how to balance investment in releasing new models with efforts to strengthen the company's profitability as rising interest rates make investors more focused on the timing of expected profits, said people familiar with the company's thinking.
The debate over spending highlights the increasing pressure on the firms at the centre of the AI boom to produce sustainable cash flows sooner, thanks both to rising rates and tough competition from open-source AI providers, especially in China.
Anthropic declined to comment for this story. The potential launch would test how Anthropic can defend its enterprise market position against OpenAI while maintaining the safety-first identity that has distinguished it from competitors.
GPT-6 Astra gains enterprise traction
OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra on September 3, touting gains in computer use, software engineering, cybersecurity and professional work. The model has received a strong response from enterprise users and developers, prompting potential Anthropic IPO investors to scrutinise whether OpenAI could begin taking share from Anthropic, which has been viewed for months as the leader in enterprise AI.
Astra accounted for about 13% of enterprise AI spending tracked by corporate expense platform Ramp, compared with about 8% for Anthropic's Claude Fable, according to the latest data.
Astra has also pulled ahead on OpenRouter, a widely used platform that routes developer traffic across AI models. OpenRouter said its users spent more on OpenAI models than on Anthropic models last week, the first time OpenAI has led on that measure in more than two and a half years.
Anthropic maintains revenue advantage
Some existing investors and those who expect to invest in both Anthropic's and OpenAI's IPOs said they do not believe Astra poses a significant threat to Anthropic, given the size of its lead in the market for enterprise AI tools and the amount of time it takes to unseat incumbent vendors to large companies.
Anthropic's annualised revenue run rate topped $65 billion by the end of July, up from about $9 billion at the end of 2025. It is also projecting a 2028 revenue of roughly $190 billion to $200 billion, Reuters previously reported. OpenAI's annualised revenue run rate passed $40 billion in July.
Investors also expect leadership among Anthropic, OpenAI, Alphabet's Google and other major AI developers to shift repeatedly as companies release new generations of models, making any advantage potentially short-lived.
Bigger challenges ahead
A potentially bigger challenge for Anthropic and other leading AI providers is the rise of open-source and open-weight models, which can lower token costs and allow companies to build more of their own AI infrastructure rather than rely on providers such as Anthropic and OpenAI, investors said.
The shift could put pressure on the economics of the AI industry as companies have more options to develop and run models outside the leading commercial providers, broadening the competitive threat beyond the race between Anthropic and OpenAI.
Meta Platforms has been among Anthropic's largest customers, but is looking to reduce its use of Anthropic's models as it develops more AI capabilities internally, people familiar with the matter said.
OpenAI, meanwhile, has taken some pressure off the race to public markets. Its CEO, Altman, confirmed on Saturday that the company would not go public in 2026, saying concerns around AI safety made this an ill-advised time for a listing.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI) President Faheem Ur Rehman Saigol has called for stronger cooperation between Pakistan's business community and diplomatic missions to promote trade, attract investment and build business-to-business linkages.
Speaking at the LCCI Ambassadors' Dinner 2026, Saigol said embassies and their commercial sections helped Pakistani businesses find new markets, identify reliable partners and gain confidence to invest abroad. He praised them for arranging business meetings, sharing trade information and connecting local firms with companies in their countries. "This support is especially valuable for businesses entering unfamiliar markets."
Saigol said diplomacy had become even more important for business because companies needed peace, stability and predictable policies to grow. He hoped wisdom would prevail and tensions would ease.
He saw potential for cooperation in agriculture, textile, pharmaceuticals, information technology, renewable energy, logistics, mining, tourism and other sectors, and said that Pakistan's large population offered opportunities for international partnerships.
He also asked for more support for small and medium enterprises, saying they could offer quality products but needed guidance on global market requirements and quality standards. He stressed that the LCCI was ready to work with missions through regular meetings and sector-specific interactions and proposed follow-up mechanisms so that contacts made at such events could lead to practical business. Chief Guest Atadjan Movlamov, Turkmenistan's Ambassador and Dean of the Diplomatic Corps, said economic diplomacy had become an indispensable tool of international relations. He said goodwill should be turned into practical, high-impact economic cooperation, and the event's success should be judged by the business delegations, joint ventures and removal of trade barriers that would follow it.
Movlamov named trade facilitation, investment, renewable energy, agriculture, textile, IT and logistics as key areas. He said Pakistan's location could connect South Asia with Central Asia and the Middle East.
He described the TAPI gas pipeline as an example of regional cooperation and said work on it was progressing. He also referred to cooperation in power transmission and fibre-optic links, and said Turkmenistan saw Pakistan as an important maritime gateway.
German Ambassador Ina Lepel said the strongest themes were business-to-business linkages, trade and investment, private-sector cooperation, vocational and technical education, climate and sustainable development. She said Germany attached great importance to stronger economic cooperation with Pakistan and saw considerable potential to expand trade, investment and business links. Portugal Ambassador Paulo Domingues said his country was keen to strengthen economic and commercial ties with Pakistan through more trade, investment and private-sector linkages. He said there was significant potential in agriculture, IT, education and the blue economy. He stressed the importance of stronger institutional and business-to-business connections.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) disposed of 98% of its adjudication caseload, issuing decisions in 573 cases and imposing penalties exceeding Rs4.73 billion for violations of the Companies Act and other applicable laws.
Following the appointment of SECP Chairman Dr Kabir Ahmed Sidhu, the commission further strengthened its adjudication functions. Of the 969 Adjudication Recommendation Notes available for assessment, 953 were reviewed, while proceedings in 573 cases were concluded through the issuance of orders, said a news release. The remaining recommendations for initiating legal proceedings were subsequently processed through strengthened oversight and effective case management, resulting in the clearance of the entire adjudication backlog.
The proceedings involved listed, unlisted and private companies, as well as regulated entities including securities' brokers, insurance companies and Non-Banking Finance Companies (NBFCs). The violations related to the Companies Act, the Securities Act and other applicable laws and regulatory requirements.
The commission also placed particular emphasis on compliance by state-owned enterprises and issued 117 adjudication orders concerning violations of applicable corporate and regulatory requirements by the SOEs. Major violations included failure to submit financial statements and statutory information, delays in holding annual general meetings, non-disclosure of mandatory information, breaches of financial-reporting and corporate-governance requirements, and failure to appoint female and independent directors.
The SECP chairman said the commission was ensuring timely, transparent and evidence-based decisions in all adjudication matters. He said the SECP's priorities included expeditious disposal of pending proceedings through effective case management, strengthening the rule of law, promoting a culture of regulatory compliance among companies and protecting the interests of investors, particularly minority shareholders.
Furthermore, the SECP on Friday approved Shaamilkar Tajir, a digital application offering Shariah-compliant financing of up to Rs3 million to eligible small businesses. Developed by the SECP-licensed Shaamilkar Financial Services, the application will enable micro-entrepreneurs to purchase inventory from approved suppliers through a simpler and faster digital process, said a news release. The initiative aims to bring underserved businesses into the formal credit system and help them expand their operations.
"Technology-enabled financing can expand access to formal credit for underserved businesses," SECP Chairman Dr Kabir Ahmed Sidhu said, adding that the commission would facilitate responsible digital financing while ensuring regulatory oversight and consumer protection.
The approval supports the federal government's access to finance agenda for SMEs and other priority sectors. Between July 2025 and June 2026, the licensed lending NBFCs provided Rs253 billion through 2.5 million loans to micro, small and medium enterprises. APP

items.author: Daily Trust
items.content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has declared that President Bola Tinubu, the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dele Alake, and the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, have 37 unexplained deaths on their hands and must not be allowed to hide behind propaganda or sacrifice junior officers to protect those at the top.
In a statement issued on Saturday by his Senior Special Assistant on Public Communication, Mr Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the victims were arrested alive by agents of the Nigerian government, detained under state authority and never returned alive to their families.
He said the administration must answer one simple but devastating question: “How did 37 Nigerians die after the government arrested them and assumed responsibility for their safety?”
“Thirty-seven Nigerians, many of them teenagers, entered government custody alive. Thirty-seven of them died there. The Tinubu administration cannot explain away 37 bodies with press releases, suspensions and bureaucratic excuses.
Social media abuzz as Aisha Buhari, Seyi Tinubu, Dino Melaye, others attend pre-wedding in Spain
Tinubu: Nigerians already enjoying cheaper transport fares
“These were not casualties of Boko Haram. They were not murdered by bandits. They did not die on a battlefield. They died after agents of the Nigerian government arrested, transported and detained them inside a government facility.
“The government seized their freedom and assumed responsibility for their safety. It must now account for every life lost. President Tinubu, Dele Alake and Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo cannot hide behind propaganda while 37 Nigerian families bury their children.
“In 2014, at least 16 young Nigerians died during the Nigeria Immigration Service recruitment tragedy. The supervising minister, Abba Moro, was investigated and subsequently prosecuted over matters arising from that exercise. Why should the standard be different today? Are these lives worth less because the victims were poor, unemployed and accused of illegal mining?
“These Nigerians were arrested during an operation against alleged illegal mining and detained by the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, an agency supervised by the Ministry of Interior. Survivors have alleged that they were crammed into an overcrowded, poorly ventilated cell where they struggled to breathe.
“That allegation demands an immediate and independent criminal investigation. It cannot be resolved through an internal inquiry in which government officials investigate government agents and present government-approved conclusions to Nigerians.
“Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo has direct and unavoidable questions to answer. He supervises the agency in whose custody these Nigerians allegedly died. He cannot claim credit for the NSCDC’s achievements and then outsource responsibility when 37 people die in its custody.
“Dele Alake must equally account for the enforcement operations surrounding the sector he supervises. Instead of confronting this catastrophe with the gravity it demands, he remained conspicuously silent while occupying himself with political propaganda. When 37 Nigerians die following an operation connected to your sector, silence is not neutrality; it is an abdication of responsibility.
“President Tinubu bears ultimate responsibility for the conduct of his government. He cannot behave like a spectator whenever his administration is confronted by tragedy, scandal or failure. The buck stops at his desk, and 37 unexplained deaths cannot be delegated away.
“The administration is attempting to bury the central question beneath suspensions and carefully managed explanations. But Nigerians will continue to ask: How did 37 citizens enter government custody alive and emerge dead?
“Suspending a few officers is not justice. Junior officers must not be turned into sacrificial lambs while those who authorised, supervised and controlled the operation escape scrutiny.
“In any responsible democracy, the unexplained death of even one person in state custody would provoke a national reckoning. Here, 37 citizens are dead, yet the government appears more interested in managing public outrage than establishing the truth.
“If Boko Haram had killed these Nigerians, the government would rightly blame Boko Haram. If bandits had killed them, it would blame bandits. But this was neither Boko Haram nor a bandit attack. These citizens died under the direct watch of the Tinubu-led APC government.
“The state arrested them. The state transported them. The state detained them. The state controlled the facility and assumed responsibility for their welfare. The state cannot now run away from their deaths.
“There is an even deeper tragedy. With education, opportunity and modest start-up capital, these young Nigerians could have become innovators, entrepreneurs and job creators. They could have supported their families, transformed their communities and contributed meaningfully to Nigeria’s development.
“Instead, the unemployment, poverty and hopelessness deepened by the Tinubu administration drove many young Nigerians into dangerous and unlawful mining simply to survive. This government denied them opportunity in life; poverty drove them into the pits; government agents arrested them there; and now their families have received corpses and excuses.
“These young people were failed three times: first by an economy that offered them no future; second by a state that criminalised their struggle for survival; and finally by a government that failed to protect them after taking away their freedom.
“Illegal mining is robbing Nigeria of its resources, destroying communities and threatening national security. It must be confronted firmly. But fighting illegal mining is not a licence for state agents to arrest citizens alive and return their bodies to their families.
“An allegation is not a death sentence. An arrest warrant is not a warrant to kill. Government custody must never become a gateway to the mortuary.
“Every official involved in the arrest, transportation and detention of these Nigerians must be identified, suspended and subjected to an independent criminal investigation. The inquiry must establish the entire chain of command: who authorised the operation, who ordered the arrests, how many people were confined in the cell and who was responsible for their welfare.
“It must determine when the detainees first showed signs of distress, who was informed, what medical assistance was provided and the precise cause of every death. It must also establish what Dele Alake and Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo knew, when they knew it and what actions they took.
“All detention registers, operational records, communication logs, medical reports, photographs and available surveillance footage must be secured immediately. Independent autopsies must be conducted, the victims’ families must be represented and all evidence must be protected from alteration, disappearance or destruction.
“Until the Tinubu administration provides a credible and independently verifiable explanation, Nigerians are entitled to suspect criminal negligence, abuse of power and a possible cover-up.
“The blood of these young Nigerians will continue to cry out for justice until the truth is told and everyone responsible is held accountable. Their blood cannot be silenced by propaganda, their deaths cannot be buried beneath bureaucracy, and their lives cannot be cancelled with press releases.
“Thirty-seven lives mattered. Thirty-seven families are grieving. Thirty-seven Nigerians entered government custody alive and never returned home.
“Suspensions are not justice. Propaganda is not an explanation. Silence is not accountability. Tinubu cannot look away, Alake cannot propagandise his way out of responsibility, and Tunji-Ojo cannot wash his hands of deaths recorded under an agency he supervises.”

Saror, who served as ABU Vice Chancellor between 1991 and 1995, said the crisis became particularly intense towards the end of his tenure when some members of the academic community opposed his leadership.
He said he first became aware of a petition written against him by members of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) while returning from Gboko, where he had gone with his family for a chieftaincy ceremony.
He spoke on Reminiscences, a programme, on Trust TV.
Miners&#8217; deaths: Tinubu, Alake, Tunji-Ojo owe Nigerians answers &#8211; Atiku
Social media abuzz as Aisha Buhari, Seyi Tinubu, Dino Melaye, others attend pre-wedding in Spain
“I got to hear about it when I came home with my family to receive a chieftaincy title in Gboko on December 31, 1994.”
“On the way back to Zaria, on the radio I was hearing how ASUU had written a petition against me. I was dumbfounded”, he recalled.
Saror said he subsequently went to the Kaduna office of the Nigerian Television Authority (NTA) and requested an opportunity to respond to the allegations contained in the petition, which he said was granted.
He, however, said the controversy did not end there.
He said demonstrations followed and the university’s Senate Building was reportedly locked during the crisis.
According to him, the hostility was partly connected to disagreements over the management of the university following the implementation of the Structural Adjustment Programme (SAP), which affected the university system.
Saror said some members of ASUU wanted greater involvement in the management of universities, a position he resisted as vice chancellor.
“At the end of that agreement, they really wanted to be part of the management of the universities, which was a bit weird. And because I stood firm, they were not happy with me,” he said.
The former vice chancellor said the opposition became so intense that he eventually heard that a snake had been brought into his office as part of efforts to frighten him into resigning.
Asked about the snake issue, the foreman VC and former senator said:
“Oh yes. It was very real,” Saror said, recalling that a local snake charmer from Shika, whom he identified as Haruna, was brought into the matter.
“There was a snake in my office. A man called Haruna from Shika, whom I knew, was a snake charmer. They recruited him and he brought the snake. They wanted me to resign, but I refused. I told them only Abacha, as the head of state and visitor to the university, could remove me”, he submitted.
He said the people behind the move wanted him to resign, but he refused, insisting that only the military government had the authority to remove him from office.
The crisis also attracted the intervention of the military government, with then Head of State, General Sani Abacha, setting up a commission of inquiry headed by Major-General Mamman Kontagora to investigate the unrest.
Saror said he was surprised that the commission submitted its report shortly before the end of his tenure and recommended that he be removed, even though he had already informed the university council that he would not seek a second term.
He said he was eventually allowed to complete his tenure and handed over to Kontagora, who was subsequently appointed sole administrator of the university.
ABU’s official history lists Saror as the university’s seventh vice chancellor, serving from 1991 to 1995, before Kontagora took over as sole administrator from 1995.
Saror said the controversy did not permanently sever his relationship with the university.
He noted that he later sold his agricultural farm in Zaria to ABU and was also honoured by the university’s alumni association years after leaving office.
He said the experience nevertheless influenced his decision not to seek another term, as the hostility had become intense enough for him to worry about the safety of himself and his family.

Security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to establish a check post for abducting people and snatching vehicles along the Pakistan Highway near Kalat, rescuing 23 abductees and killing five terrorists, the military’s media wing said on Sunday.
According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the operation was conducted during the night of Sept 18-19, when terrorists belonging to Fitna al Hindustan attempted to disrupt the movement of people along the Chaman-Karachi N-25 highway near Kalat.
The terrorists were allegedly trying to establish a check post for abductions for ransom, extortion and vehicle snatching, the statement said.
Read: Security forces kill seven terrorists in two Balochistan operations: state media
“Security Forces responded immediately, and after intense fire exchange, five terrorists belonging to Indian-sponsored proxy of Fitna al-Hindustan were sent to hell due to effective response by Armed Forces,” the ISPR said.
The federal government last year officially designated all terrorist groups operating in Balochistan as Fitna al-Hindustan, accusing India of sponsoring a proxy war through the outfits.
Security forces also recovered 23 abductees from the terrorists’ hideout, along with six trucks, three buses and two cars.
A large quantity of weapons, ammunition and explosives was also recovered from the hideout, according to the statement.
The ISPR said the successful operation had thwarted the “nefarious designs” of the Indian-sponsored proxy of Fitna al-Hindustan.
“Sanitisation operations are continuing in the surrounding areas to eliminate any remaining terrorists and ensure the safety and security of the local population and the vital National Highways,” it said.
The military’s media wing said the counter-terrorism campaign under the vision of “Azm-e-Istehkam”, approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, would continue “with full resolve”.
Read More: Security forces kill three terrorists during IBO in Balochistan's Awaran: state media
“Security Forces and Law Enforcement Agencies remain committed to eliminating the menace of foreign-sponsored and foreign-supported terrorism from the country,” the statement said.
Terrorism is a growing problem for Pakistan, with the number of attacks rising every year since 2022, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), a global monitoring organisation. Data from ACLED shows attacks in Pakistan rose nearly fourfold to 2,425 in 2025 from 658 in 2022.
Although Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) has borne the brunt of terrorism, Balochistan has also remained a major target of Indian proxies, which often target civilians and military installations in the province.
In one such attack on the last day of 2025, terrorists targeted innocent civilians in Balochistan’s Gwadar and Kharan districts, where 18 people, including women, children, the elderly and labourers, embraced martyrdom.
On August 21, security forces, in coordination with police, killed 49 terrorists in a series of IBOs across K-P and Balochistan over several days.
Earlier this week, security forces killed seven terrorists in Balochistan; six more were killed near Kalat.
A few days ago, security forces killed three terrorists during an IBO in the Badrang area of Awaran district, according to security sources. The operation was conducted under Operation Radd-ul-Fitna 3 against terrorists affiliated with Fitna al-Hindustan, with weapons and ammunition recovered from those killed.

Another user, @Monday357745, commented: “They will be fighting in public, yet they dine and wine with each other in private. Life of politicians.”

Another X user, @Coal004, criticised the gathering, writing: “See how comfortable they are. Omo, we are not even trying. These people just get too much audacity…”
Meanwhile, @ohamadike22140 focused on the apparent freedom of movement of the Nigerians at the gathering, writing: “No soldier or police with heavy arms sighted, they are all freely enjoying themselves, moving around with no single bodyguard in another man’s working country. Nigerians .”

items.title: Houthis threaten ‘decisive’ response if Pakistan, Türkiye intervene in Yemen
items.summary:
As tensions between Yemen’s Houthi rebels and Saudi Arabia mount amid renewed attacks, the group has issued a direct warning to Pakistan and Türkiye, threatening a “decisive and painful response” if either country intervened militarily alongside Saudi Arabia in Yemen.
Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a member of Ansar Allah’s political bureau and governor of Dhamar, made the remarks during an interview with the Iraqi television programme Another Reading.
“By God, if Türkiye and Pakistan become involved, we will strike them with an iron fist,” al-Bukhaiti said, adding that the Houthis would “teach” both countries a lesson if they joined what he described as Saudi aggression against Yemen.
A senior Houthi political figure has issued an unusually direct warning to Pakistan and Türkiye, threatening a “decisive and painful response” if either country intervenes militarily alongside Saudi Arabia in Yemen.
Mohammed al-Bukhai
items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
As tensions between Yemen’s Houthi rebels and Saudi Arabia mount amid renewed attacks, the group has issued a direct warning to Pakistan and Türkiye, threatening a “decisive and painful response” if either country intervened militarily alongside Saudi Arabia in Yemen.
Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a member of Ansar Allah’s political bureau and governor of Dhamar, made the remarks during an interview with the Iraqi television programme Another Reading.
“By God, if Türkiye and Pakistan become involved, we will strike them with an iron fist,” al-Bukhaiti said, adding that the Houthis would “teach” both countries a lesson if they joined what he described as Saudi aggression against Yemen.
A senior Houthi political figure has issued an unusually direct warning to Pakistan and Türkiye, threatening a “decisive and painful response” if either country intervenes militarily alongside Saudi Arabia in Yemen.
Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, a member of Ansar Allah’s political… pic.twitter.com/ZKTW3AjjjS
— BPI News (@BPINewsOrg) September 19, 2026
The warning comes as continued Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have placed growing attention on the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Türkiye.
Al-Bukhaiti nevertheless acknowledged what he described as strong sympathy for Yemen among the Pakistani and Turkish populations, saying his warning was directed at their governments if they became militarily involved.
The Houthi warning has brought renewed focus on Pakistan’s position following the signing of the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Türkiye defence agreement earlier this year.
Signed by Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia on August 7, the pact is based on the principles of shared responsibility and regional ownership amid growing regional and global instability. It aims to promote security, peace, stability and prosperity while strengthening collective deterrence.
Under the agreement, an attack against any one of the signatory states will be considered an attack against all parties.
The pact has assumed greater significance amid the renewed attacks between the Houthis and Saudi Arabia and growing concerns over possible military involvement by its signatories.
Türkiye signals support
The Houthi warning came as Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Saudi Arabia’s territorial integrity and sovereignty had come under serious attack and that Türkiye, bound by its alliance commitments, stood in solidarity with Riyadh.
“Saudi Arabia may need military-level support. As the Makkah Alliance, we will take this up with Pakistan and can provide the necessary technical support,” Fidan said.
He said Türkiye’s Foreign Ministry had condemned attacks on oil infrastructure near Makkah and that the alliance was closely monitoring the situation.
Fidan added that any military needs would likely centre on specific technical areas.
Yemen has been gripped by war since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led Arab coalition to intervene in 2015 in support of the internationally recognised Yemeni government.
The group has been engaged in renewed fighting with government forces since July, when it declared a maritime blockade on Riyadh, and has recently claimed advances along the Red Sea coast and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
The Houthis have also targeted Saudi Arabia’s oil infrastructure, further raising concerns over oil prices in the international market.
