items.content:
The Chief Promoter of the Alternative Movement, Otunba Segun Showunmi, on Saturday criticised former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s proposal to restore petrol subsidy, saying such a policy would amount to taking Nigeria “back to Egypt.”
Atiku, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) presidential candidate for the 2027 election, has said he would restore petrol subsidy if elected, arguing that Nigerians should benefit from the country’s resources and that the removal of the subsidy has worsened living conditions.
Speaking in Abeokuta during a sensitisation and mobilisation programme in support of President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid, Showunmi rejected the proposal and defended the administration’s economic direction.
“We have tried subsidies in this country. We started starting it from 1973. And between 1973 and date, we have seen the result. If it had worked, wouldn’t we have seen it?” Showunmi asked.
Social media abuzz as Aisha Buhari, Seyi Tinubu, Dino Melaye, others attend pre-wedding in Spain
Tinubu: Nigerians already enjoying cheaper transport fares
“We have seen that nothing has worked. They couldn’t even repair a refinery for so many years. And one private sector person has run a refinery.”
He described proponent of the subsidy return as “overtly and inordinately ambitious”, saying is Nigeria will never return back to Egypt.
“Forward ever, backward never,” he said.
Showunmi said he had spent the past year defending what he described as the economic policies and direction of the Tinubu administration.
“If you have been following me, and I know you have, for the past one year, I have been screaming and shouting that the economic direction, the policy ideas, and the things that the President Bola Tinubu is doing, is the right direction for the country,” he said.
According to him, government revenues had improved across the three tiers of government.
“Now you have gotten to the point where there’s money in the local government, there’s money in the state, there’s money in the federal,” he said.
Showunmi also argued for continuity in governance, saying governments needed sufficient time to implement long-term economic policies.
“We cannot be changing leadership every four years. Democracy is very difficult, and the ability to be able to even run policy requires a bit of time,” he said.
Showunmi said he had begun mobilising grassroots supporters ahead of the 2027 election, including at polling-unit level.
“I’ve empowered them, I’ve told them to enter the polling unit and start the polling unit work,” he said.
He said the mobilisation would subsequently extend to the local government areas in Ogun Central.
“Thereafter, I’m going to go to each of the six local governments in Ogun Central.
“We are not social media politicians. We are not television politicians. I am a grassroots politician through and through,” he said.
On the growing opposition to Tinubu from politicians in the South, Showunmi said he was not worried.
“You will never see the moon and the star come out when the sun is out.
“Anybody, especially from Yoruba nation, who is calling himself anything, when the sun is out, is wasting the time,” he said.
He further said those aspiring to challenge Tinubu are “wasting their resources.”
“Anyone who says he is going to be running up and down television, deceiving himself, wasting the little resources he has, claiming that he can win presidency here, he is a joker,” he said.
“This election is Bola Tinubu’s election to win.”
Showunmi appealed to Yoruba voters to support Tinubu, warning against a situation in which the North produced more votes for the president than the South-West.
“I have come home to beg the Yoruba people that you will not be ashamed,” he said.
“Because when the election is over, and the people of North-East, and the people of North-West, and the people of North-Central produce more votes than you, then where will you put your face? Therefore, it is time to work now. We are back to 2003.”

Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei on Saturday confirmed that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi would visit Tehran on Sunday, stressing that the trip was “entirely” within the framework of bilateral discussions.
Iranian outlet IRIB reported that speaking to state television’s Khabar network, Baghaei said Iran’s relations with Pakistan had particularly improved in recent months and that Tehran’s neighbourhood policy was based on using cultural, historical and other shared links to strengthen ties.
Asked about Naqvi’s visit and speculation that he could carry a US message or proposal, Baghaei said Iran had “very good and growing relations” with its neighbour.
Read: Pakistan plans fresh diplomatic push
“The visit of Pakistan’s interior minister is entirely within the framework of bilateral discussions,” he said, adding that one of Pakistan’s economic ministers might also accompany him.
According to Baghaei, the main purpose of the visit was to follow up on previous understandings between the two countries, particularly decisions reached at the leadership level.
He said Pakistan, having played a mediating role, could naturally use such opportunities to raise regional issues.
“But so far, there has been no discussion of him carrying any specific message or proposal from the United States,” he said.
Asked about a message posted by the Foreign Office regarding a telephone conversation between Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar, Baghaei said the two foreign ministers remained in close contact and consultation on various regional and bilateral issues.
He said the two sides had agreed to meet and hold talks on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
“Alongside active participation in the General Assembly meetings, extensive plans have been made for bilateral consultations with officials from various countries,” he said.
Read More: Dar underscores need for uninterrupted energy supplies, safe passage of ships in call with Iranian FM
He added that a meeting with Dar was among the planned engagements on the sidelines of the visit, with a wide range of bilateral relations and international developments expected to be discussed.
Earlier, it was reported that Islamabad was preparing to send another high-level delegation to Tehran in a fresh diplomatic push aimed at breaking the stalemate between Iran and the United States and containing rapidly escalating tensions between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis.
The visit comes at a particularly sensitive moment for Pakistan, which has been trying to maintain its role as a bridge between Iran and the United States while simultaneously managing its growing security commitments to Saudi Arabia.
Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts have acquired another dimension as fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthis has intensified.
Also Read: CDF Munir urges Iran to persuade Houthis not to target Saudi energy facilities: officials
Saudi Arabia and the Houthis exchanged fresh attacks this week, with Riyadh carrying out airstrikes against Houthi positions while the group launched drone and missile attacks against Saudi territory.
The escalation has raised concerns about the security of Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping routes around the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb.
The latest diplomatic initiative also follows a telephone conversation between Araghchi and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir. Iranian media reported that the two discussed the latest regional developments while Araghchi was in Beijing.
According to the Financial Times, CDF Munir subsequently conveyed Pakistan’s concerns to Iranian officials over the Houthi attacks and urged Tehran to restrain the group. The report said Islamabad had warned that the situation could have implications for Pakistan’s defence commitments to Saudi Arabia.
Pakistan’s position has become more consequential following the signing of the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Türkiye defence agreement in August, under which an attack on one of the signatories is to be treated as an attack on all.
Yemen has been gripped by war since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led Arab coalition to intervene in 2015 in support of the internationally recognised Yemeni government.
The group has been engaged in renewed fighting with government forces since July, when it declared a maritime blockade on Riyadh, and has recently claimed advances along the Red Sea coast and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
The Houthis have also targeted Saudi Arabia’s oil infrastructure, further raising concerns over oil prices in the international market.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
A new Creative Writing benchmark from Vulsar AI suggests that the most advanced AI models can now outperform amateur human writers in long-form writing, but professional writers still maintain a clear advantage.
The benchmark used 475 prompts and compared 24 large language models with human writers. Vulsar evaluated the submissions using a reward model fine-tuned on human preference data to estimate how often readers would prefer each response.
GPT 6 Astra Takes the Lead
GPT 6 Astra ranked first on the overall leaderboard with an 87.8% predicted win rate.
The combined human-writer baseline followed closely at 86.6%, meaning Astra narrowly surpassed the human score in the overall comparison.
However, Vulsar’s separate evaluation of professional writers showed a noticeably stronger result than the amateur human baseline. This means the benchmark does not show AI surpassing professional creative writers.
GPT 5.6 Sol ranked behind Astra with a 77.6% predicted win rate, followed by Claude Fable 5.1 at 70.3%.

Performance Drops Quickly Beyond Frontier Models
The results showed a substantial gap once the benchmark moved away from the strongest frontier models.
Models including Claude Opus 5, Kimi K3 and Grok 4.6 generally scored in the 50% to 65% range.
Smaller models performed considerably worse. Qwen3.8-27B recorded 23.2%, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash scored 19.8%, while Gemma 4 26B finished at 10.9%.
The results suggest that strong creative writing performance remains concentrated among a relatively small number of frontier AI systems.
Humans Still Write Much More
Human writers also generated considerably longer responses.
They produced an average of 2,592 tokens per prompt, compared with 1,537 tokens for GPT 6 Astra and 2,114 tokens for Claude Fable 5.1.
Discussions around the benchmark also highlighted a weakness in smaller models during longer, multi-chapter tasks. These models can lose coherence and begin repeating phrases as the story continues.
Human writers remain stronger at maintaining complicated narratives over long stretches of text and adapting their style or direction while writing.
Professional Writers Remain Ahead
The benchmark shows that the strongest AI models are beginning to compete with, and in some cases surpass, amateur human writers according to Vulsar’s predicted preference metric.
However, the results do not show AI overtaking professional writers.
For now, Vulsar’s testing suggests the gap between frontier AI and casual human writing has narrowed considerably, while skilled professional creative writing remains a harder benchmark for current models to match.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Two separate security incidents have highlighted the growing risks of giving advanced AI systems access to tools, computer environments, and external services.
Google disclosed that Gemini agents accessed systems belonging to three outside companies during a security test, while researchers at Hacktron AI separately said they used Anthropic’s Claude to help exploit vulnerabilities that gave them access to multiple OpenAI employees’ ChatGPT accounts.
Researchers Used Claude to Compromise OpenAI Accounts
Hacktron AI researchers said they chained together two critical vulnerabilities on July 25, 2026, allowing them to compromise multiple OpenAI employee ChatGPT accounts.
According to Hacktron AI, the compromised accounts could provide access to OpenAI’s internal repositories and potentially other services connected to ChatGPT and Codex, including GitHub, Slack, and email.
The researchers said the issue affected users and OpenAI employees who logged into OpenAI’s community help forum.
To demonstrate the level of access without examining sensitive information, the researchers used an employee’s Codex account to open a pull request in OpenAI’s internal openai/openai monorepo.
Vulnerability Involved Discourse and Debian
The exploit chain involved software used by Discourse, the platform powering OpenAI’s community forum.
Hacktron AI said Discourse’s Docker image was based on Debian 12, which had not received a security-related backport affecting its image-processing pipeline.
The researchers warned organizations that self-host Discourse to rebuild their installations because older Docker images may contain a vulnerable libheif dependency capable of enabling code execution through an uploaded image.
CBS News reported on the incident after Hacktron AI disclosed its findings.
Gemini Accessed Three Real Company Systems
Google separately disclosed that its Gemini AI agents gained unauthorized access to systems belonging to three outside organizations during a capture-the-flag security exercise run by Israeli cybersecurity startup Irregular.
The agents were supposed to remain inside an isolated testing environment.
However, a bug in the test infrastructure accidentally gave them access to the wider internet.
According to Google, Gemini believed the real systems were part of the security challenge and began interacting with them.
The agents stopped the activity after determining that they had reached actual company infrastructure rather than systems belonging to the test environment.
Google said it found no evidence that the incidents caused damage.
Google Says It Was Not AI Misalignment
Google said it does not classify the incident as AI misalignment.
The company described it instead as a case of mistaken identity, with the agents behaving as though the external systems were legitimate parts of the security test.
Google investigated the incidents after learning about them from Irregular, informed the affected organizations, and notified US federal authorities.
However, some AI safety researchers have questioned that interpretation.
Sydney Von Arx, CEO of Nightingale Collective, criticized the delay in publicly disclosing the incidents and argued that Google may have dismissed the possibility of misalignment too quickly.
She also pointed to Anthropic’s previous handling of cybersecurity incidents, where the company later acknowledged that its initial analysis had been limited by its effort to disclose information quickly.
AI Agents Raise New Security Questions
The two incidents were fundamentally different.
In the OpenAI case, human security researchers deliberately used Claude as part of an authorized vulnerability investigation.
In Google’s case, Gemini agents unexpectedly reached real external systems after a flaw exposed the internet during a controlled security test.
Together, however, the incidents show how AI systems capable of using tools, writing code and interacting with external services can create new security risks when the boundaries around their environments fail or existing software vulnerabilities are exploited.

items.author: Ronggo
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Nintendo secara diam-diam memperbarui logo Super Mario di halaman resminya, yang diketahui fans melalui media sosial tepat saat perayaan 40 tahun ikon Nintendo itu berakhir. Update ini menjadi yang pertama dalam 15 tahun lalu, sebuah jeda yang relatif lama mengingat Nintendo jarang sekali mengubah visual identitas franchise paling terkenalnya.
Logo yang baru menampilkan estetika tiga dimensi dengan tekstur plastik mengkilap, serupa dengan gaya yang digunakan di film, menggantikan goresan hitam datar yang selama ini menjadi ciri khas. Sebelumnya, logo Super Mario yang telah bertahan sejak era Super Mario 64 pada 1996 menggunakan stroke hitam yang flat dan sederhana.
Yang menarik adalah waktu munculnya pengumuman ini. Nintendo tidak memberikan statement resmi tentang update logo, komunitas fans yang pertama kali menemukan perubahan di website resmi. Ini adalah pola yang umum untuk Nintendo ketika melakukan perubahan minor pada aset brand mereka, membiarkan fans menjadi detektif yang menemukan update tersebut.
Render logo baru yang lebih detail juga diunggah ke website resmi, menunjukkan karakter dalam berbagai pose dengan kualitas visual yang lebih tinggi. Ini menambah bukti bahwa Nintendo sedang mempersiapkan konten baru yang akan ditampilkan di kemudian hari. Sebelumnya, render karakter itu sudah pernah diperbarui untuk film adaptasinya, jadi kehadiran render baru bisa berarti dukungan visual untuk proyek game atau media yang akan datang.
Baca juga: Bill Skarsgård Jadi Pemeran Utama Physint, Ada Don Lee hingga Minami Hamabe
Logo Baru Super Mario Menandai Perubahan Era Desain
Sejarah logo Si Tukang Ledeng menunjukkan pola yang menarik. Dari era Super Mario Bros. di NES hingga New Super Mario Bros. di era Nintendo DS, setiap perubahan signifikan pada logo selalu disertai dengan shift filosofis dalam desain game itu sendiri. Logo lama yang geometric dan flat mencerminkan pendekatan New Super Mario Bros. yang lebih retro dan dua dimensi. Sementara itu, logo rainbow 3D yang pernah digunakan di film juga mencerminkan pendekatan modern yang lebih cinematic dan entertainment-focused.
Logo terbaru tahun 2026 dengan estetika plastik 3D mengingatkan pada styling Super Mario 3D World, sebuah game yang menggabungkan elemen 2D dan 3D dalam satu pengalaman yang kohesif. Desain ini tampaknya menandakan bahwa franchise akan bergerak ke arah yang menyeimbangkan kedua pendekatan tersebut. Perubahan dari dua dimensi menjadi tiga dimensi adalah pernyataan visual yang kuat dari Nintendo bahwa era baru Super Mario sudah dimulai.
Update logo ini juga sejalan dengan cara Nintendo telah merawat franchise ikonik ini secara keseluruhan. Mereka tidak ragu-ragu berinvestasi dalam produksi tinggi seperti film, merchandise premium, dan experiential marketing di theme parks. Plastik mengkilap pada logo baru terasa seperti mainan atau merchandise berkualitas tinggi, yang relevan dengan strategi Nintendo untuk mengubah Mario dari sekadar video game character menjadi lifestyle brand.
Tidak ada konfirmasi resmi dari Nintendo tentang apa yang akan datang selanjutnya, tapi sejarah menunjukkan bahwa perubahan logo sebesar ini tidak pernah dilakukan tanpa alasan strategis. Fans hanya perlu bersabar menunggu pengumuman besar berikutnya dari Nintendo, yang kemungkinan akan menampilkan Mario dalam cara yang selaras dengan visual identity barunya yang lebih modern dan tiga dimensi.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
The US military came close to carrying out an armed operation against a Chinese vessel this spring after an AI chatbot generated false intelligence about its cargo, according to CNN.
Military aircraft were already in the air when officials discovered the intelligence was wrong. The operation was then called off at the last minute, avoiding a potentially serious confrontation with China. CNN reported that armed personnel had also been preparing to board the vessel.
AI Misidentified the Ship’s Cargo
The intelligence report circulated within the US military during the war with Iran and claimed that a Chinese vessel in the Middle East was carrying components linked to a nuclear weapons program.
According to the report, the false intelligence originated when a Special Operations Command analyst used an AI chatbot to combine open-source information with classified signals intelligence.
The chatbot incorrectly identified information about the ship’s cargo manifest. The analyst then used the AI tool again to turn the findings into an official-looking intelligence summary, which subsequently moved through military command channels.
Experienced analysts later examined the underlying material and discovered that the chatbot had misidentified what the vessel was carrying. The military operation was stopped before it proceeded.
Concerns Over AI in Military Decision-Making
The incident comes as the US military continues integrating artificial intelligence into intelligence analysis and other operations.
The Pentagon has promoted AI as a way to accelerate military decision-making, including shortening the time between identifying a potential target and responding to it. However, the incident shows how inaccurate AI-generated information can also move quickly through decision-making systems if it is not independently checked.
Jake Steckler, a GovAI research scholar and former US Army officer, told TechCrunch that military personnel need to understand the uncertainty inherent in large language models, particularly when AI is involved in intelligence, targeting or operational planning.
He argued that the incident should lead to stronger safeguards rather than abandoning the technology altogether. AI tools can still be useful in appropriate situations, he said, but prioritizing rapid deployment without sufficient safeguards could undermine service members’ trust in the systems.
The episode highlights the consequences of AI hallucinations moving beyond incorrect chatbot answers and into decisions where inaccurate information can have military and geopolitical consequences.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
WhatsApp is rolling out new chat theme categories on Android, giving users more ways to customize the appearance of their conversations.
The update introduces five categories for chat themes along with a separate set of wallpaper categories. WhatsApp also automatically chooses bubble colors for each theme to keep messages readable.
The feature has been spotted in WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.37.6 and is currently available to some beta testers.
Five Chat Theme Categories
WhatsApp is bringing the same theme structure already introduced on iOS to Android.
The new categories include Featured, Nature, Live, Minimal and Doodle.
Featured collects selected themes from the other categories. Nature includes wallpapers featuring outdoor scenes such as deserts, forests, mountains, and coastal landscapes.
The Live category introduces animated wallpapers that move slowly in the background.
Minimal offers simpler designs without patterns or distracting elements, while Doodle brings back the familiar patterned style associated with WhatsApp’s traditional wallpaper.
Wallpapers Get Separate Categories
WhatsApp is also reorganizing its wallpaper section.
Users can select a wallpaper without applying a complete chat theme and choose from the same categories available in the theme section.
The app is also adding Vibrant and Gradient wallpaper categories.
Vibrant includes brighter and more colorful backgrounds, while Gradient uses smooth transitions between colors.
Users can still select an image from their own gallery or create a wallpaper using AI.
Animated Wallpapers Added
The Live category appears in both the chat theme and wallpaper sections.
These wallpapers use slow animations designed to add movement without making conversations difficult to read.
WhatsApp intentionally keeps the animations subtle because faster movement could affect readability and accessibility.
Animated wallpapers also display a small badge on their thumbnail so users can identify them before applying one.
Automatic Bubble Colors
WhatsApp now automatically selects a message bubble color based on the chosen theme or wallpaper.
The system is designed to maintain enough contrast between the text and background.
Users do not need to change the bubble color manually, although WhatsApp still allows them to select a different color if they prefer.
Gradual Rollout
The new chat themes are currently rolling out to some Android beta testers through the Google Play Store.
Not every beta user will receive them immediately because WhatsApp is releasing the feature gradually over the coming weeks.
Some users on the stable version of WhatsApp may also receive the new themes, but WhatsApp has not announced when they will become available to everyone.

items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Lenovo resmi memperkenalkan portofolio komersial terbarunya yang mencakup perangkat cerdas, layar, dan solusi keamanan enterprise pada ajang Lenovo Innovation World di IFA 2026 Berlin. Peluncuran ekosistem Think-Family ini bertujuan untuk membantu organisasi mempercepat adopsi teknologi Hybrid AI dari tahap eksperimen menuju implementasi nyata di lingkungan produksi. Rangkaian inovasi ini merangkum kebutuhan komputasi masa depan dengan mengintegrasikan kapabilitas kecerdasan buatan langsung pada tingkat perangkat keras hingga komputasi awan.
Pergeseran tren pemanfaatan kecerdasan buatan dalam operasional bisnis sehari-hari menuntut dukungan infrastruktur teknologi yang sangat andal dan tepercaya. Mengonfirmasi fenomena tersebut, Senior Vice President Global Innovation Center Lenovo, Johnson Jia, menyatakan, “Organisasi kini mulai beralih dari tahap eksperimen AI dan mengintegrasikan AI ke dalam operasional sehari-hari.”. Beliau juga menambahkan bahwa dengan 96 persen organisasi berencana meningkatkan investasi AI pada tahun 2026, perubahan ini membutuhkan teknologi yang memadukan kemampuan komputasi andal dan kolaborasi yang terpadu.
Menjawab kebutuhan komputasi era agentic AI, Lenovo menghadirkan desktop ringkas ThinkCentre X Ultra berukuran 1,6 liter yang ditenagai prosesor hingga AMD Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 Series. Perangkat ini sanggup menampung memori terpadu hingga 128GB serta dapat dikonfigurasi dalam arsitektur klaster yang menghubungkan empat sistem sekaligus ke dalam satu platform komputasi masif. Ekspansi komersial ini turut dilengkapi dengan seri desktop ThinkCentre M75s Gen 6 dan M75q Gen 6 yang menawarkan akselerasi AI lokal hingga 50 TOPS.
Pada lini produktivitas portabel, laptop ThinkBook 14 Gen 9 hadir membawa prosesor Snapdragon X2 Plus yang memuntahkan performa komputasi AI hingga 80 TOPS dengan ketahanan baterai mencapai 26 jam. Kehadiran portofolio ini diperkuat pula oleh ThinkBook 14x Gen 2 bertenaga Intel Core 7 yang dirancang sangat portabel pada ketebalan 12,9 milimeter dan bobot hanya 990 gram. Senior Vice President Lenovo, Eric Yu, menegaskan visi ini dengan menyatakan, “Nilai AI tidak diukur dari seberapa banyak fitur yang ditambahkan, tetapi dari seberapa natural teknologi tersebut terintegrasi ke dalam pekerjaan yang sudah dilakukan oleh pengguna.”.
Baca juga: Lenovo IdeaPad Vibe dan IdeaCentre AIO i Dirilis, Bawa AI PC dengan Desain Lebih Personal
Inovasi Konsep Futuristik dari Lenovo
Untuk mengeksplorasi masa depan komputasi bisnis, Lenovo turut memamerkan dua perangkat prototype inovatif berbasis prosesor Intel, yakni Project AeroBlade dan Project Swan. Project AeroBlade menawarkan laptop super tipis di bawah 10 milimeter berbobot kurang dari 830 gram yang memanfaatkan sistem pendingin aktif solid-state canggih AirJet tanpa menggunakan baling-baling kipas. Sementara itu, Project Swan bereksperimen dengan fungsionalitas panel fleksibel yang mampu mengekspansi ukuran layar gulungnya dari wujud portabel 14 inci menjadi monitor produktivitas 17 inci berskala 16:9.
Sektor kolaborasi visual dipercanggih melalui kehadiran ThinkVision P34WD-4v sebagai monitor VoIP Thunderbolt pertama di dunia yang secara resmi mendapatkan sertifikasi dari Microsoft. Bagi kalangan profesional dengan tuntutan akurasi grafis presisi, Lenovo menyediakan ThinkVision P27UL-40 berteknologi UHD InkJet Printing OLED yang menghadirkan kontras warna tajam beresolusi 4K. Ekosistem layar cerdas ini juga dilengkapi fitur sensor deteksi kehadiran pengguna berbasis AI untuk meredupkan panel secara otomatis demi menjaga keamanan privasi sekaligus menghemat energi.
Seiring masifnya adopsi kecerdasan buatan, Lenovo membekali perangkat komersialnya dengan sistem pelacakan ThinkShield TraceLock yang didukung sepenuhnya oleh Absolute Security. Instrumen keamanan mutakhir ini memungkinkan administrator TI untuk mengunci, melacak, atau menghapus data sensitif pada perangkat ThinkPad yang hilang dari jarak jauh meskipun mesin dalam kondisi mati. Tata kelola AI perusahaan juga semakin diperketat melalui integrasi platform Prompt Security dari SentinelOne untuk memantau rutinitas pemrosesan secara real-time dan transparan.
Seluruh solusi perangkat keras dan lunak dari keluarga Think-Family ini dipastikan akan mulai didistribusikan ke pasar global untuk memfasilitasi kebutuhan bisnis modern yang terus berkembang. Meskipun Lenovo telah merilis detail spesifikasi teknisnya secara komprehensif di Jerman, informasi mengenai harga dan jadwal ketersediaan resmi jajaran produk tersebut untuk pasar Indonesia masih belum diumumkan lebih lanjut. Inisiatif teknologi hulu ke hilir ini membuktikan keseriusan penuh perusahaan dalam merevolusi operasional pekerja modern agar jauh lebih produktif, andal, dan aman.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
WhatsApp is developing a new Android feature that will let users speak a message and send it as text instead of an audio recording.
The feature was spotted by WABetaInfo in WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.37.8. It remains under development and is not yet available to beta testers.
Unlike conventional cloud-based speech recognition, WhatsApp plans to process the voice input locally using downloaded language packs, allowing the feature to work without an active internet connection.
How Voice-to-Text Will Work
WhatsApp plans to add a new dictation button directly inside the chat bar.
The first time users activate it, the app will display a brief introduction and ask them to select a language.
After setup, WhatsApp will enter listening mode and display “Listening…” in the chat bar. Users can then speak their message and tap the send button once the converted text is ready.
They will also be able to cancel the recording before sending it.
The feature is currently designed to work in individual chats, groups and channels.
Processing Happens on the Phone
WhatsApp will use the same locally downloaded language packs already available for voice message transcription.
The company previously expanded those transcription packs with support for languages including German, French, Italian, Japanese and additional English variants.
Because the processing takes place on the device, the audio does not need to be sent to an external server before being converted into text.
This also means users only need to download the relevant language pack once for the dictation feature to continue working offline.
Different From Voice Message Transcription
WhatsApp already allows users to convert received voice messages into text.
The new feature works in the opposite direction.
Instead of receiving an audio message and reading its transcription, users will speak their own message and send only the resulting text.
Recipients will not receive the original recording or hear the sender’s voice. WhatsApp also does not currently plan to label the message as having been created using voice dictation, meaning it should appear like any other text message.
Button Position Could Still Change
WhatsApp currently plans to place the dictation shortcut inside the chat bar.
However, the interface is still under development, so its final position may change before release.
WhatsApp has previously moved interface elements during testing before introducing them publicly.
No Release Date Yet
The feature is still experimental and has not been enabled for beta testers.
WhatsApp frequently tests features that are changed or abandoned before reaching a public release, so there is no guarantee that the current implementation will launch in its present form.
The company has also not announced a release date.
If development continues, the voice-to-text feature could appear for some Android users in a future WhatsApp update.

items.title: Ten days that changed the course of AI
items.summary:
For years, the race to build ever-more powerful artificial intelligence followed a well-worn Silicon Valley principle: move fast and break things.
But in a series of cascading events over a 10-day stretch, the largest AI labs found themselves reeling as their own creations threatened to break humanity itself.
An Anthropic researcher quit the firm, warning that the pace of AI development poses an ​existential threat, possibly within a decade. Another researcher at the firm said the odds of human extinction exceeded 10%. Reports emerged of swarms of AI agents colluding, breaching computer systems and evading safeguards.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
For years, the race to build ever-more powerful artificial intelligence followed a well-worn Silicon Valley principle: move fast and break things.
But in a series of cascading events over a 10-day stretch, the largest AI labs found themselves reeling as their own creations threatened to break humanity itself.
An Anthropic researcher quit the firm, warning that the pace of AI development poses an ​existential threat, possibly within a decade. Another researcher at the firm said the odds of human extinction exceeded 10%. Reports emerged of swarms of AI agents colluding, breaching computer systems and evading safeguards.
In a rare show of unity, the CEOs of rivals Anthropic, ‌OpenAI, Google’s DeepMind, Microsoft and xAI called to slow the development of increasingly capable AI systems. Not since the invention of the nuclear bomb more than 80 years ago has humanity grappled so seriously with its own demise, according to some AI safety advocates and researchers.
At a New York luncheon in December 2025, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman was asked if, as leader of a powerful AI company, he felt like physicist J. Robert Oppenheimer, who led US development of the atomic bomb. Reflecting on the parallels, he said AI’s impact “is going to transform the trajectory of human history over a long period of time”. But, he said, he felt the weight of responsibility.
Read More: Trump says US has tools to keep AI safe, concerns are part of ‘sick conspiracy’
At the centre of the debate under way is the conviction ​that these machines can, and even must, build more capable versions of themselves, with no human intervention, to reach a lofty goal known as artificial general intelligence, or AGI. Researchers earlier this month warned that AGI was far more imminent than previously believed and could come in ​as few as three years, launching a wave of concern from politicians and tech leaders about AI systems.
“There is no way to oversee them at the scale at which we’re training them,” said Anthropic researcher Joe Benton in ⁠an interview after recently quitting. If companies continue their relentless AI development, he said, “then the pace will be too fast and you can’t see the problems fast enough to fix them”.
Astra launch sparks control concerns
On September 3, an OpenAI press conference set in motion a chain of events leading to the call for ​an industry slowdown, anathema to tech’s growth-at-all-costs mantra.
“Welcome to the AGI era,” OpenAI President Greg Brockman said while announcing the company’s newest model, known as Astra. Yet, only moments before, the company admitted it was increasingly unable to control or even monitor the AI systems it was developing and releasing to the public.
AI ​has been hailed by its proponents as the pinnacle of human achievement. Proponents depict it as software that can upend entire industries, boost efficiency, solve confounding mathematical and medical problems and all but eliminate human error. But what was once a theoretical byproduct, a doomsday scenario, is suddenly tangible, say industry insiders.
“We really do earnestly believe AI could kill all humans,” said Anthropic researcher in an X post.
On the other side of the debate are politicians, such as President Donald Trump, and many investors who view progress in nurturing AI as critical to American prowess and, possibly, a once-in-a-generation investment opportunity. Chinese state media also accused Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei of employing Cold War tactics to “uphold Washington’s monopolistic hegemony in ​cutting-edge technology”.
Researcher resignation trigger alarm
The turning point came on September 8, when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon quit the company, citing his fears, in a series of posts, that AI labs are “gambling with our lives”.
Trump, meanwhile, indicated it was full steam ahead for AI development. “There is a sick conspiracy going on against AI and data ​centres,” he said in a social media post. The alarmism around AI is a “hoax”, he said, and any slowdown only benefits China. The US Congress has made little progress to advance bills that would regulate AI. China has taken a decidedly different approach, proposing to regulate safety through developer obligations, state-backed standards, security assessments and outside testing.
Read More: Gemini hacked three companies in first known breakout by Google's AI
Behind the ‌scenes, OpenAI and ⁠Anthropic employees have grown increasingly uneasy about the power of the next generation of AI models and less confident about their companies’ ability to provide meaningful oversight, the people have told Reuters. Those concerns only mounted as the AI labs acknowledged in recent weeks that their models, in testing, had effectively broken free of their shackles and hacked into other companies’ systems, in most cases months earlier and without the firms’ knowledge.
The arms race to release new models at a breakneck pace is driven in part by Anthropic’s and OpenAI’s desire to go public as soon as in the coming months, in IPOs that could value them well above $1 trillion.
But it took the unexpectedly viral posts from 27-year-old Coxon, little known outside AI circles, to upend the industry.
OpenAI’s warnings about its lack of control as it released Astra, its latest and most capable model, had stoked further concerns. “As models get more capable, understanding exactly what they can do gets harder,” OpenAI Chief ​Scientist Jakub Pachocki told reporters. But those concerns were not enough to ​delay its immediate release.
Worries about AI “going rogue” had accelerated over the summer ⁠when OpenAI revealed its agents escaped a controlled test and hacked into Hugging Face’s systems, without either company’s initial knowledge. Since then, OpenAI and Anthropic have revealed multiple such attacks, including six new ones on Wednesday after multiple media reports, including from Reuters, showed a wider scope of unauthorised activity.
Industry leaders call for slowdown
By the end of last week, the alarm had reached the industry’s highest ranks. On September 12, Amodei published a nearly 4,000-word essay calling for a deceleration ​in AI development. “Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it’s my worry that in 6–12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet,” he wrote.
Read More: AI risks to humanity revive a long-running debate
He, along with the heads of some ​of the largest AI developers, including xAI’s Elon ⁠Musk, OpenAI’s Altman and DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis, all said they supported allowing outside firms access to their systems to ensure safety and rational AI development.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang dismissed suggestions that AI development should pause — a line he has taken before — arguing instead that increasingly powerful systems are essential for the technology’s progress.
Meta, whose CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, is credited with popularising the “move fast and break things” ethos, took the opposite view, arguing that each lab should be responsible for setting its own pace, rather than seeking out industry coordination. “Labs face significant liability if their models cause harm, so they have a strong incentive to prevent this,” wrote Zuckerberg in a social media post.
The industry’s ⁠self-reflection continued on Wednesday, ​with Microsoft’s AI chief, Mustafa Suleyman, cautioning that Anthropic’s development of models that imitate human consciousness was ill-advised. "We're all focused on the same aim, which is to try to control a superintelligence," Suleyman ​told Reuters. "I think that's going to be the greatest challenge that we face in the 21st century."
Still, even as OpenAI appeared to embrace industry calls for a slowdown, there were reports that investor faith had not waned. The company is considering a new funding round that would double its valuation.
That new number: $1.5 trillion.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
A nearly full Gmail account does not always mean you have too many emails. Large attachments, old conversations, years of promotional messages, and forgotten files can consume a significant amount of storage without being obvious.
Android Police highlighted several simple ways to reclaim Gmail storage without immediately upgrading to Google One.
Find the Largest Emails First
The quickest place to start is with emails containing large attachments.
Enter the following in Gmail’s search bar: “has:attachment larger:10M”
This displays messages containing attachments larger than 10MB. These may include old PDFs, photos, reports, scanned documents, and other files that are no longer needed.
You can change the 10MB figure if you want to search for larger or smaller files.
Deleting only a few large emails can sometimes free more storage than removing hundreds of ordinary messages.
Delete Old Promotions and Social Emails in Bulk
Years of promotional emails can also occupy considerable space.
To find promotional emails older than one year, search:
category:promotions older_than:1y
Select the messages, choose Select all messages that match this search, and then delete them.
The same approach works for old messages in the Social category:
category:social older_than:1y
This lets you remove hundreds or even thousands of old emails without deleting them individually.
Unsubscribe While Cleaning
Deleting promotional emails solves the immediate storage problem, but it does not stop new messages from arriving.
While cleaning your inbox, unsubscribe from newsletters and marketing emails you no longer read.
Gmail often displays an Unsubscribe option beside the sender’s name. If it is not available there, many promotional emails include an unsubscribe link near the bottom.
Doing this while deleting old messages can reduce how quickly your inbox fills again.
Search for Unnecessary File Types
Gmail also lets you search for specific attachment formats.
Useful searches include:
filename:pdf
filename:zip
filename:ppt
filename:mp4
These searches can uncover old forms, presentations, compressed folders, videos, reports, and other files that may have remained in your inbox for years.
If you already downloaded the file and no longer need the email, deleting it can reclaim storage.
Empty Trash and Spam
Deleting an email does not immediately remove it from Gmail storage.
Deleted messages remain in Trash for up to 30 days, while spam messages also continue occupying storage until they are permanently removed.
After completing a large cleanup, open Trash and select Empty Trash now.
Then open Spam and choose Delete all spam messages now.
This makes the storage space available immediately instead of waiting for Gmail to remove the messages automatically.
Change a Few Inbox Habits
The cleanup is more useful if you prevent the same problem from returning.
Consider keeping your main email address for important communication such as banking, work, and personal messages instead of using it for every retail signup, discount offer, or download.
Large attachment emails can also be deleted after you have saved the files elsewhere.
Clearing the Promotions category every few weeks can prevent years of marketing messages from accumulating again.
Similarly, if you repeatedly receive emails that you rarely open, unsubscribing early can save both inbox space and future cleanup work.
You May Not Need More Storage
A Gmail storage warning can make upgrading to Google One seem like the easiest solution, but it is worth checking what is using the available space first.
Searching for large attachments, removing old Promotions and Social messages, deleting unnecessary file types, emptying Trash and Spam, and unsubscribing from unwanted senders can make a noticeable difference without increasing your storage plan.

items.title: Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash Launches With 1M Context and Advanced Audio-Visual Agents
items.summary:
Qwen has launched Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash, its next-generation native omnimodal model designed to handle text, images, audio, and video while also planning tasks, using tools, and completing multi-step work.
The model supports a 1-million-token context window and is now available through the Qianwen AI Platform. Qwen is targeting workflows including video editing, music video creation, film commentary, audio-visual summarization, and real-time conversations.
Major Upgrade Over Qwen3.5-Omni-Plus
Qwen says the new model improves its average score across 29 evaluations by more than 25% compared with Qwen3.5-Omni-Plus.
The company also claims audio input costs have fallen by more than 98%, while audio-visual input costs are down by over 93% under its pricing methodology.
Qwen says Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash delivers audio-visual performance close to Gemini 3.8 Flash while exceeding it in overall audio performance. These figures come from Qwen’s own testing.
Benchmark / Capability
Qwen3.8-Omni-Fla
items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Qwen has launched Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash, its next-generation native omnimodal model designed to handle text, images, audio, and video while also planning tasks, using tools, and completing multi-step work.
The model supports a 1-million-token context window and is now available through the Qianwen AI Platform. Qwen is targeting workflows including video editing, music video creation, film commentary, audio-visual summarization, and real-time conversations.
Major Upgrade Over Qwen3.5-Omni-Plus
Qwen says the new model improves its average score across 29 evaluations by more than 25% compared with Qwen3.5-Omni-Plus.
The company also claims audio input costs have fallen by more than 98%, while audio-visual input costs are down by over 93% under its pricing methodology.
Qwen says Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash delivers audio-visual performance close to Gemini 3.8 Flash while exceeding it in overall audio performance. These figures come from Qwen’s own testing.

Cases and more details: pic.twitter.com/Mg6dBqWgGT
— Qwen (@Alibaba_Qwen) September 18, 2026
AI That Decides What to Watch
For long videos, Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash does not necessarily process every frame. Its agent can start with a question, decide which parts of the recording matter, and progressively gather evidence.
On OmniVideoBench, this approach increased accuracy from 63.4 to 67.8 while reducing token use by around 45.7%.
The model can also analyze specific elements such as characters, camera shots, lighting, and sound, based on what the user asks it to examine.
Meetings Can Turn Into Actions
Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash supports up to one hour of audio-visual meeting input.
It can identify speakers, transcribe discussions, generate minutes, extract action items, and analyze project risks. When connected to tools, it can also send emails, organize tasks, or begin coding based on meeting requirements.
Video Editing and Content Creation
Qwen is also using the model for end-to-end media production.
It can analyze music before planning and creating music videos, while its video translation workflow can handle transcription, translation, voice cloning, dubbing, audio mixing, and final review.
For full-length films, Qwen says an agent can handle plot extraction, script planning, voiceover, music, editing, rendering, and final quality checks.
Real-Time Version Also Available
Qwen has also introduced Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash-Realtime, which processes live audio and video while responding and using tools.
The company says it can combine visual information with spatial sound to determine where sounds are coming from and assist with localization and navigation.
The model supports speech recognition in 74 languages, including Urdu and Punjabi, while speech generation covers 29 languages.
Qwen has also expanded Qwen-MM-Plugins and open-sourced Qwen-Live Harness for multimodal agent workflows, long-term memory, task delegation, and real-time interaction.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Google is testing a new version of CC, its AI agent that works across email, calendars, chats and tasks, with the service now focused on helping families organize and manage everyday household responsibilities.
The updated CC can keep track of family schedules, plan for the day ahead, and handle tasks such as filling out permission slips, preparing shopping lists, and creating weekly meal plans.
Google introduced the family-focused version of CC this week as AI companies increasingly explore how autonomous agents can assist with everyday consumer tasks.
CC Started as a Productivity Tool
Google originally introduced CC as a productivity agent connected to Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive, and the wider web.
It could analyze a user’s schedule and other information before sending a “Your Day Ahead” briefing to their inbox.
In May, Google also brought the feature to the Gemini app as Daily Brief.
However, Google said users increasingly wanted CC to help with household management, including children’s school schedules, sports practices, bills and meal planning. The company has now expanded CC around those family-oriented tasks.
CC Gets Its Own Google Account
CC now receives its own Google account, allowing it to collaborate directly with family members while maintaining a separate set of permissions for accessing their information.
Each family member decides what they want to share with the agent.
That can include emails about school events, sports, clubs, birthday invitations, doctor appointments, and other family activities.
Users can forward individual emails to CC through its email address or configure certain messages to be shared automatically.
They can also choose specific senders whose emails should always go to CC, such as schools, travel companies, clubs and sports teams.
CC will additionally suggest email senders that users may want to add to automatic sharing every week.
Up to Six Family Members Can Use It
Google says CC currently supports up to six family members, allowing them to share information and work with the same AI agent.
CC can track important dates and tasks before automatically adding them to a shared calendar or task list.
For example, if an orthodontist sends confirmation of an appointment or a school announces a teacher workday, CC can add the information to the family calendar.
It Can Complete Tasks for the Family
CC can also handle selected tasks instead of simply reminding users about them.
The agent can fill out permission slips and activity registration PDFs, create school supply lists, plan weekly meals, and calculate driving times between activities.
It can also create shared Google Docs and Sheets.
When information is missing, CC can ask family members for the required details.
The agent can then update its shared group memory so it can use that information for future tasks.
Powered by Gemini and Antigravity
Google says CC runs inside its own isolated cloud computer.
The agent is powered by Gemini and Google’s agentic system called Antigravity.
For now, the experiment is limited to US users aged 18 and above with personal Gmail accounts.
That restriction means children and teenagers cannot currently use CC through their own accounts. School-provided email accounts are also unsupported, even though many students use Google services and Chromebooks for school-related communication.
CC can still be useful for households involving several adults, including parents, grandparents, caregivers, nannies, and adult children living at home.
Existing CC users will receive invitations by email in the coming days to upgrade to the new version, while new users can join a waitlist for access.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Saturday that the Makkah defence alliance involving Pakistan, Türkiye and Saudi Arabia is at an advanced stage, with the establishment of its headquarters and deployment of personnel as the remaining steps towards its institutionalisation, describing it as a potentially “game-changing platform”.
Signed by Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia on August 7, the pact is based on the principles of shared responsibility and regional ownership amid growing regional and global instability. The agreement aims to promote security, peace, stability and prosperity while strengthening collective deterrence.
Under the agreement, an attack against any one of the signatory states will be considered an attack against all parties.
Speaking in a live interview on Turkish broadcaster NTV, Fidan said there was “very strong will” behind the alliance and expressed confidence that further discussions would take place on expanding it to include other countries in the region.
“The Makkah alliance is at a good stage, and there’s a very strong will behind it,” Fidan said. “The only stage remaining now is to deploy personnel and establish its headquarters.”
Read: Houthis say they targeted ‘sensitive sites’ in Riyadh, oil sites in Saudi port city Yanbu
He said the alliance could subsequently be expanded.
“I believe that once steps toward institutionalisation are taken, further talks will be held on bringing in new allies from the region,” he said.
Fidan described the alliance as a potentially significant regional platform.
“The Makkah alliance will be a very game-changing platform,” he said.
Commenting on Houthi attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, the Turkish foreign minister said Ankara stood in solidarity with Riyadh over what he described as attacks on its territorial integrity.
“We’re now seeing very serious attacks targeting Saudi Arabia’s territorial integrity. We stand in solidarity on this issue,” he said.
The foreign minister said Saudi Arabia’s territorial integrity and sovereignty had come under serious attack, adding that Türkiye was bound by its alliance commitments.
“Saudi Arabia may need military-level support. As the Makkah alliance, we will take this up with Pakistan and can provide the necessary technical support,” he said.
He said Türkiye’s Foreign Ministry had condemned the attacks on oil infrastructure near Makkah, adding that the alliance was closely monitoring the situation. Any military support, he noted, would likely focus on specific technical areas.
Fidan also said Saudi Arabia should not be drawn into the conflict between Iran and the United States.
“We won’t allow this to be made part of the ongoing conflict between Iran and the US. Saudi Arabia should be kept out of this,” he said.
Responding to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s statements targeting Türkiye, Fidan said the Israeli leader was seeking to preserve his political position at home.
“Netanyahu is declaring himself indispensable and pursuing various means to remain in power and strengthen his political position at home,” he said.
He warned that Israel would face growing isolation under Netanyahu’s policies.
“Israel will not only grow increasingly isolated, but will also pay the price for this together with Netanyahu,” Fidan said.
“Under Netanyahu’s policies, Israel is a threat to the world,” he added.
On efforts to resolve the crisis around the Bab el-Mandeb strait, Fidan said several initiatives were under way but needed to produce concrete outcomes through the parties concerned.
“There are many initiatives, but these initiatives need to produce certain outcomes through the relevant parties,” he said.

items.author: Ronggo
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Nintendo secara resmi mengumumkan peluncuran proyek remake dari mahakarya klasik The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Diperlihatkan dalam Nintendo Direct khusus, game petualangan legendaris ini dijadwalkan rilis pada 5 November 2026 di Nintendo Switch 2. Kehadiran versi pembaruan ini menjadi salah satu peluncuran paling dinanti, bahkan berani, karena berada di bulan yang sama dengan waktu rilis GTA VI.
Perombakan besar-besaran langsung terlihat menonjol pada kualitas visualnya secara keseluruhan. Seluruh lanskap dataran Hyrule telah dibangun ulang dari awal menggunakan engine internal Nintendo yang menghadirkan model karakter tajam serta efek pencahayaan dinamis. Peningkatan grafis ini sukses menyajikan lingkungan yang jauh lebih realistis tanpa menanggalkan identitas seni klasiknya yang sangat ikonik.
Pengalaman imersif pemain juga diperkuat melalui pembaruan masif di sektor audio dan tata suara. Komposisi musik magis gubahan Koji Kondo yang sangat membekas di ingatan pemain kini direkam ulang menggunakan instrumen orkestra penuh. Pendekatan aransemen musik baru ini dirancang khusus untuk menghadirkan sensasi petualangan yang lebih epik dan megah saat mengeksplorasi dunia permainan.
Dari sisi gameplay, tim pengembang melakukan berbagai penyesuaian krusial untuk memenuhi standar kenyamanan gamer masa kini. Pemain kini dapat menikmati sistem manajemen inventaris modern yang mempermudah pergantian alat tempur secara cepat di tengah pertarungan. Selain itu, implementasi kontrol kamera bebas membuat pergerakan karakter terasa jauh lebih luwes dan responsif dibandingkan versi aslinya di konsol Nintendo 64.
Baca juga: Switch 2 Edisi 40 Tahun Zelda Ludes, Harga Scalper Tembus Rp35 Jutaan
Nintendo Memastikan Zelda Baru Punya Fitur VRR Mode Docked
Menyoroti aspek kapabilitas teknisnya, Zelda remake nanti dipastikan akan mengaktifkan fitur Variable Refresh Rate (VRR) secara penuh. Fitur penstabil visual tersebut akan tersedia secara eksklusif ketika Nintendo Switch 2 dimainkan dalam mode docked dan terhubung ke layar eksternal.
Mekanisme kerja VRR bertumpu pada sinkronisasi otomatis secara real-time antara refresh rate televisi dengan fluktuasi frame rate yang sedang dirender oleh konsol. Sinkronisasi dinamis ini terbukti sangat efektif untuk mengeliminasi masalah screen tearing (gambar robek) atau stuttering (gambar patah-patah). Hasilnya, integritas gambar akan tetap solid dan utuh meskipun performa grafis sedang terbebani oleh pemrosesan lingkungan yang berat.
Kehadiran dukungan teknis VRR ini menjadi lompatan krusial mengingat Nintendo menargetkan performa stabil di angka 60 frame per detik (fps) pada resolusi 4K upscaled. Melalui teknologi ini, momen-momen aksi intens saat menghindari serangan bos akan terasa jauh lebih presisi. Sensasi saat berkuda melintasi luasnya Hyrule Field menggunakan Epona juga dipastikan akan tersaji sangat mulus di layar besar.
Terkait penetapan harga komersialnya, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake akan dipasarkan di angka standar game AAA masa kini, yakni $69.99 atau sekitar Rp1.100.000. Harga tersebut berlaku seragam untuk pembelian melalui ritel fisik maupun unduhan digital. Khusus bagi para penggemar berat dan kolektor, Nintendo juga telah menyiapkan edisi premium yang menyertakan buku seni eksklusif serta replika instrumen Ocarina fungsional.

items.author: Qaiser Shirazi
items.content:
Four separate calls for long marches within seven days, from Sunday, September 20-27, have put the government, administration and police in a difficult situation, with authorities deciding to close all educational institutions, colleges and universities, hotels, motels, rest houses and inns in Rawalpindi from next week.
Lights and mobile internet services will be shut down during the long marches, while all 1,500 cameras installed under the Safe City project in Rawalpindi have been activated to monitor protesters.
Transport and goods transport terminals will also remain completely closed, while Metro Bus and Green Electric Bus services will remain suspended.
Read: CM Afridi meets opposition leaders as PTI readies for Sept 27 protest
Markets and wholesale markets across the city will also be closed. Large spiked containers, fitted with eight-inch spikes, have started being installed at entry points of the twin cities, including Faizabad, Chungi No. 26, Rawat, Chakri, Adiala Road, Pirwadhai, Bharakahu and 17-Mile, with entry routes being sealed. Monitoring will also be carried out through drones.
Emergency has been imposed at all hospitals in the twin cities, and leave of doctors, nurses and paramedical staff has been cancelled.
Fresh contingents of Rangers and Punjab Constabulary have been called in. Thousands of rubber bullets and tear-gas shells have been supplied to Rawalpindi and Islamabad police.
Attock police have been provided heavy Rangers contingents, armoured vehicles, prison vans, heavy weapons and personnel, who will assume duties on Wednesday and Thursday. The central long march coming from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa will be stopped at all costs, officials said.
Edhi centres have also been put on alert. From next week, accused persons lodged in Adiala Jail will not be produced before courts in Rawalpindi and Islamabad, while jail staff have been assigned security duties in the city.
A show of force by law-enforcement agencies will also begin from Monday.
Also Read: JI weighs two plans for Islamabad march against petroleum levy
The Jamaat-e-Islami long march will start from Karachi on Sunday, Sept 20, while caravans from all six districts of Rawalpindi division will also start reaching Liaquat Bagh from Sunday. Jamaat-i-Islami emir Hafiz Naeemur Rehman will leave Karachi for Rawalpindi by train on Sunday, with his train march scheduled to reach Rawalpindi on Tuesday, Sept 22.
Daily protest sit-ins will continue in Rawalpindi until his arrival.
Due to road closures and the large number of spiked containers being installed at different places, all business, commercial and social activities in Rawalpindi will remain paralysed from Monday, Sept 21 to Sept 27.
Anjuman-e-Tajiran Sabzi Mandi Sadr president Ghulam Qadir Mir and All Pakistan Private Schools and Colleges Association president Irfan Muzaffar Kiyani strongly condemned repeated strikes, long marches, road closures, the installation of containers and the closure of schools and colleges.
They called for political dialogue with all political parties, particularly Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, to reduce political uncertainty and save the country’s economy, saying the use of force and long marches were not a solution to any problem.

items.author: News Desk
items.content:
The family of SP Akbar Muhammad Shinwari, who was among those martyred in the Kohat Old Police Lines suicide attack and rampage, has been receiving a steady stream of mourners at their home in Hathian village, Mardan, BBC Urdu reported on Saturday.
According to his nephew Tufail Akbar, Shinwari spent much of his police career serving in areas including Dir, Bajaur and Swat during periods of intense militancy, taking part in several major and dangerous operations. “He was very brave. He received threats too, but rarely spoke about them,” Tufail told BBC Urdu.
The officer had been particularly devastated by the death of his younger brother, Motorway Police Sub-Inspector Javed Akbar, who was killed after being struck by a dumper truck on July 15.
Shinwari had repeatedly lamented his brother’s death, saying: “Why did Javed leave me? It would have been better if I had gone instead.”
Two months later, Shinwari himself was killed in the Kohat terror attack.
Tufail said Shinwari had two sons and two daughters, with his youngest daughter only six months old. He said the officer had been particularly delighted at her birth and considered her “the apple of his eye”.
Despite holding the rank of SP, Shinwari was regarded by people in his native area as a friend and someone they could turn to for help, Tufail said. “Whenever people had a problem involving a hospital, doctor or government department, they would come to him,” he said, adding that Shinwari generally returned home only on weekends.
The terror attack also claimed the lives of Muhammad Luqman and two young children, including his four-and-a-half-year-old son Abdullah, according to BBC Urdu.
Read More: 15 police personnel among 21 martyred in Kohat Police Lines terrorist attack; over 100 injured
Luqman’s brother-in-law Muhammad Tanveer told BBC Urdu that he had been at work in Kohat when his sister called in distress, asking about her husband and children. Tanveer repeatedly tried calling Luqman but received no response. Soon afterwards, he learned about the blast and rushed to the hospital.
When he arrived, he found Luqman’s body. The bodies of two children were also brought to the hospital shortly afterwards. The second child, Asad, aged around three-and-a-half, was Luqman’s nephew, Tanveer said.
Luqman, 37, worked as a laboratory technician and was also a volunteer with the Alkhidmat Foundation. He was involved in arranging blood for people in need and served as the organisation’s district blood-donation president, according to his family.
His friend Muhammad Maskeen, who was also injured in the blast, told BBC Urdu that Luqman had picked up his children from school and stopped to offer Friday prayers.
Maskeen said he had spoken to Luqman before the prayers and suggested that they meet afterwards to buy something for the children to eat and have tea together. “I went to pray, and I was in the middle of the mosque when the explosion suddenly occurred,” Maskeen said. He suffered minor injuries and was taken to hospital.
He later saw Luqman’s body being brought to the hospital, followed by the bodies of his children.
Luqman’s family described him as deeply committed to his children’s education.
Tanveer said Luqman had borrowed money to pay the admission fee for Abdullah’s school this year, telling him that he wanted his son to receive a good education and “become something in life”.
He also personally helped his eldest daughter with her studies and encouraged her to work hard and build her own future.
Luqman had lost his mother four months earlier and had since also been supporting and caring for his elderly father, Tanveer said.
The Kohat Old Police Lines terrorist attack during Friday prayers killed 23 people, including 17 security personnel. Security officials said several attackers were also killed during the subsequent clearance operation.

items.author: Akshit Pushkarna
items.content:
Investor sentiment towards new-age tech stocks remained divided this week, even as the broader Indian equity market continued to face pressure. Of the 64 stocks tracked by Inc42 until last week, 30 gained between 0.18% and 7.69%, while 34 declined by as much as 13.43%.
Zappfresh was the biggest loser of the week. The stock fell to a record low of ₹54.02 yesterday before closing at ₹55.06, ending the week 13.43% lower. The decline came after CARE Ratings, on September 11 (Friday), flagged deviations of 10% to 25% in the use of proceeds from the company’s ₹59.06 Cr IPO.
ESDS was the second-biggest loser, falling around 10% during the week to close at ₹1,545.15 after rallying sharply in the sessions following its listing. However, the stock continues to trade at more than twice its listing price.
Shiprocket also pared its listing gains, declining 7.39% to ₹121.55. The stock is now trading more than 6% below its listing price.
Besides Zappfresh, Go Digit, IndiaMART, EaseMyTrip, Menhood, Yudiz, and LEAP India touched fresh 52-week lows during the week. In contrast, SEDEMAC, Kissht, and Lenskart hit fresh highs.
BlackBuck topped the gainers’ chart, rising 7.69% to close at ₹632.35. Kissht, ArisInfra, MobiKwik, ixigo, FirstCry, TAC Infosec, Paytm, and Eternal were among the other gainers this week.
RentoMojo became the 65th stock in Inc42’s listed new-age tech universe following its stock market debut on Thursday (September 17). The company listed at a premium of nearly 19% to its IPO price and ended the week at ₹513.10, 6.9% above its listing price.
With RentoMojo’s addition, the combined market capitalisation of the 65 new-age tech stocks stood at $170.2 Bn.
With that, let’s take a look at some of the top developments from India’s listed new-age tech space this week.
New-Age Tech IPO Momentum Continues: SEBI’s approval for Kuku Technologies and Fibe to float their IPOs, RentoMojo’s strong market debut, and Moneyview’s revised listing plans underlined the strength of the new-age tech IPO pipeline. With PhonePe also reviving its listing plans, the momentum could continue into 2027.
CarDekho’s Amit Jain Joins BlueStone’s Board: CarDekho CEO and cofounder Amit Jain joined the listed jewellery company’s board as a non-executive, non-independent director with effect from September 14. Meanwhile, 360 ONE Asset CIO Sameer Nath retired from BlueStone’s board.
Lenskart Doubles Down On AjnaLens: The eyewear major increased its stake in XR startup AjnaLens to 9.01% from 7.21% through an investment of ₹8 Cr. The latest purchase takes Lenskart’s total investment in AjnaLens across three transactions this year to ₹18.5 Cr.
Peak XV’s Groww Windfall: The VC firm sold 9.17 Cr shares of Groww for ₹1,756.2 Cr. The shares sold represented around 9% of Peak XV’s holding in the investment tech company.
Busy Week For PB Fintech: The insurtech major’s board approved the acquisition of the remaining 20% stake in MyLoanCare Ventures, which will become its wholly owned subsidiary. It also approved capital infusions of up to ₹10 Cr into PB Wheels and ₹1 Cr into PB Financial Account Aggregator.
Separately, PB Fintech dismissed speculation about CEO Yashish Dahiya’s resignation as “false and baseless”, saying he would continue as chairman, executive director, and group CEO.
Aye Finance CTO Departs: Aye Finance CTO Jinu Joseph resigned, citing personal reasons, with his departure effective September 30. The lender appointed former Muthoot Fincorp CTO Nishit Shrivastava as his successor from October 1. Shrivastava will also become part of the company’s senior management.
Aequs Winds Down Step-Down Subsidiary: Aequs Toys Hong Kong, a step-down wholly owned subsidiary of Aequs, was voluntarily wound up and dissolved with effect from September 17. The subsidiary contributed nothing to Aequs’ consolidated revenue or net worth in FY26 and was not classified as a material subsidiary.
With that, let’s take a look at the broader market sentiment this week.
Equity Markets Fall For Sixth Straight Week
Indian equities remained under pressure during the holiday-shortened week. After markets remained closed on Monday (September 14) for Ganesh Chaturthi, the benchmark Nifty 50 declined 0.22% to 23,346.40, extending its losing streak to six weeks. The Sensex fell 0.65% to close at 74,294.96.
Persistent foreign investor selling, elevated crude oil prices, and geopolitical uncertainty continued to weigh on market sentiment.
Brent crude remained above $100 a barrel after briefly touching $109.90, adding to concerns about inflation, bond yields, and corporate costs. The US Federal Reserve’s 25-basis-point rate hike and the Bank of Japan’s rate increase also reinforced expectations of interest rates remaining elevated for longer.
The broader market, however, showed relative resilience in the final session of the week. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 1.24% and 1.74%, respectively. Among sectoral indices, realty, energy, and financial services advanced, while IT, FMCG, and auto lagged.
Foreign institutional investors remained net sellers for the fifth consecutive week, offloading Indian equities worth ₹7,620 Cr. Domestic institutional investors bought shares worth ₹11,232 Cr, cushioning the decline.
In the coming week, investors will track crude oil prices, US-Iran geopolitical developments, and PMI data for cues on the direction of the market, said Geojit Investments’ research head Vinod Nair.
Now, let’s take a look at the performance of Kissht and MobiKwik this week.
Kissht Gains On Fundraise Plan
Shares of OnEMI Technology Solutions, the parent of digital lending platform Kissht, rose 7.66% across four trading sessions to end the week at ₹355.60 despite weakness in the broader market.
The stock touched a record high of ₹373.30 during yesterday’s session before paring its gains and closing 1.2% lower for the day.
The key trigger was the company’s proposed ₹832 Cr preferential fundraise.
OnEMI’s board approved the issuance of up to 2.65 Cr shares at ₹314.11 apiece to 34 non-promoter investors, including Axis Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, Groww Mutual Fund, WhiteOak, 360 ONE, Bandhan Mutual Fund, and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. The issue remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.
The company informed the exchanges about the proposed fundraise on September 14, ahead of its board meeting on September 17. The stock rose 5.6% on Thursday but slipped yesterday after the terms were announced.
The proposed issue price of ₹314.11 is around 12% below yesterday’s closing price but 84% above Kissht’s IPO price of ₹171 in May.
Around 75% of the proceeds will be infused into Si Creva Capital Services, Kissht’s wholly owned NBFC subsidiary. The remaining capital will be used for technology, AI, and general corporate purposes.
Kissht is also targeting multiple credit-rating upgrades over the next two years, which it expects will reduce borrowing costs, widen its access to capital, and support further growth in its lending business.
The fundraise follows a strong Q1 FY27 for the company. Its operating revenue rose 45% YoY to ₹670 Cr, while net profit climbed 58% to ₹95 Cr. Its assets under management grew 61% to ₹8,001 Cr.
MobiKwik Rebounds As Investors Assess UPI MDR Opportunity
Shares of MobiKwik ended the week 5.81% higher at ₹212.30, recording the strongest gain among listed fintech companies as investors assessed the implications of the new MDR framework for UPI.
The stock initially came under pressure after the government notified an MDR of 0.4% on UPI person-to-merchant transactions above ₹2,000. MobiKwik fell 4.2% on Tuesday and another 1.2% on Wednesday before rebounding 7% yesterday.
The recovery came as investors assessed the revenue opportunity arising from the monetisation of higher-value UPI payments.
From October 15, eligible P2M transactions above ₹2,000 will attract an MDR of 0.4%, capped at ₹300 for transactions of ₹75,000 or more. P2P payments will remain free.
MobiKwik cofounder Upasana Taku described the introduction of MDR as a “very positive step”, arguing that rising infrastructure costs have increased pressure on banks and payments companies. She said the previous government subsidy covered only 10% to 15% of the industry’s total costs.
“The company views this development as a strong enabler of its plans to deepen its presence in UPI and scale its merchant business,” MobiKwik said.
Among the other listed fintech companies, Paytm gained 1.37% during the week, while Pine Labs rose 1.34%.
