items.content: Indian banks may be closer to a re-rating than their recent performance suggests. Bank of India Mutual Fund CIO Alok Singh says lenders have the fundamentals investors typically look for—low non-performing assets, healthy return on assets and equity, and loan growth—but lingering concerns over net interest margins and FCNR-related liquidity flows have kept the trade from taking off.That overhang could ease as policy announcements emerge and banks disclose stronger business numbers, Singh said in an interview.Public- and private-sector banks are fairly valued and have become cheaper since last quarter, even as their underlying businesses continue to perform well. “The consensus trade just hasn’t come through yet,” he said, adding that this disconnect cannot persist indefinitely if the operating trend holds.Edited excerpts from a chat:Congratulations on the wonderful performance of your smallcap fund. Everybody these days is talking about small and mid caps, but the smallcap benchmark itself hasn't moved much in the last one year — just 4-5%. So there must be a lot of stock-picking opportunities in the fund?Small-cap is a large space with a large number of stocks. Even the Small Cap 250 index is only 250 stocks. If you look at stocks above ₹1,000 crore market cap, there are roughly 1,450-1,500 of them. Remove the top 250 (or even top 500), and there are still 900+ stocks left — so it's a much bigger universe.As the market and economy normalise, not everything does well — some things do well, some don't — so bottoms-up stock selection becomes more important. Post-COVID, the entire small-cap space benefited from re-rating, so stock picking mattered, but simple allocation to the space also worked as long as you were exposed. I think this is the first time we're looking at a truly normalised economy — even the government has chosen 2024 as its base year, implying normalisation happened after that. This is getting reflected in portfolios: if you're not in the right stocks, you won't participate as much.How much of your portfolio goes beyond the Small Cap 250 index?We have always run a bottoms-up portfolio and use the benchmark more for risk management than for portfolio construction. That said, while we look at all stocks above ₹1,000 crore market cap, it's not that we only look beyond the top 250. My portfolio's average market cap is around ₹24,000 crore, and the weighted average is around ₹25,000 crore. There is hardly any large-cap exposure — maybe 2-3%. So it's predominantly a small-cap portfolio with some mid-cap. It's not about concentrating in one place — it's about finding where newer pools of profit are being generated and building the portfolio around that.Purely from a market-cap perspective, is there a "sweet spot" you hunt in — say, ₹10,000-20,000 crore?No, we don't look at it from a market-cap point of view — we look at it from a business point of view. We're not "growth hungry" either; across our portfolio we buy anything that makes sense on a relative basis, whether that's value or growth. If you're buying value, there has to be some change or inflection point happening, otherwise the value doesn't get unlocked — growth similarly doesn't sustain without an inflection point.In one line: we look at things on a relative basis. If something makes sense relatively, we're okay looking at it — whether it's a ₹5,000 crore, ₹10,000 crore, ₹20,000 crore, or even ₹50,000 crore market cap company. That's not how we approach it.So once an idea makes sense, allocation becomes key?Yes — and that's where we believe the real differentiation lies. Everyone stresses finding new ideas, but what you do with an idea is equally important. No idea stays exclusive to you for long, because in the mutual fund world, once you buy something and your monthly portfolio is published, the whole market knows what you've bought — even without doing the fundamental work themselves, others can reverse-engineer why. So finding a good, scalable business or one going through a transformation is only one part. How you size it and scale it up in the portfolio is most important — especially for us, since we don't run either very concentrated or very spread-out portfolios.You currently have around 90 stocks in the portfolio. Tell us about your position sizing and churn.Yes, right now it's around that, but we like to run 70-80 stocks and may moderate it — it's a bit of a transition period currently. Since the fund launched in 2018, we've generally run a 70-80 stock portfolio, and that's where we wish to stay on a long-term basis. Sometimes the number ticks up a bit due to a few transitional additions. In terms of position sizing, 3-4% is the highest we buy.Because we run about 90 stocks, there is naturally some churn happening — something is going in or out, which is why the stock count and turnover sometimes rise. But we don't do a clean, sharp exit from any stock unless there's a specific reason for concern. On a long-term, steady-state basis, turnover would be more like 0.65-0.7x.Within small and mid-cap, where do you currently see both growth and valuations that aren't excessive — i.e., no euphoria?Frankly, after the last 3-4 months' up-move in mid and small caps, I don't see any pockets that are screamingly undervalued. The market looks fairly valued to me right now — wherever you see slightly above-mean multiples, those are being driven by the earnings those stocks are delivering. So across small, mid, or even large cap, the market seems fairly priced in terms of multiples. That means any further movement has to be driven more by earnings, which is why there's some nervousness — earnings depend on visualisation and assumptions around execution, which people may or may not agree on.On a steady-state basis, though, the market appears fairly priced. That's why markets have largely gone sideways over the last month or so. Going forward, I believe earnings will play a bigger role in shaping the market than further multiple re-rating.Q1 earnings were very good, Q2 is also expected to be good, but the concern is Q3 onward — especially in pockets affected by GST and income tax rate cuts. Is that a worry?The base effect will play a role, but if you look at GST collections, we've actually surpassed prior levels — so collecting more GST at a lower rate, with goods and services volumes unchanged, means volumes have actually picked up. So I don't think the base effect will be a major issue.One thing to appreciate: markets were surprised by Q1 earnings because, when the Middle East crisis happened, the consensus was that Q1 would take most of the hit and Q2 onward would see recovery, normalizing in the second half. As we analyzed results, we realised the impact wasn't concentrated in April but more in the May-July window, due to low-cost inventories and similar factors — so there will be some spillover into Q2 as well, which wasn't the earlier consensus. That's adding to market nervousness, since there's now uncertainty about whether the impact ran through June, July, or even August.That said, I don't believe the impact goes beyond Q2 — which also has its own seasonality with Diwali falling a month later this year. Adjusting for these factors, I think earnings should actually be better, because high-frequency demand indicators — vehicular traffic, power demand, GST collections, toll collections, passenger traffic — are all suggesting decent buoyancy in the economy. If that continues into the festive season, the season should be good, since festive spending typically follows a build-up rather than appearing suddenly. Overall, I think external disruptions (freight movement, transit times, buyer-seller reconciliation) have now normalised and shouldn't be a surprise element unless something changes from here.Can you get more sector-specific on where you expect strong earnings momentum over the next couple of quarters?The capital goods space — specifically industrial automation, industrial products, power equipment — is seeing a good tailwind from both domestic and global demand, and I expect that to continue. Precision engineering, part of capital goods, is also seeing decent order flows.On BFSI, I think banks at large should do well. Earlier there were concerns about NIMs (going back to Q4 of last year), and now there's some worry about FCNR-related spillover effects. But I don't think liquidity pressure is as large as the market anticipates — RBI has repeatedly tried to suck out excess liquidity, and even a recent ₹7 lakh crore reverse repo saw limited takers. If liquidity were truly excessive and suppressing NIMs long-term, banks wouldn't be holding it back from RBI — any reasonable treasury head would rather place it with the RBI than sit on it. That tells me it's transitory — CBLO might dip to 2-3% for a few weeks, but that's not permanent. So banking should be another sector that does well.In the broader segment, capital goods and banking look okay to me. In a smaller segment, metals look good given demand and government policy, with decent capacity utilisation — not a large weight in the index, but earnings growth there looks decent. Elsewhere: pharma is mixed — some doing okay, some facing issues; FMCG faces margin and inflation pressure; consumer durables — some are doing fine; auto is doing okay but fairly priced, so while we stay positive, I don't see a major surprise element there since the earnings are largely already discounted.Among these sectors, do banks have the higher chance of re-rating if earnings pick up?Yes. A large part of large-cap underperformance has come from IT, but banks also haven't done the "heavy lifting" they should have, given their index weight and valuations. Whichever way you look at it — public or private — banks are fairly priced, and all the boxes that should tick for a bank are ticking: low NPAs, decent ROAs leading to decent ROEs, and loan growth. The consensus trade just hasn't come through yet because of lingering worries about NIM pressure and possible rate moves. As policy announcements come through over the next few weeks, I think this will reconcile. Business-wise, most banks are doing well and have gotten cheaper since last quarter without the market reacting — but that can't continue indefinitely if the trend persists.Credit growth wasn't a problem for banks anyways, and now deposits are also coming back via FCNR. So both sides of the balance sheet are sorted?Correct. Banks running high CD ratios will be able to access liquidity now. Also, some NBFCs benefit indirectly — as pressure on larger banks to raise deposits eases, and money needs to be deployed, one avenue is lending to NBFCs. It may not offer the best spread, but it avoids negative carry. So NBFCs become an indirect beneficiary of FCNR flows too. I think the FCNR-related NIM-pressure overhang that the market is pricing in won't be as large as feared, and as banks disclose business numbers, there should be a positive surprise.Crude has again crossed $100, and there have already been about $1.5 billion of outflows this month, with the rupee under pressure — the macro setup is weakening this month. How much of a worry is the Middle East tension?Obviously oil has an overhang on us — there are two sides: the inflation side and the availability side. Availability is the bigger question; every time there's escalation, the possibility of supply being cut increases. The market is more worried about a potential availability cut than about the price level of $100 or $110 per se, because a higher price only impacts margins, whereas zero oil availability means no margin at all.That said, yes, $100 or thereabouts does affect inflation and could have a broader margin impact via the Reserve Bank's response. It's a very hot-and-cold situation, so it's difficult to take a decisive view. If it sustains at these levels for a longer period, we'd need to be more worried — but I'm not worried about it today. If there is an actual sustained supply-side issue, that concerns me more than the price being $100 or $110, because economies will adjust to price; there could be some disruption here and there, but on the whole we'd be okay. Non-availability is a bigger issue to me than $100 oil.

items.author: Ronggo
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Motorola mengumumkan Signature 27 lewat serangkaian teaser yang menampilkan spesifikasi kamera impresif dan sistem operasi baru yang sama sekali berbeda dari Android biasa. Peluncuran resmi dijadwalkan 22 September di Snapdragon Summit, hanya tinggal menghitung hari.
Dari teaser yang ada, setidaknya kita dapat melihat jelas bahwa ponsel ini akan dilengkapi kamera 200 megapiksel dengan kemampuan zoom 100x dan dukungan Dolby Vision, sesuatu yang belum pernah Motorola lakukan sebelumnya di lini Signature. Teaser tersebut juga menunjukkan dua pilihan warna yang sudah disesuaikan dengan palet Pantone: Coal Smoke dan Capulet Olive, keduanya dengan tekstur anyaman atau materi mirip kulit di bagian belakang bukannya kaca.
Sementara itu, spesifikasi kamera menunjukkan sensor utama kemungkinan menggunakan Sony LYT-901 dengan piksel 0,7 mikron, yang sudah memiliki zoom optik 4x bawaan, sedangkan pencapaian 100x harus berasal dari modul telefoto terpisah atau kombinasi zoom hibrida.
Informasi dari berbagai sumber menunjukkan bahwa Motorola akan menggunakan Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, prosesor paling canggih Qualcomm untuk tahun ini. Hanya saja dengan kode nama Wukong, yang kemungkinan besar adalah nama internal untuk Signature 27, Motorola belum secara resmi mengkonfirmasi hal tersebut. Timing pengumuman bersamaan dengan Snapdragon Summit adalah indikasi yang sangat kuat bahwa ponsel ini memang akan menggunakan chip flagshipnya Qualcomm.
Satu detail penting yang sering terlupakan adalah fitur Arm Memory Tagging Extension atau MTE yang sudah ditambahkan Qualcomm ke chip terbaru mereka termasuk Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5. MTE adalah teknologi keamanan yang meningkatkan proteksi terhadap serangan memori dengan menambahkan tag unik ke setiap alokasi memori, membuat eksploitasi cacat memori jauh lebih sulit dilakukan. Ini adalah fitur yang belum dimiliki oleh ponsel Pixel generasi manapun saat ini, memberikan Signature 27 keunggulan keamanan hardware yang unik.
Baca juga: Motorola Moto Pad 70 Resmi Meluncur, Bawa Layar 12,1 Inci dan 5G
GrapheneOS dan Komitmen Motorola pada Privasi Pengguna
Kabar lain dari Signature 27 adalah bahwa ini akan menjadi ponsel Motorola pertama yang diluncurkan dengan sistem operasi GrapheneOS, OS berdasarkan Android yang fokus penuh pada privasi dan keamanan. GrapheneOS telah menjadi jawaban pabrikan ini terhadap peralihan OS ke perangkat non-Pixel, dan Signature 27 kemungkinan akan menjadi debut peluncuran mereka di platform Motorola.
GrapheneOS sendiri dikenal karena membatasi tracking berbasis iklan, mencegah pengumpulan data diagnostik tanpa persetujuan eksplisit, dan memberikan kontrol granular atas izin aplikasi. Sistem operasi ini juga secara aktif mengamankan kernel Linux dan menerapkan hardening keamanan di berbagai lapisan sistem operasi. Sebelum Motorola, GrapheneOS hanya tersedia di ponsel Pixel, pilihan yang sangat terbatas mengingat tidak semua orang ingin membeli ponsel buatan Google. Kehadiran GrapheneOS di Motorola membuka kemungkinan jauh lebih luas bagi pengguna yang menginginkan privasi tinggi tanpa terkunci pada ekosistem Pixel.
Kombinasi Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 dengan MTE support dan GrapheneOS menciptakan trifecta keamanan yang belum pernah ada sebelumnya di ponsel Android mainstream. Pengguna akan mendapatkan perangkat keras yang dirancang untuk keamanan memori, sistem operasi yang mengutamakan privasi, dan prosessor paling bertenaga yang tersedia saat ini untuk pekerjaan berat. Ini bukan sekadar ponsel dengan spesifikasi tinggi, tapi pernyataan filosofi Motorola bahwa privasi dan keamanan penting bagi pelanggan mereka yang premium.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
OnePlus is preparing its next flagship smartphone, the OnePlus 16, and a new leak has revealed several major specs ahead of the official launch. The company has already started teasing the device, including confirming its high refresh rate display.
According to information shared by well-known tipster Digital Chat Station on Weibo, the OnePlus 16 will use Qualcomm’s upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro chipset. This would place the smartphone among the next generation of high-end Android devices.
OnePlus has already confirmed that the OnePlus 16 will feature a 165Hz system-wide refresh rate. This is higher than the refresh rates found on most current flagship smartphones. The leaked information also claims that the display could reach up to 185Hz when playing certain supported games.
OnePlus 16 Key Specs Leak Ahead of Launch – Here’s What We Know So Far
The higher refresh rate could make animations, scrolling, and gaming feel smoother. However, the actual benefits will depend on whether games and other applications support the higher refresh rate.
The OnePlus 16 is also expected to focus heavily on battery capacity. The leaked specifications point to a large 9,000mAh battery. If confirmed, this would give the phone considerably more battery capacity than many flagship smartphones currently available.
The device is also expected to support 100W wired charging and 50W wireless charging. The combination of a large battery and fast charging could allow users to spend less time connected to a charger while still having enough capacity for heavy daily use.
OnePlus 16 Camera Specifications
The camera system could be another major highlight of the OnePlus 16. The leaked information claims that the phone will have a 200MP primary camera with a 1/1.4-inch type sensor.
The main camera could be joined by a 50MP ultrawide camera. A 50MP periscope telephoto camera is also expected, with a 1/1.95-inch type sensor.
The combination would give the phone three high-resolution rear cameras designed for different types of photography. The primary sensor would handle standard photos, while the ultrawide camera could be useful for landscapes and group shots. The periscope telephoto camera could provide better results when photographing distant subjects.
However, camera megapixel counts and sensor sizes alone do not determine image quality. Image processing, lenses and software will also play an important role in the final photography experience.
High-Refresh-Rate Display
Previous reports have suggested that the OnePlus 16 could feature a 6.78-inch display with a 1.5K resolution. The screen is expected to be one of the phone’s key features, especially because of its unusually high refresh rate.
OnePlus has confirmed the 165Hz system-wide refresh rate, while the leaked information claims that some games could push the refresh rate as high as 185Hz. This could make the phone particularly interesting for users who regularly play games on their smartphones.
The higher refresh rate could also improve everyday interactions such as scrolling through websites, switching between apps, and navigating menus.
See Also: The End of an Era? OnePlus May End its Operations in International Markets
Android 17-Based Software
The OnePlus 16 is expected to launch with ColorOS 17 based on Android 17. This means the smartphone could offer the latest version of Android software from the start.
The software will be an important part of the overall experience, particularly alongside the powerful Snapdragon chipset and high-refresh-rate display. OnePlus is also expected to add its own features and interface changes on top of Android 17 through ColorOS 17.
What to Expect From the OnePlus 16
The leaked specifications suggest that OnePlus is preparing a flagship with a strong focus on performance, battery life, charging, and display technology.
The Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro chipset could provide the processing power needed for demanding apps and games. Meanwhile, the 9,000mAh battery could make the phone suitable for users who want longer battery life.
The 200MP main camera and two 50MP secondary cameras could also give the OnePlus 16 a versatile camera setup. The combination of a high-refresh-rate display and powerful hardware could further strengthen its position as a performance-focused flagship.
OnePlus has not officially confirmed most of these leaked specifications yet. The final hardware, features, and availability could therefore differ from the information currently circulating online.
More details about the OnePlus 16 are expected to emerge as OnePlus moves closer to its official launch.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Adviser to the Prime Minister on Industries and Production, Haroon Akhtar Khan, said on Friday that the government would unveil a new Auto Policy shortly.
In a media talk on the opening day of Pakistan International Auto Show 2026, he said the policy aimed to incentivize all stakeholders, including auto part makers.
The government, under the vision of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, is striving to support auto part makers in enhancing exports, he said.
The Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (SMEDA) is participating in the 21st Pakistan International Auto Show (PIAS) 2026 as a ‘strategic partner’ of the Pakistan Association of Automotive Parts & Accessories Manufacturers (PAAPAM).
Govt Will Unveil New Auto Policy Soon, Haroon Akhtar Khan Says
The three-day show – which offers an opportunity for industry professionals to showcase their products, expand into fast-growing international markets and explore new avenues for partnerships – began at the Expo Center, Lahore.
Foreign dignitaries from China and other countries joined Pakistan’s industry leaders and businessmen at the inauguration ceremony.
SMEDA’s collaboration is part of its efforts to support Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in line with the strategic direction of the Ministry of Industries and Production, spearheading the drive to achieve national economic objectives.
Haroon Akhtar Khan, Adviser to the Prime Minister on Industries and Production, earlier said the government was committed to transforming Pakistan into a competitive manufacturing economy by empowering MSMEs and strengthening industrial value chains.
See Also: BYD Unveils the Future at PAPS 2026 with New Lineup, Introducing Pakistan’s First Locally Assembled BYD Sealion 6
“Pakistan’s automotive industry has demonstrated remarkable resilience and potential. Platforms like the Pakistan Auto Show play a vital role in promoting local manufacturing, encouraging innovation and attracting investment,” he said.
He stressed that the event should be presented as a “grand global show” with a focus on B2B, MoUs and joint ventures for a meaningful contribution to the economy. He directed SMEDA to fully support PAAPAM and enable MSMEs in the sector to participate and gain market linkages.
In a statement, CEO Nadia Jahangir Seth said the automotive sector was one of Pakistan’s most dynamic industrial segments with tremendous potential for SME-led growth.
“A number of MSMEs form the backbone of Pakistan’s auto parts and engineering industry. Through this strategic partnership with PAAPAM, SMEDA aims to provide these enterprises with a platform to showcase their capabilities, build strategic partnerships, adopt modern technologies and explore new domestic and international business opportunities,” she said.
Welcoming SMEDA as a strategic partner, convener of PAPS 2026 Salman Saleem earlier said the collaboration would further strengthen the exhibition’s objective of showcasing Pakistan’s automotive industry to the world.
“We are pleased to have SMEDA on board as a strategic partner for PAPS 2026. Its support will significantly enhance SME participation and reinforce our collective efforts to promote indigenous manufacturing under the ‘Make in Pakistan’ vision,” he said.
He said a symposium would be held on Sept 19 on the sidelines of the event, and it would help make a roadmap for the future.

items.title: Huawei Luncurkan Atlas 960E, Infrastruktur SuperPoD Berbasis NPO Pertama di Dunia
items.summary:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Huawei secara resmi meluncurkan Atlas 960E SuperPoD yang menjadi infrastruktur komputasi berbasis Near-Packaged Optics (NPO) pertama di industri global. Peluncuran teknologi mutakhir ini bertujuan khusus untuk mempercepat proses pelatihan dan inferensi pada model kecerdasan buatan yang memiliki hingga 10 triliun parameter. Inovasi tersebut diperkenalkan langsung oleh Deputy Chairman of the Board dan Rotating Chairman Huawei, David Wang, pada ajang HUAWEI CONNECT 2026 di Shanghai.
Strategi pengembangan AI dari Huawei saat ini sangat berpusat pada daya komputasi dengan fokus utama optimalisasi nilai komersial perangkat keras. Melalui pemusatan upaya pada arsitektur SuperPoD dan SuperCluster, perusahaan bertujuan membangun sebuah fondasi komputasi semikonduktor yang sangat solid. Langkah progresif ini juga dibarengi dengan komitmen teguh untuk mengembangkan ekosistem komputasi melalui pendekatan sumber terbuka (open source) dan sistem terbuka (open system).
Seir
items.author: Ronggo
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Huawei secara resmi meluncurkan Atlas 960E SuperPoD yang menjadi infrastruktur komputasi berbasis Near-Packaged Optics (NPO) pertama di industri global. Peluncuran teknologi mutakhir ini bertujuan khusus untuk mempercepat proses pelatihan dan inferensi pada model kecerdasan buatan yang memiliki hingga 10 triliun parameter. Inovasi tersebut diperkenalkan langsung oleh Deputy Chairman of the Board dan Rotating Chairman Huawei, David Wang, pada ajang HUAWEI CONNECT 2026 di Shanghai.
Strategi pengembangan AI dari Huawei saat ini sangat berpusat pada daya komputasi dengan fokus utama optimalisasi nilai komersial perangkat keras. Melalui pemusatan upaya pada arsitektur SuperPoD dan SuperCluster, perusahaan bertujuan membangun sebuah fondasi komputasi semikonduktor yang sangat solid. Langkah progresif ini juga dibarengi dengan komitmen teguh untuk mengembangkan ekosistem komputasi melalui pendekatan sumber terbuka (open source) dan sistem terbuka (open system).
Seiring dengan peningkatan kemampuan model fondasi yang kian mendekati angka 10 triliun parameter, infrastruktur SuperPoD menjadi pilihan paling ideal. Untuk mendukung sistem tersebut, Huawei turut memperkenalkan Hi-ONE sebagai mesin optik NPO pertama di dunia yang berhasil diproduksi secara massal. Mesin cerdas ini mampu menghadirkan kapasitas transmisi luar biasa sebesar 7,2 Tbit/s sekaligus menjadi satu-satunya instrumen NPO di industri dengan sumber cahaya terintegrasi.
Perangkat Atlas 960E SuperPoD ini ditenagai secara optimal oleh perpaduan teknologi jaringan UnifiedBus dan mesin optik Hi-ONE. Infrastruktur canggih ini mengadopsi arsitektur ortogonal terkini serta memanfaatkan desain yang sepenuhnya didinginkan menggunakan sistem pendingin cair. Berkat pengalamatan memori terpadu UnifiedBus, satu SuperPoD dapat diskalakan hingga 4.096 NPU yang membuahkan kinerja 8 EFLOPS pada presisi FP8 dan 16 EFLOPS pada presisi FP4.
Baca juga: HUAWEI Pura X View Resmi Meluncur, Bawa Layar Unik 16:9.5 dan Baterai 7.000 mAh
Efisiensi Daya dan Skalabilitas SuperCluster dari Huawei
Penggunaan arsitektur baru ini memberikan efisiensi masif karena integrasi 5.500 unit Hi-ONE mampu menggantikan kebutuhan 48.000 modul optik 800G tradisional. Pengurangan perangkat keras keras tersebut sukses memangkas konsumsi daya listrik sistem hingga lebih dari 550 kilowatt secara signifikan. Selain itu, inovasi ini juga berhasil menggandakan waktu pengoperasian sistem tanpa gangguan sehingga ketersediaan operasionalnya melonjak mencapai angka 99,8%.
Penerapan arsitektur SuperPoD turut diaplikasikan pada sistem komputasi serbaguna melalui kehadiran produk TaiShan 950 SuperPoD yang telah ditingkatkan secara menyeluruh. Varian tangguh ini mendukung konfigurasi hingga 4.096 node dengan kapasitas unified memory pool masif yang menyentuh angka 256 TB. Sebagai pelengkap ekosistem penyimpanan, Huawei juga meluncurkan klaster OceanStor M900 bertenaga UnifiedBus yang sanggup menyediakan KV cache berskala petabyte untuk lapisan L3.5.
Skalabilitas luar biasa dari jaringan UnifiedBus atau RoCE memungkinkan beberapa unit Atlas 960E SuperPoD dihubungkan menjadi sebuah SuperCluster raksasa. Mengandalkan arsitektur Clos dua tingkat dan empat plane, klaster raksasa ini sanggup menghubungkan tenaga komputasi hingga 512.000 NPU secara bersamaan. Kapasitas fantastis tersebut bahkan dapat ditingkatkan kembali hingga menampung satu juta NPU apabila dikombinasikan dengan topologi jaringan multi-rail.
Menyadari pentingnya kolaborasi pengembang global, Huawei memastikan bahwa platform komputasi CANN kini telah resmi berstatus sumber terbuka yang digerakkan oleh komunitas. Terkait dedikasi ini, David Wang menuturkan, “Di Huawei, kami berkomitmen membangun infrastruktur AI yang kuat serta menerapkan pendekatan sumber terbuka dan sistem terbuka untuk membangun ekosistem komputasi,”. Infrastruktur yang lebih memadai ini diyakini akan memperkuat dukungan pelatihan native untuk model fondasi utama pada ekosistem Ascend demi memajukan dunia yang cerdas.

items.summary: Several smartphones under Rs. 75,000 offer hardware suited to demanding mobile games, including high-end processors, fast displays and large batteries. The Poco X8 Pro Max stands out with its 9,000mAh battery and dedicated cooling system. The Vivo X200T rounds out the list with the Dimensity 9400+ chipset and a 120Hz AMOLED display.

Key Startup Funding Highlights Of The Week
Enterprise services attracted the most capital this week, with three startups raising $42.5 Mn. Advertising services startup Flam accounted for the bulk of this funding with the week’s largest round of $40 Mn.
Consumer services recorded three deals, with startups in the sector raising a total of $4.8 Mn.
AJVC was the most active investor this week, backing MoroMaa, Beijan and Slayd. The VC firm also saw PE firm Novastar Partners as a limited partner for its fund.
Five startups at the seed stage raised about $10.1 Mn, led by VerifAIX’s $5 Mn round.
Startup Fund Updates This Week
India Accelerator’s Finvolve announced the first close of its ₹250 Cr growth stage fund at ₹90 Cr. It intends to build a portfolio of 30-35 growth and late stage startups over the next three to four years.
AI focused VC firm Activate closed its maiden fund at $105 Mn within a year of its launch. It is targeting to back 25-30 startups operating across the AI sector.
Dani Family Office’s Asiana Fund and Taiwan-based VC firm JC Capital launched the ₹1,000 Cr Asiana-JCC Advanced Manufacturing & Innovation Fund, with a primary corpus of ₹600 Cr and a green shoe option of ₹400 Cr.
Startup IPO Updates Of The Week
SEBI cleared the IPOs of Kuku Technologies and Fibe this week.
Rentomojo made a strong listing this week after receiving an overwhelming investor interest, giving hefty returns to early backers like Accel.
After receiving SEBI approval for its IPO, Moneyview has now halved the fresh issue component to ₹750 Cr and trimmed the offer for sale (OFS) component to 10.04 Cr equity shares.
With greater clarity around the monetisation of UPI payments, PhonePe is set to revive its IPO plans. Inc42 learnt that the company would be looking to file its updated IPO papers for an IPO that could value it at about $10 Bn. The company is now targeting a listing between February-March 2027.
Other Developments Of The Week
Coursera-backed edtech startup Unstop acquired gaming startup PerspectAI for an undisclosed sum this week. The acquisition adds a combination of gaming and data science to Unstop’s engagement and hiring platform.
Over a month after Yulu’s $93 Mn Series C round, its early-backer 3one4 Capital announced that the round gave it a “successful, profitable” exit from the startup. The investor didn’t disclose who was the buyer of its stake in the secondary transaction.
Eyewear major Lenskart upped its stake in XR startup AjnaLens’ parent Dimension NXG with an ₹8 Cr investment to acquire an additional 1.8% stake in the startup.
PB Fintech’s board approved the acquisition of the remaining 20% stake in MyLoancare Ventures for ₹5 Cr to make it a wholly owned subsidiary. The board also approved capital infusions of up to ₹10 Cr into PB Wheels and ₹1 Cr into PB Financial Account Aggregator, both wholly owned subsidiaries.

items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Honor secara resmi meluncurkan Tiangong AXB35, series workstation kompak yang diperuntukkan untuk mereka yang mencari kebutuhan komputasi AI. Perangkat desktop baru ini sudah memuat NVIDIA RTX Spark ke dalam chassis bervolume 2 liter dengan berat hanya 1,5 kg. Boleh dibilang kehadiran produk baru ini, menjadi upaya Honor memasuki segmen AI workstation yang sedang berkembang pesat dengan pendekatan yang fokus pada portabilitas ekstrem tanpa mengorbankan performa.
Model Ultra dari series ini dilengkapi 128GB unified memory LPDDR5X dan 2TB NVMe SSD, dirancang untuk menjalankan large language model secara lokal tanpa ketergantungan cloud. Platform RTX Spark yang dikombinasikan dengan Grace CPU berbasis Arm architecture memberikan kombinasi GPU Blackwell dengan CPU 20-core yang mampu memberikan performa hingga 1 peta-level dalam FP4 calculations, angka yang mengesankan untuk packaging sebanding ukuran toaster.
Dari sisi power consumption, sistem ini fleksibel dengan tiga mode daya yang dapat dipilih: 55W untuk pekerjaan ringan, 85W untuk workload menengah, dan 132W untuk performa maksimal. External power supply 240W sudah cukup untuk semua kebutuhan, jauh lebih efisien daripada multi-GPU tower yang biasanya membutuhkan PSU 1.000W ke atas. Windows 11 dan Ubuntu sudah disertakan secara pre-installed, memberikan fleksibilitas OS kepada users yang menggunakan stack development yang berbeda.
Dengan dimensi Tiangong AXB35 tercatat 203 x 70 x 192 mm, membuatnya jadi salah satu workstation teringkas yang pernah ada di pasaran untuk kategori ini. Saking ringkasnya, pengguna bahkan bisa menggenggam dengan satu tangan dan tanpa beban berarti sebab bobotnya hanya 1,5 kg saja.
Baca juga: Honor 700 Pro Dikabarkan Ikuti Xiaomi, Bawa Layar Kedua di Bagian Belakang
Honor Tiangong AXB35 Ultra Memahami Kebutuhan Developer
Keunggulan sebenarnya dari Tiangong AXB35 Ultra bukan hanya size-nya tapi kemampuannya untuk menjalankan model AI besar secara lokal di mesin single. Dengan 128GB unified memory yang shared antara CPU dan GPU, users dapat load dan run LLM yang sebelumnya membutuhkan cloud access atau multi-GPU setup tanpa khawatir lag atau bottleneck memory. Ini berarti developer bisa experiment dengan model tuning, fine-tuning, dan inference secara private tanpa mengirim data ke cloud service mana pun.
Spesifikasi yang dihadirkan begitu mengindikasikan bahwa Honor mehamai kebutuhan developer lokal yang menginginkan kebebasan tanpa cloud vendor lock-in. Konektivitas standard termasuk Ethernet 1GbE, USB Type-C Thunderbolt, dan multiple USB-A ports memberikan fleksibilitas untuk connect external storage atau accelerator cards kalau dibutuhkan. Fakta bahwa unit ini support Ubuntu juga important untuk Linux developers yang mungkin uncomfortable dengan Windows ecosystem.
Series Tiangong AXB35 juga menawarkan varian dengan processor lain, bukan hanya RTX Spark. Intel variant menggunakan Panther Lake-H dengan penyimpanan 512GB, AMD variant dilengkapi Ryzen AI Strix Halo dengan 1TB storage, sementara model Ultra NVIDIA mendapat 2TB untuk pekerjaan data-intensive. Semua varian berbagi chassis yang sama dan performa yang sebanding untuk keperluan development kecil hingga menengah, memberikan pengguna pilihan sesuai ekosistem software yang mereka familiar dengan.
Segmentasi produk ini cukup jelas, mulai dari AI developers, researchers, dan professionals yang butuh komputasi lokal yang powerful. Sayangnya belum ada informasi tentang harga dan kapan tepatnya produk ini dirilis.

items.author: Ronggo
items.content:
Jakarta, Gizmologi – Meta secara resmi meluncurkan pembaruan fitur Pengawasan Orang Tua pada aplikasi Threads bagi pengguna di kawasan Asia Pasifik. Kehadiran instrumen kendali ini merupakan kelanjutan komitmen perusahaan dalam menyediakan perangkat bantu bagi orang tua untuk memantau aktivitas daring remaja di seluruh ekosistem aplikasinya. Sistem pengawasan digital ini dirancang untuk bekerja secara beriringan melengkapi seluruh fitur perlindungan bawaan yang sebelumnya telah terpasang pada Akun Remaja di platform Threads.
Lewat pembaruan ini, para orang tua atau wali kini dibekali dengan hak akses langsung untuk mengendalikan serta memonitor rekam jejak aktivitas anak remajanya melalui portal Family Center. Mulai pekan ini, wewenang kontrol atas akun Threads milik anak akan sepenuhnya sama mutlaknya dengan tingkat pengawasan pada layanan-layanan Meta lainnya. Orang tua kini berhak menjadi pengambil keputusan utama perihal diizinkan atau tidaknya remaja berusia di bawah 16 tahun melonggarkan batas pengaturan akun mereka.
Profil Akun Remaja di Threads sendiri memang telah dibentengi oleh sistem perlindungan otomatis sedari awal. Mekanisme perlindungan bawaan tersebut mencakup penetapan status akun yang dikunci menjadi privat secara default. Selain itu, platform juga secara otomatis menerapkan pembatasan ketat terhadap jenis maupun kategori konten yang diizinkan untuk dilihat oleh audiens remaja.
Setelah sinkronisasi fitur Pengawasan Orang Tua ini diaktifkan, berbagai wawasan analitik mendalam akan langsung terbuka dan bisa diakses oleh wali. Salah satu kemampuan utamanya adalah fitur pelacakan waktu (Time Spent), di mana orang tua dapat melihat total akumulasi durasi penggunaan Threads harian anak dalam seminggu terakhir. Sistem analitik ini bahkan mampu mengalkulasi sekaligus menampilkan rata-rata penggunaan waktu harian remaja tersebut secara akurat.
Baca juga: Mengenal Muse, Personal AI Agent yang Diciptakan oleh Meta
Threads Beri Pengendalian Waktu dan Privasi Digital
Guna mencegah risiko kecanduan media sosial, fitur ini turut menyertakan opsi penetapan batasan waktu penggunaan aplikasi (Time Limits). Orang tua dapat menentukan batas alokasi durasi harian maksimal sekaligus memblokir total akses Threads pada hari maupun jam-jam tertentu yang telah disepakati. Skema pembatasan durasi ini juga berlaku secara menyeluruh (akumulatif) sekalipun sang anak membuka akunnya melalui beberapa perangkat yang berbeda.
Fitur krusial lainnya yang disematkan adalah penyelarasan Mode Tidur untuk menjaga kualitas waktu istirahat remaja pada malam hari. Melalui fungsi ini, seluruh notifikasi akan dimatikan seketika dan fitur balasan otomatis akan aktif secara default dari pukul 10 malam hingga 7 pagi waktu setempat. Tentu saja, pihak wali diberikan otoritas mutlak untuk menyesuaikan ulang, membatasi, atau bahkan memblokir keseluruhan akses pada jendela waktu malam hari tersebut.
Fokus pengawasan platform tidak sebatas pada manajemen waktu semata, namun turut merambah pada ranah keamanan privasi interaksi digital. Wali atau orang tua diberikan wewenang penuh untuk menyortir dan menentukan siapa saja pengguna yang diperbolehkan menandai (tag) akun anaknya dalam sebuah postingan. Lebih jauh lagi, fitur ini memungkinkan wali untuk mengelola, menyeleksi, hingga menyetujui preferensi konten-konten sensitif apa saja yang layak tayang bagi remaja.
Bagi pengguna yang ingin segera mengaktifkan instrumen pengawasan ini, dapat langsung mengakses portal resmi di tautan familycenter.meta.com/supervision. Pihak Meta berjanji akan terus mengembangkan perangkat pemantauan ini agar semakin mempermudah orang tua dalam menelusuri pengaturan dan mendapatkan wawasan bermanfaat. Seluruh dedikasi ini bermuara pada satu tujuan luhur, yakni menghadirkan dukungan pengalaman digital yang positif dan aman bagi audiens remaja di seluruh portofolio aplikasinya secara terpusat.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Ghanaians regard Robert Mensah as their best goalie, ahead of Edward Doodo Ankrah, John Naawu, Joseph Carr, John Baker and Richard Kingston. One man who found a way round the goalie was Christian Madu, a Nigerian born in Kumasi.
Madu’s salad days in the Gold Coast were spent with his parents, Herbert and Ezinne, who relocated from Ndiama Oka – Ugiri in the Isiala, Mbano area of today’s Imo State. Soon the boy moved from Adenisimiah to Accra Hearts of Oak.
Mensah, from Cape Coast, rose through Mysterious Dwarfs to Sekondi Independence before landing at Kumasi to join Asante Kotoko. He also featured for Tema Textile Mills when Madu had joined Accra Great Olympics.
While Madu was lifting Accra Hearts, Mensah was solidifying the Kotoko rear. A game between both teams was like Enugu Rangers against Shooting Stars or Arsenal versus Manchester United. Mensah was always the centre of attraction with his saves. The only player who always rattled him, was the  penalty specialist.
Mensah became an idol after Kotoko won their first continental title, the CAF Champions League in 1970. It happened in far away Kinshasa, against the great TP Englebert ( now Mazembe). The Congolese earned a 1-1 draw in the away first leg and were tipped to win the returned leg.
It did not turn out as predicted. By the 89th minute, the Ghanaians were 2-1 ahead thanks to goals by Malik Jabir and Abukari Gariba. Then in the very last minute, the referee awarded a penalty to the hosts. Skipper Pierre Kalala, the leading scorer, with four goals, stepped forward.
Kotoko, captained by the Nigerian, Ibrahim Sunday, planned to walk out. That was what eliminated Stationery Stores in the second round when they left the field in Kumasi against the Porcupines. Mensah knew the implications.He encouraged his team mates to stay put.
Englebert fans insisted that there was juju in Mensah’s cap which prevented their team from  scoring more than one goal in the match. The goalie removed the cap and quietly walked back to the net. As Kalala moved to fire, Mensah maintained gaze on the taker. The ball flew over the bar.
Madu never missed a penalty against Mensah even when they trained together in the Black Stars Camp. Both were in the team that lost 2-1 to the Green Eagles in a Mexico 1970 World Cup qualifier decided at the Liberty Stadium ,Ibadan in 1969.
While Mensah was not beaten by Kalala from the penalty spot in 1970( the game was actually decided in January 1971 ), Madu beat another legend, Thomas Nkono of Canon Sportif, from the spot, in the first leg final of the 1977 African Winners Cup.
Mensah was so good that at the Sudan 1970 African Nations Cup, the Golden Boot winner and Player of the Tournament, Laurent Pokou could not beat him. Ghana defeated Cote d’Ivoire in the semi finals. Pokou had scored five times in the previous game against Ethiopia ending up with a total of eight goals.
Madu later left Ghana to join Enugu Rangers in 1975. The Flying Antelopes had beaten Great Olympics, home and away, in the first round of the 1975 African Winners Cup. Oly had a formidable side, led by Black Stars captain, Awuley Quaye. 
Joseph Nartey, and the Hammond brothers, Obley and Sabban, were overwhelmed. Keeper Emmanuel Okala was fantastic. Patrick Iluno, scorers Alex Nwosu and Kenneth Abana, Ernest Ufele, Stanley Okoronkwo and Harrison Mecha played their hearts out.
One account said Madu was on his way to Alyufsalam Rocks, when Rangers cornered him.  Proprietor of the Ilorin side, Alhaji  Yusuf Salami had gone to Korley Park, in the Sabon Zango area of Accra to recruit players. Madu frequented their and spoke fluent Hausa.
When he eventually settled for Rangers, the newcomer found company in Hausa speaking players like Ogidi Ibeabuchi, Sam Onyeaka, Nwabueze Nwankwo, Emeka Onyedika, Stanley Okoronkwo and Abana. In the 1976 GA Cup grand finale, Rangers beat Alyufsalam 2-0.
There were sad stories.  On  October 30, 1971, Mensah was stabbed at Credo Bar, Tema. It was believed the goalie would have left the country on November 2, for greener pastures overseas. That was the day he died. The next day, his wife was delivered of a baby.
Madu was buried in November 2017, three months after his demise in August. The man died in penury. He was sacked by Enugu State military governor, Col Sule Ahman who forced non indigenes out of Enugu State Civil Service. His wife, Vera, was also affected.
How strange that a man who was spared by Ghana  when the Kofi Busia government sent Nigerians parking in 1968, was not spared by his country men. Contrary to reports that it was because he changed his surname from Madumere to Madu, the truth is that the Igbo who lived in Ghana were not asked to go because they were seen as Emeka Ojukwu’s people.
Ojukwu was popular in Ghana. He taught at the Military Academy in Teshie. His half sister, Esther, had a Ghanaian husband named Davies. Living in exile, the Biafran leader, opened an office in Accra and chose a name, Dr. Kofi.
Peduase Lodge, offered Nigeria lasting peace in 1967. Yakubu Gowon lost it. 
Mensah has a stadium named after him in Cape Coast. He was cousin to former President John Atta Mills, one of the backers of Accra Hearts. Madu played for Green Eagles. His younger brother, Ransom also did. They had a cousin in Takoradi. Another cousin, Boogaloo, created waves in Ghana as a musician.

items.title: What happens to your brain after 50?
items.summary:
By Sola Ogundipe
It starts innocently. A name refuses to come. You walk into a room and forget why you’re there. Your phone is in your hand, yet you spend several minutes looking for it. An old friend’s face is familiar, but the name just won’t come. “It’s old age,” someone says.
For millions of people, especially as parents and relatives move into their 50s, 60s and 70s, such moments have become almost too ordinary to question. But scientists are beginning to see the ageing brain differently.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Sola Ogundipe
It starts innocently. A name refuses to come. You walk into a room and forget why you’re there. Your phone is in your hand, yet you spend several minutes looking for it. An old friend’s face is familiar, but the name just won’t come. “It’s old age,” someone says.
For millions of people, especially as parents and relatives move into their 50s, 60s and 70s, such moments have become almost too ordinary to question. But scientists are beginning to see the ageing brain differently.
New research has found that the human brain undergoes a major biological shift between about 50 and 75. Deep inside the brain, some of the immune cells that have been there since early development begin to decline. They are increasingly replaced by cells with stronger inflammatory characteristics.
At the same time, cells that help maintain the brain’s protective barrier become less abundant, while the highly organised three-dimensional structure of DNA inside several types of brain cells begins to deteriorate.The changes are happening long before most people would think of themselves as elderly, and that is what makes the discovery particularly intriguing.
For Nigerians, 50 is often an age of peak responsibility rather than retreat. There are children in university, ageing parents to support, businesses to run, careers to manage and, increasingly, plans to remain economically active well into the 60s and 70s. Life may be moving faster than ever. Yet, underneath it all, the brain may already be undergoing a profound transformation.
Published in Science, the study could help explain why advancing age is the strongest known risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease and other neurodegenerative conditions. It doesn’t mean that turning 50 sets off dementia. Nor does it mean that every forgotten name is a warning sign.
But it does raise a question many families may want answered: when does ordinary forgetfulness stop being “old age”, and what exactly is happening inside the ageing brain?
For quite a number of people approaching middle age, as well as those caring for older relatives, this study offers a reason to pay closer attention to brain health. Growing older isn’t just about changes we can see in the body, the brain, too, undergoes profound biological changes, many of which scientists are only beginning to unravel.
The brain has specialised cells that protect nerve cells, clear away cellular debris and respond to injury or infection. These cells known as microglia play a vital role in keeping the brain’s internal environment healthy. But researchers have found that this cellular workforce changes considerably during midlife.
Between approximately ages 50 and 75, the population of microglia that originated during embryonic development declined sharply, at the same time, cells with molecular features resembling immune cells found in the bloodstream became more prominent. The replacement microglia-like cells also showed stronger inflammatory characteristics.
That finding challenges the long-standing assumption that the brain’s original immune cells remain its dominant defenders throughout a person’s life. It also raises questions about whether the changing immune environment contributes to chronic inflammation and makes the ageing brain more vulnerable to damage.
Bing Ren, one of the study’s corresponding authors, said microglia are essential for maintaining the brain. When their basic functions fail, toxic materials can accumulate, triggering inflammatory processes that may contribute to neurodegenerative diseases.
For the average person, it doesn’t mean that everyone over 50 will develop dementia, or that these changing cells automatically cause Alzheimer’s disease.
The discovery, rather, offers scientists a possible explanation for how the ageing brain may become more susceptible to damage.. The study identifies biological changes, it does not establish that those changes directly cause disease in every older person.
In many homes, forgetfulness in older people is readily dismissed as old age. An elderly father asks the same question several times, a mother forgets where she kept her belongings, an older relative struggles to recall a familiar name. Some forgetfulness is a normal part of ageing, but when memory problems persist, worsen or begin to interfere with everyday activities, they deserve medical attention.
The new research does not establish that the cellular changes identified are responsible for any individual’s symptoms. What it does is add to the growing scientific effort to understand the biological processes involved in neurodegenerative diseases.
For families, the practical lesson is straightforward: don’t automatically write off significant changes in an older person’s memory or behaviour as “old age.” A medical assessment can help identify possible causes and determine whether further investigation is necessary.
The scientists also observed a substantial decline in cell populations involved in maintaining the blood-brain barrier. This barrier serves as a protective filter between the bloodstream and brain tissue. It regulates the movement of substances into the brain and helps shield delicate neural structures from potentially harmful materials circulating in the blood. As people age, changes in the cells supporting this barrier may affect how well it functions.
The finding is particularly relevant in a country where older adults may also be dealing with hypertension, diabetes and other chronic health conditions. However, the study did not establish how those conditions influence the specific cellular changes observed. Neither did it examine a distinct population. The findings, therefore, point to an important area for further biological research.
Nathan Zemke, Director of Single-cell Genomics at the Center for Epigenomics at the University of California, San Diego, described the study as an important step towards understanding how ageing reshapes the human genome in brain cells. Still, the research remains focused on identifying biological changes. It does not establish a treatment, nor does it show that lifestyle changes can reverse the genome alterations observed.
Can you do anything to protect your brain?
While the study did not test specific lifestyle interventions or establish that any particular diet, supplement or exercise programme can prevent the cellular changes it identified, the findings offer an opportunity to revisit the established principles of maintaining good health as we age.
For middle-aged and older Nigerians, this includes paying attention to blood pressure, blood sugar, physical activity, sleep and other ongoing health needs. Regular medical check-ups can help identify conditions that require treatment. These measures shouldn’t be presented as a proven way to stop the particular brain changes described in the study. Rather, they’re part of preventive healthcare, which becomes increasingly important with advancing age.
For now, the study offers a different way of looking at ageing. Brain ageing isn’t necessarily a simple, steady decline. Between midlife and older age, several biological systems may change together, including immune cells, vascular support systems and the organisation of the genome.
As scientists work to understand what these changes mean, one point deserves emphasis: protecting brain health shouldn’t be a conversation that begins only after memory problems appear.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By Douglas Baye-Osagie
dbayeosagie@yahoo.com
This season, Nigeria was represented by four clubs on the continent. Rangers International and Rivers United in the CAF Champions League, and Shooting Stars and El-Kanemi Warriors in the CAF Confederation Cup. The story is already familiar – while two have bowed out in their very first game of the tournament, the two that remain now face a heavy North African hurdle. We celebrate qualifiers in June, we get humiliated in September. Rivers United and Shooting Stars are just the latest victims. But the problem is not juju, not luck, not referees. It is systemic. These were teams who had pole position to advance but they refused to do what was needed to get over the line.
The NPFL is now a feeder league for the continent’s smaller leagues. That is how far we have fallen. Our local players have taken their football to African countries whenever the slightest opportunity arises.
We pay our champions peanuts. How can you pay a star striker N150,000 a month and expect him to face a Tunisian defender earning $10,000? Good players don’t stay. They emigrate to Rwanda, Tanzania, Sudan, Kenya, Europe, even Vietnam. We export goals and import regrets. Just look at Shooting Stars – their best two players last season, Ayobami Junior and Tijani Al Ameen, who even made the Super Eagles squad for the Unity Cup derby, have now moved on to clubs in Algeria and Zimbabwe. Think of how much experience and quality is lost by these departures.
Recruitment is corrupt. It’s “man-know-man” football. Players are sacked by cleaners. That doesn’t breed a professional environment. Agents bring their players, commissioners bring their cousins, chairmen bring their clients. Talent is optional.
Some coaches have turned selection into business. If you don’t pay, you don’t play. The best 11 never plays. The richest 11 plays.
We lack tactical preparation. African football has gone scientific. North Africans press with GPS data, video analysis, and set-piece coaches. We do “come out and play” and shout “ginger yourselves” from the bench.
Technically, we are still in 1999. First touch heavy, second touch tackle. Rivers United assistant coach Yemi after the game says there are no strikers in Nigeria. What a way to divert attention from himself and the coaching crew who couldn’t do the needful at home.
Most of our clubs are owned by state governments. Football is treated as a political settlement. A Commissioner for Sports who has never run a kiosk is suddenly managing a club with a continental budget.
Football has left that era. It is now business. Al Ahly is a corporation. Raja Casablanca is a brand. Orlando Pirates is almost a brand of sponsors. We are still a Ministry Department.
No pre-season planning. We start buying players 2 weeks before CAF registration closes. The Fire Brigade Approach. Even the coach who qualified Shooting Stars was not good enough as he was sacked for Salisu Yusuf.
No continuity. A new Governor comes in, sacks the entire management, sacks the coach, sacks 20 players. How do you build a team like that?
We don’t respect away games. You can’t go to Tunisia to defend a 1-0 lead. In Africa, to qualify, you must go to score. North Africans see defense as invitation.
We don’t scout our opponents. They have 50 clips of us. We have zero of them.
Fitness levels are shameful. By minute 70 in North Africa, our players are cramping. Theirs are just starting.
We have no sports psychology. We fear the name “Esperance” and “Wydad” before the bus enters the stadium.
Infrastructure. You train on a bad pitch in Nigeria and expect to play well on a lush green modern hybrid grass in Algiers, Tunis or Morocco. Impossible.
Poor welfare kills motivation. Unpaid bonuses, 6 months salary owed, then you ask a man to die for the badge in Casablanca.
No youth system. Moroccan clubs have academies producing stars for Europe. We have trial grounds every pre-season.
This brings me to ENYIMBA. Why did they succeed where everyone else failed?
In the early 2000s, Orji Uzor Kalu took politics OUT of football. He brought in professionals. He gave Felix Anyansi Agwu a free hand. He paid Enyimba players MORE than the national team. He kept Kadiri Ikhana and later Okey Emordi, bought the best legs in the country – Vincent Enyeama, Obinna Nwaneri, Joetex Frimpong – and did a 6-week close camping in Abia. They didn’t just prepare, they OVER-prepared.
That is how you win Africa back-to-back. Enyimba proved that Nigerian clubs CAN conquer the continent, but only when run like a professional club, not a political campaign office.
And let’s be honest with ourselves – in a fixture that looked like Enugu Rangers were going to have it easy against a Benin Republic club side, it took the luck of penalties to go through. Against a team from Algeria, you don’t win with luck.
Until we sack the political approach and hire professionals, pay professionals, and think like professionals, we will continue to crash out in the first round.
Rangers vs USM Alger and El Kanemi vs Raja Casablanca are not football matches. They are audits. And African football is about to audit us again. We hope and pray they prepare well and live up to the expectations.
The post CAF Inter-club competitions: Why Nigerian clubs fail appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe
GOMBE — Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, has pledged the state government’s support for the accelerated take-off of newly established Nigerian Army formations in the state.
Yahaya gave the assurance when a delegation representing the General Officer Commanding, GOC, 3rd Armoured Division, Nigerian Army, paid a courtesy visit to the palace of the Mai Kaltungo, Engr. Saleh Mohammed.
Represented by the Secretary to the State Government, SSG, Prof. Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, the governor expressed appreciation to President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for approving the establishment of the 271 Tank Battalion in Bajoga and 272 Tank Battalion in Kaltungo.
He said the new formations would strengthen the security architecture of the state and contribute to protecting lives and property in the North-East, which continues to face insurgency, banditry and other security challenges.
Yahaya also commended the Federal Government and the state government for their roles in facilitating the conversion of the Snakebite Hospital, Kaltungo, into a National Snakebite Research Centre.
Njodi further commended the Mai Kaltungo for his contributions to the development of the chiefdom and initiatives aimed at improving the welfare of its people.
Earlier, the representative of the GOC, 3rd Armoured Division, and Commander, 301 Artillery Regiment, Gombe, Col. S.O. Bike, said the establishment of the new formations was part of the Nigerian Army’s expansion from eight to 12 divisions.
Bike, who is also Team Lead of the Technical Assessment Team, said the delegation was in Gombe to engage the state government on arrangements for the commencement of operations of the 27 Armoured Brigade and its component units.
He listed the formations as the 27 Armoured Brigade Garrison, 271 Tank Battalion and 272 Tank Battalion.
According to him, the team’s visit to Kaltungo was also to assess facilities provided for the initial take-off of the 272 Tank Battalion.
He commended the Gombe State Government and the traditional institution in Kaltungo for their cooperation and support towards the establishment of the formation.
Responding, the Mai Kaltungo, Engr. Saleh Mohammed, thanked President Tinubu and Governor Yahaya for supporting the establishment of strategic Federal Government institutions in the chiefdom.
He pledged the continued support and cooperation of the people of Kaltungo to the Nigerian Army and the newly established 272 Tank Battalion.
The delegation subsequently inspected a proposed temporary site at a private boarding school designated for the initial take-off of the battalion.
The Technical Assessment Team expressed satisfaction with the facility and commended the Mai Kaltungo and residents of the chiefdom for their efforts in providing a temporary location.
The team also acknowledged the identification of about 90 hectares of land for the permanent development of the military facility, as well as available accommodation for officers.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe
The Federal Road Safety Corps, FRSC, has dismissed as misleading a viral social media publication alleging that the member representing Balanga/Billiri Federal Constituency of Gombe State in the House of Representatives, Hon. Ali Isah, secured 50 recruitment slots for his constituents.
The Corps, in a statement dated September 16, 2026, signed by its Corps Public Education Officer, Mr Osondu Ohaeri, and obtained by our correspondent in Gombe on Friday, said no appointment letter had been issued to any candidate under its ongoing 2026 recruitment exercise.
The clarification followed the circulation of a social media publication purportedly linking the lawmaker to the allocation of 50 FRSC recruitment slots to his constituents.
According to the FRSC, candidates who have successfully passed various stages of the screening and interview processes have only been invited to designated training schools and the FRSC Academy for further stages of the exercise.
The Corps stressed that such invitations should not be interpreted as appointment letters.
It explained that candidates must still undergo and successfully complete prescribed training, screening, regimentation and other mandatory processes before they can be considered for appointment.
The statement read: “Only candidates who satisfactorily complete all the required stages and emerge without any disqualifying record will be considered for appointment in accordance with established procedures.”
The FRSC further maintained that no political office holder, individual, group or external interest has the authority to confer appointments into the Corps outside its established recruitment framework.
It said the ongoing recruitment exercise, under the leadership of Corps Marshal Shehu Mohammed, mni, was being conducted in accordance with the principles of merit, transparency, due process and institutional integrity.
The Corps urged applicants and members of the public to disregard unverified claims suggesting that recruitment slots had been allocated to particular individuals, constituencies or political interests.
It also warned that such claims could expose unsuspecting applicants to fraudsters who might exploit the perception that FRSC appointments could be secured through political influence, payment or personal connections.
The Corps said it would continue to provide official information on the recruitment exercise through its authorised communication channels, advising applicants to rely only on verified information from the FRSC.
It reiterated that the 2026 recruitment exercise remained subject to the completion of all statutory and administrative procedures, stressing that no candidate should regard himself or herself as an FRSC appointee until the process was concluded and a formal appointment communicated by the appropriate authority.
The FRSC’s position is that no appointment has been issued under the 2026 recruitment exercise and that candidates must complete all prescribed stages before any formal appointment can be made.
The post FRSC denies 50 recruitment slots for Gombe lawmaker appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Gift Chapi Odekina, Abuja
Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has called on the World Trade Organisation (WTO) to deliver concrete outcomes on food security and investment facilitation, warning that prolonged delays could weaken confidence in the multilateral trading system.
Kalu made the call on Friday in Geneva, Switzerland, while speaking at the 57th Session of the Steering Committee of the Parliamentary Conference on the WTO (PCWTO), attended by WTO Director-General, Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala.
The session, co-chaired by Bernd Lange of the European Parliament and Secretary-General of the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU), Anda Filip, brought together parliamentarians from national and regional legislatures, trade policy experts, the European Parliament and the IPU.
The committee reviewed developments in multilateral trade negotiations, follow-up actions from the 14th WTO Ministerial Conference (MC14), and outcomes of the PCWTO session held in Yaoundé, Cameroon.
Kalu acknowledged progress on fisheries subsidies and development issues but said the WTO’s credibility would ultimately depend on its ability to deliver tangible outcomes for developing countries.
He expressed concern over the absence of a permanent solution to public stockholding for food security, 13 years after WTO members committed to addressing the issue at the 2013 Bali Ministerial Conference.
According to him, Nigeria had co-sponsored the demand by the African Group, African, Caribbean and Pacific Group and G33 for a permanent solution.
“Thirteen years cannot be explained as an ordinary negotiating delay. Behind every delayed outcome are farmers, workers and families living with the consequences of decisions we defer,” Kalu said.
As an interim measure, the Deputy Speaker proposed that WTO members consider a waiver under Article IX:3 of the Marrakesh Agreement to cover qualifying public stockholding programmes.
He argued that the absence of consensus should not render an existing treaty mechanism unusable when countries were facing pressing food security challenges.
Kalu also raised concerns over the Investment Facilitation for Development Agreement, saying broad support for the agreement had been stalled by a single formal objection.
He called for greater accountability from national parliaments and proposed that participating legislatures submit reports on concrete steps taken to advance PCWTO and WTO outcomes before each Steering Committee meeting.
“Too often, our discussions focus on what Geneva has or has not done. We should devote equal attention to what our own governments and legislatures have done since the last meeting. Accountability must run in both directions,” he said.
The Deputy Speaker further cautioned that improved attendance at parliamentary trade meetings alone would not address the challenge of legislative relevance in global trade governance.
He said many legislatures received briefings only after negotiating positions had already been finalised.
Kalu proposed that future PCWTO sessions focus on specific economic issues, including public stockholding, investment facilitation, the e-commerce moratorium and digital trade rules.
Such an approach, he said, would enable parliamentarians to communicate clear conclusions and areas of disagreement to trade ministers before negotiations.
Kalu, who joined the PCWTO Steering Committee in February 2025, also secured a reaffirmation from the IPU Secretary-General of the organisation’s commitment to working with him towards the successful hosting of the PCWTO event scheduled for Abuja in 2027.
He reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to a fair, credible and development-oriented global trading system.
“Nigeria is not here to add to the diagnosis. We are here to help restore that trust,” Kalu said.
Earlier, Okonjo-Iweala presented an update on WTO reforms, covering decision-making, development, special and differential treatment, fairness and dispute settlement.
She noted that while consensus gives all WTO members an equal voice, its application as unanimity had enabled single objections to block outcomes with broad support.
The WTO Director-General urged parliamentarians to move beyond criticism and propose practical solutions for rebuilding confidence in the organisation, citing transparency and improved notifications as possible confidence-building measures.
She also called for deeper engagement between parliamentarians and Geneva-based trade actors, including national WTO representatives, the Chair of the General Council, reform facilitators and committee chairs.
Okonjo-Iweala acknowledged that the multilateral trading system had not served many developing and poorer countries effectively, while defending the continued relevance of special and differential treatment.
She also stressed the importance of investment facilitation to developing economies and said restoring an effective two-tier dispute settlement system remained part of the WTO reform agenda.
The post Kalu urges WTO action on food security, investment appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Moses Nosike
African journalists need to look beyond crisis-driven coverage and tell more stories about the people and institutions building connections across borders, fellows at the 2026 MTN Media Innovation Summit in South Africa have said.
The call came during a session moderated by one of the MIP fellows Tolulope Ajibola, titled “Storytelling Across Borders: Finding the Untold Nigeria–South Africa Stories,” held as part of the South African study visit for the fifth cohort of the MTN Media Innovation Programme (MIP).
The fellows noted that African journalism often looks beyond national borders when there is a crisis, while stories about entrepreneurs, students, artists, researchers, technology innovators and professionals building relationships across countries receive less attention. They called for more coverage of everyday experiences and relationships between communities in Nigeria and South Africa.
The discussion was part of the two-day summit held at the University of Johannesburg, which brought together 25 senior Nigerian journalists selected from a pool of applicants, alongside South African editors, researchers and media practitioners.
Professor Sifiso Mnisi, Director of the Centre for Data and Digital Communications at the University of Johannesburg, said the summit provided an opportunity for journalists from both countries to examine how media narratives influence relationships between nations and social cohesion.
He noted that perceptions in Nigeria and South Africa are often shaped by news reports, social media and popular culture rather than direct interaction, placing greater responsibility on journalists and editors in shaping how citizens understand one another.
The summit also examined how media practitioners can report conflict without worsening tensions. A session moderated by Progress Godfrey, an MIP 5 Fellow, titled “From Xenophobia to Social Cohesion: Reporting Conflict Without Fueling It,” stressed the importance of historical context, verified information and perspectives from communities working towards reconciliation.
Another session, moderated by Goitsemang Mvula, called for collaborative investigations, regional reporting projects and stronger editorial partnerships to help African audiences understand continental issues beyond national boundaries.
Closing the discussions, Funso Aina, Senior Manager, External Relations at MTN Nigeria, said the summit represented more than a professional development initiative. He noted that by bringing together journalists, newsroom leaders, content creators and communication professionals, the programme has become a platform for strengthening journalism’s role in promoting democratic participation, regional integration and social cohesion.

By Henry Umoru
ABUJA — The Confederation of West African Youths has called for greater youth participation in governance, accountable leadership and policies capable of creating more economic opportunities for young Nigerians.
The Regional President of the organisation, Ambassador Israel Akinola, made the call yesterday in Abuja when a delegation of the group paid a courtesy visit to the National Secretariat of the Social Democratic Party, SDP.
Akinola described the confederation as a platform for African youths committed to promoting effective leadership and governance, saying it had members across West African countries.
He said Nigeria required a new approach to governance, with greater emphasis on citizens’ welfare, accountability and opportunities for young people.
According to him, young Nigerians face challenges including economic hardship, unemployment and limited opportunities to develop and commercialise their skills and ideas.
Akinola, who said he had previously been involved with the SDP, explained that the visit was aimed at engaging the party intellectually on its ideas for addressing the country’s challenges.
He also called for stronger public-private partnerships, saying government policies should have tangible effects on citizens, particularly young people and those at the grassroots.
“We want what will make every African country experience leadership and governance at its peak,” he said.
Akinola criticised what he described as poor governance and alleged misuse of public resources by some political leaders, saying Nigeria needed leaders who would focus on delivering tangible results for citizens.
“We need people who understand what leadership truly is. And we need a government that the citizens would have a direct feeling of. We need a government that poor masses can actually have a direct feeling of,” he said.
He said the confederation was seeking to promote practical solutions to Nigeria’s challenges rather than merely criticising those in government.
Speaking, the SDP presidential candidate for the 2027 election, Prince Adewole Adebayo, thanked the delegation for the visit and highlighted the historical role of West African youth movements in the struggle for independence and self-government.
Adebayo urged the youths to take their engagement beyond political meetings and into communities across the country.
He said meaningful political participation depended on sustained interaction with citizens at the grassroots and polling-unit levels.
The presidential candidate also urged young people to build a common sense of purpose around national development and engage citizens honestly on issues affecting their communities and the future of the country.
Responding, the SDP Vice National Chairman, Senator Ugochukwu Uba, who represented the National Chairman, Professor Sadiq Gombe, said the party was committed to pursuing what he described as a different approach to governance.
Uba said the SDP’s programme was anchored on the Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy contained in Chapter Two of the Nigerian Constitution, particularly provisions relating to the welfare and security of citizens.
He said growing interest among young Nigerians in the party indicated increased engagement with its message and policy proposals.
According to him, the party’s recently presented manifesto contains programmes aimed at addressing some of Nigeria’s development challenges.
Uba argued that Nigeria had remained underdeveloped despite its human and material resources, saying leadership and governance remained central to addressing the situation.
He said the SDP was seeking a change in the country’s political culture through what he described as a different approach to governance and national development.
The visit provided an opportunity for the youth organisation and the SDP leadership to exchange views on governance, youth participation, economic opportunities and Nigeria’s development challenges.
