By Olasunkanmi Akoni
LAGOS — The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress, APC, on Friday inaugurated its campaign council for the 2027 general elections, with party leaders setting ambitious targets for voter mobilisation in support of President Bola Tinubu and the party’s governorship candidate, Dr. Obafemi Hamzat.
The campaign council, comprising more than 1,200 members, was inaugurated at the APC Secretariat on Acme Road, Ikeja, as the party formally commenced preparations for the elections.
The party’s campaign structure lists Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu as chairman, with Hamzat as deputy chairman, while former Senator Musiliu Obanikoro is the Director-General. Rasaq Ajala is the Deputy Director-General and Adekunle Olayinka is the Campaign Secretary.
The inauguration was attended by senior party leaders, including APC Lagos Chairman, Pastor Cornelius Ojelabi; leaders of the Governance Advisory Council, GAC; former governors Babatunde Fashola and Akinwunmi Ambode; Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly, Mudashiru Obasa; Senator Tokunbo Abiru; Senator Wasiu Eshilokun; former speakers of the state Assembly, Adeleke Mamora and Adeyemi Ikuforiji, among others.
Under the advisory structure, Prince Tajudeen Olusi is listed as Chairman of the Governance Advisory Council, while Sanwo-Olu is Advisory Council Chairman, with Fashola and Ambode as Co-Chairmen.
Other members of the advisory structure include the President’s Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila; Obasa and former Minister of Health, Adeleke Mamora.
The campaign council has directorates and sub-committees covering legal and compliance, party and inter-party affairs, administration and logistics, traditional institutions, diaspora engagement and residents’ associations.
Hamzat urges aggressive mobilisation
Addressing members of the council, Hamzat urged them to intensify grassroots mobilisation and campaign on the basis of the records and achievements of the APC-led administrations.
He highlighted what he described as economic milestones under the Tinubu administration, including tax reforms, increased agricultural and urea production, infrastructure development and efforts to tackle terrorism and kidnapping.
Hamzat said the party should be proud of its candidate and urged members not to be afraid to campaign for Tinubu.
He said: “We should be proud of our candidate. Our President has done the right things for this country. We should be very proud.
“We should not be fearful to go and campaign, because the President has stabilised the economy of this country.”
Hamzat also cited what he described as Nigeria’s trade surplus with the United States, attributing the development to increased agricultural and urea production.
He linked the development of the Lekki Free Trade Zone to Tinubu’s tenure as Lagos governor.
On tax reforms, Hamzat said the administration had undertaken changes to modernise the country’s tax system and commended members of the National Assembly for supporting the reforms.
He urged party supporters to mobilise voters for Tinubu, saying the party should improve on its previous electoral performance in Lagos.
“We have registered 7.3 million people in Lagos. As a member of our party, we cannot be voting only one million. We must do three, four million people to make sure that we galvanise votes for our President,” he said.
Hamzat also canvassed support for APC candidates at the senatorial, House of Representatives, governorship and state Assembly levels.
Speaking on Lagos, he described the state as a major contributor to Nigeria’s economy and highlighted its infrastructure projects, particularly the rail network.
He said the state’s economic importance made it necessary for residents to support candidates who, according to him, understood the state’s history, geography and development needs.
Hamzat said the campaign would be conducted under the banner, “Lagos Forward Together.”
Ojelabi demands grassroots mobilisation
The APC Lagos chairman, Ojelabi, urged all candidates to cooperate with the campaign council and conduct issue-based campaigns in line with the Electoral Act.
He described the inauguration as a milestone in the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections and charged council members to approach the assignment with discipline, accountability and a clear sense of purpose.
Ojelabi cautioned party members against complacency, noting that other political parties would also be working to win the elections.
With 118 days to the presidential election, he said the task before the campaign council was enormous and urged members to take the campaign to communities across the state.
He unveiled the strategy as “Operation Man Your Polling Booths”, with the party targeting mobilisation across the state’s 13,325 polling units.
Obanikoro urges unity
Obanikoro, the Director-General of the campaign council, urged members to work together and set aside personal differences ahead of the elections.
He also highlighted Hamzat’s public-service experience, including his service as a commissioner in Lagos, his work in the Federal Ministry of Works, Power and Housing and his tenure as deputy governor of Lagos State.
Obanikoro described Hamzat’s experience as a strong qualification for the governorship contest and commended the party for supporting his candidacy.
Olusi seeks united campaign
Speaking through former Deputy Governor Abiodun Ogunleye, Olusi commended the party’s leadership and expressed confidence in the campaign structure.
Ogunleye urged party members and political stakeholders to unite and intensify grassroots mobilisation across constituencies.
He said the party’s candidates possessed the experience and capacity required to represent the APC at various levels.
The inauguration ended with party supporters singing and expressing support for Tinubu and Hamzat ahead of the 2027 elections.
The post Lagos APC targets millions of votes for Tinubu, Hamzat appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
By Sola Ogundipe
Scientists at Israel’s Weizmann Institute of Science have uncovered a cellular mechanism that could deepen understanding of tissue regeneration while offering clues to why some cancers return after treatment.
Published in Nature Communications, the study identified a population of cells that begins the process of programmed cell death but survives to help rebuild severely damaged tissue. Named DARE cells, they multiplied rapidly and replenished nearly half of the damaged tissue within 48 hours in experiments involving fruit fly larvae.
The discovery sheds light on compensatory proliferation, a biological process in which surviving cells multiply to replace those lost through injury. However, the same survival mechanism could potentially enable cancer cells to withstand treatment.
Apoptosis, commonly known as programmed cell death, helps the body eliminate damaged, ageing and unwanted cells. Caspases, a group of enzymes, initiate and execute the process.
Research led by Prof. Eli Arama of the Weizmann Institute’s Department of Molecular Genetics has shown that caspases can also perform functions beyond cell destruction. His team suspected they might contribute to tissue regeneration.
Led by Dr. Tslil Braun, the researchers recreated a classic 1970s experiment in which radiation-damaged fly larvae regenerated functional wings. Using modern genetic tools, they tracked cells that activated the early stages of apoptosis but survived. “We set out to identify cells that push the self-destruct button but survive anyway,” Braun explained.
The researchers discovered DARE cells, which not only survived radiation but multiplied and repaired nearly half of the damaged tissue within 48 hours. They also identified a second population, called NARE cells. Unlike DARE cells, NARE cells had not activated their initiator caspase, although they survived and contributed to regeneration.
The distinction was crucial. When DARE cells were removed, compensatory proliferation disappeared. The researchers also found that signals from dying cells activated DARE cells, triggering rapid tissue repair. The study found that apoptosis begins normally in DARE cells. However, the process stops before the effector caspases can complete cellular destruction.
The researchers linked this interruption to a molecular motor protein that appears to tether the initiator caspase to the cell membrane, preventing activation of the enzymes responsible for completing cell death. When the team silenced the motor protein, DARE cells died and tissue regeneration was impaired.
Arama noted that overactivation of the same protein had previously been associated with cancerous tumour growth, raising the possibility that cancer cells could exploit a similar mechanism to evade apoptosis.
The finding does not establish that this process causes cancer recurrence in humans, but it provides a pathway for further investigation.
The scientists next examined whether DARE cells could pass their resistance to death to their descendants. After exposing the tissue to radiation a second time, they found that cell deaths during the initial hours were half those recorded after the first exposure. Most of the cells that died belonged to the NARE population. Descendants of DARE cells were reportedly seven times more resistant to cell death than cells in the original tissue.
“We wanted to understand whether resistance to death is inherited by the descendants of death-resistant cells that survived the initial irradiation,” Arama said. The finding may help explain how surviving cells acquire characteristics that allow them to withstand subsequent injury. In cancer, however, similar resistance could potentially enable tumour cells to survive treatment and contribute to recurrence.
The researchers stressed that their experiments were conducted in fruit flies, and the relevance to human cancers remains to be established. The study also revealed a feedback system that appears to prevent excessive regeneration.
DARE cells release growth signals that promote the multiplication of nearby NARE cells. In return, NARE cells release signals that inhibit DARE cell growth. This negative feedback loop allows tissue repair to proceed while helping prevent uncontrolled proliferation.
According to Arama, understanding these mechanisms could eventually support efforts to accelerate healthy tissue regeneration and improve cancer treatment strategies. “Many cancers originate in epithelial cells that have lost normal growth control, and many traditional cancer treatments aim to cause them to self-destruct through apoptosis,” he said. “Our findings pave the way for understanding why such treatments sometimes fail and how they could be improved.”
The discovery offers a new perspective on the body’s response to injury. A mechanism that helps healthy tissue recover could, under different circumstances, provide dangerous cells with a means of survival. The next challenge for researchers is to understand how to harness the regenerative benefits without enabling cancer cells to escape treatment.
The post Cells that cheat Death: New clue to why some cancers return appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Henry Umoru
ABUJA — National Leader of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Senator Seriake Dickson, has described the Court of Appeal’s decision upholding the party’s registration as a protection of Nigeria’s democratic space.
The Court of Appeal, sitting in Abuja, had set aside the June 26 judgment of the Federal High Court, Lokoja, which reversed an earlier decision directing the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to register the NDC as a political party.
The appellate court’s decision followed an appeal by the NDC against the judgment delivered by Justice Isah Dashen of the Federal High Court, Lokoja.
In a statement posted on his Facebook page on Friday, Dickson commended the judiciary, particularly Justices Mohammed Danjuma and Muslim Sule Hassan, for what he described as upholding the integrity of the judicial system and expanding the scope of multiparty democratic participation in Nigeria.
Dickson said the Court of Appeal had set aside the Lokoja judgment, which, according to him, had purported to deregister the NDC.
He said: “Today, the Court of Appeal, sitting in Abuja, has set aside the judgment of the Federal High Court, Lokoja, delivered by Justice Isah Dashen a few months ago, which purported to order the deregistration of our party, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC).
“In a judgment delivered by the presiding Justice, Justice Mohammed Danjuma and read by Justice Hassan, the Court ruled in favour of allowing our appeal, which challenged the faulty ruling of the Federal High Court, Lokoja, and accordingly, set aside Justice Dashen’s judgment.”
The NDC leader further commended Justices Danjuma and Hassan, saying their decision had, in his view, strengthened multiparty participation.
Dickson said the party was established to expand the frontiers of multiparty democracy, adding that the earlier Lokoja judgment had created uncertainty over its participation in the electoral process.
He said: “Happily, today, by the decision of the Court of Appeal, the Nigerian democratic space has been protected, and the NDC’s right to participate in all political activities as a registered political party has been upheld.”
He congratulated members and candidates of the party and thanked Nigerians for their support.
Dickson also declared that the NDC’s registration remained valid and that the party and its candidates would participate in the 2027 elections.
“Everyone should now focus on the campaigns, prepare for the elections, and focus on the task ahead,” he said.
He added that the party remained confident in its message, members and candidates, while expressing optimism about its participation in the forthcoming elections.
The dispute over the NDC’s registration followed a December 10, 2025 judgment directing INEC to register the party. On June 26, 2026, however, Justice Dashen set aside that judgment after an application by the Peace Movement Party, which argued that its interests, including those relating to the party’s symbol, had been affected without it being joined in the original suit.
The Court of Appeal has now overturned that June 26 decision, with the appellate court holding, among other things, that the Federal High Court could not sit on appeal over its own final judgment.
The post NDC: Appeal Court protected Nigeria’s democracy – Dickson appeared first on Vanguard News.

By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa
Former President Goodluck Jonathan has called for the harmonisation of structures and salary scales across Nigeria’s federal and state civil services.
Jonathan made the call in Yenagoa during the foundation-laying and fund-raising ceremony for the Bayelsa State Association of Retired Permanent Secretaries’ Secretariat Complex.
The former President commended the retired permanent secretaries for the initiative, noting that the calibre of personnel in the Bayelsa State public service compared favourably with their counterparts at the federal level.
Jonathan recalled that during his tenure as governor of Bayelsa State, he restructured the civil service by creating Grade Level 17 for directors who previously retired at Level 16.
He said the adjustment was intended to ensure that directors in the state civil service enjoyed the same grade level as their counterparts in the federal civil service.
Jonathan said, “The civil service of the federation is the civil service of the federation, whether you are working at the state level or you are working at the federal level, and I believe that the salary structure should be the same because it is the same government.
“A professor lecturing in a federal university should receive the same salary as a professor lecturing in a state university. So why should a director in the state be on Level 16 while a director at the federal level is on Level 17?”
He recalled that after discovering the disparity in the grade levels of directors in Bayelsa State, he directed the Secretary to the State Government, Head of Service and Accountant General to restructure the service and create Grade Level 17 for directors.
According to him, those previously on Level 16 were reclassified as deputy directors and promoted accordingly.
Jonathan said the proposed secretariat complex would serve the retired permanent secretaries and the wider public, describing the project as a worthwhile contribution to the state and the country.
“I have to thank all of you and I appreciate you for your service to the states and, by implication, to the country. And for this noble project that you are doing, I commend you,” he said.
He added that the facility would serve not only government officials but also private citizens.
Also speaking, Bayelsa State Governor Douye Diri, represented by the Head of Service, Dr Ebiye Sawyer, pledged government support for the project and commended the retired officials for their vision and dedication.
Sawyer said the project represented more than the laying of a foundation stone, describing it as the beginning of a lasting legacy for retired permanent secretaries in the state.
“On behalf of His Excellency, Senator Douye Diri, the necessary support will come from government towards completing this project,” he said.
In his welcome address, Chairman of the association, King Collins Ebi Daniel, described the proposed complex as an institutional edifice designed to preserve the legacy of public service.
He said the facility would comprise administrative offices, event halls, conference rooms and recreational facilities.
King Daniel disclosed that the project was estimated to cost N500 million and was expected to be completed within two years.
Other dignitaries at the event, including the Chairman of the occasion, Professor Imiri, a former Director-General of the Nigerian Law School, Yenagoa Campus, and the Chief Launcher, Chief Maxwell Oko, pledged their support.
They urged the association to consider developing the facility into a policy institute that could contribute to state and national development.
Also present were traditional ruler, King Amalate Turner, and the Senator representing Bayelsa East Senatorial District, Senator Benson Agadaga.

items.content:
By Udeme Akpan, Energy Editor
The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has threatened to revoke petroleum prospecting licences (PPLs) whose holders fail to meet their statutory work commitments, giving affected operators until October 31, 2026 to disclose challenges delaying the development of their acreages.
The warning covers holders of licences awarded under the 2020 Marginal Field Bid Round, 2022/2023 Mini Bid Round and 2024 Licensing Round.
In a circular dated September 14, 2026 and signed by the Commission Chief Executive, Mrs Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, NUPRC said it was moving to enforce the “drill-or-drop” provisions of the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021 as part of efforts to increase oil and gas production.
The Commission warned that it would enforce the provisions against non-performing acreages, including “refusing extension, requiring relinquishment, calling in the work performance security and commencing revocation proceedings.”
NUPRC said: “Acreage is held to be worked, and acreage that is not worked within its term returns to the Federal Government.”
The regulator said the licences carry specific obligations covering approved work programmes, minimum work programmes and work performance security, adding that continued ownership of the acreages was conditional on meeting those obligations within the prescribed licence terms.
However, NUPRC stressed that the enforcement drive was intended to unlock production rather than simply dispossess operators of their acreages.
The Commission stated: “The Commission’s objective is to increase production, not forfeiture.”
It acknowledged that operators could face legitimate challenges in executing their obligations, including financing, rig availability, security, host-community engagement, infrastructure, regulatory approvals and partner arrangements.
Accordingly, it directed affected licensees facing such constraints to notify the Commission by October 31, 2026.
The submissions, according to NUPRC, must state “the level of compliance with its licence obligations including the execution of its approved work programme,” the specific constraints affecting implementation, proposed mitigation measures and revised timelines.
The Commission said it was prepared, within the limits of its statutory mandate, to help resolve issues affecting timely execution of licence obligations.
It cautioned, however, that engagement with NUPRC would not suspend the term of a licence or relieve operators of their statutory obligations.
“Internal disagreement will not excuse failure to meet licence obligations,” the Commission warned, particularly in relation to disputes among partners.
NUPRC urged licensees to ensure that partnership and financing agreements clearly address participating interests, operatorship, deadlock, cash calls, default, assignment, change of control and dispute-resolution mechanisms that allow operations to continue.
The Commission said it could facilitate discussions where such intervention falls within its mandate, but would not assume jurisdiction beyond its statutory powers or displace agreed dispute-resolution mechanisms or the jurisdiction of the courts.
It also clarified that the latest circular was “general advisory” and did not constitute a formal notice of default under the PIA or its subsidiary instruments.
Under the PIA, the Commission said, a PPL is granted for a defined initial exploration period, with any extension dependent on the terrain of the acreage and the fulfilment of applicable work commitments.
NUPRC said the enforcement of the drill-or-drop provisions was therefore aimed at ensuring that licensed oil and gas acreages are actively explored and developed rather than held without corresponding investment and operational activity.

By Golok Nanmwa, Jos
Gunmen on Friday night stormed a busy vegetable market in Mangu town, Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State, killing three persons and injuring scores of others.
The attack occurred at about 8:30 p.m. as traders and buyers were preparing to close for the day, sending people into panic and forcing them to flee in different directions.
The ensuing stampede reportedly left several other persons injured as traders, buyers and passers-by scrambled to escape the scene.
President of the Mwaghavul Development Association, MDA, Bulus Dabit, who confirmed the incident, said the gunmen opened fire on a vehicle leaving the vegetable market, killing two women and a young man.
Dabit said the identities of the victims were not immediately known, adding that several passers-by were seriously injured and were being referred to the Jos University Teaching Hospital, JUTH, for treatment.
He said, “At about 8 p.m. on Friday, gunmen shot several times at a vehicle leaving the vegetable market in Mangu, killing two women and a young man.
“The names of the victims are not known yet. “Several passers-by were seriously injured and are being referred to the Jos University Teaching Hospital for treatment.”
Another source, John Haruna, who also confirmed the incident, said several persons sustained injuries during the attack.
Haruna said the sudden shooting created panic at the market, with people running in different directions in an attempt to escape, resulting in more persons sustaining injuries.
Dabit condemned the attack and urged security agencies to deploy intelligence and technology to identify and apprehend the perpetrators.
He said, “Security agencies must leverage intelligence and technology to apprehend the perpetrators of these dastardly acts, as they would not be far from the scene of the crime.”
The attack came only hours after the MDA raised concerns over continued threats to communities in Mangu, claiming that more than 750 Mwaghavul people had been killed in attacks since 2023.
The association in a statement made available to newsmen on Friday and signed by its Director of Public Affairs, Friday Derwam, after a joint meeting of its national executive, women’s leadership and youth leadership had earlier called for an immediate investigation into the recent killings of people in the council.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Dickson Omobola
Nigerian passenger, Abdullahi Salisu, has alleged that a dispute with Ethiopian Airlines over a ticket change and refund has left him stranded at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, since June 29.
Salisu, who was scheduled to fly from Abuja to Cairo, Egypt, on June 29, said he had booked the ticket on June 17 but could not obtain the required visa/OK-to-Board clearance before his scheduled departure.
He said he visited the Ethiopian Airlines office at the airport on June 27 to request that his flight be rescheduled to July 1.
He told Vanguard that a staff member changed the date but did not initially inform him that he would be required to pay a fare difference and change fee.
He said he was later informed that he would have to pay more than N474,000 for the change, which he could not afford.
He lamented that although he involved the Nigeria Civil Aviation Authority, NCAA, in the matter, the agency could not resolve the issue.
Speaking to Vanguard, Salisu said: “I have been stranded in the airport since June 29. I booked my ticket on June 17 to fly on June 29. On June 27, I walked into the Ethiopian Airlines office at the airport to inform them that they needed to reschedule my flight for July 1.
“So, one Ethiopian Airlines staff member changed it and he never told me that I had to pay any fare change. When he had already changed it, he told me that I had to pay. That’s N474,000 plus. I told them to change it to its actual date because I could not afford to change it.
“They then told me that my seat was already occupied. They told me not to bother and that I should just come on June 29 for me to board.
“I came as early as 8 to the airport. They had not even come to their office until 10 o’clock when they opened their counter. Then I told them that I had come for the trip. They then told me that there was no economy seat. I had to pay for a business seat.
“I told them, how could you tell me that? It’s you that told me that I should come on my actual day to fly. But why are you telling me that there’s no economy seat to give me unless I buy another business-class seat for N400,000, N700,000, N800,000 or something?
“But I checked their online app and I saw that there were many seats unoccupied in economy class.
“I was with them at the airport until the time of the departure of the plane. So, I reported to the NCAA counter at the departure hall. They told me that I could request a refund. So, I told them that I had even purchased refund protection with that ticket. One of the NCAA staff and I went into the office and explained.
“They (Ethiopian Airlines staff) told me that I could apply for a refund, but they couldn’t issue it by themselves. I had to do it online. On that same day, June 29, I sent them a request. But they told me that my ticket was non-refundable.
“I said, how could you say that my ticket was non-refundable when I purchased refund protection? Even their staff at the Abuja office told me that it was refundable. At last, they told me that what made their ticket non-refundable was that I bought it at the lowest fare.
“In order to catch them red-handed, I booked another ticket, the lowest one again. Then I told them to confirm whether it was refundable or non-refundable. They confirmed that it was refundable.
“Since that time, I have been sleeping at the airport departure area. And on Monday, they now dragged me out, saying that they had seen my bag on CCTV camera. I had gone to eat and returned when I found out that my bag was not there. I had to go and recover it at AVSEC. It is either they (Ethiopian Airlines) refund me or get me another air ticket without any fare charge. It is because I couldn’t return to Egypt before the date I was given by my boss that I lost my job there. I worked at Crispy Chicken Restaurant in Giza as a cleaner.”
Ethiopian Airlines react
Reacting to the allegations, Ethiopian Airlines told Vanguard that on “June 27, 2026, the passenger visited our airport office requesting a date change because he was unable to secure the required Visa/OK-to-Board for Cairo due to an issue involving his travel agent. To avoid a no-show, he requested that his travel date be changed from June 29 to July 1, 2026.
“Our team advised the passenger to wait, as there was still a possibility that the visa issue could be resolved before his original departure date. However, he insisted that this would not be possible and requested that the date change be processed immediately. Accordingly, the booking was changed as requested, and the applicable change fee and fare difference were communicated to him.
“The passenger disputed the charges, stating that he had been informed over the phone that no payment would be required. It was explained to him several times that the amount consisted of the applicable change fee and fare difference. Despite these explanations, he remained unwilling to pay and continued to request a free date change.
“The passenger later requested to be reinstated on his original travel date after it had already been changed at his request. Upon checking availability, it was found that the ADD–CAI sector was fully booked in Economy Class, with only Business Class seats available. He was informed that his original booking class was no longer available and that any alternative class would require payment of the applicable fare difference. He was also advised to come to the airport on the day of departure in case seats became available in his original booking class.
“On the day of departure, Economy Class remained fully booked. The passenger spoke with our staff and was again advised of the situation. He subsequently approached NCAA officials, alleging that he was willing to pay but that we had refused to assist him. The matter was explained to the NCAA representatives, who understood the situation and also clarified it to the passenger.
“Shortly before counter closure, we were able to secure availability in a lower booking class at a reduced additional cost and advised the passenger of the revised amount in the presence of the NCAA representative. However, the passenger again declined to make the payment. He later sought assistance from another NCAA official, to whom the same explanation was provided.
“After the flight departed, the passenger returned and acknowledged that he understood the situation and the explanations given.
“Regarding the Refund Protection purchased by the passenger, the policy applies only under specific circumstances (conditions attached). As this was a voluntary date change requested by the passenger, the Refund Protection is not applicable.”
The post Ethiopian Airlines fare dispute strands passenger at Abuja airport for two months appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
Brentford exposed Chelsea’s defensive problems to inflict a damaging 3-0 defeat on Friday that gives Xabi Alonso plenty to ponder over a three-week international break.
After a promising start to life under the former Real Madrid coach, Chelsea have picked up just one point from their last three league games.
Goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fabio Carvalho took unbeaten Brentford above their west London neighbours and up to third in the table.
Chelsea had quickly earned the reputation as the Premier League’s great entertainers under Alonso with their opening four games containing 19 goals.
But the loss of Joao Pedro to a knee injury subdued the Blues’ free-flowing attack as Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers were comfortably kept in check by the Bees.
Alonso said after last weekend’s 2-2 draw against Hull he was hoping for more “boring” games going forward.
The Spaniard sought control as he made four changes in all, handing Jordan Henderson his first Chelsea start against the 36-year-old’s former club.
Alonso got his wish during a flat first half in which neither goalkeeper was seriously tested, but Brentford were the more threatening side in the second period.
The visitors’ frailty from set-pieces led to the opening goal when Jannick Schuster rose highest to meet Mikkel Damsgaard’s corner and Anthony was left with a simple task to head into an unguarded net just after the hour mark.
Chelsea’s response was muted and as they pushed forward in search of an equaliser, Alonso’s men were picked off on the counter-attack.
Kevin Schade should have scored the second goal himself when played clean through on Emi Martinez.
But even after the Argentine goalkeeper spread himself to save, the rebound fell kindly for Thiago to end his goal drought.
The Brazilian netted 25 times last season, earning a shock call-up to Carlo Ancelotti’s World Cup squad as a result.
Thiago has looked shorn in the early weeks of the campaign and tore off his shirt in celebration after netting for the first time in the Premier League this season.
Chelsea have conceded at least twice in all five league games under Alonso and there was further punishment to come in stoppage time.
Schade’s low cross was deflected into the path of Carvalho who fired high past Martinez to leave Brentford boss Keith Andrews yelling into the night sky in delight.
Brentford, who also beat Tottenham 3-0 on the opening weekend of the season, sit behind only defending champions Arsenal and Manchester City at the top of the table.
By contrast, Chelsea were handed another reminder of the gap Alonso must bridge to make them title contenders once more.

items.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi
ABUJA: Ahead of the 2027 presidential election, the Nigeria Forward Project has urged political stakeholders in Northern Nigeria to respect the principle of power rotation and allow President Bola Tinubu from the South to complete his eight-year presidential tenure before seeking to reclaim power. 
The positions were canvassed on Friday in Abuja at the formal unveiling of Nigeria Forward NF, a mass mobilisation platform established to promote national unity, citizen engagement and continuity in governance ahead of the 2027 general elections and beyond, built around the belief that sustaining the gains of the administration’s Renewed Hope reforms is a collective responsibility.
Speaking at the event, Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology and a Convener of the movement, Dr Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh, said the Federal Government’s ongoing reforms were designed to move Nigeria “from infrastructure and connectivity to production, jobs and prosperity”.
He described the administration’s development trajectory as a progression “from reform to infrastructure, infrastructure to connectivity, connectivity to production, production to jobs and jobs to prosperity.”
Udeh said Nigeria Forward would bridge the gap between government policies and citizens by providing Nigerians with information on projects, investments, opportunities and the impact of government programmes in their communities, stressing that Nigeria’s development story, particularly that of the North, should not be reduced to political slogans or isolated project announcements.
Speaking at the event, the Co-Convener of the project and Kano State Commissioner for Information and Internal Affairs, Comrade Ibrahim Waiya, argued that the North should not seek to return to the presidency after only one term of the current administration, insisting that allowing Tinubu to complete an eight-year tenure would promote continuity and give the government the opportunity to consolidate its policies.
He urged Nigerians to focus on consolidating what he described as the gains of the administration rather than allowing electoral competition to reopen sectional divisions.
Waiya said Tinubu inherited significant economic and security challenges on assuming office in 2023, and that the administration had since introduced measures which, in his assessment, were putting the country on a different trajectory.
Urging Nigerians to look beyond what he called primordial sentiments deployed by opposition politicians for electoral purposes, he cited local government autonomy, increased financial resources accruing to sub-national governments, and moves towards establishing state police structures as reforms capable of strengthening governance and improving security.
He disclosed that Kano State had already set up a state police implementation committee, which he said would contribute to job creation and enhance security once fully implemented.
Waiya, however, cautioned that addressing poverty in Northern Nigeria should not be regarded solely as the President’s responsibility, arguing that democracy required citizens, governments and other stakeholders to engage and demand solutions.
“Democracy is a social project,” he said, stressing that Nigeria Forward was established to encourage citizens to match political discussions with practical action.
He described the platform as a “rainbow coalition” belonging to Nigerians rather than any particular political party, and called on citizens to rally around the national interest, insisting Nigeria had the potential to become a great country if its people remained united and committed to moving the nation forward.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
By Yinka Kolawole
The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) has described the further moderation in Nigeria’s headline inflation rate to 15.39 per cent in August 2026, from 15.43 per cent in July, as a positive but fragile development, urging the Federal Government to shift attention from merely managing inflation to tackling the structural costs that make local manufacturing expensive.
In a statement on Friday, MAN Director-General, Segun Ajayi-Kadir, said the marginal 0.04 percentage-point decline was important for business planning, investment and consumer welfare. However, he noted that a lower inflation rate does not necessarily translate into lower production costs for manufacturers.
According to the association, manufacturers continue to contend with high energy costs, logistics challenges, foreign exchange-related expenses, elevated raw material prices and multiple fiscal and regulatory charges.
“The current inflation trend should therefore provide an opportunity for the government to implement measures that reduce the cost of production and improve productivity.
“Manufacturers are often unable to pass the full increase in production costs to consumers because of weak purchasing power, leaving profit margins under pressure and increasing working capital requirements,” Ajayi-Kadir stated.
He added that persistent high energy, financing and logistics costs were keeping investment decisions cautious, while some firms could be forced to reduce production where the cost of additional shifts or inputs becomes commercially unsustainable.
The development, MAN warned, could also weaken the competitiveness of locally produced goods against cheaper imports, constrain capacity utilisation and limit employment expansion.
To reverse the trend, MAN called for measures to reduce industrial energy costs, including dedicated electricity supply to major industrial clusters, priority gas access for industrial users, incentives for captive power and renewable energy investments, and a review of electricity tariff structures affecting productive industries.
The association urged the government to prioritise the rehabilitation of major transport corridors linking ports, industrial clusters, agricultural production zones and markets, while eliminating unnecessary road charges and overlapping transport levies.
It also recommended a targeted, long-term manufacturing financing window at below-market rates to support working capital, machinery acquisition and productivity-enhancing investments, particularly for MSME manufacturers.
MAN said the objective should be to create conditions that enable manufacturers to produce more at lower cost, attract greater investment, create jobs and compete more effectively.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
EVEE has showcased the S1 Air Self Drive at PAPS 2026, presenting an experimental version of its existing electric scooter that can move and remain balanced without a rider controlling it.
The prototype is based on the regular EVEE S1 Air but adds dedicated motorised hardware and a control system for self-driving and balancing functions.
EVEE says the technology is still in the research and development phase, with no confirmed launch date or price.
The company also claims that the model would become Pakistan’s first self-driving electric scooter if it eventually reaches production.
Based on the Regular S1 Air
The S1 Air Self Drive uses the same basic platform as the standard S1 Air, with the key difference being the additional hardware required for autonomous movement and balancing.
The regular S1 Air uses a 2,200W motor, offers a claimed 90–110km range, and has a top speed of around 65–70 km/h.
It uses a 76.8V 32Ah Phylion lithium battery.
The regular EVEE S1 Air Lithium is currently priced at Rs. 319,900.

What Makes It Different?
The main addition is the self-driving system, supported by additional motor hardware that lets the scooter move independently during demonstrations.
The balancing system also lets the scooter stay upright while operating without a rider.
EVEE has not yet disclosed the complete sensor setup, control software, or final hardware architecture behind the system.
That means the S1 Air Self Drive should currently be viewed as a development-stage prototype rather than a production-ready scooter.

EVEE has not announced when, or if, the self-driving version of the S1 Air will reach showrooms.

The University of Notre Dame has opened applications for the Deans’ Fellowship 2027 for students applying to master’s and PhD programs in the United States. The fellowship is available to incoming graduate students across academic fields.
Selected students will receive financial support through stipends, health insurance coverage, and tuition scholarship assistance, depending on their academic program.
Doctoral fellows can receive a stipend of $43,500 to $44,000 for 12 months, while master’s fellows can receive $20,000 to $30,000 for nine months.

The University of Notre Dame awards the Deans’ Fellowship to entering doctoral students who show strong academic performance and potential for graduate studies and professional development.
Around 15 new doctoral and master’s students receive the fellowship each year. PhD fellows receive a stipend between $43,500 and $44,000 for 12 months, depending on their academic program.
The fellowship can support doctoral students for up to five years. Fellows also receive full coverage of the University’s health insurance premium.
Deans’ Fellowship for Master’s Students
The Deans’ Fellowship also supports entering master’s students at the University of Notre Dame. The fellowship is available across different graduate fields for eligible students.
Master’s fellows receive a stipend ranging from $20,000 to $30,000 for nine months, depending on their academic program.

What Does the Deans’ Fellowship Cover?
The Deans’ Fellowship provides financial support to selected graduate students at the University of Notre Dame.
Doctoral fellows receive a stipend ranging from $43,500 to $44,000 for 12 months, depending on their academic program. The fellowship can support PhD students for up to five years.
Master’s fellows receive a stipend ranging from $20,000 to $30,000 for nine months. The exact amount depends on the student’s academic program.
The fellowship also covers the full cost of the university’s health insurance premium for selected students.
Tuition scholarship support is also available, but the amount varies by academic program. The relevant graduate program decides and awards this tuition support.
Eligibility Criteria
The Deans’ Fellowship is available for entering master’s and PhD students at the University of Notre Dame. Applicants must apply for admission to a graduate program and meet the fellowship requirements to be considered.
The fellowship supports students who show strong academic performance and potential for success in graduate studies and their future professional careers.
Applicants must be U.S. citizens or permanent residents to qualify for the fellowship. Eligible candidates must also meet at least one of the fellowship’s background criteria related to students from groups that have been historically underrepresented in higher education.

The University of Southern Queensland (UniSQ) has announced the International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship 2027 for international students who plan to start or continue PhD studies in Australia.
Offering complete financial support, the fully funded scholarship provides a stipend of AUD $39,000 ($28,000) per year and covers tuition fees for up to three years of full-time PhD study.
Candidates who have already completed part of their doctoral degree can receive funding for the remaining eligible study period.
Through this scholarship, UniSQ supports research projects that align with its flagship research areas. Applicants must first complete the separate PhD admission process before applying for scholarship consideration.
Interested students must submit their applications for the International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship 2027 by September 27, 2026.

International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship 2027
The University of Southern Queensland offers this scholarship to international students pursuing a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in 2027.
The opportunity is available across different research areas, but applicants must ensure that their proposed research aligns with UniSQ’s flagship research priorities.
Candidates can apply for both stipend and tuition fee support through a single online scholarship application.
What Does the UniSQ PhD Scholarship Cover?
Selected scholars receive financial support throughout their PhD studies at the University of Southern Queensland.
The scholarship provides an annual AUD $39,000 stipend to help students manage living expenses during their doctoral research.
In addition, UniSQ covers tuition fees for up to three years of full-time equivalent study. For students who have already started their PhD, completed study periods will reduce the remaining scholarship duration.
Eligibility Criteria
The scholarship is available for international students who plan to commence or continue a PhD program at the University of Southern Queensland in 2027.
Applicants must first complete the PhD admission process before they become eligible for scholarship consideration.
Candidates should propose research that matches UniSQ’s flagship research areas and demonstrate strong academic and research potential.
Selection Criteria
The selection process considers:
Academic achievement and qualifications.
Research capability, including publications, presentations, and research experience.
Quality and relevance of the proposed research project.
Alignment with UniSQ research priorities.
Experience and suitability of the proposed supervisory team.
Documents Required
Candidates need to provide the following documents:
Statement of Claim completed by the student and supervisor.
Curriculum vitae (CV), including research publications and presentations.
Preliminary Research Thesis Topic Proposal.
Proof of citizenship.
Academic qualifications, including degree certificates and transcripts.
Opportunities for PhD Scholars
The UniSQ scholarship provides international students with financial support while completing advanced research in Australia.
The annual stipend helps students manage living costs, while tuition fee coverage reduces the financial burden of doctoral studies.
Selected scholars can continue their research in areas linked with UniSQ’s flagship research priorities and work with experienced academic supervisors.
How to Apply for UniSQ Scholarship 2027
Applicants should first apply for admission to a PhD program at the University of Southern Queensland.
After completing the admission process, eligible candidates can submit their scholarship application through the university’s online portal.
Students should review the latest admission and scholarship requirements before applying.

Under the revised token system, eligible 800cc car users will receive one token every 10 days. Each token covers 10 litres of petrol at a Rs. 100-per-litre discount, providing Rs. 1,000 in relief per token.

The Remick Graduate Fellowship provides financial support to selected PhD students at the University of Notre Dame. The fellowship covers the full tuition fee for eligible students throughout their graduate studies.

Applicants must meet the admission requirements set by their selected engineering graduate program. The listed academic requirement includes a minimum GPA of 3.0.
Notre Dame’s graduate departments review eligible students for the Remick Graduate Fellowship. The departments nominate suitable candidates, and the university selects fellows through a competitive review process.

items.author: Shahabullah Yusufzai
items.content:
At least 21 people, including 15 police officials, were martyred on Friday when an explosives-laden vehicle detonated near a mosque in Kohat Police Lines, followed by terrorists storming the compound and attacking police facilities, according to an initial incident report issued by DHQ Hospital Kohat medical superintendent and the district health officer.
All seven attackers were killed in the explosion and the gun battle that followed, police said in a statement.
The interior ministry said the "cowardly actions" of the attackers could not weaken the "nation's firm resolve".
The report said the blast occurred at approximately 1:20pm during Friday prayers at a mosque located at Police Lines on Hangu Road in Kohat, followed by a terrorist attack involving around five to seven terrorists.
Of the 21 people killed, 15 were police personnel and six were civilians. The report identified one of the deceased civilians as Dr Israel Khan Aurakzai, Chief District Specialist (Paediatrics) at Liaqat Memorial Hospital, Kohat.
It further said 103 injured people had been received at the two hospitals, including 13 at Liaqat Memorial Hospital and 90 at DHQ Hospital Kohat. The injured comprised 73 police personnel and 30 civilians.
Of the total injured, 34 were admitted for treatment, while five patients underwent laparotomy, a surgical procedure involving an incision into the abdomen.
The report said four of the patients who underwent laparotomy had been referred to tertiary care facilities in Peshawar for further treatment.
It added that the situation was being closely monitored and all possible medical assistance was being provided to the injured at the relevant health facilities.
According to the police, seven armed terrorists infiltrated the police lines following vehicle-borne improvised explosive device (VBIED) detonated at the boundary wall near the mosque. The police said six terrorists, including the suicide bomber, had been killed so far. Initially, a suicide attacker blew himself up near the Special Branch building after the explosion, it added.
Ittihadul Mujahideen Pakistan (IMP), led by Afghanistan-based Hafiz Gul Bahadur, has claimed responsibility for the deadly bombing and rampage involving multiple attackers. Islamabad has repeatedly asked the Taliban regime to deny the use of Afghan soil for terrorist attacks inside Pakistan. However, the de facto rulers in Kabul have been reluctant to take action against terrorist groups operating from their territory.
In a statement, K-P Police Public Relations director said the operation against the terrorists had entered its final stages under the direct supervision of the K-P Inspector General of Police Zulfiqar Hameed, with security personnel carrying out a clearance operation in the area.
Hameed said authorities were tracing the terrorists and their facilitators and would ensure their complete elimination. He stated that police and the Counter Terrorism Department were engaged in an operation against Fitna al-Khawarij inside the police lines compound.
"Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa Police is standing as an iron wall against terrorism. Cowardly attacks cannot weaken our resolve," he said. "The blood of the martyrs will not go to waste. The terrorists and their facilitators will meet an exemplary fate," he added.
Earlier, Rescue 1122 spokesperson Bilal Ahmed Faizi stated that 14 ambulances, rescue vehicles, a recovery vehicle and more than 45 rescue personnel were participating in the operation.
District Emergency Officer Noor-ul-Amin was personally supervising the rescue operation, he said, adding that relief activities would continue until the operation was completed. He added that further details would be issued as more information was received.
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif strongly condemned the bomb blast in Old Police Lines, Kohat, Radio Pakistan reported on Friday.
In separate messages, they expressed deep grief and sorrow over the injuries suffered by several people in the blast.
The president said that the complete elimination of Fitna-al-Khawarij and terrorists operating with foreign backing was inevitable for national security.
The prime minister sought a report from the authorities concerned on the blast and directed them to expedite relief operations.

items.author: Kamran Yousaf
items.content:
Pakistan is preparing to send another high-level delegation to Tehran in a fresh diplomatic push aimed at breaking the stalemate between Iran and the United States as well as containing rapidly escalating tensions between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis, officials said on Friday.
There was no official confirmation of the planned visit from Islamabad or Tehran. However, a senior government official told The Express Tribune that another visit to the Iranian capital was being planned and could take place very soon.
The official did not disclose the composition of the delegation, but diplomatic and government sources indicated that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi was likely to lead the delegation.
The proposed visit comes at a particularly sensitive moment for Pakistan, which has been trying to maintain its role as a bridge between Iran and the United States while simultaneously managing its growing security commitments to Saudi Arabia.
Pakistan's diplomatic efforts have now acquired another dimension as fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthis has intensified.
Saudi Arabia and the Houthis exchanged fresh attacks this week, with Riyadh carrying out airstrikes against Houthi positions while the group launched drone and missile attacks against Saudi territory. The escalation has raised concerns about the security of Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping routes around the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb.
The latest diplomatic initiative also follows a telephone conversation between Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Asim Munir. Iranian media reported that the two discussed the latest regional developments while Araghchi was in Beijing.
According to the Financial Times, Munir subsequently conveyed Pakistan's concerns to Iranian officials over the Houthi attacks and urged Tehran to restrain the group. The report said Islamabad had warned that the situation could have implications for Pakistan's defence commitments to Saudi Arabia.
Pakistan's position has become more consequential following the signing of the Pakistan-Saudi Arabia-Türkiye defence agreement in August, under which an attack on one of the signatories is to be treated as an attack on all.
Islamabad has since repeatedly stressed its commitment to Saudi Arabia's security. On Friday, Director General Inter-Services Public Relations Lieutenant General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry said Pakistan's commitment to the kingdom's security was "unconditional", amid the escalating Houthi attacks.
The possibility of Pakistani military involvement, however, has not been formally raised by Riyadh, and Islamabad has continued to emphasise diplomatic efforts.
The proposed Naqvi visit could, therefore, serve two parallel objectives: conveying Pakistan's concerns to Tehran over the Houthi escalation while also trying to revive the broader diplomatic track between Iran and Washington.
Pakistan has already made several mediation attempts during the seven-month-old conflict. Islamabad hosted indirect contacts between the United States and Iran and has continued to argue that the dispute cannot be resolved through military means.
Those efforts have gained urgency as the conflict has begun affecting both major maritime energy routes in the region. Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains severely reduced, while the security situation around Bab el-Mandeb has also deteriorated. Reuters reported on Friday that only four commodity vessels transited Hormuz on Thursday, compared with a 10-day average of 16.
The latest escalation has also pushed up global energy prices and increased pressure on Gulf states to find a diplomatic way out. Reuters reported that oil prices eased on Friday after diplomatic outreach, including efforts to persuade Iran to rein in Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure.
Meanwhile, Washington and Tehran remain far from resolving their differences. US President Donald Trump has said he hopes the war with Iran is nearing an end, but negotiations remain stalled.
Against this backdrop, Islamabad appears to be attempting a delicate balancing act: maintaining its strategic relationship with Saudi Arabia while keeping channels open with Iran and using its access to both sides to push for de-escalation.
Meanwhile, Pakistan has strongly condemned Houthi attacks on merchant shipping in the Bab al-Mandab Strait and called for their immediate cessation, as the UN Security Council holds its second major discussion this week on the escalating threat to the strategic waterway and its wider implications for regional security and global trade.
"We call upon [the] Houthi militia for immediate cessation of these provocative acts which could have dire consequences for maritime security, and regional peace and stability," Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, tells a Security Council Arria Formula meeting convened by Bahrain.
The ambassador says Houthi attacks seriously undermine maritime security and threaten peace and development in regional countries, "especially the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia", which he adds is facing "blatant and unprovoked aggression" by the Houthis.
26 strikes
Yemen's Houthis claim that Saudi Arabia launched 26 strikes against areas under their control over the past 24 hours, as the group and Yemen's Riyadh-backed government clash in the country's revived civil war, AFP reports.
The group adds that the number of Saudi strikes on its positions reached 300 over the last week, saying they targeted areas across Houthi-held Yemen.
Global trade is facing its worst disruption in 80 years as supply chain bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz threaten global food and fertiliser prices, Anadolu reports citing the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) director-general.
Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, speaking on the sidelines of the WTO's Public Forum in Geneva, tells Anadolu that the global trading system remains resilient, but the ongoing Middle East conflict presents a major test for the organisation's 166 member countries.
She notes that global trade in goods has grown by an unexpectedly strong 4.6 per cent this year despite geopolitical pressures, while 72pc of all global commerce continue to operate under WTO rules.
The initial projection for overall goods trade growth is 1.9pc for the entire year, but the first-quarter growth rate of 3.2pc outpaced expectations.
Italian aircraft
An Italian aircraft was hit during attacks on airbases in Saudi Arabia, Anadolu reports quoting Defence Minister Guido Crosetto.
Crosetto notes that he followed the situation in Saudi Arabia's Taif airbase, "Which was the target of several attacks and where Italian personnel are present as part of Operation Inherent Resolve," according to ANSA news agency.
He reaffirms that no Italian military personnel were involved.
"During the attack, an Italian F-2000 aircraft was hit. It was inside the base, in a remote area. There is no other damage to vehicles or infrastructure used by our personnel," Crosetto says, adding that he asked for a further assessment of the evolving situation, the condition of personnel and possible operational options.
Crosetto says he has been reassured that all security measures to protect military personnel were put in place some time ago.
"The situation is being followed with the utmost attention, with the aim of ensuring the full protection of our personnel and operating with the necessary responsibility," Crosetto explains.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that any act resulting in the infringement of citizens' fundamental rights constitutes a violation of the Constitution, warning that public office holders responsible for such violations would also be deemed to have breached their oath of office.
The ruling came in a detailed 37-page judgment on a petition concerning the proposed nationwide PTI protest towards Islamabad on September 27, 2026. PTI had announced the march to demand release of party founder Imran Khan and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution.
A citizen, Waqas Ahmed, had challenged the planned move on the grounds that the protest could disrupt routine life, traffic and business activities in the federal capital.
A three-member bench headed by Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar and comprising Justice Muhammad Asif and Justice Muhammad Azam Khan issued the judgment.
The bench had announced its short order on September 14 after hearing Attorney General for Pakistan Mansoor Awan, Additional Attorney General Amir Rehman, the advocate generals of the four provinces and Islamabad, and counsel for the petitioner, Barrister Akhter Cheena.
The court described the case as requiring an "unusual degree of constitutional balance" between the right of political parties and citizens to assemble peacefully and express dissent, and the rights of other citizens to life, liberty, dignity, free movement, trade, business, property, and access to hospitals, educational institutions, courts and workplaces.
"The question is not whether a political party is entitled to protest. It plainly is, subject always to the Constitution and law," the judgment observed.
The court held that the right to peaceful assembly could not be exercised in a manner that infringed the fundamental rights of other citizens.
A key objection raised by the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa advocate general concerned the territorial jurisdiction of the IHC over provincial authorities functioning outside Islamabad.
Rejecting the objection, the court held that Article 199(1)© empowered a high court to issue directions where a governmental power or function was being exercised "in, or in relation to" territory within its jurisdiction.
The court clarified, however, that the provision did not confer general supervisory jurisdiction over another province. A high court could issue directions to an authority outside its territorial seat where the governmental function had a direct and proximate legal relation with territory within its jurisdiction and intervention was necessary to protect fundamental rights there.
The bench also observed that where executive action or inaction was likely to infringe the fundamental rights of citizens within Islamabad, the court was under a "bounden duty" to assume jurisdiction under Article 199(1)©.
The court also rejected the objection that the petition was not maintainable because KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi had not been impleaded as a respondent. It noted that the Advocate General KP was representing both the provincial government and the chief minister.
The court further rejected the argument that the petitioner had an adequate alternate remedy under the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act, 2024.
It noted that no application had, admittedly, been filed under Section 3 of the Act and observed that its provisions had not been adhered to by the KP chief minister and others who had announced their intention to march towards Islamabad.
The judgment extensively referred to the Supreme Court's decision in the Faizabad sit-in case, observing that the constitutional right to assemble and protest was protected but remained subject to restrictions where its exercise infringed the fundamental rights of others.
The IHC also referred to the Supreme Court judgment concerning the PTI march of May 25, 2022, noting that assurances regarding a peaceful rally and non-obstruction of the Srinagar Highway had not been honoured.
The judgment referred to damage to public and private property, fires in the Blue Area greenbelt, injuries to police personnel and the subsequent invocation of Article 245 to call in the armed forces in aid of civil power.
The court also cited its November 21, 2024 order directing that no protest, rally or sit-in be allowed in violation of the Peaceful Assembly and Public Order Act. It observed that the order had also been flouted.
During the proceedings, the court allowed the Islamabad deputy commissioner/district magistrate to place electronic material on record. Video clips of the 2022 and 2024 protests were played before the bench, which described the conduct shown in the footage as "highly disturbing and reflective of violence and aggression".
The court noted that PTI was in power in K-P during both episodes and observed that provincial government resources had been used in pursuit of political objectives.
Regarding the proposed September 27 march, the court held that the petitioner's apprehension was not merely speculative. It noted that the date and destination of the proposed gathering were known and that statements attributed to the K-P chief minister indicated that the date was firm and that he intended to lead the march.
While disposing of the petition, the court directed that no political party, political leader, provincial government or public office holder could lawfully occupy roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas, buildings or similar public places within, or leading to or from, Islamabad in a manner that obstructed free movement or hindered trade, business, professions or access to medical and educational facilities.
The provincial governments and chief ministers were directed to ensure that no government resources, public funds, officials, vehicles, machinery or equipment were used directly or indirectly to facilitate any march, rally or procession towards Islamabad.
They were also directed to ensure that no public servant was compelled, coerced or induced to participate in such activities.
The chief secretaries, police chiefs, federal interior secretary, chief commissioner and IG Islamabad were ordered to issue instructions prohibiting officials from complying with orders requiring them to facilitate such marches.
Officials facing coercion were directed to report the matter to the relevant authorities, while helplines or other communication mechanisms were ordered to be established for this purpose.
The court further directed the authorities to take departmental action against officials who violated the directions.
In a significant finding, the court held that any person whose activity resulted in a violation of the fundamental rights of citizens in Islamabad would be deemed to have violated the Constitution and would be liable for consequences under the law.
It further declared that any public office holder whose activity resulted in a violation of citizens' fundamental rights would be deemed to have violated both the Constitution and his or her oath of office.

California Governor Gavin Newsom on Friday ordered officials to explore the creation of a "kill switch" for advanced artificial intelligence (AI) systems, while fresh research showing sophisticated cyberattacks and growing safety concerns added pressure on the rapidly expanding industry.
The move came as security researchers said they had used Anthropic's latest software to breach OpenAI's internal systems, highlighting how rapidly advanced AI technology can be deployed in sophisticated cyberattacks.
"I just issued an executive order to accelerate the implementation of safety checks and advance the creation of a 'kill switch' within frontier AI programs," Newsom, a Democrat, wrote on X, while accusing President Donald Trump of doing nothing on the issue.
Researchers from security firm Hacktron said they exploited a security flaw in OpenAI's public help forum that enabled them to take control of the site, underscoring concerns about the potential misuse and security implications of increasingly capable AI systems.
Concerns intensified after Anthropic employee Jacob Coxon resigned while warning that the industry was "gambling with our lives". Coxon, who previously worked at OpenAI, received support from former colleagues, including one who raised concern that AI could cause humanity's extinction.
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei last weekend called for AI development to slow. However, OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar dismissed concerns that slowing the release of state-of-the-art technology would hurt its business, saying the amount of intelligence already available was "massive".
Amodei argued that AI development is moving faster than governments can regulate and urged leading developers to submit to oversight by permanent embedded evaluators. However, Kristian Kersting, a professor of AI at Germany's Technical University of Darmstadt, termed the proposals "regulatory capture".
"If a handful of large companies decide for themselves what constitutes 'dangerous', select the appropriate inspectors and demand an exemption from competition law, that is no longer genuine regulation," Kersting said.
Germany's digital affairs ministry said stopping AI development was unrealistic given Europe's need for digital sovereignty, while Daniel Abbou, head of Germany's AI
industry association, said Europe should focus on closing the
technological gap.

Cuba's electricity grid suffered a total collapse on Friday, plunging the island into a nationwide blackout as fuel shortages, deteriorating infrastructure and prolonged power cuts continue to strain its ageing energy system.
"A total disconnection of the electrical system has occurred," the energy ministry said in a post on X, without specifying the cause of the latest failure. The blackout is the seventh major nationwide power outage reported in Cuba this year and the 12th since late 2024.
The outage underscores the deepening difficulties facing the island's electricity sector. Cuba, home to about 9.4 million people, has endured frequent power cuts for years as its ageing thermoelectric plants struggle to meet demand.
The situation has deteriorated sharply since January, when Washington imposed what Havana describes as a de facto energy blockade in an effort to pressure the Cuban government. Severe fuel shortages have made it increasingly difficult to keep power plants and backup generators operating.
Cuba relies heavily on imported fuel, including diesel, to run generators used when the national grid is unable to meet demand. Even when the grid remains operational, rolling blackouts frequently affect large parts of the country, leaving millions without electricity for prolonged periods.
In recent weeks, outages in Havana have lasted more than 30 hours, while blackouts in some outlying provinces have extended beyond 60 hours. The power crisis also disrupted essential services, affecting water supplies and phone networks and adding to the difficulties faced by households and businesses.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The opposition alliance on Friday decided to convene an all-parties conference to help address the country's political and economic crises and declared that its September 27 long march would be a "peaceful, constitutional and democratic" struggle.
According to a statement issued after a meeting chaired by Tehreek-e-Tahafuz-e-Aain Pakistan (TTAP) chief and opposition alliance leader Mahmood Khan Achakzai, the bloc has agreed to bring all democratic political forces onto a single platform to address the country's crises.
Burning issues such as inflation, unemployment, petrol prices and law and order will be made central issues for the September 27 protest, the meeting agreed.
The participants also agreed on the protection of the Constitution, Parliament, the federal system, provincial rights, the National Finance Commission (NFC) and the resources and powers of the provinces.
The meeting was attended by Senate Opposition Leader Allama Nasir Abbas, Balochistan National Party chief Sardar Akhtar Jan Mengal, Zain Shah and Mustafa Nawaz Khokhar.
Participants discussed the country's political situation, the ongoing crisis in the Middle East and its impact on Pakistan.
The meeting also deliberated on the law and order situation in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the proposed 28th Amendment and the creation of new provinces.
The participants were briefed on the September 27 protest and the visits of K-P Chief Minister Sohail Afridi to Sindh and Punjab.
The statement said that after all doors to justice had been completely closed, peaceful protest remained the only option.
It said that on September 27, the people's right to rule would be reclaimed through the strength of public support.
The opposition alliance decided to convene an all-parties conference to help end the political and economic crises and called on all democratic political forces to unite on one platform to pull the country out of its difficulties.
Responsibilities and committees have also been assigned for contacting other political parties.
The participants agreed on the protection of the Constitution, Parliament, the federal structure and provincial rights, including the NFC and the resources and powers of the provinces.
The statement maintained that a "non-representative government" had no authority to break up provinces or divide them merely into administrative units, denouncing such proposals as harmful to the federation, the national units and the federal structure.
It further said that provinces could not be deprived of their constitutional rights through a referendum or by any other means.
The meeting particularly stressed maintaining Sindh's existing geographical and administrative status.
On the treatment of PTI founder Imran Khan, the opposition alliance said that instead of implementing the Supreme Court's decision regarding his treatment, the matter had been turned into another crisis. It demanded direct access to the founder and accurate information about his health.
The meeting also expressed concern over severe water shortages in the Indus River system, saying Pakistan's environment, agriculture and the Indus Delta faced serious threats.
The participants demanded that no new canals or water projects be initiated and that controversial projects already under construction be scrapped.
The meeting called for the immediate recovery of forcibly disappeared persons and demanded that the bodies of those missing persons who had died be handed over to their families.
It also called for an end to target killings, fake encounters, extrajudicial killings and death squads.
The opposition alliance condemned raids on the homes of Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf workers and their arrests, as well as violations of the sanctity of the "chadar and char deewari" (privacy of home).
The participants agreed on the immediate restoration of border trade and rejection of the Mines and Minerals Act.
They also demanded that the relevant provinces and local populations be taken into confidence before decisions concerning natural resources were made.
The meeting further called for an end to the displacement of civilian populations under the pretext of security operations.
The opposition alliance condemned the treatment meted out to Sohail Afridi during his visit to Punjab.
Inflation, unemployment, petrol prices and the law and order situation were made part of the core agenda for the September 27 protest.
The meeting also supported an effective diplomatic and mediatory role for Pakistan to help bring an end to growing tensions in the region.
The participants condemned the re-arrest of Imaan Mazari following her release.
The statement concluded that the September 27 long march would be a peaceful, constitutional and democratic struggle.
