items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s proposed Telecommunication Competition Rules, 2026, remain unfinalized as a dispute over regulatory authority continues between the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) and the Competition Commission of Pakistan (CCP).
PTA has challenged the judgment before the Supreme Court, according to documents cited in the September 17 briefing. The appeal remains pending, leaving the dispute unresolved at the highest judicial level.
Documents presented during the briefing on a Senate question indicate that the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication has yet to finalize the rules, despite several rounds of consultations with PTA this year. The delay leaves a proposed sector-specific framework for telecom competition awaiting approval.
The disagreement centers on which regulator has the authority to oversee competition-related matters in the telecommunications industry.
PTA maintains that the Pakistan Telecommunication (Reorganization) Act, 1996, gives it a role in promoting fair competition among telecom operators. The ministry, however, has taken the position that competition enforcement falls outside PTA’s jurisdiction.
The legal dispute reached a significant point in November 2025, when the Islamabad High Court upheld CCP’s authority to investigate anti-competitive conduct and deceptive marketing in the telecom sector. The court distinguished CCP’s competition-law mandate from PTA’s technical, operational, and licensing responsibilities while recognizing that both regulators retain roles under their respective laws.
Repeated Draft Revisions Fail to Break Deadlock
Work on a dedicated telecom competition framework stretches back to amendments introduced in 2006. An earlier draft, titled the Pakistan Telecommunication Fair Competition Rules, was circulated in 2009 but was never finalized.
The latest effort began with a draft shared by the IT ministry on January 21, 2026. Following correspondence and consultations, the ministry forwarded an amended version on July 7, and PTA submitted its comments on July 27. The matter remains with the ministry.
Under Section 57 of the 1996 telecom law, the federal government has the authority to frame rules, while the Telecommunication Policy assigns responsibility for their development to the Ministry of IT.
The continuing delay creates uncertainty over the proposed rules governing competition in Pakistan’s telecom market, although existing competition legislation and the regulators’ established statutory powers remain in force.
With the Supreme Court appeal pending and the revised draft still awaiting finalization, no date has been announced for the notification of the Telecommunication Competition Rules, 2026.

items.summary:

Google-Pakistan partnership has raised concerns about data protection, government access to user information, and safeguards for digital rights.
Media watchdog Freedom Network has written an open letter to Google and the Pakistani government, asking for greater transparency about the agreements signed between the two sides. items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Google-Pakistan partnership has raised concerns about data protection, government access to user information, and safeguards for digital rights.
Media watchdog Freedom Network has written an open letter to Google and the Pakistani government, asking for greater transparency about the agreements signed between the two sides. The organisation said the partnership could support Pakistan’s digital economy but stressed that strong safeguards are needed to protect citizens’ personal information.
Google recently expanded its presence in Pakistan and signed memoranda of understanding and other agreements with the government. However, Freedom Network said the details of these agreements have not been made public.
Google-Pakistan Partnership Under Scrutiny Over User Data Protection
The watchdog asked Google and the government to clarify what exactly has been agreed and whether all MoUs, contracts and other arrangements will be published. It also questioned what legal basis would apply if some parts of the agreements remain confidential.
Another major concern involves access to user data. Freedom Network asked whether the agreements include any commitments allowing government authorities to access user data, content, metadata or government databases.
The organisation also questioned under what circumstances Pakistani authorities could request information about Google users. It called for such requests to follow valid legal procedures and, where required, judicial oversight. It further asked whether Google would reject requests that are overly broad or do not comply with fundamental rights.
The watchdog specifically highlighted the need to protect journalists and their confidential sources. It asked whether the agreements include safeguards against government access to journalists’ Gmail, Google Drive, Photos, YouTube accounts and search-related information.
Freedom Network also raised concerns about content removal and blocking requests. It asked Google to ensure that content is not removed simply because a government agency requests it. According to the watchdog, such requests should be assessed under clear and transparent legal standards, while users should receive notice and an opportunity to challenge decisions where legally possible.
Data storage is another issue highlighted by the organisation. Pakistan is developing a national data-governance framework that focuses on data sovereignty, limited disclosure and citizens’ right to know who has accessed their information.
See Also: Google Reveals Location of Its First Office in Pakistan
Freedom Network asked Google whether data belonging to Pakistani users would be stored within Pakistan, overseas or in both locations. It also called for an assurance that there would be no informal or undocumented data-sharing arrangements between Google and the government.
The watchdog further asked who would independently monitor Google’s compliance with privacy and human-rights safeguards in Pakistan. It said such oversight should not rely solely on the government.
The concerns come as Pakistan seeks to expand its digital economy and attract major global technology companies. Greater transparency around data protection and user privacy could therefore become an important part of discussions surrounding the country’s growing digital partnerships.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
The Directorate General of Immigration and Passports is considering cooperation with Easypaisa to make passport fee payments easier through digital payment methods.
Director General Immigration and Passports Chaudhry Muhammad Ali Randhawa recently met with an Easypaisa director and a delegation to discuss ways to simplify the payment process for passport applicants.
During the meeting, the Easypaisa delegation presented proposals for introducing digital payment solutions for passport fees. The proposed system could give citizens more convenient options to pay their fees without relying on traditional cash-based methods.
Pakistan Considers Easypaisa Partnership for Digital Passport Fee Payments
The two sides also reviewed the potential of digital payments to make passport-related services faster, easier and more citizen-friendly. Digital payment options could help applicants complete the fee payment process more conveniently while reducing the need to visit payment counters.
The proposed cooperation is also in line with the government’s broader push toward cashless and digital public services. In June 2026, the government decided to introduce a cashless system at passport offices as part of efforts to modernize passport services.
If implemented, the collaboration with Easypaisa could provide passport applicants with another digital channel for paying their fees. However, the latest meeting focused on proposals and possibilities, and further details about the launch, payment process and implementation timeline have yet to be announced.
The move reflects the government’s continued efforts to expand digital payments across public services and reduce dependence on cash transactions.

items.title: New Green Card rules from September 18: Full list of categories affected
items.summary: Effective September 18, the USCIS will enforce new public charge regulations for Green Card applicants. These updated guidelines impose stricter financial evaluations and recognize a broader range of public benefits. This modification impacts family and employment-based Green Card submissions lodged from that date forward. items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
In July this year, OpenAI’s models were being tested in a controlled cybersecurity environment and tasked with spotting and exploiting software vulnerabilities. The models found ways around the intended network restrictions and created a “swarm”, with different agents delegating tasks to one another, during an unintended attack on the infrastructure of AI platform Hugging Face.
The incident turned longstanding concerns about autonomous AI systems into a more immediate question: what happens when increasingly capable models find ways to operate beyond the restrictions imposed on them? It also became one of the “warning shots” cited by researchers calling for frontier AI labs to coordinate on safety.
The debate intensified last week when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon publicly quit the company and accused leading AI labs of racing towards self-improving superintelligence without adequate safeguards.
Soon after, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei turned these concerns into a concrete proposal, urging frontier AI companies to “pace” their development. His proposal included independent evaluators, common safety standards, and greater coordination between governments and AI companies.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman backed parts of the proposal, saying pacing the frontier has become a primary topic of discussions at OpenAI and that the company would commit to independent evaluations.
However, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has rejected calls to slow AI development. “Run as fast as you can,” he said, arguing that companies should continue advancing the technology but hold back products until they know they are safe.
The disagreement has sharpened the debate over what pacing means, whether it can work amid intense competition, and who should decide where the brakes are applied.
AI’s Shift From Answers To Actions
AI has moved from models that largely responded to prompts to reasoning systems capable of using tools, executing code, and coordinating multiple agents to solve complex tasks.
Anthropic has warned that agents interacting with codebases, markets, and other digital systems could create a new class of risks, with machine-to-machine interactions eventually outpacing human oversight.
Shayak Mazumder, founder of agentic AI venture studio Adya, said newer agents can bypass instructions because they can explore paths developers may not have anticipated, creating a gap between what developers intend and what a system may discover it can do.
OpenAI’s own evaluations have also highlighted advances in agentic coding and cybersecurity, prompting it to strengthen network and tool restrictions and monitor risky actions.
Ganesh Gopalan, cofounder of Gnani.ai, pointed to jailbreaks, including the Hugging Face incident, and recursively self-improving systems as evidence that the risks are becoming harder to dismiss, even if their precise nature remains unclear.
“There is evidence that definitely there is some risk, for sure. But the point is how do you control those risks and what actions will be taken? I think that’s where it’s a completely grey area,” Gopalan said.
Who Gets To Write The AI Rulebook?
Amodei said pacing does not mean halting AI development. His proposal calls for frontier companies to give embedded third-party evaluators ongoing, employee-like access to assess safety practices and report incidents. He also wants companies in democratic countries to establish common standards before seeking broader international coordination.
Pacing could mean slowing the training of more capable models, restricting experiments involving recursive self-improvement, or evaluating models more rigorously before release.
However, Gopalan said the lack of a common definition creates a fundamental problem. If some frontier AI companies slow down, it remains unclear whether the same rules would apply to their competitors or to other countries.
“If you’re going to say, pacing it, are you going to stop? Are they ready to allow other companies or countries to catch up?” he said.
Mazumder believes mandatory checks are needed before frontier models reach users. “We need to come up with global standards and national standards to ensure that LLM has passed those checks before it can be released to the public,” he said.
Amitabh Kumar, cofounder of content governance platform Contrails.ai, said frontier companies should have a voice because of their technical expertise, but universities, independent scientists, and policymakers should have an equal seat at the table. He is particularly sceptical of company-appointed evaluators.
Could Safety Become A Competitive Moat?
Mandatory evaluations, audits, compute controls, and other safety requirements would also increase the cost of developing frontier AI.
For Gopalan, the risk is not merely the cost of regulation but the concentration of power it could create around a handful of well-funded companies.
“Right now, it’s more of a few companies that are becoming all-powerful,” he said, warning that safety rules should not be used to prevent other companies or countries from catching up.
Large AI labs may be able to absorb the cost of audits and repeated evaluations. Smaller companies may struggle, particularly if controls extend to advanced GPUs, computing infrastructure, or training resources.
Kumar pushed back against the idea that safety requirements would necessarily become a barrier, arguing that regulation inevitably carries a cost that can become part of doing business in a high-risk industry.
Meanwhile, a managing partner at a Bengaluru-based VC firm, who didn’t want to be named, pointed to the gap between private valuations and profitability, along with the capital required to keep developing increasingly powerful models.
The investor questioned if the valuations being discussed for the potential public listings of companies like Anthropic and Open AI could be justified, given their profitability timelines and infrastructure spending. “Profitability is far away and infrastructure commitments are out of control,” the investor said.
The investor also speculated that safety concerns could give the companies’ CEOs grounds to postpone their listings. However, there is no evidence linking the calls for pacing AI development to their IPO timelines. The more immediate question is whether future safety requirements would constrain the largest AI labs or reinforce their advantage over emerging rivals.
While Anthropic is moving towards a possible IPO, Altman has said OpenAI will not go public this year, citing the risks posed by increasingly powerful AI systems. OpenAI is meanwhile reportedly exploring fresh funding at a $1.2 Tn valuation.
The Geopolitics Of Slowing AI
Even if US frontier labs agree to pace development, there is no guarantee that companies elsewhere will follow.
Amodei argued that failing to build advanced AI could hand the technology to authoritarian powers, while moving too quickly could create uncontrollable risks.
The US, therefore, has an incentive to reduce AI risks but also economic and national security reasons to prevent China from overtaking it. Huang’s argument reflects the concern that slowing American labs may only allow rivals to close the capability gap.
For countries outside the current frontier, the concern is that safety could evolve into a nuclear-style non-proliferation regime, restricting access to advanced models, chips, or computing infrastructure, according to Gopalan.
The issue is relevant for India, where Chinese open-source models have already found significant traction. “If Chinese AI models are cheaper, free, faster, whatever, startups should not be stopped from using them,” the investor quoted above said.
Can The AI Race Police Itself?
The divide between Amodei and Huang captures the central fault line. One side believes frontier capabilities are advancing too quickly for existing safety mechanisms to keep up. The other believes development should continue at full speed, with companies responsible for ensuring that unsafe products do not reach users.
Both approaches carry risks. Voluntary commitments may collapse under competitive pressure, while standards shaped primarily by incumbent labs could raise barriers for smaller competitors and concentrate control over the frontier.
Pacing AI development, therefore, is not merely a technical safety question. It is also a contest over who controls the technology, who bears the cost of making it safer, and who gets to participate in the next phase of the AI race.
Edited by Vinaykumar Rai

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Samsung has quietly introduced the Galaxy A08, an entry-level smartphone featuring a larger 6,000 mAh battery, Android 17 with One UI 9, and extended software support.
The device has appeared on Samsung’s regional websites in Serbia and Bosnia, revealing its specifications ahead of a wider market rollout. While the Galaxy A08 retains much of its predecessor’s design, it brings improvements in battery capacity and software longevity.
The smartphone features a 6.7-inch PLS LCD with HD+ resolution and a 90Hz refresh rate. It retains a waterdrop-style notch and a side-mounted fingerprint sensor.
One of its main upgrades is the 6,000mAh battery, up from the 5,000mAh capacity of the Galaxy A07 4G. Charging remains limited to 25W.
For photography, the Galaxy A08 offers a 50MP primary camera and an 8MP front-facing camera. Other features include a microSD card slot, a 3.5 mm headphone jack, and 4G LTE connectivity.
The device runs Android 17 with One UI 9 and is expected to receive up to six major operating system upgrades and six years of security updates.
Samsung has not explicitly identified the chipset in its regional specifications, although reports suggest the device could feature MediaTek’s Helio G99 processor. This detail remains unconfirmed.
Samsung Galaxy A08 Expected Price and Release Date in Pakistan
Samsung has yet to announce the Galaxy A08’s official price or release date in Pakistan.
Based on its early international pricing and positioning in the Galaxy A series, the smartphone could arrive in Pakistan at approximately Rs 40,000 to Rs 50,000. This is a preliminary estimate rather than an official price.
The device is expected to reach the Pakistani market in the coming weeks, potentially during October 2026, although Samsung has not confirmed a launch schedule.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
Healthtech startup Practo has overhauled its top leadership, appointing former COO Jagnoor Singh as CEO, while cofounder and former CEO Shashank ND Singh has moved to the expanded role of MD and executive chairman.
Singh’s appointment took effect on September 1. He will lead Practo’s overall strategy, growth, and operations across its global markets, the startup said in a statement.
Meanwhile, Shashank will focus on Practo’s long-term vision, product and strategy, innovation agenda, capital strategy, inorganic growth, and corporate development initiatives.
Singh joined Practo as COO in January 2025 and has since worked on its growth strategy, operational execution, and entry into new markets. Before joining Practo, he held senior positions at Bharti Airtel, Unacademy, and OYO.
Practo has also expanded the responsibilities of three senior executives as part of the leadership reshuffle.
Cofounder Siddhartha Nihalani has taken on the additional responsibility of COO – B2C and will oversee Practo’s consumer businesses. Rowel Coelho, previously its head of monetisation, has been appointed COO – B2B and will lead the soonicorn’s enterprise and corporate businesses.
Meanwhile, cofounder Abhinav Lal has been named chief scientist. In the research-focused role, he will lead Practo’s exploration of AI applications in healthcare, build research partnerships, and develop an innovation hub focused on emerging technologies.
Practo’s IPO Preparations
The leadership changes come as Practo steps up its international expansion and prepares for a proposed public listing. Earlier this year, the startup appointed former Union health secretary CK Mishra as an independent director as part of efforts to strengthen its board.
Inc42 previously reported that Practo was in advanced discussions to raise $100 Mn to $125 Mn in a pre-IPO funding round at a post-money valuation of around $700 Mn. The startup is reportedly targeting a public listing in 2027.
Practo claimed that it is currently growing at 40% YoY and has remained profitable for the past two-and-a-half years.
The startup turned EBITDA profitable in FY25, reporting an operating EBITDA of ₹15 Cr on revenue of ₹234 Cr. This marked a turnaround from FY24, when it posted an EBITDA loss of ₹17 Cr on revenue of ₹240 Cr.
Founded in 2008 by Shashank and Lal, Practo operates a digital healthcare platform that allows patients to find doctors, book appointments, consult physicians online, order medicines, and schedule diagnostic tests.
It also offers practice management software for doctors, clinics, and hospitals, and operates 40 co-branded dermatology clinics across India.
Its platform connects patients with more than 7 Lakh doctors and healthcare providers across over 2,400 cities globally. Practo also operates Insta, a hospital information management system used by more than 500 clients across over 1,200 facilities.
Besides India, Practo has expanded into the US and the UAE. It entered the UAE last year and launched a pilot in the US, where it claims to have onboarded more than 2 Lakh doctors and built an annual GMV run rate of over $75 Mn.
It has raised a total funding of about $230 Mn to date from investors like Peak XV Partners, Sofina, Thrive Capital, and Capital G.
The leadership reshuffle also comes months after Shashank launched preventive healthcare startup Cent alongside former Ola CMO Anshul Khandelwal and sales executive Arpit Garg. Cent raised $5 Mn in seed funding from OneFlow Holdings, Shashank’s family office, and South Park Commons.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
On the directive of the Prime Minister, the SMS service for registration under the Prime Minister’s Petrol Relief Scheme has been made completely free of cost, allowing citizens across the country to register without incurring any additional expense.
Under the scheme, eligible citizens, motorcycle, rickshaw, and small vehicle (up to 800 cc) owners, can avail a discount of Rs. 100 per litre on petrol. Motorcycle and rickshaw owners are entitled to up to 20 litres of subsidized petrol per month, while owners of vehicles up to 800 cc can avail up to 30 litres monthly.
To register, citizens must send an SMS from their own registered SIM to 9771 in the following format: REG, CNIC number, vehicle registration number, provincial code, and vehicle registration date (in DDMMYYYY format), with no dashes or extra spaces. Once registration is successfully verified, users receive a confirmation SMS. Before visiting a petrol pump, users must also send TOK to 9771 to receive their fuel relief token, which must be shown at the pump to avail the discounted rate.
Federal Minister for IT and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja visited several petrol pumps alongside the district administration to personally review the on-ground implementation of the scheme. This marked the third consecutive day that the federal minister engaged directly with the public, answering their questions and addressing concerns related to the initiative.
Speaking on the occasion, Shaza Fatima Khawaja said that since yesterday, the Prime Minister’s Petrol Relief Scheme has been benefiting citizens across the country. She emphasized that the targeted relief has been specifically designed for the deserving segments of society.
The federal minister directed the administration to play its full role in ensuring an uninterrupted supply of subsidized petrol to eligible citizens. She warned that the administration would deal strictly with anyone found delaying or creating hurdles in the provision of discounted petrol.
She also urged citizens to complete their registration strictly through the prescribed procedure to avoid any inconvenience or delay in receiving the benefit.

items.author: Tom Jackson
items.content:
South African agri-tech startup Divisi is a farm management platform that helps smallholder farmers know what to grow, when and how, in order to minimise losses and consistently achieve high yields.
Founded this year by Isaac Chikutukutu, Divisi computes agronomy for one farmer’s actual field, rather than their district. A farmer adds the field’s boundaries once, and from there the app scores over 70 crops against that exact plot’s soil, climate history and terrain, works out when the planting window opens and closes, and turns the crop cycle into dated jobs.
Under the hood is the FAO’s Global Agro-Ecological Zones methodology — a suitability cascade refined by agronomic researchers since the 1980s, which cuts a crop’s potential back step-by-step by temperature through the growing cycle, water against crop demand, soil chemistry, and terrain.
“It is deterministic – the same field and the same crop parameters return the same answer every time, and every score names the factor that limited it. No part of a recommendation is generated by a language model. That kind of analysis has existed for decades for anyone with a GIS workstation and a budget. What hasn’t existed is that computation on a smallholder’s phone, telling them what to do on a Tuesday,” Chikutukutu told Disrupt Africa.
Start with the farmer. Most smallholders have no formal agricultural training and no reliable way to know what to plant, when, or how.
“So a season is closer to a coin flip than a plan. The weather information they do get is broadcast – forecasts pitched at a whole province, El Niño coverage on the evening news. Too broad to act on, and functioning as entertainment rather than information. So people copy whoever did well last year, and follow the herd,” Chikutukutu said.
“Then the records. Paper is fragile, admin is nobody’s favourite job, and most farmers finish a season without knowing which crop is profitable or whether they made money. That absence of information affects the entire value chain. An agri-financier looking at a farmer with no training credentials, no verifiable production history and no financial record has no way to price the risk — so they price it high, or they don’t lend at all.”
Divisi looks to fix all that – helping farmers increase their yields, demonstrate their performance, and access finance to grow. One month since its launch, it already has 500 active users, and is now looking for a research institution, NGO or development agency to run a trial with it.
“We’ll open the methodology, the parameter tables and the anonymised data to make it possible,” said Chikutukutu.
Divisi is totally self-funded.
“No outside capital, nothing raised. The past year went into building rather than fundraising — I wanted a product worth showing before asking anyone for anything. That changes now – we’re currently making grant applications and pursuing B2B customers in parallel so we can scale our impact and help mitigate against ElNino risk in the upcoming season,” said Chikutukutu.
He believes Divisi has global potential.
“Africa is the focus and SADC is where the roots are, but the tool works anywhere by design. The engine runs on global soil databases, global climate reanalysis and global elevation models, so there’s no country-by-country data acquisition step between us and a new market — most agronomy tools have to buy or build a soil dataset per country, which is what makes their expansion slow and expensive. If a farmer in Peru or India adds a field tonight, and they have, the cascade runs,” Chikutukutu said.
The startup had built paid tiers before it launched, but chose to remove them.
“Farmers never pay — every feature free, permanently, and we don’t sell farmer data,” Chikutukutu said. “Revenue comes from B2B Divisi Partner programme – outgrower schemes, agro-processors, exporters, input suppliers, agri-finance and insurers pay per active enrolled farmer for consented visibility into fields they already work with. Government, extension services, research institutions and registered NGOs get access for free.”

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
WhatsApp is working on a new feature that could allow iPhone users to add up to three accounts to the same app. The company currently allows users to manage two accounts on one device, but the upcoming change could make it easier for people who use multiple phone numbers.
According to WABetaInfo, the three-account feature was spotted in WhatsApp beta for iOS version 26.37.10.15 through TestFlight. The feature is still under development and is not currently available for beta testers.
WhatsApp Is Testing Support for Three Accounts on iPhone
WhatsApp introduced multi-account support on iPhone with the WhatsApp for iOS 26.22.76 update. The feature allows users to add a second account without logging out of their primary account. Each account operates independently, with its own chats, notifications, backups, and settings.
The upcoming update will extend the same system to a third account.
WhatsApp Will Keep Accounts Separate
The third account will work in the same way as the first two accounts. Users will be able to keep separate chat histories, notifications, privacy settings, backups, and media for each profile.
Notifications will also identify which account has received a new message. This should help users avoid confusion when managing several WhatsApp accounts from the same app.
WhatsApp’s App Lock feature will also work separately for each account, allowing users to protect individual profiles with their own authentication settings.
How to Add a Third WhatsApp Account
Once the feature becomes available, users will be able to add another account directly from WhatsApp’s settings.
The Account List will show all accounts currently added to the device. After two accounts have been added, users will see an option to add another phone number.
Users will also be able to access the feature through the “Switch accounts” option. The interface will remain familiar, with each account showing its name, profile picture, and phone number. A green checkmark will indicate the account that is currently active.
See Also: WhatsApp Rolling Out 2x Video Playback for Status Updates
Third Account Could Help Users With Multiple Numbers
The additional account could be useful for people who manage three phone numbers. For example, someone may use separate numbers for personal communication, work, and another purpose.
Previously, users who needed more than one WhatsApp account on an iPhone had to use a second device or rely on WhatsApp Business. The existing two-account feature reduced that need, and a third account could provide even more flexibility.
The new option could also save users from constantly switching between devices or deciding which accounts to keep on their main phone.
Feature Is Still Under Development
WhatsApp has not yet made three-account support available to beta testers. The feature remains under development, so its design and functionality could change before release.
The company has also not announced when it plans to roll out support for three accounts to the public. Users will have to wait for a future WhatsApp for iOS update to see when the feature becomes available.
WABetaInfo also notes that WhatsApp could potentially increase the account limit beyond three in the future, although there is no official confirmation of such a change.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Snap has revealed more details about its new Specs augmented reality glasses, giving users a better look at what the expensive smart glasses can actually do. The company says the device is designed to make computing more natural by bringing digital content and AI features directly into the user’s view.
Snap first announced the latest Specs in June at the Augmented World Expo. The glasses are priced at $2,195 and are expected to start shipping to customers in fall 2026.
Snap Reveals What Its $2,195 Specs Smart Glasses Can Do
The Specs combine augmented reality with several everyday features. Users can make phone calls through Bluetooth, listen to music through Spotify, and capture photos and videos. The glasses also include a display that allows users to watch content from services such as YouTube and HBO Max.
The glasses can also be used for shopping. Through a partnership with Shopify, users can view 3D versions of products, place them virtually in their surroundings, and complete purchases.
Real-Time Translation and Sports Features
One of the more useful features is real-time language translation. The Specs can listen to another person speaking a different language and provide a translation through the built-in speakers. The translated text can also appear on the glasses’ display.
Snap has partnered with Tripadvisor to expand the translation experience. Users can translate local phrases, reviews, and currencies while traveling.
The company is also developing augmented reality experiences for sports. Through partnerships with the NBA and WNBA, the Specs can provide visual guides and training instructions when users practice basketball using real hoops and balls. Similar AR features are planned for sports such as soccer and golf.
For golf, the glasses are designed to provide information that could help players improve their technique. Snap is also developing other interactive experiences that blend virtual elements with the physical environment.
Games and Entertainment
Snap is using the Specs for entertainment as well. An HBO Max partnership brings Harry Potter-themed AR experiences to the glasses. Users can interact with virtual elements and take part in experiences inspired by the franchise.
Two people wearing Specs can also play digital games together. Supported experiences include chess, ping pong, Battleship and dominoes.
The glasses can even interact with physical books. While reading, users can highlight passages, save sections, and bookmark their position.
Snap is also promoting features for meditation and digital DJ experiences, expanding the glasses beyond traditional smart-glasses functions.
Specs Target Businesses Too
Snap is also positioning the Specs as a tool for businesses. The company has partnerships with Salesforce, Amazon, and Nvidia to develop enterprise applications.
These applications could allow workers to see information, codes, or product specifications directly in their field of view. The glasses could also help employees locate specific parts or check whether products are available in backstock.
This puts the Specs in competition with other AR devices aimed at industrial and workplace applications.
Snap Focuses on Privacy
Privacy remains an important issue for camera-equipped smart glasses. Snap says its Specs do not record the surrounding world simply to understand it and do not use facial recognition to identify people.
The glasses also include an LED indicator that turns on when the cameras are taking photos or recording video. This is intended to make it clearer to people nearby when the cameras are active.
New Specs Intelligence AI Service
Alongside the glasses, Snap has introduced a new AI service called Specs Intelligence. The service is available on iPhone and Mac as well as the Specs, meaning users can access it without owning the glasses.
Snap describes Specs Intelligence as an “anticipatory AI” system. Instead of only responding to individual questions, it is designed to learn about a user’s routines, priorities, and goals and anticipate what they may need.
The service can connect with selected apps and tools, including calendars, email and location information. It can then help users with tasks such as finding hotels, planning trips, and answering questions.
Snap organizes information into areas such as work, family, and personal goals. The approach requires users to connect different sources of personal information so the AI can build a broader understanding of their routines.
Despite the range of features, the $2,195 price and the physical size of the Specs could affect their appeal. The glasses are considerably larger and heavier than ordinary eyewear, raising questions about comfort during activities such as sports.
Snap plans to give potential buyers an opportunity to test the glasses before purchasing. A Specs First Look demonstration will begin on October 1 at Westfield Century City in Los Angeles.
The company is betting that augmented reality, AI, and hands-free computing can make its Specs part of everyday life. Whether consumers will be willing to pay $2,195 for that experience will become clearer once the glasses reach the market.

Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Following its first sale in Pakistan, the realme C100 Series has introduced something relatively uncommon in this price segment: an 8000mAh Titan Long-Lasting Battery built around the demands of Gen Z’s always-on lifestyle. That capacity immediately gave the lineup a strong point of differentiation and helped generate early market attention. Since then, interest has continued to build, with demand increasing and availability beginning to tighten.
For Gen Z, a smartphone is expected to handle almost every part of the day — from classes and work to gaming, content creation and social life. The C100 Series brings together the features that matter across those roles: a large battery, fast charging, durability, smooth performance, a capable camera and a choice of colours that gives the lineup its own identity.
8000mAh Is the Number Everyone’s Talking About
The conversation starts with the battery.
The 8000mAh Titan Long-Lasting Battery gives both the realme C100 and C100x the endurance to support up to 40 hours of heavy usage on a single charge. For Gen Z users moving constantly between study, work, gaming, streaming and content creation, that means less time thinking about the next charging point and more freedom to stay connected throughout the day.
The realme C100 also supports 45W Fast Charging.
Both the realme C100 and C100x support reverse charging — 6W on the C100x and 10W on the C100 — and are backed by 7-Year Battery Health. It is not simply about having a larger battery. It is about giving users more freedom to use their phone harder and for longer without planning the day around a charger, and in this price segment, that difference is standing out.
From Buzz to Real Demand
The C100 Series has now moved beyond launch attention, with growing interest translating into real demand as the devices reach buyers.
The 8000mAh battery may have started the conversation, but its relevance to Gen Z’s multi-role lifestyle is helping sustain it.
For younger users especially, a smartphone is no longer just for calls and messages. It is the screen for classes, work, gaming, entertainment, social life and content creation. When one device has to support all of those roles, compromises become more noticeable, and the C100 Series is positioned around reducing those compromises.
Built to Handle More Than the Battery
The C100 Series does not stop at battery life.
Both models feature 2m Drop Resistance and ArmorShell Protection for everyday bumps and falls. The realme C100 adds IP69 Pro Water Resistance with up to 6m protection, while the C100x comes with IP64 resistance. Both also feature Rain Touch Mode, helping keep the screen responsive when wet.
A 120Hz Smooth Display supports fluid scrolling, gaming and everyday interaction across both models. The realme C100 further offers up to 1200 nits brightness, alongside GT Boost, Hyper Cooling and the MediaTek Helio G92 Max, while the C100x reaches up to 900 nits brightness for clear everyday viewing.
Both phones also feature a 50MP AI Camera, giving users a capable setup for everyday photography, social content and content creation.
More Ways to Make It Yours
The realme C100 is available in Dream White, Frost Purple and Dark Coffee, while the C100x comes in Golden Coast and Deep Blue Tides, giving buyers more choice in how they want their device to look and feel.
The realme C100 Series is available in the following variants:
realme C100x 6GB + 128GB — PKR 64,999
realme C100x 8GB + 128GB — PKR 74,999
realme C100 8GB + 256GB — PKR 89,999
When Gen Z Attention Turns Into Market Momentum
Launch attention can be short-lived. For the realme C100 Series, however, the conversation is continuing to build.
Its 8000mAh Titan Long-Lasting Battery gave Gen Z a clear reason to notice the lineup, while its durability, display, performance and camera give the product enough depth to stay relevant beyond the headline feature.
As demand continues to build and availability tightens, the C100 Series is moving from being a talked-about launch to becoming a stronger presence in the market. More importantly, that momentum is being shaped by the same audience the product was built around: Gen Z users looking for a phone that can keep up with the different roles they move through every day.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
TECNO has just brought the SPARK 50 Pro to Pakistan, and it’s easy to see what the phone is built to argue against: batteries that die by evening, cameras that blur every photo of a moving kid or pet, and screens that crack the first time the phone meets a tiled floor. It’s part of the brand’s “Never Miss Out” push, priced at PKR 74,999 for the 8GB+128GB version, and it’s already sitting on shelves nationwide in four colours, Ink Black, Titanium Grey, Dynamic Orange and Midnight Blue.
Battery anxiety is the first thing TECNO tries to kill off. The SPARK 50 Pro’s 60W Super Charge gets a dead phone back to 100% in under an hour, backed by a 6000mAh cell, and even a rushed 15-minute charge is enough to get through the rest of the day. TECNO says the battery is good for over 1,900 charge cycles, ensuring six years of normal use. There’s also some thought put into keeping the battery healthy long-term: Super Charge, Smart Charge and Low-Temp Charge modes adjust depending on what you’re doing, and AI Charging Protection steps in to avoid unnecessary wear.
For the camera, TECNO went with a 50MP Sony LYTIA 600 sensor and leaned into speed. FlashSnap uses a 1/10,000-second shutter to fire off six shots in five seconds, which is the difference between catching a moment and catching a blur when something’s actually moving. BestMoment then quietly picks the sharpest frame out of the burst, so you’re not stuck scrolling through five near-identical photos trying to find the one that’s in focus.
Then there’s the part most phones in this range skip entirely: durability that’s actually been tested by someone other than the manufacturer. The SPARK 50 Pro carries IP68 protection down to 6 metres of water for 30 minutes, the deepest rating in its class, plus IP69 for high-pressure jets and Level 6 dust protection. It has also earned SGS’s Five-Star Premium Drop certification, having survived 41 drops from various angles and heights of up to 1.8 metres. None of that is TECNO’s own claim; it’s independently verified, which is usually the difference between marketing and a phone that actually survives your pocket.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
The Clean Label Credibility Test
India’s clean-label boom is facing its toughest test yet. FSSAI’s recent crackdown on health and purity claims is threatening the marketing language that helped many D2C brands grow. Can “healthy” food startups survive when every claim must stand up to evidence?
The Label Under Fire: FSSAI’s recent notices to 20 legacy and D2C brands has brought claims such as “100% natural” and “healthy” under scrutiny. Brands built on “ingredient transparency” were caught using date powders and fructose while advertising zero added sugar. Rather than challenging the FSSAI’s notices, several brands quietly opted to scrub these absolute claims and overhauled their packaging.
But the situation took a sharp turn after the SC began questioning what a front-of-pack warning label should look like.
SC Weighs In: The apex court accepted FSSAI’s proposed red hexagon warning for packaged foods high in sugar, salt and saturated fat. At the same time, it also sought more clarity on scientific thresholds, label size and possible confusion with existing food markers. The next hearing in the matter could establish a clearer path for how health warnings must appear, potentially reshaping packaging and product listings across India’s food market.
Trust Needs Proof: Experts believe that the crackdown can potentially create a better opportunity for brands to demonstrate better ingredients, transparent formulations and verifiable nutritional claims. However, it will raise the cost of entering the category and will require the brands to rethink product formulations.
So, will new-age food brands adapt or will this regulatory reckoning shatter consumer trust in “clean-label” promises? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
PhonePe Eyes 2027 IPO
The Walmart-backed fintech giant has revived its IPO plans after the Centre introduced a new MDR framework for UPI. PhonePe is now targeting a listing between February and March 2027.
PhonePe will now look to file its updated draft red herring prospectus with SEBI by the end of this year, seeking a valuation of $10 Bn.
The fintech major had confidentially filed its DRHP with SEBI in late-2025 and received approval for an OFS-only issue earlier this year. The startup later postponed its IPO plans citing global market volatility and escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
Lendingkart Finance’s Q1 Snapshot
Lendingkart’s NBFC arm managed to narrow its losses by 62% YoY to ₹32.4 Cr in Q1 FY27, signalling that the sharp deterioration seen through FY26 may be bottoming out. Meanwhile, operating revenue also tanked 55% YoY to ₹52.7 Cr.
The company also booked a net loss of ₹70 Lakh on fair value changes and a ₹80 Lakh loss on assignment of loans in Q1. During the quarter, the NBFC also transferred stressed loans worth ₹94.7 Cr to an asset reconstruction company for a consideration of ₹2 Cr.
Lendingkart Finance, which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Lendingkart Technologies, serves as the licensed lending vehicle for the group’s MSME-focussed digital lending business. Fullerton Financial Holdings took over the group in a fire sale in 2024.
VerifAIX Bags $5 Mn
The AI-native semiconductor verification startup has raised about ₹48 Cr in its seed round co-led by Endiya Partners and Bluehill VC to accelerate product development, expand deployments and grow its engineering teams in India and the US.
Founded in 2024, VerifAIX is developing an AI-native platform to help semiconductor engineering teams verify chip designs. Its platform flags gaps and potential errors in chip specifications and recommends fixes.
The fundraise comes amid growing investor and policy interest in India’s chip ecosystem. At the heart of this push is the homegrown semiconductor market, which is projected to become a $155 Bn opportunity by 2031.
UPI Concentration Eases In August
Sachin Bansal-led Navi improved its UPI market share, in terms of transactions, to 4.4% in August, marking a steady climb in a market still dominated by PhonePe and Google Pay. Navi processed 108 Cr transactions worth ₹52,512 Cr last month.
PhonePe remained the market leader and processed 1,125 Cr transactions worth ₹14.3 Lakh Cr in August, but its volume share slipped to 45.9% during the month. Google Pay’s market share also edged down to 32.4% from 32.5% in July.
The timing is significant as UPI is all set to be monetised. Payments above ₹2,000 will attract a 0.4% MDR starting October 15, potentially making scale and merchant activity more valuable for payment apps than they were under the zero-MDR regime.
RentoMojo’s IPO Windfall
Shares of the furniture and appliance rental startup are all set to list on the bourses later today. Ahead of the D-Street debut, the IPO’s offer for sale component delivered sizeable returns for the platform’s early backers as well as cofounder Geetansh Bamania.
While Bamania pocketed ₹34.31 Cr by selling 8.49 Lakh shares, Accel sold shares worth ₹317 Cr – translating into a gross return multiple of 8.6X. Madison India also pocketed raked in ₹96.9 Cr, clocking a gross return of 7.2X.
RentoMojo’s ₹1,256 Cr IPO comprised a fresh issue of shares worth ₹150 Cr and an OFS of up to 2.74 Cr shares worth ₹1,105.6 Cr. Its public issue received bids for 158.68 Cr shares against 2.18 Cr shares on offer, taking the overall subscription to 72.88X.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Can Discovered Materials Help Chips Beat The Heat With AI?
As AI chips grow more powerful, heat and material limitations are threatening to slow the semiconductor progress. Discovered Materials is tackling this bottleneck with AI agents that can search, simulate and validate new materials for advanced chips.
Materials Science Meets AI: Founded in 2026, Discovered Materials uses AI agents to accelerate the discovery of new materials for semiconductors. Its AI agents generate candidate structures and estimate properties and distinguish theoretically-attractive candidates from materials that can ultimately be manufactured and deployed.
Beyond Discovery: The startup claims to have so far generated more than 500 previously unknown materials, which it claims are computationally stable. However, only a small number may have plausible synthesis routes. To address this, Discovered Materials is building experimental and verification capabilities that connect candidate generation to synthesis and lab validation.
The IP Ambition: The US-based startup’s long-term ambition is to become a materials and intellectual-property company, potentially licensing discoveries to semiconductor and chemical companies. It also plans to focus on expanding its laboratory infrastructure and computational capabilities.
With India’s semiconductor market projected to become a $155 Bn opportunity by 2031, here is how Discovered Materials is searching for cooler chips, one material at a time…

items.content: Mumbai: After heavy buying in the June quarter, India's retail investors turned sellers in the secondary market in July and August while stepping up investments in IPOs as primary-market activity accelerated. Retail investors sold a combined ₹5,674 crore in the secondary market in July and August after buying ₹42,774 crore in the June quarter, according to data compiled from NSE. In contrast, they invested more than ₹12,618 crore in the primary market during the two months, compared with ₹1,307 crore in the June quarter.Analysts said the run-up in mid-cap and small-cap stocks since the rebound in early April could have prompted some investors to lock in gains and move money to fresh issuances. "Investors are rotating liquidity from existing stocks towards primary issues," said Saurabh Jain, Head of Fundamental Research, SMC Global Securities. "It appears more like a tactical shift in allocation. Some investors may be booking profits and becoming selective amid elevated valuations and market volatility. At the same time, the strong IPO pipeline is providing fresh opportunities, including potential listing gains and new growth stories."134296977So far in FY27, retail investors have bought nearly ₹37,070 crore in the secondary market and ₹13,925 crore in the primary market, taking their cumulative investments across the two markets to ₹50,995 crore in the first 5 months of the financial year.Read more: NSE IPO: Every Rs 10 move in shares could swing Radhakishan Damani’s wealth by nearly Rs 40 croreIn FY26, retail investors sold nearly ₹5,803 crore in the secondary market while investing ₹42,608 crore in the primary market. Gains from India's main indices in July and August were moderate, while the broader markets continued to strengthen. The Sensex and Nifty gained 0.1% and 0.3%, respectively, over the two months, while the BSE MidCap 150 and BSE SmallCap 250 indices rose 3.5% and 2.6%. The shift towards primary issues coincided with a sharp pick-up in IPO activity. Twelve IPOs raised ₹28,648 crore in July, while 23 issues raised ₹23,453 crore in August. Average listing-day gains rose to nearly 14% in July and 29% in August, compared with 1.44% between January and June.Read more: Rupee languishes at six-week low ahead of Fed outcome, RBI limits lossesPuneet Singhania, director, Master Capital Services, said the shift reflects profit booking, selective buying and reallocation of liquidity rather than an exit from equities. "Investors have become more selective about valuations in the secondary market. Importantly, retail participation in mainboard IPOs has increased to 29% in FY27 from 23% in FY26, showing that retail investors continue to deploy capital into equities. Strong SIP inflows, which reached a record ₹32,297 crore in August, further reinforce this trend," he said. The selling in the secondary market is therefore more of a tactical shift than a structural withdrawal, Singhania said.

items.content:
By Shina Abubakar
A final year student of Obafemi Awolowo University, OAU, Oluwole Oluwasegun of the department of Marerial Science and engineering has reportedly committed suicide.
A statement issued by the Public Relations Officer of the institution, Olarewaju Abiodun on Wednesday disclosed that the incident occurred on Tuesday afternoon at the off campus hostel of the deceased.
Abiodun added that the management was informed of the incident in the afternoon that the deceased committed suicide at his residence located around Damico area of Ooni layout in the ancient town.
“Upon receipt of the information, the University’s Quick Response and Security (QRS) Team immediately proceeded to the location. The Nigeria Police was immediately contacted, and officers from the ‘A’ Division, Moore, Ile-Ife, joined the University’s security personnel at the scene.
“The student was subsequently conveyed to the University Health Centre, where he was certified dead by a medical doctor”, Abiodun added
Abiodun disclosed that University is deeply concerned by the circumstances surrounding the death, hence, it handed relevant information and items recovered from the scene to the Police for further investigation.
The Police have commenced investigation into the circumstances of the incident.
“The University has also notified the appropriate student affairs authorities for necessary follow-up, particularly with respect to the welfare and support of students affected by the incident”, he said.
Abiodun further disclosed that the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Simeon Bamire has extended the heartfelt condolences of the management to the family, friends, classmates and colleagues of the deceased at this difficult moment.
He said the school further encouraged any student experiencing severe emotional distress, relationship difficulties, financial pressures or other personal challenges to seek help promptly from trusted persons
and the appropriate University support structures.
The Vice Chancellor has reaffirmed his commitment to the welfare of staff and students, adding, “no student should feel that he or she has to confront overwhelming difficulties alone.”

By Hadiza Yusuf
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Kano State has selected Alhaji Muhammad Sani Abacha, son of former Head of State General Sani Abacha, as its candidate for the 2027 governorship election.
He emerged following the withdrawal of the party’s previous candidate, Muhammad Bello Dalha.
The decision was taken at an expanded state executive committee meeting held in Kano on Wednesday, where the party conducted an affirmation and replacement primary.
The state PDP Chairman, Dr Bello Gambo Bichi, said the process was carried out in line with the party’s constitution and electoral laws.
Bichi explained that Bello Dalha had earlier won the party’s primary but later withdrew following consultations among party stakeholders in Kano and Abuja.
“The law says that as a result of withdrawal, a replacement primary must be held. That is what brought us here today. We have affirmed Muhammad Sani Abacha as the gubernatorial candidate of our great party in Kano State,” Bichi said.
The affirmation was followed by a replacement primary, where Abacha was formally declared the winner by the chairman of the electoral panel, Dr Abba Abdullahi.
Abdullahi said the exercise followed the party’s guidelines and relevant electoral regulations, adding that Abacha met the requirements for nomination.
As part of efforts to settle the party’s internal disagreements, the PDP also allocated the deputy governorship slot to the group led by Kabiru Tanimu Turaki.
The party subsequently named former factional chairman and ex-commissioner for Land and Agriculture, Alhaji Yusuf Ado Kibiya, as the deputy governorship candidate.
Bichi said the decision followed consultations and reconciliation among the different groups within the party.
“As part of the reconciliation process, we also replaced some of our National Assembly and State Assembly candidates. Representatives of INEC were present and witnessed the entire exercise,” he said.

items.content:
Raphinha scored a hat-trick as Barcelona ripped Racing Santander to shreds in a spectacular 7-2 triumph in La Liga on Wednesday.
Hansi Flick’s league leaders preserved their 100 percent record with a thumping victory over their promoted opponents, moving three points clear of Real Madrid.
Joao Cancelo, Gabriel Jesus and Lamine Yamal also scored for the unstoppable Catalan giants, who have netted 33 goals in seven games across all competitions.
With lightning flashing above Camp Nou, Barca started at rapid pace and took the lead with a thunderbolt from Cancelo.
The defender crashed a shot in off the crossbar from long range in the eighth minute to get Flick’s side up and running.
Dani Olmo twice came close before Raphinha won and converted a penalty for Barca’s second.
The Brazilian was clumsily brought down by Pedro Felipe and thrashed the spot-kick into the bottom right corner.
Racing Santander pulled one back when Maguette Gueye barged his way through and produced a neat finish to beat Barca goalkeeper Joan Garcia.
However it proved only brief respite for the visitors, with Cancelo provoking the third with another long-range effort which deflected in off Asier Villalibre.
Raphinha, thriving playing as Barca’s centre-forward, bagged Barca’s fourth after he was played in on goal by Olmo.
Teenage star Yamal should have added a fifth after the electric Karim Adeyemi was brought down in the box, but Julen Agirrezabala saved his penalty.
Barca reserve goalkeeper Wojciech Szczesny replaced Garcia at half-time after the Spain international appeared to hurt himself while slipping as he went to get the ball.
Yamal hit the post and later had a goal ruled out for offside, as the youngster suffered a more frustrating night than some of his colleagues.
In the second half Yassir Zabiri pulled another back for Racing after a dreadful error from Szczesny, who tried and failed to dribble the ball.
Zabiri tackled him to score. Barcelona’s fifth arrived almost immediately with another penalty after Adeyemi was brought down.
Raphinha completed his hat-trick from the spot for his ninth league goal, extending his lead as the league’s top goalscorer.
He was replaced by his compatriot Gabriel Jesus, who added the sixth with a sharp finish into the top corner after being played in by Yamal.
The winger eventually got his goal when Adeyemi roared down the left wing and set him up for Barca’s seventh and final goal.

items.author: efosataiwo@vanguardngr.com
items.content:
Manchester United’s problems mounted as they crashed out of the League Cup after blowing a two-goal lead in a stunning 3-2 defeat against Brighton on Wednesday.
Michael Carrick’s side slumped to their second successive home defeat following a wretched collapse in the third round at Old Trafford.
United led through goals from Shea Lacey and Mason Mount inside just 10 minutes.
But Charalampos Kostoulas sparked Brighton’s revival and Pascal Gross equalised before Maxim De Cuyper grabbed the winner to leave Carrick shell-shocked as his team were booed off.
It was another brutal blow for United after their controversial 1-0 home defeat against Manchester City on Sunday.
The referees’ governing body admitted that VAR officials were wrong to allow City striker Erling Haaland’s winner, which left United with only one win from their first four Premier League matches.
Having led United to third place last season in his spell as interim boss, Carrick was expected to oversee a title challenge this term after being appointed on a permanent basis.
But United have already lost three times in six games in all competitions, putting Carrick under pressure to turn the tide at Fulham in the top-flight on Sunday.
A defeat in west London at the weekend would leave United in a full blown crisis barely a month into the new campaign.
Amid criticism of United’s close-season transfer recruitment, Carrick’s decision to make eight changes exposed the lack of depth in his squad.
At least Lacey offers hope for the future at United, unlike fellow highly-rated teenager JJ Gabriel, who has reportedly expressed his wish to leave Old Trafford.
The 19-year-old midfielder showed why Carrick has put his faith in him after eight minutes.
Taking possession just inside the Brighton penalty area, Lacey bagged his first ever goal for United as he lashed a clinical finish into the bottom corner.
Mount doubled United’s lead two minutes later, pouncing to fire into the roof of the net after Marcus Rashford’s shot was saved by Jason Steele.
But United’s defensive issues resurfaced in first half stoppage-time when Kostoulas punished poor marking from Ayden Heaven to drill past Karl Darlow.
– Sloppy United –
That setback unnerved United and they conceded a 65th minute equaliser as Gross controlled Luka Vuskovic’s header and fired home from close-range.
Carrick’s men were in disarray and Brighton struck again in the 70th minute when De Cuyper swept Kostoulas’s pass into the net from six yards after sloppy United defending.
Carrick sent on Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha in the closing stages but United were unable to find an equaliser.
Brighton have now knocked United out of two cups in the space of nine months after winning in the FA Cup at Old Trafford in January.
It was the first time in 50 years that United had lost after being 2-0 up at home.
Tammy Abraham starred as Aston Villa won for just the second time this season, beating Coventry 3-1 at the CBS Arena.
Villa and Coventry are both in the Premier League relegation zone after dismal starts to the season.
Unai Emery’s men, beaten three times in four league games, showed signs of stopping the rot as Abraham slotted home from George Hemmings’s deft pass in the seventh minute.
Victor Torp hauled Coventry level with a superb free-kick in the 27th minute.
Ross Barkley restored Villa’s lead five minutes before half-time with a header from Ibrahim Mbaye’s corner.
Abraham killed off Coventry when he slotted home from Barkley’s flick in the 59th minute.
Charly Alcaraz came off the bench to seal Everton’s 1-0 win over second tier Wolves with a curling strike in the 80th minute.
Fourth tier Fleetwood Town reached the fourth round for the first time, beating Championship side Sheffield United 1-0.
On Tuesday, Arsenal won 4-2 at Ipswich, Liverpool beat troubled Tottenham 3-1, Fulham claimed a 3-2 win at West Ham and Brentford won 2-1 at Reading.
Holders Manchester City host Norwich on Thursday.

By Dayo Johnson
The Ondo State government has said that 49 people have now died from suspected poisonous alcohol consumption, with 170 others affected across the state.
Commissioner for Health, Dr. Banji Ajaka, who released the updated figure said that surveillance and emergency response have been scaled up in the affected communities.
Ajaka said that eight of the latest deaths were recorded in lrele council area, while investigations continue to trace the source of the killer substance.
He said that the casualty figure had increased and extended to Irele Local Government where eight people were reported to have passed away following the same way.
“As we are now, Irele (LG) is where we have serious issue now, our people were there and many people have died . About eight people have been recorded to have died as at yesterday’s night.
“So all the people that have been affected altogether now is about 170, those that have been admitted and those that have died. “
He however noted that the state government was being proactive about it to prevent further spread to other local governments as the medical and health officers and other stakeholders immediately moved to anywhere they heard the report.
“We are always be fast about it wherever and whenever we heard the report of the issue, our teams are already in Irele as I’m talking to you now “
The state is collaborating with NAFDAC, NDLEA, DSS, NSCDC and other agencies in the ongoing probe.
Ajaka noted that Ondo’s rapid response was commended at a national meeting of health commissioners and officials of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC).
Ajaka had traced the Odigbo incident to locally brewed alcohol and herbal mixtures served at two naming ceremonies in communities including New Town, Odole, Okele, Orita Odigbo, Araromi-Obu and Oniparaga.
He disclosed that at one of the ceremonies, an outsider brought the drink consumed by guests.
Ajaka warned residents to avoid unregulated drinks, saying even those marketed as herbal medicine can be deadly when contents are unknown.
Recall that the state police command through the spokesperson DSP Jimoh Abayomi said that 15 suspects have been arrested in connection with the sale and distribution of a local herbal alcoholic mixture popularly known as “monkey tail,”
‎Abayomi said that the command had commenced investigation into the circumstances surrounding the deaths.
According to him, one of those arrested is Oloruntoba Babatunde, alias “Meko,” who is suspected of being involved in the production of the toxic substance believed to contain methanol.
Abayomi said Babatunde was assisting the police with investigations, adding that substances suspected to be methanol had also been recovered and sent for forensic examination to determine their composition and possible link to the reported deaths.
The arrests followed the state government’s ban on the sale and distribution of unverified alcoholic drinks after 30 people reportedly died and 50 others were hospitalised in Odigbo after consuming the herbal alcoholic mixture.

By Adegboyega Adeleye
A member of the House of Representatives, Abdulmumin Jibrin, has expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu will win Kano State in the 2027 presidential election, despite the political influence of former governor Rabiu Kwankwaso.
Jibrin, who represents Kiru/Bebeji Federal Constituency of Kano State, stated this on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, while discussing the political situation in Kano ahead of the 2027 election.
Kwankwaso, a former two-term governor of Kano, is the running mate to the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, Peter Obi, in the 2027 election.
Jibrin, who has previously been associated with the Kwankwasiyya political movement, said he and other APC politicians in Kano understood the movement and its political structure.
He said, “Who is more Kwankwasiyya than us? We understand the entire dynamics, Seun, if you want me to put a bet, I will put a bet with you, we will deliver Kano for the President (Tinubu), and the president will win in the 2027 election.”
The lawmaker said the political perception surrounding Tinubu’s support in Kano should not be mistaken for the actual electoral outcome, arguing that the result of the election would provide the clearest picture of voters’ choices.
“Yes, there is always perception but I keep telling people that what will produce the real picture of what is on ground is the election results. Nigeria is a not a country that you could say you have a cooling system that could give you an idea of what the people are going through. Yes, there are challenges,” he said.
Jibrin further claimed that Tinubu’s support had increased in northern Nigeria.
“The president has never been liked so much as he is being liked in the Northern part of the country,” he said.
On the APC’s preparations in Kano, Jibrin said the party’s political leaders were already working together ahead of the election.
“In Kano, we are preparing ourselves, the governor is very much on ground and experienced. The deputy governor is extremely experienced, the deputy senate president is there. Senator Hanga is there, Kabiru Gaya is there, Shekarau is there, the chairman, appropriations committee is there (Bichi), we are meeting daily, we understand the dynamics,” he said.
Jibrin’s comments come amid heightened political realignments ahead of the 2027 presidential election, with Obi and Kwankwaso now campaigning together on the NDC ticket, while Tinubu seeks a second term on the platform of the All Progressives Congress.
The lawmaker had also previously expressed confidence that Tinubu would defeat Kwankwaso in Kano, while acknowledging that the former governor remained influential in the state and retained a significant support base.

items.content:
By Henry Umoru
The National Assembly has transmitted to the Houses of Assembly of the 36 states for consideration and approval, the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026.
With the transmission, the National Assembly has asked state legislatures to consider the bill in accordance with their respective legislative procedures and communicate their resolutions to the National Assembly upon completion of their deliberations.
The Clerk to the National Assembly, CNA, Kamoru Ogunlana disclosed this on Wednesday in a statement he signed and the transmitted bill is State Police Establishment bill, being the only constitutional alteration bill that had been passed by both the Senate and the House of Representatives in the current 10th Assembly .
Recall that the Senate on the strength of Executive bill received from President Bola Ahmed Tinubu on Tuesday , June 23, 2026, expeditiously considered and passed the State Police Establishment Bill for third reading on Wednesday, June 24, 2026, while the House of Representatives later considered the same executive bill and it was read the passed for third reading on July 23, 2026.
The transmission marks the commencement of the next phase of the constitutional alteration process, just as it was carried out in pursuant to Section 9 and a directive from the leadership of the National Assembly.
The 2/3 concurrence means that at least, 24 out of the 36 States Houses of Assembly, must concur to the Constitution alteration bill before final transmission to President Tinubu for presidential assent.
The National Assembly also emphasised that the state legislatures remain constitutionally independent in considering the proposed amendments.
The development is significant because the Constitution requires substantial support from the state legislatures before the National Assembly can proceed with constitutional alterations, even as Section 9 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, provides that a bill seeking to alter the Constitution cannot be passed by either chamber of the National Assembly unless it is approved by resolutions of not less than two-thirds of the Houses of Assembly of the 36 states.
Meanwhile, the Constitution does not prescribe a deadline for the state Houses of Assembly to communicate their resolutions, but the National Assembly said it expects them to do so within 30 days of receiving the bill.
Kamoru Ogunlana who noted that the 30-day period is only an administrative timeframe and does not constitute a constitutional deadline, said, “It is noted that the Constitution does not prescribe a specific period within which the State Houses of Assembly are required to communicate their resolutions on a constitutional alteration Bill.
“Nevertheless, in the interest of an orderly, coordinated and timely conclusion of the constitutional alteration process, the State Houses of Assembly are expected to consider the Bill and communicate their respective resolutions to the National Assembly within 30 days of receipt.
“For clarity,” he stressed, “the 30-day period is an expected administrative timeframe and does not constitute a constitutional deadline.”
Ogunlana who explained that the federal legislature recognised the responsibility vested in the state Houses of Assembly and would respect their independence throughout the process, said, The National Assembly recognises the constitutional responsibility vested in the State Houses of Assembly and respects their independence in the consideration of the Bill.”
The CNA who further explained that the transmission was intended to facilitate the orderly discharge of the state legislatures’ constitutional responsibility rather than dictate the outcome of their consideration, however assured that the National Assembly would adhere strictly to constitutional requirements and due process as the exercise progresses.
He said, “The National Assembly remains committed to ensuring that the constitutional alteration process is conducted in strict compliance with the Constitution and in accordance with the principles of due process, institutional cooperation and respect for the legislative responsibilities of all tiers of the legislature.”
The state Houses of Assembly are now expected to commence their respective legislative consideration of the Sixth Alteration Bill.
After receiving their resolutions, the National Assembly will determine the next steps required under the Constitution.
Ogunlana said: “Upon receipt of the resolutions of the State Houses of Assembly, the National Assembly will proceed with the necessary steps in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.”
The transmission of the bill to the 36 state legislatures therefore brings the constitutional amendment process to a critical stage, with the required state-level approval now forming the next major hurdle before further action by the National Assembly.

items.content:
The combined revenues accruing to Nigerian state governments have risen from N4.8 trillion in 2022 to N15.5 trillion following the removal of petrol subsidy, but spending on education and healthcare as a proportion of state budgets has declined, African Democratic Congress, ADC, candidate for Lagos State House of Assembly, Eti-Osa Constituency 2, Ayo Adio, has said.
Adio questioned how governors have deployed the increased revenues, arguing that the major justification for subsidy removal was that additional resources would be channelled into infrastructure, education and healthcare.
Speaking during an interview on Arise TV, Adio said the proportion of state budget spending on education had fallen from 14 per cent to 12 per cent, while healthcare spending had declined from seven per cent to six per cent.
“The amount in terms of percentage of budget spending that has gone into education has actually shrunk from 14 per cent to 12 per cent. The combined amount in percentage terms of that revenue that has accrued to states for healthcare spending has shrunk from 7 per cent to 6 per cent,” he said.
Adio also said the number of states relying on loans to fund budget deficits had increased from 19 to 25, questioning whether the additional revenues had translated into improved public services.
“So, I ask you, what is working? What is working?” he asked.
He also questioned the level of infrastructure investment across the country, citing prolonged traffic and delays on major highways, including the Ore Expressway and routes linking travellers to Agbor, Ilorin and Kaduna from Abuja.
“When you travel across this country, you don’t need a prophet to tell you that not enough has gone into spending of infrastructure,” Adio said.
The ADC candidate argued that the increase in government revenues should prompt a review of how the resources are deployed, particularly in addressing the rising cost of living and production.
He backed targeted subsidies for local refiners, saying the government could provide crude to domestic refiners to improve efficiency and potentially reduce petrol prices.
Adio cited the use of targeted subsidies by countries including the United States and South Korea to support strategic industries.
“States across the world use targeted subsidies at production so that they can either become competitive to create jobs and in certain instances to pass lower costs to the end user on the last mile,” he said.
He said the rising costs of petrol, electricity, education and housing were placing additional pressure on households, and questioned whether Nigerians would benefit more from allowing governors to control increased revenues or from deploying part of the resources towards targeted industrial subsidies.
“Then you have to ask the fundamental question whether you want governors to be controlling the excess revenues that they claim that they have, or whether you want an industrial subsidy that guarantees lower prices for you at the pump,” he said.
