items.content:
By Naeemah Junaid
The National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) and the National Hajj Commission of Nigeria (NAHCON) have renewed their commitment to deploying digital technology to enhance Hajj administration, improve operational efficiency and strengthen service delivery to Nigerian pilgrims.
The commitment was reached when the Chairman of NAHCON, Ambassador Ismail Abba Yusuf, led a delegation of the Commission on a strategic visit to NITDA headquarters in Abuja, where he met with the Director-General of the Agency, Kashifu Inuwa Abdullahi, CCIE.
The engagement focused on strengthening technical cooperation between the two institutions and exploring practical ways of integrating technology across the various stages of Hajj operations.
Speaking during the meeting, Inuwa said NITDA was ready to support NAHCON in building a more coordinated and sustainable digital framework for Hajj administration.
He noted that the complexity of Hajj operations, which involves registration, payments, aviation, accommodation, transportation, feeding, healthcare and the movement of large numbers of pilgrims, required systems capable of working together seamlessly.
The NITDA DG cautioned against treating digital transformation as a one-time technology project, stressing that sustainable transformation required continuous improvement and institutional commitment.
“Digital transformation is not a one-off project. It is a journey and a journey that needs constant improvement,” he said.
Inuwa explained that technology should be deployed as an enabler of institutional objectives and not as an end in itself.
“Digital transformation is not just about technology. It is about your business value proposition. It is about the business, not technology. Technology enables you to deliver your business objectives,” he added.
He urged NAHCON to address the challenge of siloed systems by developing an integrated digital architecture that would allow information to move efficiently across different aspects of Hajj administration.
According to him, an integrated system would provide end-to-end visibility of operations, improve coordination and enable management to make timely, data-driven decisions.
The NITDA DG also drew attention to the growing relevance of artificial intelligence and intelligent digital systems, noting that emerging technologies could provide new opportunities for improving institutional processes and service delivery.
He recalled NITDA’s previous support to NAHCON in areas including training and process documentation, expressing the Agency’s readiness to build on the existing relationship through renewed technical collaboration.
Inuwa further encouraged the Commission to explore Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models in implementing major digital projects, noting that such arrangements could attract private-sector expertise and investment while reducing the financial burden on government.
He said NITDA would also continue to promote quality and value for money in government technology projects through proper system design, certified implementation and independent quality assurance.
On capacity development, the DG assured NAHCON of the Agency’s readiness to support training for ICT personnel and digital orientation for state coordinators and other stakeholders involved in Hajj administration.
He stressed that successful digital transformation must become embedded in the institution and should not depend on the tenure of individual officials.
“It is not about the board. It is not about just the chairman. It is about the institution,” Inuwa said.
Earlier, the NAHCON Chairman, Ambassador IsmailIsmail A. Yusuf, said the Commission’s visit was prompted by the need to accelerate the digitalisation of Hajj arrangements in Nigeria and align its operations with global best practices.
Yusuf noted that Saudi Arabia had made significant advances in the digital management of Hajj, adding that Nigeria needed to strengthen its systems to improve coordination and service delivery.
While acknowledging the progress already recorded by NAHCON, he said several processes remained manual and required further automation and integration.
“We’re trying to digitise Hajj arrangements in line with global best practice,” the Chairman said.
He explained that NAHCON was seeking NITDA’s technical expertise in areas such as system assessment, capacity building, process improvement, data management and the integration of existing digital platforms.
The Chairman said closer cooperation with NITDA would help strengthen the Commission’s digital infrastructure and ensure better coordination of information between Nigerian and Saudi systems.
“That is why our cooperation with NITDA is very, very important, that we work together. We are on the same page in everything we do. We compare notes and all that,” he said.
Presenting an overview of NAHCON’s digital solutions, the Commission’s Head of ICT, Shehu Raji said several platforms had been developed in-house despite budgetary constraints.
These include electronic registration, package and programme management, aviation management, automated flight manifests, seating distribution, real-time logistics, accommodation allocation, feeding management, electronic medical records, passport release management and the Hajj Companion application.
He said the Hajj Companion application provides pilgrims with mapped information on accommodation and major Hajj locations in Makkah, Madinah, Mina and Arafat, helping them navigate the various sites during the pilgrimage.
However, Raji noted that some of the systems were only partially deployed and required further development, integration and technical support.
He said improved interoperability would eliminate unnecessary duplication of data entry, enhance data accuracy and facilitate better coordination of pilgrim information.
Raji also emphasised the importance of data security and integrity, noting that reliable information was critical to effective accommodation, transportation, security and other Hajj arrangements.
At the conclusion of the engagement, both institutions agreed to strengthen their partnership through technical collaboration, capacity building, system integration, process improvement and quality assurance.
The two organisations also agreed on the proposed establishment of a technical working group to coordinate priority areas and ensure sustained engagement.
The renewed partnership is expected to advance the development of a more integrated, secure and efficient digital Hajj ecosystem in Nigeria, while improving accountability, reducing manual processes and enhancing the overall experience of Nigerian pilgrims.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹10 Lakh on ride unicorn Rapido for misleading advertisements, unfair trade practices, unfair contract and dark patterns, where consumers are prompted to pay more before their rides are confirmed.
The order, passed by a bench comprising chief commissioner Nidhi Khare and commissioner Anupam Mishra, follows a sector-wide examination of cab aggregators operating in India to understand pre-ride tipping and dynamic pricing practices in India.
During the investigation, the CCPA found that Rapido’s app displayed users prompts suggesting specific top-ups of ₹10, ₹20 or ₹30 to improve their chances of getting a ride.
The regulator held that Rapido’s algorithm first quoted a fare, and then, once the rider had booked at that fare, asked the rider to pay more because ‘Captains’ (drivers) were supposedly not accepting the fare. That created a false impression that getting a ride quickly depends on paying extra fees.
The CCPA held this to be “confirm shaming”, a dark pattern listed under the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023, as it creates urgency and a fear of losing the ride if the rider does not agree to pay more.
Separately, the regulator examined Rapido’s “set your price” slider and found its colour coding was steering pricing decisions. Raising the price surfaced a green message about a higher chance of getting a ride, while lowering it triggered a red or orange warning.
This design, the CCPA held, amounted to a second dark pattern — “interface interference”.
A tip, as the regulator observed, is a voluntary payment made after a service has been rendered, and can not be presented as a condition for the service being provided at all.
It also pointed to the Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025, which require any tipping feature to be offered only after a ride is completed — not at the time of booking or during the ride.
Rapido had argued that tipping on its platform is voluntary, and that the prompts simply mirrored the kind of real-time negotiation that happens offline between a rider and a driver.
The CCPA rejected these submissions, holding that the timing and design of the prompts applied pressure at the moment the users seemed to be the most dependent on the platform. It also noted that Rapido had not shown any data to show that paying more actually improves a rider’s chances of getting a ride, making the claim unsubstantiated and misleading.
The action against Rapido is part of the CCPA’s broader scrutiny of advance-tip and dark-pattern practices across ride-hailing and bike-taxi platforms.
The regulator had earlier issued notices to Uber, Ola, Rapido and Namma Yatri, directing them to comply with the 2023 dark patterns guidelines and file self-declarations on compliance. Its examination of Uber and Ola is still ongoing.
Besides, it also adds to the ongoing regulatory scrutiny over the advance tipping dark patterns employed by ride-hailing platforms. Earlier in August, the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) directed ride-hailing aggregators to remove tipping prompts shown before or during rides, saying these violate the Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines, 2025.
The ministry reiterated that passengers can tip drivers only after completing a ride, with the entire amount going to the driver. Platforms also cannot suggest that tipping could improve ride confirmation, driver acceptance or service quality.
The directive comes amid wider scrutiny of aggregators, including NHRC action over alleged overcharging. The 2025 guidelines also cover licensing, driver training and insurance, vehicle safety, fares and penalties, including licences of up to five years and fines of up to ₹1 Cr.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Foodtech unicorn Rebel Foods managed to cut its net loss for the fiscal year FY26 by 16.3% to ₹281.8 Cr from ₹336.6 Cr in the previous fiscal.
Operating revenue rose 20.7% to ₹1,951.6 Cr compared to ₹1,617.4 Cr in FY25.
The rise in revenue was led by product sales. Revenue from the sale of food items rose 20.9% to ₹1,891.9 Cr in the year under review from ₹1,565.3 Cr in FY25, while service revenue — commission, storage and franchise income — stayed broadly flat at ₹32.7 Cr.
Other operating revenues, which includes delivery services income, rose 38.5% to ₹27 Cr from ₹19.5 Cr last year.
Meanwhile, international revenue jumped 38.8% YoY to ₹283.81 Cr, while revenue from India grew 18% to ₹1,667.75 Cr. Revenue from overseas contributed 14.5% to the startup’s top line in FY26, a slight improvement from 12.6% in FY25. Rebel Foods currently operates 45+ brands across India, the United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom.
Including other income of ₹43.4 Cr, the total income stood at ₹1,995 Cr in FY26, up 20.3% from ₹1,658 Cr in the previous fiscal.
EBITDA loss also narrowed about 50% to ₹62.4 Cr from ₹123.7 Cr in the previous fiscal.
The startup said that a stronger consumer engagement and continued improvements across store operations, tech and supply chain contributed to higher productivity and margin expansion in the fiscal year.
“FY26 marks an important step forward for Rebel Foods, with growth and profitability increasingly coming together. As our platform scales, we are seeing the benefits of stronger consumer engagement, higher store productivity and operating leverage flow through to the business. Our focus remains on building a predictable, sustainable and highly scalable food platform for the long term,” cofounder and global CEO Ankush Grover said.
Founded in 2011 by Kallol Banerjee and Jaydeep Barman, Rebel Foods started as a delivery-only brand with ‘Faasos’. Over the years it has expanded the number of labels it operates.
Its portfolio of quick service restaurant (QSR) brands includes names like Behrouz Biryani, Mandarin Oak, Oven Story Pizza, Sweet Truth, LunchBox, The Good Bowl, Firangi Bake, the Biryani Life and Wendy’s, serving across 120+ cities.
The startup has raised $773 Mn in funding to date from the likes of KKR, Temasek, Lightbox, Evolvence, among others. The startup entered the unicorn club in 2021 after raising $175 Mn in its Series F round from investors Qatar Investment Authority, Coatue and Evolvence.
Rebel Foods has been recalibrating its financial and operational strategy as it reportedly eyes a public listing in India. Earlier, it had launched QuickiES, a 15-minute food delivery service, and planned to expand its offline footprint through physical restaurants and food courts. However, the startup had to shut down the vertical earlier this year amid high cash burn.
It has also been seeking to leverage its global presence and multi-brand portfolio, while improving unit economics and moving towards EBITDA breakeven. A leadership reshuffle, with Ankush Grover elevated to global CEO and Jaydeep Barman moving to chairman and group CEO, further aligned the organisation for its next phase ahead of a possible public listing.
Magnifying Rebel Foods’ Spending
The startup’s total expenses for the fiscal rose 14.1% to ₹2,265.9 Cr in FY26 from ₹1,986.6 Cr in the previous year. Here is a breakdown of where Rebel Foods spent the most:
Cost of Raw Materials Consumed: Comprising 34.6% of the total expenses, the spend on raw materials, components and packing materials rose 15.6% to ₹784.4 Cr during the year under review from ₹678.5 Cr in FY25.
Employee Benefit Expenses: Employee costs, which includes salaries, wages, gratuity fund and provident fund, rose 6.3% to ₹412.3 Cr from ₹387.8 Cr in FY25.
Brokerage And Commission: The biggest expense growth in FY26 was from this head, where it rose 30.6% to ₹317.7 Cr from ₹243.3 Cr in the previous fiscal.

items.title: 6 Tren Selfie Kekinian, Gampang Bikin Pakai Kamera Depan 85° Samsung Galaxy S26 FE

items.author: Bambang Dwi Atmoko
items.content:
Buat generasi yang terbiasa membagikan momen lewat TikTok dan Instagram, selfie bukan lagi sekadar soal memastikan wajah masuk ke dalam frame. Pose, outfit, gestur, hingga lokasi tempat foto diambil ikut menjadi bagian dari cerita. Karena itu, sudut kamera depan yang terlalu sempit bisa membuat sebagian momen justru hilang dari foto.
Samsung Galaxy S26 FE menjawab kebutuhan tersebut melalui kamera depan 12MP dengan Field of View (FoV) hingga 85°. Sudut pandang yang lebih luas memberikan ruang tambahan di dalam frame, sehingga pengguna dapat memasukkan lebih banyak orang, bagian outfit, maupun ambience di sekitar tanpa harus terus-menerus menjauhkan smartphone.
Bagi pengguna yang gemar bereksperimen dengan pose, kemampuan ini bukan sekadar angka pada spesifikasi kamera. Field of View yang lebih lebar dapat membuat sejumlah gaya foto yang populer di media sosial menjadi lebih mudah dilakukan, termasuk ketika ingin mengambil gambar dari sudut atas atau membuat komposisi yang melibatkan objek di sekitar.
Smartphone Mumpuni yang Mendukung Kebutuhan Tren Selfie 
Perubahan cara Gen Z membuat konten ikut mengubah kebutuhan terhadap kamera depan smartphone. Foto selfie sekarang sering kali digunakan untuk menunjukkan keseluruhan look, mulai dari pakaian yang dikenakan hingga suasana tempat seseorang sedang berada.
Dalam sebuah foto saat hangout, misalnya, wajah memang tetap menjadi titik perhatian. Namun, teman yang berdiri di samping, outfit, meja restoran, dekorasi kafe, hingga latar kota dapat menjadi bagian dari cerita. Masalahnya, semua elemen tersebut membutuhkan ruang.
Kamera dengan sudut pandang sempit membuat pengguna harus memilih antara memasukkan wajah lebih dekat atau memperlihatkan lebih banyak lingkungan. Ketika smartphone dijauhkan, komposisi memang menjadi lebih luas, tetapi cara ini tidak selalu praktis, terutama ketika berfoto bersama beberapa orang.
Kamera depan 12MP Samsung Galaxy S26 FE dengan FoV hingga 85° memberikan alternatif dengan memperluas area yang dapat masuk ke dalam satu frame. Hasilnya, pengguna memiliki lebih banyak ruang untuk bereksperimen dengan komposisi tanpa harus selalu menggunakan tongsis atau meminta orang lain mengambil gambar.
1. Upper View, Pose dari Atas yang Memperlihatkan Seluruh Look
Salah satu gaya yang menarik untuk dicoba adalah upper view. Smartphone diangkat tinggi di atas kepala, kemudian kamera diarahkan ke bawah sementara pengguna mendongak menghadap lensa.
Sudut seperti ini membuat foto tidak hanya berisi wajah. Badan, outfit, hingga permukaan lantai atau jalan dapat ikut menjadi bagian dari komposisi.
Dengan kamera depan Samsung Galaxy S26 FE yang memiliki FoV hingga 85°, ruang tambahan dalam frame membantu pengguna mengambil pose tersebut tanpa harus mengangkat smartphone terlalu jauh dari tubuh.
Untuk hasil yang lebih menarik, posisi tubuh dapat dibuat sedikit diagonal atau kaki diarahkan mengikuti perspektif kamera. Dengan begitu, area kosong di sekitar tubuh bisa dimanfaatkan untuk membuat komposisi foto terasa lebih dinamis.
2. From Above, Close-Up Tanpa Membuat Frame Terasa Sesak
From above merupakan versi yang lebih dekat dari upper view. Wajah menjadi objek utama dan memenuhi sebagian besar frame, tetapi kamera tetap mengambil gambar dari sudut atas.
Tantangannya adalah mempertahankan bahu dan sedikit bagian latar agar foto tidak terasa terlalu penuh.
Di sini, sudut pandang yang lebih luas dapat membantu. Kamera depan 12MP Samsung Galaxy S26 FE memungkinkan pengguna mempertahankan jarak relatif dekat dengan wajah sambil tetap memberikan ruang untuk bahu dan background.
Pose ini cocok ketika pengguna ingin menonjolkan ekspresi sekaligus mempertahankan karakter tempat pengambilan foto.
3. Finger Spread, Tangan Dekat Lensa Tetap Masuk Frame
Finger spread mengandalkan perspektif dengan telapak tangan didekatkan ke kamera, sementara wajah berada di belakangnya. Hasilnya menciptakan kesan playful karena tangan terlihat lebih besar dibandingkan wajah.
Pada kamera dengan sudut pandang sempit, pengguna mungkin harus menjauhkan tangan agar keduanya tetap masuk ke frame. Dengan FoV hingga 85°, area yang tertangkap kamera lebih luas sehingga tangan dapat tetap berada dekat dengan lensa tanpa harus terlalu memanjangkan posisi tangan.
Kuncinya adalah menjaga tangan tetap berada sedikit di samping atau depan wajah dan memastikan ekspresi wajah masih terlihat di sela-sela jari.
4. Face Screen, Wajah Tertutup tetapi Outfit Tetap Bercerita
Pose face screen biasanya menggunakan smartphone kedua untuk menutupi wajah. Fokus foto kemudian bergeser dari ekspresi menuju outfit, aksesori, serta suasana di sekitar.
Pose seperti ini sangat bergantung pada ruang dalam frame. Jika kamera terlalu sempit, pengguna harus memilih antara memperlihatkan tubuh lebih banyak atau mempertahankan latar.
Dengan kamera depan Samsung Galaxy S26 FE yang menawarkan FoV hingga 85°, pengguna dapat mengambil foto dari jarak yang relatif nyaman sambil mempertahankan area di sekitar subjek. Smartphone yang menutupi wajah tetap menjadi elemen utama, tetapi outfit dan ambience tidak harus ikut terpotong.
5. Big Things, Dua Tangan dan Dua Objek dalam Satu Frame
Gaya big things memanfaatkan kedua sisi frame. Pengguna merentangkan tangan sambil membawa atau memegang benda di kiri dan kanan tubuh. Bisa berupa aksesori, makanan, merchandise, atau benda lain yang sedang menjadi bagian dari momen.
Tantangannya sederhana: semakin banyak elemen yang ingin dimasukkan, semakin besar kebutuhan terhadap ruang horizontal. FoV hingga 85° pada kamera depan Samsung Galaxy S26 FE memberikan ruang yang lebih lega untuk komposisi seperti ini.
Pengguna juga tidak harus selalu mengambil foto dari jarak sangat jauh. Ini membuat pose lebih praktis ketika berada di ruangan atau lokasi yang memiliki ruang terbatas.
6. Through Glasses dan No Face, Manfaatkan Ruang Kosong
Ada pula pose yang lebih eksperimental, seperti through glasses atau no face. Pada through glasses, kamera memanfaatkan kacamata sebagai elemen foreground, sedangkan wajah dan lingkungan berada di belakangnya.
Sementara no face justru sengaja menghilangkan wajah dari pusat perhatian, misalnya dengan menutup wajah menggunakan tangan, rambut, atau objek lain.
Kedua gaya tersebut mengandalkan negative space atau ruang kosong di sekitar subjek. Kamera dengan FoV lebih luas membuat ruang tersebut lebih mudah dipertahankan, sehingga foto tidak terasa terlalu padat meski objek utama berada dekat dengan kamera.
Lebih Praktis untuk High-Angle Group Selfie
Kemampuan kamera depan Samsung Galaxy S26 FE juga relevan ketika selfie dilakukan bersama banyak orang. High-angle group selfie biasanya membutuhkan posisi smartphone lebih jauh agar semua wajah dapat masuk.
Masalahnya, tidak semua situasi memungkinkan pengguna menjauh. Saat berada di meja restoran, depan panggung, area konser, atau tempat wisata yang ramai, ruang gerak bisa sangat terbatas.
FoV hingga 85° memberikan ruang pandang lebih luas sehingga beberapa orang dapat masuk dalam satu frame tanpa harus menjauhkan smartphone secara berlebihan.
Artinya, pengguna tidak selalu membutuhkan tongsis hanya untuk mendapatkan komposisi group selfie yang lebih lega. Smartphone dapat tetap berada dalam jangkauan tangan, sementara lebih banyak orang dan latar tetap masuk ke frame.
Dari Hangout hingga Setelah Performance
Kebutuhan tersebut muncul dalam banyak situasi sehari-hari. Saat hangout, misalnya, selfie dari angle atas dapat digunakan untuk menangkap wajah sekaligus outfit dan suasana tempat.
Mirror selfie bersama teman juga menjadi lebih fleksibel karena area di sekitar tubuh memiliki ruang lebih besar. Begitu pula setelah performance, ketika pengguna ingin mengabadikan momen bersama teman tanpa kehilangan suasana panggung atau venue di belakang.
Untuk video bersama inner circle, kamera depan dengan sudut pandang lebih luas juga membantu memastikan lebih banyak orang tetap berada di dalam frame. Pengguna tidak perlu terus mengatur ulang posisi smartphone hanya karena satu orang berada sedikit di luar jangkauan kamera. Keunggulan FoV hingga 85° bukan hanya soal memperlebar gambar. Kemampuan tersebut memberi pengguna lebih banyak pilihan dalam menentukan bagaimana sebuah momen ingin diceritakan.
Bikin Konten Selfie Fenomenal dengan Galaxy S26 FE 
Samsung Galaxy S26 FE melalui kamera depan 12MP dan FoV hingga 85° pada akhirnya memberi lebih banyak ruang untuk bercerita. Wajah tetap menjadi bagian penting, tetapi bukan lagi satu-satunya elemen yang menentukan sebuah foto. More friends, more stories, and more moments can fit into one frame.
Tertarik untuk bikin konten selfie yang fenomenal? Galaxy S26 FE hadir untuk menemani pengguna yang ingin mengeksplorasi lebih jauh, menangkap lebih banyak perspektif, dan mengubah ide spontan menjadi karya yang stand-out. 
Untuk mendukung pengguna menikmati pengalaman Galaxy S26 FE, Samsung menghadirkan berbagai penawaran menarik yang dapat disesuaikan dengan kebutuhan. Galaxy S26 FE tersedia dalam varian 8GB/128GB dengan harga setelah promo Rp9.249.000 dan 8GB/256GB dengan harga setelah promo Rp11.249.000. Harga normalnya sendiri adalah Rp11.999.000 untuk varian 8GB/128GB  dan Rp13.999.000 untuk varian 8GB/256GB. Samsung juga akan merilis varian 8GB/512GB dalam waktu dekat.
Artikel berjudul 6 Tren Selfie Kekinian, Gampang Bikin Pakai Kamera Depan 85° Samsung Galaxy S26 FE yang ditulis oleh Bambang Dwi Atmoko pertama kali tampil di Gizmologi.id

items.author: Bambang Dwi Atmoko
items.content:
Kolaborasi di industri telekomunikasi tidak hanya berlangsung dalam urusan jaringan, layanan, maupun transformasi digital. Asosiasi dan pelaku industri juga membangun kolaborasi melalui kegiatan sosial yang memberikan dampak langsung kepada masyarakat.
Hal tersebut terlihat dalam kegiatan donor darah yang digelar Asosiasi Penyelenggara Telekomunikasi Seluruh Indonesia (ATSI) bersama komunitas industri ICT dan digital di Kantor Pusat Telkomsel, Gedung Telkomsel Smart Office (TSO), Jakarta Selatan, Senin (15/9/2026).
Bekerja sama dengan Palang Merah Indonesia (PMI) DKI Jakarta, kegiatan tersebut berhasil mengumpulkan 228 kantong darah. Seluruh darah yang terkumpul akan diserahkan kepada PMI DKI Jakarta untuk kemudian disalurkan kepada masyarakat yang membutuhkan.
Jumlah tersebut memang masih di bawah target awal penyelenggara sebanyak 300 kantong. Menurut Sekretaris Jenderal ATSI, Merza Fachys, sebagian calon pendonor tidak dapat mendonorkan darah karena tidak memenuhi ketentuan yang ditetapkan PMI. Namun, kegiatan tersebut tetap memperlihatkan keterlibatan berbagai elemen dalam ekosistem telekomunikasi dan digital, mulai dari asosiasi, operator, vendor, regulator hingga komunitas ICT.
Kontribusi ekosistem telekomunikasi
Inspektur Jenderal Kementerian Komunikasi dan Digital (Komdigi), Arief Tri Hardiyanto, menilai kolaborasi antara regulator dan pelaku industri perlu terus dijaga. Menurutnya, kepercayaan terhadap industri dibangun dalam waktu panjang sehingga perlu dipertahankan melalui hubungan dan kolaborasi yang baik antara seluruh pihak dalam ekosistem. “Membangun trust take years, but menghancurkan trust take second,” ujar Arief.
Ia juga mendukung kegiatan donor darah sebagai bagian dari rangkaian Hari Bhakti Postel ke-81 karena memberikan manfaat langsung kepada masyarakat sekaligus menjadi bentuk kegiatan bersama lintas elemen industri. Komposisi pihak yang hadir dalam kegiatan tersebut memperlihatkan luasnya ekosistem telekomunikasi Indonesia. Selain ATSI dan Telkomsel, hadir pula pejabat Komdigi, Asosiasi Pengembang Infrastruktur dan Menara Telekomunikasi (ASPIMTEL), PMI DKI Jakarta, serta perwakilan asosiasi, operator telekomunikasi, vendor dan komunitas ICT dan digital.
Sementara Direktur Keuangan dan Manajemen Risiko Telkomsel, Daru Mulyawan, melihat donor darah memiliki keterkaitan dengan fungsi dasar industri telekomunikasi: menghubungkan pihak yang berada di tempat berbeda. Menurutnya, kegiatan tersebut mempertemukan orang-orang yang memiliki keinginan untuk mendonorkan darah dengan masyarakat yang membutuhkan. “Tugas kita adalah menghubungkan pihak-pihak yang berada di tempat yang jauh menjadi terasa lebih dekat.”
Dalam konteks industri, analogi tersebut menarik karena fungsi konektivitas memang menjadi salah satu fondasi telekomunikasi. Namun, kegiatan sosial seperti donor darah menunjukkan bahwa hubungan antarpelaku ekosistem juga dapat diarahkan untuk kebutuhan di luar layanan teknologi. Daru juga menilai donor darah dapat menjadi bentuk kepedulian yang diwujudkan melalui tindakan sederhana dengan dampak yang besar bagi penerimanya.
Dari sisi penerima manfaat, kegiatan tersebut memiliki dampak yang lebih konkret. Ketua Bidang Kerja Sama dan Kemitraan PMI Provinsi DKI Jakarta, Isac Kharis Tahtawira, mengatakan rumah sakit di Jakarta membutuhkan sekitar 1.000–1.200 kantong darah setiap hari. Dengan 228 kantong yang terkumpul, kegiatan donor darah tersebut secara matematis setara dengan sekitar 19–23 persen dari kebutuhan harian yang disebutkan PMI DKI.
Kolaborasi ekosistem telekomunikasi dalam rangkaian Hari Bhakti Postel ke-81
Merza Fachys mengatakan kegiatan donor darah yang dilakukan dalam rangka Hari Bhakti Postel menjadi salah satu bentuk komitmen komunitas telekomunikasi dan digital untuk membantu memenuhi kebutuhan darah masyarakat. Ia juga melihat keterlibatan semakin banyak pihak dalam berbagai kegiatan Hari Bhakti Postel sebagai bagian dari konsolidasi industri. “Konsolidasi dari industri ini, kerja sama dari tiap-tiap pelaku industri akan membentuk sebuah kekuatan yang betul-betul besar.”
Pernyataan tersebut menggambarkan sisi lain dari ekosistem telekomunikasi. Industri ini tidak hanya terdiri dari operator yang menyediakan layanan kepada pelanggan, tetapi juga melibatkan perusahaan infrastruktur, vendor, regulator, asosiasi, serta berbagai komunitas pendukung.
Kegiatan donor darah menjadi salah satu agenda terakhir sebelum puncak peringatan Hari Bhakti Postel ke-81 yang akan berlangsung pada 27 September 2026 di Bandung. Ketua Umum Panitia Hari Bhakti Postel ke-81, Theodorus Ardi Hartoko, mengatakan rangkaian tahun ini mencakup berbagai bentuk kegiatan, mulai dari forum bisnis dan kolaborasi, olahraga, esports, hingga kegiatan sosial.
Sebelum donor darah, rangkaian HBP ke-81 telah diisi antara lain Konferensi dan Pameran Transformasi Digital Indonesia (DTI-CX), Fun Walk APJATEL, serta turnamen esports Mobile Legends oleh ASPIMTEL.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
Training of Punjab’s police field force in the use of body-worn cameras has been completed, with the project being launched initially in Lahore, where docking points for the cameras at police stations are being installed.
The body-worn cameras will be connected to Smart Safe City systems established in 43 cities across the province. Personnel of the Punjab Police, Highway Patrol, Dolphin Force and traffic wardens will wear the cameras while performing their duties.
The cameras’ digital facial recognition feature will help identify suspects. The state-of-the-art devices will also facilitate automated reading of motorcycle and vehicle number plates, while an instant threat alert can be generated in an emergency.
Also Read: 
The cameras are equipped with a calling facility for immediate communication. Police personnel will be able to record audio and video and take photographs through the devices. During duty, recordings will also be stored in the cameras’ built-in memory.
After completing their duty, personnel will place the cameras at designated docking points, where the recorded data will automatically be transferred from the devices and securely stored.
A ‘push-to-talk’ facility will enable field-duty officers to establish immediate contact with the control room, while an SOS emergency button will allow them to alert the control room in emergencies.
The cameras will be connected to a central monitoring system, with live monitoring carried out at the respective district Safe City control rooms.
Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif said the body-worn cameras would not only facilitate monitoring but also help curb corruption.
“Ensuring a sense of security among the public, particularly vulnerable segments, is the real measure of success,” she said regarding the initiative.
She said protection of the life and property of every individual in Punjab was the foremost responsibility of the government.
In a message on the International Day of Democracy, the chief minister said an informed citizenry, honest leadership and the rule of law were essential for the success of democracy.
She termed accountability a key pillar of democracy and reaffirmed the government’s resolve to hold corrupt elements accountable.
She said a systematic campaign against corruption was under way in Punjab.
The chief minister said supremacy of the Constitution was the essence of democracy, while an active civil society and effective institutions were crucial for promoting and strengthening democratic traditions.
Meanwhile, Naseerabad police in Lahore arrested two men for allegedly impersonating police officers and intimidating citizens in Gopal Nagar’s main market.
According to police, the suspects, Muhammad Asif and Abdul Majid, were wearing police caps with white shalwar kameez and allegedly presenting themselves as officials. When questioned, they failed to provide proof of their identity or employment.
Police arrested the two men and registered a case under Sections 170 and 171 of the Pakistan Penal Code for impersonating police officials and illegally using official police caps.

items.author: Shahbaz Rana
items.content:
Pakistan International Airlines Holding Company (PIAHCL) – the new entity established to keep loans and retain some assets before the airline's privatisation – incurred Rs21.6 billion losses during the first half of the last fiscal year, taking its total losses to Rs741 billion, official statistics reveal.
The continued losses despite PIA's privatisation have also put a question mark on the privatisation strategy that the government adopted and now wants to replicate for the sale of three profitable power distribution companies. The government has approved the transaction structure for the privatisation of power distribution companies under which it will retain most of the liabilities and pensioners by setting up two more companies like the PIA holding company.
According to the biannual report (July-December) 2025 of State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs), the PIA holding company incurred Rs21.6 billion fresh losses, becoming the sixth largest loss-making entity. With the increase, cumulative losses jumped to Rs740.6 billion – the fourth highest by any state-controlled entity in the civilian setup.
To service old debts, the government has allocated at least Rs30 billion in this fiscal year's budget. The interest cost for the current fiscal year alone is three times the Rs10 billion the government received against the sale of 75% stakes. Of the Rs135 billion total bid money, the government received Rs10 billion, while the remaining amount was being invested in PIA by the successful bidder. The remaining 25% shares would also go to the same bidders for Rs45 billion cash.
The Central Monitoring Unit (CMU) of the finance ministry tracks the financial health of Pakistan's public sector companies. Its report showed that net fiscal flow from these entities to the state sharply fell by 91% to a mere Rs35 billion during July-December 2025, down from Rs427 billion in the corresponding period, due to higher cash support and lower contributions. There was no reduction in overall losses, which remained at Rs343 billion during the first half of the last fiscal year, including Rs21.6 billion losses by the PIA holding company.
According to the biannual report, the National Highway Authority (NHA) topped the list of loss-making entities with Rs124.6 billion losses. Its cumulative losses jumped to Rs2.17 trillion – the highest by any entity. However, there is a fundamental flaw in the treatment of the NHA losses.
The federal government compels NHA to expand the national road network and gives the money from the development budget as a loan instead of a grant. During the period under review, the government booked Rs113 billion loans against the NHA. It then deducts interest on these loans before releasing the allocated budget.
The CMU report showed that the power sector's financial situation further deteriorated and the sector continued causing huge losses. Quetta Electric Supply Company's (QESCO) losses decreased to Rs35.3 billion – the second highest in the first half of the last fiscal year. This took the cumulative losses of the entity to Rs844 billion but yet it did not come on the merit of privatisation set out by the Privatisation Commission, which is more interested in selling the few profitable entities.
Third highest losses of Rs34.8 billion were caused by Sukkur Electric Power Company (SEPCO) during the first half of the last fiscal year, taking its cumulative losses to Rs554 billion. Pakistan Railways caused Rs29.4 billion losses, the fourth highest.
The fifth highest losses were also caused by a power distribution company – Peshawar Electric Supply Company (PESCO), incurring Rs23.7 billion losses and taking the total tally to Rs770 billion. PESCO too is not on the priority list of the Privatisation Commission.
The seventh highest losses were also caused by another power distribution company – Hyderabad Electric Supply Company (HESCO) – with Rs18 billion losses, taking total losses to Rs582 billion.
The Neelum Jhelum hydropower project, which has become a symbol of poor design and governance, also caused Rs14.5 billion losses. Its total losses stood at Rs100 billion, showed the official report.
In yet another case of bad governance and poor financial state of affairs, the closed Pakistan Steel Mills incurred Rs13 billion losses during the first half of the last fiscal year, taking its total losses to Rs275 billion, showed the report. The Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz (PML-N) government had closed the mill in 2016 and it is still incurring losses.
The CMU stated that the power distribution companies (DISCOs) continue to suffer from weak recoveries, technical losses, governance failures and tariff under-recoveries. These feed directly into the circular debt chain and disrupt generation companies (GENCOs), the Central Power Purchasing Agency-Guaranteed (CPPA-G), fuel suppliers and the sovereign balance sheet.
The CMU warned the cabinet committee on SOEs that the circular debt was posing high fiscal risks due to delayed recoveries from DISCOs, CPPA-G and public entities impairing the liquidity of Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL), Pakistan Petroleum Limited (PPL), Pakistan State Oil (PSO) and Pak-Arab Refinery Company (PARCO). Under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) 9 rules, aging receivables previously treated as "guaranteed recoverable" now generate direct impairment charges – exposing systemic fiscal interconnectedness, warned the CMU.
However, instead of addressing these fiscal risks, the Cabinet Committee on SOEs on Monday approved changing the law that warranted fiscal discipline and transparency.
The CMU has underlined that the IFRS risks were higher; the recognition of expected credit losses could materially reduce retained earnings and dividend-paying capacity across multiple SOEs. Debt covenants and leverage ratios may come under stress as accumulated profits are impaired, it added.
The CMU has also operationalised an integrated, policy-compliant cloud-enabled digital platform for the centralised management, reporting and analytics of SOE data.

Pakistan and Canada will resume negotiations on the Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA) in the first week of October, with both sides seeking to address outstanding issues and conclude the agreement, according to a statement issued on Tuesday.
The October round was agreed during a meeting between Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan and High Commissioner of Canada to Pakistan Tarik Ali Khan at the Ministry of Commerce. Senior officials, including Secretary Commerce Jawad Paul, attended.
The Canadian high commissioner described FIPA as a foundational step for increasing Canadian investment in Pakistan, saying it would give investors confidence through legal protection, arbitration and dispute-resolution mechanisms while paving the way for more joint ventures and broader trade arrangements. He noted Canadian companies recognised the scale of Pakistan's consumer market, but a predictable investment framework was essential.
He said the agreement would also send a positive signal to over 300,000 Canadians of Pakistani origin.
Kamal Khan said the government was committed to addressing legitimate concerns of investors and directed officials to hold preparatory consultations ahead of the next negotiating round.
"We are as ambitious as Canada in taking this process forward. Our objective is to resolve outstanding matters and establish a strong, mutually beneficial framework for long-term economic cooperation," he said.
Both sides also discussed cooperation in agriculture, mining, clean energy, aviation and value-added industries. The meeting reviewed a proposed hybrid renewable-energy project in Jhimpir, while a Canadian delegation is expected at an upcoming minerals investment forum in Pakistan.

items.content:
Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) staged a modest rebound on Tuesday as the benchmark KSE-100 index gained 1,421.67 points, or 0.85%, to settle at 169,392.33, driven by renewed buying across key sectors and improved investor sentiment.
The index moved between the intra-day high of 169,988 and low of 169,189, during which investors rebuilt positions in index-heavy stocks and helped fuel a broad recovery across the market.
The rebound was aided by emerging confidence after the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) decided on Monday to keep its policy rate unchanged at 11.5%. The decision eased concerns over an unexpected monetary policy shift and lent support to rate-sensitive shares.
Buying was seen across auto assemblers, cement producers, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration firms, refineries, power generation and oil marketing companies, which signalled widespread participation in the recovery.
The market regained some of the recent lost ground despite lingering uncertainty surrounding the US-Iran conflict and heightened risks to regional oil supplies. Crude prices rose nearly 2% on Tuesday as concerns over supply disruptions persisted after attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure left the kingdom's East-West pipeline offline and cast doubt on efforts to reduce shipping risks in the Gulf.
According to Ahmed Sheraz, equity trader at KASB KTrade, the stock market maintained a positive tone throughout the session. It was well supported by commercial banks, cement, pharmaceutical and oil & gas stocks, reflecting broad-based buying interest across key sectors.
Individually, UBL, Fauji Fertiliser, Lucky Cement and Bank Alfalah were among the notable positive contributors, helping sustain the index's upward momentum. The bourse also took cue from the improving sentiment in global markets, which provided a favourable backdrop for local equities.
Overall, the session reflected renewed confidence after the SBP's rate hold, with spreading buying across multiple sectors. Going forward, Sheraz said global sentiment, oil prices and macroeconomic developments would remain the key triggers.
Arif Habib Limited Deputy Head of Trading Ali Najib said investors opted for selective buying across auto assemblers, cement firms, commercial banks, E&P companies, refineries, power firms and OMCs, following the SBP's decision to leave the policy rate unchanged at 11.5%.
On the corporate front, Mughal Iron & Steel Industries reported a 2.6-time year-on-year rise in profit to Rs2,487 million in fiscal year 2026, with earnings per share at Rs7.41, driven by improved margins, lower finance costs and higher other income. The company declared a dividend per share of Rs2 after a hiatus of two years.
UBL, Fauji Fertiliser, Lucky Cement, Bank Alfalah, Pakistan Services, Pakistan Oilfields, Engro Holdings, Bank AL Habib, MCB and Systems Ltd emerged as major gainers, collectively adding 1,024 points to the index. Najib expects market activity to remain volatile, with selective profit-taking and stock-specific moves expected amid the ongoing result season.
Overall trading volumes decreased to 372 million shares compared with Monday's tally of 570.5 million. The value of traded shares stood at Rs17.2 billion.
In the ready market, shares of 494 companies were traded. Of these, 280 stocks closed higher, 166 fell and 48 remained unchanged.
Cnergyico Pk was the volume leader with trading in 56.2 million shares, remaining unchanged at Rs12.81. Foreign investors bought shares worth Rs143 million, the National Clearing Company reported.

"A digital transformation that leaves women behind is neither economically viable nor socially just," Iqbal asserted, reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to inclusive tech policies.

items.author: SHAHRAM HAQ
items.content:
Chinese automaker Geely is set to enter Pakistan's auto market, already straining under underused production capacity, as Bestway Automotive Private Limited (BAL) on Monday confirmed it has been appointed the brand's sole authorised distributor in the country, with vehicle bookings expected to open before the end of 2026.
BAL, part of the United Kingdom-based Bestway Group, unveiled its partnership with Geely at a media briefing in Lahore, positioning the tie-up as part of the conglomerate's long-term investment strategy in Pakistan, where it already operates across cement, banking, insurance, packaging, renewable energy and consultancy. Group Managing Director of the group's non-banking businesses in Pakistan, Muhammad Irfan Anwar Sheikh, said the partnership reflected the company's long-term view of the market. "For us, this partnership is a long-term commitment to Pakistan. Our group has been investing in and building businesses here for decades, across sectors including cement and banking, and that experience and track record provide reassurance to our stakeholders, partners and customers that we are here to build for the long term. With Geely, we are bringing together that local strength and experience with the technology, safety and global capabilities of a major automotive manufacturer," Sheikh said.
Geely vehicles will initially be brought in as completely built units (CBUs) before BAL shifts to local assembly at a completely knocked-down (CKD) facility it has recently acquired, the company said. Globally, Geely sold more than 3.02 million vehicles in 2025, including 1.69 million new-energy vehicles.
The automotive brand's arrival adds to what is now one of the most crowded automotive line-ups in Pakistan's history, with the number of assemblers operating in the country having climbed to around 17 in recent years as Chinese and other new entrants joined established Japanese and Korean players. Industry analysts note that this expansion has coincided with a widening gap between capacity and actual output. Pakistan's installed manufacturing capacity is estimated at between 500,000 and 600,000 vehicles annually, yet plant utilisation has slipped below 50% in recent periods, down sharply from levels above 80% seen less than a decade ago, according to industry data cited by manufacturers.
Analysts tracking the sector say several of the newer Chinese brands that entered Pakistan over the past few years have struggled to match early sales enthusiasm with durable after-sales networks, spare-parts availability and resale value, denting consumer confidence even as competitive pricing and modern features drew initial interest. Some smaller entrants have scaled back operations or seen showroom footfall taper once warranty and servicing gaps became apparent, industry analysts say, a pattern they caution any new entrant, including Geely, will need to avoid through sustained investment in service infrastructure.
Even so, sector experts argue Pakistan's automotive potential remains underexploited, pointing to a low car-ownership base, a young population and the government's still-pending long-term auto policy for 2026-31 as factors that could eventually help absorb idle capacity, provided policy consistency improves and financing costs remain manageable. They added that the market's near-term challenge is less about attracting new manufacturers and more about ensuring the ones already present, and those now arriving, can sustain the after-sales commitments their launches promise.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
Investment firm Novastar Partners has made its maiden India bet by investing an undisclosed sum in Aviral Bhatnagar-led venture capital fund A Junior VC (AJVC), becoming a limited partner (LP) for the firm.
Founded in 2024 by Bhatnagar, AJVC is a pre-seed focused investment firm that closed its maiden fund at ₹200 Cr last year. It has made 32 investments to date, backing early-stage startups like Iztri, Handy Panda, Mindcase, among others.
Backing startups at the pre-seed or idea stage, AJVC typically invests ₹1.5 Cr for 9% equity. The firm then works closely with founders to build out the business by helping refine product, optimising hiring and people strategy, assisting in sales and marketing, while also aiding in finance, legal and compliance operations.
Investment firm Novastar, which is building a private equity fund-of-funds, intends to support AJVC and its portfolio companies by facilitating follow-on funding rounds and providing networking opportunities as well as direct operational assistance.
AJVC’s investment strategy, its tech-led sourcing infrastructure, and Bhatnagar’s network in the early-stage investment ecosystem were the key reasons driving Novastar’s decision to back the firm, Novastar’s managing partner Dhruv Jhunjhunwala shared with Inc42.
“We believe a programmatic approach, like the one that AJVC is pursuing, where you build a sufficiently broad portfolio of a number of companies while maintaining discipline around selection, can be one of the most effective ways of investing at the pre-seed stage,” he added.
Founded by Jhunjhunwala in 2025, Novastar operates a SEBI-registered category II alternative investment fund (AIF) that aims to back leading venture capital funds as a LP, as well as making direct startup investments.
The fund focuses on sectors like AI, consumer tech, financial services, healthcare, and deep tech. It also aims to diversify its bets across the startup life cycle with plans to allocate around 15% of its capital to early stage strategies, the majority towards growth stage strategies, and a small share towards late stage strategies including secondaries and continuation funds.
Jhunjhunwala declined to share details around how much capital Novastar has raised till now or the capital it plans to deploy.
“In the medium term, we would love to announce our next set of investments that would be across funds and companies. But right now, our focus is on continuing to build the right portfolio and partnering with the right set of fund managers,” he said.

The proposed package included 20,000 MK-84 bombs, 20,000 BLU-117 bombs and 20,000 I-2000 Penetrator warheads. The weapons would be purchased with US taxpayer funds.
The MK-84 was among the most destructive conventional munitions in Western military arsenals. Its blast could propel metal fragments thousands of feet, penetrate thick concrete and metal and create large craters.

The proposed package included 20,000 MK-84 bombs, 20,000 BLU-117 bombs and 20,000 I-2000 Penetrator warheads. The weapons would be purchased with US taxpayer funds.

Breaking news: The Trump administration is preparing a $2.8 billion sale of 2,000-pound bombs to Israel, the largest single sale of the controversial munitions in recent years, a U.S. official told The Post. https://t.co/OBZqGeTtgw
— The Washington Post (@washingtonpost) September 15, 2026
The proposed package would exceed previous US transfers of 2,000-pound bombs to Israel under both the Biden and Trump administrations.
It would also be larger than a controversial $2.04 billion arms sale approved in 2025 that bypassed the standard congressional review process.
US public support for Israel had fallen since the Gaza war began in 2023, particularly among Democrats. A June Quinnipiac University poll found 48% ​of voters and 66% of Democrats believed the US ​was too supportive of Israel, up from 16% and 20% when the question ‌was ⁠first asked in 2017.
Trevor Ball, a former US Army explosive-ordnance-disposal technician, described Israel's use of the weapons, saying they were frequently employed when targeting buildings.
“If Hezbollah or whoever is in a building, an MK-84 will bring down the whole building,” Ball said.
Read More: US approves $151.8m emergency bomb sale to Israel during Iran war
The MK-84 was nicknamed the “hammer” by US pilots during the 1991 Gulf War. It was the only munition whose shipment to Israel was temporarily suspended by former president Joe Biden in 2024 over concerns about civilian casualties.
Trump reversed the policy in January 2025.
Brian Finucane, a senior adviser at the International Crisis Group, said there were “real concerns” over how such weapons could be used in densely populated areas, given Israel’s conduct of its air campaign in Gaza and, to some extent, in southern Lebanon.

items.author: Gaurav Bagur
items.content:
After months of anticipation, UPI operator National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) has introduced the merchant discount rate (MDR) fees framework for select high-value UPI transactions. MDR on UPI will take effect precisely one month from today, that is, October 15.
Under the framework, standard person to merchant (P2M) transactions above ₹2,000 will attract an MDR of 0.4%, capped at ₹300 for high-value payments of ₹75,000 and above. However, peer-to-peer (P2P) transactions will continue to be free.
“MDR is a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem. It is not a charge on customers making UPI payments. Banks have been advised to ensure that merchants do not pass MDR charges on to customers. UPI application providers are expressly prohibited from imposing platform fees or hidden charges,” the Ministry of Finance said in a statement.
Further, small merchants, including street vendors, receiving up to ₹1 Lakh per month through UPI QR codes under the person to person merchant (P2PM) category will continue to enjoy zero MDR on all transactions.
The revenue generated from the MDR will be split between ecosystem partners as follows, 0.28% as interchange fee to the issuer bank, 0.12% to the payment service provider (PSP) of the payer, and 0.08% to app providers.
The Ministry noted that the framework protects individuals, micro-enterprises and small businesses while introducing a limited charge on larger merchant transactions.
“Data analysis indicates that MDR will apply to only about 4% of merchant transactions. This means that approximately 96% of merchant transactions will remain unaffected, as they are either below the ₹2,000 threshold or covered by the zero-MDR framework for small merchants,” the statement read.
Specific merchant categories — railways, telecom, insurance and fuel — will operate on a flat fee of ₹5 for payments exceeding ₹2,000, in order to maintain low costs for critical public services, utility bill collection, thin-margin sectors like fuel retail, and other essential consumer services
Additionally, capital market transactions will incur a lower rate of 0.02%, capped at ₹300, to encourage participation in the markets ecosystem. This applies to payments towards mutual funds, stockbrokers, securities dealers, and investment platforms.
The framework’s aim is to support UPI’s long-term sustainability while keeping transactions free for consumers and small merchants, the Centre reiterated.
Under the plan, 5% of total MDR collections will be allocated to a dedicated fund to promote UPI adoption and usage among small merchants.
Revenue from larger merchant transactions will help banks, payment service providers and UPI apps invest in payment infrastructure, particularly across rural and semi-urban areas.
Introduced under the recently amended Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007, the framework follows deliberations by the UPI Steering Committee on rates, operations and consumer safeguards. It also aligns with the Standing Committee on Finance’s call for a viable revenue model for UPI.
The Rationale Behind The Implementation Of MDR
The new frameworks come at a time when the adoption and utilisation of UPI in the Indian digital transaction ecosystem is breaking records almost every month. For instance, monthly UPI transactions touched an all-time high in August, with transaction volume rising nearly 4% MoM to 24.51 Bn from 23.66 Bn in July.
However, annual infrastructure, cybersecurity, and operational upkeep costs for the UPI system is increasing parallely, costing around ₹20,000 Cr per year. On the other hand, the Centre’s allocations for digital payments incentives had amounted to just a fraction of this amount.
As a result, industry leaders have been advocating for the re-introduction of MDR so that banks, aggregators, and other financial institutions could monetise UPI transactions and cover their costs.
“Most global payment systems (including Digital Public Infrastructures) have economic models that support infrastructure and innovation. India’s approach continues to prioritise accessibility, scale and inclusion,” the NPCI said.
Avoiding sole reliance on government subsidies provides revenue predictability for acquiring banks, payment service providers, and fintech apps and enables them to make long-term investments in upgrading technology, it added.
NPCI believes MDR revenue can help fund investments in cybersecurity, AI-led fraud detection and encryption upgrades, while also creating a more viable business model for payment players.
“The introduction of MDR on UPI would materially change the narrative around fintechs. The sector has long been viewed as one where scale has been built without a clear path to monetisation. A sustainable revenue model for UPI would alter that perception, improve investor sentiment and give the fintech ecosystem a significant boost,” Pine Labs CEO Amrish Rau said.
Commercialisation could also open up the UPI market to smaller and newer players that may struggle to compete with larger companies that can absorb sustained losses. The ecosystem is currently dominated by PhonePe, Google Pay and Paytm, with the top two accounting for around 78% of UPI transactions.
A portion of the MDR revenue will also be used to create a dedicated fund for merchant onboarding and digital payment infrastructure in Tier III and IV regions, including the northeastern states, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. The fund is aimed at improving UPI adoption among small businesses and supporting wider financial inclusion.
NPCI is expected to notify the fund framework in consultation with the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) within the next three months.

items.content:
The world's biggest AI companies are working on creating a standards body, ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said on Tuesday, as fears rise about the dangers of AI and pressure is on to create a safer version of the technology.
OpenAI said it was working with Anthropic and Google on an idea that originated from a proposal by Google DeepMind's Demis Hassabis for a self-regulatory body modeled after the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority that oversees US brokers and investment firms.
In July, Hassibis called for the United States to create an organization that would test the most powerful AI systems before they are released to the public.
"Funding would need to be substantial and likely mostly come from industry, in order to attract world-class technical talent and provide the necessary compute resources for large-scale testing," Hassabis wrote.
There is no consensus on how to move forward, though.
The chief of Canadian AI company Cohere recently accused the dominant American AI labs of forming a "cartel" under the guise of safety.
"AI needs guardrails. That is not the dispute and never has been. The dispute is over who writes them, who gets to participate and whose interests the rules are protecting," Cohere co-founder and CEO Aiden Gomez wrote in a blog post on Sunday.
Read More: Ex-Google DeepMind researcher adds to warnings that AI could 'kill all humans'
Concerns about AI safety have escalated in recent weeks, including warnings from two workers who resigned from major AI developers amid concerns about the industry's risks.
Last week, Jacob Coxon left Anthropic and warned that AI companies were "gambling with our lives." He also previously worked at OpenAI.
On Monday, former Google DeepMind researcher Bilal Chughtai echoed the concerns raised by Coxon and others.
"I earnestly believe that AI has the potential to kill us all, and that we might be running out of time to avoid this outcome," Chughtai wrote on social media.
On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slowdown in the pace of AI development, a sentiment that OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Hassabis all supported.
US President Donald Trump has however dismissed warnings about the risks of AI as "hoaxes."
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has also pushed back.
"The confluence of these words and then the prediction is alarming and troubling and it shouldn't be done. It's irresponsible," Huang said Monday at a conference in Los Angeles where Trump called him while he was on stage.
The dire outlook that AI could destroy humanity "is not grounded on science," Huang said.

items.author: Bambang Dwi Atmoko
tags: LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA
items.content:
Berapa biaya listrik yang dibutuhkan sebuah AC setiap hari? Pertanyaan ini menjadi semakin relevan ketika perangkat pendingin udara digunakan dalam durasi panjang. LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA, AC inverter berkapasitas 1/2 PK, kini memiliki hasil pengujian efisiensi energi dari Universitas Indonesia (UI) yang memberikan gambaran mengenai konsumsi listriknya.
Berdasarkan hasil pengujian laboratorium Universitas Indonesia (UI), konsumsi listrik LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA sekitar Rp912 per hari dalam kondisi uji tertentu. Angka tersebut menjadi dasar bagi LG untuk menyoroti efisiensi energi pada produk AC terbarunya.
Baca juga: LG Electronics Pamerkan 7 Inovasi Perangkat Smart Home Berbasis AI di IFA 2026 Berlin
“Dengan efisiensi energi menjadi salah satu pertimbangan penting konsumen saat memilih perangkat elektronik rumah tangga, hasil pengujian dari Universitas Indonesia ini menjadi bentuk tanggung jawab kami dalam memasarkan LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator model K05NVA dengan pengoperasian hemat energi sebagai salah satu superioritasnya,” ujar Ha Sang-chul, President of LG Electronics Indonesia, saat mermpekenalkan produk AC terbarunya ini di Jakarta (15/9).
LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA Pakai Dual Inverter Compressor dan Watt Control
Salah satu teknologi utama pada LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA adalah Dual Inverter Compressor. Teknologi inverter memungkinkan kompresor menyesuaikan kecepatannya berdasarkan kebutuhan pendinginan ruangan. Artinya, kompresor tidak harus selalu bekerja pada tingkat kecepatan yang sama ketika kondisi ruangan sudah mendekati temperatur yang diinginkan.
LG mengaitkan kemampuan menyesuaikan kecepatan tersebut dengan konsumsi energi yang lebih rendah. Perusahaan juga menyebut perubahan kecepatan kompresor memungkinkan proses pendinginan berlangsung lebih cepat dibandingkan model konvensional tertentu.
Bagi pengguna, mekanisme tersebut menjadi salah satu aspek penting dari AC inverter. Konsumsi energi tidak hanya ditentukan oleh kapasitas AC, tetapi juga bagaimana kompresor beroperasi selama perangkat digunakan. Pada LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA, teknologi tersebut dipadukan dengan fitur yang memberikan pengguna kontrol lebih terhadap penggunaan daya.
Selain teknologi inverter, LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA dilengkapi Watt Control. Fitur ini memungkinkan pengguna memilih tingkat konsumsi daya AC sesuai kebutuhan. LG menyediakan empat tingkatan pengoperasian hemat daya. Misalnya, ketika AC digunakan pada malam hari dan kondisi lingkungan relatif lebih sejuk, pengguna dapat memilih tingkat konsumsi daya yang lebih rendah. Dalam pengaturan tersebut, laju kerja kompresor dapat diperlambat.
Dengan Watt Control, pengguna tidak sepenuhnya bergantung pada pengaturan otomatis AC. Konsumsi daya dapat disesuaikan dengan kondisi penggunaan.
Dari Dual Swing Auto Hingga Gold Fin dan Auto Cleaning
Efisiensi energi bukan satu-satunya aspek yang dibawa LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA. AC ini memiliki fitur Dual Swing Auto yang membantu mengarahkan udara dingin ke berbagai arah secara otomatis. Sistem tersebut ditujukan untuk membantu penyebaran udara yang lebih merata ke area ruangan.
Fitur ini berkaitan langsung dengan aspek kenyamanan. Ketika udara dingin tidak hanya terfokus pada satu arah, distribusi udara di dalam ruangan dapat dibuat lebih menyeluruh. Meski demikian, LG tidak mencantumkan rekomendasi luas ruangan secara spesifik untuk K05NVA dalam materi yang diberikan. Karena itu, kebutuhan luas ruangan yang ideal untuk AC 1/2 PK ini masih perlu mengacu pada informasi teknis resmi produk atau hasil konsultasi instalasi.
Pada unit outdoor, LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA menggunakan teknologi Gold Fin. Teknologi tersebut berupa lapisan pelindung pada permukaan unit outdoor yang ditujukan untuk membantu menghadapi korosi akibat pengaruh lingkungan. Sementara itu, Auto Cleaning membantu mengurangi kelembapan di bagian dalam unit sekaligus menjaga area evaporator tetap lebih bersih.
Efisiensi Energi Jadi Nilai Jual
Laboratorium Universitas Indonesia (UI) melakukan pengujian LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA selama 8 jam. Hasilnya, AC LG inverter 1/2 PK tersebut mencatat konsumsi energi 0,63 kWh dengan estimasi biaya listrik Rp911,96 atau sekitar Rp912. Pengujian dilakukan pada suhu 24°C dan Watt Control 40% di ruangan berukuran 7,5 meter persegi.
Jika dihitung secara sederhana, angka tersebut setara sekitar Rp27.360 untuk 30 hari. Namun, angka bulanan tersebut merupakan perhitungan matematis dari angka hasil uji, bukan angka tagihan listrik aktual yang dijanjikan LG kepada pengguna.
Namun perlu diperhatikan, konsumsi listrik AC sangat bergantung pada cara perangkat digunakan. Konsumen sebaiknya tidak hanya melihat angka biaya harian. Hasil aktual di rumah akan bergantung pada bagaimana AC digunakan dan kondisi ruangan. AC yang menyala beberapa jam sehari tentu memiliki pola konsumsi berbeda dibandingkan perangkat yang beroperasi sepanjang hari. Begitu pula temperatur yang dipilih. Semakin besar kebutuhan pendinginan ruangan, semakin besar pula pekerjaan yang perlu dilakukan sistem pendingin.
Harga Rp4 Jutaan, Garansi hingga 10 Tahun
LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA menyasar konsumen yang mencari AC inverter berkapasitas 0,5 PK. Berdasarkan penelusuran Gizmologi di website LG Indonesia, harga LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA tercantum sekitar Rp4,3 juta. LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA di LG Indonesia
Dari sisi layanan purnajual, LG memberikan garansi kompresor hingga 10 tahun untuk produk ini. Garansi hingga 10 tahun juga diberikan untuk spare part dan PCB, dengan syarat dan ketentuan yang berlaku.
Pada akhirnya, LG DUALCOOL Inverter New Terminator K05NVA menawarkan kombinasi antara teknologi inverter, pengaturan konsumsi daya, distribusi udara otomatis, serta fitur perawatan. Sementara hasil pengujian UI memberikan informasi tambahan bagi konsumen yang menjadikan konsumsi energi sebagai salah satu pertimbangan ketika memilih AC.

items.author: Prasetyo Herfianto
items.content:
The Pokemon Company baru saja mengumumkan sejumlah inisiatif yang disiapkan untuk tahun fiskal 2026 – 2027 secara khusus untuk Indonesia. Melalui sebuah acara konferensi pers khusus yang digelar Senin (14/9), The Pokemon Company memperkenalkan sejumlah proyek baru yang terdiri dari berbagai sektor bidang, mulai dari budaya tradisional Indonesia hingga olahraga dan game.
Inisiatif serta rencana baru The Pokemon Company sendiri digelar sekaligus menyambut eksistensi Pokemon yang sudah akan menginjak tahun ke-30. Sang COO, Takato Utsonomiya mengatakan bila tahun ini siap menjadi tahun yang sangat bersejarah bagi Pokemon, di mana akar perjalanan yang dimulai dari sebuah game, tengah berkembang menjadi sesuatu yang jauh lebih besar dari itu. Dan pihaknya siap menghadirkan pengalaman game yang baru untuk masyarakat Indonesia.
“Melalui interaksi kami dengan masyarakat Indonesia, saya merasakan bahwa budaya Jepang tidak sekadar dikenal di sini, melainkan dipahami dan dinikmati secara mendalam. Karena itu, kami pun ingin belajar dari Indonesia, salah atunya dari kesenian tradisional seperti Wayang. Kami sangat menghormati dan ingin mempelajari kekayaan budaya tersebut, sembari menciptakan pengalaman baru khas Pokemon bersama Anda semua. Melalui Pokemon, kami berharap dapat menghubungkan Indonesia dengan dunia,” tambah Takato.
Baca juga: Fitbit Air Edisi Spesial Pokemon Sleep, Rayakan Hari Jadi ke-30 Tahun Pokemon
Siap Merayakan Budaya Indonesia Hingga Ajak Masyarakat Lebih Aktif Berolahraga
Seperti yang sudah disebutkan sebelumnya, setidaknya ada lima inisiatif berbeda yang siap dilakukan oleh The Pokemon Company secara khusus di Indonesia. Salah satunya merupakan kolaborasi antara Pokemon dan Wayang sebagai salah satu budaya tradisional melalui “Poke Wayang”. Kolaborasi ini ditujukan agar anak-anak Indonesia mendapatkan ruang lebih untuk mengenal budaya mereka lebih dekat, sembari mengajak berbagai generasi lainnya untuk menemukan kembali pesona kesenian Wayang.
Di dalam kisah Poke Wayang nantinya juga akan disematkan sejumlah pesan moral untuk anak-anak Indonesia, seperti nilai-nilai terkait bekerja sama dengan teman, hingga saling mendukung bersama orang-orang terekat. Pertunjukkan perdananya sendiri akan dijadwalkan pada 22 Oktober 2026, yakni pada ajang World Conference on Creative Economy (WCCE). Dan The Pokemon Company juga siap menggelar tur pertunjukkan Poke Wayang ke berbagai sekolah dasar di seluruh Indonesia.
Dua inisiatif lainnya yang terkait dengan olahraga, adalah peluncuran “MilkLife Sports Project with Pokemon” dan “Pokemon RUN 30”. Berkolaborasi dengan MilkLife, Pokemon bersinergi dengan inisiatif sepak bola putri dan bulu tangkis yang digagas oleh MilkLife, yang ditujukan untuk mendukung semangat olahraga anak-anak. Dengan sesi coaching clinic khusus yang bakal digelar di Jakarta mulai 17 September 2026.
Sementara itu, Pokemon RUN sebagai acara lari tematik interaktif juga kembali hadir, sekaligus memperingati hari jadi Pokemon ke-30. Siap digelar 13 Desember 2026, acara ini bakal digelar di GBK dan Jalan Sudirman Jakarta, dengan kategori lari 5 kilometer serta biaya pendaftaran Rp899 ribu—sudah termasuk Race Pack Eksklusif ”Pokemon Run 30 Runner’s Kit”.
Siap Hadirkan Bahasa Indonesia Ke Game Populer Pokémon
Bagi Gizmo friends yang senang bermain game Pokemon Trading Card Game Pocket di smartphone, The Pokemon Company siap menghadirkan dukungan pilihan Bahasa Indonesia di dalam aplikasi mulai Januari 2027. Inisiatif satu ini hadir sebagai bentuk komitmen dan apresiasi dari The Pokemon Company, dengan jumlah total unduhan lebih dari 200 juta secara global, 5,2 juta unduhan di antara berasal dari pemain di Indonesia.
Tidak hanya bisa bermain dengan bahasa yang lebih familiar dan mudah dipahami, The Pokemon Company juga siap berikan hadiah item spesial di dalam aplikasi, berupa “Pikachu Berkemeja Batik”. Terakhir, gelaran “Pikachu’s Indonesia Journey” siap kembali dgelar di Central Park Mall, Jakarta bersamaan dengan peluncuran resmi konsol Nintendo Switch Series pada 10 Desember 2026.
“Meski kita berasal dari negara, bahasa, dan budaya yang berbeda, kita tetap bisa memainkan game yang sama, bersenang-senang dengan kartu yang sama, dan menjalin ikatan pertemanan dari sana. Saya percaya, itulah kekuatan sejati yang dimiliki oleh Pokemon. Ke depannya, bersama para mitra di Indonesia, kami berkomitmen untuk terus menghadirkan kegembiraan, kejutan, dan kenangan indah khas Pokemon bagi seluruh masyarakat Indonesia,” tutup Takato.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
The Delhi High Court has asked the RBI to mediate a dispute involving Prosus-backed fintech platform PayU Payments, YES Bank, ICICI Bank, other acquiring banks, and Visa over interchange reimbursement fee (IRF) claims arising from the alleged misclassification of merchant category codes (MCCs).
The court directed the parties to maintain the status quo on claims arising from past transactions and barred acquiring banks from making further deductions from PayU’s settlements while the mediation is underway.
It also restrained Visa from issuing final determinations on pending IRF claims concerning past transactions.
The order was passed by a single-judge bench of Justice Subramonium Prasad after the court heard arguments for four consecutive days on the maintainability of PayU’s suit and its plea for interim relief.
The court asked the RBI to depute a senior officer familiar with the payments sector to help the parties reach a resolution within 30 days. The matter will next be heard on October 27.
The development was first reported by Bar & Bench.
What’s The Dispute?
The dispute relates to IRF claims raised by ICICI Bank before Visa against YES Bank and three other acquiring banks for allegedly assigning incorrect MCCs to certain merchants.
An MCC is a four-digit code identifying a merchant’s principal line of business. It is used to determine the interchange fee payable by an acquiring bank to an issuing bank.
PayU told the court that it does not assign MCCs. The payment aggregator said it collects and verifies merchants’ business information and forwards it to the relevant acquiring bank, which independently assesses the business and assigns the appropriate code.
According to PayU, YES Bank deducted amounts from its ongoing settlements towards the IRF liability. Although the bank subsequently reversed more than ₹5.95 Cr, it continues to retain ₹6.88 Cr, the court order said.
PayU has sought the return of ₹6.88 Cr, along with annual interest of 18% from the date of deduction.
The payment aggregator has also flagged the possibility of further deductions. According to the order, ICICI Bank has raised claims of about ₹5.26 Cr, ₹27.3 Cr, and ₹8.82 Cr against three other acquiring banks.
The court observed that it was unclear who assigned the allegedly incorrect MCCs that led to the claims and subsequent deductions.
Court Puts Claims On Hold
PayU has also challenged Visa’s IRF compliance process, arguing it does not comply with the dispute-resolution mechanism prescribed under Section 24 of the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.
Visa, however, told the court that the claims were being processed under its rules and compliance framework. It said it had no role in deductions from PayU’s settlement accounts, as any recovery would depend on the agreements between PayU and the acquiring banks.
The court said the RBI was best placed to help resolve the matter as the payment ecosystem involved was operating under authorisations granted by the central bank and under its supervision.
“The senior officer of the RBI would be the most competent person to assist the parties to come to a solution pending the mediation process,” the court said.
However, the court clarified that the RBI would act only as a mediator and facilitator, and not as a dispute-resolution body under Section 24 of the PSS Act.
During the mediation, Visa cannot issue any final determination on the pending IRF claims concerning past transactions against YES Bank and the three other acquiring banks. The banks, in turn, cannot deduct, debit, or recover the disputed amounts from PayU.
ICICI Bank and any other issuing bank involved in the proceedings have also been barred from raising further claims for interchange-income losses arising from alleged MCC misclassification in PayU transactions conducted before the suit was filed.
The directions apply only to transactions in which merchants were allegedly assigned incorrect MCCs. The court said the order would not affect routine transactions between the parties or their existing and future contractual and legal rights.
